(23’) Burnley displaying the same bravery they have showed all season, and results to match these high-intensity showings would have seen them retain their top-flight status. Ings and Barnes again link up well and the in-form striker fires low and hard, but Butland again makes a strong save.
(21’) Stoke now calming proceedings down in midfield, after many dangerous chances from their attacking opposition. Butland goes long in search of Diouf up front, who has been isolated so far.
(19’) Ings sends in a dangerous delivery which ends up at the feet of Boyd, but another superb save from Butland denies the eventual shot from Jones. Top class goalkeeping from the Stoke number one, who is keeping his side in this game at the moment!
(17’) At the other end, Heaton is called into action for the first time, but he only has to come and calmly collect a broken down Burnley move. Boyd tries to get in behind the Stoke defence from a wide right position straight after but the towering figure of Shawcross blocks his attempts.
(15’) England Under-21 manager Gareth Southgate looks on from the stands, as Ings continues his ongoing battle with Butland, two players who are sure to make an impact in the summer's European Championship competition. The Under-21 skipper and goalkeeper makes several great stops to deny his international teammate as Stoke survive an attacking onslaught.
(13’) Barnes draws a foul from Shawcross to win a free-kick in a dangerous position on the edge of the panelty area. Trippier's resutling set-piece fails to cause any trouble though, as Butland eventually collects without any hassle.
(11’) Ings does brilliantly to track back and win the ball back for his side. Although Barnes is unable to make the most of his strike partner's efforts, subsequently playing a poor forward pass towards Boyd on the right wing.
(9’) Shackell and Duff being deal with several long throw-ins from wide right to clear any possible dangerous. Stoke failing to make any impact going forward, with Hughes' Potters needing just a point for their highest ever top-flight finish.
(7’) Stoke continuing to be pegged back by this already relegated home side, but now have their first real spell of possession with N'Zonzi in the centre. Adam's lofted corner is a poor one and the visitors' attack breaks down, as Butland ends up with the ball at his feet.
(5’) It's all Burnley in these opening stages, with Barnes and Ings making lively starts. The club's top scorer this season has drifted out wide and cut in on his ferocious right foot twice now and is looking dangerous.
(3’) So Turf Moor bids farewell to Premier League football for another season, but Burnley will look to bow out in style! Set up in a familiar 4-4-2, the hosts are attacking from the flanks early, and Ings cuts inside from wide left to strike on goal. Though his shot goes straight at Butland.
(1’) The home side get the game going and are shooting from left to right in this first-half!
We are just 10 minutes away from kick-off here at Turf Moor!
The Clarets are one of only two teams (along with Watford) to have played in more than one Premier League season and been relegated each time. While, the Potters have 50 points this term and one more will be a new club record in the top-flight.
Victory would see Burnley record a top-flight double over Stoke for the first time since the 1967-68 season. The Potters have not won a top tier match at Turf Moor since 1975, although that covers just one game; a 1-1 draw in the Premier League in 2010.
Burnley play their final home game of the campaign knowing they will be playing in the Championship next season. Although the Clarets have been hardworking and unified under Sean Dyche, a small consolation but one that should give them confidence for a possible return to the top-flight for the 2016-17 season.
Stoke subs: Begovic, Wollscheid, Wilson, Ireland, Odemwingie, Sidwell, Crouch.
Stoke starting line-up: Butland; Cameron, Shawcross, Muniesa, Pieters; Whelan, N'Zonzi; Walters, Adam, Arnautovic, Diouf.
Burnley subs: Gilks, Keane, Vokes, Kightly, Ulvestad, Jutkiewicz, Ward.
Burnley starting line-up: Heaton; Trippier; Shackell, Duff, Mee; Boyd, Arfield, Jones, Taylor; Barnes; Ings.
Team news: The hosts have Kevin Long (knee) and Dean Marney (knee) unavailable through injury, while Victor Moses (hamstring) and Bojan Krkic (knee) are absent for the visitors.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of today’s Premier League clash between Burnley and Stoke City. I’m Lee Gormley and I’ll be guiding you through all of the action from Turf Moor!

QPR fans meanwhile have rushed the pitch, celebrating the victory with the players. They might be in the Championship next year but a good run of form at the end of the season can send them down with the belief that they can come right back up. Thank you for joining us here today!
For Newcastle, it was a great first half performance but a very poor second half, with no answer after Fer scored his wondergoal. They are in serious danger of relegation now, needing a win against West Ham next week at home to ensure they stay up!
(90’) And it's a poor effort, going right to McCarthy, and it turns out to be the last meaningful action of the game! QPR have come from behind, despite already being relegated, to defeat Newcastle 2-1 at home!
(90’) Barton takes down Jonas just outside the box and this is surely a golden opportunity to equalize! Cisse stands over the ball, ready to direct his effort on goal.
(90’) Three minutes of injury time have just been announced by the fourth official, with QPR swarming the visitors with every touch of the ball.
(88’) Newcastle take yet another corner - their 11th of the match - but it's poor, right into the arms of McCarthy. They're minutes away from staring down the barrel of defeat, knowing this leaves them in a reckless position for relegation!
(86’) Newcastle look well and truly sucker punched ever since that second goal - they haven't offered much, though Perez does well to keep the ball in the box but Cisse can't poke it into the net when McCarthy spills it!
--- 84’ Yellow card It's a caution for Yoon after a poor challenge down his own flank and Newcastle take the ensuing free kick into the box, but it's cleared and QPR are countering, winning a corner in the process. ---
(82’) SISSOKO JUST WIDE! Off a mistake at the back that sees the ball hit two players and fall kindly for the midfielder, he takes a shot from inside the box towards the far post that goes millimetres wide!
(81’) Newcastle are really just hanging on now, with Sissoko conceding a free-kick that the home side play short before sending an overhit cross into the box.
(79’) Barton takes a wild shot from outside of the box that was going well wide but takes a fortunate deflection off the QPR defence and begets a corner!
(77’) It's still been all QPR since that second goal of theirs, with them entrenched deeply down the left Newcastle flank, winning a series of throw-ins that ensures they stay near the box.
(75’) Perez concedes a free-kick after stepping late on Barton's foot with the midfielder down, just outside of the QPR box. The Rangers aren't really in a hurry to take this here, and hoof it up to their frontline.
--- 73’ Substitution Cabella, who's had a bit of a quiet and frustrating day, comes off for Ameobi as Newcastle make one last roll of the dice with the end of the 90 minutes rapidly approaching for the visitors. ---
(71’) Colback does very well to shepard the ball out of his box under immense pressure from the home side, who continue to try and build on their lead as they seek a third.
(69’) Both sides miss chances in quick succession, with Gutierrez firing right at the keeper following a solid run in the midfield, and Fer firing over from a smart cutback under pressure from a tackle from Gutierrez.
(68’) Sissoko plays the ball up to Aarons but the QPR defence clears it well. The visitors do not look like they have much of a strategy to score their second at the moment, with the plan looking just like crosses from either wing.
(66’) Newcastle now are in serious trouble and need to do everything they can to score again. With Hull currently losing to Tottenham, this is the chance they can take advantage of to ensure safety - but a loss for them too means that it can go down to the final day!
--- 64’ Substitution R. Aarons enters the game and replaces R. Taylor. ---
(64’) Taylor comes off for Aarons, as perhaps a precaution given the midfielder's history of knee trouble and the hit he took just a few short minutes ago, and Riviere makes his exit for CIsse.
--- 63’ Substitution P. Cissé enters play, replacing E. Rivière. ---
(63’) Dummett skies his shot from the corner after finding the ball fortunately bouncing right in front of him, from nealry point blank range! What a chance that was!
(62’) Taylor tries to emulate Fer on the other end of the pitch but his shot takes a touch off the keeper and he wins his side a corner.
--- 61’ Assist M. Phillips provided the assist. ---
--- 61’ Goal! AN UNREAL GOAL FROM FER! WHAT A SENSATIONAL STRIKE! AND QPR ARE IN THE LEAD! Just like that, Newcastle are trailing! Fer collected the ball from ten yards outside the box and curled a fantastic effort into the top corner that left Krul no chance to save! ---
(60’) Newcastle's seventh corner of the day is headed out of the box but kept alive by Janmaat, before Cabella crossed it back into the box. QPR counter and Austin goes for it from just inside the area that Krul saves easily.
(58’) The game is even here, with Taylor standing over a free-kick in the heart of the pitch, played up to Sissoko and forced out for a corner by Yoon.
(56’) Guiterrez just brushes aside Barton on the wing to get to the box and deliver a cross, and though it initially comes to nothing, the pullback allows Janmaat to shoot on target after the advantage is played when Taylor is fouled from behind.
--- 54’ Assist Assist by C. Austin. ---
--- 54’ Goal! PHILLIPS EQUALIZES! WHAT A DAGGER TO NEWCASTLE! Again it's a simple finish from a simple play: a nice cross whipped in from the wing from Austin that hangs perfectly in the air for the number 7 to head into the net! GAME ON! ---
(52’) AUSTIN JUST WIDE! Newcastle's defending was nowhere to be seen as a high ball over the top fooled Coloccini and Dummett, with the striker taking the ball down, hoodwinking both of them, and firing just wide of the far post!
(51’) Both goalkeepers have been busy collecting stray balls in their boxes but neither sides' offense are really generating chances in the area, to the relief of both defences.
--- 50’ Yellow card J. Barton is yellow-carded. ---
(49’) During the half time interval, Henry and Caulker came off for Cox and Yoon as the home side look to get back into this one now. Newcastle take a free-kick short that Cabella whips into the box, just over the head of Dummett!
(47’) QPR NEARLY EQUALIZE! A fantastic ball played into the box finds Fer unmarked, who's making a run towards the far post, and he sticks his boot out to volley it into the net. Coloccini slides in to make a tackle that diverts the ball out for a corner!
--- 46’ Substitution J. Hoilett is replaced with R. Grego-Cox. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Suk-Young Yoon enters the game and replaces S. Caulker. ---
(46’) The second half is now underway! It begins the way the first ended, with a good run into the box from Perez that McCarthy scoops up.
QPR meanwhile were largely dull and devoid of ideas, with a single shot attempted in the first 45 minutes and offering no real threat besides a few crosses in from Hill that Krul collected easily.
It was an open, engaging and rather even affair until Krul's assist to open the goal that gave all the momentum to Newcastle. For the visitors, this is exactly what they need in terms of points and performance and they'll want to keep it up in the second half.
(45’) And that's the half! It's ends 1-0 to Newcastle after the first 45 minutes thanks to a classy finish from Riviere.
(45’) Hill passes the ball back from his keeper under heavy pressure from the Newcastle's frontline, who are incessantly pressing at every opportunity.
(45’) Into the first of four minutes of injury time and Sissoko has a shot blocked in the box that goes out for a corner, which Coloccini nearly diverts into the net on a flying diving header!
(43’) With the half drawing to a close here, QPR are playing a dangerous game and just trying to hold on until the whistle. There's been immense pressure from Newcastle ever since the goal and in some ways the home side are fortunate to only be down by one.
(41’) Close again from Newcastle! They're cutting in from the left dangerously and whipping crosses in time and time again that are just nearly missing the men making runs into the box.
(39’) QPR are looking to copy the strategy that Newcastle used so effectively to score, sending high balls to Austin from the defence, but they're not troubling Krul so far.
(37’) Barton is still pushing his side forward, and he goes down in the middle of the pitch but is soon on his feet again. The match is quite scrappy right now, with neither side being able to hang onto the ball.
(35’) Green does indeed come off as McCarthy comes on the pitch to replace his keeper. His first involvement is a goal-kick, and soon the match is back underway.
--- 34’ Substitution A. McCarthy comes on for R. Green. ---
(33’) Green is still being evaluated on the pitch. He's on his feet, talking to the physios and the referee as they try to stem the bleeding. It remains to be seen if he's coming off.
(31’) Green rushes out to grab a dangerous ball that Sissoko ushered into the area but collided his head with Barton's knee in the process. He's got a cut above his eye and he's bleeding - he's being evaluated now and this might raise some questions about the Premier League's concussion protocol if he doesn't come off.
(29’) Somewhat predictably that goal has really bolstered Newcastle's confidence and they're swarming the area outside of QPR's box at will, looking to break down the resistance.
(27’) QPR have to be careful not to let their heads get away from them now - Austin commits a foul high in the midfield to concede a free-kick to the visitors.
(26’) Newcastle nearly double their lead off a whirling Taylor free-kick from just outside the area that bends just a little too far past the far post!
--- 24’ Assist T. Krul provided the assist. ---
--- 24’ Goal! GOOOOOAAALLLL NEWCASTLE! COULD THIS BE THE GOAL THAT KEEPS THEM UP?! It's simple route one football: a high ball over the top that Riviere beat the offside trap to take down and slot in past Green! 1-0 to the Magpies! ---
(22’) Barton is doing all he can to urge his teammates forward here. He's been all over the midfield, plugging in where needed to shield the defence.
(21’) A fantastic team move from Newcastle works the ball well inside of the box but Onuoha slides in to concede the corner before Riviere can pull the trigger!
(19’) Onuoha works a cross into the area after Newcastle fail to truly clear the ball but it's Krul who comes to the rescue and plucks it out of the air.
(17’) It's a physical battle out there with quite a high number of throw-ins resulting from tackles in the midfield. Barton plays a quick free-kick up towards Austin that forces the Newcastle defence to concede a throw-in deep in their own half.
(15’) Slowly but surely, Newcastle are working the ball forward, but the progression is halted when Onuoha is knocked over by Riviere and a foul is blown just outside of the box for QPR.
(13’) Janmaat again intercepts the ball excellently down his flank but his forwards aren't on the same page and lose the ball just as quickly as he won it. Newcastle are struggling to keep the ball, instead forcing QPR into several throw-ins.
(12’) A corner for the home side nearly results in a chance, but Krul collects the ball just over the head of Henry.
(10’) It's been all QPR up to now, switching from one flank to another as they look to use their width, but Janmaat wins possession and forces a corner.
(8’) Hill is trying to pump a steady stream of crosses into the box but Newcastle's defence is dealing with them quite easily. QPR are working it carefully down the left, trying to carve an opening.
(6’) A half chance for the visitors! Riviere races into the box to get on the end of a long cross to try and poke it into the net, but Green shields it carefully over the line.
(5’) Hoilett goes on a mazy run through the middle of the pitch, bypassing several players, but he takes on one man too many and loses it, with his teammates angry that he didn't send it wide.
(3’) A good cross is drilled into the near post by Phillips but Krul is off his line to collect it. It's been a fairly open match so far, with both sides bypassing the midfield easily.
(1’) And we have kick-off! QPR quickly take possession and hoof it up but Coloccini heads it clear. The home side keep the ball near the box for a good spell but the visitors keep it outside of the area.
We're just minutes away from kickoff now! The teams are walking onto the pitch, Newcastle in their black and white stripes and QPR in white and blue.
There are a huge rash of absences for both sides today. The home side will miss Zarate, Isla, Faurlin and Vargas while the visitors will have to do without de Jong, Tiote, Williamson and Taylor.
Newcastle (4-2-3-1): Krul; Gutierrez, Dummett, Coloccini, Janmaat; Colback, Taylor; Cabella, Sissoko, Ayoze; Riviere.
QPR (4-4-1-1): Green; Onuoha, Caulker, Dunne, Hill; Phillips, Barton, Henry, Hoilett; Fer; Austin.
And with QPR effectively relegated, the visitors today will be hoping that they can get the points they need. The Rangers are the only Premier League team not to win at home yet this calendar year but only Newcastle have collected fewer points in 2015.
Recent history between these two sides favours the visitors but only slightly. Newcastle have won all of their last four games against QPR but only by a single goal each, and haven't been defeated in nine meetings.
Hello all and welcome to our live match coverage of QPR vs Newcastle! This is a match that has much on the line: with just two games to go, Newcastle are only two points above the drop. Even with QPR relegated, the result today could decide if John Carver's team joins them!

Full time at the Stadium of Light and Leicester are staying up! Nigel Pearson's men looked dead and buried a few months ago, but a 0-0 stalemate away to Sunderland has saw them gain the point necessary to avoid relegation. The battle continues for the Black Cats, who failed to claim the win in a match which lacked a lot of quality in the final third! I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
(90’) Three minutes of added time allocated by the referee and it is all-Sunderland in the latter stages as Leicester look to leave with a point and secure their Premier League status. The home side are running out of time to claim that vital win!
(88’) Leicester take the quick free kick and Albrighton collects before knocking the ball past van Aanholt and speedily bursting by the left-back. The subsequent cross into the box from the former Aston Villa winger is superb, but the recently introduced Reveillere solidly heads away at the back post!
--- 86’ Substitution A. Réveillère enters play, replacing B. Jones. ---
(86’) The tension is there for all to see in the Stadium of Light as there are musings of discontent every time a Sunderland player gives the ball away. One mistake could prove vital here, so you get the feeling that both sides may indeed settle for a point.
(84’) FLETCHER GOES CLOSE! Johnson cuts in from the right-hand side and whips a teasing cross to the centre of the box for the former Hibernian striker, who rises high before glancing a lovely header towards goal, but his attempt just goes the wrong side of the post! Unlucky!
(82’) The game really has been lacking in any kind of quality for the last 10 minutes or so as both sides begin to show signs of fatigue. Its not looking likely that a moment of creative brilliance is going to settle this, so it will probably be a mistake at the back or a set-piece.
--- 80’ Substitution S. Fletcher enters play, replacing D. Graham. ---
(80’) Another positive throw of the dice from Advocaat now as he introduces Steven Fletcher in place of Danny Graham as Sunderland's central striker. The Scotsman and Johnson have entered the action now, so lets see if they can make an impact.
--- 79’ Yellow card S. Larsson goes into the referee's book. ---
(78’) Albrighton is fouled near the edge of the penalty area and Cambiasso stands over the free kick. An opportunity to make amends for all the previous poor set-pieces comes up but this one from the Argentine is the worst of the lot as he sends a strike at goal at least five yards over the bar. Really poor.
(76’) Some positive news for both Sunderland and Leicester as their relegation rivals, Hull and Newcastle, are both losing their respective matches this afternoon. If those results stay the same than a victory for either outfit today will go a massive way to avoiding the drop! Do we have a winner?!
--- 75’ Substitution A. Kramarić enters the game and replaces L. Ulloa. ---
(74’) It looks like Ulloa won't be able to continue after that knock to the back and he'll be replaced by Leicester's record signing, Kramaric. The Croatian certainly has the quality to provide us with the opening goal, and he has just over 15 minutes of normal time to do so.
(72’) The set-piece delivery from both sides today has been desperately disappointing. Larsson is the guilty party for Sunderland, with Cambiasso and Albrighton also failing to cause problems from their free kicks and corners. That trio is usually excellent from dead balls - but not this afternoon.
(70’) Some worrying scenes for Leicester at the moment as Ulloa is currently down clutching his back after landing awkwardly in an aerial challenge with O'Shea. It looks like the former Brighton striker is going to be okay, but they'll certainly need him firing on all cylinders if they are going to claim a vital away win today.
(68’) First change of the match from Nigel Pearson and it sees Mahrez, who has looked decent on the ball a few times but tailed off after the break, replaced by Drinkwater, who'll certainly add some more legs and solidity into that midfield. The Leicester boss noticing that he may just need to tighten things up in there for the last 20 minutes or so.
--- 67’ Substitution R. Mahrez is done for the day. D. Drinkwater is his replacement. ---
--- 66’ Yellow card C. Wickham receives a yellow card. ---
(66’) The yellow cards are coming thick and fast now and Wickham is the latest player to go into the book, and deservedly so as he comes in with his boot far too high on King. That had the potential to be nasty, but luckily the Sunderland striker pulled out slightly at the last minute.
(64’) Another booking registered which has been a long time coming and it is brandished to Huth, who has always looked capable of going into the book today. His offence is coming straight through the back of Graham with a forearm to the back. Needless foul again.
--- 63’ Yellow card R. Huth is cautioned by the referee. ---
(62’) Albrighton, who has looked more and more bright as the second half has gone on, gets into an advanced position down the right and swings a wicked cross to the front post. Ulloa attempts to get ahead of his marker again but this time O'Shea does well to stick his head in where it hurts to clear the danger.
--- 60’ Substitution L. Bridcutt is done for the day. A. Johnson is his replacement. ---
(60’) First substitution of the match now and it sees Bridcutt, who picked up an injury after tackling Vardy in the first half, come off for Adam Johnson, which certainly signals a positive change in tactics from Dick Advocaat.
(59’) Bridcutt strides ahead through the middle and finds himself 25 yards out, but Cambiasso retreats back and puts the former Brighton midfielder under massive pressure. In the end Huth comes out to help out his team-mate, but concedes the foul in the process.
(57’) Albrighton powers forward on the right flank and stands a teasing cross to the back post, which Cambiasso fancies getting on the end of. The Argentine collects with a bouncing touch to his chest but Pantilimon does well to come off his line and claim out of the air.
(55’) Bridcutt released Graham into the right channel and the former Hull man hits the byline before squeezing out a cross to the front post, but Huth is on hand to clear the danger behind for a corner kick! That piece of play triggers an appreciative cheer from the home crowd!
(53’) SUPERB BLOCK BY MORGAN! Defoe typically manages to find a yard of space inside the box and looks poised to find the back of the net with a drilled strike, but the Leicester captain darts across his penalty area to make the magnificent interception!
(51’) Van Aanholt collects possession at left-back and strides forward before looking to burst beyond Albrighton, but King is over supporting his team-mate and the Leicester duo combine to win the ball back before catalysing a counterattack.
(49’) Scrappy opening to the second period as both sides battle for dominance in the middle of the park. Leicester have came out after the break with slightly more impetus in their passing, but quality in the final third has evaded them so far.
(47’) Albrighton whips in a corner kick to the front post and Ulloa manages to get ahead of O'Shea before bulleting a header towards the bottom corner, but the attempt just screws wide of the right-hand post! Good start to the second half from the Foxes!
(46’) We are back under way in this Barclays Premier League clash!
Half time at the Stadium of Light. With the stakes as high as they are for both sides, it is understandable that Sunderland and Leicester have been slightly apprehensive in their attacking play today, but we have still seen fleeting moments of quality in the final third. There is definitely a goal in this, which will probably prove vital as to who goes ahead first. Intriguing second period in store!
(44’) Perhaps predictably, Cattermole risks the wrath of the referee once again as he cynically trips up Albrighton as Leicester attempt to counterattack. The official doesn't let him off with this one and swiftly produces the booking, which means the central midfielder will be walking on egg shells for the majority of this match.
--- 43’ Yellow card L. Cattermole gets yellow. ---
(42’) Cambiasso strives to get on the end of a high ball on the left-hand side and does so before sweeping a pass down the channel first time for Vardy. The Leicester striker typically chases it down with gusto but Pantilimon proactively comes off his line to pounce on possession.
(40’) Ulloa shakes off the attentions of the Sunderland defenders once again before lifting a neat pass out wide to Mahrez, who looks to take on the defender before smashing a cross into the box but van Aanholt is positioned well enough to turn behind for a corner.
(38’) Disappointing from Sunderland as Larsson opts to lay the free kick off, which results in Wickham's strike being swiftly shut down by three or four Leicester players who had burst out of the wall.
(37’) Pantilimon punts a long ball up top and Defoe collects with a neat touch before firing a pass into the feet of Wickham, but the former Ipswich striker is taken out by a combination of Huth and Wasilewski. Free kick to the hosts in a very useful position on the edge of the penalty area.
(35’) Leicester have just turned up the tempo of their pressing in the last couple of minutes and Sunderland have proved themselves to be susceptible to a mistake on the ball in dangerous areas. Cattermole is the guilty party this time as his heavy touch results in another foul committed on Mahrez. The Algerian has had the Sunderland man's number so far.
(33’) A corner kick is swung into the Sunderland penalty area and there is so much pushing and pulling going on that the referee almost doesn't know who to penalise. In the end the play goes on and the ball drops for Schlupp at the back post, who looks to squeeze a shot away, but his attempt deflects behind for yet another corner.
(31’) Most of the battling has come in the middle of the park as both sides aim to grab an ascendancy with some hard tackling. The three-pronged midfield of Cattermole, Bridcutt, and Larsson have probably just shaded it so far, but Cambiasso has displayed his quality at times too.
--- 29’ Yellow card L. Bridcutt is yellow-carded. ---
(29’) There have been a few decent attempts on goal so far, with Schmeichel the more busier of the goalkeepers, but there has been a lack of what you would call out-and-out goalscoring opportunities. The best chance was arguably the Graham volley at the back post, but it wasn't converted for the home side.
(27’) Bridcutt takes a heavy touch inside the centre circle and then, in his attempts to retrieve possession, goes in extremely late on Vardy with a poor tackle. The Sunderland midfielder actually comes off worse in the challenge, but the referee doesn't show sympathy and awards him a yellow card - the first of the match.
(25’) Mahrez turns sharply midway through the Sunderland half but ends up going down under the soft challenge of Cattermole, who is penalised for the foul. The Algerian picks himself up to have a crack at goal from the resulting free kick, but his attempt goes disappointingly high and wide north of the bar.
(23’) SAVE FROM SCHMEICHEL! Cattermole picks up the ball 30 yards out and drives into the space before lifting a lovely pass into the back post for Graham, who turns his body to squeeze an awkward looking volley towards goal! Not the best executed strike, but the Leicester keeper still makes the solid stop!
(21’) Graham receives the ball to feet deep down the right channel and keeps Huth away with some solid hold-up play, but the Leicester defender allows his frustration to get the better of him before conceding a daft foul with a shove to the back. Free kick to the hosts near the right touchline.
(19’) Schlupp sends a long throw-in down the left wing and Ulloa superbly collects in to his chest before lifting a decent pass into the path of Mahrez. The Algerian finds himself in a great position in front of the Sunderland box but O'Shea just manages to stretch out a leg to poke the ball away from danger.
(17’) O'Shea commandingly clears a cross out of the box and Cambiasso diligently collects before sliding a pass into the feet of Schlupp, but the winger's touch lets him down which allows Jones to step in before bursting into the space that opens up in front of him.
(15’) Van Aanholt displays decent attacking ambition to get beyond Wickham on the overlap down the left flank before hitting the byline. The Dutchman has a few team-mates to pick out inside the box but his reversed cross weakly finds Morgan at the front post, who easily clears.
(13’) The quality of the passing has just drifted away slightly as a few speculative long balls have been pumped up towards the strikers. Both sides do have players who can prosper from these types of passes, such as Ulloa and Wickham, but defences are on top at the moment.
(11’) A very entertaining opening 10 minutes or so in this Barclays Premier League clash. Both outfits are going about their business in a positive fashion and if the tempo remains this high we are sure to see the opening goal soon! But who will find it?!
(9’) A couple of great chances for either side here! Albrighton gets to the back post and turns the ball back into the danger area for Ulloa, but the Leicester striker can't stretch out enough to get a strike on goal! Sunderland swiftly counterattack and possession finds its way to Graham, who swings a deflected strike just beyond the post for a corner kick! Cracking atmosphere inside the Stadium of Light at the moment!

(61’) Mahrez was very close to completing a sublime hat-trick, but there's still plenty of time in this game, and judging by Southampton's defensive showing so far, he may yet get another chance to claim the match ball.

(53’) It's evident why Leicester have started to recently rack up the clean sheets, with yet another dominant defensive showing here on home soil.
(51’) Clyne having a strong start to this second half on the right flank, with England manager Roy Hodgson looking on from the King Power Stadium stands in possible delight. The Saints are again pushed back though, with the Foxes showing great discipline in their backline.

(47’) The Saints have started brightly as they search for a goal which would get them back into this game. Pelle, though, is still being isolated in attack with the visitors resorting to long balls forward to the Italian.
(45’) Southampton get the second-half going as they look to overturn a two-goal deficit!

(45’) Schmeichel's lofted goal-kick finds Cambiasso, but for the first time in this match he loses out to Southampton's sea of red and white shirts in midfield.
(45’) Ulloa tracks all the way back from attack to help out his defence and win the ball back deep in his own half. Leicester closing in on a deserved 2-0 half-time lead.
(45’) Southampton look to peg a goal back before the half-time whistle but Leicester keep their shape and, again, deal with the onslaught as five minutes of added time are signalled.
(44’) Koeman will struggle to find any positives from his side's first-half performance. With Leicester looking impressive towards the end of proceedings here in this first period.

(40’) Mahrez, Ulloa and Vardy have been superb for Leicester, forcing the Saints to now sit deep in case of any further swift front movement. Half-time approaching quickly, as Schlupp sees his delivery go straight into the arms of Gazzaniga from wide left.
(38’) Southampton failing to make any impact on proceedings at all, dominating possession but unable to force any sort of an opening. Although, a heart-in-mouth moment from Morgan almost gifted Davis with a chance to go clean through on goal, but Schmeichel was aware of the danger to clear safe.

(32’) Southampton were one of the top-flight's best performers at the beginning of the season but they look a completely different side today. Koeman will be worried about his defence too, which is looking increasingly vulnerable to the speed of Leicester's forward line.
(30’) A superb first half hour from the home side, with the Saints so far failing to cause any genuine danger and create an opening. Wasilewski's lofted throw-in eventually ends in a foul and a free-kick to the visitors deep in their own half.

(26’) Southampton are struggling to deal with the runs of Ulloa and Vardy in behind their defence, with Cambiasso continuously playing searching balls forward to his available strikers.
(24’) Southampton are all over the place in defence, with Leicester continuing to threaten dangerously on that left flank with Schlupp and Mahrez getting involved too. Clyne gets forward now to help Elia, and Mane gets on the end of the full back's cross but it goes well over the crossbar.
(22’) What a start this is from Pearson's men in their search to avoid relegation! Reed has a long range strike but it can only sting the hands of Schmeichel in goal, as it remains 2-0 early in this first period.

The Saints have picked up just one point in their last five league games on the road, giving Pearson's men a boost.
In contrast. the Foxes have kept three clean sheets in their last four PL games, the same number that they kept in their previous 19 in the competition.
There is further hope for the Foxes as Southampton have kept just one clean sheet in the five league games since Forster got injured. The former Celtic stopper has a joint league-high 13 clean sheets in 2014/15.
Leicester have won five of their last six league games, as many victories as they had collected in their previous 39 PL matches, giving them hope of securing safety this season.
Nigel Pearson will aim to continue his side’s revival against Southampton, who have dipped in form by comparison in recent weeks. Leicester have won five of their past six games and will know that another victory will take them closer towards safety.

Home team news: Andy King (hamstring) remains the only injury absentee for Nigel Pearson, who has been named Premier League manager of the month for April.

The players are out on the pitch, with kick-off just a few moments away.
It has been a tumultuous week for Newcastle in the lead up to this clash. The fall-out from Carver's suggestion that Mike Williamson deliberately got himself sent off against Leicester City brought about player meetings and crisis talks among the staff, before Coloccini released a public letter urging support from the fans as they still look to avoid the drop. Carver then claimed on Thursday that he was the "best coach in the Premier League" and produced a further rallying cry to the fans. They are in very real danger of suffering relegation and a 2-0 win for bitter rivals Sunderland earlier in the day means the pressure is on against West Brom.
By contrast, West Brom manager Tony Pulis effectively has a full squad to pick from today. James Morrison has won his battle to be fit after picking up a knock in training and he takes a place on the bench, with Ben Foster - out until October with a knee injury - the only absentee. The visitors, who beat Manchester United last time out, line up with an almost-identical team to the one which left Old Trafford with all three points, Victor Anichebe replacing Saido Berahino for the only change.
Newcastle's issues have been well-documented in the build-up to this match, much of which have stemmed from a dismal run of eight successive defeats in the Premier League. However, a significant injury list has hardly helped Carver's efforts, with no less than seven players - including the likes of Cheick Tiote and Steven Taylor - absent today. A makeshift backline has been named, with captain Fabricio Coloccini the only recognised defender. Nevertheless, the hosts are able to welcome back Papiss Cisse and Rolando Aarons, both of whom take places on the bench.

That must be an incredibly satisfying victory for Mark Hughes for a number of reasons. The fact that they have done the double over Tottenham Hotspur for the first time in the Premier League and in the process of doing so they have matched their best ever points tally. Plenty of reasons to be cheerful. Vlad Chiriches getting himself sent off certainly made the task of claiming the three points a lot easy but make no mistake the Potters were excellent value for their win.
As for Spurs, well that was a fairly desperate display. After giving Manchester City a run for their money last Sunday, Mauricio Pochettino must be left scratching his head as to how the same group of players can put in such a limp performance. Tottenham's travelling fans deserve and expect a lot better than that. The absence of Danny Rose really unsettled the usually shaky back four. Southampton and Spurs are embroiled in a desperate battle to avoid the Europa League but both will probably end up competing in it next term.
Well people will look at this result and wonder were Stoke that good or Tottenham that bad? In truth, as is often the case, it was a combination of the two. The Potters started on the front foot and never let Spurs off the hook. Charlie Adam continued his rich vein of form and Marko Arnautovic turned in what surely must be one of his best performances of the season. Man for man the home side won their individual battles all over the pitch.
(90’) That's it full time here at the Britannia Stadium. A resounding 3-0 victory for Stoke City!
(90’) Harry Kane is cutting a rather forlorn and frustrated figure up front. He has been starved of service all game and has had to feed off of scraps. That said he has worked tirelessly for the cause and it is this kind of effort, as well as his goals that have endeared him to the Spurs fans.

--- 86’ Assist Assist by M. Arnautović. ---

(86’) GOAL! 3-0! And now Mame Biram Diouf does get the goal that he has been hunting for all afternoon.
--- 84’ Substitution P. Odemwingie comes on for J. Walters. ---

(79’) MISS! And this is a fairly astonishing miss from Jonathan Walters. Ireland and Shawcross had done very well in the build up to set up a chance.

(75’) Nearly another goal for Stoke City as Ireland's cross is nodded down unselfishly across the area by Diouf but Walters is unable to turn the ball home. Maybe Diouf could have gone for goal himself there?

(73’) Mason absolutely clatters into a tackle with Ireland and win the balls cleanly but seems to have hurt himself more than his opponent. Dembele is readying himself to come on and it may well be in place of the young England international.
(71’) Bit of a surprising substitution from Stoke with Charlie Adam being taken off, to a standing ovation, for Stephen Ireland. Adam for my money has been the best player on the park this afternoon but maybe Mark Hughes is looking to protect him and give Ireland a decent run out.
(69’) Eriksen has seen plenty of the ball this half and has tried to ignite something but to no avail so far. No Premier League side has played more games than Tottenham Hotspur this season and perhaps this long season has contributed to a pretty lacklustre display so far. Stoke on the otherhand have been very energetic right from the off.
(67’) Spurs have upped the tempo since the break but have been completely hamstrung by that early red card. Stoke have often been toying with their opponents and have always looked a lot more composed in the final third.
(65’) Tottenham force not one but two corners in a row but they can't make it count. The final ball from Lamela and more often Eriksen has been lacking so far today. The visitors certainly aren't giving up but Stoke are in total control against ten men.
(63’) Adam puts in a devillish cross from the left full of bend and pace which is miscontrolled by Walters at the back post before it is fumbled by Lloris. The Spurs goalkeeper does manage to collect the ball but the referee had already given a foul.
--- 61’ Substitution N. Chadli is replaced with Soldado. ---
(61’) CHANCE! Dier meets Eriksen's cross from the left and forces a corner from the away side. His header was decent but it was deflected up and over the bar by Shawcross. (59’) SAVE! Good stop by Lloris to turn Adam's low bending right footed effort around the post. The Stoke playmaker has really called the tune all game much to the annoyance of the travelling Tottenham supporters who are not his biggest fans. There have been a number of incidents between the player against Spurs in the past.

(53’) CHANCE! Shawcross gets across his man from the resulting freekick but the Stoke skipper can't direct his header on target and the ball goes wide after hitting the turf.
--- 51’ Red card! RED CARD FOR CHIRICHES! Absolute madness from the Romanian captain, who is already on a booking, fouls Diouf in exactly the same way that he did in the first half to Jon Walters. Clattenburg has no option but to show a second yellow card. ---
(49’) Adam nicks the ball from Bentaleb in the centre of the pitch and strides forward towards the Spurs penalty area. (47’) SHOT! Eriksen works the ball onto his right foot and whips it at goal from 30 yards out. There is plenty of swerve on it and Butland opts to punch the ball to safety rather than attempting to catch it. Lamela is then got offside from the subsequent corner.
(46’) Tottenham get the second half restarted. They had to wait after a pitch invader held up proceedings. A disturbing lack of stewards chasing the man down mean that he was on the field of play for longer than you would've liked. No substitutions for either side as of yet.
Spurs have recovered 17 points from losing positions this season and that is a record that is only bettered by Crystal Palace in the Premier League. It will take a fairly miraculous second half recovery to keep Tottenham's distant Champions League prospects alive. If the Potters can keep it tight for the first ten minutes or so of the second half it seems very unlikely that a turnaround will be on. Townsend, Dembele and Soldado could come off the bench to freshen things up. If the pattern remains a third Stoke goal looks more likely.
As for Tottenham, what now for Mauricio Pochettino? His charges really haven't been at the races for the majority of the first fourty-five minutes. He will demand a much better showing for the travelling fans after the interval. The back four haven't played together much and it has certainly showed. They have been nervy and indecisive from the get-go and this hasn't been helped by a rare mistake from Lloris that handed Stoke a two-nil advantage.
Mark Hughes will be absolutely delighted with his sides first half performance. They have been better than their opponents from back to front. Jack Butland hasn't had a huge amount to do but his fingertip save to flick the ball onto the bar may turn out to be vital as it was 1-0 at that stage of the game. The Potters have played with a great tempo and fierce intensity and Spurs simply haven't been able to cope with it so far.
(45’) Half time 2-0 to Stoke City.
(45’) Harry Kane has shown his usual dogged determination to force a corner which Lamela will take. Muniesa heads the ball clear and it eventually works it's way out to Vertonghen who crosses into the area. His cross falls to Mason on the edge of the box but the midfielder scuffs his shot wide. Perhaps he should have done better there.
(45’) There will be two minutes of added time at the end of this first half.
(44’) Stoke seem quite content at times to drop in deep and get men behind the ball before springing onto the counter when it breaks down from Spurs. The Potters have looked very lively on the counter attack and the pace of their attacks have caused their opponents real problems.
(42’) SHOT! I'm almost losing count of the amount of times Arnautovic has hit the target so far today. He is giving Eric Dier a torrid time and on this occasion he takes it down the outside before letting fly with his left foot. Lloris gets down sharply to keep it out at his near post.
(40’) Stoke haven't given much away at all and it has therefore been hard for the Spurs attackers to get into the match. Shawcross and Muniesa have read the play very well and have snuffed out any potential threat.
(38’) Kane wins an excellent tackles in the middle of the Stoke midfield which breaks kindly for Lamela, who appears to pull back Pieters but the referee allows play to continue. (36’) Stoke have been by far the better side thus far but it must be said that the visitors have contributed to their own downfall with some fairly dreadful defending in this first half. If the home side can get through to half-time with this two goal cushion intact they will feel very confident of going on to claim all three points here.
(34’) SAVE! Mason drills a low shot from the edge of the box that stings the palms of Butland but the rookie goalkeeper at this level shows good handling to make sure the ball sticks. Spurs could desperately have done with an immediate reply.

(31’) GOAL! A great finish from Steven N'Zonzi makes it 2-0 to the Potters. Calamitous defending.
(29’) SHOT! Once again Arnautovic tests the reflexes of Hugo Lloris but the curling shot is too central and is well held by the France no.1. Stoke still carrying the greater threat when the go forward.
(27’) Tottenham have reacted reasonably well to going behind, let's face it they are used to it after conceding more than 50 Premier League goals this season. (25’) Stoke then look to launch a counterattack and Mason is lucky to escape a booking. The young midfielder initially did well to intercept a pass towards Diouf but then pulled his man down. Clattenburg showed a lot of leniency there particularly after showing Chiriches a yellow card earlier.
(23’) OFF THE BAR! Spurs nearly straight back on level terms after Lamela's inswinging freekick is flicked on by Muniesa and the ball loops over Butland is hits the woodwork. So close to an equaliser.

(20’) GOAL! STOKE MAKE THE BREAKTHROUGH AND IT'S THE MAN OF THE MOMENT CHARLIE ADAM!

A victory for Stoke City today would take them onto 50 points which is what they managed at the end of last season with still two games remaining. They are also looking to do the double over Tottenham Hotspur after winning 2-1 at White Hart Lane in November. Spurs have an excellent away record this term which is bettered only by Arsenal and Chelsea. They have done well recently at the Britannia winning four of their last five visits.

Jack Butland continues in goal for Stoke City in place of Asmir Begovic.

Mark Hughes makes two changes with Marc Wilson dropping out and Marc Muniesa returning after a hamstring injury. FULL TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 1-2 MANCHESTER UNITED. Marouane Fellaini's late winner cancels out Jason Puncheon's equalizer as the Red Devils take three big steps toward securing a top four place and a spot in next season's Champions League.
(90’) IT'S ALL OVER!
(90’) Palace are committing men forward in search of the equalizer, and they don't have much choice at this point. It's worked around well on the left, but Souare's cross is sent straight into the arms of De Gea. Two of the four minutes of stoppage time are now behind us.
(90’) Superb break from United who nearly put the game to bed! They push forward with pace and Falcao picks out Young, but he can't control it. The pressure stays on and it comes to Mata at the far post, but his side-footed volley is pushed over by Speroni.

(86’) DE GEA SAVES THE DAY AGAIN! Spectacular play from Murray, who chests a pass into the air and turns to volley a thunderous drive at goal, but the Spaniard somehow gets down and reacts quickly enough to make the save!

(82’) Evans to the rescue! Souare picks out Zaha with a lovely cross-pitch pass and the forward escapes Jones to break into the area. He tries to cut around Evans, but the substitute stands his ground! It's a vital intervention from the defender who very well could have just saved a goal.
(80’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United are unbeaten in their last six trips to Selhurst Park across all competitions (W4, D2), outscoring the Eagles 11-2 over that span.
--- 78’ Assist A. Young gave the assist. ---
--- 78’ Goal! FELLAINI HEADS UNITED BACK IN FRONT! Oh has it ever been coming! Young is the architect, curling a sensational cross in for Fellaini at the far post. The Belgian shows great determination, bullying his way onto the end of it with three defenders in the area. ---
(77’) OVER! Young is proving to be the catalyst as United push for a winner. He sprints past Ward with ease and breaks into the area. He manages to pick out Mata with his cutback, but the Spaniard lifts his first-time effort over the bar!
(75’) DEFLECTED WIDE! Young is picked out in space on the left, and he's inexcusably allowed to walk into the area as he cuts into the centre. There's no one pressuring him, but he can't pick out the far corner with his shot as it deflects behind for a corner!
(73’) End-to-end stuff here in South Norwood as these two sides exchange punches in search of a winner. The game has opened up, which is making for wonderful viewing from a neutral standpoint. Surely there is at least one more goal in store here.
(71’) DENIED SENSATIONALLY BY DE GEA! It's absolutely brilliant from the Spaniard, who turns aside Murray from point-blank range! The whole of Selhurst Park was up and ready to celebrate, but De Gea had other plans!
(69’) The match is starting to tilt again in United's favour. They are winning the midfield battles and advancing the ball well up the pitch. Mata and Fellaini link-up well atop the area, before the ball is thread across for Young on the left, but his final delivery is dreadful.
(67’) Crystal Palace have won 18 points this season from losing positions, the highest total among teams in the top flight, including two impressive come from behind victories over Liverpool and Tottenham at this very venue. (65’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United have played 17 Premier League matches this season without Michael Carrick in the lineup and 18 with him. They have just six victories in the midfielder’s absence, compared to 13 when he has featured.
(63’) Mata aims a long cross in at Falcao, but Dann arrives first to head clear. That's the first time I've noticed the Colombian striker since his arrival, which is more of a comment on the way the team are playing behind him than Falcao himself.
(61’) STEERED WIDE! McArthur wins the ball back in the attacking half and breaks forward with pace. He has options a plenty, but opts to go in alone, poking an effort just wide of the far post! United are on their heels and Palace are taking advantage!
(59’) It did indeed take a deflection en route to goal, off the head of Blind. The slight change in direction very well may have kept it just high enough to prevent De Gea from making the save, and the Palace drought is broken.

(35’) Louis van Gaal watches on in disbelief as his players start dropping like flies. His team was just starting to get healthy, but they have a few fresh concerns here as Wayne Rooney and Luke Shaw both require treatment. The striker appears to have a dead leg, leaving his status up in the air, though the left-back appears much worse for wear.
(33’) Ward is springing to life as he tries to take matters into his own hands. The right-back makes a clever run into the penalty area, but Fellaini tracks back brilliantly to keep him out and force the ball behind for a goal kick.
(31’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United remain unbeaten against Crystal Palace in 11 all-time Premier League meetings (W9, D2). They have kept nine clean sheets over that span.
(29’) Ward makes a meal of a challenge from Young, but the replay shows there was little, if any, contact made. He sold that like a used car salesman and Oliver bought it. It's a smart move by the right-back to get Young on a warning so he's forced to sit back on his heels a bit. Both players like to get up the pitch, which really is making for another intriguing chess match out on the flank.
(27’) The hosts are starting to grow into the game now, with Jedinak imposing his physical presence in midfield. The Australian is going toe-to-toe with Fellaini and Blind in the middle of the park, which is making for a fascinating battle to observe.
(25’) CLOSE! Much better from Palace, and you get the sense that their best way back into this game may be through a set piece. Ledley delivers a superb cross from a corner and Jedinak rises above Blind to meet it, but his header glances just inches wide of the post.
(23’) The visitors are looking very comfortable in possession and Palace are showing no signs of making life difficult on their opponents. They're trying to feed the ball to Murray when they get the chance, but he doesn't have the technical ability to hold it up and wait for support.
(21’) STAT ATTACK: This is the first time since December 2001 that Manchester United have lost three Premier League matches in a row. They haven’t lost four consecutive league games since 1961.
--- 19’ Goal! MATA CONVERTS! It's a terrific penalty from the Spaniard, who slots it home with power and percision just inside the near post. There's no keeping that one out, and United's scoring drought has finally come to an end! ---
(19’) PENALTY TO UNITED! Palace are livid with the decision, but there's isn't much doubt about this one. Young's cross is blocked by the arm of Dann, who had plenty of time to react to it, and Michael Oliver doesn't hesitate in pointing to the spot.
(17’) Fantastic work from Zaha on the left! The winger is always looking to take on a defender one-on-one, and he usually comes out ahead. Eager to make an impact against his former team, he beats Valencia and sends a teasing cross into the area, but Smalling manages to clear ahead of Murray's impending arrival.
(15’) HERRERA! Palace can't seem to keep the ball, with United very eager to win it back after conceding possession. They have started brightly and certainly aren't shying away from trying their luck from distance. Herrera is the latest to have a go, and doesn't miss by much at the far post.
(13’) Ward curls an inviting ball toward Zaha at the far post, who manages to escape the grasp of Herrera. He cuts back to create space for a cross, but his final ball is poor as it's driven long and far, safely behind for a goal kick.
(11’) DELICIOUS HIT! Daley Blind takes a pass in midfield and rather ambitiously looks to drive a shot at goal from 40-yards out. He gets tremendous pace and movement behind it, but Speroni reacts acrobatically to turn it onto the post and behind for yet another United corner.
(9’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace and Manchester United have each lost three consecutive Premier League matches without scoring a goal. The Eagles last scored in a 4-1 triumph at the Stadium of Light on April 11, while the Red Devils haven’t managed a goal since their convincing derby win over Manchester City on the following day.
(7’) The Red Devils make their intent clear in the early stages of the match, eager to attack down the flanks. Young provides plenty of pace on the left, more so than Mata, but Valencia and Shaw also appear eager to get forward on the overlap.
(5’) Pape Souare, starting today ahead of Adrian Mariappa, is put under pressure from Antonio Valencia. The right-back makes a determined run down the right and manages to win his side a corner, but it comes to nothing as Palace clear their lines convincingly.
(3’) Ashley Young shows great determination to push forward and pressure Palace in possession, stealing the ball near the corner flag. United work it around patiently in the attacking third, but a good defensive intervention from Joel Ward sends the ball out for a Palace throw.
(1’) And we're off! Manchester United in white, attacking right to left, with Crystal Palace sporting their blue and red stripes.
Alan Pardew is buoyed by the returns of Glenn Murray and captain Mile Jedinak from injury, with the duo both moving straight back into the starting lineup. Their arrivals come at the expense of Jason Puncheon and Jordon Mutch, who are dropped to the bench, joining Frazier Campbell and Marouane Chamakh, also making their return from injury.
Michael Carrick is out for the season with a calf injury, but the visitors are boosted by the return of defenders Phil Jones and Luke Shaw, who both slot into the starting lineup, while Jonny Evans returns to the bench. The return of the former Southampton left-back pushes Daley Blind back into a holding role, where he anchors the gap between defence and midfield. The Dutchman's ascent up the pitch sees Wayne Rooney move back to striker in place of Robin van Persie, who is rumoured to be suffering from a virus.

MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Evans, Falcao, Januzaj, Valdes, McNair, Pereira, Wilson.

Crystal Palace are chasing their highest finish in the top flight since 1991, but that dream would die with a defeat today. Nonetheless, Alan Pardew has done a wonderful job erasing the damage inflicted by Neil Warnock, and had the Eagles safe from relegation with over a month to spare – a dream many Palace fans didn't think was possible midway through the season, as they sat third from the bottom when the former Newcastle manager took over. They have little to play for over the final three games, but the players would certainly like to put an end to this unwelcome losing skid today and end their hijinks against Manchester United.
This match could very well cap off a superb week for Manchester United over their rivals Liverpool. The Red Devils beat them to the signature of Memphis Depay, and could conceivably clinch a place in next season’s Champions League with a victory and either a loss or draw for the Reds against Chelsea. The signing of the Dutchman will likely be the first of a plethora of summer arrivals, but it all starts today by picking up three points and taking a big step towards clinching a top four place in the Premier League.
Hello Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to London! Selhurst Park is our venue today as Manchester United try and boost their hopes of a top four finish and a spot in next season’s Champions League when they take on a Crystal Palace side who are left playing for pride over the final three weeks of the season. FULL TIME! Man City seal QPR's relegation to the Championship with a commanding 6-0 win, with Aguero contributing three goals to the Citizens' cause. Other goals from Kolarov, Silva and Milner wrapped up the three points for Pellegrini's men, as Ramsey's side bow out with a whimper. That's all that we have time for from the Etihad, I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again next time.
(90’) Bony stumbles through a couple of challenges, but can't get the space to shoot, with Man City continuing to try and rack up more goals. There are two minutes of stoppage time and we're into the first. Caulker receives some treatment after going down holding his hamstring.
(89’) Bony is nearly fed into the penalty area by Aguero, but a timely interception from Dunne denies the substitute. Man City are holding onto the ball in the dying stages, with QPR looking to be utterly out of motivation and ideas.
--- 87’ Assist W. Bony provided the assist. ---
--- 87’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOOAL! SILVA MAKES IT SIX! The Spaniard is found by a brilliant backheel by Bony, before the former Valencia midfielder dances around Green and slots a composed finish into the back of the net! Coolness personified from the diminutive Spain international. ---
--- 86’ Substitution Suk-Young Yoon is done for the day. S. Wright-Phillips is his replacement. ---
(86’) Wright-Phillips is introduced for the final five minutes, with the former Man City crowd giving the Englishman a brilliant reception! The substitute gets involved immediately, firing a near-post towards goal that Hart has to save.
(84’) The QPR players will be asking for the final whistle sooner rather than later. Kranjcar attempts to whip a cross in from the left-hand side, but the Croatian's delivery is absolutely terrible. On the basis of this performance, the visitors deserve their relegation.
--- 82’ Substitution Jesús Navas enters play, replacing J. Milner. ---
(82’) Close for Bony! The former Swansea striker lashes an effort towards the near post, but the ball cannons off the upright and away from Milner's control! That proves to be the Englishman's last contribution, with Navas coming into the fray.
(80’) Just wide from Toure! The substitute breaks beyond the midfield line, before lumbering into the box, but the Ivory Coast international can only stroke an effort with the outside of his boot beyond the near post! QPR are managing to keep hold of the ball at the moment, but aren't doing anything constructive with it.
--- 78’ Substitution N. Kranjčar comes on for L. Fer. ---
(78’) QPR try to push down the left-hand side, but an offside flag denies them once again. They have been caught out a criminal amount of times. Fer is then withdrawn for the visitors, with Ramsey throwing Kranjcar into the fray for the remaining minutes.
(76’) Fernandinho is withdrawn for the home side, with Yaya Toure making his way onto the field in his place. Fer musters up a shot from range, but the Netherlands international drags his effort well wide of the left-hand post. That would have had to have been a special volley to arrow into the back of the net from there. Toure then shoots from 25 yards out, but fires straight at Green.
--- 75’ Substitution Fernandinho is replaced with Y. Touré. ---
(74’) QPR win themselves a free kick out on the left-hand side, which Barton will deliver. The former Man City man angles in a teasing cross, but it is headed away with ease. Ramsey's side just can't create anything at all. Hart has had an easy time of it this side of the interval.
(72’) QPR throw a cross into the box from the right-hand side, but it is easily cleared, with the away side having absolutely no luck in this contest. They have been hapless in all areas, with Aguero and Silva running absolutely riot.
--- 70’ Assist The assist came from S. Agüero. ---
--- 70’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! The aforementioned corner is flicked on well at the near post by Bony, before Aguero cuts back an unselfish pass! Milner is on hand to place the simplest of finishes into an unguarded net, with QPR bowing out of the Premier League in some style. ---
(69’) Good save from Green! Bony is allowed to steam towards the near post after a neat pass from Silva, but the Ivory Coast international sees his effort denied by the foot of the goalkeeper! Man City earn themselves a corner.
(67’) Almost four goals for Aguero! The Argentine goalscorer is caught narrowly offside, before seeing a powerful effort pushed away by Green. Man City are relentless, pushing forward continuously despite already holding a commanding lead.
--- 65’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! AGUERO SEALS HIS HAT-TRICK FROM THE SPOT! The Argentina international slots the ball to the left-hand side of the goalkeeper, with Man City racking up quite the scoreline at the Etihad. ---
(64’) PENALTY TO MAN CITY! A cross is whipped into the back post, with Phillips ploughing into the back of the awaiting Silva! Clumsy stuff from the former Blackpool man.
(64’) Good save from Green! Barton gives away a free kick on the edge of the penalty area, before the Serbian left-back curls another brilliant strike over the wall! The QPR goalkeeper leaps to his left to make a strong stop. Bony is then injected into the game at the expense of Lampard.
--- 63’ Substitution W. Bony comes on for F. Lampard. ---
--- 62’ Yellow card J. Barton goes into the referee's book. ---
(62’) Silva manages to wriggle free of pressure from Dunne, before scampering into the penalty area and placing a finish goalwards! Green makes a timely save, with the Englishman preventing this scoreline from getting embarrassing.
(60’) There is only half an hour left for QPR to orchestrate a comeback, with the visitors heading down to the second tier as it stands. Austin hasn't been able to create any opportunities thus far in the second half.
(58’) Dunne tries to send Hoilett down the right-hand side, but the former Man City defender's pass is cut out. Moments later, the former Blackburn winger unleashes a powerful effort from range, but Hart paws the shot away from danger.
(56’) Over from Lampard! The former Chelsea midfielder is picked out around six yards out from goal, but can only guide Zabaleta's cross high and wide of the target! He really should have done better there, it could so easily have been 4-0.
(54’) Austin goes down heavily after clashing with Kolarov, with the Englishman landing rather awkwardly on his shoulder. QPR win a free kick as a result, but Fer and Dunne collide, meaning that neither player can get a header on target.
--- 53’ Substitution B. Zamora is replaced with J. Hoilett. ---
(52’) Hoilett is readied for the away side, with Ramsey's men needing an absolute miracle here. Barton attempts to swing a cross in from the right, but it is easily dealt with, as Hart continues to have a rather easy day in between the posts.
--- 50’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! AGUERO MAKES IT 3-0! Phillips breaks down the flank to the right byline, before cutting a cross into the direction of Austin, but Zabaleta comes across well to head clear. Silva scampers away, before slotting a through ball beyond Suk-Young, which the South Korean should really clear. The Argentine slides a composed finish beyond Green after racing into the clear. ---
(48’) Aguero is nearly fed in behind the QPR back three, but Henry tracks back brilliantly to match the run of the Argentine and defuse the danger. Despite needing three goals, Ramsey has stuck to his guns and kept the same 11.
(46’) We are underway in the second half at the Etihad! QPR need to step up a gear and find three goals from somewhere, with Austin going close a few times in the first half without luck. This could be any scoreline, with Aguero and Silva looking in good form.
HALF TIME! A nightmare half for QPR has left the away side will it all to do in the second period of play! Man City are 2-0 ahead, meaning that the visitors have to score at least three goals if they are to have any chance of staying in the Premier League.
(45’) There is one minute of stoppage time.
(44’) Offside once again for Austin! Phillips breaks down the right-hand side, before curling in a near-post cross, which the Englishman strokes beyond the closest upright! The linesman's flag is already raised, however, with the visiting striker making his run far too early. Man City go down the other end, with Silva dancing past two players and lashing a ferocious effort into the stands.
(42’) Zamora is having no luck up top, with the former England international's touch failing him on many occasions. Balls into the box from deep areas by Barton have been QPR's only real moments of inspiration.
(40’) Milner drives down the right-hand side, before cutting back a cross, but it is angled terribly. Barton cuts it out, before QPR try to break themselves, but the visitors' attack peters out to nothing. Not long remains in the first half for Ramsey's men to try and stage the start of a comeback.
(38’) Man City are keeping the ball well, with QPR unable to break with any kind of regularity. Zamora attempts to turn in behind Demichelis, but the Argentine unceremoniously dumps his fellow veteran on the turf. The resulting free kick is turned onto the bar by a looping Fer strike, before Zamora's rebounding header is caught by Hart.
(36’) Less than 10 minutes remain in the first half, with QPR now needing three goals to keep their hopes of staying in the Premier League alive. A comeback isn't looking likely for the visitors, with Man City appearing to be in the process of hammering the final nail in their coffin. Aguero manages to race in behind enemy lines, before outpacing Dunne, but Green gets down well to make a one-on-one save.
(34’) Man City immediately break down the right-hand side, with Milner angling in a cross that is narrowly missed by Aguero. As a result, QPR break themselves, with Phillips picking out Zamora at the far upright, but the former Fulham striker lashes a volley high and wide of the target!
--- 32’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! KOLAROV MAKES IT 2-0! After Dunne concedes a free kick for a push on Aguero, the Serbian left-back steps up well to curl a strike over the wall and into the back of the net! Green just can't get down quickly enough to deny the Man City goalscorer! The wall could well be to blame, there. ---
(30’) Kolarov whips a cross in from the right-hand side, before a looping clearance from Dunne isn't claimed by Green! The former England international spills it under pressure from Milner, with the former Leeds midfielder being penalised for a supposed push.
(28’) Austin and Zamora exchange possession on the edge of the box, but neither striker has enough space to try and work a shot at goal. QPR haven't been able to test Hart, unless Austin has been caught offside in the build up. Pellegrini will want his side to grab another goal sooner rather than later, however.
(26’) Close for Mangala! Milner whips in a cross from the right-hand side, after a wonderful ball in behind from Silva once again. The former Villa midfielder lays a pass to the back post, but the former Porto defender can't apply a finishing touch from close range! It should be 2-0!
(24’) Side netting from Fernandinho! Lovely interplay from Man City! The Brazilian and Silva combine brilliantly, before a one-touch pass from Lampard is slightly too heavy! It gives the former Shakhtar midfielder an awful angle to try his luck from.
(22’) Austin is nearly fed in behind enemy lines, with Hart needing to be light on his feet to get in ahead of the former Swindon striker and clear the danger. Man City have had the majority of the ball, but QPR's top scorer has started to look dangerous in flashes.
(20’) OFFSIDE! Austin is picked out by a cross from the left-hand side, before diverting a neat header inside the near post, but the linesman's flag is raised! It was a wonderful attempt, Hart didn't get anywhere near it.
(18’) Barton whips a free-kick delivery in from the right-hand side, but Fernando does enough at the back post to pressure Dunne. The former Aston Villa defender can only knee a terrible effort a considerable way over the crossbar with the aid of a deflection. The second corner isn't immediately cleared, before Austin fouls Kolarov. The Englishman went on to strike the bar, but it wouldn't have counted anyway.
(16’) Another half chance for Aguero! The Argentina international scampers into the clear after being found in behind by Fernandinho, but Green races off his line to smother. Moments later, a cross is whipped into the back post, but Milner sees a looping square ball headed clear by Barton! Lampard was close to nodding, before Milner lashed the rebound high and wide.
(14’) Hill covers across the penalty area to deny a diagonal run from Aguero, with the QPR man sliding in to frustrate the goalscorer. The hosts take the resulting corner, but Milner's cross is headed away by Dunne. The away side are struggling to create anything.
(12’) Dunne tries to poke a pass back to Green, but Aguero is onto it in a flash! Fortunately for the former Man City defender, his goalkeeper is alert to the danger and slides in to defuse the situation. Moments later, Zabaleta breaks down the right-hand side, but Green sees a cross-cum-shot loop clear of danger.
(10’) The hosts have had it all very easy in the opening minutes, with QPR not managing to have any kind of meaningful possession. Silva drives down the left-hand side, before feeding the overlapping Kolarov, but the Serbia international's eventual cross is blocked by Barton.
(8’) Fer tries to bundle his way through the heart of the Man City midfield, but picks up a free kick after he is pushed to the ground. Zamora asks for the set piece to be placed onto his head, but the delivery instead rolls through to Hart.
(6’) Man City continue to stream forward, with QPR having the nightmare start. Anything less than a win will confirm the club's demotion to the Championship, but they've fallen behind already. It must be said, their back three certainly isn't adequately mobile to deal with Aguero.
--- 4’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! AGUERO GIVES THE HOSTS THE LEAD! The Argentina international scampers into the box, beyond several lumbering bodies, before lifting a finish over the onrushing Green! Far, far too easy from the former Atletico man. ---
(3’) Chance for Aguero! Silva and the Argentine forward combine well on the break, but the latter sees a shot just inside the penalty area well blocked by Dunne! Man City look bright from the off.
