FULL TIME - Chelsea 1-1 Liverpool: Terry gave the champions an early lead, but Gerrard equalised moments before the break. It was a hotly contested game, but the Reds lacked the ability to add to their tally and get the win that they needed in order to keep their Champions League ambitions alive.
(90’) There is the final whistle!
(90’) Sterling gets past Cuadrado and stands a cross up at the back post from the byline. It drops to Can, who fires an ambitious attempt straight into the side netting. That could be Liverpool's final chance!
(90’) Ibe dribbles into the box from the right, beating both Filipe Luis and Willian. However, he runs into a Terry-shaped wall and concedes a free kick moments later in his attempts to regain possession for the visitors.
(90’) We are into the first of four additional minutes!
(90’) JUST WIDE! Lucas clips a ball into the box that is headed away by Cahill, but only as far as Henderson. He controls the ball on his chest before releasing a volley that arrows just outside of the upright. It may well have taken a touch off Terry, but it wasn't spotted.
(89’) COUTINHO! The Brazilian pulls the trigger from 25 yards and his effort takes a wicked deflection off Cahill. Courtois is already diving the other way, but the centre-back's touch takes enough pace off the ball for him to be able to recover and smother the shot.
(88’) Time is running out for Liverpool now. Failure to win here could spell the end of their Champions League hopes!
(86’) Sinclair receives the ball from Coutinho 20 yards from goal and tries to force his way into the box. The ball ricochets between Cahill and himself but Courtois races out to ensure that he is the first man to the loose ball.
--- 84’ Substitution L. Rémy is done for the day. J. Cuadrado is his replacement. ---
(84’) Mourinho makes his final change of the afternoon, replacing Remy with Cuadrado.
(83’) The resultant free kick is whipped in by Henderson, but he sends it in far too deep and the ball bounces behind for a goal kick.
--- 82’ Yellow card Filipe Luis is yellow-carded. ---
(82’) Filipe Luis is shown a yellow card for hauling back Ibe to stop Liverpool from counterattacking after he was caught in possession by the Reds man.
(81’) Sterling uses his pace to run around the outside of Ivanovic towards the byline on the left before firing in a cutback. It hits both the right-back and Cahill, deflecting the ball towards goal and forcing Courtois to get down and keep it out!
--- 79’ Substitution Lucas Leiva comes on for S. Gerrard. ---
(79’) Rodgers makes his final substitution, replacing Gerrard with Lucas Leiva.
(78’) Ivanovic finds Hazard in the centre of the Liverpool half with a brilliant pass, and the Belgian instantly turns and bears down on goal. He tries to dribble his way to the penalty spot but is thwarted at the last moment by a tackle from Lovren.
(76’) Filipe Luis robs Can of the ball near the corner flag and drives into the box. His cutback is intercepted but Chelsea keep the move alive, with Fabregas receiving the ball at the top of the box before bulldozing his way into the area. His shot is deflected behind for a corner, though.
(74’) Fabregas carries the ball forward from the right, spring diagonally towards the box. Space continues to open up for him so he enters the area and chops onto his left foot to create room for a shot. He doesn't catch it well enough, though, and Mignolet makes a routine stop.
(72’) Another change from Rodgers now, with Jordon Ibe replacing Lallana.
--- 71’ Substitution J. Ibe enters play, replacing A. Lallana. ---
(71’) Hazard and Fabregas combine well down the left, but when the former gets to the byline and cuts a cross back into the box there is no one there! Remy was just lingering on the edge of the area, showing no intent of getting on the end of it.
(69’) Liverpool's positivity has been curbed in the past few minutes, with Chelsea making a few more forays forward. That final ball just doesn't seem to be there, though, as the Reds' defence remains resilient.
--- 68’ Substitution J. Sinclair enters play, replacing R. Lambert. ---
(67’) Rodgers makes his first change of the afternoon, with 18-year-old striker Jerome Sinclair replacing Lambert.
(65’) Sterling again gets away from Filipe Luis relatively easily, and upon reaching the top of the box he attemps to roll a shot beyond Courtois. Cahill slides in and makes enough contact to take the pace off the ball so his keeper can claim it with even greater ease.
(63’) Liverpool have certainly enjoyed the greater share of possession in the second half. Chelsea are still threatening on the break, though their latest attempt breaks down as Hazard's attempt to feed Remy on the left rolls out of play before the Frenchman can bring it under control.
(61’) Skrtel stays up following a corner and Lallana's cross from the right runs all the way through to him. He goes for a rather acrobatic effort by his standards and fails to keep it down, instead blazing the ball over the top!
--- 60’ Substitution N. Matić comes on for R. Loftus-Cheek. ---
(60’) Sterling is not closed down as he bears down on the box and he uses the space to feed Lallana inside the box. He takes a touch and shoots, with his effort looping behind off a blue shirt! Matic comes on in place of Loftus-Cheek for the remainder.
--- 58’ Yellow card J. Obi Mikel receives a yellow card. ---
(58’) Another yellow card is brandished by the referee, and this one is directed at Mikel, who blocked off Sterling as he attempted to dribbled down the right wing.
(57’) Almost the same again for Chelsea, though this time it is Remy who dribbles across the top of the box before teeing up Willian. The Brazilian's shot is deflected behind off Skrtel and Liverpool managed to clear the delivery capably.
(55’) GREAT EFFORT! Chelsea break at pace, with Hazard dribbling inside off the left. He passes across to Willian who stands up Johnson before quickly shifting the ball onto his right and shooting in one swift movement. The hand of Mignolet keeps it out of the far corner, but it was hit with so much power that the officials miss the keeper's touch and award a goal kick.
(53’) STAT: Mourinho has lost just one of his 96 Premier League games as Chelsea boss at Stamford Bridge, winning 75 and drawing 20.
(51’) Liverpool continue to play positively in this second half, but both Lallana and Can flight crosses into the box that fail to find a team-mate. Rodgers will be pleased with his side's performance this side of the interval, though.
(49’) SO CLOSE! Sterling runs across the top of the box and spins away from Filipe Luis after reaching the left side. He cuts a pass back to Coutinho who fires a first-time shot that ripples the outside of the side netting! It fools a few people into thinking it went in!
(47’) Henderson plays a one-two with Lambert midway inside the Chelsea half before laying the ball off to Lallana in the box. The former Southampton man shoots on the spin but sends his attempt far wide of the upright on the opposite side of the goal.
(46’) We are back underway!

HALF TIME - Chelsea 1-1 Liverpool: It's all-square at the interval in a game that is showing no signs of an end-of-season wind down. --- 68’ Substitution R. De Laet enters play, replacing M. Wasilewski. ---
(67’) First change of the match from Leicester now and it will see Wasilewski come off to be replaced by Ritchie De Laet. No reason to risk any players going forward for Nigel Pearson here - they still have some vital games to play this season!
(66’) The Leicester fans are actually starting to 'Ole' with every single pass at the moment and we are only just past the hour mark! Still 25 minutes to go here but the home crowd already basically know they are going home with three points in the bag!
--- 64’ Substitution E. Rivière is done for the day. V. Anita is his replacement. ---
(64’) Another change from Newcastle now and it will see Riviere, who has been pretty awful out there, replaced by Anita. Unclear as to who will plug the gap at the back, but the visitors are really up against it now. They desperately need to avoid a hiding here.
(63’) WILLIAMSON IS SENT OFF FOR NEWCASTLE! The defender, whilst on a booking, goes straight through the back of Vardy near the touchline, sending the Leicester striker straight into a camera at the side of the park! Nasty challenge and a deserved second yellow and subsequent red! What was Williamson thinking?!
--- 62’ Red card! M. Williamson gets a second yellow card and is sent off! ---
(61’) Riviere attempts to open up play with a pacey run down the right-hand side but before he can get a cross into the box he is dispossessed by the retreating Schlupp, who was with him all the way back. Terrific workrate from the winger, and from Leicester as a whole.
(59’) Fantastic save from Krul! A lovely cross is teased into the box and Ulloa typically gets ahead of his Newcastle marker before bulleting a header towards goal, but the goalkeeper manages to get across goal to tip over the bar! That looked a certain goal!
--- 58’ Substitution S. de Jong enters the game and replaces R. Taylor. ---
(58’) First change of the match from John Carver and it will see Siem de Jong come on to replace the ineffectual Taylor. The Dutchman has been hounded by health and injury problems this season, but will be tasked with providing a little more up top for the visitors here.
(56’) Newcastle are all over the place at the back here! Vardy gets beyond Krul but has to cut back as he is right next to the byline. Albrighton ends up receiving the ball and drives towards goal before smashing a cross across, but Coloccini is there to turn behind for yet another corner.
--- 55’ Yellow card M. Williamson goes into the referee's book. ---
(54’) Mahrez collects possession in midfield and glides forward before cleverly clipping the ball through the legs of Williamson, who ends up going right through the Algerian international, committing the foul in the process. Booking there for the Newcastle defender.
(52’) Poor miss from Albrighton! Cambiasso receives the all on the edge of the box and slides a perfect pass into the channel for Schlupp, who reverses a teasing cross into the box. The former Aston Villa winger meets it but attempts to drill it with pace into the corner, only to flash his attempt wide! Newcastle let off the hook!
(50’) You really do have to feel for the Newcastle fans. Each and every time they go to a match they must be thinking it will be the time they will stop the rot, but once again they have been let down by abject performances from the players. Still plenty of time in the match, but would you expect a miracle comeback from the Magpies? Probably not.
--- 48’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLLLL FOR LEICESTER! Ulloa steps up and confidently dispatches his penalty by whipping it into the top left corner! The Foxes love scoring at the start of halves! Three-nil! ---
(47’) PENALTY KICK TO LEICESTER! Wasilewski attempts to get on the end of a corner to the front pushed but is rashly shoved shoved to the floor by Riviere! Such a daft challenge!
(46’) We are back under way at the King Power Stadium! Can Newcastle salvage anything from this or with Leicester power ahead for more goals?
Half time at the King Power Stadium. A lightning-quick start from the home side sees Leicester head into the break with a comfortable 2-0 lead over lowly Newcastle. Leonardo Ulloa opened the scoring in the first minute with a glanced header and Wes Morgan doubled the lead in the 17th minute with a close range finish past Krul. Perez has looked bright for Newcastle, but the Magpies have a mountain to climb now!
(45’) Two minutes of added time signalled by the referee and Newcastle are actually enjoying a nice little period of possession before the break. Doubt they'll have enough time to muster up an opportunity though.
(43’) Considering James is on a yellow card, he is arguably lucky to still be on the pitch as he commits a hand ball offence inside the Newcastle box in an attempt to control the ball. Unclear or not as to whether he meant it, so probably the correct decision from the ref to let him off with it.
(41’) Newcastle have actually been half-decent going forward through Perez, but losing a goal in the first minute has just completely damaged their confidence for the remainder of the half. They'll be wanting to hear the half time whistle now so they can hope to regroup.
(39’) Newcastle fail to clear a corner kick with any kind of authority and James collects the loose ball before moving forward and fizzing a cross-come-shot into the box. Cambiasso strives to get a head on the end of it but the visitors end up getting the goal kick as it flies by the post at pace.
(37’) SAVE FROM SCHMEICHEL! Taylor strides forward through the middle and decides to try his luck with a crack at goal from 25 yards. It is a lovely strike from the former Wigan man and it moves all over the place, but the Leicester keeper gets his body behind the ball to make the solid save. Much better from Newcastle!
(35’) Perez attempts to jink his way into the penalty area but is dispossessed by a strong Huth challenge. Gutierrez collects possession 30 yards out and hits a strike at goal first time, which takes a deflection on the way through before sizzling behind for another corner. Ryan Taylor is usually decent in his set-piece delivery, but it has been disappointing so far.
(33’) Riviere collects a neat pass from Perez inside the box and looks poised to get a shot away, but ends up bizarrely falling over before he can pull the trigger! If there ever was an incident to sum up Newcastle's current performance and form - it is that.
(31’) Albrighton bursts down the right flank, holding off the challenge of Gutierrez in the process. The former Aston Villa winger then cuts back inside on his left foot to whip a cross into the danger area, but Newcastle defend much better this time and clear through a Coloccini header.
--- 29’ Yellow card M. James is yellow-carded. ---
(29’) James, in turn, also receives a yellow card and there is perhaps an element of revenge involved as the tackle goes in on Gutierrez. The Leicester midfielder gets the yellow and Newcastle can attempt to get a decent delivery into the box with a free kick down the right.
--- 28’ Yellow card J. Gutiérrez receives a yellow card. ---
(27’) Gutierrez is the latest player to go into the book and it is force a rash challenge on Cambiasso inside the home side's half. Needless from the Argentine and the referee makes no mistake in brandishing the yellow card.
(25’) Leicester's pressing has been tremendous so far, with Vardy in particular leading the charge with intense pressure on the Newcastle defenders, who are in turn forced to pump aimless balls up to the commanding Leicester backline, who are easily gobbling them up.
(23’) Unlucky from Perez! The former Tenerife striker takes the ball down with an assured touch on the edge of the area and spins round before rifling a strike towards the left corner. In the end the attempt slams into the side-netting but Schmeichel certainly wasn't sure it was going wide!
(21’) Janmaat strides forward down the right-hand side and clips a speculative pass into the channel for Perez, but the Newcastle striker is ushered out of the way by Morgan as the ball runs harmlessly through to Schmeichel. Just no creativity coming from the visitors in their passing!
(19’) Newcastle are sinking without a trace here and they've got more defending to do once again as Albrighton whips in another dangerous corner kick. On this occasion Williamson manages to clear at the back post, but Leicester recycle possession near the touchline to keep the pressure up.
--- 17’ Assist M. Albrighton provided the assist. ---
--- 17’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAALLLLL FOR LEICESTER! THE HOSTS DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! Albrighton curls a teasing free kick into the box and Morgan meets it with a scrappy touch which takes the ball beyond Krul! Awful defending from Newcastle once again! Two-nil! Perfect start for the Foxes! ---
--- 16’ Yellow card D. Janmaat is cautioned by the referee. ---
(16’) Newcastle had that little spell when they were looking decent going forward, particularly through Perez, but they never truly threatened Schmeichel in between the sticks, which will certainly be a frustration for John Carver.
(14’) Albrighton does brilliantly to swing a pass in behind the Newcastle defence for Vardy, with the defenders looking for the offside against the striker. The Englishman was actually inside his own half though and takes advantage to dart forward and attempt to take on Dummett, but the left-back does well to put out for a throw-in.
(12’) Perez takes the ball down with a wonderful touch inside the box and turns swiftly before driving towards the byline. He attempts to find a team-mate with a square pass but the ball ends up bouncing off him to go disappointingly behind for a goal kick. The young Spaniard has looked bright for the visitors so far!
(10’) Dodgy moment at the back for Newcastle as Krul comes off his line to meet a pass to Vardy outside the box. The Dutchman actually does pretty well to head away whilst Williamson stands there watching, and ends up taking a sore one from the Leicester striker. Good goalkeeping in the end but what was his defence doing?
(8’) Some decent build-up play on the edge of the box from Newcastle here involving Riviere and Perez. The ball ends up with Gutierrez 25 yards out who attempts an extremely difficult volley towards goal whilst being completely off-balanced. Perhaps unsurprisingly it flies over the bar, not troubling the keeper.
(6’) Perez manages to get in behind the Leicester defence and finds a yard of space to lash a right-footed shot towards goal. It is a tight angle for the Spaniard though and his attempt ends up flashing harmlessly by the left-hand post. A little more promising for the Magpies now.
(4’) Sissoko turns sharply to get beyond Schlupp near the touchline and drives forward with authority, but his eventual cross into the box is easily pounced upon Schmeichel, who darts off his line to claim possession.
(2’) What an electric start this has been for Leicester! Intense pressing from the very first kick of the ball and it has paid off! The King Power is absolutely BOUNCING at the moment! Can Newcastle sort themselves out before any further early damage is caused?!
--- 1’ Assist Assist by M. Albrighton. ---
--- 1’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAALLL!!! GOOOAALLLLL!!! GOOOAAAALLLL FOR LEICESTER!! Some high pressing from the get-go allows the home side to earn a corner kick. It is swung to the front post and Ulloa gets ahead of his marker to glance a superb header into the corner! One-nil! What a start! ---
(1’) We are under way at the King Power Stadium! A vital three points up for grabs here!
The teams have made their way to the pitch and we are almost ready for kick off!
Leicester and Newcastle have already faced each other twice this season, with each recording a 1-0 home win. The Magpies won the corresponding league clash in October, but Pearson's men got their revenge with a narrow win in the FA Cup in January.
Three changes for Leicester from the 3-1 loss against Chelsea. Konchesky, King, and Drinkwater are all withdrawn, with James, Mahrez, and Schlupp coming into the starting XI. Newcastle make two alterations from the loss against Swansea, with Anita and Cabella replaced by Dummett and Sissoko.
Newcastle (4-4-2): Krul; Janmaat, Coloccini, Williamson, Dummett; Gutierrez, R.Taylor, Colback, Sissoko; Riviere, Perez.
Leicester (3-5-2): Schmeichel; Wasilewski, Huth, Morgan; Albrighton, Cambiasso, James, Mahrez, Schlupp; Ulloa, Vardy.
TEAM NEWS...
The other manager in the dugout today, Pearson, gained some unwanted media attention this week after a bizarre post-match press conference against the defeat to Chelsea, in which he compared a probing journalist to an ostrich – also labelling them “daft” and “stupid”. The Leicester boss has since apologised for the comments, and will be eager to put he incident behind him and concentrate on the win today.
The level of performances from the Newcastle players recently has actually resulted in some fan boycotts and a high level of criticism aimed at Carver, but a win or two should be enough to secure their Premier League status for the next campaign.
Conversely, Newcastle are in a horrendous run of form and have lost their last seven matches including last week's 3-2 loss against Swansea at St. James' Park. Indeed, if the league started after John Carver took charge of his home town club, the Magpies would be rock bottom in 20th place. The visitors today are four points ahead of their opponents but this is mainly due to some decent form in the first half of the season. They'll need to stop the rot soon or risk being embroiled in the relegation battle.
With Chelsea having nearly sewn up the title and the top four starting to take shape, much of the remaining focus of the Barclays Premier League season will be on the battle against the drop. For much of the campaign, Nigel Pearson's men looked destined to be playing Championship football next year, but a fantastic run of four consecutive wins before the midweek loss to Chelsea has catapulted Leicester out of the relegation zone into 17th – one point ahead of Sunderland.
I'm Martin Macdonald, and I'll be taking you through the action!
Good afternoon folks! Welcome to LIVE coverage of the first Barclays Premier League clash of the weekend featuring Leicester taking on Newcastle from the King Power Stadium!

That's all I've got time for this afternoon. I'm still trying to catch my breath after such a thrilling 90 minutes. Enjoy the rest of your weekend and thanks so much for joining. I've been Chris Baker and I'll see you again next time!
Villa climb up to 14th in the table with this win and if they keep playing the way they are then I'd expect them to pick up quite a few more points between now and the end of the season. As for Everton they are very much marooned in midtable on 44 points in 11th place.
This was at times a pulsating encounter with play going from end-to-end but you always felt that Villa had an element of control and could've scored more if they had needed to. Tim Sherwood will be unhappy at the relatively soft nature of both of Everton's goals and the fact that they both came from set pieces.
Everton really paid the price for a dismal first half display which ultimately gave them far too much to do. Roberto Martinez will take some positives from the second half performance but in truth the final score of 3-2 massively flatters the Toffees. They were second best for much of this contest and Aston Villa fully deserve their victory. If Lukaku and co. had some as much intent in the early stages as they did towards the end of this match then it could have been a different story.
Three precious points which all but confirm that Aston Villa will be playing Premier League football once again next season. The decision to sack Paul Lambert and replace him with Tim Sherwood has been completely vindicated. This side look unrecognisable from the tame, limp outfit that we saw a few months ago. The Villa fans can now begin to relax and look forward to their date with Arsenal at Wembley.
(90’) And there is the final whistle! Full time here at Villa Park. Aston Villa 3-2 Everton.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card S. Given receives a yellow card. ---
--- 90’ +2 Goal! P. Jagielka has scored a goal for Everton! ---
(90’) GOAL FOR EVERTON! 3-2 JAGIELKA PULLS ONE BACK!
--- 90’ Substitution C. N'Zogbia is done for the day. J. Cole is his replacement. ---
(90’) Former Liverpool midfielder Joe Cole will come on for what remains of this  match in place of Charles N'Zogbia, who has been a real handful this afternoon. Picking a man of the match is going to be a tricky task but suffice to say it will be someone in a claret and blue shirt.
(88’) Barkley tries to play in Lukaku after being found by Lennon's clever back heel but the through ball is way overhit and Given is able to collect. More frustration for Everton. The chances of a grandstand finish look to be ebbing away.
(86’) Grealish, who has been a joy to watch today, is fouled by McCarthy. This young man looks to have a great future ahead of him if he can play like this on a consistent basis. He shows great awareness on the ball. Maturity beyond his years.
--- 84’ Yellow card R. Vlaar is yellow-carded. ---
(84’) McCarthy beats Vlaar all ends up and the Dutch defender simply takes out the Irish midfielder to stop him progressing into the penalty area and is correctly booked. Baines takes the free-kick short to Lennon who chips the ball to the back post but it is easily headed away by Okore. A wasted opportunity for Everton there.
(82’) Everton give the ball away not once but twice, which has been a theme of this afternoon, to hand the initiative back to Aston Villa. The home side are now quite content just to keep possession at the moment. Eventually Hutton tries to set up Benteke for his hat-trick but the cross is well cleared by Jagielka.
--- 81’ Substitution A. Hutton comes on for L. Bacuna. ---
(80’) As we head into the final ten minutes here at Villa Park it is now or never for Everton whole the home team will have their designs on going 4-1 up. Bacuna is rather surprisingly taken off, to a fantastic ovation, for Alan Hutton - a like for like swap.
(78’) SHOT! Osman does really well to wriggle past a couple of challenges but can only direct his effort straight at Given. The two substitutes have made a real impact for Martinez's men. They have injected some directness into Everton's midfield which had been rather pedestrian at times.
(77’) Benteke appears to make contact with Gareth Barry with a stray arm but there is nothing doing from the referee. It seemed accidental but the former Villa man didn't make anything of it and so the game continues at a frentic pace.
(76’) Barkley wastes no time in getting involved in the action as he crashes a shot towards goal which is well blocked. Lennon found himself with the ball in the area but couldn't create enough space to threaten the Villa goal himself.
--- 75’ Substitution L. Osman comes on for K. Mirallas. ---
--- 75’ Substitution R. Barkley enters the game and replaces S. Naismith. ---
--- 75’ Substitution C. Sánchez enters play, replacing A. Westwood. ---
(74’) As expected Osman and Barkley do come on. While Ashley Westwood is withdrawn and replaced by Carlos Sanchez, who scored his first Villa goal away at the Etihad stadium last time out.
--- 73’ Yellow card S. Coleman is cautioned by the referee. ---
(72’) Roberto Martinez has stuck with his starting eleven up until now but changes appear to be afoot with Leon Osman and Ross Barkley preparing to enter the fray. Coleman tugs back Grealish, who has tormented the Everton defence all day long and finally the referee brandishes a card from his pocket.
(70’) SAVE! Gareth Barry has a pop from fully twenty-five yards out but his well struck shot is right down the throat of Shay Given who holds onto it comfortably. Everton need a goal back and they need it soon if they are to have any hope of getting an unlikely draw.
(68’) Benteke is really calling the tune at the moment. He is winning every header. This time he knocks it down for Cleverley who does well to hold onto the ball before giving it to N'Zogbia who dances inside from the right wing and tees up Delph. The Villa midfielder lets fly but it is scuffed well wide.
(66’) Before Cleverley's goal all you could hear where the travelling Everton fans but now Villa Park is positively rocking. Aston Villa were wobbling a little after Lukaku's penalty and it is a tremendous reaction to get themselves another goal so quickly.
--- 64’ Assist L. Bacuna gave the assist. ---
--- 64’ Goal! T. Cleverley has scored a goal for Aston Villa! ---
(64’) Bacuna's through ball was the definition of a defence splitting pass. It completed dissected the Everton rearguard. Cleverley's run was excellent and his shot was emphatic. Sidefooting the ball high into Howard's net. No chance for the goalkeeper there.
(64’) 3-1 TO VILLA! Cleverley restores the two-goal cushion with a fantastic finish.
(62’) Lukaku looks like a different player since the half-time break. Whatever his manager said to him has down the trick. This time he is set away down the right channel by Coleman and does well to get a cross in but it is too close to Given who plucks the ball out of the air.
(60’) There are some (very) half-hearted appeals for another Everton penalty as Mirallas goes down in the area under the challenge of Vlaar. In fairness to the Belgian winger he wasn't asking for a penalty but the Villa fans wanted  a booking for simulation after he had been played in by Lennon.
--- 59’ Goal! GOAL! Lukaku rolls the ball into the bottom left corner after a stuttering run-up. Game on here at Villa Park. ---
(58’) Lukaku has really been taking the fight to Aston Villa. The Everton no.10 makes a rampaging run towards the Villa defence before the ball felt into the path of Naismith with his back to goal. Vlaar put in a very clumsy and unnecessary challenge and gave Clattenburg no option but to award the spot kick.
(58’) PENALTY TO EVERTON!
(56’) After a promising reaction from Everton at the start of the second half the game has returned to a similar pattern of the first; with Villa dictating the match. The visitors are struggling to string their passes together and are being penned back.
(54’) It's getting a little heated here as Delph is fouled once again, this time by McCarthy who then appears to leave his foot in which angers the Villa midfielder. Referee Mark Clattenburg manages to break things up and again shows leniency to all those involved.
(52’) Baines may well end up getting booked after an acculumation of fouls. The beginning of this half has been much more end-to-end and if it continues in this manner it is going to be a very open contest. Grealish wins his side a free-kick that Delph will take. The ball is swung in towards the back post but Everton do well to smuggle it clear.
(50’) N'Zogbia is playing in a way that Villa fans would have liked to have seen a lot more often since coming here. He has been bright and looked to combine with Benteke at every opportunity. This time he forces a corner in front of the Holte End but it comes to nothing and Everton clear their lines.
(48’) You imagine the usually cool Roberto Martinez may have had some harsh words for his player's during the half-time interval. Everton have certainly started this half with a sense of purpose, that was desperately lacking in the previous fourty-five minutes. Much better from the Toffees.
(47’) SAVE! Lukaku takes the fight to the heart of the Aston Villa defence. Everton broke after a Villa freekick and the Belgian striker finally forced Shay Given into action with a low shot that was tipped wide.
(46’) Everton get the second half going.
Another Aston Villa goal would settle this as a contest. Sherwood may look to protect Fabian Delph if possible, as he has been on the receiving end of a couple of robust tackles from Everton. The Toffees are lucky not to have one or two players in the book. Martinez has some decent options on the bench but he needs his the attitude and application of his starting eleven to change if his team are to turn this around.
Well things can only get better for Everton? Surely they can't get any worse. After looking reasonably comfortable to begin with they were totally rocked by Benteke's opener and have never truly recovered. The Villa hitman has totally overshadowed his international teammate Lukaku who has been out of sorts today. The visitors have been everything you wouldn't associate with Roberto Martinez's side.
Villa go into the break two goals to the good and it looks like a fairly unassailable lead at this point. Shay Given has been completely untroubled despite all the pre-match talk of him replacing Brad Guzan in goal. It really should be game over as Ron Vlaar put his header wide when he should've scored. If the home side continue in this manner then three points and Premier League survival are in the bag.
(45’) That's half time 2-0 to Villa.
(45’) A dreadful end to what has been a dreadful first fourty-five minutes for Everton. The defending there was absolutely woeful. How on earth the ball can go across the penalty area to Aston Villa's most dangerous player is simply beyond me.
--- 45’ Assist Assist by R. Vlaar. ---
--- 45’ Goal! Grealish's corner goes all the way through to Benteke at the back post who has the incredibly simple task of stabbing the ball into the roof of the net. incredibly, he was totally unmarked. ---
(44’) GOAL! BENTEKE MAKES IT TWO! IT'S SO EASY FOR VILLA!
(42’) Villa are just looking to see this through to half-time and should do so comfortably. Everton's first half performance has certainly not been in keeping with their recent results. Martinez must be mystified to say the least.
(40’) Given's long punt up the field finds it's way up to N'Zogbia who looks to take on Stones, who is the last man. His touch is a bit heavy but the Everton defender appeared to pull back the Villa winger. The home fans are baying for a free-kick and a yellow card but neither are forthcoming.
(38’) Bacuna looks to launch a one man counter attack and charges infield from the right back position. The Villa full back is then halted in his tracks by a crunching tackle from McCarthy. Everton then promptly give the ball away as Barry hits an aimless pass upfield. The Toffees have been so poor on the ball, so unlike them.
(36’) Slight delay in proceedings as Delph stays down after being caught late by Steven Naismith. The midfielder looks to be in a bit of trouble here and there are looks of concern on the Villa bench. The former Leeds player has been oustanding thus far and it would be a major blow to lose him. for the moment he looks ok to continue after some treatment.
(34’) Today's game is the 200th meeting between these famous two English sides. And on the basis of how it's gone they will be facing each other in Premier League football next season.
(32’) The visitors must have been anticipating a quick start for Aston Villa but they haven't reacted as Roberto Martinez would have liked. They haven't mustered a shot of any description so far. Coleman makes a surging run and tries to pick out Mirallas but the Belgian winger had gone to the near post while the ball went to the far. Sums up how its gone for Everton so far really.
(30’) Everton has been rather passive in their play since falling behind and are being dominated all over the pitch. They look like a side with not much to play for at this present time while Aston Villa have been such the opposite. Tim Sherwood must be delighted with his sides approach to this match so far. How they could do with the security of a second goal before half-time.
(28’) CHANCE! And it really should be 2-0! Ron Vlaar meets Westwood's inswinging corner and puts his free header wide of the post. A goal looked like an inevitably when the Dutch centre back got his head to that cross. Villa may come to regret missing such a big opportunity to increase their lead.
(26’) After a very fast start this contest has just calmed down a touch and the atmosphere inside the stadium has followed suit as it is rather subdued at the moment. Villa have looked purposeful in possession and the physical presence of Benteke gives them a constant outlet. It must also be said that Delph, Grealish, Westwood and Cleverley have been excellent so far. So energetic and busy in midfield.
(24’) Lennon has been fairly bright for Everton in these early stages but on this occasion he is a little too eager to get in behind from Coleman's pass and is caught offside. The Toffees have regained their composure after looking very nervy early on.
(22’) N'Zogbia bursts down the left wing and curls the ball into the box. Howard rather curiously elects to punch the ball away to safety rather than catch the cross. Perhaps the veteran American goalkeeper needed a shout from one of his defender's there? That Benteke goal has definitely unsettled the Everton back four.
(20’) As you would expect from a Roberto Martinez side the Toffees are sticking to their principles and are being patient on the ball. That said they haven't really clicked yet as an attacking unit. They have shown enough of a threat for Tim Sherwood's side to stay on their guard.
(18’) Everton are really struggling to keep hold of possession at the moment. The Villa midfielders are swarming their counterparts and giving them absolutely no time to settle. The renewed confidence in the home team is clear for all to see.
(16’) Baines is very fortunate not to be the first man to be cautioned this afternoon after he clattered his England teammate Delph in the middle of the park. The Villa fans are not be pleased with the referee there. That looked like a nailed on yellow card.
(14’) Delph is bodychecked by Barry and N'Zogbia will take the free-kick. The former Wigan and Newcastle winger fires a low shot on target which Tim Howard does well to parry away. Everton just need to weather the storm at the moment.
(12’) Aston Villa's first effort on target gives them the lead. Benteke has been in tremendous form recently and has given the hosts a dream start. Everton had looked pretty comfortably up until the goal.
--- 10’ Assist The assist came from F. Delph. ---
--- 10’ Goal! Delph with the assist. The England midfielder got half a yard on the left-hand side and wasted no time in getting the ball into the box. The cross takes a deflection but Benteke still manages to rise majestically inbetween Stones and Jagielka before burying his header into the bottom corner. Lift off for the home side! ---
(10’) GOAL! Benteke does it again. 1-0 to the Villa!
(8’) Richardson's whipped cross in is headed out of play by Jagielka for the games first corner. Westwood takes it and Benteke glances on the delivery but can't get enough purchase on the ball and it goes out for a goalkick. Had it gone in referee Mark Clattenburg may well have disallowed it as the Aston Villa striker was climbing all over John Stones.
(6’) No chances to speak of so far but Villa are certainly playing with a lot of intensity. They just need to calm down and relax a little bit more in possession. Kieran Richardson has seen plenty of the ball in defensive and attacking areas.
(4’) As you would Gareth Barry is being roundly booed by the Villa Park faithful everytime he touches the ball. The Toffees are starting to settle into their usual passing rhythm and are playing with their customary width. Coleman and Baines bombing forward with Lennon and Mirallas trying to use their pace to stretch the opposition.
(2’) Neither side have been able to get hold of the ball so far. Both teams trying to get going by hitting by long balls towards their respective big Belgian centre forwards Lukaku and Benteke respectively.
(1’) And we're underway! The home side get this massive match underway. Aston Villa are in their famous claret and blue home strip while Everton are in their away kit of white shirts, navy shorts and white socks.
The player's are out on the pitch and are going through the usual pre-match formalities. There is a great atmsphere building here inside a packed Villa Park.
On the positive side for Villa the form of lack of it from Sunderland and Newcastle United, who are absolutely sinking like a stone at the moment, should be a major source of encouragement for the Midlanders. That said this match is must-not-lose rather than must-win for the Lions. Aside from the confidence that has been injected by Tim Sherwood the most significant turnaround has been that fact that the previously goal shy Aston Villa are now finding the back of the net on a regular basis.
As for Everton they come into this match on the back of an outstanding result and performance against Manchester United last Sunday, running out comfortable 3-0 winners. It should therefore come as no surprise that Roberto Martinez names an unchanged side. The Toffees are finishing the season in excellent fashion which will be a source of frustration and optimism for Evertonians after an incosistent campaign.
Aston Villa may have an FA Cup final to look forward to at the end of the month but it is all about Premier League survival this afternoon. The remarkable upturn in form for Leicester City will have Tim Sherwood's team looking nervously over their shoulders. Good afternoon and welcome along to Villa Park for this potentially decisive match in the Premier League relegation battle. Aston Villa take on a resurgent Everton side. Three points today would surely see Tim Sherwood's side secure their status in the top division. I'm Chris Baker and I'll be describing all the action for you today.

And Rodgers may not have won over his skeptics, either, relying on a very late winner against a poor team down a man  while his side missed numerous chances and defended very poorly on QPR's goal. Three points are three points however and for today, that'll do. Thanks for joining us here!
QPR nearly nicked a point from the home side but came undone thanks to Gerard's header and, in all reality, it could've been much worse as Lallana and Sterling missed guilt-edged chances while the Liverpool captain missed his penalty as well. Their relegation fears were not allayed today.

(90’) Skrtel goes down in agony under a challenge from Austin and the striker is booked for that. It turns out to be the last meaningful action of a very eventful match- Liverpool win 2-1!
(90’) There are some signs of life from QPR, after Barton takes a free-kick and Sandro a follow-up shot that forces Mignolet into action twice in quick succession.

--- 87’ Assist The assist came from Philippe Coutinho. ---

(86’) Ibe continues to be a thorn in the side of the visitors' defence as he forces a corner from Phillips after a swift cut into the box from the flank. Rangers clear the initial effort but just end up conceding another when Dunne deflects Coutinho's shot.

(81’) QPR are piling the pressure on the home side, with Austin pulling wide to keep possession.
(79’) Penalty saved by R. Green!

--- 79’ Yellow card N. Onuoha is cautioned by the referee. ---

(77’) Liverpool's turn for a free-kick now which Henderson plays into the box, but it's cleared. Ibe tries to turn on the afterburners and send a cross back in but he overruns it and it's a goal-kick for Green.
--- 76’ Yellow card R. Dunne is yellow-carded. ---

(61’) This is better from QPR, who are maintaining some possession in the midfield though not really doing much with it.
(59’) Onuoha steps off his line to clear the ball but the Rangers just can't keep it off the home side now. They're desperately clearing cross after cross but crossing their own half is proving quite difficult.

(47’) Dunne plays a hard pass back to his keeper under pressure from Lambert that forces Green into an aawkward clearance, creating a corner. Eventually it gets to Lovren who takes an odd, whooping shot that nearly dips in under the crossbar.
--- 46’ Substitution Yun comes on for Caulker as QPR make the first change of the game just before the second half kicks off. Immediately Can plays a fantastic cross into the QPR box from deep in his flank that nearly finds Lambert's head! ---
QPR meanwhile aren't doing nearly enough up front. They've looked quite blunt and haven't been able to work wide possesssion centrally or get crosses to Austin. Join us in 15 for the second half!
As for Liverpool, they're doing well enough to snuff out QPR's attacks and race forward themselves, and could've had a second from a great Gerrard free-kick. Rodgers may want them to take more shots and work the ball centrally more, with many of their crosses being cut out.
(45’) And that's the half! QPR are down thanks to a very quality strike from Coutinho which separates the sides at the half.
(44’) Austin nearly gets on the end of a ball in the box but he's offside as he takes it down. QPR haven't gotten their leading goalscorer involved in this match at all.
--- 43’ Yellow card Sandro is yellow-carded. ---

(39’) Can slips past Sandro but not Barton as he twisted towards the middle of the pitch. Barton is furious, arguing he got the ball, but it's a free-kick well within shooting position for Liverpool, central and not far out of the box.

--- 18’ Yellow card The first booking of the game goes to Gerard, who clipped Fer from behind as QPR countered though the contact looked a little incidental to be fair to the home side's captain. ---
(17’) Lallana plays a sterling through pass right to... Sterling, which cuts out two defenders and lets the forward run towards the box but he shows a little too much of it to Caulker.

(5’) Lovren draws some applause as he slides in to keep the ball in play. The pitch is quite wet after some recent rain which might just promote slick, passing play from these two sides.

As the teams walk out of the tunnel and onto the pitch, the crowd at Anfield cheers loudly, holding up a sign for Gerrard as a banner flies over the stadium calling for the return of Rafa Benitez. In 5 meetings between these two sides since 2012, Liverpool have only lost once and won four times, but only two Premier League sides have worse records than the home side over the last five matches.
Plenty of players our injured for both of these sides today: Balotelli, Sturridge, Sakho, Flanagan, Zarate, Traore, Ferdinand, Vargas, and Faurlin amongst others.
Both sets of players will be wearing black armbands today in commemoration of Rio Ferdinand's wife, Rebecca, who passed away today after a short battle with breast cancer. She was just 34.
QPR (4-4-2): Green; Onuoha, Dunne, Caulker, Hill; Phillips, Barton, Sandro, Henry; Fer, Austin.
Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Mignolet; Ca, Skrtel, Lovren, Johnson; Gerrard, Henderson; Lallana, Coutinho, Sterling; Lambert.
The visitors are four points from safety but can take solace in the fact that Liverpool have not scored in their last two matches against teams in the bottom half. With Southampton and Tottenham creeping up the table very close to Liverpool, Brendan Rodgers may look to Philippe Coutinho to continue his goalscoring form against QPR: he's scored in both matches he's played against Chris Ramsey's men.
Despite QPR's abysmal away record this season they'll fight tooth and nail for those points as well. They've scored seven goals in their last two matches away from home and have taken four points - they'll want to keep up momentum as they look to push themselves out of the relegation zone!

FULL TIME - Sunderland 2-1 Southampton: The Black Cats secure a massive three points in their bid for Premier League survival, but they remain in 18th position. Jordi Gomez's two penalties proved enough for the win, despite a howler from Pantilimon which afforded Saints a first-half equaliser. The visitors' European ambitions take a blow, but Advocaat's men worked extremely hard for the win.
--- 90’ +5 Yellow card G. Pellè is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) There's the final whistle!
(90’) WHAT A SAVE FROM PANTILIMON! The Romanian keeper atones for his earlier error by parrying a shot from Alderweireld off to the side when the Belgian looked sure to score!
(90’) Sunderland manage to get the ball out of their own half and wind down the clock near the corner flag. They are just a few moments away from a huge three points.
(90’) We are into the first of four added minutes now. This is a big moment in Sunderland's season.

(87’) Sunderland are staying deep and just want to see the remainder of the game out. They are getting numbers forward on the break when they do eventually get in possession, though, so there could well be a goal still left in this match.
(86’) Clyne breaks forward on the right and has Pelle and Elia to aim for inside the box. However, he cuts the ball back to a red and white shirt on the edge of the area and the hosts look to break.
(84’) Saints continue to see plenty of the ball, but they've not been able to test Pantilimon in this half. Given the error he made for their goal earlier in the game, you would have thought they would have been raining shots down on his goal.

HALF TIME - Sunderland 1-1 Southampton: The hosts took the lead at an electric Stadium of Light when Jordi Gomez fired home from the penalty spot after Fonte had felled Graham. However, their advantage was wiped out within a minute as a howler from Pantilimon left Mane with a simple finish that he duly converted. Stay tuned for the second half!

(29’) STAT: Sunderland have only been victorious once in their last nine Premier League meetings with Southampton, drawing four and losing four.

As for Palace, the excellent four-game winning run that they embarked on in March and April was brought to a disappointing end by West Bromwich Albion two weeks ago, and last weekend saw them lose once again against struggling Hull City. With nine points separating themselves and 18th-place Sunderland, the Eagles are in no danger of dropping down to the Championship thanks to the great work Alan Pardew has done at the club since taking over in January, but he will be looking to give their loyal fans more to smile about over the coming weeks as they aim to end the season on a high.
Thanks to last weekend’s hard-fought 3-1 victory against in-form Leicester City, Chelsea head into today’s game with the opportunity to claim their first Premier League title in five years if they are able to see off their fellow Londoners. Whilst it is all but guaranteed that Jose Mourinho’s men will be crowned champions whatever happens this afternoon, they will no doubt be desperate to wrap up what has been a truly sensational campaign in front of a packed house in West London today. From start to finish, the Blues have looked brilliant in all areas of the pitch, and they are most certainly worthy winners of the league crown after treating us to so much delightful football this season.

However, in the end, their poor display in the opening 45 minutes meant that it was a relatively easy evening for the Gunners, who were able to hold on to pick up three well-deserved points.

The North London side will have been further boosted by Manchester United’s disappointing 1-0 defeat against West Bromwich Albion on Saturday, meaning that they now have the opportunity to move five points clear of the Red Devils if they are able to see off Hull this evening. With games in hand over both Manchester sides and with an overwhelming feeling of confidence and belief surrounding the club, Arsenal’s chances of finishing in second place for the first time in 10 years are firmly in their own hands, and they look more than up for the fight.
As for Arsenal, they are in need of points as well, but for completely different reasons. After embarking on a brilliant eight-game winning run from the start of February up until three weeks ago, Arsene Wenger’s men were finally held to a draw by Chelsea last weekend, meaning that they start the day three points behind second-place Manchester City, although with two games in hand over the reigning champions.
Steve Bruce’s side looked incredibly likely to fall into the relegation zone after picking up just two points from six league games before last weekend’s clash away to Crystal Palace, but they bounced back in fine fashion at Selhurst Park, beating the impressive South Londoners 2-0 before going on to record an even better 1-0 win at home to Liverpool on Tuesday evening, a result that would have seemed almost unthinkable just three weeks ago. However, the Tigers’ work is far from done, and they desperately need to avoid defeat tonight if they are to have any hope of keeping their place in the Premier League.
Chelsea may have finally clinched this season’s Premier League title with their 1-0 win at home to Crystal Palace yesterday, but it’s still all to play for at the bottom of the table, where eight teams are battling fiercely to avoid falling into the dreaded drop zone as we enter the final few weeks of the campaign. Hull head into tonight’s tough clash in a particularly precarious position, perched just one point clear of the relegation zone in 16th place, equal on points with in-form Leicester City and with two difficult games against Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester United to deal with before the end of the season.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
On paper, the two sides look rather evenly matched, with both managing to win two of their last five Premier League encounters, but Tottenham have recent history on their side, winning all of the last five meetings between the two teams. October’s game at White Hart Lane, which Spurs won 1-0 thanks to a first-half Christian Eriksen goal, was a tense affair, however, so expect the same this afternoon as the two sides fight tooth and nail.
Today’s game also marks Mauricio Pochettino’s first return to St. Mary’s since his departure from the club at the end of last season, and the Argentine’s presence in the opposition dugout is sure to make this clash a fiery contest.
A victory for either side today will lift them above the Reds, if only for a few hours, and also to within just a few points of Manchester City, who have looked less than convincing in recent weeks. Whilst there may not be quite enough time left for any of the aforementioned sides to catch the reigning champions, the race for fourth place is still on as we enter the final stretch of the season.
With both sides battling fiercely for a place in next season’s Europa League, this afternoon’s game could prove to be pivotal in the race for European qualification. Southampton head into today’s clash just one point behind Tottenham in seventh place, with fifth-place Liverpool, who are in the first of the two currently open qualifying spots, sitting equal on points with Spurs, albeit with a game in hand over the North Londoners and the Saints.

FULL TIME - Burnley 0-1 Leicester: The Foxes secure their fourth consecutive victory with Vardy's goal proving the difference against Burnley. Pearson's men move up to 17th position and out of the relegation zone, while Dyche's side remain rooted to the foot of the table.

--- 73’ Yellow card D. Ings goes into the referee's book. ---

Two teams fighting for their Premier League survival go head-to-head this afternoon, with Burnley hosting Leicester City at Turf Moor. Just two points separate the Clarets, who sit at the foot of the table, from the 18th-placed Foxes, who only sit in the relegation zone due to an inferior goal difference to that Hull City, who occupy 17th. It won’t be easy, however, as they still have to face Stoke, Arsenal, Manchester City and Crystal Palace before the end of the season, meaning that today’s game against an out-of-form opponent is a must-win, to say the least. The Swans have recent history on their side, too, with Newcastle only managing to avoid defeat in one of the last five meetings between the two sides. That result came last October when the Magpies came from behind twice to draw 2-2 thanks to a Papiss Cisse double. The Senegalese striker’s seven-game suspension has hit his side hard, as they have only managed to score two goals since his incident with Manchester United’s Jonny Evans.
In stark contrast to Newcastle, Swansea City are in inspired form and have surely been one of the most impressive teams this season. Despite a minor blip against Leicester last weekend, it has been an excellent campaign for Garry Monk’s men, and they head into today’s clash in eighth place in the table, just one point ahead of Stoke City and, with 10th-place West Ham United in free fall at the moment, on course to finish there if they are able to hold off the Potters over the next five games.
With only two wins from his 15 games in charge, it is virtually guaranteed that the club will choose not to give him the job permanently in the summer, but, with such a precarious gap between themselves and the dreaded drop zone, which division will they find themselves in come the start of the next campaign? Leicester City, who currently sit at the top of the relegation zone in 18th place, are on an excellent run of form, winning all of their last three league clashes, and, whilst it is unlikely given the short amount of time left, it is not outside the realms of possibility that Newcastle could slip into the bottom three in the final moments of the season.
It’s been an absolutely woeful two months for Newcastle, who start the day in 14th place in the Premier League table, just seven points clear of the relegation zone and with only one win in their last eight games, with the rest of those seven clashes all ending in defeat. The Magpies’ losing streak now stands at six games, their worst in the top flight since 1977, leaving manager John Carver a dead man walking.
