(76’) SAVE! Dunne is on the end of Phillips' cross but the big defender, nicknamed the 'Honey Monster', can only direct his header straight at Adrian.
(74’) Joey Barton has given a real captain's performance this afternoon and has really led by example, which certainly can't always be said of the controversial character. Barton wins a header in midfield and Charlie Austin collects the ball but is given offside. The QPR striker is then booked for dissent after throwing the ball into the turf in anger. It's been a frustrating afternoon for the R's top scorer.
(72’) The ball is in the back of the West Ham net but it won't count! Dunne thought he'd given his side a precious lead but the goal has been ruled out for a foul by Steven Caulker on the goalkeeper. The home fans are unsurprisingly unhappy but the referee appears to have got that big all absolutely right.
(70’) The QPR fans have been right behind their side all game and are urging their players to attack at every opportunity. There certainly hasn't been a lack of effort from the R's but an absence of quality. Joey Barton described his team as the 'worst' in the Premier League this week on that basis.
(68’) After being heavily criticised and rightly so after their rather limp display away at the Etihad stadium last weekend it must be said that West Ham have defended very bravely this afternoon and have put their bodies on th line for the cause.
--- 67’ Substitution L. Fer enters the game and replaces B. Zamora. ---
(66’) Leroy Fer is the latest substitute to be brought into the action and Bobby Zamora is the man to go off. The QPR striker receives a generous reception form fans all around the stadium. This will mean a change of shape for the home side who will revert to a 4-4-1-1 formation.
(65’) Their is no real rhythm to either team's play at the moment which is turning the match into a bit of a stalemate at present. QPR really need to produce a big performance as this match heads towards the last quarter.
--- 64’ Substitution Suk-Young Yoon enters the game and replaces C. Hill. ---
(62’) Chris Ramsey makes his first sub of the game by replacing the veteran Clint Hill with Korean defender Suk-Young Yoon better known as Yun coming on in his place. The left-back should give the R's a bit more pace and width.
(60’) That said West Ham do look a bit ragged at the back when the ball is delivered into the box. Reece Burke has been a bit hesitant with his clearances since the start of the second half. He needs his central defensive partner James Collins to guide him through these kind of moments on his debut at this level.
(58’) Carlton Cole has given West Ham some variety in their attack since coming on. They have mixed things up nicely and it is allowing the midfielder's the chance to join up with their striker's more frequently.
(56’) Great work again from Rob Green who raced off his line to foil Stewart Downing who thought he was clean through on goal. The QPR stopper did very well to mop things up and not handle it outside of the area or bring down the West Ham winger. It must be said that Downing seemed to pull out of the challenge when he saw Green steaming out of his area.
--- 55’ Substitution C. Cole comes on for M. Jarvis. ---
(54’) First substitution of the afternoon sees Carlton Cole come on to replace the anonymous Matt Jarvis. The former Wolves winger hasn't seen much first team action this season and on the evidence of this afternoon's display you can see why.
(52’) Big Sam obviously had a few strong words with his player's at half-time as West Ham have been much more aggressive since the restart. QPR then launch a counter-attack and there is a bit of pinball in the West Ham area. Adrian and Burke just about hack it clear after the youngster almost scores an own goal.
(50’) SAVE! And it is a brilliant reaction stop by ex-Hammer Rob Green tips Cresswell's excellent free-kick over the bar. The left-back, who scored a beauty against Stoke recently almost repeated the trick there. A bit of genuine quality from both taker and goalkeeper there, those moments have been few and far between so far.
(49’) Sandro, not for the first time today is rather rash in the challenge and is lucky not to be booked. The former Tottenham midfielder was very late on Valencia there. The free-kick is in a central position and Cresswell will take it.
(47’) CHANCE! Zamora side foots the ball into the grateful arms of Adrian after Clint Hill's header back into the danger area. In Zamora's defence I don't think the QPR centre forward had any idea how much time he had there. if he had then it might have been a different story.
(46’) Both sets of player's are back on the pitch and QPR will get the second half underway.
Chris Ramsey has some excellent options to call upon in the second period if he wishes to. Leroy Fer has been out for a long time and has been a big miss for the Hoops. The likes of Kranjcar and Taarabt can be both magnificent and frustrating in equal measure but have the ability to be match winners on their day.
The big talking point of the first fourty-five minutes is of course the potentially crucial penalty miss by Charlie Austin. Usually so reliable from twelve yards, the QPR striker's shot was not the best and Adrian was once again the West Ham hero. Rangers though to their credit did not allow their heads to drop and continued to press forward in search of an opening goal.
QPR started this match in exactly the right way, going after their opposition from the word go. Sandro almost gave the home side the lead as early as the second minute but his low drive was well saved by the legs of West Ham keeper Adrian. The Hammers grew into the game and had opportunities of their own with Reece Burke coming oh so close a fairytale start to his Premier League career but his header was cleared off the line.
(45’) Half-time here at Loftus Road. QPR 0-0 West Ham United.
(44’) After a pretty frentic start to the game the action has rather gone by the wayside. Both teams look to have settled to be at 0-0 at half-time and be ready to go again in the second half.
(42’) There have been plenty of long balls so far today as you might expect from these two sides. The Hammers do lack a focal point aerially to their attack so it wouldn't be a massive surprise if Carlton Cole enters the fray in the second period to give the visitors a target.
(40’) West Ham look quite happy to try and see this out until the half-time interval. It has been a pretty even game so far but QPR will look back on that penalty miss and feel that they really should be ahead.
(38’) SAVE! A nice easy one for Rob Green but Kevin Nolan will be desperately disappointed with his shot which wasn't good. The ball had broken kindly for the West Ham skipper but he didn't get hold of it at all. Has to do better there, he had plenty of time and space to line it up.
(36’) The QPR supporters want a corner but goal kick is the decision from the referee and it looks to be the right call. Zamora held the ball up well and laid it off to Phillips who gets away a snap shot but the deflection was from one of his teammates rather than a West Ham defender.
(34’) Rob Green delivers an excellent kick upfield and it is warmly greeted by the QPR fans, almost ironically. Austin wins the knock-down and Zamora is brought down by Reece Burke. Barton floats the delivery into the box but it easily dealt with.
(32’) Nearly a chance for Valencia as Downing gets to the byline but can't keep his cross in play and it will be a goal kick to QPR. The West Ham midfielder has the beating of Clint Hill and is taking him on every time he gets the ball.
(30’) QPR are trying to throw the ball into the West Ham penalty area whenever they can. Burke and Collins, bar giving the penalty away, have dealt with the aerial bombardment very well. Phillips then jinks inside from the right wing but drags his left foot shot wide. It was a tame effort.
(28’) An early contender for the worst free-kick of the weekend as Downing, who is normally so reliable from dead ball situations, hits the ball harmlessly into the gloves of Green. What a waste.
(26’) Half a chance for Karl Henry who met a deep cross at the back post with a left-footed volley but couldn't get enough purchase on the ball to trouble Adrian. QPR have reacted really positively to the setback of missing the penalty.
(24’) WIDE! Enner Valencia slips past Dunne but then selfishly shots from a tight angle rather than looking to play in a teammate. It was going to be almost impossible for the West Ham striker to score from that position.
--- 23’ Missed penalty It's a rotten, rotten penalty from QPR's leading scorer. Austin went to belt it down the middle but got it all wrong and Adrian read the scuffed effort. What a let off for the Irons! That could be a massive moment not only in this match but for Rangers' season. ---
(23’) Penalty saved by Adrián!
(23’) SAVED BY ADRIAN!
(22’) PENALTY TO QPR! Blatant handball from James Collins to block Zamora's flick.
(20’) The game is just going through a bit of a lull at the moment with both sides giving the ball away cheaply. All got a bit scrappy, particularly in the middle of the park.
(18’) QPR perhaps understandably look very nervous at the moment. They are being far too hasty on the ball. They need their experienced player's like Barton and Henry to get it down and bring some composure to their play.
(16’) Matt Phillips has been a real shining light for the R's in recent weeks and has provided plenty of ammunition for Charlie Austin. Chris Ramsey will want to see his wide man see much more of the ball than he has done so far.
(14’) Width has been a feature of West Ham's play this season with Carl Jenkinson and Aaron Cresswell being consistently impressive. The left-back Cresswell has seen plenty of the ball so far this afternoon and is seemingly always available for his teammates.
(12’) SHOT! Zamora does well to win a thrown in high up the field from Burke. Rangers keep the ball alive and eventually it drops to Joey Barton who takes the half-volley on but he can't control his shot and it goes well wide.
(11’) Rob Green's kicking today hasn't shown any signs of improvement after his error contributed to Chelsea's winner last weekend. It may be something that West Ham will look to exploit.
(9’) The Hammers have looked very comfortable on the ball since those nervy early moments. They are clearly trying to get the ball up to Enner Valencia at every opportunity. His pace will be a worry for the QPR back four.
(7’) After a fast start from Rangers the visitors have settled down nicely and have created a few chances of their own. Chris Ramsey will not want the occasion to get the better of his player's. Calm heads are what is needed in a relegation battle.
(5’) West Ham force two corner's in quick succession. In the aftermath of the set piece Downing is very nearly fouled in the area by Sandro who put in a rather wild tackle. QPR got away with one there, very honest play from the winger there.
(4’) OFF THE LINE! Debutant Reece Burke's header is hacked away. Nearly a dream start for the youngster. The defender did really well to meet Matt Jarvis' inswinging corner.
(4’) Valencia races down the left hand side but has no support and does well to force a corner from Richard Dunne.
(2’) SAVE! Almost an immediate goal for QPR as Matty Phillips seized on some sloppy play from Mark Noble and raced downfield before playing in Sandro whose fierce low shot is well saved by Adrian with his legs. Great start for the home side. Excellent positive intent.
(1’) West Ham get the game going!
Impeccably observed by both sets of supporters.
Before the match gets underway there will be a minute's silence for the fans who tragically lost their lives in the fire at Bradford City's Valley Parade on 11th May 1985.
The player's are on the pitch and it is a glorious afternoon here in west London. The atmosphere is crackling, the QPR supporters know how important this match is and kick off is just moments away now...
On the face of it West Ham look like potentially good opposition for Rangers. Allardyce's side seem to have lost their way in recent week's and their good season is in danger of petering out. A win for the Hoops would put them right back in the mix and put pressure on the sides above them like Sunderland and Aston Villa.
As for the Hammers, Big Sam hands a Premier League debut to youngster Reece Burke who is just 18-years-old. Kevin Nolan and Matt Jarvis come back in to the starting lineup with Carlton Cole, Winston Reid and Alex Song dropping out.
This fixture must have been circled as 'must win' by QPR Head Coach Chris Ramsey. They are running out of matches and three points is essential this afternoon for the west Londoner's. Leroy Fer returns to the matchday squad after being out with a knee injury. Experienced defender Richard Dunne comes back into the starting eleven with Isla dropping to the bench.
WEST HAM UNITED SUBS: Jaaskelainen, O'Brien, Poyet, Nene, Oxford, Cole and Amalfitano.
QPR SUBS: McCarthy, Yun, Isla, Fer, Wright-Phillips, Kranjcar and Taarabt.
West Ham United (4-4-1-1): Adrian; Jenkinson, Collins, Burke, Cresswell; Jarvis, Kouyate, Noble, Downing; Nolan (c); Valencia.
QPR (4-4-2): Green; Onuoha, Caulker, Dunne, Hill; Barton (c), Henry, Sandro, Phillips; Austin, Zamora.
The team news is in and we'll start with the our hosts QPR...
Good afternoon and welcome along to this crucial Premier League clash between Queen's Park Rangers and West Ham United here at Loftus Road. I'm Chris Baker and I'll be guiding you through this London derby today.

In all honesty, Stoke may be more than a little aggrevated that they were not able to convert such a dominant first half performance into all three points, but between poor finishing and Pantilimon, they just were not able to do it today. Thank you for joining us here!
That's the match! The game ends in a draw, with Sunderland earning a point after suffering for much of the first half but coming out strongly in the second.
(90’) Shawcross tucks a cross behind the line for a Sunderland corner, and with just a minute left here, this is a superb opportunity for the visitors to sneak a win! Gomez lines up the ball and sends a ball towards the back post... but once again it goes out of bounds before coming back in!
(90’) N'Zonzi takes down Defoe right around the halfway line and is booked for his trouble. Sunderland ae taking this free-kick cautiously, keeping their defenders back and hoofing it into the box where Bardsley has to head it clear quickly before Defoe can get his boot onto it!
(90’) Cattermole just wide! He had run onto Van Aanholt's low squared ball, just outside of the box, where Stoke had left a pocket of space but the effort could not be placed on target.
(90’) Coates pokes the ball out of his box for a Stoke throw, which works its way up to Crouch but his header goes over. Four minutes of stoppage time have just been announced here!
(88’) Graham has the ball wide in the box but Pieters is following his every move, forcing him out wide; he tries to cross the ball but it's deflected for a throw-in, deep in Stoke territory.
--- 87’ Substitution P. Bardsley enters the game and replaces G. Cameron. ---
(87’) WHAT A SAVE FROM PANTILIMON! Adam takes a superb shot from far outside the box that looks destined for the top right corner but the goalie is more than equal to it and makes a diving save to keep it out! Cameron comes off for Bardsley.
(85’) Both sides are pushing for a winner here - Defoe was nearly in a shooting position seconds ago but the ball never arrived to him - but are trying to balance the desire to win with the fear of conceding. As a result, there are many players forward and some left behind, with not many midfielders in between.
(83’) And that's some block by Coates who just knocks Ireland's cross for Crouch out in front of the striker, just when it looked certain that the former Liverpool man was about to contort his body into a shooting position!
(82’) Pieters comes across and reads the game fantastically to cut off Wickham before he can get a shot at net. Sunderland take the ensuing corner short and Ireland knocks it out for a throw-in.
(81’) The free-kick is cleared but the ball worked back around from the left, and just when Arnautovic tries to feed Crouch in the middle, the tall striker climbs all over O'Shea and the referee blows his whistle.
--- 80’ Substitution P. Odemwingie enters the game and replaces J. Walters. ---
--- 80’ Yellow card Jones is booked for pulling back Arnautovic with the tricky forward just about to spin past the player. Stoke have a free-kick, right outside the box on the left, but first Odemwingie comes on to massive applause after 8 months out injured for Walters. ---
(78’) Cattermole and O'Shea both throw their bodies on the line to stop Walters' shot after Stoke countered quickly. Arnautovic gets frustrated with the blue shirts in front of him, doesn't see any teammates open, and cuts in before targeting the far post and watching his shot drift wide.
(77’) Wickham to Grahama to Defoe, with the ball worked to the right, and Jones playing a low ball into the box that's knocked out. The visitors play it back and forth, left to right, waiting for the Stoke defence to break, but it never does!
(76’) Rodwell again decisive here in these late stages, positioning himself well in the box to block Crouch's low effort towards net. Jones knocks the ball out for a throw-in seconds later as Stoke look to have roared into an effective attack here, but the opportunity ends when Ireland's throw-in goes right to Pantilimon.
(75’) Crouch tries a header in the box to his teammates but Rodwell - who, incidentally, has been very quiet today - does enough to nudge the ball the other way. Arnautovic takes down Gomez on the sideline but no call is made.
(73’) The chances just won't stop coming! Wickham now tries his effort from just outside the box, on the left, but his shot goes wide on the right. Neither midfield is doing a particularly good job to sheild the defence, partially causing all these chances, but both of these teams also like to play the ball wide and send in crosses.
--- 71’ Substitution Crouch is coming on for Diouf now before the corner can be taken. The corner is poor, however; easily cleared and not finding any teammates in the box. ---
(69’) PANTILIMON WITH AN ENORMOUS SAVE! Adam's free-kick is perfectly played into the back post where Diouf has ended up unmarked. The striker chests the ball down and tries to volley into net but the onrushing goalie saves it with the side of his torso!
(68’) Gomez's corner is very poor, going directly out of bounds for Begovic to take a goal-kick. O'Shea commits a foul by pushing Walters down while the Stoke player rose for a header; Stoke want the captain to be booked and sent off, but the referee decides not to book him.
(67’) Sunderland have a free kick that Gomez sends into the box with a low ball. Adam sticks a leg out to deflect it out for a corner as the Sunderland centre-backs come into the box to get in position.
(65’) And now Walters rushes onto the end of a cross and sends his header wide! This game has seen chance after chance for both sides with neither one capitalizing on the abundance!
(63’) Somehow - somehow! - Jones cuts across midfield, waltz his way into the box, gets in a central position, and drills his shot wide! It takes a touch from Begovic to beget a corner but he should have scored from there!
--- 62’ Yellow card A risky moment at the back for Sunderland as Coates makes a risky pass to his own keeper from a deep cross, but it's handled well and played all the way down to the other end where Defoe earns a corner after his cross is deflected. Gomez plays it in, Begovic collects it, and O'Shea is booked after pulling back the goalie to prevent him from launching a quick counter with the Sunderland defence out of position. ---
--- 60’ Yellow card P. Wollscheid is yellow-carded. ---
(60’) SHAWCROSS WITH A GAMESAVING TACKLE! Wollschied, who's having a bit of a nightmare, loses the ball in midfield to Wickham. As he readies his shot in the box, Shawcross just throws his body in front of it, which blocks the initial effort and is enough to send the follow-up wide!
(59’) Diouf tries to win the ball off of Pantilimon after O'Shea's backpass to his keeper, and he slides in to win it, but he catches the goalkeeper's feet after he clears it and is duly booked for the foul.
--- 58’ Yellow card M. Diouf is cautioned by the referee. ---
(57’) From the corner, the ball is played across the goalmouth and no Sunderland player can reach it to poke it into the net! Stoke break quickly, and Arnautovic plays a cross into the path of Diouf that lands a stride in front of the striker in the box!
(55’) The game is back and forth in terms of possession but becoming more and more congested in the midfield now. Van Aanholt creates space down his flank and sends a cross in that gets deflected out wide, and the follow up is deflected by Adam for a Sunderland corner.
(53’) Van Aanholt makes an acrobatic clearance in the box, but it's only to Adam, who shoots from outside the area and sends his effort over the bar! Chance after chance in this game has come and gone begging because the shots are being sent too high!
(52’) Sunderland continue to poke and prod around the box but just cannot figure out how to get the shot off, before Van Aanholt races on the end of the ball from outside the box and skies his shot.
(51’) Defoe draws a save from Begovic! He had slipped in between the centre-backs as Wickham slotted the ball right through, and the former Toronto FC man took in in stride to force a corner!
(50’) Stoke try to work their way into the box with some intricate one-touch passing near the edge but it's intercepted. Sunderland look far better in these early minutes of this half at keeping the ball than they did for much of the first!
(48’) Good chance for the visitors! Gomez on the half volley in the box tries to send it past Begovic but the goalie makes a very good diving catch to keep it out of the far corner!
--- 46’ Substitution And we're back! The second half begins with O'Shea indeed back on the pitch, face covered in butterfly bandages. Graham comes on for Buckley. It's back and forth for the early moments but the match settles as O'Shea himself knocks the ball out for a corner. ---
The match is certainly still wide open, with the home side perhaps upset that they couldn't convert their dominance into a lead. Join us in 15 for the second half!
What a match we've had here so far, with an early goal from Sunderland, Stoke's incessant pressure that lead to an equalizer, and a late mini-revival from the visitors.
(45’) O'Shea is up and walks off the pitch, to applause from the crowd. The whistle is blown for halftime and the rest of the players follow him into the tunnel, with the match tied at 1-1.
(45’) First half stoppage time is technically over but O'Shea is still being treated - he's bleeding quite a bit and it seems dubious if he'll be able to stay on.
(45’) Coates, comfortably one of Sunderland's best players this half, slides to tuck a Pieter's cross out for a corner. Adam fails to clear the first man and Wollscheid ends up kicking O'Shea directly in the face with his studs as the defender went down low to head clear the ball. He's receiving medical attention now.
(45’) Sunderland are finally coming alive here as the first half ends, turning a free-kick into a corner as Diouf clears it behind his own line. The corner is taken quickly and deflected kindly for Van Aanholt, who tries to first-time his effort from outside the box and watches it sail high and wide of the net.
(43’) Jordi Gomez wins a free-kick after N'Zonzi knocks him over roughly 15 yards outside of the box. Wickham takes the effort but his shot is very far off target, drawing jeers from the crowd.
(41’) Sunderland work the ball down the right and Jones now tries a cross but Shawcross is easily able to head it away. As Stoke try to counter, Coates steps off his line to intercept but it's back with the home side after Cameron is fouled.
(39’) Arnautovic has the ball on the left side of the box - he spots Adam making an unmarked run into the middle, and passes to the midfield, but sending him wide. Adam tries a first-time effort from this awkward angle and it sails wide and high.
(38’) It's all O'Shea can do to head the ball behind the line for a corner after Arnautovic twisted and turned his way into sending a sharp cross across the box! From the ensuing corner, Walters gets a weak shot off that Pantilimon has no trouble scooping up.
(37’) Another minute, another cross from Stoke, as Arnautovic whips one in from the left that Pantilimon catches.
(36’) WHAT A MISTAKE! WHAT A CHANCE! Diouf races around Coates, leaving the centre-back in his wake on the left flank, and spots Ireland open in the middle. He tries to pass it to the player but his pass is well underhit and arrives behind him!
(35’) Van Aanholt rises ahead of Diouf to head clear a cross, and as Stoke try to reorganized, Wollscheid again loses the ball. Defoe nearly slips in behind the defence again but Stoke recover in time. Sunderland are not attacking often but Stoke's backline looks very, very penetrable when they do!
(33’) To no avail: Adam pounces on a loose ball in the midfield and hesitates for too long before slotting it to Ireland, but Coates read the situation and rushes across to clear. It falls to Arnautovic who cuts inside and fires towards net, right into the torso of Pantilimon.
(32’) This is slowly getting better for the visitors, who are now at least keeping Stoke out of their box. The play is slow but that seems deliberate, as they seem to want and try to take the wind out of the home side's sails.
(30’) From a corner, Shawcross races towards the middle of the box and jumps high to head the ball but it's over the bar with Pantilimon watching it well the entire way.
(29’) If Sunderland couldn't control the game before, they look in even more trouble now, as Stoke have just become more voracious since equalizing. They've shown how dangerous they can be with just one touch against Stoke's defence but they have not yet worked out how to keep the ball!
--- 27’ Assist M. Arnautović provided the assist. ---
--- 27’ Goal! THE EQUALIZER HAS FINALLY COME! AND IT'S WHO ELSE BUT ADAM! It's an astonishing, brilliant finish, with Sunderland's defence far too deep and failing to clear from the box. Arnautovic is able to poke it to Adam before falling over and the midfield lashes his effort first time into the top right corner! 1-1 and GAME ON! ---
(25’) Defoe hits the side netting! Once again, it's just a moment of mistake from the Stoke defence, as Wollschied tries to clear Cattermole's excellent probing pass but misses completely. Defoe pounces, races into the box and fires wide!
(23’) And it's yet ANOTHER Adam cross, who has sent in an astonishing amount, that goes just beyond the leg of Walters as he rushed towards the net!
(22’) Cameron whips in a cross from the right flank that goes over the head of Arnautovic, and Adam wins it back, sends it back in the box, and Wollscheid is relieved just to be able to knock it clear.
(20’) Stoke have nearly 70% possession here since the early goal but nothing to show for it yet, though Adam tries a long range effort that goes not terribly far over the bar.
(19’) Adam's turn to hit the wall now but he's claiming there was a handball - and the fans in the stadium ferociously agree - but nothing is called!
--- 18’ Yellow card Cattermole is shown the first yellow of the game for barging directly into Walters right outside of the Sunderland box as the Stoke player released the ball to a teammate. There isn't much in the way of a protest from his teammates there and the home side have another set piece opportunity in a great position! ---
(17’) The crosses keep coming from Stoke, with Arnautovic now hooking it into the box from the left, but the large and lanky Pantilimon has absolutely no trouble grabbing that before it gets to Diouf.
(16’) Gomez leads a rare charge for Sunderland, playing it wide for Buckley, but Cameron knocks it out for a throw-in. From the ensuing play, van Aanholt tries to get it over the top to Buckley but the wide player has drifted into an offside position.
(15’) Sunderland just cannot get the ball at the moment. Adam plays a long ball into the box that gets deflected for Ireland to volley, and it takes a touch before bending just wide of the near post!
(13’) Van Aanholt nudges Walters from the back while trying to win possession near the halfway line, just as the visitors looked to be mounting a sustained attack. Stoke break quickly and draw a sliding tackle from Coates to clear the ball near his box.
(12’) Stoke's pressure is incessant and mounting. Pieters crosses from the left, it's cleared, it's played back to Pieters, and now Adam tries a cross, with Coates clearing both times.
(11’) Adam tries a looping cross into the box that Pantilimon collects. The former Liverpool man has been incredibly active in these early stages of the game, but he's now holding his knee in some discomfort after Cattermole ran right into him.
(10’) That's a great play from Stoke! It's worked around the width of the box before Diouf lays it off for Walters, who drives a shot towards goal that Pantilimon dives low to parry.
(9’) Diouf goes down a little too easily under a challenge from Coates and it's the visitors now who break quickly. Buckley looks free on the left but Wollscheid recovers his positioning and pokes the ball off his foot.
(8’) Sunderland haven't seen much of the ball since the goal but they don't seem to mind much! Adam goes down in the box chasing a cross and he argues he's been clipped by Buckley after they both jump for the ball but the play is waved on.
(6’) Stoke have settled into this nicely now, working the ball across the pitch as they try to get forward. Adam again tries a wide pass up towards Walters and Cameron but it's again overhit; the visitors are set up well and forcing Stoke into making these high-risk passes into poor areas.
(5’) And it's Arnautovic who takes it, looping his shot into the wall in a disappointing effort. The home side regain possession but are forced all the way back to their own box to keep it.
(4’) O'Shea can't control Diouf and sticks out his right leg, bringing down the forward millimeters outside of the box. Arnautovic and Adam are standing over the ensuing free-kick, surely looking to go right on target.
(3’) ADAM LOOKS FOR AN IMMEDIATE EQUALIZER! Stoke play the ball beautifully up the pitch and cut it back for Adam, who takes a touch and hammers a whipping shot that Pantilimon stretches to collect!
--- 1’ Goal! AND WE HAVE KICK OFF.... AND A GOAL! WICKHAM HAS SCORED! It was a nightmare of a defensive performance from Stoke there, who simply could not clear the ball. It began with a run from Defoe that opened up space for Buckley to turn and fire a cross into the box. Begovic dives low and uncharacteristically spills it for Wickham to pounce on and poke it into the net! 1-0 to the visitors! ---
The two teams are about to walk onto the pitch. We're just moments away from kick-off now!
Diouf and Adam have both notched twice for Stoke in their last four matches whereas Sunderland have scored just three goals entirely in their last four matches, each by a different player. Their profligancy in front of net is a major factor in their slide towards the bottom of the table.
Needless to say, Dick Advocaat's side would warmly welcome a result here, as the coach has just one win since taking charge of the team, back in the Wear-Tyne derby. FULL TIME: WEST BROM 0-0 LIVERPOOL. The hosts get what they wanted from the match as they fend off a toothless Reds attack to inch a point closer to safety. (90’) INCHES WIDE AT THE DEATH! That was the chance! A top drawer delivery from Steven Gerrard is met by Lovren at the far post. He rises well to head it towards goal, but it crashes agonizingly into the side netting! And that will do it!
(90’) Liverpool muster one last desperate push forward but there's no way through for them. It's been a common theme throughout, and say what you want about West Brom's approach, but it looks like it will get them the point they were hoping for.
(90’) There will be four minutes of time added on at the end of the match, with West Brom currently looking the likelier side to break the deadlock.
(89’) McManaman! The substitute has been as busy as an accountant during tax season since coming on and has made the most of his time in attack. He weaves his way through the left channel and in towards the byline, but his shot from a tight angle is kicked behind by Mignolet!
(87’) The Baggies appear content with a draw, and a point would serve them well in their quest for safety. They advance the ball into attack and win a throw, which Gardner is in no rush to take. Into the final few minutes here and a breakthrough is appearing all the less likely with each passing second.
(85’) It continues to be a daunting task for Liverpool to try and find a breakthrough, as they are afforded no way through this West Brom defence. Perhaps we should have expected as much, however, as Tony Pulis has never lost a home game against Liverpool as a manager in six tries (W3, D3).
(83’) West Brom have defended admirably throughout, though it has been a real team effort. They seem to be playing with wax legs now at the back, however, as fatigue begins to set in. Can Liverpool take advantage? They're pressing here and a scoring chance does appear to be on the horizon.
--- 81’ Substitution J. Morrison is done for the day. C. Baird is his replacement. ---
(81’) STRAIGHT AT MIGNOLET! Tremendous footwork from McManaman to dance through midfield. He gets to the top of the area and lays it off for Gardner, but the midfielder sends his shot right at Mignolet who makes a comfortable stop.
(79’) STOPPED BY MYHILL! Gerrard is teed up for a shot atop the area and tries to place it in with a side-footed effort towards the near post, but he can't really trouble the keeper. What a storyline that would have been!
(77’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool have picked up 35 points in the league since Boxing Day, with only Arsenal managing a better record over that span (39).
--- 75’ Substitution B. Ideye comes on for S. Berahino. ---
--- 75’ Substitution F. Borini enters play, replacing M. Balotelli. ---

(75’) Brendan Rodgers is forced to dip into his bench as they try to find a dramatic, late winner. A draw would be very detrimental to Liverpool's top four hopes, so it's time for them to go for it. (73’) Sterling and Coutinho link-up well, as Liverpool again enjoy a prominent spell of possession in the attacking third. They get two real shooting chances, but West Brom have EIGHT defenders packed inside the penalty area like sardines, as they get some important blocks in and continue to hold firm.
(71’) West Brom sense an opportunity to get forward and try to snatch this game from Liverpool's grasp. They are starting to commit men forward, and a late goal could very well be enough to secure their place in the Premier League, which has the crowd buzzing in anticipation.
(69’) Sterling is showing plenty of intent to try and create, but he's being afforded little space in attack. Full credit has to be given to West Brom in how they have defended the threat of the forward, smothering him in possession and preventing him from using his pace.
(67’) OFF THE LINE! A ball into the area from Berahino isn't dealt with by Skrtel. It comes to Morrison, who lunges in bravely with a header, but Lovren recovers to save a goal and usher the ball to safety!
(65’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have picked up just one point this season against the top five teams in the Premier League (D1, L5). They were outscored 13-4 in those matches, with their sole point coming in a 2-2 draw at home to Manchester United in October.
--- 64’ Substitution C. McManaman comes on for V. Anichebe. ---
(63’) OFF THE BAR! Is the opening coming for Liverpool? Ibe works a tidy one-two with Balotelli, and surges into the area after taking the return pass. He has a clean look at goal, but smacks his effort off the frame of the goal! What a chance that was for the opener!
--- 61’ Yellow card C. Dawson gets yellow. ---
(61’) Great bit of trickery from Ibe who dummies the ball for himself, turning up the pitch to chase down a pass. He has the beating of Dawson, who is forced to tug back the shirt of the speedy youngster to prevent a break. That's a clear free kick, and a yellow card for the defender.
(60’) Liverpool aren't getting into the final third nearly as often as they managed in the first half. When they do, the West Brom defence is more congested than the streets of Manila on a summer afternoon, affording very little space for the Reds to try and create.
(58’) WONDERFUL VOLLEY! Brunt does well to fend off challenges on the left before whipping a cross in towards the far post. Johnson is too nonchalant in defending, allowing Gardner to sneak in behind and meet it with a volley, but he blasts it into the side netting!
(56’) INCREDIBLE DOUBLE SAVE! Frantic defending from West Brom but they're bailed out by their keeper! Balotelli holds the ball up well in the area, but sees his shot blocked. It comes to Coutinho, who sees his effort palmed out by Myhill, who then does brilliantly to deny Henderson on the follow up!
(54’) Encouraging! In the end it's nowhere near the goal, but a good delivery into the area from Fletcher following a free kick is met by McAuley. The crowd buzzes in anticipation, but the defender's header is sent miles wide of the far post.
(52’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool conceded four goals in their last away match in the Premier League, something they have only done four times since 2001. On each occasion they responded in their next road game with a victory (December 2001, April 2003, April 2004 and September 2011).
(50’) Liverpool need to show a bit more urgency with their approach. West Brom have come out in this second half full of running, pressing much higher up the pitch. (48’) The second half starts with a bit more West Brom possession, but it's all very sloppy from the hosts. They struggle to string more than a couple of passes together and as a result is sees the ball being contained largely in midfield. This match has hardly been very easy on the eyes.
(46’) Here we go again! Who, if anyone, can provide a breakthrough?
HALF TIME: WEST BROM 0-0 LIVERPOOL. It's been a very uneventful first half at The Hawthorns as the Reds have nothing to show for their dominance. There's been few efforts at goal from either side and, despite a large gap in possession, neither team deserves to hold the lead at the break.
(45’) The one minute of stoppage time has come to an end and that is it for the first half from West Midlands.
(44’) The Reds are enjoying some excellent possession in the final third and West Brom aren't looking like winning it back anytime soon. They have bodies waiting in the centre, but still can find no way through as frustration begins to set in. Henderson tries to pick out Balotelli with a cross but sends it straight into the waiting arms of Myhill.
(42’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool have lost just twice in their eight trips to the Hawthorns in Premier League play (W5, D1).
(40’) The battle out on the left flank between Sterling and Dawson has been intriguing throughout the first half. The winger does well to get into a bit of space and try to send a cross in, but the right-back recovers to block it behind for a corner. The ensuing delivery comes to nothing as Henderson is called for a foul inside the area.
(38’) Dreadful delivery! Berahino runs his tail off to chase down a long ball forward. He keeps it alive and plays it back for Gardner, who has options in the centre, but gets way too much behind his cross as it sails over everyone's head and behind for a goal kick.
(36’) This match has taken the shape of a Sunday stroll through the park. The desire and flair is nowhere to be found from either side, while the pace is fizzling out to a near stand-still as we near half time at The Hawthorns.
(34’) Anichebe, pressing much higher up the pitch now, tries to block a Lovren clearance, but fails to do so and actually catches the defender on the follow-through. The contact was indeed incidental, but the Liverpool defender is feeling the effects of that challenge.
(32’) Liverpool have nothing to show for their dominance as we pass the half-hour mark. It has been quite comfortable for them in possession - perhaps too comfortable if you ask Tony Pulis - but for all their time on the ball, they have yet to carve out any clear-cut scoring opportunities.
(30’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool’s 4-1 defeat at Arsenal on the first weekend of April ended a six-match unbeaten run away from home in the Premier League in which they didn’t concede a single goal.
(28’) CLOSE TO THE OPENER! Gerrard and Henderson stand over it, but it is the man making his 500th appearance who takes. The midfielder curl a well-hit shot towards the near post with Myhill surely beaten, but it sails inches over the bar!
(27’) Great work from Balotelli! The striker unselfishly passes up the opportunity for a shot after some good link-up play and holds the ball up well as he runs across the top of the area looking for an outlet. He gets toppled over clumsily by Berahino and this is a real chance for the Reds from the ensuing free kick.
(25’) Tony Pulis is urging his side to show a bit of life and push higher up the pitch. It has been all too comfortable for Liverpool in possession and the Baggies' boss is trying to change that. They have to get after Gerrard and Henderson in midfield, with the duo pulling the strings for the visitors in possession.
(23’) The bulk of this match is being played in the West Brom end and Liverpool are making themselves at home it attack. The hosts have everyone behind the ball to defend, however, which is making it very hard on the Reds to find gaps and create chances.
(21’) Coutinho shows a bit of frustration with his side's inability to create, and lets fly from the same spot from which he scored against Southampton earlier this season. It's an ambitious effort, but certainly not his best, as it sails well over the bar.
(19’) STAT ATTACK: There have been 11 goals scored in the first 15 minutes of matches at The Hawthorns this season, more than at any other Premier League venue - but none today!
(17’) West Brom win a free kick in a good area for a cross, from 40-yards out on the right. Morrison lifts an encouraging ball into the box and Lescott does well to win it at the far post, heading back across goal, but the flag is up for offside.
(15’) Gerrard is dropping very deep, between Skrtel and Lovren, as he tries to get on the ball as often as possible and dictate possession. He's doing a great job through the first quarter of an hour to transition them into attack, but they are just lacking that killer instinct in attack at the moment.
(13’) A lovely pass forward from Coutinho sends Sterling in, but some good defensive work forces the attacker to retreat and slow the pace of the attack. West Brom have defended admirably thus far, but it's all a bit flat from them going forward.
(11’) Balotelli shows great work ethic, tracking back and dispossessing Yacob near the halfway line. He lays it off for Coutinho and the Reds break quickly into attack. The Italian takes a return pass, but McAuley recovers well to jump in and block the final effort.
(9’) The Baggies fans are not happy with referee Roger East as we approach the 10-minute mark. Henderson gets away with a handball in midfield and just seconds later Fletcher is called for a foul on Sterling. It's more possession for Liverpool, who refuse to squander it for more than a few seconds.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: Steven Gerrard is making his 500th Premier League appearance for Liverpool today. Only Ryan Giggs and Jamie Carragher have managed more with a single club.
(5’) It looks as though Liverpool are lining up in more of a 4-3-3 here, not the expected 3-4-3. Glen Johnson and Emre Can are lining up at left and right-back respectively, when it was assumed that the English defender would be acting as more as a wing-back, along with Ibe.
(3’) Liverpool dominate possession early on. Jordon Ibe shows some good intent from the first whistle to get forward and nearly finds a way through Brunt and Lescott into the area. Balotelli of course is leading the lines for the visitors, and he will be relied upon to put in the required work up top, to move around and create space for his teammates off the ball.

FULL TIME: ARSENAL 0-0 CHELSEA. For the third time in four seasons, these two sides settle for a scoreless draw at the Emirates. The Blues will feel hard done by as they had two valid appeals for a penalty turned aside in the first half, but the Gunners were the far more positive side after the break, though had little to show for it. (90’) Into the fourth and final minute of stoppage time here and Chelsea make their final substitution, allowing more time to run off the clock. Cuadrado comes on, but it's hardly a tactical switch from Mourinho as it is a time waster.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution Willian is replaced with J. Cuadrado. ---
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Cazorla gets yellow. ---
(90’) WHAT A CHANCE! Sanchez does well to slide Monreal through on the left, who then plays a teasing ball across the face of goal. Ozil fails to direct it goalwards from six-yards out and then a slight deflection takes it through the legs of Welbeck!
--- 90’ Substitution Mourinho makes his second change and it's Kurt Zouma who will come on to help see out the draw. Fabregas is the man to give way and he gets a very mixed reception from his former fans, though the boos did seem to drown out the cheers as he takes an awfully long time to make his way off the pitch. ---

(86’) Chelsea have not dropped points away from home in the Premier League since a 5-3 defeat at the hands of Tottenham on New Year’s Day. (78’) Chelsea are showing every sign of sitting back and defending. The bus has been parked, for the most part, and it will be up to Arsenal now to try and change the outcome. It will take something truly special to breakdown this Mourinho defence, but they have to start by winning the ball back as Chelsea are playing keep-away in possession at the moment.

The German is played through on the flank and sends an encouraging ball in, but Matic does well to intervene. The pressure stays on and the ball is worked to Cazorla inside the penalty area, but he drags a shot well wide of the far post. And here's the change, as Welbeck is set to come on in place of Coquelin.
(74’) STAT ATTACK: Arsenal have not scored in their last four meetings with Chelsea across all competitions, while conceding 10 times. The last Gunners goal against the Blues was scored by Theo Walcott in a 2-1 defeat at Stamford Bridge in January 2013.
--- 72’ Yellow card B. Ivanović goes into the referee's book. ---

It was a needless intervention from the right-back, who could be in for a nerve-wracking final 20 minutes now as the Chilean will no doubt look to run at him from here on out.
(71’) Finally there are signs of life on the Arsenal bench as Welbeck and Wilshere are up and jogging along the touchline. Wenger may have waited a few minutes too long, however, as you really would have liked to see a couple of these substitutes get a lengthier go at trying to make their presence felt.

Play continues and Willian gets his boot up into the face of Koscielny, which will earn him a yellow card.

Ramsey works hard to pressure Willian and Chelsea wind up conceding possession before Sanchez wins a free kick in attack as Fabregas is penalized for a cheap foul.

(83’) STAT ATTACK: The Baggies have conceded 10 goals in three games, having previously let in only seven goals in their first nine games under Pulis.
--- 81’ Substitution J. Olsson enters the game and replaces C. Gardner. ---
(81’) Alan Pardew clearly wants something from this game as Palace go 4-3-3 as they continue to look for a window back in to this game. For Tony Pulis, though, he introduces Olsson to proceedings to stiffle their opponents some more.
--- 80’ Substitution Y. Sanogo comes on for J. McArthur. ---
--- 79’ Yellow card C. Brunt gets yellow. ---
--- 79’ Yellow card C. Gardner is yellow-carded. ---
(79’) OVER! The hosts go with three up front and it draws Puncheon out from his deep midfield role this afternoon. The tactical change almost works as the midifelder hits a dipping volley over the bar.
(77’) GOOD SAVE! It could have been three. Berahino profits from some poor defending in the Eagles' box and pokes his shot against the legs of the on-rushing Speroni and wins a corner for his side.
(74’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom are winless in 10 away matches (D5, L5) since the 1-0 victory at Leicester on 1 November.
(72’) CLOSE! Ward ventures forward and turns McAuley and sends a lovely cross into the box that starts to swing towards Myhill's goal before sailing out of play for a goal-kick.
--- 71’ Substitution C. Dawson is done for the day. A. Wisdom is his replacement. ---
(70’) Bolasie received a yellow card for kicking the back of Dawson's standing leg. The centre-back takes his sweet time to get back to his feet after receiving treatment but it now looks like he is going off.
--- 69’ Yellow card Y. Bolasie is cautioned by the referee. ---
(68’) Puncheon stands over a central free-kick and sends it into the six-yard box towards Murray but Myhill is there to pluck his header across goal and then proceeds to thrash the ball out for a throw-in.
(66’) WIDE! Berahino has looked very impotent in front of goal today but manages to slip past Dann successfully before flashing his shot wide of the far post.
(64’) Tony Pulis is encouraging his charges to keep it tight across the pitch at the moment as the home side are still proving a threat. Bolasie slips past Lescott and sends a low right-footed effort in on goal but McAuley gets his leg in the way to block.
--- 61’ Yellow card J. Puncheon is cautioned by the referee. ---
(61’) Albion are doing their best to strangle any flow of play that Palace have in this game - taking their time over throw-ins, set-pieces and frustrating their hosts.
(59’) HITS THE WOODWORK! Gayle, fresh on as a subsititute, picks up on a cross after Murray misses it and strikes the near post from six yards. When it isn't your day...
(57’) STAT ATTACK: Alan Pardew's men have claimed 15 points from the last 18 available (W5, L1); only Arsenal and Manchester United have fared better over this period.
(55’) The form book has gone out of the proverbial window, here. Palace's run of four wins on the bounce does not look like being extended to five right now.
--- 54’ Yellow card S. Dann gets yellow. ---
--- 53’ Goal! WHAT A GOAL! My word. What a strike. Albion win a corner but the hosts fluffs their lines as the ball falls to Gardner who lashes it from 30 yards past Speroni. Could that be the best goal of the weekend? ---
(51’) There is immense pressure on the Baggies' penalty area at the moment as Myhill carries a cross from the left behind for a corner. If they can weather the storm then they will be confident they can catch their opponents on the break.
(49’) STAT ATTACK: Albion have claimed just 18 points from a possible 48 against fellow bottom half sides. Only Burnley and Leicester have fared worse.
(47’) YET ANOTHER PENALTY SHOUT! The Eagles are incensed as Gardner is all over Zaha again in the penalty area. Exasperated appeals from the hoem support fall on deaf ears as the visitors clear.
--- 46’ Substitution P. Souaré enters the game and replaces J. Ledley. ---
--- 46’ Substitution M. Jedinak is replaced with D. Gayle. ---
(45’) And we are back with Palace shifting their system to 4-4-2 and getting us back underway.
HALF TIME - CRYSTAL PALACE 0-1 WEST BROM. Morrison's second minute header seperates the two sides at the break at Selhurst Park. Both sides have had a penalty shout turned away by Jonathan Moss as the Eagles have created the best chances, with Bolasie going close on numerous occasions. More to come after the break...
(45’) There will be TWO minutes of added on time.
(45’) OVER! The Eagles win a free-kick. Puncheon sees Jedinak in space to the left of Myhill's goal, but the midfielder can't keep his shot down as it sails over the bar.
(43’) Puncheon hasn't had the best of games so far and is crowded out by Yacob and Brunt and ends up giving away a throw-in. West Brom are putting all 11 men behind the ball and are putting in a dogged display right now.
(41’) The Selhurst Park turf is cutting up terribly out there and it is having a detrimental effect on the game as both sets of players are slipping and sliding all over the place! Somewhere, the groundsman has his head in his hands!
(39’) Ward is doing well down the right-hand-side as he overlaps with Zaha. The full-back sees Murray and puts a diagonal cross into the penalty area but Lescott heads it clear.
(37’) STAT ATTACK: The Eagles can equal a top-flight club record of five successive wins if they can overturn the current deficit.
(35’) OUCH! Fletcher has to stretch to reach a pass from Brunt but gets his studs caught in the turf and falls to the ground in agony. The Manchester Unied loanee gets back up on his feet but will take a little while to shake that one off!
(32’) Murray has his head in his hands as Bolasie sends a beautiful delivery into the box but the striker didn't read the play and lets it go out for a goal kick.
(30’) SAVE! Myhill is definitely winning a personal battle with Bolasie right now. The Eagles man goes for the spectacular and overhead kicks a lovely effort but the keeper is up and tips it away. What a goal that would have been!
(28’) BOLASIE AGAIN! The midfielder is in the form of his life and cuts in from the left flank and floats a dangerous ball to Myhill's back post, but the keeper is equal to it as Murray was ready to pounce.
(26’) ANOTHER PENALTY SHOUT! Ooh, Jonathan Moss, you have bottled it. Zaha peels off to the back post to meet the corner kick and he is steamrollered by Gardner. The home fans are furious as the referee waves the appeals away!
(25’) GREAT SAVE! Anichebe beats the ground in frustration as he fails to win another free-kick and the ball breaks to Bolasie, whose low shot is blocked from close range by Myhill.
(23’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have lost their last three league games. It is the first time a Tony Pulis side has suffered three defeats since his then-Stoke team in March - April 2013.
(21’) The Eagles are just beginning to come back in to this game. Zaha gets Dawson on the break and beats him for pace but Yacob steps in to thwart the winger.
(19’) The visitors have really started on the front foot here. Gardner comes inside and looks to slip Brunt in on the overlap but Zaha is tracking back and breaks down the attack to a ripple of applause from the Selhurst Park faithful.
(16’) PENALTY SHOUT! Anichebe looks like he is pushed to the floor by Jedinak and the former Everton man is up in arms as Jonathan Moss waves away any penalty claims. He certainly had a shout...
--- 14’ Yellow card G. McAuley receives a yellow card. ---
(14’) McAuley gets too tight to Murray and receives the first booking of the afternoon. Its clear that Pulis has set the Baggies up to stiffle the home side.
(12’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace have failed to keep a clean sheet at home since Pardew took over in January this year.
(10’) SAVE! McArthur cuts inside on his left foot and takes his time to place a shot low to Myhill's right but the keeper is down quickly and smothers the ball.
(9’) The hosts are probing their opponent's defence and taking their time on the ball. Alan Pardew's men certainly will not panic but he will be bitterly disappointed to be behind already.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: James Morrison's opener was the Baggies 10th goal away from home in the Premier League this season.
(5’) OVER! The Eagles soar up the other end and win a free-kick on the edge of the box. It finds its way to Murray, who blasts his effort over the bar from ten yards.
--- 2’ Assist C. Brunt provided the assist. ---
--- 2’ Goal! WHAT A START! West Brom have scored inside the first two minutes. Berahino wins a corner on the left and Morrison is left totally unmarked and meets Brunt's set-piece with a bullet header into the back of the net. ---
(1’) The referee blows his whistle and we are off...with West Brom kicking from right to left.
TEN MINUTES TO GO! The players, along with referee Jonathan Moss, return to the dressing rooms as Selhurst Park continues to fill up...this should be a great game today!
PRE MATCH STAT ATTACK: I'm sure hoping this won't be the commentator's kiss of death! Seventeen goals have been scored in the previous five Premier League meetings between these two sides - an average of 3.4 goals per game.
Meanwhile for the Baggies, who need to pick up a few more results to ensure their top-flight status, Brown Ideye is replaced by Victor Anichebe as manager Tony Pulis makes his first return to his former club after his shock resignation just two days before the start of this season. Will he be taking three points back to the Midlands?
Eagles' boss Alan Pardew was so pleased after last week's 4-1 demolition of Sunderland he went as far as labelling his side's performance was like watching Brazil! He makes just one change to the South London samba boys with Joe Ledley replacing Pape Souare.

Burnley must now turn their attention to next weekend's relegation showdown with Leicester City which is shaping up to be a pivotal match. With the Foxes winning three on the bounce it will be another testing afternoon for Sean Dyche's men. As for Everton their good form continues and if they continue to play in this manner and become a bit more ruthless in attack then they will finish the season in a very positive manner.
Burnley's fight to stay in the Premier League is going to be incredibly difficult if they keep failing to find the back of the net. For all their honesty and endeavour they created precious little in front of goal. David Jones missed a golden chance just after Kevin Mirallas' goal and that proved very costly indeed.
Even the most ardent Burnley supporter will struggle to say that Everton weren't worthy of their win but the Toffees certainly made hard work of it this afternoon. Roberto Martinez's side had countless opportunities to make the game safe but failed to do so. One-nil is always a nervy and dangerous scoreline but the Clarets couldn't ever mount enough pressure to force an equaliser.
(90’) And that's it! Full time here at Goodison Park. Everton 1-0 Burnley.
(90’) Burnley still believe they can get something from this contest and are chucking the ball forwards whenever they can but the passes are more in hope rather than expectation at the moment.
(90’) SHOT! Barkley hits the target but is once again denied by Heaton. The Everton midfielder had Lukaku in support but opted not to use him. Safe to say that the striker looked far from impressed with that decision.
(90’) Naismith, as busy as ever, does very well to win his side a corner that Baines will take. The corner is overhit and Burnley eventually smuggle the ball clear after Barry didn't take the opportunity to shoot.
--- 88’ Substitution J. McCarthy is done for the day. M. Bešić is his replacement. ---
(88’) The visitors are now in the last chance saloon and are chucking the kitchen sink into the Everton penalty area. Enough cliches there? Burnley are giving it a real go. Meanwhile Martinez has been forced into a substitution as McCarthy has picked up a knock and has to go off. Besic has come on to see the game out.
(86’) CHANCE! And it is a big one as Ings heads over from about eight yards after a decent cross into the danger area from Trippier. Burnley have rarely threatened since going down to ten men but that was a huge opportunity for them to draw level.
--- 84’ Substitution M. Taylor comes on for D. Jones. ---
--- 84’ Substitution R. Wallace enters the game and replaces G. Boyd. ---
(84’) Sean Dyche gambles by bringing on two players who are just returning from long-term injuries with Matthew Taylor and Ross Wallace coming on for George Boyd and David Jones. Burnley have used all of their substitutions now.
(82’) WIDE! McCarthy strikes the ball very cleanly after being set up by Ross Barkley's knock down. Heaton could only stand and watch as the shot flew just past the post.
--- 80’ Substitution A. Koné is done for the day. S. Naismith is his replacement. ---
(80’) Arouna Kone has not had a particularly effective game and it is no surprise to see the industrious Steven Naismith come on in his place. You imagine that the Scottish forward will play in behind Lukaku.
(78’) Burnley just beginning to string a few passes together as they look to build up some momentum as we head towards the final ten minutes of the match. Shackell and Duff are knocking some hopeful looking long diagonal balls which are being easily dealt with by Jagielka and co.
(76’) Baines' free-kick finds Barry completely unmarked at the back post. The holding midfielder elects to strike the ball first time but he surely had time to have a touch before firing goalwards. Another decent chance goes begging for Everton.
(74’) Almost a great opportunity for Lukaku as he is picked out brilliantly by a flighted through ball by Gareth Barry. Unfortunately for the Toffees the former Chelsea centre forward is let down by his first touch and allows Heaton to race off his line and claim the loose ball.
(72’) It is now over six hours of Premier League football since Burnley last scored a goal and they need to change that statistic in the next twenty minutes or so if they are to get anything out of this match and aid their survival bid.
(70’) CHANCE! Good hold up play by Lukaku brings Kone into play who shimmies across the top of the penalty area before laying the ball off to Lennon who gets his shot off first time but it is deflected by Ben Mee and easy for Heaton to gather.
(68’) As we head into the final quarter of the match it remains one-nil to Everton. The Toffees have almost totally dominated the second half but have found that killer second goal elusive so far. Burnley will be happy that they are still in the match.
(65’) SAVE! Burnley just can't clear their lines at the moment. This time it is Leighton Baines who stings the palms of Tom Heaton after being teed up by Aaron Lennon. A second goal for Everton looks much more likely than an equaliser at the moment.
(63’) Lukaku is now on but not in place of Kone as you might have expected but alongside him. Fellow Belgian and goalscorer Kevin Mirallas is the man to be replaced.
--- 61’ Substitution K. Mirallas is replaced with R. Lukaku. ---
--- 61’ Yellow card J. Shackell goes into the referee's book. ---
(60’) Lukas Jutkiewicz, formerly of Everton, is the first substitute of the day coming on in place of Sam Vokes. The sub is immediately involved in the action and forces a corner for his side. Trippier takes the set-piece but his cross is easily headed away by Stones.
--- 59’ Substitution S. Vokes is replaced with L. Jutkiewicz. ---
(58’) OVER! Danny Ings leads a Burnley counter attack after Everton make a mess of a short corner. The England Under 21 international cuts inside from the left wing onto his right foot but can only sky his shot miles over the crossbar.
(56’) WHAT A MISS! James McCarthy sidefoots the ball wide of the post after Lennon and Baines had combined to great effect down the left wing. He simply has to score there, an absolute sitter. Everton may live to regret their wastefulness in front of goal.
(54’) OVER! Kone fires his shot high wide and not very handsomely after excellent approach work from Baines. The Everton striker had options to his right and should really be doing better in that position.
--- 53’ Yellow card S. Arfield goes into the referee's book. ---
(52’) Yellow card for Mirallas and the Belgian winger is perhaps lucky not to see red as he rakes his studs down the shin of Boyd with the ball nowhere to be seen. Arfield then goes into the book for hacking down Barkley in the centre of midfield. This game is in danger of getting out of hand.
--- 51’ Yellow card K. Mirallas is cautioned by the referee. ---
(50’) Corner to Burnley. Set-pieces will be crucial for the away side in the second half as their numerical disadvantage shouldn't be as much of an issue. Trippier whips in a devilish delivery that bounces up off of Jagielka and into the grateful arms of Howard. Let off their for Everton.
(48’) The Toffees have begun the second half in the same vein as they started the first. Baines as usual fires in a low cross to the near post and Kone gets across his man to turn the ball goalwards. The former Wigan striker then sees his effort hit the bottom of the post. The rebound falls to Ross Barkley who has his shot smothered well by Heaton. Close to 2-0.
(46’) Everton get us underway for the second half. No alterations so far for either team.
With relegation rivals West Bromwich Albion and Leicester City leading at half-time Burnley have no other option but to go all-out for an equaliser and then a winner. Will the red card for Barnes mean a substitution for the Clarets or just a tactical reshuffle? Danny Ings may play out wide and leave Sam Vokes as the lone striker. Roberto Martinez will be confident that his players can exploit the gaps that will inevitably open up as this match progresses.
As for Burnley, where do they go from here? Despite being second best for the majority of the opening 45 minutes they are still very much in the game. They will rue the chance missed by David Jones that could have given them an instant equaliser but be very grateful to goalkeeper Tom Heaton who saved a penalty from Ross Barkley. Ashley Barnes' dismissal on the brink of half-time will make it an uphill battle in the second period.
Roberto Martinez will have mixed emotions at the half-time interval. He will no doubt be very pleased from what he has seen from his side going forward and some of the combination play in attack has been exceptional. However, he will be extremely frustrated that they are only a goal to the good and that his team have shown their defensive vulnerabilities at times. Getting a second goal as quickly as possible after the break will be vitally important for Everton.
--- 45’ +2 Red card! A. Barnes gets a second yellow card and is sent off! ---
(45’) Half-time Everton 1-0 Burnley. The visitors down to ten men.
(45’) RED CARD FOR BURNLEY! What a terrible way to end the half for Sean Dyche's men. Ashley Barnes who was already on a yellow card makes a very silly tackle on Coleman and is given his marching orders. That could be a pivotal moment in the match as the referee promptly blows for half-time.
(43’) Slight delay here as Ings requires some attention from the Burnley physio after catching the ball full in the face from close range by Barry's half-volleyed pass. The striker seems a little groggy but will be fine to carry on.
(41’) Another nervy moment this season from veteran goalkeeper Tim Howard who has his clearance charged down by Ings. The Everton stopper took far too long and was nearly punished for his sloppiness. The Toffees are creating their own problems at times and are giving the visitors encouragement.
(38’) Danny Ings does really well to first hold the ball up with his back to goal before playing in Barnes. But just when the Burnley forward thought he was in on goal his shot was very well blocked by Gareth Barry, who had tracked his run all the way.
(36’) Danny Ings has gone seven games without a goal and could desperately do with finding the net this afternoon. The Burnley no.10 has failed to find the net since scoring at Old Trafford in a 3-1 defeat. Ings has been linked with a move to Liverpool and will be keen to impress on Merseyside.
(34’) Everton continue to pile on the pressure and Kone is proving to be a handful for the Burnley central defenders of Duff and Shackell. This match could be close to being over as contest if the home side had taken their chances. As ever though the Clarets have looked to attack at every opportunity even though they have been few and far between.
(30’) CHANCE! And what a chance for Burnley to hit back immediately. David Jones was left with just Tim Howard to beat but put his shot over the bar. That was a massive opportunity for the away side to draw level. In their current situation they really can't afford to miss chances like that.
--- 29’ Assist Assist by A. Koné. ---
--- 29’ Goal! Lennon is once again involved and plays in Coleman. The Irish right back pulls the ball back to Kone who miscontrols it and it falls kindly to Mirallas who stabs home at the second attempt. The goal has been coming and is no less than Everton deserve. ---
(29’) GOAL! 1-0 Kevin Mirallas breaks the deadlock!
(26’) Everton have started this match at an excellent tempo. The speed and incisiveness of their passing has caused their opponents all sorts of difficulties. Burnley just need to hang in there at the moment and weather the storm.
(24’) Ashley Barnes is the first man to go into the referee's notebook this afternoon and not before time. Burnley's players have certainly been fully committed but they have overstepped the mark on one or two occasions and the officials have decided that enough is enough. It was a late and potentially dangerous tackle by Barnes on McCarthy.
--- 23’ Yellow card A. Barnes gets yellow. ---
(22’) SHOT! Danny Ings with a snap shot on the half-volley almost catches Tim Howard unawares from all of thirty yards but the Burnley striker's effort on goal doesn't have enough power to seriously trouble the Everton goalkeeper. Better from the visitors.
(20’) Sean Dyche will be very concerned with how this match has started but relieved that they are not behind. The Everton midfield players are being allowed far too much room to operate in. Burnley's 4-4-2 formation is leaving the back four exposed with Jones and Arfield currently being overrun in the centre of the park.
(18’) WIDE! Lennon is just inches away from giving Everton the lead. The winger, on loan from Tottenham Hotspur, drifted into a central position and ran at the heart of the Burnley defence. He worked the ball onto his favoured right foot but his low shot is pulled wide of the post.
(16’) SAVE! A deep cross came in from Seamus Coleman on the right that Heaton failed to deal with and the ball fell invitingly to Leighton Baines who fired in a rasping half-volley which was well saved in the end. Good pressure from the home side.
(13’) Unlike the previous incident involving a tug-of-war between Mirallas and Baines it seemed that Ross Barkley was the designated as the pre-match penalty taker. Romelu Lukaku has scored his last couple of penalties and must be frustrated that he wasn't on the field to take it.
(11’) Penalty saved by T. Heaton!
--- 11’ Missed penalty ---
(11’) The Burnley fans are absolutely jubilant. Sean Dyche and his player's will feel that some sort of justice has been done as they were adamant that it should have been a free-kick instead of a penalty. Either way it is still 0-0.
(11’) SAVED BY TOM HEATON! Not the best spot kick from Barkley but an excellent save from the Burnley keeper. Very surprised not to see usual penalty taker Leighton Baines or Kevin Mirallas assuming the responsibilities.
(9’) PENALTY TO EVERTON! Aaron Lennon raced towards the penalty area and was brought down by David Jones. The initial contact seems to been made outside the box.
(6’) Jagielka is down in a heap after being caught with a stray arm from Vokes. The Everton skipper has blood coming out of his mouth so will need to leave the field for some treatment. No suggestion of intent from the Burnley striker. Gareth Barry will temporarily drop into defence alongside John Stones.
(4’) OVER! Kieran Trippier is given far too much time and space out wide on the right wing. The full-back cuts inside onto his left before flighting the ball into the area. His cross is meet by Sam Vokes but the big Welsh centre forward can only direct his looping header over the crossbar.
(2’) SHOT! Barkley has been in the thick of the action so far this afternoon. On this occasion he picks up the ball just inside the Burnley half and drives towards goal. The England international gets a shot away but badly drags it wide.
(1’) First tackle of the day and it is a bad one from Ross Barkley on Ashley Barnes. The Everton midfielder is lucky not to be cautioned for that late challenge. Probably only escaped a booking as it was inside the first 30 seconds of the match.
(1’) We are underway here at Goodison Park which is beautifully bathed in sunlight. The playing surface looks magnificent and should suit both teams that always look to get the ball down and play their football. Burnley kick us off! Both teams are in their traditional colours.
The player's are out on the pitch and the atmosphere is building nicely. Kick off is just a couple of minutes away now...
On the other hand Burnley will feel a little hard done by that they didn't get at least a point from their game against in-form Arsenal. Goalscoring has been a problem for the Lancashire team. The Clarets have failed to find the net since George Boyd's winner against Manchester City. It is an issue that Sam Vokes, Danny Ings and Ashley Barnes in particular will need to address urgently.
Roberto Martinez's side are in reasonable form and will be looking to finish the season strongly despite not having a great deal to play for. They have won three of their last five matches and played well in spells last time out away against Swansea. Evertonians will be expecting three points today but will be wary of a Burnley side who are fighting for their lives.
Leon Osman misses out with a groin injury but the good news for the Toffees is that Romelu Lukaku returns to the squad after four weeks out with a hamstring problem but has to settle for a place amongst the substitutes. As for the Clarets it is yet another unchanged team for Sean Dyche. Burnley midfielder Ross Wallace comes back into the matchday 18 after recovering from a knee injury.
BURNLEY SUBS: Gilks, Wallace, Kightly, Taylor, Jutkiewicz, Ward and Keane.
EVERTON SUBS: Joel, McGeady, Lukaku, Naismith, Besic, Garbutt and Alcaraz.
BURNLEY (4-4-2): Heaton; Trippier, Duff, Shackell (c), Mee; Boyd, Arfield, Jones, Barnes; Vokes, Ings.
EVERTON (4-1-4-1): Howard; Coleman, Stones, Jagielka (c), Baines; Barry; Lennon, McCarthy, Barkley, Mirallas; Kone.
The lineups are in and these are two of the most predictable teams in terms of team selection in the division...

(90’) We are now into the first of three additional minutes at the end of this game.

(90’) Alderweireld is stretchered off and looking quite immobile as he goes - very worrying scenes. The game continues, with the Saints now down a man and a goal.

(52’) Diouf fires his header just over from the corner, hanging near the far post and leaning back just slightly to get his head onto it!
(51’) Stoke battle well to win the ball in their own box and break quickly. Arnautovic breaks away from Fonte and squares it to the other side, where N'Zonzi wins a corner.

Join us in 15 for the second half!

(25’) It's well-worked from the corner and winds up on the head of Shawcross, who glances a header towards the far post and watches the ball drift wide.
