(76’) Hazard dribbles to the edge of the box once again, before being robbed of the ball as he looked to line up an angle from which to shoot! Only the Belgian and Drogba are getting forward with any regularity, with Matic, Ramires and Zouma sitting very deep indeed. Mourinho is determined to see this result out.
(74’) Hazard is picked out on the edge of the 18-yard box, but can only sweep a tame effort into the gloves of De Gea! The Spain international had all of the time in the world to get down to his right to make that save. Chelsea are happy to take their time with throw ins now, let it be noted.
(73’) Van Gaal has shuffled his pack, with Di Maria and Januzaj adding a bit more creativity and unpredictability into the Man United forward line. Courtois takes a long kick, which is nodded down to Hazard by Ramires. The Belgium international continues to link together everything that has been good for Chelsea this evening.
(71’) Good block from Cahill! Falcao is picked out on the penalty spot, but the former Bolton defender steps across his man brilliantly to deny a goal-bound strike! The rebounding ball falls to Fellaini, who is caught in an offside position.
--- 70’ Substitution A. Januzaj enters play, replacing Mata. ---
--- 70’ Substitution A. Young is done for the day. Á. di María is his replacement. ---
(69’) Chelsea remain content for their opponents to see all of the ball, but Courtois remains very well protected, with Man United only working the odd overload on either flank. Valencia clips a cross into the box from the right flank, but Ivanovic heads away confidently.
--- 67’ Substitution Oscar is done for the day. Ramires is his replacement. ---
(67’) Just wide from Falcao! The former Monaco lashes a powerful strike just wide of the right-hand post, with the blue portion of Stamford Bridge rather concerned! Ramires does indeed come into the fray, on the right-hand side of midfield, with the booked Oscar withdrawn.
(65’) Man United have settled back into their rhythm, with an equaliser looking to be back on the cards after a couple of scares. Ramires is being readied on the sideline, with the introduction of the Brazilian sure to show that Mourinho is tightening up.
--- 63’ Yellow card Oscar receives a yellow card. ---
(63’) Just wide from Rooney! The Man United captain is found on the edge of the box after a cushioned pass from Fellaini, but his eventual shot is deflected wide of the target! The resulting corner is whipped in by Mata, but loops embarrassingly over the penalty area and into Chelsea's possession.
(61’) McNair sees a shot saved! The defender shoots from about 25 yards out once again, with a whole host of bodies unsighting Courtois slightly! The rebound is claimed by the visitors, with Shaw racing down the left flank to the byline, but the Englishman's cut back is sent spiralling over the bar by Mata!
(60’) Man United are still in this game as we reach the hour mark, but Van Gaal just might have to make a few changes. The presences of Matic and Zouma in defensive midfield are limiting the amount of impact Fellaini can make in the air, with Falcao getting no service at all. Shaw whips in a cross from the left, but Zouma clears.
(58’) Mata takes the free kick short, sending the ball into the path of Rooney, who sweeps a shot into a ruck of bodies. Courtois continues to be a spectator in this game, with good quality chances proving to be rather elusive. The majority of this contest is playing out in midfield.
--- 57’ Yellow card B. Ivanović gets yellow. ---
(57’) Mike Dean goes to his pocket once again, this time booking Ivanovic for tugging on the shirt of Shaw as the left-back looked to overlap down the left flank. This free kick is in a great position for a cross to be delivered, with Mata and Young standing over it.
(55’) Two huge chances for Chelsea! Drogba is set away after another mistake in the visiting midfield, with the hosts' striker seeing a deflected effort loop over De Gea and into the box! Hazard follows up, but the goalscorer can only divert a hurried effort onto the crossbar!
--- 54’ Yellow card D. Drogba goes into the referee's book. ---
(53’) Drogba picks up a yellow card for a late tackle on McNair, with that being the experienced striker's only real contribution to proceedings this evening. Despite everything he has done for the club in the past, it is as though Chelsea are playing with 10 men at the moment.
(52’) Man United are labouring while moving the ball from flank to flank, with the absence of Carrick fairly obvious. Chelsea break down the left-hand side, but Smalling comes out well to close down Hazard and concede a corner, which eventually comes to nothing.
(50’) Chelsea have started with a nice spell of possession, with the home fans responding to their side looking slightly more comfortable. Man United have only managed to test Courtois on one occasion since the opening minute, with Falcao failing to produce any kind of magic on a rare start.
(48’) Zouma sees a shot charged down on the edge of the box, as Chelsea look to start the second half in bright fashion. Neither coach has opted to make any changes, though Mourinho's options are slightly thinner on the ground than his adversary's.
(46’) We are underway in the second half at Stamford Bridge! The Blues have a narrow advantage with 45 minutes to play, which would see the hosts go 10 points clear at the top of the Premier League.
HALF TIME! The two sides go in at the break with Hazard's goal the difference between them, in what has been a gritty performance from Chelsea thus far. Mourinho's men are sitting deep and closing down angles, allowing Man United to have plenty of the ball but not permitting them any space to do anything with it. Be sure to rejoin us for the second half!
(45’) Good stop from Courtois! Falcao is denied at close range by the former Atletico goalkeeper, pushing the ball behind for a corner, before the Belgium international claims the resulting set piece too.
(44’) Only a few minutes remain of the first half, with Chelsea happy to sit back and maintain their one-goal advantage. This hasn't been pretty from the hosts, with only Hazard looking like making a real difference throughout, but it is all Mourinho's men need to do in order to keep edging towards the title.
(42’) Stamford Bridge certainly has less nervousness in the air now, with the home supporters beginning to make some more noise. Man United are still seeing the majority of the ball, but Van Gaal's side just aren't moving it quickly enough to ask any questions of the Chelsea back four.
(40’) Tempers flare up slightly at Stamford Bridge! Falcao throws himself into a physical tackle on Terry, perhaps due to the treatment he received minutes earlier from the Englishman, before the two tangle on the turf. Azpilicueta separates the two, who are both asked to calm down.
--- 38’ Assist Oscar provided the assist. ---
--- 38’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! HAZARD OPENS THE SCORING FOR CHELSEA! The hosts manage to win the ball back on the halfway line, before Oscar flicks a pass into the path of the Belgium international. He scampers into the penalty area, before slotting a finish through the legs of De Gea and into the back of the net! Falcao is claiming that he was pushed over by Terry in the buildup, however. ---
(37’) Less than 10 minutes remain in the first half, with Man United perhaps slightly fortunate to still have 11 men on the field after that error in judgement from De Gea. The away side continue to retain possession, but much of it is inside their own half, with Chelsea unwilling to come out and engage too high.
(35’) Chelsea manage to break down the right-hand side, before a looping crossfield ball in search of Hazard is elbowed clear of the danger zone by De Gea. The Man United goalkeeper might have been just out of his box there, but a presence of another defender obscured the linesman's view of the incident.
(34’) Young spreads play wide to the overlapping Shaw, before the former Southampton man gives Herrera the ball. Fabregas attempts to close down his compatriot, but is penalised for being a little too rough. Young delivers the dead ball, but it fails to even get over the first man.
(32’) The opening half an hour couldn't have gone much better for the away side, unless Rooney's early strike actually had made its way into the back of the net. The visitors have had control of the game, despite failing to create many chances in the final third. Patient, probing possession is the order of the day.
(30’) Falcao gives away a free kick for a stupid push on Hazard, allowing for Chelsea to try their luck from a 30-yard dead-ball situation. Drogba can merely thump the ball directly into the wall, with the former Galatasaray striker not having the best evening thus far.
(28’) Falcao is almost presented with a chance merely eight yards from goal, but the Colombia international sees the ball nodded away from him at a vital time. Chelsea immediately try and counter, but Smalling is on hand to hook away a clearance. The hosts keep the move alive and earn themselves a corner, but De Gea punches the delivery away, before Hazard sees a shot blocked.
(26’) Valencia drives down the right, before feeding Mata, but the former Chelsea midfielder can only pull a ball back to the edge of the box to find a blue shirt. The home side attempt to piece together an attack, but quickly lose possession. Man United are looking after the ball far better than their opponents.
(24’) A poor pass from Herrera is picked up by Hazard, before the Belgian attempts to exchange a one-two with Fabregas! The former Lille wide man's touch escapes him, however, with De Gea able to mop up the scraps. The Chelsea duo continue to look like the hosts' sole goalscoring threat.
(22’) Drogba tries to lift a first-time ball over the top for Oscar to chase, but Shaw does well to intercept ahead of the Brazilian midfielder. The opening minutes have been all Man United, with the Red Devils forcing the league leaders onto the back foot. Chances have been at a premium, mind.
(20’) Chelsea have had a couple of brief forays forward, but Fabregas and Hazard look to be their main outlets. Drogba has thus far been unable to contribute while leading the line, but the experienced striker has had the knack of netting important goals during his Blues career.
(18’) Van Gaal's men continue to move the ball the better of the two sides, with their confidence evident. That said, Smalling and McNair aren't the neatest in possession at centre-back. A cross is whipped in by Shaw on the left-hand side, but the Chelsea-supporting full-back sees his delivery blocked.
(16’) Matic releases Drogba down the left-hand side, with Hazard making a good run into the channel ahead of his teammate. The former Ivory Coast international, however, is too lazy in his execution and stabs a tame pass within reach of Valencia. Stamford Bridge groans.
(14’) Just wide from McNair! The young defender drives past two challenges in midfield, before unleashing a long-range effort that deflects off Terry and wide of the target. Mata whips in the corner, but Fellaini can't get his head on it despite outclimbing his marker.
(12’) Herrera spreads play out to the left-hand side, before receiving the ball back from the flank and trying his luck from range! The former Athletic Club midfielder fires way wide and immediately apologises to his teammates for his poor decision to shoot.
(10’) Man United are continuing to keep the ball well, with their fans making plenty of noise. Given their form heading into this contest, Van Gaal would have expected to start the game in this manner. Mourinho's inclusion of Zouma in midfield appears to have been a smart move.
(8’) Hazard is picked out on the left-hand side, before the Belgium international stabs a pass towards the byline for Fabregas! The Spanish midfielder forces a save from De Gea at his near post, with the resulting corner being headed some way over the crossbar by Drogba.
(6’) Van Gaal will be fairly pleased with his side's start here! Terry is forced to hack a hurried clearance away at the back post, with the away outfit seeing plenty of the ball early on. Given their injuries, there is a feeling that this contest might be one that Mourinho simply doesn't want to lose.
(4’) Just wide from Rooney! The England international curls the ball just beyond the left-hand post, with half of the stadium thinking that his effort had struck the post and nestled in the back of the net! De Gea even turns to the United away supporters and celebrates!
(3’) Man United are prepared to push plenty of red shirts forward to press, with Fellaini essentially playing as a secondary striker alongside Falcao. Rooney will look to provide the drive from central midfield, with Herrera having to play a more withdrawn role.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at Stamford Bridge! The Blues are looking for a win that would all but seal the Premier League title, while Man United are hoping to cement themselves in third place come the end of the season.
Man United substitutes: Rafael, Di Maria, Januzaj, Van Persie, Valdes, Blackett, Pereira.
Man United starting line-up (4-5-1): De Gea; Valencia, Smalling, McNair, Shaw; Mata, Herrera, Rooney, Fellaini, Young; Falcao.
Chelsea substitutes: Cech, Filipe Luis, Ramires, Mikel, Willian, Cuadrado, Solanke.
Chelsea starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Ivanovic, Cahill, Terry, Azpilicueta; Zouma, Matic; Oscar, Fabregas, Hazard; Drogba.
TEAM NEWS: Luke Shaw comes into the back four, with Daley Blind suspensded for the visitors. Jonny Evans also sits out due to a ban, with Phil Jones picking up a recent injury, meaning that Chris Smalling is partnered by Paddy McNair in central defence. Michael Carrick is out, meaning that Wayne Rooney will be dropped into midfield as a case of needs must, meaning that Radamel Falcao gets a rare start up top. Ashley Young and Juan Mata retain their places out wide, with Angel di Maria continuing to warm the bench. Robin van Persie is among the substitutes.
TEAM NEWS: Both Loic Remy and Diego Costa miss out through injury for the home side, with Didier Drogba starting his second game in succession. Oscar is preferred to Willian on the right-hand side of midfield, with Kurt Zouma slotted into defensive midfield to partner Nemanja Matic. Cesc Fabregas is given more freedom in behind the striker as a result. Ramires drops to the bench for the hosts, with Dominic Salanke taking a seat on the bench as a striking option.
I'm Simon Harrison and I will be keeping you up to date with all of the action, as the Blues look to tighten their grip on the Premier League title even further. Chelsea did struggle, however, to break down a well-drilled QPR outfit last time out, with Man United in much better form than Chris Ramsey's side. Four consecutive wins have put Van Gaal's men in with a solid chance of finishing just below the eventual title winners in the league table - an unthinkable feat at the start of the season.
Hello and welcome to this evening's late Premier League kick off, as Manchester United travel to the capital to face Jose Mourinho's Chelsea! The hosts have the chance to move 10 points clear of second-placed Arsenal with a win at Stamford Bridge, while the Red Devils will be looking to extend their lead over rivals Manchester City to a temporary seven points. If Louis van Gaal's side can pull a result out of the bag, the away side would move into second for the time being.

My name is Ben Cullimore and it's been an absolute pleasure describing all of the action to you today. Until next time, goodbye.
As a result of the victory, City stay in fourth place but are now just one point behind Manchester United heading into next weekend's game at home to Aston Villa. As for West Ham, they remain in danger of dropping into the bottom half of the table as they face fellow Londoners Queens Park Rangers in six days' time.
In the end, it was an incredibly comfortable afternoon for City, who deservedly picked up three much-needed points to keep alive their hopes of finishing in front of bitter rivals Manchester United come the end of May. The reigning champions dominated from the start and never looked as if they were in any danger of losing their lead after Collins put them ahead with a comical own goal after just 18 minutes. From then onwards, it was plain sailing, with the Hammers' strikers struggling to find a way past the hosts' defence on the rare occasions that they were able to push forward.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 WEST HAM UNITED
(90’) It's all City at the moment as they boss possession in the West Ham half of the pitch but, unsuprisingly, they seem content to keep the ball as they look to hold on to their comfortable two-goal lead.
--- 90’ +7 Yellow card Noble is brought down by Toure, and West Ham are awarded a free kick near the halfway line as a result. They take the set-piece quickly but lose the ball almost immediately, allowing Kolarov to break forward before being clipped from behind by Downing, resulting in a yellow card for the winger. ---
(90’) Toure bursts through the centre of the West Ham midfielder, muscling his way past several players before sending a great pass into the feet of Dzeko. The substitute then breaks forward towards the edge of the penalty area before firing a fierce strike towards goal, but it's sent straight at Adrian, who is easily able to deal with the shot.
(90’) West Ham scream for a penalty! The visitors earn themselves a free kick near the halfway line, which is whipped into the heart of the box, where it finds Reid. The defender chests the ball down before seemingly being bundled over from behind by Fernandinho, but the referee shakes his head and waves play on.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution And now City have made their final substitution of the afternoon, with Dzeko coming on to replace Aguero for the final eight minutes. ---
(90’) Great chance for Toure! A West Ham attack breaks down, allowing Navas to sprint forward before comfortably beating Jenkinson on the edge of the penalty area. He then tees up Aguero, who quickly plays the ball into the feet of the Ivorian, but the midfielder ends up sending his shot just over the top of the crossbar.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be nine minutes of added time.
(89’) A poor pass from Navas allows Nolan to pick up possession and charge towards the edge of the penalty area. He does well to get forward before trying to beat Hart, but the goalkeeper does well to make himself big and save the midfielder's effort.
--- 88’ Substitution City have decided to make their second change of the afternoon, with Lampard making way for Fernandinho. ---
(88’) Excellent play by Valencia! The Ecuadorian twists and turns on the left wing, comfortably beating both Demichelis and Fernando before trying to curl a shot towards the far post, but, off balance, he ends up missing the goal by a few yards.
(87’) Once again, a wonderful pass finds its way through the West Ham defence and into the path of Aguero. This time the Argentine is onside but the Spaniard's through-ball is slightly overhit and can only find Adrian, who rushes out quickly to deal with the danger.
(86’) Nasri skips past two City players before teeing up Aguero with a lovely through-ball, but, not for the first time this afternoon, the Argentine's run is slightly mistimed and the linesman's flag is immediately raised just as the striker is getting ready to shoot.
(84’) City keep the attack alive and Navas immediately sprints down the right wing before cutting the ball back to Toure. In an almost identical position to a few moments ago, the Ivorian unleashes a shot towards the near post, but, under pressure from Reid and Collins, he ends up firing it well wide of its intended target.
(83’) Toure breaks into the right-hand side of the West Ham penalty area and is left in acres of space, allowing him to take all the time in the world before firing a shot towards goal, but, once again, it's blocked well by Reid at the vital moment.
(82’) West Ham exchange a series of quick passes just outside of the City half of the pitch before Jenkinson is seemingly tripped over by Nasri near the byline, but the referee judges that the defender went down far too easily and instead awards the hosts with a throw-in.
(80’) And now it's Downing who's able to put the City defence under pressure after good play from Jarvis on the left-hand side of the box, but the West Ham winger's low strike is blocked well by Mangala before it's able to trouble Hart.
(79’) Kouyate is able to muscle his way past two City players before attempting to curl a cross towards the back post, but it's completely mishit and ends up sailing out of play for a goal kick.
(77’) Toure charges forward before teeing up Navas on the right flank, and the Spaniard then whips a low cross into the middle of the West Ham penalty area. It meets Lampard, who, with his back to goal, quickly cuts the ball back to the Ivorian, but the latter's first-time shot is deflected away from goal before being collected by Adrian.
--- 75’ Substitution After almost 10 minutes down on the floor, Silva is eventually stretchered off to thunderous applause from both sets of fans, and Nasri comes on to take his place for the final quarter-of-an-hour. ---
(73’) It looks as if Nasri, who is warming up on the sideline, is going to replace Silva once he's able to safely make his way off the pitch.
(71’) It's now been over five minutes since Silva went down, and the Spaniard is still on the floor being looked at by the City medical staff, who, understandably, don't want to rush him off the pitch and risk any further damage.
(69’) Silva seems to be in serious discomfort after that clash with Kouyate, and he's still on the floor receiving medical treatment near the halfway line. It looks as if his game might be over as the stretcher is brought out onto the pitch.
--- 67’ Yellow card Kouyate skips past Silva before smashing the Spaniard in the cheekbone with a flailing arm, and the referee immediately brings the game to a stop to show the Senegalese midfielder a yellow card. ---
--- 66’ Substitution And the second is Jarvis, who takes the place of Song. ---
--- 66’ Substitution West Ham have decided to make a double substitution as they look to find a way back into the game. The first player to come on is Nolan, who replaces Cole. ---
(64’) Valencia picks up the ball in the middle of the pitch and immediately breaks away on a quick counter attack. He has Cole on one side and Downing on the other but ends up holding onto possession for far too long and is eventually dispossessed before he's able to unleash a pass.
(63’) Aguero wins the ball back and sets up Toure, who spins near the halfway line before slotting a pass through the fragmented West Ham defence and into the path of the Argentine. It almost finds the striker but his run was slightly mistimed, resulting in the linesman's flag being immediately raised.
(62’) City quickly regain possession and work the ball back to Silva, who skips past Downing before firing a shot towards the top left-hand corner of the goal that is blocked well by Jenkinson.
(61’) Silva is easily able to break into the West Ham penalty area before earning his side their sixth corner of the game. It's curled towards the near post but once again Collins is there to deal with the danger.
(60’) West Ham are finally able to push forward on an attack down the right flank before Jenkinson curls a dangerous cross towards the back post, but every available player is in an offside position and the linesman's flag is immediately raised.
--- 58’ Yellow card Silva and Reid battle for the ball after a heavy touch from the Spaniard, and a flailing arm from the midfielder ends up striking the defender in the face, resulting in a yellow card for the City man. ---
(57’) It's all City at the moment as they put West Ham under an incredible amount of pressure in and around their own penalty area. If it continues like this, the hosts could well find the back of the net once again very soon.
(55’) Lovely play by City! Navas breaks down the right flank before sending a dangerous low cross into the penalty area. It finds the feet of Aguero, who then spins quickly before firing a shot towards goal, but it's blocked well by Reid.
(53’) Toure powers into the right-hand side of the West Ham penalty area before earning his side a corner. It's flung into the heart of the box and almost finds Mangala, but Collins does well to meet it first before clearing the danger with a strong header.
(51’) After a few moments on the sideline, Aguero gingerly makes his way back onto the pitch to rejoin the action. Dzeko has been summoned to warm up, however, just in case the Argentine is unable to continue.
(50’) Aguero looks to have picked up a nasty looking injury after clashing with Jenkinson, and the Argentine seems to be struggling as he receives medical treatment near the byline as the corner is taken.
(49’) Great chance for Aguero! Toure and the Argentine play a lovely one-two before the latter breaks into the left-hand side of the penalty area and looks set to shoot, but Jenkinson flies into the striker and dispossesses with with a wonderfully-timed tackle at the vital moment.
(47’) Lampard and Silva link up quickly just outside of the West Ham penalty before the latter sets up Navas on the right flank. The Spaniard then tries to find Aguero with a low cross but it's cut out by Reid before it can meet the Argentine in front of goal.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
It's been an incredibly easy opening 45 minutes for City, who enter the half-time break with a well-deserved two-goal lead and in complete control of the game. West Ham have offered very little at either end of the pitch, with Collins' woeful own-goal summing up the Hammers' overall first half performance. Cole and Valencia have been largely spectators so far, whilst Aguero, Silva and Navas have been running riot in the final third of the pitch, causing Adrian a plethora of problems.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 WEST HAM UNITED
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be one minute of added time.
(44’) Toure picks up the ball near the halfway line and sends an excellent lofted pass over to Aguero on the right flank. The Argentine collects it well before trying to play a one-two with the Ivorian, but Noble is just about able to get in the way to cut out the danger on the edge of the penalty area.
(42’) After a lengthy period of City dominance, West Ham are finally able to push forward once again, but they quickly find themselves crowded out by the hosts' well-organised defence, denying them opportunity to penetrate the penalty area.
(40’) City come back once again, with Lampard twisting and turning on the right-hand side of the penalty area before chipping a cross towards the back post. It's overhit, however, and fails to find Aguero before bouncing harmlessly out of play on the opposite flank.
(38’) Another poor mistake from West Ham almost results in a third goal for City. This time it's Song who loses possession, allowing Kolarov to break away down the left wing before sending a dangerous cross into the heart of the penalty area. It's only half dealt with by Collins but, after a few nervy moments, the visitors are finally able to thump the ball away from danger and towards the halfway line.
--- 36’ Assist Assist by Jesús Navas. ---
--- 36’ Goal! GOAL! It's 2-0! Downing loses possession midway inside the City half of the pitch on the right flank, allowing the hosts to break away on an extremely quick counter attack. Aguero sprints forward before sending the ball over to Navas, who immediately tees up the Argentine once again, and the striker is then calmly able to slot the ball past Adrian and into the back of the net. ---
--- 35’ Yellow card City keep the attacking move alive before Silva is eventually dispossessed by Song just outside of the box. The Cameroonian midfielder then darts forward before being cynically brought down from behind by Navas, who receives a yellow card as a result. ---
(34’) Great tackle by Jenkinson! City slowly make their way towards the edge of the West Ham penalty area before Silva tries to tee up Lampard with a deft through-ball, but the right-back is there to cut out the pass with a vital interception.
(32’) Aguero does well down the right flank, beating two West Ham players before chipping a deft cross into the heart of the visitors' penalty area. It finds the head of Silva just inside the box but, unsurprisingly, the little Spaniard's effort is poorly struck and ends up flying well wide of the goal.
(30’) Valencia finds himself in acres of space in the middle of the pitch, allowing him to sprint forward before unleashing a 25-yard strike. It's well hit but is saved comfortably by Hart.
(29’) Terrible mistake by Demichelis! The defender falls asleep with the ball at his feet, allowing Valencia to dispossess him before quickly teeing up Cole. The striker charges towards the edge of the City penalty area before firing a shot towards goal, but Hart does well to dart out and save the strike with a strong stop.
(27’) Fantastic block by Collins! A lofted pass forward from Fernando finds Navas on the right-hand side of the penalty area, and the Spaniard immediately fires a volleyed cross towards the edge of the six-yard box. It finds Silva, who takes a quick touch before unleashing a shot, but the Welsh defender jumps in front of the strike to stop it from troubling Adrian.
(26’) Silva twists and turns on the edge of the West Ham penalty area, looking as if he is going to shoot. He eventually decides to tee up Kolarov, who immediately fires a low cross towards Aguero, but it's cut out well by Jenkinson before it can meet the Argentine striker.
(25’) West Ham patiently work their way down the right flank before Downing curls a dangerous cross into the penalty area, but both Cole and Valencia are at least six feet offside and, as a result, both of them leave the attempted pass to bounce out of play for a goal kick.
(23’) The ball rolls out for a corner, which is then flung towards the back post. It meets the head of Cole, but the striker's headed effort is poor and is comfortably dealt with by Hart.
(22’) An awful pass from Zabaleta gifts the ball to Kouyate, who immediately charges into the City half of the pitch. He almost meets the edge of the penalty area but is stopped at the vital moment by Fernando, who dispossesses the Senegalese midfielder with an excellent sliding tackle.
(20’) West Ham are finally able to string together a series of passes inside the City half of the pitch, but the move is brought to a disappointing end by Cresswell, who ends up carelessly straying offside down the left wing.
--- 18’ Goal! GOAL! City have taken the lead! A poor goal kick from Adrian can only find Navas, who out-muscles Cresswell before darting down the right flank and curling a low cross into the penalty area. It can only find Collins, but the defender ends up spooning the ball up into the air, over the head of the West Ham goalkeeper and into the back of the net to give the hosts a well-deserved one-goal lead. ---
(17’) The resulting set-piece bounces around the West Ham penalty area before falling at the feet of Aguero, but the Argentine ends up firing his half-volleyed strike well over the top of the crossbar.
(16’) What a strike by Kolarov! The Serbian steps up and fires an excellent shot from the resulting set-piece that takes a slight deflection off the wall to help it sail just past the near post and out for a corner.
(15’) Zabaleta and Lampard attempt to play a quick one-two just outside of the West Ham penalty area but the latter is brought crashing to the ground by Reid, resulting in a free kick for City in an incredibly dangerous position.
(14’) West Ham are finally able to fight their way out of their own half of the pitch, and they earn themselves a corner on the left flank as a result. They play it short before working the ball over to Song, who tries to chip a deft pass over the top of the City defence and into the path of Cole, but it's slightly overhit and is easily cut out by Hart.
(12’) And now it's Song that loses possession in a dangerous position, and Navas immediately charges into the right-hand side of the penalty area before cutting the ball back to Aguero, who quickly spins and fires a low shot that flies through the legs of Collins before being stopped well by Adrian.
(11’) Valencia is caught in possession deep inside the West Ham half of the pitch, allowing the hosts to quickly play the ball across to Silva, who is completely unmarked 25 yards away from goal. He takes a quick touch before firing a great shot that beats Adrian but ends up flying over the top of the crossbar.
(10’) A terrible cross-field pass from Cresswell gifts possession to Aguero, who immediately breaks forward towards the edge of the West Ham penalty area. The Argentine takes far too long on the ball, however, and ends up running into a cul-de-sac of dark shirts, bringing a promising attacking move to a disappointing end.

As for Sunderland, they are still in danger of dropping into the relegation zone and head to North London knowing that just one point is all that is needed for them to pull off a second consecutive great escape. They have looked incredibly impressive in recent weeks as well, with Dick Advocaat leading the determined Black Cats on a four-game unbeaten run, with just one of their last six league games ending in defeat. As a result, three points separate themselves and 18th-place Hull City, whilst fierce rivals Newcastle United, who sit precariously close to the bottom three in 17th, are just one point behind with one game remaining.
With just two games of the season left to play, both sides are battling hard as they aim to win two very different prizes. A disappointing defeat against Swansea City and an arguably lucky draw away to Manchester United dented their chances to pipping the reigning champions to second spot, but they will be able to finish as runners-up for the first time in a decade if they win their last two clashes and Southampton see off City at the Etihad on Sunday.

(44’) A very nervy moment for the visitors as Morgan tries to wait for a high ball to fall, though Ideye nearly slips in and steals it in the box! Morgan just about gets away with his hestitation!
(43’) Pearson can take heart in the fact that Ulloa's knockdowns for Nugent are causing serious problems for the home side but his side should be even here after that opportunity!
(41’) This is better from West Brom who are no longer pegged back in their own area, though they continue to give the ball away far too cheaply. (39’) Leicester are keeping up the pressure here but West Brom's defence is refusing to break. The home side have faded since their second goal, however, and Tony Pulis may just be glad to get them into halftime without conceding another.

(34’) Brunt is furious that the assistant has waved for a free-kick to the visitors after his foul on James. Leicester play the free-kick into the box, and it's cleared to De Laet before Albrighton's cross gets knocked out for a corner.
(32’) A few minutes ago, Schmeichel went over to the assistant referee to argue that Dawson was offside and interfering with his line of sight when Gardner scored his goal, but nothing comes of his argument.
(31’) After a couple of minutes of evaluation, Vardy is gingerly on his feet and looking like he's willing to try and play on.

--- 26’ Assist The assist came from B. Ideye. ---

(23’) The midfield battle has become crowded and hectic, but eventually Nugent wiggles free and fires off a shot that sails past the near post.

(15’) The corner is played to Ulloa around the near post but his flick towards net goes wide. Morrison soon after fouls Albrighton to give the visitors a free-kick.

(12’) Leicester are yet to impose themselves here with Brunt delivering a free-kick from deep in his own half to just outside of the visitors' box. It's knocked around before Berahino can intervene and earn his side possession.
(11’) Cambiasso is still arguing the goal with referee Atkinson but the decision is no doubt the correct one, with goal-line technology confirming the ruling.
(9’) As the 9th minute occurs, the crowd rings out applause for Jeff Astle, a West Brom legend whose new foundation was launched today in an effort to raise awareness about traumatic head injuries.

(2’) Vardy sneaks down the right side to get on the end of a loose ball near the box but places a poor cross, though he atones for his error moments later when he races back to his own box to win it back.

The teams are in the tunnel and about to walk onto the pitch. We'll have kick-off in just a few minutes!
Recent history between these two sides strongly favors the home team, who have won all of the last four fixtures. In fact, the Foxes have only won once in the last 21 attempts at the Hawthorns! The data suggests there will be goals, as the home side have conceded more goals at home than any other team this season, and the visitors have the joint-fewest number of clean sheets in the Premier League as well.
A fair few players will be missing in action today, with Foster injured and Mulumbu suspended for the home side and Upson, Hammond, and Bakayogo all out via injury for the visitors.
Leicester City (4-4-1-1): Schmeichel; Schlupp, Huth, Morgan, De Laet; Albrighton, Cambiasso, James, Vardy; Nugent; Ulloa.
West Brom (4-4-2): Myhill; Dawson, McAuley, Lescott, Brunt; Morrison, Fletcher, Yacob, Gardner; Ideye, Berahino.

They managed to put three in the net away at Tottenham but still lost before finally earning their first league win since January with a 2-1 victory over West Ham last matchday. They now have five goals scored and conceded in their last two matches - this one could be a thriller!
Let's start with the home side: Tony Pulis' men were given one of the shocks of the season when they were trounced 4-1 at home by QPR and they've now lost three of their last five. They're still some ways above the relegation zone, with a solid seven point gap and four teams between them and 18th place, but they'll certainly want the points today to not have to even consider that possibility.
Hello all and welcome to our live match coverage of West Brom vs Leicester City! It's 14th hosting 20th in the Premier League today in a match that will have massive implications for the relegation race!

(55’) Both sides beginning to play long, lofted balls forward towards their front men. Adam is finding it hard to get into the game in midfield now, as West Ham keep possession.

Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League encounter between West Ham United and Stoke City. I'm Lee Gormley and I'll be guiding you through all of the action from Upton Park.

FULL TIME: BURNLEY 0-1 ARSENAL. Aaron Ramsey's early goal is all that separates the side after 90 minutes, but it's a big three points for the Gunners who move to withing four points of Chelsea - though the Blues have two games in hand. It's also the first eight-match league winning streak for Arsene Wenger's side since the year of the Invincibles.

(84’) STAT ATTACK: Arsenal are the only Premier League side this season yet to lose a match against opponents in the bottom half of the table (W13, D3).

This should provide Burnley with plenty of confidence heading into the break.

(40’) There's been quite a stark contrast between the two halves of these opening 45 minutes. It started incredibly lively and Ramsey's goal looked to be the first of many to come, but slowly the pace has gone and the match has become quite cagey, which actually works in favour of the hosts.
(38’) Arsenal have completely taken control of the match, dominating possession and preventing Burnley from breaking out of their own half. They look very confident on the ball, and though they are taking a patient approach, they still do look to get the ball forward every chance they get.
(36’) The foul count is beginning to rise for Burnley and the home fans are none too happy. You have to wonder how much leeway Mike Dean is going to give the hosts here, as Mee commits another foul, getting his arm up into the face of Giroud, but escapes a second yellow. He can't afford to be so reckless or it could cost Burnley dearly.
(34’) Clever defending from Trippier! Giroud wins a free kick for his side, and while Ozil's initial delivery is cleared, Mertesacker hooks the follow-up back into the danger area. It bounces to Trippier in a dangerous area, but he calmly heads the ball back to his keeper to sniff out the chance.
(32’) STAT ATTACK: While they have played like a new team in recent weeks, Arsenal have the exact same record they did at this stage last season (W19, D6, L6).
(30’) The pace has slowed a bit now as the always hard-working Burnley midfield begin to close down gaps and eat up space in the middle of the park. It has been a very quiet period since the Cazorla free kick.
(28’) Meanwhile, that sequence for Burnley was far from ideal as half of their back line have now been booked. That is far from ideal against an Arsenal side who like to move the ball around quickly in attack, often forcing defenders to take risks to try and win back possession. This is definitely something to keep an eye on.

(23’) Barnes has looked more than up for the occasion in midfield, working hard to win every ball for his side. He stands his ground well and flicks a header on for Ings, before being taken out by Koscielny to win his side a free kick from just under 30-yards out.
(21’) STAT ATTACK: Burnley have picked up 13 points – exactly half of their season’s total – this campaign in matches against the top 10 teams in the Premier League, more than any of the bottom six teams they find themselves in a relegation fight with.
(19’) Arsenal manage a good period of pressure here, controlling possession in the final third. They get bodies forward, but an errant pass from Koscielny, intended for Ramsey, rolls out of play and Burnley can regain their composure here and settle things down.
(17’) Wasted opportunity! The free kick from Jones is smacked straight into the wall and up in the air. Plenty of bodies gather in the penalty area as the ball goes up in the air, but Ospina gets off his line to punch clear with great authority.
(16’) Clumsy challenge! A headed clearance sails towards the top of the Arsenal penalty area and Coquelin carelessly bundles into the back of Jones, who was facing away from goal. The hosts have a real opportunity to make something happen from this ensuing free kick.
(14’) Well what a start we've had in this match! The pace has been superb and both teams are showing plenty of intent to get forward and attack. Arsenal have struck first, but if the first 10 minutes has been any indication, there are more goals to come.

It deflects kindly into the path of Ozil, who is denied by a fine save by Heaton at the near post. (10’) STAT ATTACK: Arsenal have won seven consecutive Premier League matches for the first time since February to March of 2012. That run was eventually ended by a 2-1 defeat at QPR. They have not won eight league matches in a row since January to March of 2004, the season of the Invincibles.
(8’) Good defending by Mertesacker. The home side are now the ones in control, being urged forward by the home fans. Boyd makes himself a nuisance in the penalty area and gets into a good area, but Mertesacker is able to intervent and play the ball off the midfielder and behind for a goal kick.

(4’) Arsenal have started very positively, and you wouldn't have expected anything else with the form they are in. Alexis is looking very dangerous in attack, moving well off the ball and causing a few problems for the Burnley defence.
(2’) It took no more than 90 seconds for the first chance of the match! Alexis Sanchez wins a free kick for his side and then proceeds to take it. He gets good movement behind it and Heaton appears to over-commit to his right, but recovers to keep it out.

Arsenal are on a terrific run of form that has seen them fight their way into second place in the Premier League table and essentially secure their place in next season's Champions League. It may be too little, too late for a title push, trailing Chelsea by seven points, but the stark contrast in the form of the two teams should at least make things interesting in the season's final two months.
There is no lack of belief within this Burnley squad, and it’s hard to argue against them being the hardest working team in the Premier League. This is undeniably an important mix for a team fighting to remain in the top flight, but they still need a little something extra to push them over the edge. They were superb defensively against Tottenham last weekend, but Danny Ings missed two glorious chances in the first half and they were forced to settle for a draw. These are points they can’t afford to be dropping if they are to avoid the drop. They managed to shock Manchester City at this same venue a month ago – let’s see if they can do it again against the hottest team in the Premier League.

(85’) We're into the final five minutes, with nerves now bound to be setting in for both sides. This game has huge implications on both ends of the table and it appears that QPR are going to be able to hold out for a share of the spoils. Ramsey's men have battled and fought brilliantly.
--- 83’ Substitution B. Zamora is replaced with J. Hoilett. ---

The Canadian winger should be deployed out on the left, with Kranjcar perhaps being pushed into a more offensive midfield role as a result. Chelsea win themselves a corner, but Barton heads away at the near post.
(82’) Sandro takes his leave, possibly due to a combination of fatigue and that yellow card, with Henry moving into a more familiar central midfield role. Phillips unleashes a shot from 25 yards out, but it is easily blocked by Azpilicueta and bobbles behind for a corner. The set piece is brought down by Austin, who sees his first shot blocked by Cahill, before Courtois claims the second.
--- 81’ Substitution N. Kranjčar enters the game and replaces Sandro. ---

(80’) A corner is whipped in from the right-hand side by Fabregas, but Barton clears at his near post. The rebounding ball is picked up by hazard, who rifles a long-range effort way over the crossbar. Hill goes down in a heap after being accidentally trodden on by Cahill, while Mourinho replaces Willian with Cuadrado.
--- 78’ Yellow card Sandro receives a yellow card. ---
(78’) Phillips tries to control a ball into his midriff on the edge of the box, but the Scotland international is promptly dispossessed. The game is getting a bit stretched, with a few yellow cards on show due to required cynical challenges. Sandro commits the latest, with the former Spurs midfielder now needing to watch his step.
(76’) Willian scampers down the left-hand side, but the former Shakhtar man's cross is cleared by the head of Caulker. Chelsea are starting to dominate proceedings as we edge towards the final 10 minutes, but Green remains an avid spectator.
--- 75’ Yellow card B. Zamora goes into the referee's book. ---
(74’) Oscar sees a shot blocked on the edge of the hosts' penalty box by Sandro, with Mourinho's men trying to move the ball at pace from side to side in order to find a gap. Drogba is continuing to struggle against the physical presences of Onuoha and Caulker, with the QPR central defensive duo appearing to have the Chelsea veteran figured out.
(72’) Austin almost manages to get in behind enemy lines, but Cahill tracks his man well to ensure that the QPR striker can't add to his sizeable goal tally for the season. But for a couple of good saves from Courtois, Chelsea's back four haven't really been tested too often. Phillips has faded from the game in the last quarter of an hour, too.
(70’) The home fans continue to make plenty of noise, with this game still poised dangerously at 0-0. Courtois has been much the busier of the two goalkeepers, with Drogba really struggling to make anything happen up front for Chelsea. Mourinho hasn't really got much else available on the bench to change things, save for young forward Izzy Brown.
(68’) Willian spreads play out to Ivanovic, whose off-target shot is hooked away neatly by Onuoha. QPR continue to defend very well, despite Hazard being matched up against Hill in the second half. The Englishman is using all his vast experience to keep tabs on the former Lille winger.
(66’) Hazard drives inside from the right-hand side, before Caulker makes an interception ahead of Oscar. QPR counter attack, with Phillips jinking inside from the left, but Willian tracks back well to help Ivanovic. Ramsey's men are starting to get on top, before Sandro blasts a 30-yard effort high and wide.
(64’) Fantastic save from Courtois! Phillips is fed the ball from the right-hand side, before pivoting very smartly to give himself space to shoot! The Belgium international goalkeeper throws himself to his left to deny the QPR wide man, before the resulting corner comes to nothing.
(62’) Hazard shows a good change of pace to break down the left-hand side, before the Belgian chops onto his right foot and swings a cross beyond the far upright! Hill just eased Drogba out of the way as the former Ivory Coast international looked to challenge for the ball.
(61’) Less than half an hour remains for Chelsea to take maximum points, with the chasing title pack perhaps able to gain some confidence should Mourinho's men only come away with a point. The visitors are really struggling to piece together any meaningful passages of play, with Hazard fairly anonymous.

(59’) Just over from Hill! Ivanovic manages to bomb on down the right-hand side, before providing a cross which the QPR defender can only flick over his own crossbar. The first delivery is put behind for a second set piece, before the next flashing across the face of goal and to safety! That merely needed a touch!
(57’) Oscar finds Ivanovic breaking towards the edge of the penalty area, before the Serbian right-back clips a pass across the box which is so easily intercepted by Phillips. QPR then try to foray down the right as a result, but their attack quickly peters out. Chances are few and far between at Loftus Road.

(55’) Onuoha tries to clip a looping delivery into the Chelsea box, but the huge frame of Courtois is present to collect. Oscar is getting ready to come into the fray for the Blues, with the visitors clearly needing a bit of outside inspiration to act as a catalyst.
(53’) Drogba blasts way over! Ramires tries to scamper down the left-hand side, before being robbed of the ball, but the rebounding ball is thumped into the stand behind Green's goal. Mourinho will be a little concerned, as his offensive options just haven't offered a great deal this afternoon.
(51’) Almost a rare goal for Hill! The Englishman manages to turn an effort goalwards after being found at the back post, but Courtois is able to pounce upon it! Henry spread a ball out wide, but Hill's curling effort was comfortable within the goalkeeper's grasp. Moments later, Barton blasts way wide from 25 yards out.
(49’) Just wide from Phillips! The Scotland international cuts inside onto his left foot, before curling a low delivery just beyond the far post! Zamora wasn't quite close enough to throw himself at the ball, but that was a great opportunity for the hosts to try and take the lead!

(46’) We are underway in the second half at Loftus Road, with Chelsea needing to find a bit of inspiration if they are to come away this afternoon with more than a point. QPR, meanwhile, will be hoping for more of the same, after competing well in central midfield.
HALF TIME! The two sides go in level at the interval, despite a couple of late chances for Austin and Fabregas! Courtois has been the busier of the two goalkeepers, with QPR doing well to frustrate the visitors in the centre of the park. Drogba has struggled as a lone striker, with Ramsey's men certainly thinking that they can snatch at least a share of the spoils at the moment. Be sure to rejoin us in 10 minutes!
(45’) Big chance for Fabregas! Ivanovic whips in a cross from the right-hand side, which Drogba fails to make contact with, before the ball bounces through to the former Barcelona midfielder. He attempts to loop a header over the stationary Green, but the Spaniard's effort spirals some way over the crossbar!
(44’) Decent stop from Courtois! Austin lets fly from 25 yards out, with the Belgian goalkeeper sprawling to his right to push the ball away from danger! It was at a comfortable height, but that attempt from the Englishman was really travelling!
(43’) Austin is knocked to the floor accidentally by Ivanovic, with the former Burnley man needing to be a little bit stronger there, but the referee blows for a free kick. Mourinho and Farias are straight off their bench in frustration, with the away fans incensed too.
(41’) We're into the final five minutes of what has been a competitive first half in the capital city. It has been fairly scrappy and low on quality, with the outcome of this contest certainly proving to be very hard to call. Mourinho might want to re-think his system at the break, with QPR nullifying his current set-up well.
(39’) QPR whip in a second corner delivery in quick succession, with Sandro nodding an effort clear of the crossbar, before claiming that Ramires got a touch to deflect it to safety. The home side are pressing forward in the late stages of the half, before Terry and Austin have a little tussle off the ball. The former England international puts his arm across his adversary, who promptly dumps the Chelsea defender on the floor with a push! Loftus Road enjoyed that.

Austin is nearly picked out by a very early pass forward, but again Courtois is able to react quickest and make a clearance on the periphery of his box.

The former Galatasaray striker and Ivanovic have a little argument on the field, after the Chelsea striker failed to show for a throw in.
