Take your pick - there were about three players that could have latched onto that ball, and Smalling was the lucky one, heading home! ---
(72’) Wayne Rooney seems to be enjoying playing in his favoured position leading the United line. That last assist for Mata was his 90th in the English top flight for his career.
(71’) The noise inside Old Trafford is ear splitting. The fans are loving this, and such an accomplished performance against the defending champions is as big a sign as any that the Van Gaal master plan is beginning to take shape. Since that loss to Arsenal in the FA Cup, the Red Devils have found a winning formula.
(69’) City's task goes from entirely possible to monumental. Pellegrini looks dumbfounded on the touchline, with his team in the midst of throwing this game away. They started so dangerously - what happened?
--- 67’ Assist W. Rooney gave the assist. ---
--- 67’ Goal! MATA MAKES IT THREE! Fellaini drags Demichelis out of position, and the ball is worked to Rooney. He takes it on the turn in a flash, and before Toure can close him down, he slides a cute ball in for Mata behind the defence. The Spaniard advances on Hart and guides a neat finish home! ---
(66’) There's not a lot happening in terms of chances, but the tension has not dissipated from this match one bit. The next goal will be absolutely vital. A United strike will probably spell the end for City, but a goal from the visitors will absolutely throw everything back into the fire.
(64’) Milner departs with a limp after suffering an injury from a challenge, although he was probably set to make his exit anyway, with Nasri already warming up on the touchline for a while.
--- 63’ Substitution S. Nasri comes on for J. Milner. ---
(63’) City have held onto possession for the past few minutes but are lacking the cutting edge that defined their start to this game. Credit to Van Gaal and the United defence for cutting out the once-porous gaps that were spawning behind their full-backs.
(61’) Assured defending from Chris Smalling, who feels the musky breath of Aguero on his neck, and takes no chances from Milner's cross, clearing it away from goal. Just over an hour gone in the Manchester derby and still no telling who will emerge with the spoils from this one, even with the hosts in the lead.
(59’) THE OFFSIDE FLAG IS UP! Mata shapes up a wonderful inswinging cross from the right flank and United have three players suddenly free of their markers. Young is the man to make the initial header, but the flag is up not long after that as at least two of those players were beyond the last defender.
(57’) Manchester City are winless in the last 86 Premier League games where they've trailed at the interval. By contrast, Manchester United have never lost a league game at Old Trafford when they've led at the break.
(55’) Fellaini and Demichelis both rise for a high ball and the defender comes off worse for wear after a clear yet unintentional forearm shiver from the Belgian. The City man is down on the deck in apparent pain, but rises to his feet almost instantly to confront Clattenburg. That destroyed the illusion of his agony, and the referee doesn't think a card for Fellaini is warranted.
(53’) MADNESS IN THE BOX BUT CITY SURVIVE! Rooney curls a lovely free-kick to the top corner but Hart parries. However, his save keeps the ball in play and from there, it's pinball on steroids in the area. Young, Mata and Herrera all have swings at the ball, with some desperate blocks preventing the ball, somehow, from reaching the target! That was an extraordinary sequence!
(51’) Here's a stunning little tidbit for you - Manchester City have not led a Premier League game at half-time since boxing day, when there were 3-0 up against West Bromwich Albion. That, as much as anything, tells you how badly the Citizens have fallen off in the new year.
(49’) Navas hangs a cross into the area that finds Aguero free for a moment, but the Argentine can't get a crucial second touch on the ball. City keep it alive and Silva attempts to tee up Toure for the piledriver, but his layoff doesn't even travel the two or three yards it needs to reach the Cote d'Ivoire midfielder.
(47’) One change to round up from the break, and it's an important one. City captain Kompany will play no further part in this game, with an injury forcing his withdrawal. Mangala will step in to take his place in the back four for the second half of the derby.
--- 46’ Substitution E. Mangala enters play, replacing V. Kompany. ---
(46’) Here we go again!
That will do it after a treat of a first half at Old Trafford. Manchester City took an early and deserved lead through Aguero's 99th strike for the Citizens, and threatened to score further. However, United orchestrated a spirited turnaround, with Young forcing in a leveler, before setting up Fellaini to head in the go-ahead goal. There's been chances but not too much controversy here in the Manchester derby. It's all set up nicely for the second half, which I'll be bringing you in just a bit. Stay tuned.
(45’) Into the final minute of first-half stoppage time now, and there's a glimpse of a chance as Valencia beats his man before hooking one in for Fellaini. He wins the knockdown, but Rooney can't bring the ball under control in time, with Herrera's follow-up from the top of the box leading nowhere.
(45’) YELLOW CARD! Kompany slides in recklessly on Blind, completely missing the ball and taking a chink out of the Dutchman's shin. That looked a painful one, but Clattenburg takes his time to make up his mind despite appeals from both sets of players. Good decision from the referee.
--- 44’ Yellow card V. Kompany receives a yellow card. ---
(43’) MAGNIFICENT DEFENDING FROM VALENCIA! Aguero is played in behind the defence and he has Silva for company, completely unmarked in the centre. However, the Ecuadorian hounds the City striker to the byline, and as a result, he can't even get the cross in! Old Trafford stands and applauds that crucial effort from the winger turned defender.
(41’) Wow. Milner will not want to see that again. A measured yet purposeful City buildup sees Aguero work the ball from the right to the Englishman on the opposite side. He's right on the edge of the box and has space to take a touch, but elects for a first-time curler which is shockingly bad.
(39’) It's Manchester United in the ascendancy as the first half draws to a close. City have been penned back in their own half in recent minutes, with a lot of play focused down the left side where Blind, Young and Fellaini have been combining to good effect.
(37’) Mata shifts the ball onto his left foot and hangs a lovely ball out to the left side of the box. Blind is making a great overlapping run, but Fellaini steps in front of him to take that pass down on his chest. Unfortunately, the Belgium midfielder was in an offside position.
(35’) Another booking, and once again it goes to a City player. David Silva didn't leave anything on the table when trying to win the ball off Young, sending the goalscorer tumbling just outside the United box.
--- 34’ Yellow card David Silva is yellow-carded. ---
(33’) The rain has kicked up a notch over Old Trafford, adding another wrinkle to this already captivating contest. De Gea shows great reactions to race off his line and hack the ball away just as Aguero was set to latch onto it and orchestrate a finish. Close call!
(31’) With their only two shots in this game, Manchester United have turned a 1-0 deficit into a 2-1 advantage. City have allowed their fast start to fade into nothingness, but Pellegrini should want his team not to panic, and continue their encouraging attacking play.
(29’) Poor Clichy has been the man with the spotlight on him through both United goals. You wouldn't really place full blame at the Frenchman's door for either of them though - even though he was beaten by his direct opponent twice. But what about Young, whose fingerprints are all over this Manchester United turnaround with a goal and an assist!
--- 27’ Assist A. Young provided the assist. ---
--- 27’ Goal! SPOKE TOO SOON! THE BIG MAN HAS TURNED IT AROUND! Blind and Young bide their time on the left-hand side, exchanging passes before the England winger hooks a beautiful inswinger to the back post. Fellaini storms on Clichy, and there's only one winner in that aerial duel, with the midfielder pummeling a header into the back of the net! ---
(26’) Fellaini wins the header from the set-piece, but United can't profit any further from it. The Belgian has barely been a factor in the opening 26 minutes of this match, with the pace of the game rather passing him by.
(25’) First booking of the game and it goes to James Milner. No complaints from the England midfielder, who was guilty of tugging back Herrera in plain view of Clattenburg. A decent opportunity to swing the ball into the mixer now.
--- 24’ Yellow card J. Milner gets yellow. ---
(24’) Blind is caught out again with the run in behind from Navas, but this time, the Spaniard is found to be offside. Still, the ease with which City have advanced down that side surely has not been lost on Van Gaal.
(22’) SCRAMBLE! Aguero tries to slide a finish into the bottom corner, but misses the target by a few feet. The play stays alive though, and only a last-ditch clearance from Smalling presents Silva from applying the smash deep inside the box! This is dangerous from the visitors.
(20’) The tempo of the match has just died down since that United equaliser. City are still the team attacking with more purpose, with the flanks in particular looking a ripe source of promise. Blind and Valencia, the full-backs for the home side, have not been on their game defensively.
(18’) Sergio Aguero has now scored in four consecutive Manchester derbies, with five goals in that span. He's ended his six-game goal drought and what's more, he's one goal away from a century of City strikes. If he does it tonight by scoring again, then he'll be the fastest-ever player to achieve that milestone for the Sky Blues.
(16’) Enthralling start to the Manchester Derby! Young needed a little fortune to convert that, but his desire to get first to the rebound cannot be understated. This match has been flush with commitment, energy and hustle, with a few sprinklings of quality football to boot.
--- 14’ Goal! UNITED HAVE DRAWN LEVEL! Herrera takes a long ball out of defence in stride, and spots Young making a darting run to the near post. He angles a low cross in that direction, and despite an initial challenge from Clichy, the ball sits up just long enough for the winger to convert on the turn from point-blank range! ---
(13’) Clichy is probably on his final warning already, as he clatters into Young, who was leading a United break down the right-hand side. Mark Clattenburg opts to lecture the Frenchman again, and it's probably wise that he doesn't set an early precedent with a booking.
(12’) United are inviting more and more pressure on themselves with a few amateur turnovers in midfield. Navas looks a good bet to end his 39-game goal drought on the right side of the City midfield, and he seems to have Blind bettered for raw speed whenever he wants. The Dutchman will need more help from Young.
(10’) Manchester United are RATTLED. There's no denying City that opener - their play since the first whistle has been menacing. The Red Devils have been forced to rely on some last-ditch defending to clear their lines, but they simply switched off on their right flank during the buildup to the goal. Take nothing away from the Sky Blues though, who orchestrated that to perfection.
--- 8’ Assist David Silva provided the assist. ---
--- 8’ Goal! IT'S IN! MANCHESTER CITY HAVE THE LEAD! Clichy plays the ball to Milner, and the England midfielder slips in Silva with a beautiful reverse pass. The Spaniard advances to the byline and squares to Aguero, who has the simplest of tasks, prodding the ball into the back of the net from about a yard or two out! ---
(7’) NAVAS IS IN AGAIN! And this time, it's nearly critical! The former Sevilla winger beats Blind for pace again and scampers through on goal. With no support in the centre, he goes for goal at the near post, but De Gea makes himself big enough to produce a vital block!
(6’) A warning shot has been fired by Manchester City down the right-hand side, as Navas gives a demonstration of his searing acceleration to torch Blind and drive a low ball into the area that falls into the realm of neither cross nor shot. United need to tighten up there.
(5’) Sergio Aguero has played his last six games for Man City without scoring. The Argentine has never gone seven without a goal for the Sky Blues. Meanwhile, Hart has to race quickly off his line to smother at the feet of Rooney after a momentary lapse by the men in front of him.
(3’) Early challenge on Mata by Clichy, and the former Arsenal full-back will be summoned over to Mark Clattenburg for an early lecture. Lively opening to this game, with some typically intense derby spirit from both sides. United have put together some lovely passes already.
(1’) Off we go then!
Edin Dzeko, despite scoring four times at Old Trafford in his City career, will have to settle for a place on the bench, as James Milner takes his place in the side. Sergio Aguero will be the lone striker, supported by David Silva. The other change from Pellegrini sees Bacary Sagna replaced by Pablo Zabaleta at right-back. Eliaquim Mangala once again can't dislodge Martin Demichelis from the centre of the visitors' defence.
Only the one change from Van Gaal, with Chris Smalling, who was dismissed in the reverse fixture at the Etihad in November, recovering from an illness to replace Marcos Rojo in the back four. Wayne Rooney captains the side and leads the line, with Marouane Fellaini expected to be the most offensive of the United central midfielders. Juan Mata and Ashley Young will man the flanks, while Antonio Valencia plays on the right side of defence.
Manchester City subs: Caballero, Fernando, Nasri, Dzeko, Kolarov, Lampard, Mangala.
Manchester City (4-4-1-1): Hart; Zabaleta, Kompany, Demichelis, Clichy; Navas, Toure, Fernandinho, Milner; Silva; Aguero.
Manchester United subs: Valdes, Rafael, Rojo, Di Maria, Falcao, Januzaj, McNair.
Manchester United (4-1-4-1): De Gea; Valencia, Smalling, Jones, Blind; Carrick; Mata, Herrera, Fellaini, Young; Rooney.
The past seven Manchester derbies in the league have seen six City wins, with the Sky Blues taking full points from their last four meetings with United. Another triumph this afternoon will make it five EPL wins in a row against the Red Devils - a feat that no other team has ever managed. However, Pellegrini is also on the cusp of an unwanted record, because if he comes away empty handed here, he'll be the first City boss since Stuart Pearce to lose four consecutive away games in the Premier League.
Form is something that has deserted Manchester City in 2015. Their title challenge to Chelsea has fallen embarrassingly by the wayside and they now sit in fourth, a point behind tonight's opponents, five behind Arsenal and a whopping 12 behind Jose Mourinho's team. Manuel Pellegrini, a man whose future is anything but secure, confessed that his team's performances in the last three months essentially threw their season into the garbage.
The Red Devils have won four straight in the league, with only an FA Cup defeat against Arsenal sandwiched in between. The top four and Champions League football is pretty much a lock for them at this stage of the season, but I'm sure that Louis van Gaal will want to secure a top-three finish for automatic entry into the European tournament next season.
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of the Manchester derby at Old Trafford! It's United vs City on the agenda, and with both teams practically neck-and-neck in the Premier League standings, there's more than pride on the line this afternoon. I'm Keeghann Sinanan, your designated scribe for all the action.

I am Alex Moretto and I would like to thank you all for joining me here today. Good bye!
FULL TIME: LIVERPOOL 2-0 NEWCASTLE. Raheem Sterling and Joe Allen help the Reds continue their dominance over the Magpies, who lose a fifth consecutive Premier League match. It was fairly straightforward for Brendan Rodgers' side, though it could have been a bit more comfortable had they capitalized on more of their chances.
(90’) THAT'S IT! The final whistle sounds and Liverpool secure three important points in their chase for a top four finish.
(90’) Gutierrez wins the ball from Allen atop the area and starts Newcastle forward. Cabella makes a lovely run into the final third and wins a free kick from 25-yards out. Perhaps a chance for the visitors to grab a consolation goal?
--- 90’ Yellow card Into the first of four minutes of added time and Alberto Moreno has picked up a booking for a tackle near the halfway line. Newcastle concede possession shortly after and Liverpool can run more precious time off the clock. ---
--- 89’ Substitution R. Lambert enters the game and replaces R. Sterling. ---
(89’) There is very little happening out on the pitch as the final second tic off the clock. The ball is being contained in midfield, with Liverpool predominantly in possession, though showing little intent to get forward and add to their lead.
(87’) Liverpool are cruising through the final minutes here, playing keep away from Newcastle. This win will put them four points behind Manchester City in fourth, but they still have plenty of work to do to catch the Sky Blues with just six games remaining.
--- 86’ Substitution Y. Gouffran comes on for Ayoze Pérez. ---
(85’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle won five consecutive Premier League matches in October to November of this season. If you take out that run, they have just four victories from their remaining 26 league games (W4, D8, L14).
--- 83’ Red card! NEWCASTLE DOWN TO 10 MEN! It's a fine line between working hard and being careless, and Sissoko has crossed it here. He lunges into a challenge in midfield and gets his studs up into the shin of Leiva. It's a horrendous tackle that should have been a straight red, but nonetheless, it's a second yellow and a sending off for the Frenchman. ---
(82’) CHAOS! Liverpool get their big men forward from the back to cause havoc in the area and they do just that. Lovren meet it at the far post, but his header is blocked. Newcastle don't clear and Lovren gets a second shot at goal, but play is blown dead as Krul is fouled as he rushes off his line.
(80’) Lovely one-two! Superb link-up between Sterling and Coutinho on the flank, and Taylor can't deal with the forward's pace. He gets into the area and has teammates waiting in the centre, but Janmaat does well to block the cross behind for a corner.
--- 78’ Yellow card G. Johnson gets yellow. ---
--- 78’ Yellow card Tempers are starting to boil over as Sissoko gets in the face of Johnson near the touchline in anticipation of a throw in, and the Liverpool defender isn't backing down. Second later he causes another scene out of frustration and picks up a booking for his actions. ---
(76’) Liverpool are playing much more relaxed now and that could make it very difficult on Newcastle, who make their second change. Abeid is the one to give way, surprisingly considering the game he has had, while Adam Armstrong takes his place on the pitch.
--- 75’ Substitution A. Armstrong comes on for M. Abeid. ---
(74’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle are winless in their last 19 trips to Anfield (W16, D3). The Magpies’ last victory over Liverpool in Merseyside came almost exactly 21 years ago – April 15, 1994.
(72’) This may be too big a mountain for Newcastle to climb now and they are looking discouraged out on the pitch as Liverpool get forward to try and add to their lead. They win another corner and Lovren rises well to meet it, but he sends his header disappointingly over the bar.
--- 70’ Goal! JOE ALLEN DOUBLES LIVERPOOL'S LEAD! The corner is cleared initially, but played back into the area. The Welshman misses his first header, but again Williamson can't deal with it, and the Liverpool midfielder makes no mistake on the follow up, placing his shot past Krul at the near post for his first goal for the Reds at Anfield. ---
(69’) HAS TO BE BETTER! A dreadful miscue by Williamson allows Borini in along the right channel. The substitute has plenty of options in the centre but takes far too long to get his head up, allowing the defender to recover and knock the ball behind for a corner.
--- 67’ Substitution Jonas Gutierrez comes on for the visitors, making his 200th appearance for the club. It's a remarkable achievement for the midfielder, who just one short year ago had a much more important battle on his hands. There's a lovely applause from both sets of fans as he makes his way onto the pitch in place of Gabirel Obertan. ---
(66’) Obertan puts in a good run along the right to put pressure on the Liverpool defence via the counter. Lovren gets back to block the cross, but the Reds still have a corner to deal with here. That will be the last contribution of the match from the Newcastle-man.
(64’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool had scored two or more goals in each of their last seven Premier League home matches before their 2-1 loss to Manchester United.
(62’) SMART SAVE! Liverpool are back on the front foot as they move the ball around well in the attacking third. Allen gets a shot off from 10-yards out, but Krul makes a good stop. Back the other way come Newcastle on the counter as the pace picks up, but Ayoze can't track down a long ball forward as Mignolet rushes off his line to collect.
(60’) SPECTACULAR! Coutinho makes a truly mesmerizing run into the area, dribbling his way past three defenders. It amounts to nothing for Liverpool, but that was absolutely sensational from the Brazilian!
--- 58’ Substitution J. Ibe is replaced with F. Borini. ---
(58’) HOW HAS HE MISSED FROM THERE?! Tremendous play from Henderson on the right to dribble his way into space and deliver in a cross, but it's horrendous from Taylor who not only fails to clear, but plays it straight into the path of Sterling. The forward looks to add to his tally from six-yards out and has all the time in the world, but puts his shot just wide of the near post with Krul making himself big in goal. He absolutely has to be scoring from there.
(56’) It's becoming a bit too untidy at the back from Liverpool, who are playing a dangerous game as they try and pass their way forward. Can makes a poor decision to try and play a free kick short and winds up giving it away to Sissoko, but luckily for him, the Newcastle midfielder gives the ball away shortly after and the attack comes to nothing.
(54’) Superb start to this second half for Newcastle! They're applying relentless pressure on Liverpool as the corner count continues to rise. Cabella plays the ball off Lovren for another corner, but again the visitors fail to capitalize as the Reds clear the threat with ease. They have to start making more of these set piece opportunities.
(52’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle have taken just six points against teams currently in the Premier League’s top six this season (W2, L9). They lost all five away matches over that span, by a combined score of 18-2.
(50’) After rolling around on the ground in pain, Can makes it off without any help which is a good sign as far as his participation in the rest of this game, as well as future matches, goes.
(48’) Newcastle try and pick up where they left off at the end of the first half and they do win an early corner through some good work from Abeid in attack. The set piece is dealt with by Liverpool, but it comes at a cost as Can goes down in significant pain and it's unclear as to whether or not he will be able to continue here.
(46’) The second half is underway! No changes to tell you about at the break.
HALF TIME: LIVERPOOL 1-0 NEWCASTLE. Raheem Sterling has the Reds in front at the break, and for a while there it was looking like they should have been two or three goals up at the break. The Magpies stood firm, however, and ended the half confidently. A clear shout for a penalty was denied and that is the big talking point at the break, with John Carver having a few words with the referee as they make their way into the tunnel.
(45’) ABEID FIRES OVER! It's another great chance for Newcastle, just before the half time whistle sounds. It comes at a welcome time for Liverpool, as well.
(45’) MAGNIFICENT SAVE! Fantastic football from Newcastle, who have really been on top in the last few minutes. Janmaat plays a superb ball over the top and Ayoze beats Can to get on the end of it. He heads it toward the far post, but Mignolet sails through the air to get a hand to it and knock it behind for a corner.
(43’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle have been held scoreless in five of their last eight trips to Anfield to take on Liverpool (D1, L7).
(41’) Liverpool have amped up the pressure again with half time approaching. Henderson is the puppet master in midfield, decisive in possession and providing some excellent balls forward. Meanwhile, John Carver is still having words with the fourth official and you can hardly blame him.
(39’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY DENIED! Newcastle are livid with referee Lee Mason as Ayoze takes a pass from Colback in the area before being taken out by Lovren. The centre-half swipes at the ball, but gets none of it, taking out the legs of the striker. It's a clear penalty, but somehow Mason has missed it! The visitors have every right to be livid.
(37’) SENSATIONAL STOP! Lucas does well to attack a ball in from the right and heads toward goal from the top of the six-yard box, but Krul miraculously dives to his left to get a hand to it! The flag goes up to indicate an offside on the Liverpool midfielder, but Krul knew little about that when he made the save.
(35’) LETDOWN! A great break from Sterling following a giveaway in midfield catches Newcastle short-staffed at the back. The goal scorer drives forward and lays it off for Coutinho, who sidesteps Janmaat and gets into a great shooting position. He opts not to have a go, for some reason, and his pass is intercepted bringing the move to an end.
(33’) The pace has fizzled out significantly as we pass the half-hour mark. Newcastle seem to have settled down at the back, but their inability to get forward and test this Liverpool back four is still a concern for them. The Reds have been known to leak goals, but Newcastle can't score if they don't shoot.
(31’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle have earned just nine points since the start of 2015 (W2, D3, L7). Only QPR have posted a worse record since the start of the New Year.
(29’) Finally Newcastle carve out a chance! Obertan finds acres of space on the right and sends a good ball into the area. His cross is flicked on by Perez, where Abeid meets it atop the area. The midfielder makes good contact with a volley, but hits it straight at Mignolet.
(27’) WONDERFULLY-WORKED! All Liverpool at the moment and there's no telling how they don't have a second. Ibe wins a free kick which Henderson takes. The midfielder plays it short and into the path of Coutinho, but Perez blocks his shot. The pressure stays on and Sterling gets it atop the area. He uses the run of Moreno as a decoy, but his final effort it stopped by Krul yet again.
(25’) IN AGAIN IS STERLING! It's wonderful play from Liverpool - very easy on the eyes. Lucas and Coutinho link up in midfield and the Brazilian plays a good diagonal ball through for Sterling. The forward again passes up a chance at a shot, however, and his ball across the face of goal is too close to Krul who manages to collect.
(23’) EXTRAORDINARY PLAY FROM COUTINHO! The Brazilian uses an overhead kick to get past a defender on the edge of the area before a lovely bit of technique allows him to skip past Williamson. He passes up a chance at a shot and plays it across the face of goal, but Sterling arrives just a fraction too late.
(21’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool’s derby loss to Manchester United in their last home match ended a nine-match league unbeaten run at Anfield (W6, D3). They have lost just four of their last 32 Premier League matches in front of their home supporters (W22, D6).
(19’) Sterling does well to hold up the ball and win a free kick as Abeid topples into him from behind. Henderson delivers from the left of the penalty area, but his cross drifts just a bit high and safely into the arms of Krul.
(17’) CLOE TO A SECOND! Sterling plays a wonderful ball forward for Coutinho, this time on the ground. The Brazilian has a clear path at goal, and the better angle, but lacks the pace to get on the end of it as Williamson rushes across to scramble clear. If it were Sterling or Ibe on the end of that, it could very well be 2-0.
(15’) Liverpool are having plenty of success playing the ball forward in the air. Henderson's assist on the Sterling goal came from a wonderful switch, while Lovren and Moreno have both provided encouraging passes since then. Newcaslte are struggling to track the movement of these Liverpool players off the ball and it's causing for some panicked moments in defence early on.
(13’) BRILLIANT BALL! Lovren plays a sensational pass over the top to pick out the run of Moreno. The left-back lets it bounce and drills a half-volley at goal, but Krul stands tall to keep it out! Newcastle were caught sleeping at the back there!
(11’) It's the first attack that results in the goal for Liverpool, completely against the run of play. Newcastle had enjoyed a very encouraging start to the match. Their energy level in midfield indicates they are more than up for the occasion, preventing Liverpool from stringing more than a few passes together - but all it takes is one good ball forward and a world-class finish from Sterling and the Reds have the all-important first goal.
--- 9’ Assist Assist by J. Henderson. ---
--- 9’ Goal! FIRST SHOT, FIRST GOAL FOR LIVERPOOL! It's incredibly harsh on Newcastle who started very positively. Henderson sends a great ball across the pitch for Sterling, who brings it down superbly with his first touch just inside the area. He shows a bit of trickery to create space for a shot with Taylor defending, and curls a sublime shot past a helpless Krul. ---
(7’) STAT ATTACK: There have been 41 all-time meetings between these two teams in the Premier League, which have seen a total of 130 goals (over three per game) and not a single scoreless draw.
(5’) FIRST CHANCE! Classic counter-attacking football from Newcastle as they win the ball back and break forward with pace. Cabella gets on the end of the move and tries to curl a shot in at the far post, but it takes a healthy deflection and loops just wide at the near post for a corner.
(3’) The match is taking a few minutes to get going here, with the ball being contained in the midfield third. Neither team has been able to get the ball into attack just yet, with the players feeling each other out. It's been quite sloppy to begin here.
(1’) We're underway at Anfield! Liverpool are in their all red home strip, attacking right to left, with Newcastle sporting their classic black and white striped tops.
The always beautiful "You'll Never Walk Alone" echoes through Anfield on this beautiful night in Liverpool. There are few anthems quite like it! It's a warm, clear night with the slightest breeze blowing through the stadium, making for a perfect night for football. We are just moments away now from kick-off!
Rolando Aarons and Siem de Jong are back in training after long injury lay-offs, but neither are fit enough to return to action and thus have both been left out of the team for tonight. Vurnon Anita makes a rare start at left-back, while Daryl Janmaat is again forced to play centre-half. Gabriel Obertan is also back in the starting line-up, pushing Sammy Ameobi to the bench.
Emre Can returns from suspension for the Reds and gets the start ahead of Kolo Toure in the back four, but Steven Gerrard and Martin Skrtel are still serving the last game of their bans. Brendan Rodgers is also without Daniel Sturridge, Mario Balotelli, Adam Lallana and Mamadou Sakho, and thus has opted to play with a false nine. Raheem Sterling, Philippe Coutinho and Jordan Ibe are starting up top, with Lazar Markovic relegated to a spot on the substitute's bench.

At any rate, Ramsey has set the bar for his side, demanding a minimum of four points from their next two matches to stay in the Premier League. They know they'll need at least a tie here to stay within their manager's demands, and despite his assertion before the match that the side are upbeat, a loss today could be hugely damaging to their morale with the bar so explicitly set.
There are a few absences today that both teams will have to contend with: Ideye, Dawson, McManaman and Foster are all out for the home side, while the visitors won't be able to call upon the injured Fer, Dunne, and Faurlin.
Chris Ramsey however does seem to have his side performing slightly better when traveling; they've scored at least once in every away game since mid-December after managing just two goals in their seven away matches before then.
Where to even begin with this QPR side? Despite having some very talented players, including the fantastically performing Charlie Austin, they've lost all of their last five matches, conceding at least twice per game along the way. They have just one result on the road all season that wasn't a loss: the 2-0 win away at Sunderland.
The home side have been inconsistent in the Premier League recently, sandwiching wins over Southampton and Stoke at home with losses away to Aston Villa and Manchester City. Luckily for Tony Pulis' men, the Rangers have been dire away from home all season and they'll look at today as a massive chance to continue their climb up the table.

Danny Ings had the two best chances and will regret not taking them, but in the end, a draw is the fairest result with neither side doing enough to deserve all three points. Tottenham fall further behind Manchester United in their chase for the top four, while Burnley remain in the relegation zone, pulling level with Sunderland - who play later today.
(90’) IT'S ALL OVER! Martin Atkinson sounds his whistle to signal the end of the match, with nothing to separate the two sides here at Turf Moor.

Spurs would lose even more ground on the top four with a draw here, while Burnley would at least gain ground on a couple of the teams they are chasing.

--- 78’ Yellow card B. Mee gets yellow. ---

--- 76’ Substitution Could this be the spark? Sam Dyche makes a positive substitution as Lukas Jutkiewicz is introduced. He should provide some pace and directness in attack, which Burnley have been lacking. Sam Vokes is the one to give way. ---
(74’) Burnley generate some pressure in attack and win a corner. Set pieces have provided the bulk of their chances thus far, but nothing comes of this one as Kane rises high to head clear. The hosts need a spark in attack, because this match is certainly up for the taking. It would be a massive three points if they can find a late goal here.
(72’) DREADFUL! That's absolutely abysmal from Paulinho, as the Tottenham fans throw their arms in the air in disbelief. The Brazilian picks up the ball and skips forward with plenty of daylight ahead of him. He approaches the top of the area and opts to try an early shot - but the contact is so poor that he scuffs it more than 10 yards wide of the near post.

(67’) TIDY FROM INGS! The striker does very well to control a ball atop the area and touch is past a defender before trying to stab a shot towards goal. The midfielder bursts forward and has just one man to beat, but can't do it as Arfield intervenes well to sniff out the chance.
(65’) STAT ATTACK: A defeat today for Tottenham would mean back-to-back road losses for the first time this season, not having suffered that fate since March of 2014 against Chelsea and Liverpool. Spurs' four previous away defeats this campaign have each been followed up with victories in their next road match.

(51’) STAT ATTACK: Harry Kane (10) and Christian Eriksen (five) have combined to score 15 of Tottenham's last 17 away goals in the Premier League. Harry Kane has eight goals in Spurs' last seven league matches on their travels.

--- 47’ Substitution Walker can't catch a break! The right-back is the latest victim of a stray boot from Trippier and as if he wasn't in enough pain, that will be enough to end his night. (46’) The second half is underway!
The players trot out onto the pitch, but Kyle Walker is moving quite gingerly as he makes his way back on. The right-back appears to be experiencing significant discomfort and you have to wonder why he's still on if he's feeling considerably less than 100 per cent? It will certainly be something to keep an eye on here.
HALF TIME: BURNLEY 0-0 TOTTENHAM. It's been an incredibly tedious display of football after 45 minutes, but that will certainly play into the hands of the hosts moving forward. Spurs have enjoyed the greater share of possession, but it is the Clarets who have come closest to breaking the deadlock, twice through Danny Ings. Everything is still to play for in this second half.
(45’) The ensuing corner results in nothing, and Walker goes down injured. The training staff comes out to attend to him, but there's no rush as the first half comes to an end.

(9’) Burnley are applying relentless pressure off the ball, forcing Tottenham into some nervy moments in their own end. (7’) STAT ATTACK: Tottenham have not kept a clean sheet in seven Premier League matches, the longest current run in the top flight.
(5’) HOW HAS HE NOT SCORED THERE?! The striker has the goal at his mercy, but pings a shot straight at Michel Vorm, who knocks it aside!
(3’) It's a typical start from Burnley, running their tails off in midfield. The Clarets may be outclassed on the pitch, but they will never be outworked, a characteristic that's greatly appreciated by these home supporters. Their team costs less than a quarter of that of Spurs, yet the belief within their team is unrivaled.

Turf Moor is beaming with anticipation on this Easter Sunday, sensing the chance to leap out of the relegation zone thanks to results across England over the weekend, while Tottenham desperately need this to keep pace with the top four.
Jan Vertonghen is a late omission from the team as a result of illness, while Spurs also have to make do without goalkeeper Hugo Lloris, who has yet to recover from a gashed knee he suffered against Leicester. Vlad Chiriches and Michel Vorm take their place in the starting XI. Danny Rose is a surprise inclusion in the team, having just recovered from hamstring and hip ailments. The only other change employed by Mauricio Pochettino is the decision to drop Andros Townsend to the bench, paving the way for Paulinho to pick up a rare start.
Sean Dyche has no new injury concerns, though he has Stephen Ward back on the substitute's bench after recovering from an ankle injury. The Clarets have put out an identical starting XI to that which they used in their defeat to Southampton and victory over Manchester City in their last two games before the international break.

A roller-coaster season has seemingly caught up to Tottenham. Their chase for the top four appears futile, with their inconsistencies proving detrimental. With five of their remaining eight Premier League fixtures – including today – coming on the road, it will take something of a minor miracle for Mauricio Pochettino’s side to achieve their objective, while they can ill-afford to drop any points from here on out. Sean Dyche says he has "total belief" that Burnley will still be a Premier League side next season. They have shown they are a difficult team to beat on their day, but far too often have they dropped points in games they had no business losing. The victory moves Sunderland up to 15th place in the table, one point ahead of both Hull City and Aston Villa and, more importantly, three points clear of the relegation zone ahead of their clash at home to Crystal Palace next weekend. As for Newcastle, who are next in action against Liverpool, they stay in 13th place, sandwiched between Palace and West Bromwich Albion and now just six points ahead of their local rivals.
Despite a late surge from Newcastle, a tiring Sunderland side were just about able to hold on and pick up what is surely their biggest and best victory of the season, one that Dick Advocaat will be hoping can kick-start a late push for Premier League survival. They fully deserve all three points, too, as they impressed at both ends of the pitch, with the attacking trio of Fletcher, Defoe and Wickham causing the Magpies' defence problems from start to finish, whilst their back four did extremely well to keep Perez, who looked isolated and frustrated for large portions of the game, at bay.

(49’) Berahino does well to bring down a lofted pass forward from Fletcher before teeing up Sessegnon, but the latter is unable to find a way past Mangala, who holds his ground well before winning the ball back for the hosts.
(47’) City push forward on a quick attack straight away, with Bony charging forward before firing a brilliant shot that Myhill does well to save with a good diving stop.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
City head into the half-time break with a comfortable 2-0 lead, and, a man down and with their backs to the wall, there is surely no way back into the game for West Brom, who have spent the vast majority of the first period of the game camped deep inside their own half of the pitch. The hosts have been attacking in waves, leaving the Baggies with little chance to breathe, and that's surely not going to change in the second half as the reigning champions look to wrap up a much-needed victory with even more goals.
HALF-TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-0 WEST BROMWICH ALBION
(45’) West Brom push forward on a rare excursion into the City half of the pitch, but Bony does well to get back and dispossess Fletcher before kick-starting a quick counter attack. The hosts break forward and Aguero then unleashes a shot from the left-hand side of the penalty area that, once again, Myhill stops with a strong save.
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be two minutes of added time.
(44’) Aguero cuts inside from the left wing before firing a low shot that Myhill does well to stop with a good diving save. The West Brom defence are unable to clear the ball, allowing Zabaleta to unleash a follow-up shot from the edge of the box, but it's poorly hit and sails comfortably into the hands of the Welsh goalkeeper.
(42’) City win back possession straight away after the kick-off, and, as has been the case since McAuley's sending off, they immediately push forward on another dangerous-looking attack, forcing West Brom into camping themselves on the edge of their own penalty area.
--- 40’ Goal! GOAL! It's 2-0! The West Brom defence have looked impressive up until now, but a terrible attempted clarance from Olsson sends the ball spinning straight into the feet of Fernando, who is then easily able to tap a shot into the bottom right-hand corner of the goal to double the hosts' lead. ---
(39’) Good defending from West Brom has forced City into firing from distance once again, and this time it's Silva who sees his cross-cum-shot deflect out of play for yet another corner.
(38’) Navas skips past Gardner before curling a dangerous cross into the heart of the penalty area from the right flank. It almost meets the head of Bony but, under pressure from Lescott, the Ivorian is unable to get a head on the ball and it instead ends up bouncing away from danger.
(37’) Silva steps up and tries to curl a shot over the top of the West Brom wall, but it's horribly hit and clears the goal by quite some distance.
(36’) Morrison nudges Silva in the back and brings the Spaniard down just outside of the penalty area, resulting in a free kick for the hosts in a very dangerous position.
(34’) Lovely play by Bony! Silva tees up Bony, who then immediately flicks the ball past Lescott and into the feet of Lampard, but the midfielder is unable to get a decent shot away from the edge of the penalty area and instead sees his first-time effort trickle well wide of the goal.
(32’) Another great save by Myhill! Navas receives the ball with his back to goal and spins round Fletcher before firing a brilliant shot that forces the West Brom goalkeeper into making an even better diving stop.
(31’) Silva finds Bony with a brilliant through-ball, but the Ivorian fails to unleash a pass to Aguero soon enough, allowing the West Brom defence to regroup before cutting out the danger.
(29’) Bony sends a brilliant pass out to Silva, who twists and turns on the left flank before cutting the ball back to Clichy. The Frenchman immediately unleashes a first-time cross-cum-shot from just inside the penalty area but it ends up flying a few yards past the near post.
--- 27’ Assist The assist came from Fernando. ---
--- 27’ Goal! GOAL! City have taken the lead! West Brom fail to clear the danger, and an attempted shot from Fernando is deflected over the top of Gardner and onto the foot of Bony, who flicks the ball over his head before firing it past Myhill from close range. ---
(26’) After finding it difficult to penetrate the West Brom penalty area, Aguero is forced into firing another long-range strike that is deflected out of play for a corner.
(24’) Fantastic save by Myhill! Silva receives the ball just outside of the penalty area and unleashes a rocket of a shot towards the top right-hand corner of the goal, but the West Brom goalkeeper pulls off a wonderful one-handed stop to deny the Spaniard the opportunity to fire his side into the lead.
(22’) Bony holds up the ball well before teeing up Lampard, who immediately sends a lovely through-ball into the path of Aguero. The Argentine sprints forward to meet the pass but his run is slightly mistimed and the linesman's flag is raised for offside.
(21’) As expected, the numerical advantage has meant that City have spent barely any time without the ball at their feet, and in the last five minutes the reigning champions have had an incredible 92% of the possession.
(19’) Great chance for Lampard! A low Clichy cross pinballs around the penalty area before coming out to the former Chelsea man, who is unmarked on the edge of the box, but he ends up sending his first-time strike wide of its intended target and out for a goal kick.
(17’) Lovely play by City! Aguero chips a fantastic pass into the feet of Navas, who then cuts a beautiful ball into the heart of the penalty area from the right-hand side of the box. It meets Silva but the Spaniard is unable to get a shot away before being closed down well by Lescott.
(15’) Again, Aguero and Silva link up well before the latter tries to send a deft through-ball into the path of Lampard, but the attempted pass is cut out on the edge of the penalty area at the vital moment by Olsson.
(13’) Silva and Aguero link up well before the latter skips past three West Brom players and unleashes a fierce shot from 25 yards out, but it's poorly hit and ends up flying well wide of the goal.
(11’) The visitors are finally able to get forward and penetrate the City half of the pitch for one of the first times this afternoon, but they are unable to hold onto the ball for long before the hosts regain possession once again.
(9’) West Brom can't clear the danger, allowing Silva to break away quickly before firing a low shot from the edge of the penalty area that deflects off Olsson before flying out of play for a corner.
(8’) City patiently pass the ball around the edge of the West Brom box before Zabaleta finally sends a cross into the heart of the penalty area, but it's only able to find Fletcher, who then blasts the ball towards the halfway line.
(6’) It's going to be a tough 84 minutes for West Brom, who have already decided to camp as many bodies inside their own half of the pitch as possible in an attempt to keep the determined hosts at bay.
(4’) Lampard steps up and fires a strike from the resulting set-piece, but it's poorly hit and fails to clear the wall camped just inside the penalty area.
--- 2’ Red card! RED CARD! What a terrible start for West Brom! (1’) And we're off! West Brom get us underway, attacking from right to left.
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off.
Meanwhile, West Brom boss Tony Pulis has decided to make three alterations to the side that started last weekend's 1-0 win at home to Stoke City, with Ben Foster, Chris Brunt and Brown Ideye making way for Boaz Myhill, Jonas Olsson and Chris Baird.
Manuel Pellegrini has made seven changes to the City side that started against Barcelona during the week, with Pablo Zabaleta, Eliaquim Mangala, Gael Clichy, Jesus Navas, Fernando, Frank Lampard and Wilfried Bony all coming into the squad to replace Bacary Sagna, Martin Demichelis, Aleksandar Kolarov, Samir Nasri, Fernandinho, Yaya Toure and James Milner.
West Bromwich Albion substitutes: Rose, Wisdom, Davidson, Pocognoli, Mulumbu, Nabi, Anichebe.

There’s just over 15 minutes left to go until until kick-off, so let’s have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon…
As for West Brom, they may be 25 points and 11 places behind today’s hosts, but their league form is far better than the struggling reigning champions. The appointment of Tony Pulis at the start of the year has seen the Baggies rocket up the table and away from the dangers of the relegation zone, and, thanks to a great recent run of form that has seen them lose just one of their last five league games, they now sit in 13th place in the table, eight points clear of the dreaded drop zone and equal on points with 12th-place Crystal Palace.
It’s been a miserable month for City, who head into today's clash with just one win from their last five games in all competitions. Wednesday saw them dumped out of the Champions League by Barcelona, whilst a dreadful performance at Turf Moor last Saturday resulted in a disappointing 1-0 defeat against struggling Burnley. With each poor result, their slim chances of winning the title once again are reduced whilst Chelsea's lead at the top grows, and they are now in danger of dropping down the table if they don't improve their form, and soon. With that in mind, today’s clash is surely a must-win.

Full time at Villa Park. Swansea steal a dramatic late victory against a previously resurgent Aston Villa side thanks to a 87th minute strike from Bafetimbi Gomis after some lovely work by Wayne Routledge and Jefferson Montero. Garry Monk's outfit looked comfortable in possession all day, and are probably good value for the narrow win based on chances created. Back to the drawing board for Sherwood! I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
--- 90’ +3 Substitution Nélson Oliveira comes on for B. Gomis. ---
(90’) Routledge takes advantage of a Villa side chasing the game and ends up running through on goal one-on-one with Guzan! The American wins the duel though as he makes a solid save with his chest after a tired finish from the Swansea man! Very nearly game over!
(89’) SINCLAIR!!! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT! The former Swansea winger almost punishes his former club as he latches on to a cross to the back post to fire a lovely volley towards goal! Fabianski was beaten, but it flies just over the bar!
--- 87’ Assist J. Montero gave the assist. ---
--- 87’ Goal! GOOOAALLLLL!!! GOOOAALLLLL!!! GOOOAAALLL FOR SWANSEA! THE VISITORS SNATCH A LATE LEAD! Routledge curls a superb pass down the left channel for Montero and the Ecuadorian sends a perfect low cross into the box for Gomis, who stabs home from a few yards out! One-nil! ---
--- 85’ Substitution N. Dyer comes on for J. Shelvey. ---
(84’) Monk is going for this now as he introduces Nathan Dyer in place of Shelvey. Swansea now have three wingers and Gomis on now as they go all out for the three points. Aston Villa will still fancy their chances on the counterattack though!
(82’) Carlos Sanchez bursts out of his central midfield position and moves towards goal before looking to exchange a one-two with Agbonlahor. The return pass comes but the Colombian's subsequent first touch allows Fernandez to make the interception on the edge of the box! Important challenge there from the Argentine!
(80’) Ten minutes remaining of normal time at Villa Park and we still don't have any clear sign that we are going to find a winner here. Sherwood's men undoubtedly need the three points more than the Swans, but we still remain at deadlock. Still plenty of time for that elusive opening goal though!
(78’) Ki lays the ball back to Williams who in turn sprays a pass out wide to Taylor. The left-back aims to find the effective Montero but the pass goes too far into the territory of Villa, which means Bacuna can collect before moving the play back up the park for the hosts.
(76’) Another change from the hosts now and it sees Benteke strangely brought off for Weimann. The Belgian must be feeling the effects of that previous clash with Sigurdsson, otherwise it is an off decision from Sherwood to take off his best player.
--- 75’ Substitution A. Weimann comes on for C. Benteke. ---
(74’) Montero and Gomis link up for Swansea again. The Ecuadorian, who has been electric since coming on, drives down the left flank once again and reversed a pass into the path of his team-mate, who fires a strike towards the bottom left corner! Clark is there for Villa to make the important block! The visitors are turning up the heat on the Villans!
(72’) Montero takes on Bacuna at right back with a pacey dribble before hitting the byline and standing a cross to the front post. Gomis looks poised to get a header away but Okore is positioned well to make the vital interception. Guzan would have been in trouble there had the Frenchman got on the end of that!
(70’) Delph wins the ball in midfield and darts down the left wing before sending a precision pass into the box for Sinclair, who takes an assured touch before lashing a left-footed strike at goal. Decent attempt but it ends up being dragged wide of the post. If that had landed to Benteke it may have been a different story!
--- 68’ Substitution A. Westwood enters the game and replaces C. N'Zogbia. ---
(68’) Second change of the match from Tim Sherwood as N'Zogbia is withdrawn for Ashley Westwood. Again, this will probably lead to a change in formation to 4-3-3 for Villa. The substitute, Delph, and Sanchez in midfield now. Lets see if it pays off for them.
(66’) Montero looks to affect the game early on after coming on as he injects some pace into a run down the left wing. Routledge eventually aims to latch on to a pass in behind the Villa defence, but he is correctly flagged as offside.
--- 64’ Substitution J. Montero enters play, replacing G. Sigurðsson. ---
(64’) First change of the match from Garry Monk and it sees Sigurdsson, who has been disappointing today, replaced by Jefferson Montero. This may indeed signify a change in formation to 4-3-3 for Swansea, with the substitute and Routledge flanking Gomis up top.
(62’) The first 17 minutes or so of the second half have largely mirrored the opening period in that Swansea have looked comfortable in possession without really penetrating, and Villa have looked dangerous on the counter. The home side are starting to get a little frustrated, as they are eager to see some goalmouth action.
(60’) N'Zogbia whips a corner kick into the box and it falls straight to Okore. The central defender can't sort his feet out in time to get a shot away though and Ki marshals him out of the box. That opportunity just fell to the wrong man for Villa on that occasion!
(59’) Benteke pops back up after some attention by the physio, and it looks like he'll be okay to continue.
(58’) Some worrying scenes for Aston Villa at the moment as Benteke is currently down after a nasty collision of knees with Sigurdsson. The Belgian is currently down receiving treatment and the home fans will be hoping its an impact injury as opposed to something more sinister.
(56’) What a chance passed up by Agbonlahor! Hutton curls a cross to the back post and the ball falls fortuitously to the feet of the Villa striker, who digs out a strike at goal! The attempt looks destined to find the corner but Taylor is on hand to make a fantastic covering block to turn behind for a corner kick! That should have been converted!
(54’) Routledge displays some impressive trickery to get the better of Delph in the right channel and stands a teasing cross to the back post. Gomis gets above everyone to meet it and get the header away, but he just can't manage to get above the ball which means the attempt is powered over the bar.
(52’) N'Zogbia brilliantly flicks the ball round the corner of Taylor near the touchline but ends up being taken out by the full-back. Delph loops the resulting set piece into the box and Benteke heads into the danger area at the back post, but Williams is on hand to clear the danger before Agbonlahor can get the strike away!
(50’) Bacuna drives down the right wing and spots Benteke at the front post before curling a cross into the box for the big Belgian, who manages to glance a looping header towards goal. It is never troubling Fabianski, but the referee blows for a cheap foul on Fernandez anyway.
(48’) Bright opening to the half from Villa here. Okore brings the ball out from the back and fires a pass into the feet of Sanchez, who lifts a lovely ball down the wing for N'Zogbia. Swansea manage to get back into defensive positions fairly swiftly though and so Villa are forced back in their possession.
(46’) We are back under way at Villa Park! Some goals please!
Half time at Villa Park. Aston Villa and Swansea head into the break at a 0-0 stalemate after an opening 45 minutes which has not seen too many incidents in front of goal. Brad Guzan has been the busier of the goalkeepers so far but much of the problems at the back for the hosts have came from the poor distribution of their keeper. Swansea have been calm in their possession and Gomis has been bright, but no breakthrough. Hopefully a better second period in store!
(44’) Only one minute of added time allocated by the referee for this first half, which is probably accurate considering the lack of drama we have had. Both sides cancelling each other out so far, but moments of quality have been present, if fairly rarely.
(42’) The final ball has been pretty poor from both sides so far and it is meaning that both defences haven't been taxed too extensively. Benteke and Gomis have been bright for their respective teams, but no breakthrough as of yet in what has been an evening opening half.
(40’) Guzan's kicking has been atrocious so far and the American almost gives away yet another goal as his clearance bounces straight into the path of Gomis. It is only some excellent recovery work from Okore that lets him off the hook, as he earns a foul out of the Frenchman. If Swansea have any sense about them they will pepper that Villa goal with shots.
(38’) Gomis holds off the challenge of Clark will some neat hold up play before laying into the path of Routledge. The 30-year-old then plays a short pass out to the right wing for Naughton but the attack ends for Swansea as a lack of concentration from the January signing means he allows possession to roll under his foot for a throw in.
(36’) Clark clears off the line for Villa! Sigurdsson whips a free kick into the box and Guzan comes off his line to claim, only to spill the ball to feet of Routledge, who fires a strike towards the empty net, but the defender is on hand to get back and make the vital clearance! Almost a horror moment for the USA international keeper!
(34’) Benteke gets the better of Williams at the back post after some unsure defending by the Swansea captain. The Belgian rises high and glances a cross back into the danger area, but there are no team-mates present to latch on to it! Fabianski eventually comes off his line to claim.
(32’) Sinclair drives forward at tremendous pace down the left flank after a failed Swansea set piece and bears down on goal before slipping a pass into the left channel for Delph. The former Leeds midfielder bursts into the box and lashes a left-footed strike towards the front post, but Fabianski makes the block! Sweeping counter from the hosts there!
(30’) Villa are pressing high up the park at the moment as they look to combat Swansea's possession along the back and into midfield. Plenty of work being put into the game by Sherwood's men, but how long can they keep up this intense hunting of the ball? It may be playing straight into the hands of the visitors.
(28’) N'Zogbia gets the better of Fernandez near the touchline and fires a cross into the danger area, which is blocked. The winger picks the ball up again and finds Sinclair, who swivels inside the box to try and turn a left-footed volley towards the bottom corner, but the attempt ends up trickling into the arms of Fabianski. Benteke isn't too happy as he was screaming for a pass at the back post.
(27’) Hutton gets down the left-hand side and cuts in on his favoured right foot before lifting a speculative cross into the box. Williams heads away with authority but Bacuna collects near the touchline and recycles play for Villa, who are enjoying a nice little period of pressure at the moment.
--- 25’ Substitution T. Cleverley is replaced with C. Sánchez. ---
(25’) An early setback for Aston Villa now as it appears Tom Cleverley wont be able to continue after picking up a knock. The former Manchester United man will be replaced in the middle of midfield by Carlos Sanchez.
(23’) Ki collects possession at the edge of the box and feigns to shoot before reversing a lovely pass in behind the Villa defence for Gomis, who gets beyond Hutton before smashing a left-footed strike at goal, but it is saved solidly by Guzan at the front post. Corner kick to Swansea!
(21’) A decent opening 20 minutes or so here at Villa Park but we haven't been blessed with too many goalscoring chances as of yet. Gomis had the best opportunity which was defended well by Villa, who themselves haven't really managed to test Fabianski too much. The creative players such as Sigurdsson and Delph need to get into the game more in advanced areas.
(19’) Benteke rises high and flicks on a throw in to Agbonlahor, who looks to turn sharply and get away from Williams, but the Swansea captain is right at the back of the Villa striker and ends up commandingly winning possession. That is turning into a pretty entertaining battle between that duo!
(17’) N'Zogbia opens up his stride once again down the right wing and cuts in on his left foot before looking to crack a shot at goal. Taylor is well-positioned to make the block and the pressure eventually comes off the Swansea defence as Benteke clumsily fouls Fernandez.
(15’) Villa counterattack at pace through N'Zogbia and the former Wigan winger cuts inside before looking for Agbonlahor. The Villa striker goes down inside the box under the challenge of Shelvey, but there was nothing in it and the referee correctly waves play on.
(13’) Sigurdsson fires a pass into the feet of Shelvey and the former Liverpool man hits a fantastic first time ball into the path of Gomis which sees the Frenchman run through on goal. Rather than getting a shot away though, the former Lyon striker opts to cut back in an attempt to evade the defender, but ends up losing the ball. A decent opportunity passed up for the Swans, but great build up play!
(11’) Delph and Cleverley have just began to find their feet out their now as they look a lot more confident in possession. A nice period for Villa at the moment but Benteke and Agbonlahor have been pretty much starved of any kind of service. More required from Sinclair and N'Zogbia on the wings.
(9’) With that four-man diamond in midfield, Swansea are dominating the central areas at the moment. However, their lack of width in there should provide Hutton and Bacuna with plenty of impetus to get up and down their respective flanks to get crosses in. Not too much attacking ambition from the full backs so far though.
(7’) Swansea have typically settled into their patient possession game early on here at Villa Park. It is quite a contrast in styles today with the Swans preferring to keep the ball, with Aston Villa prospering more from counterattacking play. Let's see which tactic proves the most effective.
(5’) Fantastic block from Hutton! Taylor gets into an advanced position down the left and drives into the box near the byline before reversing inside to Gomis, who squeezes a shot towards the bottom corner, but the Scotsman covers across brilliantly to make the block! It may indeed have been a combination between Hutton and Guzan to stop that one!
(3’) Ki bursts forward from his position in midfield and slides an incisive pass through the middle. Gomis and Routledge both fancy getting on the end of it but both are flagged as offside. It looked like the Frenchman may have been on there though so Aston Villa let off the hook early doors!

The teams are making their way to the pitch and we are almost ready for this 3pm kick off!

Despite their bitter disappointment at exiting the Champions League on Tuesday evening after a brilliant display against Monaco, the Gunners have plenty to be cheerful about domestically, as a brilliant run of five consecutive Premier League victories has seen them significantly close the gap between themselves and second-place Manchester City. They could really do with a sixth win today, as tough clashes against Liverpool and Chelsea await them in two of their next three league games. With the race for the top four as close as ever, wins, and plenty of them, are desperately needed by everybody involved.

Today’s clash starts a difficult run for United, who have to face both Manchester City and Chelsea in two of their next three games. With the race for the top four as tense as ever, the Red Devils desperately need another positive result this afternoon to help put more distance between themselves and Liverpool, whilst also keeping the pressure firmly on in-form Arsenal.
As for United, they seem to have successfully weathered a New Year storm and head to Anfield looking far more confident than they have in recent months, although Louis Van Gaal will be well aware that there is still much work left to do. The Dutchman's men have only lost one of their last eight league games - a disappointing 2-1 defeat away to Swansea City last month - and start the day with three back-to-back wins under their belts, including last weekend’s impressive 3-0 victory at home to Tottenham Hotspur.
Their incredible league form is second to none, with their last defeat coming on that miserable day in Manchester three months ago. Since then, Brendan Rodgers' side have won 10 of their last 13 Premier League games, including their previous five in a row, and another victory today would be the icing on the cake, moving them above the Red Devils and into the fourth spot that they so desperately crave.
For the 192nd time, these two fierce rivals meet each other on the pitch, and with both sides desperately in need of all three points as they fight tooth and nail for Champions League qualification, this clash may prove to be one of the feistiest of the lot. Liverpool were hammered 3-0 by United in the last meeting back in December, but a lot has changed since then, and, as a result, the hosts start the day looking like an almost completely different team.

(76’) Steve Bruce is busting a blood vessel on the touchline as there seems to be confusion over the subsitutions he wants to make. Could this day go from bad to worse for the Tigers?
(74’) Nigel Pearson looks pensive in the stands as Leicester are coming on to the front foot. Can they take advantage after that red card for Huddlestone as both teams look to make changes.
--- 72’ Red card! T. Huddlestone gets a second yellow card and is sent off! ---
(72’) STAT ATTACK: There have been six red cards in the last seven league meetings between these two sides.
(70’) RED CARD FOR HUDDLESTONE! The former Spurs midfielder takes Vardy out just outside the box and the referee has no option but to produce a second yellow card. Leicester have renewed hope!
--- 68’ Yellow card A. Bruce is cautioned by the referee. ---
(68’) It's all getting very heated as both sets of players are crowding aroung the referee after Bruce goes in hard on Mahrez but again got to the ball and didn't look to touch the player!
--- 66’ Yellow card M. Dawson is yellow-carded. ---
(66’) Dawson is incensed as he is adjudged to upend Vardy but looked like he managed to get the ball first. The former Tottenham man sees yellow for his efforts.
(65’) SAVE! Elmohamady goes for the return with Livermore and manages to get a low shot away but his effort is straight at Schwarzer.
(63’) HEADER OVER THE BAR AT THE OTHER END! Huth rises highest to a corner from the left but his effort sails off target. The home side are getting frustrated right now.
--- 61’ Substitution L. Ulloa comes on for A. Kramarić. ---
(61’) OVER THE BAR! Just as the hosts show promise, the visitors go up the other end and win a corner. Jelavic climbs well but is unable to get his header on target.
(60’) Leicester are starting to show some urgency again in the final third as Schlupp fails to find Kramaric in the centre.
(58’) STAT ATTACK: Hull have lost just one of their last five league games, winning two and drawing two.
(56’) This long ball game from Nigel Pearson's men really hasn't worked today. Dawson, Bruce an McShane have acted like magnets to the danger at every turn. The hosts need to get the ball to feet otherwise they will struggle to pierce the defence.
(54’) Yet another corner to the Tigers has Schwarzer flying off his line to punch it clear under intense pressure in the six-yard-box.
(53’) Hull are proving here as De Laet blocks a Robertson cross from the right and sends the ball out for another corner. Will the pressure tell?
(51’) The momentum is stopping in the final third for the hosts as Elmohamady thwarts Mahrez on the left and shepherds the ball back to McGregor. Leicester are struggling to make an attacking impact in this game.
(49’) CHANCE! What an important block from Dawson, who slides in to get his body in the way of a left-footed effort from Cambiasso. McGregor has still been untested with 40 minutes to play.
(48’) STAT ATTACK: If the visitors win today, they could see themselves eight points clear of the drop zone.
(46’) The action resumes as Hull - kicking from right to left - get us back underway.
And we are back! The two teams are making their way back out of the tunnel - Hull to get us back underway momentarily.
HALF TIME - LEICESTER 0-0 HULL. A terrible miss from Nikica Jelavic, with the open goal at his mercy, remains the stand out moment of the first half as both teams head to the changing rooms. It has been an entertaining affair so far with both sides unable to break the deadlock. More to come after the break!
--- 45’ Yellow card A. Robertson gets yellow. ---
(45’) There will be ONE minute of added on time.
(44’) Robertson sees yellow for scything Mahrez down in a dangerous position just outside the penalty area. Dawson manages to turn away the resulting free-kick for a corner...good pressure from the hosts here!
(42’) HIGH AND WIDE: Robertson cuts inside from the left flank and finds Livermore, who tees Huddlestone up from distance, but his powerful effort sails into the stands.
(40’) STAT ATTACK: The hosts have taken 10 points from 12 matches at home - the worst record in the league.
(38’) WES MORGAN GOES FOR GOAL! The Leicester captain picks the ball up roughly 30 yards out and smashes an effort from long range into the back of McShane who concedes a corner.
(36’) McShane manages to get a header on target but it lacks power and it's simply plucked from the air by Schwarzer. The visitors are probing for supremacy...
(34’) SO CLOSE! Kramaric refuses to throw his body at a cracking deep cross from Mahrez but the striker pulled out at the last second under pressure from Bruce and the ball goes out for a goal-kick.
(32’) The game has just settled down again here as Hull win a free-kick just inside the opposition's half. Huddlestone takes it short to Robertson who is blocked out by James.
(30’) Huth's clearance is awkward under close pressure from Jelavic, who manages to get a shot away but a vital touch from Upson takes the sting out of it and Schwarzer collects.
(28’) There is some blood and thunder football now as both sides look to break on the counter. Both defences are highly organised at the moment but the atmosphere in the stadium is palpable as we near the half hour mark.
(26’) GOAL DISALLOWED! Huddlestone strikes a beauty of a cross into the six-yard-box and as Schwarzer gathers, N'Doye clatters into the Foxes' keeper and Jelavic puts the loose ball into the back of the net but Jonathan Moss blows his whistle for a foul. Neither side are happy but it was the right call from the referee.
(24’) Schlupp makes the wrong decision in an exciting passage of play for the home side and is crowded out down the left flank. It's still goaless here...how costly will Jelavic's miss prove?
(22’) STAT ATTACK: The Foxes have lost just one of their last seven league games with Hull City (W4, D2, L1).
(20’) TERRIBLE MISS! What on earth was he doing? Huddlestone plays a delicious ball in to the box that finds Elmohamady who cuts it back to Jelavic, but the striker loses concentration and bundles his effort into the grateful palms of Schwarzer.
(18’) It's lovely stuff from Leicester as brilliant build-up play from De Laet and Vardy leads to the right-back finding space and cutting the ball back from the byline but McShane is on hand to clear.
(16’) STAT ATTACK: Matthew Upson's home debut comes seven months into the season after missing the vast majority of the campaign so far through injury.
--- 14’ Yellow card T. Huddlestone goes into the referee's book. ---
(14’) It looks like we are going to see out first card of the match as Huddlestone steps right on top of Cambiasso's boot and sees yellow for his efforts.
(12’) The hosts are starting to edge this one as a cross from Vardy nearly finds Morgan - who stayed up after a free-kick opportunity nearly connects with a high ball but Dawson is on hand to head it clear.
(10’) It's been a pretty even start to this encounter with both sides battling for superiority in the middle of the park in the brilliant sunshine. Let's hope we see some sunshine football soon!
(8’) JUST OVER! Kramaric picks the ball up outside the box and shows his footwork with a few twists an turns before swinging his left foot at a cross/shot that sails high over McGregor's crossbar.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: Steve Bruce's side have taken the lead in four of their last five league games, but have only gone on to win two of them.
(5’) The Tigers win a free-kick roughly 30 yards away from goal. Ramirez swings a tame effort into the box and the ball deflects off Jelavic and out for a goal kick.
(3’) The away fans are roaring their team on from the off as Elmohamady races to meet a crossfield pass but is ushered out of play by Morgan.
(1’) Today's referee, Jonathan Moss, blows his whistle as Leicester, kicking from right to left, get us underway!
Both teams are lining up in the tunnel as kick-off looms! Who will emerge victorious from today's match? Let's find out!
PRE-MATCH STAT ATTACK: Leicester's victory over Hull in December was the first top-flight fixture between the clubs.
As for the visitors, Steve Bruce has the luxury of making just one change to his starting eleven, bringing in Gaston Ramirez for David Meyler who drops to the bench. If the Tigers can leave the King Power Stadium today with all three points, they will be 12 points clear of their opponents and edge closer to safety.
Foxes boss Nigel Pearson has handed home debuts to defenders Robert Huth and Matthew Upson as he looks to call upon their Premier League experience with the club rooted to the bottom of the table. Meanwhile, Kasper Schmeichel returns from injury and takes his place on the bench as Mark Schwarzer continues in between the sticks.

Leicester (4-4-2): Schwarzer; De Laet, Upson, Huth, Morgan; Schlupp, Vardy, Cambiasso, James; Mahrez, Kramaric.
