Villa earn an impressive 4-0 win over Sunderland, with a delightful double from both Benteke and Agbonlahor in the first-half gifting three points to Sherwood's men. That's all for our coverage today, until next time!
(90’) Delph's effort is sent well over the crossbar as the referee blows for full-time! A shocking 4-0 defeat for Sunderland at the hands of a rejuvenated Villa outfit, as they suffer a fatal blow in their bid to avoid relegation.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card L. Bridcutt gets yellow. ---
(90’) Bridcutt concedes a a free-kick in a dangerous area, but Villa play it back to keep possession. No danger from Sunderland in these later stages, a poor display in defence and attack.
(89’) Villa sitting deep now to hold out until full-time, with Bacuna doing well to defend the run of Wickham. Possession now all the way back with Guzan as the fourth official signals for four added minutes!
(87’) Wickham is again involved after finding a way into the box, but his shot is sent well wide of Guzan's net. He has offered some encouragement for Sunderland but it has come too late for his side.
(85’) Wickham turns wonderfully and has a shot on goal, but his effort sails well over the crossbar. A positive attack from the striker though, with Sunderland heading towards a catastrophic home loss.
--- 83’ Substitution D. Graham enters the game and replaces S. Fletcher. ---
(83’) Fletcher's effort sums up Sunderland's performance today, as they stumble towards a potentially fatal defeat. Poyet looks a very concerned figure on the sideline, as Cleverley lays off Bacuna down the right flank. Guzan then has to clear an attempted through ball from Alvarez.
(81’) CLOSE! Fletcher almost gives his side a consolation goal as he fought through the defence down the left wing, but his strike hits the post and is eventually cleared. The striker picks up an injury too!
--- 79’ Substitution A. Weimann enters the game and replaces C. N'Zogbia. ---
(79’) Entering the closing stages on Wearside, with Poyet's toothless Black Cats set to lose ground in the fight to avoid relegation. Bridcutt is unable to pick out Wickham in the box as another attack is thwarted.
(77’) Defoe finally has a touch in the penalty box but his efforts are to no avail, after Bacuna was strong to intercept. Benteke is keen to get a hat-trick as he bombs into the Sunderland penalty area, but his threat is cancelled out.
(75’) Benteke holds the ball up strongly and lays off Delph down the left wing. The Villa players are getting loads of time and space on the ball, as the Stadium of Light faithful continue to jeer their team.
(73’) Sanchez carries the ball from defence with ease, as no Sunderland player even makes a challenge. Poor display still in defence, with Defoe becoming a frustrated figure in attack.
(71’) Slight improvements from the Black Cats, but Agbonlahor breaks forward and finds Benteke down the middle. N'Zogbia then picks out Cleverley, as the visitors threaten to net a fifth goal!
(69’) Guzan easily collects a lofted delivery from Fletcher, with Sunderland's three strikers not able to find a way thorugh. Villa are standing strong in defence and have things under control.
(67’) Larsson continuing on, despite having had stitches on his ankle at half-time. He is unable to make an impact, as Delph finds Sinclair on the left wing. The visitors in no hurry to get forward though as they keep possession.
(65’) Sunderland finally have a spell of possession but have no creativity to get Defoe involved. Villa have a strong set up, with Larsson sending a free-kick wide from a dangerous position.
--- 64’ Substitution C. Sánchez comes on for C. Clark. ---
(63’) Comfortable for Villa, with Wickham the only visiting player to make an effort to track down the ball. Sunderland are deflated and have showed no signs of scoring at all, as Delph dictates play from the middle.
(61’) After an hour of play, Sunderland have made no genuine threat, as Defoe continues to be outnumbered up front. Villa look likely to score again from a counter attack, as the hosts push forward in search an opportunity.
(59’) Wickham has made a slight impact on proceedings, as he offers Sunderland a new attacking outlet. However, no real chances have fallen his way with Villa keeping possession well.
(57’) Sunderland's first glimpse of hope, as Alvarez sends a shot on target after Fletcher put a brilliant ball into the box. Defoe was flat-footed and unable to react to the cross!
(55’) Villa look in no danger of conceding as the hour mark approaches. They are dominating in the middle, as O'Shea comes accross to make a challenge on Delph to deny him a chance on goal.
(53’) Defoe loses the ball after poor support from his midfield, as the Black Cats continue to struggle. Poyet's men need a spark from somewhere if they are to make any impact!
(51’) Villa enjoying themselves now on Wearside, as Delph sends his shot well wide of the target. Sherwood will be over the moon with his side's performance so far. Clark then makes a sublime tackle to deny Fletcher's shot in the box.
(49’) After several minutes played of the second half, Larsson finally makes his way on to the pitch. Villa pushing hard down the right wing, but Brown clears for Defoe to pick up in the Sunderland half. However, the attack breaks down after sloppy play.
(47’) Pantilimon is almost beaten again, as N'Zogbia strikes towards the top corner, but the goalkeeper does well to stop it. Bizarre scenes as Sunderland are without Larsson and down to 10 men for these opening moments.
--- 46’ Substitution R. Álvarez is done for the day. C. Wickham is his replacement. ---
(45’) We are off and running again here on Wearside. Sunderland 4-0 down and need a miracle to recover!
It's 4-0 at half time! A double from both Agbonlahor and Benteke! Sublime display from Villa, as Sunderland look completley helpless. Big 45 minutes coming up in the race to avoid relegation.
(45’) Sunderland continue to be caught on the break, as they try to get forward in search of a goal! Real danger here of things getting embarrassing at the Stadium of Light as the referee blows his whistle for half time!
--- 44’ Assist L. Bacuna gave the assist. ---
--- 44’ Goal! GOOOOAAAALLLLLLLLL! Unbelievable as Benteke scores again with a marvellous header from Bacuna's brilliant delivery! It's 4-0 now already! Incredible stuff! ---
(43’) Villa controlling the game towards the break, as O'Shea comes out of defence and loses the ball. Sunderland can't get out of their own half, with supreme pressure coming from Sherwood's impressive side.
(41’) Villa are performing brilliantly as Sunderland try haplessly to find a spark from somewhere. Half time quickly approaching, with fans already leaving in their dozens! Agbonlahor brushes past the defence again and Delph's subsequent strike drifts just wide of the post.
(39’) Incredible scenes as Sunderland fans leave the ground before half time! An angry outburst towards their struggling team, who are in danger of suffering an embarassing defeat.
--- 37’ Assist The assist came from C. N'Zogbia. ---
--- 37’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLLLLLLL! Agbonlahor strikes again! Fantastic counter attacking goal from Villa, as N'Zogbia breaks through the middle and lays the goalscorer off, who glides past four defenders to pick his spot. ---
(36’) Benteke holds the ball up well as Villa continue to put pressure on Sunderland's stuttering defence. Sherwood's side in no rush now, as they dominate play from the midfield areas.
(34’) Penalty appeal! Larsson claims for handball after the ball strikes Clark's arm, following an effort from Defoe. The referee waves away any protests as Sunderland concede a free-kick deep in the Villa half.
(32’) Sunderland all over the place at the back, with Villa's widemen causing havoc, especially down the right flank. Delph holds possession strongly down the centre as the hosts struggle to get a grip on proceedings.
(30’) Shocking miss! Sinclair sends his shot from six yards over the crossbar, after a great run and delivery from Bacuna on the right flank. That could come back to haunt Villa, as they fail to slot in a third!
(28’) Close! Rodwell attacks a cross from Bridcutt, but the former Manchester City midfielder sends his effort wide. The hosts need the next goal to get back into this crucial relegation encounter!
(26’) Fletcher is unable to header home after connecting with Bridcutt's nicely weighted pass forward, with Villa dictating the tempo of this game from midfield. Lovely play from Delph see's the central man set up Sinclair, but the attack breaks down in the box.
(24’) The Black Cats need to claw their way back as relegation looms large! Poyet called his defence to the sideline to talk while Bridcutt received medical treatment for a knock.
(22’) Bacuna almost finds a way through for a third goal! The full back bombed forward past a helpless Sunderland defence as the home side struggle to deal with the pressure.
(20’) Incredible scenes at the Stadium of Light as Villa pounce and take a two-goal lead! Fantastic start from Tim Sherwood's Villans, as first goalscorer Benteke holds the ball up for his side to continue their attack.
--- 18’ Assist C. Clark gave the assist. ---
--- 18’ Goal! GOOOAAAALLLLLLLL! Agbonlahor strikes straight away to send Villa two goals up! The winger tucks it easily past the keeper after poor defending from O'Shea. ---
--- 16’ Assist L. Bacuna gave the assist. ---
--- 16’ Goal! GOOOOAAAALLLLLLLLLL! Villa's towering targetman Benteke slots home after lovely team play from Villa. Cleverley's pass found Bacuna down the right wing, who layed off the Belgian to open proceedings! ---
(14’) Defoe goes through on goal from an Alvarez pass, but Guzan comes out to clear the danger. The English striker looked to be heading for a one on one situation!
(12’) The game springs to life as Villa break with Bacuna and N'Zogbia after a corner, but the following shot from the wideman is easily dealt with by Pantilimon. Delph tries to slot Sinclair through on goal after possession is won back, but Sunderland stand strong to clear.
(10’) Villa keeping possession but being kept in their own half by immense pressure from the Black Cats midfield. A defensive mix up leads to Alvarez having a run at goal, his subsequent shot is blocked by Irishman Clark.
--- 8’ Yellow card L. Bacuna is cautioned by the referee. ---
(8’) Fletcher wins a free-kick brilliantly after drawing a challenge from Bacuna, who is booked. Alvarez is the target for the set-piece, but it is overhit and the home team's attack breaks down.
(6’) Rodwell surges forward and a lay-off from Fletcher almost falls for Van Aanholt in the box. Alvarez then cuts in from the left flank but is unable to get a shot away, as he is rapidly hunted down by Villa's defence.
(4’) Guzan's poor clearance almost gifts Sunderland a chance, but Villa stand strong to fend off the attack. N'Zogbia cuts in from the right and has his shot blocked for a corner, which is eventually cleared away.
(2’) Ten games to go, the relegation run in is in full swing! Today's game is crucial in that battle to remain in the top-flight. Sunderland start by sending a long ball forward towards Larsson, but Villa win back possession.
(1’) We are underway here at the Stadium of Light! The home side get the game going and are shooting from left to right in this first period.
We are just 10 minutes away from kick-off!
The Black Cats have drawn more often against Villa than versus any other opponent in their Premier League history (11 times), but a win is crucial to both sides today as they aim to beat the dreaded drop.
There have been seven red cards in the last 12 Premier League meetings between Villa and Sunderland, so expect some fireworks at the Stadium of Light today!
Gabriel Agbonlahor will be a threat, having scored in three of his last four Premier League matches against Sunderland. But Villa have scored just six goals in their last 21 Premier League away games and have gone just two minutes short of 10 hours of playing time since they last scored a goal on the road.
The home side have failed to score in five of their last six Premier League matches against Villa, netting just one in the other encounter. Gus Poyet’s men have also drawn a blank in three of their last four Premier League home matches.
Sunderland are ranked joint-lowest in the amount of home league victories this season, level with bottom side Leicester City. But a victory would see them open up a four-point gap over their opponents in the lower reaches of the table as the race for safety intensifies.
The Black Cats have won just one of their last eight league games, and are without a win in six in all competitions. With just four Premier League victories to their name this season, they are in desperate need of a positive result.
Aston Villa subs: Given, Gil, Sanchez, Kinsella, Weimann, Westwood, Hepburn-Murphy.
Aston Villa starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Guzan; Lowton, Okore, Clark, Bacuna; Delph, Cleverley; Sinclair, N’Zogbia, Agbonlahor; Benteke.
Sunderland subs: Jones, Wickham, Gomez, Graham, Coates, Vergini, Mannone.
Sunderland starting line-up (4-4-2): Pantilimon; Reveillere, van Aanholt, Brown, O'Shea; Bridcutt, Larsson, Rodwell, Alvarez; Defoe, Fletcher.
Away team: Ron Vlaar (calf) is absent and Kieran Richardson (calf) also misses out. Aly Cissokho (groin) is injured and Philippe Senderos (calf), Joe Cole (hamstring), Nathan Baker (knee), Alan Hutton and Jack Grealish (both suspended) are all ruled out.
Home team: Sunderland are without the suspended Lee Cattermole after he picked up his 10th booking of the season in the recent draw at Hull and was handed an automatic two-match ban. Adam Johnson remains suspended by the club while Emanuele Giaccherini (ankle) and Will Buckley (knee) are both ruled out.

Stoke will look to bounce back at home to Palace next weekend and will be hoping for good news on the injury front after Erik Pieters, Victor Moses and Jonathan Walters were forced off this afternoon. West Brom's next match is a daunting one at Manchester City and they will await news on the fitness of Ben Foster, another injury casualty today.
Stoke never got going, in truth, and can have few complaints with the scoreline following a match high on endeavour but generally low on quality.
(90’) That is it! West Brom end their shocking home run against Stoke and Tony Pulis can celebrate a second successive victory against his former club. West Brom are surely safe now for another season, while Mark Hughes' side must reflect on the end of their winning run following a disappointing display.
--- 90’ +5 Substitution S. Berahino is done for the day. C. Baird is his replacement. ---
(90’) Myhill cleans out Crouch on the edge of the West Brom box as the striker looks to latch on to a long punt forward, but Arnautovic delivers a terrible free-kick and that will most likely be that!
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card G. Myhill receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Bardsley tumbles in the West Brom box following Stoke's best move of the match, but Gareth McAuley got ball as well as man. No penalty!! Olsson has been positioned up front as a target man as the Baggies look to hold on.
(90’) There will be five minutes of added time for Stoke to rescue a point. Adam almost catches out Myhill with a driven effort from the left, but the goalkeeper gets down well at his near post.
--- 90’ Substitution B. Ideye is done for the day. J. Olsson is his replacement. ---
(90’) Goalscorer Ideye comes off with an apparent injury late on, to be replaced by central defender Jonas Olsson.
(89’) Another ball into the West Brom box comes to nothing, with Crouch failing to direct a flick-on into Whelan's path. Stoke look set to suffer a first Premier League defeat at The Hawthorns.
(87’) Cameron gives the ball away with a dreadful pass that pretty much sums up Stoke's performance going forward. There is still time for the Potters, but not much, and West Brom look solid as a rock.
(86’) Michael Oliver has a quick word with Fletcher during a break in play. Is the official unimpressed by some time-wasting from West Brom, perhaps?
(84’) Still no real threat from the visitors as the clock ticks down. Crouch meets a deep cross from Bardsley, but his header from a narrow angle poses no problem for Myhill at the keeper's near post.
(82’) Arnautovic is caught offside as Stoke aim to break quickly from the resulting corner. Mark Hughes has a face like thunder on the touchline.
(81’) Morrison has been excellent in the second half and he takes aim from 25 yards to bring a useful save from Begovic.
(79’) With the exception of a brief spell at the start of the second half, Stoke have not really looked like scoring. They only have just over 10 minutes left to rescue something from a fixture they traditionally fare well in.
(78’) Another decision goes against Shawcross, who continues to engage in a physical battle with Berahino. Diouf and Arnautovic have yet to make any impression following their second-half introductions.
(77’) Cameron is at the heart of the action again as he makes a sliding challenge to deny James Morrison following an excellent, surging run from the midfielder.
(76’) From a similar position, Brunt sends over another outswinging cross. The ball is nodded into Dawson's path and the defender then tumbles under a challenge from Cameron to prompt appeals for a penalty. I think Stoke get lucky as the referee waves play on.
--- 74’ Yellow card M. Diouf is cautioned by the referee. ---
(74’) Brunt delivers and Stoke get the ball away at the second attempt. Tony Pulis will be much happier with what he's seen since that brief flurry of corners for the visitors 10 minutes ago. A Diouf foul on Sessegnon brings another free-kick and a yellow card for the substitute.
(73’) Ryan Shawcross and Saido Berahino are having a right old battle and the latter is brought down by Stoke's captain to give West Brom a free-kick in a dangerous position.
(71’) A fine cross from Brunt is headed back across goal by Ideye, but no West Brom player is there to pick up the pieces. Stoke are running out of time.
(69’) Berahino and Darren Fletcher see goalbound shots charged down as West Brom look to wrap up the points with a second goal.
--- 68’ Substitution M. Diouf enters play, replacing J. Walters. ---
(68’) Sessegnon is angered by a challenge from Adam, forcing referee Michael Oliver to speak to both men. Stoke are forced into a third enforced change of the afternoon as Walters leaves the fray to be replaced by Mame Biram Diouf, a scorer against Everton last time out.
(67’) GREAT SAVE FROM BEGOVIC! West Brom's first attack in some time ends with the ball finding Ideye on the left. He cuts onto his right foot and fires towards the far corner, only for Stoke's goalkeeper to palm the shot wide.
(66’) Walters suffers a facial injury following a collision with Dawson and West Brom are eventually able to get the ball out of their own half.
(64’) Myhill almost gets caught under the resulting corner, but recovers to paw the ball behind. A third corner in succession is forced as McAuley heads clear.
(63’) A strong challenge from Bardsley gets Stoke onto the front foot. West Brom clear the initial danger, but are soon under pressure again and a clever, looping header from Walters brings a good save from Myhill.
(61’) Chances continue to prove elusive for Stoke, but they have at least gained a measure of control after being second best in the opening half. Much of the play is taking place in West Brom's half and the hosts are looking nervy.
(60’) West Brom are being pegged back, but Myhill's first touch is a straightforward one as he collects a mis-directed cross from the left.
--- 58’ Substitution M. Arnautović comes on for V. Moses. ---
(58’) Ah, Moses is down on his haunches again. We're going to lose our third player to injury this afternoon, with the forward following Pieters and Foster in withdrawing from the action. That's a real blow for Stoke, who turn to Marko Arnautovic.
(57’) Moses seems ok and will continue, for the time being at least. Stoke have dominated possession since the interval, but continue to trail to Ideye's first-half header.
--- 56’ Substitution G. Myhill comes on for B. Foster. ---
(55’) Now Moses is down injured ... and Foster is coming off to be replaced in the West Brom goal by Myhill, who started the recent FA Cup defeat to Aston Villa.
(54’) Stoke do well to clear a Craig Gardner free-kick following a cynical foul that earned Wilson a booking. Berahino then heads wide from a Morrison cross and the hosts look to have come to life again.
--- 53’ Yellow card M. Wilson gets yellow. ---
(53’) Chris Brunt takes over goal-kicking duties as play resumes. I'm not sure Foster will be able to carry on.
(52’) Foster appears to have injured his left leg when failing to collect that cross under pressure from Crouch. Boaz Myhill is warming up for West Brom.
(51’) Stoke fans familiar with the methods of Pulis may not be all that surprised to hear that West Brom have dropped deeper at the start of this second half. Foster makes a mess of a cross from the left, but Crouch cannot capitalise and Phil Bardsley fires over after Lescott had hacked the ball away.
(49’) McAuley is dispossessed by Moses, but James Morrison gets back well to halt a Stoke break. The visitors come again, with a Crouch flick-on causing momentary concern, but West Brom hold firm.
(47’) Cameron has taken up a place in the heart of Stoke's defence, which has been beset by injuries this season, with Marc Wilson shifting to left-back in Pieters' absence.

(46’) Geoff Cameron replaces Erik Pieters for Stoke at the start of the second half. Victory for West Brom would lift them 11 points clear of the relegation zone and surely guarantee safety.
Pulis has plenty of experience when it comes to ensuring teams hold on to a lead. Will West Brom be tempted to protect their advantage, I wonder?
Back to events at The Hawthorns and it might not be long until Mark Hughes turns to his bench. The likes of Mame Biram Diouf, Marko Arnautovic and the fit-again Stephen Ireland could provide the energy Stoke have lacked up to now.
While Stoke have been poor in this match so far, things are much worse for Sunderland, who find themselves FOUR GOALS DOWN at home to Aston Villa at half-time. A remarkable scoreline!
(45’) HALF-TIME: West Brom lead through a Brown Ideye header and a one-goal advantage is the least they deserve.
(45’) Dawson leaps high to head Adam's delivery away and any pressure is swiftly relieved as Moses brings down Gardner on the edge of West Brom's area.
(45’) Two minutes to be added on at The Hawthorns, where home goalkeeper Foster has had very little to do so far. Stoke have a chance to change that with a free-kick on the right.
(44’) Gardner charges down a long ball forward from Pieters, only to be penalised for handball. The atmosphere has cranked up a notch with the interval approaching and West Brom's supporters clearly feel aggrieved.
(42’) West Brom's centre-forwards are able to continue, but the home fans and players are not impressed with Adam, who kicks the ball right into the corner after the Baggies had put the ball out for Ideye to receive treatment. Fletcher has words with his fellow Scot.
(41’) Berahino and Sessegnon have caused problems throughout this first half, but the former is left limping after a seemingly innocuous collision with Charlie Adam. Brown Ideye is also hurt after a tackle from the same Stoke midfielder.
(39’) The set-piece comes to nothing. You get the feeling Stoke may be happy for half-time to arrive, so they can regroup. This has not been the sort of performance you would anticipate from a side that has won their last three.
(37’) Stoke appear to be lacking a spark at present and can consider themselves fortunate to only be a goal behind. Whelan concedes another free-kick near the corner flag on the left, fouling the lively Sessegnon.
(35’) That was a real howler from Begovic, who will be mightily relieved that his uncharacteristic blunder has not proved costly. Pulis is furious, but Ideye was offside as the initial ball was played through.
(34’) IDEYE HAS THE BALL IN THE NET AGAIN, BUT THE GOAL IS DISALLOWED!! Begovic drops the ball at the feet of the striker, who accepts the gift to score. However, the goalkeeper's blushes are spared by an offside flag.
(32’) Stoke slow things down before hitting Crouch with a diagonal ball. The former England striker attempts an ambitious half-volley on the turn, but his effort comfortably clears the crossbar.
(30’) ALMOST A SECOND FOR WEST BROM!! Dawson delivers a lovely pass into the right channel for Berahino, who drags his shot across goal with the angle narrowing rapidly.
(28’) West Brom are pressing the ball very well, as you might expect from a Tony Pulis side. A period of Stoke possession comes to nothing before Ideye wins a free-kick on halfway.
(26’) Craig Dawson overlaps down the right for West Brom and is almost found by Sessegnon. Chris Brunt swings over the resulting corner and Fletcher fires over after the initial delivery is headed out to the edge of the box by Peter Crouch.
(23’) Moses continues to look the most likely source of a goal for Stoke, who are looking to regroup after Ideye's goal. The visitors win a corner, but Adam's delivery evades everyone and goes out for a goal kick.
(20’) It looked as though Stoke were starting to get on top after their shaky start, but Mark Hughes' men now find themselves behind and with work to do to extend their winning run at this venue.
--- 19’ Assist C. Gardner gave the assist. ---
--- 19’ Goal! GOAL to West Brom! Brown Ideye!! Gardner curls over a cross from the right and Ideye is too strong for Phil Bardsley. Having got in front of his marker, he directs a low header beyond Begovic to delight the home fans! ---
(17’) Ideye goes down easily under pressure from Shawcross and the referee is less than impressed. Moses is seeing more and more of the ball as the Potters start to find their stride.
(15’) Stoke appear to have weathered the early storm and are starting to enjoy longer spells of possession. Moses sees a shot from distance blocked before Darren Fletcher does well to cut out a dangerous cross from the left.
(11’) Stoke threaten for the first time as the ball breaks to Moses 30 yards from goal. He has space to shoot, but fires high into the stand behind Ben Foster's goal.
(10’) Victor Moses tracks back well to snuff out another West Brom attack. Applause rings around The Hawthorns in memory of former Baggies striker Jeff Astle.
(8’) Another shot from Berahino takes a deflection, but Begovic is equal to the task again. Stoke are struggling to impose themselves early on.
(6’) Good work from Sessegnon leads to another West Brom corner. Pulis' men have made a very bright start here, although Glenn Whelan clears the latest set-piece at the near post.
(3’) The first chance of the game goes to the hosts, but Asmir Begovic is able to parry a 20-yard effort from Saido Berahino away for a corner.
(2’) Unsurprisingly, Albion are keen to get the ball into their forwards early in the opening minutes. Stoke will be likely to adopt a more patient approach.
(1’) Referee Michael Oliver blows his whistle and the action is under way!
The players have taken the field and we are just about ready to get started. Can Stoke continue their winning run at West Brom, or will Pulis get one over on his old team? Let's find out.
Stoke have only faced Pulis once since the Welshman departed the Britannia Stadium at the end of the 2012-13 season. On that occasion, Pulis oversaw a 1-0 home win for Crystal Palace against his former employers. A repeat of that result would do quite nicely for West Brom today, but their opponents arrive on the back of three successive wins.

FULL TIME - Burnley 1-0 Man City: The crowd at Turf Moor are jubilant as their side have defeated the reigning Premier League champions, moving up to 18th position and reducing the gap to safety to just one point! The Citizens could now go eight points adrift of Chelsea should Jose Mourinho's men defeat Southampton tomorrow. Their title challenge takes another huge dent.
(90’) There it is! It's full time and Burnley have secured a huge three points!
(90’) The whistle still hasn't gone!
(90’) Demichelis foolishly takes out Barnes midway inside the City half, resulting in a free kick for the Clarets that they send down towards the corner. They just want to run down the remaining seconds here.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution S. Reid comes on for D. Ings. ---
(90’) Steven Reid comes on for Ings to help solidfy things in the final few minutes. Bony stretches to control the ball on his chest inside the box, but he is deemed to have used his arm so the referee awards the hosts a free kick.
(90’) We are now into the second of the four added minutes at the end of this game.
(90’) PENALTY CLAIM FOR CITY! DENIED! Zabaleta bursts into the box and goes down under a challenge from Mee. The Burnley man doesn't touch the ball at all, but the Argentine is adjudged to be guilty of simulation! The City players are not happy with that decision.
(90’) Bony commits a foul on Ings inside the centre circle, and you would expect the Clarets to take their time over this set-piece, possibly just sending it down to the corner flag.
(89’) There's not much time left for City to get one back, or for Burnley to hold on. The visitors are keeping their hosts penned back inside their own half, but an overhit pass from Lampard down the right-hand channel, intended for Navas, rolls behind for a goal kick.
--- 87’ Substitution S. Ward comes on for S. Vokes. ---
(87’) Dyche makes his first substitution of the evening, with Voakes going off to be replaced by Ward.
(86’) Lampard's effort flies straight into the wall, but he manages to keep it alive by lifting the rebound out to Navas on the right. The Spaniard also fails to beat the nearest defender though, and the pressure ends with Jovetic firing high and wide from 25 yards.
(85’) Barnes is penalised for a jumping into a challenge with Lampard after the ball looped up off the turf on the bounce. The former Chelsea man is standing over the resultant set-piece, which is around 30 yards out in a central area.
(83’) Everyone but Ings is back behind the ball for Burnley now. Boyd tracks back and puts in a good challenge to deny Jovetic the chance to get a cross in from City's left. The visitors work it over to the opposite side, but the Scot is there again, inadvertently sending a header back to Heaton.
(82’) That is Toure's last contribution as he is replaced by Lampard for the remainder.
--- 81’ Substitution Y. Touré is replaced with F. Lampard. ---
(81’) WHAT A CHANCE! Navas picks up the ball on the right but rather than drive to the byline he rolls a pass back to Toure. The imposing midfielder swings a cross to the back post, where it is met by Aguero who fails to guide his header on target!
(79’) Vokes surges forward down the right and has Boyd and Ings up in support. He attempts to square inside for the Scot but his pass is intercepted. If he'd managed to pick out his team-mate then they could well have put the game beyond the visitors.
(78’) Barnes tries his luck with an effort from 25 yards but he aims it too close to Hart, who holds the shot at the first time of asking. The keeper tries to get his team moving forwards as quickly as possible but his options are limited, so he has to track back and kick it long.
(76’) Aguero feeds his striker partner, Bony, at the top of the box and the Ivorian takes a touch to create room for a shot. He then lets fly but the attempt he produces is never going to get the better of Heaton, who saves.
(75’) Clichy clips a cross into the centre of the box which Shackell heads away. He only sends it as far as Fernandinho, though, who blazes an effort from distance high over the frame of the goal.
--- 74’ Substitution David Silva is replaced with S. Jovetić. ---
(74’) Now Pellegrini makes his second substitution of the night, replacing Silva with a more direct goal threat in Stevan Jovetic.
(73’) The ball drops for Toure at the corner of the box on the near side, and he connects with it sweetly to arrow a powerful shot towards the goal. A deflection sends it far wide, though, and the corner comes to nothing.
--- 71’ Yellow card M. Duff is cautioned by the referee. ---
(71’) Duff is booked after flying through the back of Aguero midway inside his own half. The resultant free kick is clipped into the box towards Bony, but the Ivorian can only muster a weak header that bounces up and into the waiting arms of Heaton.
(69’) This would be the biggest result of Burnley's season, and could supply them with the perfect starter for a push to stay in the division.
(67’) Pellegrini still has the likes of Nasri and Lampard available on the bench, both of whom could help turn this game around.
(65’) How are City going to respond to going behind? They cannot afford to drop more points or their Premier League title defence will suffer heavily.
--- 63’ Substitution Edin Dzeko's day is done, his only real contribution producing a fine save from Heaton midway through the first half. Wilfried Bony is on to replace him, and what a time this would be for him to open his Manchester City scoring account. ---
--- 61’ Goal! BURNLEY TAKE THE LEAD AT TURF MOOR! What a goal that could be for the Clarets in their quest for survival! Kompany carelessly heads away a free kick, straight into the path of Boyd. The midfielder doesn't let it fall, hitting a brilliant first-time volley past Hart and into the far corner! Incredible scenes at Turf Moor! These fans know just how much that goal could mean for them come May. ---
--- 60’ Yellow card Burnley are looking increasingly threatening on the counter. Ings charges forward in possession and Demichelis is forced to take out the striker as he's beaten for pace, picking up a yellow card for his troubles. ---
--- 58’ Yellow card SO CLOSE! A ball is played into the area for Vokes, but Demichelis arrives first. His header only partially clears the ball, sending it straight into the path of Boyd. The midfielder shows excellent technique, driving a well-hit volley at goal, but it swerves just wide of the post with Hart surely beaten. Back the other way come City and Mee runs through the back of Navas to pick up the first yellow card of the match. ---
(56’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester City have scored at least a goal in 20 consecutive road matches, averaging nearly 2.25 per game over that span. The last time they were held scoreless in a Premier League match was in a nil-nil draw against Norwich City in February 2014 at Carrow Road.
(54’) Brilliant work from Zabaleta to burst into the area, skipping past two defenders on his way to the byline. He picks out a superb cutback pass for Aguero, but the striker turns it wide of the near post with his first-time effort!
(52’) WASTED OPPORTUNITY! Zabaleta heads away a Trippier free kick and Aguero gets the ball at the halfway line. He turns brilliantly to get past a defender and is in two-against-one with Silva. He rolls a pass across for the Spaniard, who has a clean look on goal, but he gets his first touch horribly wrong and can't test Heaton with his shot.
(50’) Tremendous work from Ings! The striker does very well to bring down a long-ball forward and bullies his way past Demichelis. His final touch is a bit heavy, however, allowing Kompany to come across and rescue his side.
(48’) Aguero is lucky to escape without a booking as he catches Duff with his cleats out. There did not appear to be any intent in the challenge, but it is a bit reckless from the striker. Duff has to make his way off for a moment, walking gingerly to the sidelines under his own power.
(46’) Underway now in the second half as Burnley kick-off. No goals and no changes to tell you about at the break.
HALF TIME: BURNLEY 0-0 MANCHESTER CITY. Chances have been few and far between after 45 minutes, with the visitors holding a slight edge thanks to a better period towards the end of the half. Pellegrini's side certainly don't appear to be full of goals today and are being held largely at bay by strong team performance from Burnley. Three points are a must for City, and though Sean Dyche would be delighted with a victory as well, a draw would do them well in their quest for survival.
(45’) The whistle sounds at 45 minutes exactly as a relatively uneventful first half comes to an end at Turf Moor.
(43’) Navas needs to pick it up along the right. He's getting the ball with plenty of space to try and create, but has yet to pick out a real testing delivery. Another attempted cross is turned behind by Mee before the Clarets deal with the resulting corner with relative ease.
(41’) City are going to have to work hard for an opener. Burnley look very comfortable in defence. It doesn't have to be pretty at this point for Manuel Pellegrini's side, but it is going to take plenty of perseverance and relentless pressure for them to find a way through.
(39’) Burnley are keeping their shape very well, affording City very few openings in the attacking half. They are absorbing the pressure well, but have to be careful here as they are seeing far less possession than they had in the first half-hour, allowing the visitors to keep pressing.
(37’) City are starting to knock on the door, but they still don't look a whole lot like scoring. They appear far too sluggish throughout this first half and though they are starting to find their legs from under them, creativity has been hard to come by for them in midfield.
(35’) STAT ATTACK: Burnley are winless in their last seven Premier League matches (D2, L4). They have just one victory in the last 12 league fixtures, with only Aston Villa picking up fewer points over that span before today.
(33’) SCUFFED OVER! Brilliant play from the Citizens. Navas runs into space on the right and picks out Silva atop the area. The Spaniard delivers a splendid first-time pass into the path of Dzeko, but Shackell does so well to break up the chance. Aguero arrives to follow up, but he can't hit the target from a difficult angle.
(31’) City are finally starting to mount a bit of concentrated pressure on the Burnley defence. Fernandinho picks up the ball atop the area following a corner and makes a good run along the right, but his low, driven cross is turned over smartly by Shackell.
(29’) SMART SAVE! Finally we have our first shot on target and it has taken nearly half an hour. Dzeko is played through inside the left channel, but Heaton sticks out a leg to keep the striker's shot out at the near post.
(27’) Now City are the ones enjoying a lengthy spell in possession, but again there is little intent being showed. The ball has hardly left the midfield third for more than a few seconds. Aguero needs to drop deeper to get on the ball because service has been sorely lacking.
(25’) Burnley pass the ball around patiently in midfield, with City showing no real intent to win it back. The hosts are doing precious little with it, however, as the match enters yet another tedious period with the ball being largely contained in midfield.
(23’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester City have won just three of their last 10 matches across all competitions (D3, L4). It is their fewest amount of victories over a 10 game span since February to March of 2010, though they only lost twice during that period.
(21’) Splendid delivery! Trippier is the focal point again in attack, making a good run into space on the right before getting on the end of a pass. He delivers a teasing ball into the area, which Vokes attacks, but the striker sends his header wide of the near post.
(19’) Sergio Aguero is starting to take matters into his own hands. He picks up the ball from 35 yards out and begins running at goal. Barnes fails to break up the move as he commits himself too early, but manages to force Aguero wide, before Mee gets an easy block in to turn the ball out for a City throw.
(17’) Another corner for the hosts, who are looking the more dangerous side at the moment. They have had more intent to get forward, though they have yet to make life uncomfortable on the City defence. This time Dzeko rises well to clear the corner, but again they cannot keep possession as they try and break forward with pace.
(15’) It has been far too predictable from the visitors thus far in attack. They certainly do not look like title contenders through the opening quarter of an hour. Burnley are trying to constrict the midfield area and have done an excellent job of not chasing the ball and falling into City's trap.
(13’) Burnley have enjoyed some of their most threatening moments in attack this season when Kieran Trippier gets forward along the flank. (11’) STAT ATTACK: Burnley's last victory over Manchester City came in October 1974, a 2-1 triumph at Turf Moor. The Clarets are winless in 13 matches against the Sky Blues since then, across all competitions (D5, L8).

The rather slow pace in the early stages here has come as a bit of a surprise, with both teams expected to show a bit of urgency in claiming all three points.

(90’) There may be time for one more attack...
(90’) Chelsea just can't find the space to put the ball in the box. Saints are holding form and are just moments away from seeing this out for a point.
(90’) Southampton manage to dispossess their hosts and quickly look to break. Pelle angles a long diagonal ball out to the right for Mane to chase but he puts too much on it and it goes out for a goal kick.
(90’) We are into the first of four added minutes.

Despite picking up an excellent 2-1 victory at home to Dynamo Kyiv in the Europa League during the week, things remain as bleak as ever for Everton on the domestic front, as a disappointing season in which they have only won six games has left them just three points clear of the relegation zone in 14th place, with only one victory from their last 12 league clashes. The Toffees’ home form has been just as poor, too, with their last win at Goodison Park coming against Queens Park Rangers in December, whilst their last four games here have all ended in draws. To say that today’s tie is a must-win is an understatement, as Roberto Martinez’s men desperately need three points to help pull them away from the jaws of the dreaded drop zone, which looks increasingly likely to swallow them up if they are not able to improve their form quickly.

(34’) What a chance for Hull! A half-hearted Sunderland attack breaks down, allowing Livermore to break away on a quick counter attack. He sprints down the right wing before trying to tee up Jelavic, but his low cross is poor and is sent behind the Croatian and away from danger.
(32’) A glorious lofted pass from Meyler finds El Mohamady on the right-hand side of the Sunderland penalty area. The Egyptian brings the ball down well before skipping past Reveillere, but, off balance, he fires his cross out of play for a goal kick.
(30’) Again, Hull put good pressure on the Sunderland midfield, forcing Cattermole into firing another long ball towards Defoe that completely misses the striker and flies into the hands of McGregor.

(27’) Robertson sprints down the left wing and into the Sunderland box, but Reveillere is just about able to tackle the youngster at the last moment, sending the ball out of play for a corner.

(17’) Sunderland patiently pass the ball around in the middle of the pitch before Cattermole attempts to send a lofted pass over the top of the Hull defence and into the path of Defoe, but it's completely overhit and comfortably sails into the hands of McGregor.

As for Sunderland, they head to the KC Stadium on the back of a disappointing four-game winless run that has seen them slowly but surely slip further towards the relegation zone. In that time, the Black Cats have lost at home to QPR and been held to a draw by West Bromwich Albion, two sides that have also found themselves at the wrong end of the Premier League table. Southampton's European push is back on track thanks to a slender 1-0 win over Crystal Palace. On the whole, the home side probably just about deserve their victory, though they were made to work for all three points, as Palace created several good chances in the second period. Nevertheless, Mane's late goal sees Saints claim the win and move back to within a point of United in the final UEFA Champions League spot.
FULL-TIME!
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card D. Delaney goes into the referee's book. ---
(90’) Forster comes out to punch the subsequent corner away, but it goes straight back out wide. Puncheon eventually tries to curl a teasing left-footed cross into the area, but it misses everyone and goes wide of the post.
(90’) Good play by Ward, as he intercepts a wayward pass, carries the ball forward and slips Bolasie in down the right. His powerful delivery is threatening, but Yoshida stretches and knocks it behind.
(90’) There will be four minutes added on here.
(87’) Palace are certainly trying for a leveller, anyway. Kelly comes forward from left-back for what must be one of the first times today and he crosses into the area. Bolasie meets it with a header, but it causes Forster no issues.
(85’) Palace have to come out of their shell again now. They appeared all set to steal a point from Saints here, with most of their men sitting back and protecting the clean sheet, but their hard work has seemingly been undone. Can they muster a late equaliser?
--- 84’ Substitution Shola Ameobi enters play, replacing J. McArthur. ---
--- 83’ Goal! GOAL!!! SAINTS HAVE THEIR GOAL! Space opens up in the final third for Ward-Prowse, who skips past the challenge of Dann and shoots from the edge of the area. Speroni fails to hold on to his effort and Mane pounces, coolly prodding over the helpless goalkeeper from close range. ---
(82’) That's a chance! Tadic latches on to Ward-Prowse's pass into the penalty area and he manages to squeeze a cross in from the left, but Long, who gets there ahead of Kelly, can only hit his first-time effort over.
(80’) Good play by Wanyama, as the Kenyan marches into the area, riding several challenges before trying to cross into the goalmouth. Ward covers well, though, and concedes a corner.
--- 78’ Substitution J. Ward-Prowse enters play, replacing F. Đuričić. ---
(78’) Tadic comes across and takes the free-kick, curling an effort over the crossbar and subsequently into the stands. A decent attempt, though it never looked like beating Speroni.
(77’) Palace are trying to create chances for themselves on the break now, with Zaha, Bolasie and Gayle all staying up along the halfway line. They have defending to do at the moment, though, as Mane is hauled down by Ledley.
(75’) After a bit of a delay, Tadic lofts his free-kick delivery in towards the Palace area, with Fonte almost getting on the end of it, but the away side clear the danger.
(73’) All the pressure is coming from Saints at the moment and they have themselves a free-kick about 35 yards from goal now, after Schneiderlin is knocked over.
(71’) Excellent defending from Fonte. Bolasie threatens to surge past him and into the area, but the Portuguese centre-back anticipates his move well and nudges him off the ball fairly, with the winger going down rather theatrically.
--- 70’ Substitution G. Pellè is replaced with S. Long. ---

(68’) Good move by Saints! Djuricic takes up possession on the left in his own half and he races away from a couple of defenders after producing a marvellous pirouette. He gets all the way to the edge of the area and finds Clyne, who instantly passes into the centre for Pelle, but Dann watches him all the way.
(66’) The match is currently going through a rather scrappy period, as neither side appears to have much control over proceedings or the tempo. Is this going to be another disappointing result for the hosts?
(64’) Clyne appears to have blood running from his nose following a collision with Bolasie, though the referee has not spotted it and he continues to play on.
(62’) Clever play by Tadic, who takes the corner short, shapes to cut inside and on to his left foot, before playing Schneiderlin in with a reverse pass. The Frenchman's delivery is aimed for Pelle, though he cannot twist his body enough in order to make contact and Palace escape.

--- 60’ Substitution D. Tadić comes on for E. Elia. ---
(59’) First throw of the dice for Koeman, as the Dutchman withdraws his compatriot Elia and introduces Tadic.
(57’) Southampton really know they are in a game in this match. However, they find themselves back on the front foot rather quickly, as Elia races up the left and cuts inside. Eventually the ball comes back to him after Wanyama managed to keep the move alive, but the Dutchman's eventual shot goes well over.
(55’) HOW HAVE PALACE NOT SCORED? Bolasie charges away from Bertrand and gets a shot away from the edge of the area. Southampton 0-0 Crystal Palace: And so ends a fairly unspectacular first half at St. Mary's. The hosts have largely dictated proceedings so far, enjoying a greater share of the possession and affording Palace few sights of goal. But at the same time, Koeman's side have struggled to create clear-cut opportunities, with the service into Pelle proving rather poor. Mane, Djuricic and Elia have all looked lively in flashes, though their final pass must improve.
(45’) HALF-TIME!
(45’) There will be a minute added on here.

This time he plays a give-and-go with Pelle, before then looking to shoot from the edge of the area. Palace do well to crowd him out, though, forcing the winger to pass out to the left and the attack comes to an end, as Elia's delivery is knocked away.

(33’) Southampton have undoubtedly had the better of this so far, but Koeman must be disappointed that his side have failed to test Speroni. Djuricic's wayward attempt from 18 yards stands as their only real opportunity until now and that never looked like troubling the goalkeeper.
(31’) The Palace set-piece goes deep and is headed back into the danger zone by Puncheon on the edge of the box. (20’) Mane is terrorising Kelly at the moment. He charges inside the full-back following a clever flick out wide and the defender pulls him back, conceding an obvious foul.

Southampton will be looking to kick-start their bid for a UEFA Champions League spot today. Ronald Koeman's men have lost three of their last five in the English top flight and have fallen four points behind fourth-placed Manchester United, while Tottenham sit just two points behind and Mauricio Pochettino's side have played a game less. Jose Fonte spoke about boosting morale before this match and a victory will undoubtedly go a long way to improving the atmosphere in the team, while Palace are hoping to claim their fourth consecutive away win in the league.

Midfielder Jordon Mutch picked up an injury in the weekend win at West Ham, joining Marouane Chamakh, Frazier Campbell, Jonny Williams, Yaya Sanogo and Jerome Thomas in the treatment room, while Glenn Murray - the recipient of a red card at Upton Park - is suspended. (47’) BONY! He should be doing better again! Silva does brilliantly to get to the byline and reverses a perfect pass into the centre, but the Ivorian drags his right-footed strike wide of the post!

Half time at the Etihad. It has, for the most part, been attack versus defence here as Manchester City aim to bounce back from their recent defeats against a sturdy Leicester side. It looked likely that we would be equal at the break until David Silva popped up on the stroke of half time to net from close range. The visitors will certainly have to show more attacking ambition in the next 45! Interesting second period in store!
--- 45’ +2 Goal! GOOOAAAAAAAALLLLLLLL FOR MAN CITY! NO SETTLING HERE!!! Kolarov breaks down the left and fires a dangerous cross into the are. There are a couple of blocked shots inside the six-yard box but the ball falls kindly for Silva, who smashes home from close range! One-nil! ---
(44’) Just the one minute of added time from the officials here as Man City pursue the opening goal before the break. Quite a low intensity though, so it looks like both sides are settling for the draw at half time.
(42’) BONYYYYY! JUST OVER! Silva comes into central midfield and dinks a sensational pass into the box for the Ivorian, who initially takes a superb touch on his chest before turning towards goal, but the left-footed strike at goal goes high and wide! Considering his recent price tag, you'd fancy him to do better than that!
(40’) After that frenzied few minutes in which Man City managed to test the goalkeeper, they have reverted back into their short passing in the middle of midfield, with Leicester sitting deep. If they can manage to take the lead before the break, it will have to signal a change in tactic from the visitors.
(38’) Aguero drops deep to receive the ball and takes on one or two opposition players before looking to exchange a one-two with Toure. The next pass comes and the Argentine looks to pull the trigger 20 yards out, but an important tackle comes in from James who just nicks the ball away!
--- 36’ Yellow card P. Konchesky is yellow-carded. ---
(36’) Konchesky is pulled back by the referee to receive a yellow card for a late challenge on Silva that went previously unpunished due to the advantage that was played in the lead up to the Bony chance. Deserved booking for the left-back.
(35’) Schwarzer to the rescue again! Navas collects the ball on the inside left channel this time and cuts inside on his right foot before bending a wicked strike towards the far right corner. The goalkeeper stretches out his sizeable frame to beat the attempt round the post, though!
(33’) SAVE FROM SCHWARZER! The referee plays an excellent advantage for City down the right wing and Navas drives at pace to the byline before reversing into the box. Bony gets ahead of his marker to turn a strike at goal, but the Australian remains solid to make the block on the line! Best move of the game from the home side!
(31’) Kramaric really is working hard as the lone striker at the moment. Cambiasso lobs a pretty nothing pass down into the right channel and the 23-year-old bursts a gut to relentlessly press and chase down Kolarov, who is forced to put out for a throw in.
(29’) A long ball is sent into the Leicester box and then falls kindly to Kramaric inside the box. The Croatian decides against hitting the ball first time and instead lays off Simpson, but the subsequent cross to the back post bounces off a Leicester leg and goes behind for a goal kick.
(27’) There are just currently one or two signs that the game is becoming a little more stretched. Leicester have Kramaric, Mahrez, and Schlupp committed forward and as a result the Man City midfield is being awarded more possession in the final third. Still waiting for some more creativity in and around the penalty area, though.
(25’) Superb goalkeeping from Hart! Mangala loses the ball in a dangerous position in midfield and Schlupp robs possession before sliding a pass through the middle for Kramaric. The Croatian just allows the ball to run ahead of him slightly which allows the England goalkeeper to claw away!
(23’) Penalty shout for Leicester! Bony and Schlupp collide inside the penalty box but the referee waves away the protests! On a second look it looked like the Leicester man may have tripped up over his own leg, so good decision from the official!
(21’) Kramaric receives the ball to feet with his back to goal near the touchline and holds the ball up well before being fouled with a daft challenge by Mangala. James floats the resulting free kick into the box and it is cleared behind for a corner kick. First real few moments of pressure from the visitors!
(19’) Again, Leicester revert back to 11 men behind the ball when City have the ball, and it has to be said that they have looked rather comfortable in their defending so far. Apart from that header from Bony that was cleared off the line, there hasn't been too much threat coming from Pellegrini's men so far.
(17’) Kramaric collects possession down the left-hand side and twists and turns next to Sagna in an attempt to find space to get a cross in. The ball into the box comes but Mangala is well-positioned to clear with a commanding header. Good defending.
(15’) In one of their only ventures forward so far, Leicester manage to break out of midfield through Schlupp. The winger slides a pass into the feet of Mahrez and looks for the one-two inside the box, but the return ball runs harmlessly through to Hart.
(13’) The way this match is panning out it looks like we are going to see attack versus defence for the majority of the time. Man City are completely dominating possession as Leicester keep every man behind the ball, looking to pounce on any loose balls. Much concentration required from the visitors at the moment!
(11’) Silva receives the ball to feet in his favourite position just in front of the opposition defence. The Spaniard spots the run of Aguero and looks to pass in behind, but again a lack of communication means the ball runs out for a goal kick. That duo, who are usually so effective, are still to wake up since the opening whistle!
(9’) Mahrez looks to take the pressure off his defence with a penetrating run through the middle before passing back to Cambiasso. The Argentine then fires a pass over the top of the defence for Kramaric, but Hart vigilantly comes off his line to clear up the park and into the stand.
(8’) Toure and Silva exchange a couple of neat passes inside the Leicester half and the Ivorian then takes a few strides forward before trying his luck from distance with a 35-yard strike. It is a decent attempt, but relatively comfortable in the end for Schwarzer.
(6’) Aguero opens up his stride through the middle and looks to dart into the penalty area, but in an uncharacteristic lack of communication, runs straight into the chest of Silva. A promising attack comes to nothing for City!
(4’) OFF THE LINE BY CAMBIASSO! Silva whips a corner kick into the centre of the penalty area and Bony rises high to glance a header towards the bottom corner, but the Argentine is on hand to clear away the danger! Almost a dream full debut for the Ivorian striker!
(2’) Perhaps predictably, City have asserted their dominance in terms of their possession rather early here. Leicester have plenty of speed up top through Kramaric, Schlupp, and Mahrez, and it looks like they'll be looking to counterattack whenever possible.
(1’) We are under way at the Etihad!
The teams have made their way to the pitch and we are almost ready for kick off!
No changes for Leicester, meanwhile.

Newcastle have stayed in 11th place after losing to Man United tonight and they now turn their attentions to a trip to struggling Everton on Sunday, while the Red Devils face Arsenal in the sixth-round of the FA Cup next Monday.

Abeid does well to initially nick the ball off Rooney inside his own half but he chooses to play the ball back to Krul, who couldn't sort his feet out from point-blank range and sliced his clearance to Young, who was on hand to supply a massive winner for Man United.
Young taps home from close range in the dying minutes to wrap up a massive three points for Man United in the race for a top-four finish. The Red Devils were the better side on the night in terms of chances created, but Newcastle have plenty of reason to feel agrieved at full-time, with the Magpies being denied a clear first-half penalty.

(90’) Janmaat latches onto a loose ball and bends in a good cross towards the penalty area, but Smalling rises high and heads away the danger. Man United are doing their best to grind out the win here.
(90’) Newcastle boss Carver looks absolutely deflated on the touchline as Man United look on course to steal all three points here tonight. The Magpies have defended well for most of the game, and had a few chances to score themselves, but a mix-up at the back has gifted Young a potential winner.
(90’) WHAT A HUGE SAVE!! Cisse latches onto a terrific cross from Gouffran and heads towards the bottom corner, but De Gea gets down tremendously to deny Newcastle nicking a late equaliser. Magnificent goalkeeping from the Spaniard.
--- 89’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAALLL!! Man United look set to pick up a massive three points on the road thanks to a last-gasp finish from Young. Abeid nicks the ball away from Rooney brilliantly inside his own box, but he plays a back-pass to Krul, who slices the ball straight to Young, who taps home from close range. ---
--- 89’ Substitution M. Rojo is replaced with M. Carrick. ---
(88’) Rojo, who was perhaps fortunate to not receive a second yellow card for a foul on Gouffran a few moments ago, walks off the pitch for Carrick, who is coming on as his replacement.
(86’) Rojo drives a cross towards Rooney, who chests down play inside the penalty area and looks to spin around, but Coloccini steps in front of him superbly well and clears the danger for his side brilliantly. It looks as though Man United could be set for an ninth Premier League draw, as Newcastle are really standing firm defensively tonight.
--- 84’ Yellow card A. Valencia is yellow-carded. ---
(84’) Valencia gets his name into the referee's book after he fouls Gouffran down the left hand side. The Newcastle substitute launches a counter-attack for the hosts, but the Man United man illegally prevents him in his tracks, before the referee awards him a yellow for doing so.
--- 82’ Substitution M. Fellaini is done for the day. Mata is his replacement. ---
(82’) Blind nicks the ball past Sissoko but fails to get a serious grip of it, before the Frenchman comes back and retrieves possession for his side. The Dutchman is hobbling gingerly from that tussle at the moment.
--- 81’ Substitution Y. Gouffran enters play, replacing Sammy Ameobi. ---
(80’) Ameobi walks off the pitch to a good reception from the home supporters, with Gouffran set to replace him. The young winger didn't really get into the game going forward, but defensively, he was excellent tonight. Fellaini is the man who is being taken off for Mata, who has scored three goals in his last three appearances at St. James' Park.
(78’) Man United could be set for another roll of the dice in search of a crucial winner, with Mata currently warming up for the Red Devils. Gouffran is also set to come on for Newcastle, too.
(76’) Januzaj picks up the ball from Herrera and attempts to cut inside from the right hand side and whip in a cross, but Ameobi again tracks back excellently to keep his side on course for at least a point come full-time.
(74’) Young drives down the left hand side past Janmaat and bends in a lovely cross towards Rooney, who climbs above Gutierrez at the back post and powers a header down towards Krul, who parries the ball wide before he grabs hold of it. Yet another great move by the visitors, but also another one that is denied from finding the back of the net.
(72’) Perez is up and moving again after Fellaini accidently stands on the young Spaniard's ankle when trying to get out of a cul-de-sac down the left hand side of the pitch.
(70’) Manchester City, Arsenal, Liverpool and Tottenham are all currently winning elsewhere in the Premier League and therefore Man United really need to push men forward here in search of a goal, if they don't want to lose ground in the mouth-watering race for a top-four finish.
(68’) WHAT A CHANCE! Perez nicks the ball off Herrera in the middle of the park and surges forward on the counter-attack. The youngster drives towards Man United's goal and feeds in Cisse, who takes the ball forward slightly before he scuffs his effort agonisingly wide of De Gea's goal. Big chance.
--- 67’ Yellow card J. Gutiérrez receives a yellow card. ---
(67’) The introduction of Gutierrez has certainly given the atmosphere inside St. James' Park a lift here, with the home supporters cheering his every action, though the referee has just awarded him a yellow card after he fouled Januzaj down the left hand side.
--- 65’ Substitution J. Gutiérrez enters play, replacing R. Taylor. ---
(65’) Loud cheers and moving tributes fly around St. James' Park as Gutierrez comes on for the remainder of the second-half. The Argentine man, who has recently made a return to the game following his battle with cancer, has also been given the captain's armband here, too.
(63’) Blind ghosts into the middle of the park and plays in a peach of a cross towards Rooney, who bursts past Williamson but, again, the referee judges him to be offisde and awards a free-kick for the hosts. Another good bit of movement from the Man United skipper.
(61’) The first involvement of Januzaj occurs as he dips in from the right hand side and attempts to play in Fellaini, but his cross flies wide of his Belgian compatriot. Replays show that Rooney's earlier goal, which was chalked off for an apparant offside, was actually onside, although, again, the officials have to make a quick decision and don't have the benefit of replays.
--- 60’ Yellow card M. Rojo receives a yellow card. ---
--- 59’ Substitution Ayoze Pérez enters the game and replaces E. Rivière. ---
--- 59’ Substitution A. Januzaj enters play, replacing Á. di María. ---
(59’) The referee awards the first yellow card of the night to Rojo, who illegally prevents Obertan getting past him down the right hand side after the Frenchman flicked the ball over the top of the Man United defender terrifically.
(57’) OFFSIDE! Di Maria spins in-field from the right hand side and floats in a cracking pass towards Rooney, who drills the ball under Krul but the referee chalks the Man United skipper's goal off for offside. That pass looks as though it will be the Argentine's last action of the night, too, with Januzaj stripped and ready to come on.
(55’) While both sides will be disappointed they haven't found the back of the net so far tonight, the two goalkeepers have been in inspired form between their respective sticks.
(53’) INCREDIBLE PLAY FROM KRUL!! Di Maria clips in a top-drawer pass to Fellaini, who chests the ball down unmarked inside the box but Krul stands tall and denies the Belgian man from point-blank range. Young latches onto the spillage inside the penalty area, but Newcastle's Dutch shot-stopper gets straight up and denies the Man United winger with another superb save.
(51’) Rooney receives a pass from Fellaini and attempts to surge forwards on the break, but Sissoko follows him closely and nicks possession away from his feet brilliantly. The hosts are looking really bright in the opening stages of this second-half.
(49’) SO CLOSE! Coloccini superbly flicks on a Newcastle free-kick towards Riviere, who taps the ball towards goal but De Gea makes himself big and prevents the Frenchman from putting his side in front. What a start to the second-half we have had here, but the Magpies forward will be disappointed he hasn't scored from just a few yards out there.
(48’) CHANCE! Fellaini receives the ball from Rooney just outside the Newcastle box and feeds an advancing Rojo from left-back, who moves into a nice pocket of space in-field and drives a shot just wide of Krul between the sticks.
(47’) With Liverpool currently beating Burnley 1-0 elsewhere in the Premier League tonight, it will be interesting to see if Man United really up the tempo in their game in the second-half here, as they look to keep hold of their place in the top-four. As things stand, Newcastle would stay 11th with a point earned on home soil tonight.
(46’) Welcome back! Man United get us under way for the second-half here at St. James' Park, with neither side making a change to their starting line-ups at the interval.
Evans looks towards the floor as he spits and catches Cisse, who reacts angrily and spits straight at the neck of the Man United defender from inches away. It was a really ugly, disgusting confrontation between the pair and something no-one wants to see happen on a football pitch.
The Red Devils have passed up a few really good chances to break the deadlock, while there will certainly be a couple of talking points tomorrow morning from this game. While it appeared that Newcastle were unfortunate to have not won a clear penalty, Cisse was later saw exchanging words with Man United defender Evans, with both players spitting at each other after the pair initially challenged for an aerial ball.
Both sets of players head towards the tunnel for the interval as a thoroughly entertaining first-half ends here at St. James' Park. Man United perhaps edged it in terms of the amount of great chances they created, but Newcastle always looked a threat on the break and were unlucky to have not found the back of the net themselves.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 0-0 MANCHESTER UNITED.
(45’) Valencia surges down the right hand side and chucks in another peach of a cross towards Fellaini, before the referee blows up for a free-kick as the ex-Everton midfielder is judged to have fouled Williamson as he attempts to latch onto the ball coming into the box.
(44’) ALMOST! Sissoko marauds through the middle of midfield on the counter-attack and slips in a magnificently-weighted pass to Riviere, who fails to get a shot away as De Gea smothers him and the ball inside the box. Another bit of great goalkeeping in this match!
(43’) GREAT SAVE! Valencia flies down the right hand side past Ameobi and Taylor and sends in a delicious cross towards an unmarked Fellaini, who heads towards goal but Krul denies the Belgian his fifth goal of the season from point-blank range.
(40’) Taylor whips in a lovely corner towards the back post, but De Gea rises the highest and punches away the danger for his side. Newcastle have started to find a lot more joy in possession in these last few minutes.
(38’) The referee awards a free-kick to Newcastle as Cisse and Evans clash in the middle of the park. Both players had their legs tangled, with replays showing that the pair appeared to spit at each other, though there was no way the referee, Anthony Taylor, could have spotted the incidents.
(36’) Ameobi forces Valencia onto the back-foot before he blocks the Man United full-back's attempted cross towards Rooney inside the penalty area. The youngster has done well defensively for Newcastle tonight, yet it was another half chance the visitors were able to create.
(34’) Blind wins a free-kick from a challenge by Sissoko and plays a quick pass to Herrera, who slips in Rooney between the two centre-backs but Coloccini recovers excellently and allows Krul to collect for the hosts. Straight up the other end, Cisse latches onto a loose ball and fires just wide of De Gea's goal from a long-range position.
(32’) The atmosphere inside St. James' Park has gone a little silent in the last ten minutes as Man United are really starting to dominate this game now, but they can't afford to keep passing up chances to break the deadlock here, as Newcastle have frequently looked dangerous when using their excellent pace on the counter-attack tonight.
(30’) WHAT A LET-OFF! Coloccini trips over his own feet down the right hand side and Di Maria takes advantage of that gift from his Argentine compatriot as he curls in a low cross towards Rooney, but Krul rushes off his goal-line to prevent the Man United forward from tapping home from close range.
(28’) Just before Rooney failed to hit the target from close range, Di Maria ghosted past Taylor with ease and drifted inside the penalty area, before a last-ditch challenge from Ameobi prevented the former Real Madrid man from getting a shot away. The Red Devils have certainly been on the front foot in the last five minutes and they are starting to sparkle now.
(26’) HUGE CHANCE!! Rooney passes up a massive opportunity for Man United to take the lead. Di Maria spins in-field from the right hand side and feeds Young, who plays a phenomenal first-time pass to Rooney, who, perhaps fearful that he was offside, slices his effort wide with the goal at his mercy. What a chance for the visitors.
(24’) CLOSE! Valencia exchanges an exquisite one-two with Di Maria down the right hand side before he sends in a delightful cross towards Rooney at the back post, but Coloccini heads away the danger at the last minute. Top-drawer defending from the Newcastle man.
(22’) Young whips in a terrific corner from the right hand side towards Fellaini, who beats Sissoko at the back post and knocks down the ball towards Krul's goal, but his effort lacks pace as Williamson collects play and clears up-field for his side.
(20’) The referee stops play as Young falls down to the ground after a challenge from Sissoko in the middle of the park. Replays show that a flailing arm slightly catches the Man United man towards his face, but there was definitely no malice intended in the Frenchman's attemps to win the ball back for his side.
(18’) Further confirmation that Man United are operating in a back four formation tonight, as opposed to a back three which they have used often in the current campaign. Rojo has been fielded at left-back, with Smalling and Evans the centre-back pairing.
(16’) Coloccini fires in a free-kick towards the penalty area from his own half, but Fellaini beats Williamson in the air to set Man United on the break. Young surges forward down the right hand side from the loose ball, but Janmaat slides in superbly to prevent the ex-Aston Villa winger sending in a teasing cross.
(14’) CHANCE! Fellaini chests down a ball from Rojo and plays a lovely one-two with Rooney before he drives an effort straight at Coloccini. From the rebound, the Man United skipper holds up play excellently and feeds Rojo, who quickly slips in an onrushing Herrera first-time, but the Spaniard blazes over from close range. Brilliant football from the visitors.
(12’) Obertan again surges down the right hand side past Young and Rojo, but the Frenchman's low cross blasts into the arms of De Gea at the near post, rather than finding a Newcastle shirt inside the penalty area. The hosts are starting to look really bright on the breakaway.
(10’) BIG SHOUT! Riviere steams into the penalty area and it appears he gets a touch to a loose ball before Smalling brings him down inside the penalty area, but the referee wasn't interested in the home side's appeals one bit. Big call from Anthony Taylor, as replays show that the Frenchman was clearly fouled by the Man United defender.
(9’) Blind plays a square ball towards Young which Obertan seizes upon and breaks forward down the right hand side on the break, but the former Red Devils winger bends his cross too high while Cisse was lurking inside the penalty area. A good chance goes begging for the hosts.
(8’) Man United are, as perhaps expected, the side dominating possession at the moment, while Newcastle are set-up to hit the Red Devils on the counter-attack. It appears that Fellaini and Di Maria are indeed both playing off Rooney up top, but the visitors are currently operating in a back four, as opposed to a back three so far.
(6’) Valencia loses possession down the right hand side and Sissoko breaks forward as he collects the loose ball from the Ecuador international and wins a corner off Smalling for the Toon on the counter-attack. However, the resulting set-play flies past every man in black and white stripes as Man United clear comfortably.
(4’) It's great to see Ryan Taylor back on a football field for Newcastle tonight, it must be said. The ex-Wigan Athletic man has been without luck in recent years, having picked up two cruciate ligament injuries in quick succession.
(2’) WHAT A CHANCE! Abeid breathes a huge sight of relief early doors as Man United come within a whisker of taking the lead just minutes into this game. Di Maria nicks the ball off the young midfielder in the middle of the park and feeds Rooney, who slides a quick reverse pass to the Argentine but he opts not to pull the trigger, which proves costly as Coloccini snuffs the danger instead.

(90’) Villa throwing every player forward but they concede a free-kick. Krul launches it towards Cisse, as the Villans clear it long. Hutton gets down the right flank, trying to get involved.

(75’) Just 15 minutes to go for Villa to salvage something from this game! Sherwood targeted six wins from the remaining 12 games, but they look to be heading for another defeat here on Tyneside. Westwood breaks from a corner but is penalised for a foul.

--- 73’ Substitution E. Rivière is replaced with Ayoze Pérez. ---
(73’) Riviere does well to turn in the Villa box and tee-up Taylor, but the attack is cleared. Cleverley sends a cross on to Benteke, with N'Zogbia eventually sending his shot well over the crossbar!
(71’) GOAL RULED OUT! Benteke has the ball in the net but is ruled for offside after slotting home a brilliant cross, following a massive goal-mouth scramble! Sherwood's side starting to show some fight!
(70’) Janmaat's break forward from deep ends with Benteke nearly levelling for Villa! Taylor gets back and clears just before the striker could pounce on Agbonlahor's low driven delivery!
(68’) Sissoko is strong in midfield and lays off Obertan who breaks and has a chance to double his side's lead. But the Frenchman runs into trouble in the form of Irish defender Clark, as the attack is thwarted. Great chance for the Magpies to kill off the Villans!

(64’) Taylor has his long range effort saved by Guzan, as Newcastle press for another goal in these later stages! Clark sends a long ball forward to Benteke who controls and lays off Westwood. The move breaks down after a poor cross from the attacker!
--- 63’ Yellow card G. Agbonlahor goes into the referee's book. ---
