--- 61’ Substitution R. Taylor enters play, replacing M. Haïdara. ---
(60’) We've reached the hour mark at St James' Park and it's still the home side that continue to dominate proceedings on Tyneside! Hadaira is down injured, with Ryan Taylor set to come on as a replacement.
(58’) Riviere holds the ball up well for his side and finds Janmaat who was making another strong run forward. Obertan then wins a free-kick after a clumsy tackle from Westwood, who had earlier let Newcastle break from his poor delivery. Cisse makes a great run in front of the defence and sends his header just wide!
(56’) Delph is still struggling with a slight knock, meaning Villa's midfield has lost even more urgency. Ameobi's cross is blocked as Agbonlahor wins a throw in against the run of Janmaat. Sinclair is caught by Obertan and a free-kick in a dangerous position is won. Westwood's subsequent cross is blocked away easily.
(54’) The game has dramatically slowed down in this second period, something Sherwood will be unhappy about as Villa desperately need to find a goal. Williamson, who was sent off in this fixture before, takes out Agbonlahor down the wing and is booked.
--- 53’ Yellow card M. Williamson gets yellow. ---
(52’) Benteke is again unable to reach a through ball, this time from Westwood. The striker is becoming increasingly frustrated as Villa fail to create a clear-cut chance for their frontman!
(50’) Newcastle's midfield is still proving to be too strong for the visitors, with Sissoko dominating proceedings. Cleverley tries to find Benteke but his lofted through ball is hit too hard for the frontman to reach.
(48’) Ameobi picks up a stray ball from the goalscorer Cisse, but his subsequent cross is easily taken by the towering figure of Guzan. At the other end, Williamson comes across to strongly defend a threatening run from wideman Sinclair.
(46’) Both Villa full backs have been cautioned in the first period, so Obertan and Ameobi will be hoping to capitalise and continue their impressive runs down the wings. Villa need inspiration from somewhere to help beat the drop this season!
(45’) We are underway again here at St James Park! Cisse's goal separates the two sides, with Villa needing a big turnaround to secure some vital points.
The home side go into the break a goal to the good, thanks to a clinical finish from Cisse! The striker fired home after Janmaat had sent a fantastic cross from the right. Villa have a lot to do to get back in this crucial clash in the second period! 1-0 to the Magpies at the moment!
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card M. Lowton receives a yellow card. ---
(45’) Sissoko lays off his midfield partner Abeid, who is unable to pick out the goalscorer Cisse behind Villa's defence. Obertan is looking dangerous on the right wing, and is taken out by Lowton. The referee blows for half-time!
(45’) Not long until half-time now, with Villa struggling to get back in this clash. Newcastle win a free-kick in a dangerous position. Ameobi's outswinging cross is too close to Guzan, who deals with the delivery comfortably in the end. Sissoko still running the game from the heart of midfield!
(43’) CLOSE! Riviere directs his header wide, despite being completely free in the penalty area. Benteke is then ruled for offside after getting on the end of Hutton's lofted delivery from the right flank.
(41’) Villa urgently trying to get back in this encounter, but Ameobi finds Obertan as the visitors find themselves under some unwanted pressure! Sherwood looks a worried boss on the sidelines at the moment!
(39’) Further misery for the Villans, but the goal came against the run of play, after Villa had dominated proceedings. Although, the clinical instincts of Cisse is the difference at the moment! Sixth assist this season for Janmaat, who has been brilliant today!
--- 37’ Assist The assist came from D. Janmaat. ---
--- 37’ Goal! GOOOAAAALLLLLL! Cisse puts the Magpies in front after getting on the end of another great Janmaat delivery. The Villa defence couldn't deal with the cross as the striker sends his side ahead. ---
(37’) The visitors have finally got a foothold on this game, with Benteke and Sinclair starting to look threatening going forward. Encouragng signs for Sherwood's outfit, but a goal still eludes them for now!
(36’) Delightful play from Villa in midfield, as great movement between Delph and Westwood leads to a first-time shot from Sinclair. However, the winger is unable to continue his fine goalscoring form, directing his volley straight at Krul.
(34’) Hutton finds Benteke again as his effort leads to a goal-mouth scramble. Delph's subsequent shot is unable to find the target after a flurry of tackles on Villa's attackers.
(32’) Penalty appeal turned down from Newcastle after Obertan looked to have been brought down by Delph, but the central midfielder got a touch on the ball. The Magpies attack down the left again with Ameobi but Cleverley thwarts the attempted move.
(30’) Coloccini bombs out of midfield and finds Sissoko, but Newcastle's attack breaks down yet again. The hosts are doing well to find their widemen from midfield, but the end product is letting them down in the end!
(28’) Hutton is showing a real threat down the right flank. Great work from the full back leads to Benteke having a confident effort at Krul, striking an overhead kick to win a corner!
--- 26’ Yellow card A. Hutton is yellow-carded. ---

(24’) Delph pumps the ball towards Benteke, as Villa look threatening going forward for now. Westwood's long lofted ball from deep finds his targetman, but the striker fails to hit the target.
(22’) Lowton's through ball is a poor one as Newcastle take control again. Sherwood will be concerned as Delph picks up a knock, having collided with Obertan earlier. Janmaat bombs down the right flank and lays off Riviere, but the forward fails to connect as Guzan saves.
(20’) Returning winger Gutierrez is given a standing ovation as he warms up down the sideline! Westwood's free-kick can only find the crowd, after a poor effort on goal. No real danger yet from the visitors, as Newcastle keep possession in midfield.
(18’) CLOSE! Hutton gets a vital tackle on Cisse, after the striker had controlled Janmaat's brilliant cross from the right wing. Great chance for Newcastle, but Villa survive thanks to their Scottish full back! The game has sprung into life now at St James' Park!
(16’) On-loan midfield man Cleverley helps drive Villa forward, as Lowton gets a cross into the danger area from the left side. But his delivery is poor, as Krul catches without any hassle. Good chance wasted for the Villans!
(14’) Riviere is outdone by Irishman Clark after a poor ball from Williamson. Agbonlahor has the ball in the net at the other end, but it is ruled out for offside!

(10’) Williamson launches a long ball forward towards Cisse, but Guzan comes and collects it easily. Sinclair tries to get in behind the home defence, but Newcastle continue to keep proceedings tight in midfield. Sissoko is showing great strength and drive through the centre for the Magpies in these early stages.

(4’) CLOSE! Benteke's deadly cross from the right is superb but Sinclair is unable to score from close range, as Janmaat clears! Good early spell from the visitors.
(2’) A crucial game for Villa, after their new boss Sherwood stated that six wins from their final 12 games would be enough to secure survival. But it's the home side who start brightly, with Obertan trying to beat Hutton down the right flank. The hosts keeping possession in Villa's half.

New coach John Carver will be hoping there are no lasting effects of last week's 5-0 thrashing to Manchester City, before the visit of Villa, as they look to get their season back on track.
The hosts have had a similarly awful year, taking three points from just one game, but thanks to their previous fine run under former boss Alan Pardew, they still sit in 11th spot.
Goals have been a rare sight this season, with just three coming in Villa’s last 11 league matches, but Sherwood will be hoping to introduce a more attacking style into his new squad.
The Magpies host Villa with the visitors still looking for their first league win of the calendar year. Sherwood’s reign got off to a frustrating and unfortunate start last week against Stoke City, with Vlaar conceding an injury-time penalty, which Victor Moses dispatched to secure a 2-1 win.
Aston Villa subs: Given, Bacuna, Weimann, Sanchez, Gil, N’Zogbia, Grealish.
Aston Villa starting line-up (4-3-3): Guzan; Hutton, Okore, Clark, Lowton; Delph, Cleverley, Westwood; Agbonlahor, Sinclair, Benteke.
Newcastle subs: Woodman, R.Taylor, Anita, Gouffran, Gutierrez, Armstrong, Perez.
Newcastle starting line-up (4-4-2): Krul; Janmaat, Coloccini, Williamson, Haïdara; Obertan, Sissoko, Abeid, Ameobi; Rivière, Cisse.
Away team: Tim Sherwood has a defensive headache, with Ron Vlaar and Kieran Richardson out. Vlaar is suspended, while Aly Cissokho is also absent, with Philippe Senderos missing out as he battles a calf problem.
Home team: Midfielder Jonas Gutierrez makes a sensational return to the squad. Full-back Daryl Janmaat has recovered from a knock, but Siem de Jong (collapsed lung), Remy Cabella (knee) and the suspended Jack Colback miss out, as well as defenders Steven Taylor (Achilles) and Paul Dummett (knee).

It was by no means a classic but it could go along way to ensuring that the Potters claim a second successive top ten finish in the Premier League. As for Hull City, they are still in the thick of a relegation dogfight but you suspect that they will feel confident in their ability to accumulate enough points to ensure Premier League survival. Given that despite today's defeat they are still four points clear of 17th placed QPR, who do have a game in hand.
Steve Bruce will feel annoyed by the simple nature of Stoke's winning goal. It was a diagonal ball that found the tall striker who had pulled onto the backpost and beat Paul McShane in an aerial duel. Hull City supporters may wonder why Abel Hernandez was brought on earlier. N'Doye also did reasonably well after coming off the bench. Sone Aluko will probably feel a bit frustrated that it was him rather than Gaston Ramirez that was replaced early on in the second half.
It became apparent very early on that it wasn't going to be a goalfest this afternoon and so it proved. That said, Stoke City will not care one little bit as they grab an important win to go level on points with West Ham United. In an otherwise uninspiring and drab match substitutes Charlie Adam & Peter Crouch combined to produce a moment of quality that ultimately settled this fiesty contest.
(90’) And that's it! Full time Stoke City 1-0 Hull City.
(90’) Hull City have gone very direct in an attempt to force an equaliser but Stoke are dealing with everything that is being thrown at them so far. Hull have huffed and puffed in the last five or 10 minutes or so but it feels like too little, too late.
(90’) Gaston Ramirez takes a devillish delivery from a corner on the right hand side that swings in from his left boot. Begovic does well to punch the ball away for another corner that Huddlestone will take. Huddlestone's cross is flicked on by Dawson into the path of McShane who takes too long waiting for the ball to drop and as a result the opportunity is lost.
(90’) Stoke are just starting to drop a little bit deeper than I'm sure Mark Hughes would like and it is inviting pressure from Hull City. Abel Hernandez has made a real difference since coming on. There will be 5 minutes of injury time to be added on. Can the Tigers find an equaliser?
(88’) N'Doye tries to spin on the edge of the area and take on a snapshot but the Senegalese striker only succeeds in taking a total airshot and ending up flat on his back, much to the amusement of the home fans.
(85’) Almost a half a chance for Hull as Abel Hernandez shows great pace and trickery down the left wing. The Uruguayan international looks to cut the ball back to his strike partner N'Doye but Wilson is well place to clear the danger. Much better from the Tigers. Good positive and direct play.
(83’) I always feel that it is a dangerous game to play for a draw, particularly away from home in the Premier League. Hull have been so defensive in their set up it then becomes very difficult to change your mindset and cause your opposition difficulties.
(80’) Aside from being behind at the moment the biggest challenge that Hull City face is getting enough of the ball to cause Stoke some serious problems. The change in formation hasn't resulted in the visitors getting more possession and time is running out fast.
--- 78’ Substitution M. Figueroa is replaced with A. Hernández. ---
--- 77’ Yellow card M. Dawson is yellow-carded. ---
(77’) Hernandez is on but in place of Figueroa rather than Ramirez. So it will be a change of shape for the Tigers, it looks like they have reverted to a 4-4-2. Hull have now made all their subs so Steve Bruce will now have to see if his side can claw their way back into contention.
(76’) Abel Hernandez is ready to enter the fray and you imagine he will come on for Gaston Ramirez. Before that change can be made Michael Dawson is booked after chopping down Victor Moses. A very simple decision for the referee there.
(74’) How do Hull City respond now? In all honesty it looked like they have been playing for a 0-0 from the get-go but they will need to commit some more bodies forward if they are to get back into this contest.
(72’) A delicious diagonal ball from Adam finds Crouch who loops a brilliant header into the far corner. Absolutely no chance there for Allan McGregor. A classic centre forwards goal. An inspired sub from Mark Hughes or should he have been brought on earlier? Either way it is a vital goal for the home side.

(68’) You feel that this game is crying out for Peter Crouch who has been in decent form of late. Stoke could really do with his aerial prowess and ability to hold the ball up. Jon Walters hasn't really been in the game and has come out to the right hand side with Mame Biram Diouf occupying the central striker position.

David Meyler conceded the freekick and is playing a dangerous game here as he brought down Charlie Adam on the edge of the box. Given that he's just been booked he shouldn't be giving the referee a chance to produce a second yellow card. The Potters fans are putting the officials under a lot of pressure everytime a decision is made.
--- 56’ Substitution S. Aluko is replaced with D. N'Doye. ---

(47’) The tackling has certainly picked up from where it left off in the first half. Erik Pieters putting in a rather risky challenge on Jake Livermore. The referee awards Hull City a freekick and the Stoke City fans once again vent their frustration at the referee.

(46’) Hull City get the second half going and will attack the stand where their supporters are massed. Stephen Ireland has not been able to shake off the effects of that tackle from Figueroa in the first half and has been replaced by Charlie Adam.

A point away from home at the Britannia Stadium is not to be sniffed at and could be crucial in Hull's bid to stay in the Premier League this season. Surely the second half will have more chances and quality in attacking areas? Here's hoping...
Mark Hughes will feel that if his side can sharpen up in the final third then they are well capable of taking all three points in the second half. Stoke have some decent options in reserve and it won't be too long before the introduction of the likes of Crouch, Adam, Sidwell and Arnautovic are considered. The Potters have been very comfortable defensively but should be wary of the threat of N'Doye, Sagbo and Hernandez on the bench for Hull City, if they get a chance to come on.
Well I think the nicest way to summarise that first half would be...uneventful. In truth, a red card has looked more likely than a goal so far this afternoon. Hull City have come with a gameplan to frustrate their opposition and hit them on the beak. They have certainly executed the first part of their manager's instructions to the letter but have rarely threatened on the counter. The Tigers have defended bravely from the first minute.
(45’) In keeping with the rest of the half, the final action of the opening 45 minutes is Victor Moses overhitting a corner that sails out of play. Stoke City 0-0 Hull City.
(45’) As we go into first half stoppage time you suspect it is Steve Bruce that will be the more satisified of the two managers at this stage. Despite the Aluko chance it has looked more likely that the home side would opening the scoring this afternoon. A 15 minute break might allow both sets of player's to calm down a bit as this match has threatened to boil over on a couple of occasions.
--- 43’ Yellow card V. Moses is yellow-carded. ---
(42’) Stephen Ireland is now on caught on the follow through of a thunderous tackle from Maynor Figueroa. It was untidy to say the least but it has been deemed unintentional. Immediately afterwards Huddlestone is struck by a failing arm from Victor Moses. Hull City are rightly awarded a freekick but the Stoke City supporters are far from impressed with the performance of the officials in this first half.

Southampton come into the game on the back of a 2-0 defeat to fellow top four challengers Liverpool. The defeat sees them lie in fifth place, but they’re just two points behind Arsenal in third. A win today for the Saints will keep them right in the mix for a coveted Champions League place. Their top scorer, Graziano Pelle, has now gone nine Premier League matches without scoring. For West Brom, Brown Ideye will be hoping his good form infront of goals continues today after netting four times in his last four matches.
The home side head into the match in relatively fine form, having kept three clean sheets on the trot in all competitions. Last time out, the Baggies took a point from the Stadium of Light in a 0-0 stalemate. Tony Pulis's men have kept an impressive six clean sheets in nine games since his arrival and will be looking to add to that tally; just as they did earlier on in the season in the reverse fixture which finished 0-0 at St. Mary’s.

As a result, the Reds pick up three much-needed points thanks to two brilliant strikes from Henderson and Coutinho, keeping their chances of Champions League qualification alive and well.

Full time at the KC Stadium! Hull secure a MASSIVE three points in the Barclays Premier League as they run out narrow 2-1 winners over fellow relegation battlers, QPR. Jelavic opened the scoring in the first period with an excellent finish inside the box, and things looked to be going all for the home side when Joey Barton was stupidly sent off. I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
(90’) Three minutes of added time here! The problem for Steve Bruce now is that he has so may attacking players out there that they may have trouble defending this lead before the final whistle! Two minutes to go!
--- 89’ Assist R. Brady gave the assist. ---
--- 89’ Goal! GOOOAAALLL!! GOOALLL!!! GOOALLL FOR HULL!! Brady collects a clearance on the left wing and swings a cross into the box for N'Doye, who gets in between the QPR central defenders to bullet a strike home! Two-nil! Late drama at the KC! ---
(88’) What a saaaaaave from Green! N'Doye gets in behind the QPR defence to get the header away but the goalkeeper beats the ball away with a magnificent close range block!
(86’) Phillips takes the pressure off his side with a powerful run down the right-hand side. Might be clever to take the ball into the corner but he decides to take on a couple of defenders before crossing into the box. Decent ball in, but there are no takers for QPR!
(84’) This is, and probably will be for the remaining minutes, attack versus defence as Hull continue to knock at the door. The most worrying thing for them is that, despite all their possession in the final third, they aren't creating too many chances.
--- 82’ Substitution D. Meyler is done for the day. S. Aluko is his replacement. ---
(82’) QPR are camped in their own half at the moment as Hull spray the penalty area with constant crosses into the box. Elmohamady is getting down the right-hand side time and time again to throw balls into the penalty area, but the visitors are surviving for the moment!
--- 80’ Yellow card M. Phillips is cautioned by the referee. ---
(80’) Steve Bruce can't really do much more here as he throws on yet another attacking player in an attempt to grab this win. Sone Aluko is the third and final Hull change and he'll replace David Meyler.
--- 78’ Substitution A. Traoré enters the game and replaces N. Kranjčar. ---
(78’) Third and final change from QPR now and it sees Kranjcar hobble off with what looks like a thigh knock for Armand Traore, who will provide plenty of pace down that left wing, offensively and defensively.
(76’) There has not been a lot of attacking quality at all in this second period - from either side. Hull should be going all out for this victory today but they have been completely stifled by the deep backline for QPR, who would certainly settle for the point. Is there a hero out there for either side?
--- 75’ Substitution C. Austin is done for the day. M. Zárate is his replacement. ---
--- 75’ Yellow card M. Zárate receives a yellow card. ---
(74’) Another change from QPR here and it sees goalscorer, Charlie Austin, who has only recently returned from injury, replaced by Mauro Zarate, who has not really been given a chance in the Premier League by the Rangers so far. Let's see how he gets on.
(72’) Just under 20 minutes remaining in this clash at the KC stadium here. If this result stays the same it will have to go down as a disappointing day at the office for Hull, who have all their big attacking guns out there yet seem unable to break down this 10-man QPR outfit.
(70’) QPR get the corner kick and Caulker, Ferdinand etc. make their way into the penalty area. With their man disadvantage, set-pieces may present Ramsay's men with the best opportunity of grabbing a winner here. Kranjcar will need to provide a better delivery than this one though, which is easily cleared.
(68’) Meyler cuts in from the right-hand side and gets into a great position on the edge of the box but strangely attempts a rather difficult pass in behind the defence for Hernandez rather than getting a crack at goal himself. In the end the Uruguayan can't get hold of the ball and QPR get the goal kick.
--- 67’ Substitution A. Hernández enters the game and replaces J. Livermore. ---
(66’) Another positive change from Hull now and it sees Abel Hernandez come on for Livermore. That is the Uruguayan, Jelavic, N'Doye, and Gaston Ramirez all on for the home side now as they go all out to claim a vital victory.
--- 64’ Substitution M. Doughty enters the game and replaces B. Zamora. ---
(64’) First change of the match from Chris Ramsay and QPR and it sees Zamora, who has been largely frustrated up top today, replaced by Michael Doughty. Midfielder on for a striker then, which may signal a change in mentality from the visitors.
(62’) Suk-Young is currently down clutching his head after taking a nasty one from the leg of McShane. Didn't look to by any intent in it and to be fair to the QPR defender he pops right up after a few seconds. QPR get the goal kick and play can continue.
(60’) QPR send a high cross into the box and Austin does brilliantly to take it in and evade a couple of challenges before teeing up Kranjcar. In the end Hull manage to retreat into their own box and the visitors' attack comes to nothing.
--- 58’ Yellow card B. Zamora is yellow-carded. ---
(58’) Zamora is the latest player to go into the book and it is a deserved one for the QPR striker, who has two or three looks at Meyler before going right through the Irishman in an aerial challenge. He'll need to watch himself for the remaining 30 minutes or so!
(56’) Elmohamady strides down the right wing and bursts past the challenge of Kranjcar and then Suk-Young before hitting the byline and standing a high cross to the back post. Perhaps predictably, Green comes off his line and goes down amongst the crowd, earning the soft free kick.
(54’) QPR actually made the better start after the break and came out with a pretty decent tempo in their passing and movement, but the man advantage of Hull has just started to shine through with the hosts enjoying the majority of possession.
--- 53’ Substitution G. Ramírez enters play, replacing A. Bruce. ---
(52’) Hull make an early first half change here and it is a positive one from Steve Bruce, which will probably signify a change in formation. Alex Bruce is withdrawn and coming on his Gaston Ramirez. The boss side clearly trying to take advantage of the extra man here.
(50’) Brady delivers the set-piece into the box and Dawson gets ahead of his marker to glance a header a goal, but there is just a little too much on it from the former Spurs man and his attempt ends up flying harmlessly over the bar.
(49’) Brady drives down the left-hand side and fizzes a cross to the front post. Jelavic looks poised to get the header away but Ferdinand is well-positioned to clear behind for a corner kick.
(47’) Henry latches on to a lofted pass in midfield from Kranjcar and then sends a high pass into the box for Austin. The goalscorer looks to get in behind the Hull defence but Elmohamady gets back to coolly cushion a header back to his keeper, McGregor.
(46’) We are back under way at the KC Stadium!
Half time in the KC Stadium. It took a little while to get going, but Hull and QPR are playing out a pretty entertaining match here. Jelavic gave the home side the lead 16 minutes in with an excellent half volley from the edge of the box and it they received another boost later on when Joey Barton was stupidly sent off. However, QPR rallied and grabbed the equaliser through the returning Charlie Austin. All to play for in the second period, but Hull have the man advantage.
(45’) HUDDLESTONE! How close was that?! The Hull midfielder latches on to a loose ball on the edge of the box and rifles a superb strike towards the left corner, but it goes by the post by no more than a yard! Almost a great goal, but QPR survive!
(43’) Dodgy moment from Green! Brady swings a teasing free kick into the penalty area and the QPR goalkeeper fumbles it inside the six-yard box! McShane is sniffing around looking for the rebound but Caulker is on hand to clear away the danger!
(41’) N'Doye nicks the ball away from the tackle of Caulker which means the QPR defender commits the foul down the right wing as he catches the striker. Hull get the opportunity to reclaim their lead with a free kick in an advanced area.
--- 39’ Assist The assist came from M. Phillips. ---
--- 39’ Goal! GOOOOAAAALLLLLL FOR QPR! WHERE DID THAT COME FROM?! The visitors equalise! Philips collects the ball on the right wing and whips a superb cross into the box for Austin, who glances a terrific header into the bottom left corner! What a return from injury! One-one! ---
(37’) The game has not really recovered from the sending off as QPR sit back and attempt to limit the damage before half time, with Hull not in any rush to dash forward for more goals.
(35’) Barton's football career has been hampered and blighted by situations like this, with today's events sadly the latest in a long line of incidents. He has completely let his team-mates down, who now face a mountain to climb in order to get anything out of this.
(33’) JOEY BARTON IS SENT OFF FOR QPR! The QPR captain gets involved in an altercation with Huddlestone and appears to strike the Hull midfielder in the stomach with a punch or a tap! Either way he has been shown a red card! Complete and utter idiocy.
--- 32’ Yellow card D. Furlong is yellow-carded. ---
--- 32’ Red card! J. Barton is sent for an early shower! ---
(32’) Furlong is booked for QPR as the youngster goes in late on Meyler down the left-hand side. Another chance for Hull to pump a dangerous set-piece into the area here, with the visitors not exactly oozing confidence from the back!
(30’) A missed opportunity for Hull! The home side steal possession in the middle of the park and counterattack at pace. Livermore leads the charge and attempts to slide a pass into the path of N'Doye, but the ball just lacks a bit of pace which allows QPR to regroup and clear! The striker would have been through on goal had he collected there!
(28’) QPR, and Zamora in particular, are showing real frustration at the moment. The former West Ham striker, who is renowned for putting himself about in the penalty area, is not being allowed any leeway by the referee at the moment in terms of his physical presence.
(27’) The free kick is swung into the box but Dawson manages to clear completed unopposed.
(26’) Phillips receives the ball to feet near the touchline and skips into the middle with pace before looking to drive into the penalty area. In the end QPR are awarded the free kick as Brady trips the former Blackpool winger. Let's see if the visitors can make anything from this set-piece.
(24’) Hull looking a lot more confident after taking that early lead, with Huddlestone and Livermore controlling things in the middle of the park. Their counterparts, Henry and Barton, haven't managed to assert any authority in those central areas as of yet.
(22’) Livermooooore! He should be doing better! Jelavic collects the ball into feet inside the box and lays the ball off for the former Spurs man, who has all the time in the world to pick his spot but ends up driving a strike harmlessly over the bar!
(20’) Almost a goal for QPR debutant, Furlong! The 19-year-old meets an aerial ball with a long range powerful header and it looks to be looping in over the head of McGregor, but the Scot manages to claw over the bar! So very nearly an equaliser for the visitors!
(18’) That goal should do well in settling the nerves at the KC here! QPR, once again, shoot themselves in the foot away from home, leaving themselves on the back foot early on. Still plenty of time to make amends though.
--- 16’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLL FOR HULL! THE HOSTS OPEN THE SCORING! A speculative long ball is played into the QPR box and Caulker's poor clearance goes straight to the feet of Jelavic, who rifles a half volley into the bottom left corner! The KC goes wild! One-nil! ---
(15’) We've got a small break in play at the moment as Brady is currently down after receiving a nasty blow to the bottom of his foot after a high boot from Phillips. Didn't look to be too much intent in it, but the Hull man is just receiving treatment. Should be okay to continue though.
(13’) The player most likely to make something happen here appears to be Kranjcar who has shows some class in possession in the middle of the park, which has been sorely missing for the most part. We hoped for the cracker, but it has been the stalemate so far.
(11’) Not too much quality on show so far as both sides are still trying to find their feet in a creative or attacking sense. With the formations the way they are, expect plenty of crosses swung into both boxes and plenty of aerial duels.
(9’) Meyler gets in behind the Hull defence and looks to burst into the penalty area, but the retreating Suk-Young does brilliantly to spring back and claw the ball away from the feet of the Irishman. QPR were opened up a little too easily there!
(7’) Furlong, who makes his first start for QPR today, gives his side width down the right wing before fizzing a pass into the feet of Zamora, who attempts to go for the return pass in behind the defender. There was just too much on it though and Hull get the throw in.

(3’) Both sides are just testing the waters at the moment with some launched forward passes to heap pressure on the opposition defence. A rare thing we have today as both sides feature with a flat two-man strikeforce. Let's see if it is Jelavic/N'Doye or Austin/Zamora who can make their mark.

TEAM NEWS...
There is a new managerial era at QPR now after the appointment of Chris Ramsay as interim head coach until the end of the season. Chairman Tony Fernandes has already suggested that the job will go to the current boss if the London club avoid the drop, so no better incentive for Ramsay to inspire his players to a win this afternoon!
Before last weekend, Hull had the worst home record in the league but put that form behind them with a 2-0 win over Aston Villa; a result which cost Paul Lambert his job. QPR, rather infamously, have only won one match away this season, which came against Sunderland. So all the stats point to a stalemate today, but with a vital three points on the line, we may end up with a cracking clash!
Key to to QPR's hopes today, and for the rest of the season, will be the return of Charlie Austin from injury. The Englishman has netted 13 times this campaign and remains his side's best hope of avoiding the drop this year.
With both sides currently embroiled in a relegation battle, today's match presents the opportunity to gain some ground from the bottom of the table and their nearest rivals. Hull are situated 16th in the league with 23 points taken from 25 matches, and QPR are one point and one position behind in 17th, so all to play for in this clash!
I'm Martin Macdonald, and I'll be taking you through the action!
Good afternoon football fans! Welcome to LIVE coverage of the Barclays Premier League clash between Hull and Queens Park Rangers from the KC Stadium!

It's going to be a long old slog from now until the end of the season for both sides. What probably separates the sides is that Berahino and Ideye have shown that they can be a real handful in recent weeks while Jermain Defoe desperately needs some support upfront for the Black Cats. That's all I've got time for today. I've been Chris Baker and thanks for joining me!
As for the Mackems, Gus Poyet wanted a reaction from his player's and supporters and he got that today. The effort and application on show this afternoon cannot be faulted. The decision making and final ball however left a lot to be desired. This is still a team that is lacking in confidence and that showed at times. Poyet will feel that his team deserved a bit more and that Mike Jones could have given them one or two decisions that would be have been vital to the Sunderland cause.
Tony Pulis will no doubt be the happier of the two manager's this evening. It was by no means pretty but it was effective as the Baggies got exctly what they came for, a point. They will take this result and carry on. With the grit, determination and organisation that has been instilled in this team it will be a huge surprise if they are in the mix for relegation come the end of the season.
Well that certainly isn't a game of football that I will be telling my grandchildren about, that's for sure. If you are a Sunderland or a West Brom fan that wasn't at the match today, stay up late as this is a banker to be last on Match of the Day this evening.
(90’) And that's the final whistle 0-0. In truth it would have been a minor miracle if there had been a goal today. Full time here at the Stadium of Light.
(90’) Darren Fletcher is fouled by Larsson so West Brom will have the chance to launch it into the Sunderland penalty area. The free-kick is a high diagonal ball that Pantilimon drops but gets away with it as O'Shea is on hand to mop up. A rare nervy moment for the home side.
(89’) Sunderland appear to have run out of ideas and West Brom are more than happy to run the clock down. In truth, this game doesn't deserve anything more than a 0-0 so far. The lack of quality has been staggering at times.
--- 88’ Substitution P. van Aanholt enters play, replacing S. Vergini. ---
--- 88’ Substitution C. Gardner is done for the day. C. McManaman is his replacement. ---
(86’) Nearly disaster for Sunderland as Pantilimon charges out of his area to try and intercept Brunt's through ball. Ideye looks set to get their first but then appears to be put off by the giant onrushing 'keeper. If the West Brom striker had played the ball he would have either had a great chance to score or he would've been fouled, as it was Pantilimon was clever enough to leave the ball and let Wes Brown hack it clear.
(84’) Adam Johnson cuts inside from the right wing and overhits a cross which goes sailing out of play for a West Brom goal kick. Gus Poyet must be so frustrated with his winger who time and time again in this second half has got himself into excellent positions but then let himself down with a poor final ball.
(81’) Brown Ideye is set away by a hopeful ball down the channel from Brunt. The West Brom striker is completed isolated, so has no choice but to go it alone and he does well to earn his side a corner. Former Sunderland man Craig Gardner takes the set piece but in keeping with the game today his cross doesn't beat the first man.
(79’) West Brom seem to have settled for a point but that is always a dangerous game to play. That said, if any team can snuff out a match then it is one managed by Tony Pulis. Ben Foster is getting a few boos from the crowd for what they see as obvious timewasting.
(76’) SAVE! Foster denies Connor Wickham. Adam Johnson's inswinging corner is flicked on at the near post but the West Brom goalkeeper is well placed to parry the ball to safety. If Sunderland don't score today it won't be through the lack of trying. Foster seems to have injured himself in making that save.
(74’) Almost a chance! Wickham bursts down the left wing and cuts the ball back to Defoe who twists and turns before getting a shot off. The effort is weak and is deflected behind for a corner. Better from Sunderland.
--- 73’ Substitution C. Baird enters the game and replaces J. Morrison. ---
(71’) As we head into the final twenty minutes the stalemate continues. West Brom would be much more satisfied with a point as things stand as they have been far from their best. Stephane Sessegnon is readying himself to come on against his former club. Will it be for one of the frontmen or a midfielder? Chris Baird enters the fray in place of James Morrison, which looks like a reaction to Sunderland bringing on two centre forwards.
(69’) Gus Poyet has seen enough and is making a double substitution. Off comes the disappointing Danny Graham and Ricky Alvarez, who has been very quiet in the second half. On in their place come Steven Fletcher and Connor Wickham. Sunderland look to have changed to a 4-3-3. The home side want the three points and are going for it!
--- 68’ Substitution S. Fletcher comes on for R. Álvarez. ---
--- 68’ Substitution C. Wickham enters the game and replaces D. Graham. ---
(66’) It's pretty much a full house inside the Stadium of Light this afternoon and it is a shame that there has been such a lack of entertainment on show for the fans that have made the effort to attend today. Sunderland are pressing forward and West Brom are dropping deeper and deeper. Can the Black Cats open up their opponents?
(63’) Larsson's first corner is headed behind for another set piece. This time the Swedish midfielder's delivery picks out Vergini in acres of space in the box but the Argentinian international conspires to head the ball wide. That was a huge chance for the home side to go ahead, particularly as there has been so few clear goalscoring opportunities. Should do better.
(60’) Defoe wants a freekick after the ball flicks up and strikes Darren Fletcher on the arm but the referee waves play on. The Sunderland forward ends up working the ball onto his left foot and gets a shot away which is deflected wide for a corner.
(57’) The game has been scrappy throughout and that will suit West Brom a lot more. The clear gameplan for the visitors is to sit back and absorb pressure and wait patiently for a chance to hit Sunderland on the counter attack. The longer the match stays at nil-nil the more Pulis will feel that they can nick this in a 'smash and grab' style away performance.
(53’) Defoe shows a side to his game that you don't often hear about as he holds the ball up with his back to goal and brings Cattermole into play. The Sunderland midfielder spreads the play to Reveillere who puts a cross into the area but Lescott meets it emphatically to head away the danger.
(50’) The Baggies are trying to get their foot on the ball and get some pattern into their play. Pulis is urging his team forward at every opportunity and it appears that West Brom are playing a little bit higher up the pitch in this second half. They were very deep at times in the first period.
(48’) Sunderland begin the second half on the front foot. Larsson swirls in another deep free-kick which is collected by Danny Graham the ball bounces up and their are some half-hearted appeals for a handball against Gareth McAuley but nothing doing for referee Mike Jones.
(46’) West Bromwich Albion get the second half going. Let's hope the quality of the football improves in the next 45 minutes.
Sunderland's most likely route to goal seems to be through their wide men who have been very bright during the first period. The Black Cats have dominated possession so far, enjoying over 60% of the ball but they need to do more with it. In Connor Wickham and Steven Fletcher they have two very ready and able replacements to call upon. Danny Graham must do more. The former Swansea striker needs to get himself in the right positions.
Rather than must-win this first half has very much had the feeling of must-not-lose. West Brom have had plenty of men behind the ball and have looked very well organised defensively but have been short of quality on the ball. If things continue in the same vein in the second half it wouldn't be much of a surprise to see the likes of Sessegnon and McManaman introduced to give the visitors a bit more pace in the wide areas.
The Premier League often calls itself the best division in the world, well it certainly wasn't on the basis of the last 45 minutes. Sunderland have definitely had the better of proceedings but they haven't been able to make it count so far. Gus Poyet will point to two crucial decisions that he will feel haven't gone his way. Tony Pulis will want to see a lot more from his side in an attacking sense in the second half.
(45’) And that's half-time 0-0.
(45’) SAVE! Ben Foster hasn't had much to do so far but his he was very quick to turn Larsson's stinging drive around the post. The West Brom goalkeeper's reflexes were up to scratch there and they had to be to make sure Sunderland didn't go in 1-0 up at the break.
(44’) Sunderland have the ball in the back of the net but it won't count as it is ruled out for offside. Adam Johnson was picked out by Vergini's cross at the far post and the former Manchester City winger took a touch around Foster before tapping in. Johnson didn't look to be offside when the ball was played by Defoe certainly was in the six yard box.
(43’) SHOT! Alvarez certainly isn't lacking in confidence even if a lot of his teammates are. The winger on-loan from Inter Milan has another potshot from distance but like his last effort his strike at goal isn't in any danger of troubling Ben Foster.
(40’) Yet again Johnson wins a corner and once again it comes to nothing dor the home side. Their has been a desperate lack of quality in the final ball from both teams so far. Player's have got into decent positions but haven't been able to make the most of the limited opportunities on offer this afternoon.
(37’) Chance but only half a chance for John O'Shea, who had ventured forward for a Sunderland free-kick after Defoe had been upended by Lescott. Larsson pinged the ball into the West Brom penalty area and his cross picked out O'Shea who was taken a little bit by surprise and could only screw his volley well wide of the post.
(34’) CLOSE! Reveillere released Jermain Defoe down the inside left channel and the Sunderland striker wasted no time in flashing the ball across the six yard box but Danny Graham was nowhere to be seen. That perhaps explains why Graham hasn't scored in the league in the last 14 months.
(31’) The Sunderland wingers have looked their most dangerous outlets so far and Poyet will want to see Johnson and Alvarez on the ball as much as possible. Their is a certain nervousness in possession for the home player's and it is easy to see why as the Black Cats have struggled at home all season. (67’) LEAD NEARLY RESTORED! Sensational build-up play from Everton! Lukaku picks out Atsu, who finds McCarthy, before the midfielder sends an improvised back-heel pass through to the striker, who is clean in on goal. Morgan does well to recover, putting Lukaku under just enough pressure as he curls his final shot just over the bar!
(65’) That has to feel good for Nigel Pearson, who for the moment looks like the hero. He makes two changes and they take no more than a minute to make their mark. This game is certainly up for grabs now, but who will be the team to really push for it? Fortune favours the brave, as they say.
--- 63’ Goal! WELL THERE IT IS! LEICESTER PULL LEVEL! And wouldn't you know it, the two substitutes link up to even the score. The pace of Vardy on the right proves to be a problem for Everton, as he gets his cross in. Howard spills it and neither Stones nor Jagielka can get to the rebound ahead of Nugent, with the poacher there to slot home! ---
--- 62’ Substitution J. Vardy comes on for J. Schlupp. ---
--- 62’ Substitution D. Nugent enters the game and replaces R. Mahrez. ---
(61’) It is a double change for Leicester City as David Nugent and Jamie Vardy are introduced. The duo will look to provide Leicester with a bit of a spark in attack as they try and get back into this game.
(59’) Same old story for Leicester City manager Nigel Pearson who has seen his time fall behind yet again after not taking their chances. There is movement now on the Foxes bench, as they can hardly afford a defeat here today in their quest for survival.
--- 57’ Assist R. Lukaku provided the assist. ---
--- 57’ Goal! NAISMITH OPENS THE SCORING FOR THE HOSTS! It is incredibly harsh on the visitors, as Everton score with their first troubling shot on target. --- 55’ Substitution C. Atsu enters the game and replaces M. Bešić. ---
--- 55’ Substitution D. Gibson enters play, replacing R. Barkley. ---
(55’) The changes are made by Everton, following the corner. It is Atsu and Gibson coming on, with Barkley and Besic giving way. The Ghanaian, who was the player of the tournament at the Africa Cup of Nations, will take up a role just in behind Lukaku.
(54’) Conditions are worsening around Goodison Park as the rain picks up. That doesn't stop Leicester from continuing their pursuit of the elusive opener, as Konchesky and Mahrez link-up well on the left before Besic puts it behind for a corner.
(52’) Enough is enough, says Roberto Martinez, as Christian Atsu and Darron Gibson are readied to come on. You have to wonder why the manager is making the change so quickly into the second half, but patience is clearly running thin.
(50’) Good stuff from Leicester at the start of this second half. Coleman concedes a corner and the visitors push men into the penalty area. James delivers and picks out Mahrez at the far post. He tries to volley it at goal, but lashes it over the bar. The technique required to hit that properly is tremendously difficult to master.
(48’) THAT SHOULD HAVE BEEN THE OPENER! Schlupp tees up Matty James for a strike at the top of the area, but Howard dives across to keep it out at the near post. Schlupp is there to follow up on the rebound, but somehow fails to put it past a beaten Howard and into the back of the net!
(46’) Everton get the second half underway, moving left to right. No changes to tell you about at the break.
HALF TIME: EVERTON 0-0 LEICESTER CITY. There has been very little of note to discuss after the first 45 minutes. The teams combined for two attempts on target, neither of which posed any threat for the opposing keeper. Everton have to do better to get Lukaku service, while Leicester can not be reluctant to commit men forward - this game is there to be had if they want to take it!
(45’) TREMENDOUS BLOCK! The last kick of the first half presents the best chance. A Simpson cross is deflected into the area and escapes both Kramaric and Jagielka. It falls kindly for Schlupp, who tees up from just outside the six-yard box, but Stones dives in to turn it behind for a corner! There won't be time to take it, however, as the first half comes to a close.
(45’) There will be one minute of added time at the end of this first half.
(43’) The last 10 minutes have been dreary and quite uninspired. There is a whole lot of nothing happening for either side in attack. Creativity look to be a major issue, while both teams do not look entirely eager to commit men forward and leave themselves exposed at the back.
(41’) STAT ATTACK: Everton have drawn half (six) of their Premier League matches this season at Goodison Park. Only Sunderland have tied a higher number of games (seven) in front of their home fans.
(39’) It is looking more and more like we will head into the break scoreless. Everton have yet to test Schwarzer in goal, and with Lukaku having to drop far deeper to get in possession than Martinez would like, service up top has been lacking and it has been far too easy for Leicester at the back.
(37’) The crowd is growing restless with the lack of activity out on the pitch. Everton games were something of a spectacle last season, but that has hardly been the case throughout this campaign. Their last four league matches have seen just two goals, with back-to-back scoreless draws at Goodison Park begining to take its toll on the supporters.
(35’) JUST OVER! Possession has been close to split thus far, with Eveton perhaps holding a slight edge. It is Leicester, however, who have done more with it. Schlupp is set up again inside the area, but with his weaker right-foot, he sends his final shot over the bar. Another wasted opportunity for the visitors.
(33’) Lennon has been a focal point for Everton on the counter, finding space well on the right and taking it. The winger has been very poor with his deliveries from the flank, however, failing to tee up Lukaku for a chance. The ex-Tottenham man seems to be lacking chemistry with the striker and you just wonder how long it will be until Everton give Atsu a chance.
(31’) KRAMARIC! Well he's certainly knocking on the door here. The Croatian striker is making himself a real menace in and around the penalty area. He is drawing plenty of attention from the Everton defence, and with good reason it would seem.
(29’) STAT ATTACK: Everton have managed only one victory from their last nine Premier League fixtures. They have scored just four times over that span and were held without a goal in six of those matches (W1, D3, L5).

--- 25’ Yellow card W. Morgan receives a yellow card. ---
(25’) Much better! Everton finally pick out a good final ball into the area, something they have desperately been lacking through the opening 25 minutes. Naismith shows impressive pace to burst through on the right channel. He cuts into the area and picks out Lukaku, but with his weaker foot the striker fails to turn it into the back of the net.
(23’) A seemingly simple pass forward is chased down by Lukaku, and Huth rather unnecessarily tugs at the shirt of the striker to concede a free kick from 25 yards out. Barkley takes it, however, instead of Baines, and his effort sails miles over the bar. That was a very poor attempt by the midfielder.
(21’) The pace has fizzled out yet again, as play becomes largely contained in midfield. There is no real tempo or flow to the match with Everton content on keeping the ball by passing it around at the back. Leicester are not pressing enough with the hosts in possession making it all to comfortable for them.
(19’) Chances have been few and far between as we aproach the 20-minute mark. The only shot on goal came just a couple of minutes in from the visitors, with Everton not doing nearly enough to get the ball into the feet of Lukaku, for whom service has been lacking thus far.
(17’) Much better from Everton! They seem to have found their rhythm now and look much more confident in possession. They are getting into some good areas in attack but need to do better to get the ball into the feet of their more creative players.
(15’) Clever attempt by Romelu Lukaku to try a back-heel pass into the path of Steven Naismith, but it doesn't work out. The visitors look up to the task defensively, early on here, with Robert Huth's no nonsense attitude at the back relieving the pressure yet again.
(13’) Leicester are not taking a conservative approach and nor should they. If they want to secure their survival in the Premier League then draws will not be good enough for the most part. They have a five-point mountain to climb and with time running out on the season, they need victories.
(11’) END TO END! Leicester commit men forward in attack, but it fizzles out with Simpson's poor strike at goal. Barkley picks it up and surges forward as Everton counter dangerously. He picks out Lennon on the right, but the winger takes too long to send in a return ball, failing to spot Barkley or Lukaku as the chance comes to nothing.
(9’) STAT ATTACK: Leicester City last recorded an away victory over Everton in December of 1985, with goals from Gary McAllister and Alan Smith securing a 2-1 win at Goodison Park.
(7’) Everton finally enjoy themselves a first real spell in possession. Their passing is hardly penetrative enough, but Coleman changes that with a darting run forward. He gets into space on the right and tries to pick out Naismith in the centre, but the defender just gets there first.
(5’) The visitors have started the game very strongly. Everton seem to be switched off at the moment, with the first five minutes being played in their end. They have been far too inconsistent this season and the tempo they had to their game on Thursday is nowhere to be found yet today.
(3’) First chance to Leicester! This is a very positive start from the Foxes who pass it around well atop the penalty area. Schlupp gets on the end of a pass and dribbles his way into the area for a shot on goal, but with his weaker right-foot, he can't force Howard into a difficult enough save.
(1’) The visitors kick-off and we are underway at Goodison Park! Everton in blue, Leicester City in red. Here we go!

(87’) Sturridge cuts inside from the left side of the box and shapes to curl a shot inside the far post with his right foot. He aims it far too close to Forster, though, who makes the save.
(86’) Despite plenty of pressure throughout the game, Southampton just haven't looked convincing in attack. Pelle has not had many opportunities to test Mignolet, who for his part has had a good outing.
--- 84’ Yellow card J. Henderson is cautioned by the referee. ---

(83’) Johnson has stayed down on the deck after sliding in to challenge Elia on the right. It looked fairly innocuous, but he appears to be in trouble as he is holding his shoulder. Will Liverpool be forced to play the remainder with 10 men?
(81’) Time is running out for Southampton. They're in danger of missing out on the chance to leapfrog Manchester United in the table, and their challenge for European football could suffer as a result.
(79’) Tadic rifles a powerful low effort through the wall, but it's held at the first time of asking by Mignolet. He's looked a lot more confident in goal today.

(78’) Moreno is the latest player to be shown a yellow card following a clumsy challenge on Mane. Saints could go for goal direct from the resultant free kick.
(77’) Mane's cross is controlled by Pelle just inside the box, but his touch takes him away from goal. Still, he smashes a shot from 20 yards on the spin which is blocked by Skrtel.

(74’) Rodgers makes another change as Johnson comes on in place of Ibe.

Moreno intercepts a lax pass from Schneiderlin and subsequently plays a one-two with Sterling, but his cross from the left is poor and fails to find a team-mate. Targett slips as he attempts to clear to the ball, sending it straight to the feet of the England striker who fires in to the back of the net! ---
(72’) Sturridge makes light work of beating Fonte inside the box, darting to the byline where he is dispossessed by a challenge from Yoshida. The Japanese had to get that right, and he did!
(70’) Schneiderlin feigns to shoot from the free kick before rolling a pass to the corner of the box for Djuricic. The Serbian wasn't on the same wavelength, though, and the best he can do is stop it from going out of play for a goal kick, though he still concedes a throw in.

(67’) Although they've brought Sturridge on, Liverpool are still sitting very deep as they look to absorb the pressure currently being applied by the hosts.

(63’) Second change of the night from Rodgers as Lallana goes off to a chorus of boos to be replaced by Daniel Sturridge.

(62’) Moreno finds Coutinho in a good position inside the Southampton half, but the Brazllian's subsequent attempt to feed Sterling is woeful. The pass is intercepted and the hosts clear it for a throw in.

(54’) Saints are awarded a free kick on the left after Henderson sends Wanyama to ground. Ward-Prowse is again given the responsibility of delivering the ball, but he fires it straight into the hands of Mignolet.

(48’) Pelle dinks the ball over the defence for Elia to run onto, but the bounce holds it up, allowing Skrtel to get back into position. The Dutchman still gets to the byline to provide a cross, but there is no one in the middle to supply a finish.

The teams are making their way back out onto the pitch, so the second half will begin in a few moments.
HALF TIME - Southampton 0-1 Liverpool: The Reds took an early lead through a truly mesmerising goal from Coutinho, but since then they've barely tested Forster. Saints, meanwhile, have been denied by Mignolet on a few occasions and have also had a number of penalty claims turned down. What a half of football that was! Be sure to stick around for the next 45 minutes.
(45’) We are into the first, and only, minute of stoppage time and Mignolet produces a great save to deny Djuricic, and neither Pelle or Elia can find the net on the follow-up! There's the half-time whistle, though!
(45’) Yet another penalty claim for the hosts is ignored! From a corner, Yoshida's header hits the hand of Lovren, who then hooks the ball to safety. The referee seemed to think about it for a moment before continuing with play.

(41’) Ibe shows good strength to draw a foul while protecting the ball near the corner on the near side. Henderson flights it in but he sends his delivery over every single head inside the box.
(39’) Liverpool have still yet to produce a second shot on goal, with Coutinho's beautiful strike their only threat on target. Rodgers will want more from his side or they could risk being pegged back.
(37’) The hosts win yet another free kick wide on the right, and it is whipped into the box by Ward-Prowse. Pelle is again the target, and the Italian gets what turns out to be the first of a series of headers on the ball. The defence can't get it clear, but a foul on Markovic from Djuricic sees the referee give the Reds a free kick.
(35’) Targett shows some flair to progress beyond Lallana on the left, but as he approaches Allen on the edge of the box he loses his footing and stumbles to ground without the ball.
(33’) STAT: Southampton have won just two of their last seven league games at home.

(29’) Southampton are awarded a free kick out on the right moments later, though, and again it is Ward-Prowse who supplies the delivery. Mignolet comes from his line to claim it but the ball slips out of his gloves. Fortunately for him their is no Saints player on hand to capitalise.
(27’) Wanyama releases the overlapping Clyne with a pass down the right, and the defender is brought down by Can as he looks to get in behind him. The home fans appeal for a free kick but nothing is given, much to their dismay.
(26’) Elia uses his pace to get in behind Can as he comes over to the right, and, although the former Juventus man digs out a cross, he is only able to send it behind for a goal kick.
(24’) Wanyama is doing a great job of dropping deep and protecting his defence against Sterling. He's not done quite as well in keeping Coutinho out of the game, though.

(20’) Markovic clips a brilliant pass into the centre of the box, looking for the diagonal run of Lallana. Fonte runs back and gets a leg up to make a crucial interception, as the Liverpool man would have been one-on-one with Forster there.
(19’) Coutinho and Sterling combine well around the edge of the box but the Englishman is crowded out as he attempts to turn into space for a shot.

(15’) Ward-Prowse swings in a corner from the left which is held by Mignolet. The home crowd are really behind their side, clearly pleased with what they are seeing despite conceding an early goal. It has been a great response from Koeman's men.
(14’) A huge cheer goes up as Lovren's attempt to switch the play to Sterling with a long pass up from the back ends up going out of play, nowhere near the forward.
(13’) Clyne throws a couple of stepovers at Markovic as he gets beyond the Serbian near to the byline. He floats a cross into the box which is narrowly out of the reach of Pelle again.

This victory takes the Gunners back into their usual position in the top four of the Premier League while Leicester remain rooted to the bottom of the table. Nigel Pearson will be encouraged by the performances of Schlupp, Mahrez and Kramaric - particularly the of the Croatian striker who was a constant thorn in the side of the Arsenal defence.
Not for the first time this season Nigel Pearson will be left to reflect on what was an excellent display against all the odds but ultimately it is another defeat for Leicester City. The Foxes should take great heart from their performance but they must sharpen up at both ends of the pitch if they are to survive in the Premier League this season.
After the painful Derby Day defeat it was all about the result and not necessarily the performance for Arsene Wenger this evening. It was by no means a vintage Arsenal display but hugely important given the circumstances. Koscielny settled the Gunners down with a well taken goal from Ozil's corner and when Walcott made it two-nil a routine victory looked on the cards.

(90’) Mahrez gets himself into a decent crossing position but his delivery bounces off Ulloa in the box and the striker ends up fouling Coquelin. Leicester are running out of time and look increasingly desperate in their attempts to fashion a chance for an equaliser.
--- 89’ Yellow card D. Simpson is cautioned by the referee. ---
(89’) Giroud cushions a header down into the path of Flamini who listens to the calls of the crowd and does take on the shot. The strike isn't the best but it does take a deflection which will give Arsenal a corner and eat up some vital seconds.
(88’) The match is getting rather scrappy with both sets of players complaining to the officials about perceived injustices. That will suit Arsenal who won't want the visitors to build up any sort of attacking momentum with so little of the game to go.
--- 86’ Substitution J. Schlupp is done for the day. D. Nugent is his replacement. ---
(85’) The Foxes have made third and final change. The impressive Jeffrey Schlupp comes off and David Nugent enters the fray. Leicester have three strikers on the pitch but can they get them into the game?
(83’) Arsenal are now starting to win the ball higher up the pitch but crucially they can't find that killer ball to put this game to bed. Nigel Pearson will be very proud of the character that his players have shown under very difficult circumstances.
--- 82’ Substitution A. Ramsey is replaced with M. Flamini. ---
--- 81’ Substitution W. Morgan is done for the day. L. Ulloa is his replacement. ---
(80’) Ulloa is now on for the visitors as Leicester go for broke. Rather worryingly for the Gunners - Aaron Ramsey has gone down injured and the subsitute has had to be replaced by Mathie Flamini for the final stages of this contest.
(77’) SAVE! Ospina makes a very simple catch but he really shouldn't have been given the opportunity. Kramaric broke the Arsenal offside trap and found himself one-on-one with goalkeeper and the Leicester striker went for an audacious Poborsky-esque chip but didn't get it right and wastes a golden chance to equalise.
(74’) Ramsey is now on in place of Theo Walcott as Wenger looks to sure things up in midfield. Leicester are showing great fighting spirit and are continuing to attack Arsenal every chance they get. They will need to be careful that they don't over commit and get caught out on the break.
--- 73’ Substitution A. Ramsey enters play, replacing T. Walcott. ---
(71’) CLOSE! Mahrez is inches, and I mean inches, away from making it 2-2. The Leicester winger whipped a shot at goal with his favoured left foot and it curled just wide of the target. Ospina was totally helpless and could only watch as the strike whistled past the post.
(69’) Alexis Sanchez was the man to be replaced and Giroud gives Arsenal the option to go more direct in these last twenty minutes or so. The match has just gone through a quiet spell. Leicester are going to need a big effort to draw themselves level.
--- 68’ Substitution A. Sánchez is done for the day. O. Giroud is his replacement. ---

(64’) The Gunners need to weather this storm and get hold of the ball again further up the pitch. The Foxes came out fighting at the start of the second half and have been rewarded for their positive endeavour. Giroud looks set to come on to give Arsenal a focal point.
(62’) That was less than convincng defending from Arsenal. Koscielny's header from the corner was weak and the ball fell invitingly to Kramaric, who steadied himself before smashing his low drive into the bottom corner. Leicester will feel that they've deserved something on the balance of the play so far.

(56’) Schlupp and Mahrez continue to look lively and Leicester will need to get those two more involved if they want to threaten the Arsenal backline. Simpson then almost sets Matty James clear but the through ball is just out of reach. So close to an opening for the away team.
(54’) Simpson flies forward on the overlap and puts in a dangerous cross into the area which is met by his fellow full-back Konchesky who tries to volley the ball across goal but his cross-cum-shot is blocked and Leicester have a corner.
(52’) SAVE! Cambiasso and Kramaric play a neat one-two on the top of the Arsenal penalty area. The Croatian striker opens himself up to bend the ball at goal but he can only fire his strike straight at Ospina.

(49’) Leicester are in a slightly difficult situation early in this second half. They could dearly do with a goal to get back into contention but if they leave themselves too exposed and concede a third then the floodgates could open.
(47’) Arsenal are straight on the attack and Sanchez forces a corner. Cazorla's set piece is headed only as far as Tomas Rosicky who hits a first time shot on the volley but his effort is well wide of the target.
(46’) The players are back on the pitch and the second half is up and running.
Leicester have some decent options on the bench and you suspect that it won't be too long before the likes of Marc Albrighton, Leo Ulloa or David Nugent are introduced.
Arsene Wenger will certainly know that his team can play a lot better than they have done so far but will be delighted to have a two-goal cushion at half-time. Leicester need to push forward to try and get back into the match and Arsenal will be confident that they can take full advantage of any gaps that appear on the counter attack.
Arsenal have produced some moments of quality when it counted and have been ruthlessly clinical in front of goal. Nigel Pearson will be fairly satisified with many aspects of his sides first half performance but they have given away two sloppy goals from their point of view.
(45’) And that's half-time. Arsenal 2-0 Leicester City. The Foxes have it all to do in the second half. If there is another goal then it simply has to be for the visitors if they are to mount an unlikely comeback.
(45’) CHANCE! Leicester almost get a lifeline just before the half-time interval. Cambiasso's deep corner is dropped by Ospina, who feels that he was fouled. Morgan tries to force the ball goalwards but Mertesacker is in the right place at the right time and hacks the ball to safety.
(45’) Cazorla tries to drive into the Leicester penalty area but he is rather unceremoniously upended by Konchesky right on the edge of the box. Ozil tries to lift his freekick up and over the wall but his effort is deflected wide.
(43’) Arsenal smell blood now and Sanchez picks the ball up in the inside left position and looks to work half a yard for a shot but he is well snuffed out by Wes Morgan. Leicester really need the half-time whistle so they can get in and regroup.

(39’) CLOSE! It's Mahrez once again who is troubling the Arsenal defence as he jinks onto his weaker right foot inside the penalty area. Mahrez tries to curl it into Ospina's top corner but on this occasion his shot bends wide.

(33’) Sanchez was on the receiving end of a heavy challenge from Robert Huth a few minutes ago and still seems to be feeling the effects of that tackle. Wenger and the Gunners faithful will be desperate not to lose their star man so soon after his return from injury. He appears ok to continue at the  moment.
(31’) That goal has noticeably lifted the crowd and more importantly the Arsenal player's who are playing with a lot more fluency now. Alexis Sanchez is seeing the ball and is running at the heart of the Leicester defence at every opportunity. If City are to get anything from this match it is vital that they don't concede again quickly.
(29’) After a fairly solid side the Premier League strugglers will be bitterly disappointed to have allowed Arsenal to score such a simple goal. The Gunners are pretty dangerous from set pieces and Koscielny did well to evade his marker.
--- 27’ Assist M. Özil gave the assist. ---
--- 27’ Goal! GOAL! Koscielny puts Arsenal in front! ---
(27’) Nigel Pearson will not be pleased with his sides defending for the goal as Koscielny side footed home from about six yards out under not a lot of pressure. It was a delicious cross from Ozil but far too easy for Arsenal.
(25’) Cambiasso chases down a seemingly lost cause and manages to win a corner from Bellerin. Leicester load the box with likes of Huth and Morgan but the delivery doesn't give them a chance and Arsenal are able to clear their lines easily.
(22’) Walcott is looking the most likely candidate at the moment to break through the wall of blue shirts. His pace and movement is troubling Konchesky and Ozil is trying to play him in at every opportunity.
(20’) Arsenal are now stringing a few passes together and are beginning to push Leicester City deeper into their own half. Cazorla and Coquelin are becoming more prominent, dominating in the central areas.
(18’) Alexis Sanchez lines up a freekick well within his range, about 30 yards from goal. The Chilean goes to whip it over the wall but only suceeds in hitting the head of Wes Morgan.
(16’) Despite that presentable opportunity for Walcott, Nigel Pearson will be very pleased with the way his side have reacted to their defeat at the weekend to Crystal Palace and the uncertainty that has surrounded the club since then. The Foxes have looke confident and well organised so far.
(14’) SAVE! Theo Walcott latches on to Mesut Ozil's perfectly weighted pass but can only hit his shot into the body of the onrushing Schwarzer. That was much better from the Gunners.

(10’) It's been a bit of a low-key start for the home side and the atmosphere has beeen understandably muted after the result at the weekend. Arsene Wenger could do with some of his senior players getting on the ball and asserting themselves on this match.
(8’) Danny Simpson bursts forwards after playing a one-two with Mahrez. Simpson hurdles a challenge from Cazorla before putting in a high and looping cross towards the back post Kramaric and Konchesky combine to keep the ball in play but the move fizzles out.
(6’) Bellerin and then Rosicky try to carry the ball forward and get Arsenal going as an attacking force but to no avail. The home side are however starting to settle into their usual passing rhythm.
(4’) The corner came to nothing but Leicester are enjoying a lot of early possession. The Foxes haven't won in their last 17 Premier League games in London and have had a troubled build up to this game with the rumours surrounding Nigel Pearson. The Emirates Stadium is slowly filling up as the latecomers take their seats.

QPR now go on to face fellow strugglers Hull in two weeks' time, whilst Sunderland face a trip to Bradford City in the FA Cup on Sunday before hosting West Bromwich Albion the following weekend.
QPR hold on to record their first away points of the season, and they are richly deserved. They were on the back foot for the majority of the second half but they looked impressive defending against a Sunderland side that were determined but lacked that spark in the final third of the pitch. As a result, the win moves them out of the relegation zone and up to 17th place thanks to Aston Villa's 2-0 defeat away to Hull City.
