Hazard picks out Matic atop the area and the midfielder's left-footed strike deflects off a defender and then off Ivanovic before nestling into the back of the net. Chelsea celebrate, but the right-back was deemed to be in an offside position when the ball came off him, and it won't count!
(83’) Everton defending desperately, booting balls out of the area in an attempt to clear their lines. Chelsea are keeping the pressure on and have seemingly everyone forward trying to bag a winner!
(81’) Stamford Bridge is buzzing now as Chelsea push hard for a late winner. They are throwing men forward, but cannot find a way through. Ivanovic hurls a long throw into the penalty area and it falls for Hazard atop the area, but the attacker gets it all wrong, scuffing a shot miles wide of the far post.
(79’) There's the threat he poses! Lukaku makes a tremendous run, taking on three defenders before laying a ball off for Mirallas. The substitute has looked lively since coming on, and he strikes for goal from 25 yards out but his shot blazes over the bar.
(77’) STAT ATTACK: Chelsea are unbeaten in their last 19 Premier League matches against Everton at Stamford Bridge (W10, D9), and have won three straight over the Toffees in London. They needed a 93rd minute winner from John Terry to secure a 1-0 victory over Roberto Martinez's men in this fixture last season.
(75’) The hosts are keeping Everton pinned in their own end, but have not been able to produce a chance since the introduction of their two new players. They are enjoying plenty of possession, but it is a bit too comfortable for the visitors in defence at the moment.
--- 74’ Substitution K. Mirallas enters the game and replaces A. Lennon. ---
--- 74’ Substitution D. Gibson enters play, replacing R. Barkley. ---
(73’) Chelsea have a sense of urgency about them now, with time running out to find a winner. Manchester City have opened up a 3-1 lead at the Britannia, and the Blues do not want to give them a glimmer of hope for a late title push. Meanwhile, Everton make their final two changes, with Barkley and Lennon being replaced by Darron Gibson and Kevin Mirallas.
(71’) Jose Mourinho has seen enough, making a double change to ensure his side do everything in their power to claim all three points. Club legend Didier Drogba is introduced, as is Premier League assists leader Cesc Fabregas, with Remy and Cuadrado giving way.
--- 70’ Substitution D. Drogba enters the game and replaces L. Rémy. ---
--- 70’ Substitution Fàbregas enters play, replacing J. Cuadrado. ---
(69’) THAT HAS TO BE IN! Oviedo gets into space on the left and sends a truly brilliant ball across the face of goal where Lukaku is there to meet it. The striker has a gaping goal in front of him, but puts it a bit too close to Cech who sticks a leg out to make the desperation save! That was the best chance of the match for either side and Lukaku really has to be scoring from there.
(67’) TREMENDOUS SAVE! Willian finds space inside the left of the penalty area and gets on the end of a through ball. He opens himself up and tries to curl a shot past Howard and in at the far post, but the keeper gets a very strong hand to it to keep it out! The American appears to be unbeatable this evening!
(65’) Chelsea's build up play has been superb, and a few wonderful runs from Hazard and company have seen Howard tested in goal. The problem for the hosts has been their inability to test the Everton defence with their crosses. They are getting into some prominent positions on the flanks, but have been lacking a good final ball into the area.
(63’) Close! It is Matic who takes, curling a shot past the wall and in towards the near post. Howard reads it well, however, and manages to dive across and get a hand to it, pushing it behind for a corner.
(62’) Hazard is taking the match over! The Belgian makes quick work of Naismith atop the area before skipping past Oviedo. He sees a sliver of space for a shot and powers a strike at goal, but Howard is able to punch it clear. The pressure remains on and Lennon fouls Willian atop the area, presenting the hosts with a great chance from the ensuing free kick...
(60’) Wonderful build up play from Chelsea as Willian slips Hazard through on the left channel. The Belgian takes on Stones and whips a dangerous ball across the face of goal, but Oviedo is there to turn it behind for a corner. The ensuing delivery is poor from Cuadrado allowing Everton to clear their lines.
--- 58’ Yellow card S. Coleman gets yellow. ---
(58’) Coleman picks up a yellow card, and it has been coming. The defender is dispossessed by Hazard in attack and is forced into a tackle to prevent the Belgian from breaking quickly.
(56’) James Milner has just restored Manchester City's lead at the Britannia, meaning Chelsea's lead atop the table could shrink if things remain the way they are. The absence of Diego Costa is showing its effects, as the hosts have been unable to capitalize on a slew of good scoring chances.
(54’) Important tackle! Back-to-back interventions from Stones prevent Chelsea from getting through on goal, as the young Everton defender shows his class, breaking up a threatening run from Ramires. He has really come into his own after strugglig through the early part of the season.
(52’) Wasteful. Brilliant movement off the ball by Barkley to free up Lennon, who receives a pass well with a positive first touch. He breaks into the area and has options for a cross, but the chance comes to nothing as he gets it all wrong, lofting the ball well wide of the far post and behind for a goal kick.
(50’) Coleman has twice now given away possession in dangerous areas, allowing Chelsea to break. Hazard takes on two defenders before laying a pass off for Cuadrado, but the Colombian shows too much of the ball to the right-back, who manages to recover by clearing the ball out for a throw.
(48’) Everton have to be appluaded for the way they have been able to organize themselves at the back. Again possession is squandered by them in midfield, but they get men back so quickly to keep their shape and prevent Chelsea from taking advantage.
--- 46’ Substitution J. McCarthy enters play, replacing M. Bešić. ---
(46’) Chelsea get the second half underway! Just one change to tell you about at the break, with James McCarthy replacing Muhamed Besic.
HALF TIME: CHELSEA 0-0 EVERTON. The Toffees are flattered by the scoreline at the break, with the hosts doing everything in attack but scoring. Cuadrado hardly looks like a man making his first Premier League start, looking more than accustomed to his new surroundings. Tim Howard has been superb in goal for the visitors in his return from injury.
(45’) There will be one minute of stoppage time at the end of the first half as indicated by the fourth official.
(43’) The pace has slowed a bit with half time approaching. It is looking more and more likely that we will head into the break scoreless, as Everton commit men back to ensure they do not make life any more difficult for themselves in the final 45 minutes by conceding late.
(41’) The hosts are back in possession now, working it around nicely in the final third. Everton are defending very deep which is allowing Chelsea to keep the pressure on. Hazard has been given the freedom to roam around in attack and has been a constant threat with the ball at his feet.
(39’) Everton have to move the ball quicker. They are winning possession in some encouraging areas but have been unable - or unwilling - to push forward quickly and expose the space being shown to them in attack. They are taking a far too patient approach to their build up play, which has allowed Terry and company to keep everything in front of them.
(37’) The tide is shifting just a bit and Roberto Martinez will hope this positive spell for his side can be carried into the break. The Toffees are lacking any real inventiveness and have not been able to trouble the Chelsea back four, but this is certainly a welcome break for their defence who have been under relentless pressure.
(35’) Everton manage their first real spell in possession in attack, though it is hardly penetrating. It is all too comfortable for Chelsea at the back, with the ball taking far too much time to get into the feet of Lukaku.
(33’) STAT ATTACK: The 54 goals scored by Chelsea in league play this season is the highest total in the top flight, while only Southampton (17) have conceded fewer goals than the Blues (21).
(31’) Important save! Cuadrado puts in more good work to win a corner, and though the ensuing delivery is poor, the Colombian winger links up well with Hazard to keep the pressure on. The Belgian cuts into the centre atop the area and drives a low, powerful strike at goal, but Howard does very well to absorb it and prevent a rebound with three Chelsea men waiting to pounce.
(29’) Great defensive play at both ends. Cuadrado charges through the middle with real intent, but he cannot get past a firm challenge from Stones, who then starts Everton forward. Lukaku is given an encouraging ball to chase, but Zouma stays with him stride for stride, sliding in to knock the ball off the striker and out for a throw.
(27’) Chelsea are applying relentless pressure on the Everton goal and it is something of a miracle that the game remains scoreless. The visitors can hardly get a second to breathe at the back, with the likes of Hazard, Willian and Cuadrado posing a serious threat in the final third.
(25’) Barry has to be careful here! Hazard skips past him in midfield and the Everton man tugs back his shirt to sniff out the chance. There did not appear to be too much in that challenge, with the Belgian making the most of it, but Barry is really pressing his luck having already been booked by referee Jonathan Moss.
--- 24’ Yellow card G. Barry is cautioned by the referee. ---
(24’) The pace of Cuadrado proves too much for Barry to deal with and the midfielder is forced to take him down with a quite cynical challenge. It is the 10th yellow card for the Everton man, who will now be forced to serve a two-match ban as a result.
(22’) With the exception of the one counter attack, Everton have been rather unimpressive in possession. The Toffees are taking far too long to move the ball up the pitch and are lacking decisiveness in attack. A lack of creativity has plagued them for much of the season, and that is already appearing to be the case here this evening. Chelsea are pushing forward, so there is space for the visitors to exploit.
(20’) They're running rampant! Chelsea are ripping the Everton defence to shreds, but cannot find an elusive opener! The Blues capitalize on a giveaway in their own end and Cuadrado starts a break forward. He picks out the run of Remy into the area, but the striker rolls a shot wide of the far post. You just start to wonder if Chelsea would be up 1-0 or 2-0 with Diego Costa available this evening.
(18’) It just needed a touch! Hazard links up well with Azpilicueta, laying off a pass for the left-back before making a run into the middle to get on the end of a return cross. It is a teasing deliviery from the Spaniard, but Hazard just fails to get a touch on it to direct it past Howard.
(16’) BLOCKED BEHIND! Hazard has been magnificent through the first quarter of an hour, this time coming out on top after a tackle from Stones in midfield and charging forward on a break. He cuts inside, disposing of his marker, before sliding the ball across for Remy. The striker cannot quite get his footing right, however, and sees his shot blocked behind by Oviedo.
--- 15’ Yellow card Azpilicueta is yellow-carded. ---
(14’) Chelsea are looking every bit like their record indicates, having won 32 of their last 39 Premier League matches at Stamford Bridge, while losing just once. They have started very positively and it appears to be only a matter of time before they are rewarded with a goal.
(12’) Magnificent stop! Chelsea could be made to rue these missed chances, the latest of which produces a superb save from Tim Howard. Remy gets on the end of a cross from Hazard and rises well to meet the ball, but his header is kept out by a strong hand from the American keeper.
(10’) What an incredible start to the match at Stamford Bridge! It is a very open start, picking up where they left off in Chelsea's 6-3 victory in the reverse fixture at Goodison Park. This time Cuadrado gets on the end of a pass on the right channel and breaks into the area, but the chance is wasted as he drags his shot wide of the far post.
(8’) BRILLIANT BREAK! It is the first attack of the match for the visitors and it produces the best chance of the game thus far. They transition so well to get into the final third, moving the ball quickly through midfield. Lukaku is played through on goal and tries to slot home at the near post, but Cech sticks out a strong leg to deflect the strike behind for a corner.
(6’) Everton need to get their legs under them, because it is all going wrong at the moment! Besic is tormented by a nifty run from Hazard and lunges himself into a challenge. That earns the midfielder the first yellow card of the match. Chelsea keep the pressure on following the free kick, and Willian makes quick work of Lennon before narrowly missing the top corner with a shot from 25 yards out.
--- 5’ Yellow card M. Bešić gets yellow. ---
(4’) WAS THAT A HANDBALL?! Shocking stuff from Naismith in the area as he throws his arm up to prevent the ball from getting to Cuadrado. He makes clear contact, but nothing is given by referee Jonathan Moss! The striker may have gotten away with one there.
(3’) Blazed over! Positive start for Chelsea as Matic's strength is on full display early on, powering through midfield under pressure from Barry, but he cannot test Howard in goal with his final shot. The league leaders look very lively to start this match.
(1’) The visitors kick-off and we are underway at Stamford Bridge! Everton in white. Chelsea in blue. A stern test awaits the champions - let's see how they do!
The players shake hands and the pre-match formalities are behind us. We are just a few short minutes away from kick-off on this cool night in London!
Tim Howard returns in goal for the Toffees after a lengthy absence as a result of a calf injury. Leighton Baines misses out yet again with a knee injury, joining Aiden McGeady, Steven Pienaar, Leon Osman and Christian Atsu on the list of absentees. James McCarthy is not fit enough to start and is relegated to a spot on the bench. Kevin Mirallas has also been removed from the starting XI, with Ross Barkley starting in his place. Meanwhile, Everton also give a first start to their new signing, Aaron Lennon.
Jose Mourinho has rotated his squad in anticipation of their all-important Champions League clash against PSG next week. Thibaut Courtois, Gary Cahill and Didier Drogba are relegated to the bench, with Oscar missing out due to a minor injury, according to the Portuguese coach. Starting in their place are Petr Cech, Kurt Zouma and Loic Remy, while a first Premier League start is given to new signing Juan Cuadrado. Diego Costa is serving the last game of his three-match ban, while Cesc Fabregas returns to full fitness, though he has been left on the bench as not to rush the Spaniard back into the starting XI.

CHELSEA SUBS: Luis, Fabregas, Ake, Drogba, Courtois, Cahill, Loftus-Cheek.

Everton do not have reason to panic just yet, though they are being dragged into a relegation battle in which they have no desire to be a part of. Going to Stamford Bridge is always a daunting task and it comes at an inopportune time, fresh off a hard-fought draw with Liverpool on Saturday in the latest edition of the Merseyside Derby. The matches start to pile up for the Toffees in February, with the Europa League getting back underway next week, but they can ill-afford to let it affect their performance domestically or it will create some nervy moments in the season's final month.
Chelsea ripped apart Everton in the reverse fixture this season, punishing the Toffees to the tune of a 6-3 scoreline at Goodison Park. Much of that can be attributed to Diego Costa bullying the Everton defence. Their back four has been much improved in 2015, however, and the Blues are without their leading goalscorer this evening, making what looks like a comfortable three points on paper much less straightforward. Their lead atop the Premier League table will have them at ease, but if they continue to play like they did at Villa Park on Saturday, it could shrink awfully quick.

The victory moves United back up to third place in the table, one point ahead of Southampton and five behind bitter rivals Manchester City ahead of their clash against Swansea City in two weeks' time. Meanwhile, Burnley remain in the relegation zone in 19th place and now face a tough game away to high-flying Chelsea in their next Premier League outing.
It was far from a vintage United performance this evening, but, once again, they have managed to get the job done and come away with three much-needed points. In the end, Burnley's missed opportunities cost them dearly, whilst Arfield's clumsy challenge on Di Maria and Van Persie's subsequent successful spot-kick ended any hopes of the visitors' pulling off a late comeback.
FULL-TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 3-1 BURNLEY
(90’) Van Persie is left in acres of space and is able to power forward before teeing up Wilson on the left hand side of the penalty area, and the youngster then fires a great shot that flies just past the near post and into the side-netting.
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Despite Ings seemingly struggling with an injury, it's Barnes who makes way for Jutkiewicz in what will most likely be Burnley's final change of the evening. ---
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be four minutes of added time.
(88’) Two great chances for United! First, Di Maria forces Heaton into pulling off a good save with a rocket of a shot from just inside the penalty area, before Januzaj fires the follow-up into Shackell on the goal line. Burnley are holding on by the skin of their teeth!

--- 86’ Yellow card And now Di Maria enters the referee's book after flying into Kightly and bringing the midfielder down with a cynical sliding challenge. ---

(81’) PENALTY! United break away quickly after dealing with the corner, and, again, Di Maria's pace causes Burnley problems, with Arfield flying into the Argentine and bring him down with a clumsy challenge on the left hand side of the box.
(80’) Great chance for Kightly! United push forward and win themselves a corner, which is flung into the heart of the penalty area. It pinballs around the box before falling at the feet of the midfielder, who then fires a fierce shot that is deflected just over the top of the crossbar.
(78’) Smalling dispossesses Kightly in the middle of the pitch and United break away on a brilliant counter attack. Di Maria then picks up the ball on the right flank before chipping a cross towards Van Persie, but Trippier does extremely well to send the attempted pass out for a corner with a vital diving header.
(76’) Januzaj cuts inside from the left flank before sprinting towards the Burnley penalty area, but he's completely outnumbered, not to mention isolated, and is only able to run into a sea of silver shirts, who eventually dispossess him.
--- 74’ Substitution United have decided to make their final substitution of the game, with Falcao, who has been poor this evening, making way for Wilson. ---
(72’) Almost immediately from the restart, Kightly sends a deep cross into the United penalty area that almost finds the unmarked Barnes in front of goal, but De Gea is just about able to cut it out before it's able to meet the head of the striker on the edge of the six-yard box.
(70’) Trippier seems to be in some discomfort after clashing with Falcao, but, after receiving medical treatment for a few moments, it looks as if he is going to be able to continue.
--- 68’ Yellow card And now Falcao enters the referee's book after elbowing Trippier in the back of the neck as the two battled for the ball in the air. ---
--- 67’ Yellow card Herrera and Arfield clash in the middle of the pitch, with the latter wrestling the Spaniard to the ground in frustration, and, as a result, he is shown a yellow card. ---
(65’) Di Maria picks up the ball on the right hand side of the penalty area before twisting and curling an absolutely wonderful cross into the heart of the box, but it's unable to find Falcao and is headed away from danger by Keane.
(63’) Cries for a United penalty, but the referee shakes his head and waves play on! Di Maria twists and turns his way into the Burnley box before seemingly being tripped over by Shackell near the byline, but Kevin Friend isn't interested in the slightest, much to the annoyance of the Argentine.

(57’) McNair almost finds Di Maria with a great through-ball that seemed destined for the feet of the Argentine, but Shackell dives in to cut out the pass at the vital moment.
(55’) Great movement by Januzaj! The youngster picks up the ball on the left flank and beats Boyd before darting towards the edge of the Burnley penalty area. He then fires a wonderful low shot that forces Heaton into a vital diving save to his left.

That was a perfect opportunity to fire his side back into the game!
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.

They have continually caused the United back four plenty of problems, with Smalling finding it incredibly difficult to deal with the strike duo of Ings and Barnes. The defenders' brace is what currently separates the two sides, however, but you can bet that the visitors will come out all guns blazing when the game resumes in 15 minutes' time.

(70’) GREAT EFFORT FROM PUNCHEON! The ball breaks kindly for him on the edge of the area and he bends an effort towards the far corner, but it flashes just past the post with Schwarzer beaten.

For Man City, they now have to gear themselves up for a midweek clash against Stoke City at the Britannia Stadium on Wednesday, with their home clash against Barcelona in the Champions League at the end of the month on the horizon.
Next up for Hull is a home clash against relegation rivals Aston Villa at the KC Stadium, in what will no doubt be dubbed in due course as a six-pointer down the bottom of the table. After that, another home clash awaits against 19th-placed Queens Park Rangers, who lost 1-0 to Southampton today.
Hull's point is enough to see them move out of the bottom three momentarily on goal difference, with Burnley not playing today. The visitors were exceptional for the whole game and always looked a threat on the break, but one moment of magic from Milner was able to thwart them from picking up all three points.
The result means Man City are now without a win in their last four league matches and sit seven points behind Chelsea, who picked up a 2-1 win over Aston Villa elsewhere in the Premier League today.
Bruce's men took a shock lead in the first-half thanks to a strike from Meyler, with Man City's defence all over the place after a series of assaults from Hull. When it looked like the Tigers were on course for a massive three points, second-half substitute Milner popped up with a superb free-kick to see the hosts snatch a last-gasp point.
The look on every single Hull City player says it all. Having come to the Etihad and defended so well, despite picking up a fantastic, hard-earned point against the Champions in their back yard, the Tigers will be gutted they haven't been able to hold on for all three.

As for West Brom, they are continuing to struggle to find much-needed victories, and they head into today's clash with just one from their last seven league games. The referee's full-time whistle is met with jeers from the home fans as Stoke City secured a last-gasp 1-1 draw thanks to Crouch. Colback had initially given the hosts the lead after a rather dull 74 minutes, though that goal seemingly brought the match to life. Carver's side should have wrapped up victory through Obertan and then Ayoza, but neither displayed the necessary composure to extend the lead and the away side ultimately hit back at the death to secure a point.
(90’) FULL-TIME!
(90’) Time is almost up now for Newcastle to steal a last-gasp winner, with the match now in the final minute of stoppage time. The hosts' recent woes look set to continue.
(90’) Newcastle really should have been home and dry before Crouch's goal, with both Obertan and Ayoze presented with glorious opportunities in the final 10 minutes. Stoke have really made the most of those let-offs.
--- 90’ Assist The assist came from G. Cameron. ---
--- 90’ Goal! GOAL!!! STOKE ARE LEVEL! Cameron is released down the right by N'Zonzi and the right-back's cross is lofted deep into the area. Crouch rises highest and meets it at the back post, looping his effort over Krul and into the net, despite Coloccini's best efforts. ---
--- 89’ Yellow card Muniesa receives a yellow card. ---
(87’) WONDERFUL RUN! Ayoze causes havoc down the left flank as he runs at Cameron, cuts inside him and then runs into the area. The young Spaniard then skips past another challenge and goes for goal, but his effort is blazed well over.
--- 86’ Substitution M. Abeid comes on for Sammy Ameobi. ---
(85’) WHAT A CHANCE FOR NEWCASTLE! Terrific breakaway by the home side, as Sissoko charges into the Stoke half and strides away from Moses. He slips a pass into the right side of the area for Obertan, who rides the challenge of Wollscheid, but instead of going for goal with just Begovic to beat, the Frenchman tries to set up a team-mate and gives the ball away. What a let-off for Stoke.
(84’) Stoke finally force Krul into action, as Bardsley tries his luck from distance after being teed up by Crouch, but the full-back's stinging drive is fired straight at the Dutch goalkeeper.
--- 82’ Substitution S. Ireland is done for the day. P. Crouch is his replacement. ---
(82’) It appears that Ireland's final contribution was to have his goal chalked off, as he is now replaced by Crouch after seemingly picking up a hamstring strain.
(80’) Stoke have ten minutes to get themselves level again if they want to avoid defeat here. They have largely controlled the possession in this second half, though chances haven't exactly been a regular occurrence for them.
(78’) Just for a few seconds Stoke think they have an equaliser, as Ireland produces a fine finish into the top-left corner from the edge of the area, but he had previously strayed just offside.
(76’) Colback may consider himself lucky to still be on the pitch to score that goal, but he made his presence count and Newcastle have the lead, despite struggling to really get to grips with the midfield battle since the break.
--- 74’ Assist The assist came from M. Sissoko. ---
--- 74’ Goal! GOAL!!! NEWCASTLE HAVE THE LEAD! The hosts work the ball really well out to the right flank, as Ayoze slips a pass down the right side of the Stoke area for Obertan, who zips a fierce low cross into the danger zone. Sissoko controls it and tees the ball up on the edge of the area for Colback, whose sliced effort nestles in the bottom-left corner. ---
(73’) Ameobi has been quiet since the break, but he comes into a central position now to get himself involved. He squares up to Whelan and then passes to Obertan to his right. The Frenchman gets a decent cross in, but the delivery is played a little behind Cisse and his header goes wide.
(72’) Colback really is walking a tightrope now. The England international goes in hard on Moses and gets nowhere near the ball, but he escapes a second yellow card. He can't have too many of those left before being sent off.
(71’) Obertan gets himself involved straight away out on the right and, after producing a stepover, he drives a cross into the area, which is cleared before Cisse can pounce.
(70’) The Newcastle fans clearly aren't impressed now. Carver brings off Cabella, a decision met with jeers from the home faithful and Obertan takes his place, making his comeback from a three-month injury lay-off.
--- 69’ Substitution G. Obertan enters play, replacing R. Cabella. ---
(68’) The goalkeeper is called into action this time, though! Haidara looks to deal with Diouf, but he finds himself robbed of the ball again and the Senegal forward fires into the area. Krul intercepts, though, much to the relief of the Newcastle left-back.
(67’) Just like in the first half, Stoke have so far had the better of the possession since the break. Though, their threat has been more suggestive than definitive, with Krul still having little to do in goal.
--- 65’ Substitution V. Anita is done for the day. P. Cissé is his replacement. ---
(65’) Carver appears to have seen enough. Off goes Anita and on comes Cisse, as Newcastle go all out to claim all three points.
(64’) It's certainly Stoke in the ascendancy at the moment, with Newcastle struggling to get out of their own penalty area. Nevertheless, with Sissoko, Ayoze, Cabella and Ameobi still sitting fairly high up, they look well set up for the counterattack.
(62’) True to form, Moses' corner delivery fails to even beat the first man, giving Newcastle the chance to clear. But, thankfully for Stoke, the clearance isn't much better and they swiftly work the ball to N'Zonzi on the left. He tries to trick his way past Janmaat, but must settle for another corner.
(61’) Newcastle have to defend a corner now, as Stoke win the set-piece seemingly out of nothing on the right flank. Moses heads across to take it.
(59’) It must be said that, so far, this second half has not been much of an improvement on the first. Neither side appears to have much control over proceedings, particularly in midfield, while chances have been infrequent. Newcastle certainly have players capable of causing problems in Cabella, Ayoze and Sissoko, but they aren't having much of an impact currently.
(57’) Stoke eventually get the ball out wide to Moses, who is in plenty of space. He runs at Janmaat, but the Dutch defender does well against the winger after showing him inside, forcing a pass back to Whelan, whose eventual delivery into the area goes straight out of play.
(56’) Stoke are enjoying an extended spell in possession in the Newcastle half, though they aren't creating much, as they continue to struggle to break down the hosts' resolute defence.
(54’) Colback now goes into the referee's book following a late challenge on Muniesa, whom he was trying to stop from crossing the ball. He accepts the booking with no protest.
--- 53’ Yellow card J. Colback is cautioned by the referee. ---
(53’) Lovely move by the hosts, as Janmaat slips a pass in towards the centre for Ayoze. The Spaniard edges into the area, skipping past Wollsheid in the process and then teeing up Cabella. The Frenchman instantly plays a return pass into the danger zone, but the former Tenerife man can't get it under control.
--- 51’ Substitution M. Wilson is replaced with G. Cameron. ---
(51’) And there is the change. Wilson's day is over and he is replaced by Cameron, who goes over to the right, with Bardsley coming to the left.
(50’) The referee is allowing a pause in play now. First it is Ayoze who is down after finding himself sandwiched between Wollscheid and Wilson, and then the latter kicks the ball out to receive medical attention himself.
(48’) One thing that has been particularly noticeable so far, is that the atmosphere at St. James' Park has been rather muted. Admittedly the fans have not been given much to shout about, but it is surprisingly quiet.
(46’) Right, off we go for the second half. Can these two sides be separated?
Newcastle 0-0 Stoke: The referee brings the first half to a close with the score still level. The hosts have generally had the better of the first 45 with regards to goal-scoring chances, as both Cabella and Ayoze have gone close. But, it is Stoke who have seen more of the ball, without doing too much with it until the closing stages. Quality has been sadly lacking, though hopefully the contest will become more open as both sides go in search of a win.
(45’) HALF-TIME!
(45’) KRUL TO THE RESCUE! Ireland finds space in the right side of the area and, although he appears to be offside, the midfielder crosses into the danger zone. Diouf gets ahead of his marker and directs a header towards goal, but the keeper palms it away.
(45’) There will be three minutes added on here.
(44’) JUST WIDE OF THE TARGET! Cabella drops into a deep position and brilliantly turns his marker, before playing a fine throughball towards the area for Ayoze. The Spaniard's first touch isn't great, but he is still able to get a shot away from 20 yards, sending a low effort agonisingly wide of the left-hand post.
(42’) Moses stands over the free-kick and fires a delivery into the danger area, but Coloccini is there to nod clear. It must be said, set-pieces have been generally poor so far toay.
(41’) Free-kick to Stoke is a great position now. Wilson plays the ball down the left wing for Diouf and he initially manages to hold off Janmaat, before going to down after being tripped.
(39’) Good defending by Newcastle. Walters plays a clever pass into the danger area for Diouf, who has Coloccini for company. The Argentine gets his feet a little tangled and appears to be in trouble, but Haidara covers well and steals possession back.
(37’) It's heating up a bit out there at the moment. Tackles are flying in and Ireland seemingly eyes retribution as he goes in hard on Ameobi, looking to block his clearance up the flank. The crowd react, though the referee ignores the protests.
--- 35’ Yellow card Sammy Ameobi receives a yellow card. ---
(35’) Ameobi is back on the pitch and his first action results in a booking, as the winger is dispossessed and in a fit of frustration, he cynically brings down Ireland.
(34’) Cabella stands over the resulting free-kick, about 35 yards from goal out on the left flank. He curls a decent delivery into the danger area, though no one is quite alive enough to get on the end of it and Stoke bring the ball away.
--- 33’ Yellow card G. Whelan is cautioned by the referee. ---
(33’) Whelan is the latest Stoke player to go into the referee's book. The Irish midfielder produced a strong challenge on Ameobi, who appears to be in some pain, and the yellow card comes out.
(31’) Newcastle are looking to exploit Cabella's pace down the flank now, as the French midfielder latches on to Haidara's pass up the wing. (30’) We have a brief pause in play now as Muniesa seeks medical attention. The Spaniard appears to have been taken out by his own team-mate, Wollscheid.
(28’) Clever feet from Ameobi. The winger comes in from his wide berth and spins past Whelan after taking up possession. Space opens up for him and he tries his luck from distance, forcing a comfortable save from Begovic.
(27’) Excellent counterattack from the hosts now. Sissoko charges forward through the centre, forcing the Stoke defence back as he hares towards them. The Frenchman slips a pass to his left for Cabella and instantly gets into the area in anticipation of the return pass, but Begovic is quick off his line to deal with the danger.
(26’) Bardsley takes the throw-in short and Diouf does rather well considering the pressure he is put under. The Senegal international squeezes past Haidara down the outside, but his eventual low delivery into the air is poor.
(25’) Stoke are trying to put together some passes in the Newcastle half, though they are struggling with the hosts' pressing tactics. The visitors do find some luck this time, however, and Bardsley wins a throw-in to the right of the penalty area.
--- 23’ Yellow card S. Ireland goes into the referee's book. ---
(23’) Strong challenge there from Ireland on Colback and the Stoke man has his name taken, somewhat unsurprisingly. Hughes isn't impressed, but it was certainly a late tackle.

(20’) Newcastle deal with the corner fairly comfortably, but Stoke remain on the front foot. The ball is knocked back out to the right for Moses, who does well to beat Haidara, knocking it past the full-back with a clever header. His delivery, however, leaves a lot to be desired and the home side get away unscathed.
(19’) Carver is not happy as Stoke are awarded a throw-in, when the ball did not appear to hit a Newcastle player last. The visitors then work the ball down the flank and win themselves a corner. It'll be controversial if they score from this!
(17’) Well, that was all a bit of a waste. The corner is cleared by the first man and then, from the following throw-in, Haidara's cross is headed well wide of the target by Ayoze.
(16’) Excellent run by Haidara there. The left-back has started well as he charges forward with the ball this time. He shrugs off one challenge, eases past another defender and then runs at Bardsley, who is forced to concede a corner.
--- 15’ Yellow card V. Moses is cautioned by the referee. ---
(15’) Good play by Walters as he brings down another lofted pass in the final third, holds off Janmaat and then plays a clever back-heel into the path of Moses. The winger runs at the Newcastle full-back, but the combination of him and Cabella snuff out the danger.
(13’) While we haven't seen too much to get excited about in this yet, it is clear that it is Newcastle who are trying to force the issue. Ameobi and Cabella have looked bright so far, while Haidara is getting forward whenever possible down the left. Ayoze will be hoping for some service, though.
(11’) NEWCASTLE GO CLOSE! The home side click into gear brilliantly down the left. Ameobi skips past a challenge, draws a defender and then slips a pass down the flank for Sissoko. The France international crosses and Cabella manages to reach the delivery with a glancing header, but Begovic is there to make the save.
(9’) There is the match's first shot and Walters exhibits some trademark physicality, as he brings a long ball down, holds off Williamson and manages to get a shot away from about 30 yards. Krul watches his effort go just wide, however.
(8’) Ameobi has looked bright during these early exchanges, picking up the ball and running at his man out on the left flank. Though, on this occasion he is tackled and he then concedes a free-kick.
(6’) Nothing comes of the free-kick, as Stoke's physically imposing backline clears the ball fairly easily. Newcastle try to keep their visitors back inside their own half with his intense pressing, but they eventually make an escape.
(5’) Newcastle change the pace of the match in an instant, as the ball is played forward by Sissoko. He finds Cabella, who tries to play Ayoze into the area, though his pass is cut out. The hosts eventually win a free-kick about 35 yards from goal, however, as Anita is tripped by N'Zonzi.
(3’) We certainly haven't seen a frantic start to proceedings here. The two sides are knocking the ball around patiently, not doing an awful lot in possession as they size up their respective opponents.
(1’) Off we go! Stoke get us underway.
The two teams are out on the pitch as kick-off approaches!
Mark Hughes also a few injury concerns to take into account. Captain Ryan Shawcross is out for three weeks with a back injury, while Erik Pieters, Bojan and Peter Odemwingie are all still out. But, Jonathan Walters is able to feature after overcoming a knee problem, but Marko Arnautovic misses out after injuring himself in training yesterday.
Carver continues to make do without a host of first-team regulars, with Tiote (Africa Cup of Nations duty), Rob Elliott, Ryan Taylor, Steven Taylor, Siem de Jong and Rolando Aaron all missing from the squad. Few will expect a similar outcome today, but Stoke will undoubtedly believe they are good enough to hit back, potentially exploiting the uncertainty that has surrounded the Newcastle team since Pardew's departure.
Newcastle come into this clash looking to build upon last week's 3-0 crushing of Hull City, a result which was John Carver's first triumph since taking over as interim manager following Alan Pardew's departure. United suffered three successive Premier League defeats before that, seeing themselves slip into the bottom half of the table. However, a win today will see the hosts swap places with Stoke, taking them up to tenth.

--- 80’ Yellow card Adrián receives a yellow card. ---
(79’) Adrian is the latest player to go into the book and it is for time wasting on his goal kicks. The Spaniard has been guilty of that throughout the game so we may indeed see a generous portion of injury time added on by the referee. Man United are going to need it!
(77’) What a sitter from Radamel Falcao! Man United pump the ball up the pitch and the Colombian gets the better of his marker to run through one-on-one with the keeper, but ends up using the wrong foot to finish and sends a right-footed strike wide of the left-hand post!
(75’) Fellaini releases Valencia down the right wing and the latter then lays the ball off to Rooney. The Man United captain looks to take on three West Ham players and ends up going down easily, rather sheepishly looking for a free kick. The referee has none of it and waves play forward.
--- 73’ Yellow card A. Song is yellow-carded. ---
(73’) We see our first West Ham booking of the match now and it has been coming for Alex Song, who once again breaks down a Man United attack with a cynical trip. It is on Rooney this time, and Van Gaal's outfit get the free kick around 25 yards out.
--- 72’ Substitution M. Fellaini enters play, replacing A. Januzaj. ---
(71’) First belated change from Man United now and it sees Januzaj come off to be replaced by Fellaini, who will certainly add a physical presence in and around the penalty area, which the visitors have been desperately lacking so far. Can the Belgian make a positive impact?
(69’) Rooney's heavy touch in the final third allows West Ham to intercept and instigate a pacey counterattack. Sakho is released down the left channel but the ascendancy of the hosts dies down due to a poor touch of his own from the Senegalese.
(67’) Valencia gets to the byline and stands a cross into the box, which is cleared out of the area by Tomkins. Januzaj latches on to it and looks to get a volley away, but it goes high and wide into the stand, despite his claims that it took a deflection. Arguably sums up Man United so far!
(65’) Di Maria stands over a corner kick from the right and whips a superb delivery to the back post. Van Persie looks poised to get the header away but Jenkinson is on hand to make a fantastic clearance before for another corner. Sights of Fellaini warming up for United now.
(63’) Jenkinson gets into an advanced position down the right wing and teases a brilliant cross to the back post. It is too far for De Gea and Valencia leaves it in fear of giving away an own goal. His namesake, Enner Valencia, can't make up the ground to turn a strike towards goal!
(61’) Di Maria drives down the right wing but seems unwilling to cross in on his right foot, so turns back, but not before being outnumbered by three West Ham defenders. The Argentine comes out of the situation unscathed and slides a pass into the channel for Valencia, but he resulting cross is easily cleared.
(59’) Much, much better from Manchester United here as they pin West Ham back into their own penalty area. Signs of improvement coming from Van Gaal's men, but they still need to test Adrian a hell of a lot more. Plenty of options on the bench for the visitors in the form of Mata, Fellaini, Herrera, and Wilson.
(57’) Shaw fires a pass into the feet of Falcao and the Colombian initially does brilliantly to shake off the attentions of Kouyate and turn into the box, however the resulting cross into the box is easily intercepted by Jenkinson.
(55’) This would normally be a relatively early time for a manager to start thinking about changing things, but Man United have been so desperately ineffective going forward that Van Gaal may want to make a switch rather soon.
(53’) SAVE FROM ADRIAN! The West Ham man is called into action for the first time in the game as Di Maria finds Van Persie with a lovely pass over the top of the defence. The Dutchman typically goes for the powerful half volley, which is well-saved at the front post from the keeper!
(51’) Allardyce's men have came flying out of the blocks in this second period, and they have managed to keep up their impressive tempo from the first half. Man United, meanwhile, are looking out of ideas in the final third!
--- 49’ Goal! GOOOOAAALLL!! GOOOAAALLL!! GOOOAAALLL FOR WEST HAM! The subsequent set-piece from the Valencia foul is floated into the box and Kouyate takes one, two, three, fantastic touches before swivelling and volleying past De Gea, who is left helpless! Sensational goal, and it is no less than the Hammers deserve! ---
(47’) De Gea's kick to the right wing pulls Valencia in a spot of bother and the Ecuadorian is forced into committing a foul on Noble after being robbedof possession. This gives West Ham yet another set piece opportunity here.
(46’) We are back under way in this Barclays Premier League clash!
Half time at the Boleyn Ground. It has been a hard-fought opening 45 minutes here between West Ham and Manchester United with the home side enjoying the better of the play and of the chances in the final third. David De Gea has been in great form in between the sticks for his side, denying Valencia twice and a Tomkins header. Van Gaal's outfit need some refreshing in the second period!
(45’) Just the one minuted of added time in this first half. Di Maria opts to take a corner kick quickly to Rooney and then eventually receives the ball back from Valencia, but the former Real Madrid man sees his cross into the box cleared by Tomkins.
--- 43’ Yellow card M. Rojo is yellow-carded. ---
(43’) In the lead up to that poor final product from Sakho, Rojo completely took out Noble with the referee rightly playing the advantage. Mark Clattenburg remembers the incident a few moments later and gives the Argentine defender a yellow card.
(41’) What is Sakho doing there?! West Ham steal possession and mount a pacey counterattack with the Senegal international leading the charge! It is two versus two but he somehow manages to find De Gea with a poor deflected cross-come-shot! A really good chance passed up there from the hosts!
(39’) Song attempts a risky pass in midfield which is swiftly pounced upon by Di Maria. The Argentine drives through the middle and releases Falcao with a precision pass down the left wing, but Kouyate marshalls the striker well and forces him near the touchline. In the end nothing comes from the attack.
(37’) Sakho and Valencia have worked their socks off so far in terms of their running into the channels to stretch the Man United defence. Jones and Rojo have been dragged around all over the place in an attempt to clear the danger, which to be fair they have did so up until this point.
(35’) Van Gaal needs to do something, anything to deal with the set-piece prowess of West Ham here. The home side have won just about every single corner kick or free kick thrown into the box in the air, but they somehow find themselves unable to take advantage each time.
(33’) West Ham continue to pile the pressure on to Man United with various crosses into the box and possession on the edge of the area. The sting slightly comes out of the play of the hosts though as Song breaks down an attack with a poor shot that is sliced well wide from 25 yards.
(31’) De Gea bails Man United out! Another West Ham set-piece is floated into the box and Tomkins shows his threat inside the opposition box again by getting a header away at the back post. The goalkeeper is positioned perfectly to make the save with his feet though!
(29’) The West Ham fans are demanding that Van Persie be shown a card here as he appears to throw a wayward arm into the face of Tomkins during an aerial challenge. The Dutchman is given the benefit of the doubt from the ref, but it did look like there was some intent in it. A yellow card probably would have sufficed.
(27’) Spaces are just beginning to open up for the Red Devils here as they look to gain the ascendancy. Having said that, Adrian has not had one single shot to deal with in between the sticks for the Hammers.
(25’) Man United find themselves all over the place at the back as Valencia gets in behind the midfield to dart forward. The striker lays the ball off for Sakho to get the strike away but the covering Valencia does brilliantly to slide in in the nick of time to prevent the shot.
(23’) Di Maria finally manages to open up his stride through the middle and releases Van Persie down the left wing. The Dutchman's cross is too deep, but is eventually collecting by Rooney at the back post, who passes inside as Man United keep up their moment of pressure.
(21’) Allardyce's men can take confidence from this opening 20 minutes or so, as they have been by far the better side. Man United have plenty of attacking firepower out there, but Rooney, Di Maria, Januzaj, Van Persie, and Falcao are just not being allowed any space to operate.
(19’) Shaw manages to get forward for the first time in the match and swings a cross to the back post. Van Persie gets into an aerial battle with Kouyate, with the West Ham defender coming out on top on this occasion. A little more creativity required from the Red Devils here.
(17’) This has been a very good start from the Hammers who look the most likely side to open the scoring here. Man United have attempted their short passing game from the get-go but the home side are not allowing them any time on the ball, and are hunting in packs to reclaim possession in central areas.
(15’) De Gea to the rescue again! Tomkins causes problems at the back post and heads a corner kick back into the six-yard box. Valencia meets the knockdown and twists his body to get a clever volley away, but the Spaniard saves his side with a top drawer save! Another corner kick to West Ham!
(13’) SAVE BY DE GEA! Rojo's poor clearance goes straight to the feet of Valencia and the Ecuadorian latches on to it before lashing a right-footed strike towards the bottom corner. The Man United keeper is on his feet though and palms around the post with authority!
(11’) We haven't seen too much of Falcao and Van Persie so far. Indeed, it has been the opposite striking duo of Valencia and Sakho who have looked the most dangerous. Rojo and Jones certainly know already they are in for a game today!
(9’) Downing swings a deep corner kick to the back post and Tomkins rises above everyone to head back into the danger area. Rooney is on hand to clear out of the box but West Ham manage to recycle possession near the touchline. Decent period for the home side at the moment.
(7’) Song gets into an advanced position this time and collects the ball in a useful area before attempting to chip a pass through to the onrushing Cresswell, but Valencia is vigilant enough to see it out for a Man United goal kick. That probably won't be the last time we see the former Ipswich defender getting forward down the left!
(5’) Very dodgy from Song! The West ham midfielder attempts a square pass along his own box which Van Persie intercepts. The Dutchman looks poised to get a shot away but is just foiled at the last minute by Kouyate who comes in with a great clearing tackle! The home side almost shot themselves in the foot there, but they survive!
(3’) Januzaj gets just beyond the West Ham midfield and looks to open up his stride down the left channel, but is rather cynically tripped up by Song. The on-loan Barcelona man apologetically gets up and eventually avoids receiving a yellow card. Lucky man!
(1’) We are under way at the Boleyn Ground!
The players have took to the pitch and we are almost ready for kick off!

Indeed, Man United have won 11 out of the last 12 meetings with West Ham in the Barclays Premier League. No time like the present to stop the rot for Sam Allardyce and his men!
In the previous clash between West Ham and Man United earlier in the season, Van Gaal's outfit ran out narrow 2-1 winners thanks to goals from Robin van Persie and Wayne Rooney, despite the latter being sent off. The United captain has actually netted 10 goals in his last nine league games against the Hammers, so will be hoping to continue that kind of form today.
After only managing a draw against Cambridge, Man United have got back to winning ways in the past week with a comfortable 3-1 home league win over Leicester and a victory against the League 2 side in the FA Cup replay at Old Trafford to progress to the next round of the competition.
After a scintillating start to the season in which West Ham got into the top four a few times in the first half of the campaign, the Hammers had a tough Christmas period in which they failed to win in five straight games. Things were looking up in the middle of January when consecutive FA Cup wins over Everton and Bristol City and a league victory over Hull were recorded, but their good form was halted last week with a 2-0 defeat versus Liverpool at Anfield.
Louis van Gaal's outfit are currently situated fourth in the table in the last remaining Champions League place, which will no doubt have been roughly the minimal target at the start of the campaign. However, with Southampton defeating Swansea to move into third yesterday, and Tottenham piling on the pressure from below after their north London derby win over Arsenal, the pressure is certainly on the Red Devils for a win this afternoon.

In the end, Steve Bruce can have few complaints about the scoreline after another poor performance from his side, whose struggles in front of goal continue to go on. (78’) Murray goes up for another, great cross but Robles again gathers well. The home team are building up a head of steam.

(73’) Puncheon looks to release Gayle but his pass is again woefully overhit and Robles takes it under no pressure. Zaha was in space on the right as well.
(72’) It's all Palace at the moment, but they lack a cutting edge. Barry intercepts and looks for Lukaku but Delaney clears well.

(70’) Palace have another free-kick, from deeper this time, which Ward floats in towards Dann  again. Delaney goes down in the box contesting the ball but the referee is unmoved. (61’) Another aimless Palace through-ball, another easy gather by Robles. Pardew needs to make a change here if his side are to come from behind again.

(56’) Sanogo, about three yards from the Toffees' goal, jumps but cannot head Gayle's excellent, zipping cross. He looked offside but should have at least connected.

(52’) Gareth Barry is hobbling after a snappy tackle in midfield, but I suspect he will be fine. He's been dishing them out and taking them his entire career.

(49’) Palace lose out in midfield and Everton look to break at speed, but the ball is cleared all the way back to Robles. He looks long but Palace win the throw.

Join me soon for the second half of Crystal Palace 0-1 Everton LIVE!
Neither side have kept the ball well or defended with any authority but Everton have made fewer errors and generally hassled Palace until the home team make a mistake. Lukaku has looked strong and purposeful and Naismith has played well.
Palace looked ascendent after that, until a cruel blow to Marouane Chamakh's blow, suffered in a totally legitimate challenge with Seamus Coleman, robbed the home side of their best player up to that point.

(45’) Everton are again looking to Lukaku on their left. It's a tactic which is yielding results as another good cross comes in, which Palace hurriedly clear.
(45’) Naismith concedes a free-kick on the halfway way and Dann lumps it into the box. It bounces as Sanogo fails to connect and then Puncheon carves a half-volley around a metre high and wide of Robles left post.
(45’) Lukaku does very well to waste some time up against Ward and Puncheon in the far right-hand side of the Palace half.

(41’) Palace are testing Baines through Ward and Puncheon. It's a clever tactic, but now they give the ball away again and Everton are able to attack.
(39’) Baines is hobbling a lot, which will be very worrying for Roberto Martinez. Coleman finds space on the overlap and tries to cross to Lukaku, but his ball is high and wide.
(38’) Ledley redeems himself with a superb tackle on Naismith having first fired a pass directly into an Everton player to concede possession. That's one of a number of times Palace have given the ball away cheaply and in dangerous areas.
(37’) Sanogo puts himself through the back of Baines to concede a free-kick. That is frustration, without doubt.
(36’) As if to prove my point, Everton fail to clear twice, almost affording first Ledley and then Puncheon shooting opportunities.
(35’) Kelly gives the ball away in midfield leaving Palacer very exposed at the bak, but Everton dither and cannot capitalise. You can see why these teams are not doing so well at the moment: neither defends with any confidence and both make silly mistakes.
(34’) Puncheon brings a low, plunging save from Robles to his left with a dipping shot from the edge of the area. It was a good, rather than a great save, but at least Palace produced an effort.

(24’) Chamakh is finally taken off on a stretcher. Gayle may push up to play off Sanogo, or Mutch may play in the number 10 spot.
(23’) All this added time will be interesting when Palace are inevitably pushing forwards in pursuit of an equaliser at the end of the first half!
(22’) Coleman is fine but Marouane Chamakh is still on the floor having his nose looked at. And treated, obviously. Only looking at it would not achieve very much.
(21’) Mutch is readying himself to come on for Chamakh. The challenge with Coleman was fair, by the way: both were contesting a high ball and had eyes only for that.
(19’) Robles puts a clearance straight out for a throw, but then atones for his error with a good take in the air followed by a swift throw to launch a counter-attack, which Palace deal with well. (18’) Baines fires over, disappointingly. Speroni goes long with the goal kick but puts it straight out.
(17’) Chamakh produces a centre-forward's challenge on the edge of the Palace box, giving Everton a free-kick in a very dangerous position from which Baines will look to profit.
(16’) Palace are playing it around nicely but their attack is thwarted when Baines tackles Puncheon well.
(14’) Delaney blocks Lukaku well and the Belgian hurls himself theatrically through the air to no avail. This is vey open, neither side looking very comfortable defensively but both pretty exciting going forwards.

(7’) Robles clears long towards Lukaku but Ward steals in and plays a good pass forwards, which Everton knock out for a throw-in.

(90’) There will be three minutes of added time as indicated by the fourth official.
(88’) They have surely done enough to see it out now. The clock winds down with United comfortably in possession yet again. They aren't forcing anything, and with Leicester having tired themselves out, this should be a fairly straightforward finish for the hosts.
(86’) Wonderful run from Di Maria to get on the end of a ball over the top. He is behind the defence as he gets into the area, but lacks composure as he scuffs his half-volley well high and wide. He had Wilson surging forward in the centre and could have done with sending a ball across the face of goal.
(84’) FIRED OVER! Surely they can't get another?! Leicester have a spring in their step now and are just giving United something to think about in the closing minutes. Wasilewski tries to return the favour, heading a ball down into the path of Albrighton, but the substitute's half-volley sails just over the bar.
(82’) Van Gaal watches on from the touchline and looks a bit disappointed with the way his side have coasted through the last 15 minutes or so. United have done very little with their possession, while Nugent and Albrighton have certainly helped the threat posed by Leicester going forward.
--- 80’ Substitution R. Falcao is replaced with J. Wilson. ---
--- 80’ Assist Assist by M. Albrighton. ---
--- 80’ Goal! Leicester keep possession following a corner and Albrighton is played through on the right before sending a lovely ball across goal for Wasilewski to head home for his first goal in three years! Jones' marking was very poor there, completely losing track of the Polish centre-back. ---
(80’) THE COMMENTATOR JINX STRIKES AGAIN! LEICESTER CITY PULL ONE BACK!
(78’) STAT ATTACK: Barring a late consolation goal, Leicester City will have been held scoreless in eight of their last 10 Premier League matches against Manchester United.
--- 77’ Substitution Mata comes on for A. Valencia. ---
(76’) Sensing that Leicester are trying to mount one last push for a consolation goal, United have slowed the tempo and are back to passing the ball around near the half-way line. They are showing no urgency to push forward, nor do they need to, as they attempt to see out the final 15 minutes and keep the clean sheet.
(74’) Following a United corner, Leicester muster up a threatening looking counter attack. They are not nearly decisive enough in possession, however, and as the attack slows it gives the hosts a chance to get back and sniff out the chance.
(72’) It is all too comfortable for United when they are in possession. While it has not been the most difficult task for them, they are doing a wonderful job of passing it around in midfield and playing keep-away from their opponents. The Foxes are showing a bit more urgenc now, but it is far too late for that.
(70’) Important touch from Daley Blind! The Dutchman reads the game so well and provides more great defensive cover here as Nugent again gets the better of Jones on the left. The striker tries to thread a ball through for Albrighton, but the ex-Ajax man tracks back and gets a foot out to direct the ball safely into the path of De Gea.
--- 68’ Substitution P. McNair enters play, replacing R. van Persie. ---
(68’) INCREDIBLE REACTIONS! United put themselves under pressure at the back and Nugent gets by Jones near the byline. The substitute tries to knock the ball past De Gea and run onto it for an easy tap in, but the keeper rushes off his line and sticks a strong hand out to prevent the ball from getting past him. Great goalkeeping from the United shot-stopper.
(66’) STAT ATTACK: Leicester had a chance to extend their unbeaten run on their travels in the Premier League to three games by avoiding defeat today, for the first time since December to January of 2003/04.
(64’) The substitutions seems to have brought a bit of life into the Leicester side, but it may be too little, too late. They win another free kick on the left, this one from over 40 yards out, however, and Cambiasso's delivery is easily collected by De Gea.
--- 62’ Substitution D. Nugent comes on for L. Ulloa. ---
--- 62’ Substitution M. Albrighton enters the game and replaces A. Kramarić. ---
(62’) Penalty claims turned aside! There was no real case for Ulloa there, who needed to stay on his feet after a wonderful run forward and first touch to take him behind the defence. He lacks the pace to get through on goal, instead trying to cut around Jones before falling to ground in search of a penalty.  That will be the striker's last contribution as Nigel Pearson utilizes his last two substitutions.
(60’) Possession is being dominated by United, who continue to dictate play in midfield. Leicester look discouraged as ever, likely accepting their fate. I cannot understand their lack of urgency, however, as they continue to resist pressuring the ball, which has made life incredibly easy on the Red Devils.
(58’) NEARLY A FOURTH! Rooney is played in behind the defence, but passes up a shot to try and set up Falcao for a tap in. His pass across the area is a bit too heavy, forcing the striker wide, and the chance fizzles out without a shot at goal.
(56’) United are the ones who look likelier to score again, bringing plenty of width to their play. They have lacked a good cross, however, which has been a theme of the match for the hosts from open play, with Schwarzer having a relatively easy task to come out and collect.
(54’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United had won nine consecutive Premier League matches against Leicester City before their 5-3 defeat at the King Power Stadium earlier this season. They had outscored the Foxes 23-3 over that span.
(52’) Jones concedes a free kick from 30 yards out to the left of goal with a foul on Schlupp. The chance is not taken by the Foxes, however, as Cambiasso's delivery is cleared by the first defender. The visitors keep possession, but the attack fizzles out at Kramaric's acrobatic volley sails over the bar.
(50’) The second half has started awfully slow and we can expect much more of this throughout the second half. United are comfortably in front and likely will not feel the need to push the pace too much, while making sure to smother Leicester and prevent them from finding a way back into the game.
(48’) The change made by Nigel Pearson at the break certainly is not a positive one, as the lively James Vardy is replaced by Esteban Cambiasso, with the visitors hoping to shore up their side in midfield and prevent this defecit from growing any bigger.
--- 46’ Substitution J. Vardy is done for the day. E. Cambiasso is his replacement. ---
(46’) Leicester City get the second half underway with a mountain to climb at Old Trafford.
HALF TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 3-0 LEICESTER CITY. It is a rather surprising scoreline, with the hosts scoring on each of their three chances. They had created very little for the most part in the opening 45 minutes, but as is the sign of any good team, they took their chances well and look well on their way to picking up all three points.
(45’) KRAMARIC! Wonderful play by the Croatian inside the area, but some desperation defending from Shaw forces Leicester to settle for a corner which comes to nothing as the first half reaches its end.
(45’) There will be just one minute of stoppage time...
--- 44’ Goal! It will go down as an own goal via a corner kick. Rooney's delivery is flicked on smartly by Blind at the near post, and Morgan cannot react quick enough as a scrambled header wind up in the back of his net. ---
(43’) THREE FIRST HALF GOALS FOR UNITED AND THIS ONE IS OVER!
(41’) Close to a third! Wonderful breakout play from United who catch Leicester lacking in numbers at the back. Di Maria and Falcao try and play a give-and-go, but the Argentine's return pass runs a bit far, forcing the Colombian to retreat. He picks out Rooney at the top of the area, who sees his cross headed behind for a corner.
(39’) STAT ATTACK: Leicester have just 17 points from 22 matches. The lowest total they have accrued in the Premier League at this stage of a season in which they avoided relegation was 26 in 1996-97.
(37’) Leicester are not closing down on the ball nearly quick enough and are making it far to straightforward for United in possession. The visitors have had a hard time creating turnovers in midfield, instead waiting for the hosts to make a mistake or see one of their attacks go out for a goal kick. They are seriously lacking urgency, which will make it near impossible for them to get back into the game.
(35’) United have slowed the tempo, though it was hardly very fast-paced to begin with. The hosts pass the ball around at the back and it appears already like they are content with keeping possession and seeing this through to half-time.
--- 34’ Yellow card D. Drinkwater gets yellow. ---
(33’) There is still plenty of game left, and although it seems like a near insurmountable deficit for Leicester, it is so vital that they do not get discouraged and let this game get out of hand. They have plenty of quality going forward and will draw some confidence from the five goals they put past the Red Devils in their reverse fixture, though it will be much more difficult at Old Trafford.
--- 32’ Goal! Van Persie picks up the ball just inside his own half and does so well to beat a defender before playing Di Maria behind the defence. The Argentine sees his shot saved, but Falcao shows great determination to follow up and bundle it over the line. ---
(31’) UNITED DOUBLE THEIR LEAD IN THE SPAN OF JUST A FEW MINUTES!
(29’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United's last four Premier League matches have been tied at half-time, three of which ended 0-0 after 45 minutes.
--- 27’ Assist D. Blind provided the assist. ---
--- 27’ Goal! It's the newest Leicester signing, Andrej Kramaric, who gives the ball away in his own end to Daley Blind. The ex-Ajax man takes a few strides forward and sends an exceptional chipped-pass over the top for Van Persie, who smashes it back across goal and into the bottom corner with a brilliantly taken first-time volley. ---
(27’) THAT IS SENSATIONAL! OUT OF NOTHING, UNITED HAVE THE LEAD!
(24’) This has been a rather cagey first half as we still await the first clear-cut scoring chance. The pressure and momentum United had been building is gone now as Leicester make it difficult for them to break into the final third.
(22’) Phil Jones is forced off the pitch temporarily as he has a problem with his boots, and Leicester try and capitalize on their numerical advantage. Schlupp latches onto the end of a pass and charges into the area, but Valencia does just enough to put pressure on the winger who sends his shot high and wide.
(20’) The pressure is starting to build on the Leicester goal as Manchester United press much more convincingly in possession. They string a number of passes together in and around the area, before Shaw charges into the area. His cross is headed clear by Wasilewski and Di Maria's follow-up shot is sent over the bar.
(18’) The Red Devils create the first half-chance of the match as Van Persie plays Falcao through on goal, but the striker cannot sort his footing as he's forced to retreat. A cross eventually comes in and Januzaj crashes into the back of Simpson, conceding a free kick.
(16’) STAT ATTACK: Manchester United have conceded just twice in their last six matches across all competitions. Their games have featured just seven goals total between them and their opponents over that span.
(14’) That's quite a letdown! After much anticipation, Di Maria convinces Rooney to let him take the free kick, but winds up lashing his shot straight into the wall before Leicester clear the threat.
(13’) Andy King commits a soft foul and United have a chance here with the ensuing set piece from 30 yards out. There appeared to be minimal contact made, but the way he lunged into the challenge forced Martin Atkinson into action.
(11’) Schlupp puts his side under unnecessary pressure, winning a foot race with Di Maria to track down a ball played over the top following a Leicester corner, and tries to usher the ball behind for a goal kick. The Argentine never gives up chase, keeping the ball in play, much to the delight of the Old Trafford supporters. His eventual cross is poor, however, as the chance fizzles out.
(9’) There is very little coming of possession from either side as we approach the 10-minute mark. United have yet to really threaten the Leicester back line, while the Foxes hardly look eager to get forward and attack just yet.
(7’) Danny Drinkwater shows he will not be intimidated early on, staying stride for stride with Di Maria, who was looking to make a run on the left. The Leicester midfielder gives him a strong nudge with his shoulder, toppling over the ex-Real Madrid man and winning back possession for his side.
(5’) With goals having been hard to come by for United, they appear to be wasting no time trying to commit men forward and end their drought here today. Daley Blind is one of the few staying in a deeper role, and he will have such a huge responsibility in defence, providing cover for the back line while taking up space and making it difficult on Leicester to attack quickly via the counter.
(3’) Wayne Rooney looks to be in a more central role, at least in the early stages, as the hosts control possession. Leicester have to be wary of their movement off the ball, with Van Persie looking up for the occasion, trying twice to latch on to long balls played over the top.
(1’) The hosts kick-off and we are underway on a beautiful, sunny day at Old Trafford. Manchester United in red, moving left to right, Leicester in blue. Here we go!
Matty James misses out on the match as a result of a suspension, while Riyad Mahrez remains on international duty at the Africa Cup of Nations. Matthew Upson could make his Foxes debut as a substitute, having finally recovered from a foot injury picked up in the pre-season. Nigel Pearson has made just one change to his team following their victory over Tottenham in the FA Cup, with Marcin Wasilewski replacing Liam Moore at the back.
Michael Carrick is set to miss a month with a ruptured muscle, while Ashley Young still requires more time to recover from a hamstring injury. As a result, manager Louis van Gaal makes three changes to his side following their FA Cup tie with Cambridge United. Robin van Persie starts up top in place of James Wilson, while Wayne Rooney and Luke Shaw replace Michael Carrick and Marouane Fellaini respectively. It appears as though Rooney is starting on the right of the midfield diamond, with Angel di Maria in behind the two strikers. This certainly appears to be an XI with plenty of goals in it, but Daley Blind will have to shoulder the defensive load in midfield as a result.
LEICESTER CITY SUBS: Konchesky, Upson, Hammond, Albrighton, Hamer, Cambiasso, Nugent.
MANCHESTER UNITED SUBS: Mata, Smalling, Herrera, Fellaini, Valdes, McNair, Wilson.
LEICESTER CITY (4-4-2): Schwarzer; Simpson, Wasilewski, Morgan, De Laet; Vardy, Drinkwater, King, Schlupp; Ulloa, Kramaric.
MANCHESTER UNITED (4-4-2): De Gea; Valencia, Jones, Rojo, Shaw; Blind, Rooney, Januzaj, di Maria; van Persie, Falcao.
