Optimism was wearing thin in the Leicester City camp at the start of 2015, and while they remain at the bottom of the table, their hopes of survival suddenly appear a little less dim. With seven points from their last four league matches, the Foxes are now just three points from safety. It will require all hands on deck for Nigel Pearson's side to avoid the drop, but all you can ask for is a chance – and they’ve given themselves that at least, for now.
Manchester United got a much needed win against QPR in their last Premier League match, but their grip on a top four spot is quickly slipping away from them. There is just one point separating the Red Devils from Arsenal, with Tottenham lurking close by as well. It is very important for Louis van Gaal’s side to claim all three points today, with the always difficult trip to Upton Park looming.
Good day Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to Old Trafford. Manchester United take to the Theatre of Dreams today in the hopes of keeping their spot in the top four when they take on bottom of the table Leicester City! I am Alex Moretto and I will be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens.

Meanwhile, QPR have just recorded their eleventh straight away loss in the Premier League and still have not won a single point on the road. Relegation is becoming a real concern; despite their efforts today, especially in the second half, they continue to have nothing to show for it. Thank you for joining us here!
THAT'S THE MATCH! Walters is the difference today as Mark Hughes' men show there can be victory without Bojan and continue their march into the top half of the table. It's been a rather solid performance for them, despite a dip in the second half.
--- 90’ +2 Goal! GOOOOOOALLL WALTERS! THE FORWARD COMPLETES HIS HAT-TRICK AND SEALS THE WIN FOR STOKE! He runs into the box to decisively power home the ball after it was losely pinging around following a failed clearance! It's a perfect hat-trick today, with a right-footed goal, left-footed goal, and a header! ---
(90’) NEARLY FROM ZAMORA! Barton's corner is played into the back post and somehow misses Zamora's head, who had risen higher than everyone else but failed to make contact! What a chance for the visitors!
(89’) The visitors break down the midfield at any rate, twice through Isla, and it's taking some desperate defending in the box to keep the shots coming, with Muniesa in particular heading away several crosses, with the most important of those coming off a diving defensive action with Zamora lurking just behind!
(88’) Just two minutes plus stoppages remain here, and Stoke remain in the lead after this second half has failed to produce a goal for either side. QPR continue to press incessantly, looking for the equalizer, but Stoke are doing better now to clog the midfield and keep the visitors back.
(86’) Fer whips the ball on goal, and it swerves towards the right post, but Begovic gets down low and decisively to powerfully parry the ball out for a corner! A very, very solid save from the Stoke keeper.
--- 85’ Yellow card Crouch nearly pulls off a fantastic solo move as he races down the flank and tries to work his way down the goal-line but prods the ball over. Seconds later, Walters pushes over Hoilett and enters the book for his trouble, giving QPR yet another free-kick that they can play into Stoke's box! ---
(84’) And it's very, very poor from Wilson, who's had a very quiet game today and hoofs a cross only into the arms of Green. The fans voice their displeasure at the side losing the ball so easily when possession has been rare in the last spell of the game.
(83’) Zamora leads a supber counter, cutting inside from the flank and trying to make something happen with Vargas, but the latter player loses the ball and Stoke collect and try to calm down play.
(82’) It's floated in well by Vargas who finds the head of Dunne but the defender's awkward header fizzles past the far post. QPR are knocking on the verge of their first away point in the league this season but simply cannot finish their chances!
(81’) There's been a lot of joy down the left flank for QPR, though they work it into the centre via Barton and Hoilett; the former is fouled by Adam, who just bundled into the player, and QPR have yet another free-kick just outside of Stoke's box, though this time it's to the right.
(80’) Aye, there's been a nasty clash of heads and Austin is forced off the pitch of his own accord as he's bleeding from around his temple. For the time being, the visitors are down a man until the medical team can stop the flow.
(79’) That effort has really energized the visitors who are looking more and more dangerous as time ticks away. Zamora tries twice in rapid succession to complete a cross in the box but fails, and Dunne does very well to slide and win the ball off of Crouch as Stoke countered dangerously!
(77’) BARTON HITS THE UPRIGHT! A matter of centimetres has kept Stoke in the lead, with Barton's effort truly fantastic, beating Begovic, and smashing the frame of the goal before bouncing away!
(76’) QPR have a free-kick just outside of Stoke's box! Muniesa looks like he clipped the front of Barton's boot as he went to shoot the ball, though the home side is arguing there was very minimal contact and the former Newcastle man has made too much of the challenge. Nevertheless, the call stands!
--- 75’ Substitution A left-back substitution from Redknapp, taking out Hill for Yun. A Stoke throw-in bobbles around the midfield before QPR settle and play it to the substitute, whose first pass is short and successful to keep possession with his side. ---
--- 72’ Substitution N'Zonzi finds Whelan who plays it around to Ireland on the other end of the box, who sends a fantastic cross in towards Crouch that the tall man just can't redirect on target! It's Ireland's final involvement as he comes off for Adam after a very, very good performance today! ---
(71’) Barton whips in a corner after winning it himself, after his shot was deflected out of the box, but it's a poor effort that's easily cleared. Walters puts Green under immense pressure on the counter and forces the goalkeeper to pass it out of bounds.
(70’) Hoilett comes on for Kranjcar, who has faded in this match despite a bright and lively start. Moses once again is working his magic down the left, sending in a smart ball for Ireland who tries to take it down but fails to. Seconds later, the former Manchester City man thinks he's clear through in the box but he's well offside and the lineman duly flags him.
--- 68’ Substitution N. Kranjčar is done for the day. J. Hoilett is his replacement. ---
--- 68’ Yellow card Barton enters the book now, becoming the third player to do so today, after running through the back of Ireland after Austin lost his side the ball with a poor pass directly out of bounds. ---
(67’) Stoke work the ball forward well and N'Zonzi decides to try an effort at goal from about 20 yards out, in a central position, though it's a tame effort truly and fails to trouble Green.
(66’) Zamora does all he can to try and keep Wollscheid's pass from going out as nearly his whole side pressed forward on the counter but he's unable to do so. Walters goes down soon after and the ball is now back in the hands of the home side.
(64’) Moses is showing the defensive side of his game as he hounds Isla deep in Stoke's half to prevent the former Juventus man from whipping a cross into the box. His tenacity pays off as the ball is deflected out and soon Stoke are able to go forward with possession.
--- 63’ Substitution Arnautovic trying to turn provider there, prodding the ball with the outside of his right boot to try and send a pass through for Walters. It's his last touch of the game in what's been a very lively affair for him as Crouch comes on in his place. ---
(61’) QPR are sustaining pressure well now and not allowing Stoke the kind of time and freedom they had in the first half. This is a markedly improved performance but without another goal to show for it as Stoke continue to try and reassert their dominance.
(60’) Austin tries a cheeky touch to work his way around the Stoke defence but it's a little too cheeky and costs his side possession. Moses counters and loops a cross into QPR's box that Green rises high to collect; the game is nearly end-to-end at this point as Zamora races onto Barton's solid through pass but the ball is deflected off his knee from Wollscheid's challenge in the box.
--- 58’ Yellow card Moses is booked for diving after going down far too easily, not really fooling anyone there. He seemed to have lost the ball and without much else to do, dramatically falls over and is duly booked. ---
(56’) OH MY AND WHAT A SAVE FROM BEGOVIC! Vargas reacts superbly to contort his body into an overhead kick after Fer's free-kick just outside of Stoke's box is deflected into his path. Luckily for Stoke, it goes very close to Begovic who can parry it away!
(55’) Walters is in some pain as he stood too close to Green, who was taking a drop-kick clearance, and smashed the ball into the back of the forward's head. He looks alright to play on though!
(54’) Isla does all he can to spread a pass before Moses can race onto it, and it sparks a QPR counter that ends when Muniesa races to clear a ball in the box that was just about to reach Fer.
(53’) OOHHHHH NEARLY SOMETHING THERE! Bardsley's effort goes over the wall and nearly dips into the net but just lands on the roof of the goal! Kranjcar races down the other end and tries his own shot but it, too, is just too high to really trouble Begovic.
(51’) These opening minutes have been very even for both sides, but Fer presents Stoke with another free-kick after raising his boot far too high trying to win the ball and hitting Bardsley in the head. There's no malicious intent in it, but Fer might consider himself lucky to not be booked.
(50’) And it falls back to Vargas after a fantastic pass from Fer finds him running towards the edge of the Stoke box; the wide player tries to take a shot quickly and sends a very disappointing effort far too high!
(49’) That's absolutely fantastic from Moses, who beats Barton and Isla on the left flank and wins a very deep throw-in. Vargas, who's had a quiet game, helps to clear, and QPR roam on the counter.
(48’) Barton commits a foul on Bardsley for a free-kick to Stoke, which Moses plays well into QPR's box and Dunne heads out for Isla to clear!
(47’) Stoke surge forward in familiar fashion, with Arnautovic racing down his flank, taking on his man, and then prodding the ball a bit too far as he lost his step for a goal-kick to the visitors.
--- 46’ Substitution K. Henry is done for the day. B. Zamora is his replacement. ---
(46’) The second half kicks off with Zamora coming on for the visitors in place of Henry, who of course was at fault for Stoke's opening goal. The home side kick off, lose the ball quickly, and then Whelan fouls Fer trying to win it back. The ensuing free-kick is played into the box, cleared, and Barton's shot from outside the box goes nowhere near the net.
Stoke, meanwhile, have been effervescent at times and should be ahead by more, but poor finishing and one mistake at the back have been costly. Nevertheless, they're still in the lead and just need to keep doing what they've been in order to secure the win today.
The scoreline flatters the visitors, who have truly been quite dire, with a defence that simply cannot contain Arnautovic, Moses and Walters, and who are lucky to only be one goal down. Harry Redknapp will want to use that gap to remind his side they can really only be better and they need just one more goal to turn this around.
(45’) Ohhhh and Stoke doing everything there except for scoring! Arnautovic is in the box, he flicks it down to Walters, who lays it off for Moses, whose shot is blocked! It's the last meaningful play of the half as the whistle is blown seconds later, as Stoke head into the locker rooms ahead 2-1.
(45’) Moses and Walters play a fantastic give-and-go for the former to get the ball on the edge of the area, run onto the pass, and fire an excellent shot that goes just over the bar! Two more minutes of injury time here and the entertainment keeps on coming!
(44’) Muniesa's first involvement is to send a ball over the top of the defence for Arnautovic but the pass is too heavy and rolls out of play for a Green goal-kick.
(43’) A very ambitious cross into Stoke's box from Dunne, who sends a looping ball centrally into the arms of Begovic. Seconds later, Austin and Begovic are getting very heated in the box as Wollscheid has been knocked over by QPR's number nine, though the centre-back has certainly made a meal of what was truly minimal and routine contact from the striker.
--- 42’ Substitution Awful scenes on the pitch as Shawcross is down again. He tried to play on but takes off his armband, throws it to his teammates, and then gingerly walks off. Muneisa comes on in his place. ---
(40’) And indeed Shawcross comes back onto the pitch as play continues. Stoke are pouring forward in search of another goal but Green jumps to collect an errant high pass and Ireland is offside soon after.
(39’) Stoke's captain is being evaluated on the pitch and is able to stand up. He walks off and Muniesa is warming up on the sidelines but it looks as though he'll be able to continue.
(37’) That QPR goal was a well-worked play, starting with a throw-in deep in Stoke's half that was sent back to the defence before being passed down the middle. The home side have more to worry about now as well, with Shawcross down and looking like he's in some pain.
--- 36’ Goal! QPR WITH AN ALMOST IMMEDIATE ANSWER! KRANJCAR PULLS ONE BACK! It's calamitous defending from Stoke in their own box as Barton slots it to Austin, who's shot is deflected off of the foot of Bardsley and falls kindly to the number 19, who's all alone and makes no mistake from such a close range! 2-1 AND GAME ON! ---
--- 34’ Assist S. Ireland gave the assist. ---
--- 34’ Goal! WALTERS DOUBLES STOKE'S LEAD! IT'S HIS SECOND OF THE MATCH! And Stoke showing a different side today as they ripped apart QPR's defence twice there - once to set Ireland free down the left, and then from Ireland himself who squared it perfectly to the onrushing Walters to fire past Green and into the far post! QPR are in serious, serious trouble now! ---
(33’) Arnautovic soon has yet another chance just moments after his last shot, racing into the box and ripping a shot that sails over the bar. Stoke continue to knock on the door of a second goal but without better shooting, their fantastic build-up play is resulting only in poor efforts.
(32’) Wollscheid's pass towards Walters is intercepted by Hill but that doesn't stem the tide of Stoke's attack as Moses once again is able to beat his man and get into the box, crossing for Arnautovic to take down and fire but his shot hits the body of the nearest defender!
(31’) Barton shows some flair to keep Fer's pass with two Stoke players surrounding him, but the visitors look very shorn of confidence as the ball is played to Dunne who struggles to control it and plays it out for a deep Stoke throw-in.
(29’) Dunne is forced to run back towards Green and play a quick pass to him for the keeper to clear before Walters can intercept. QPR think they have an opportunity on the other end but Barton's committed a foul in the buildup and the whistle is blown for a Stoke free-kick.
(28’) Moses plays a looping ball deep in the box that Hill heads out for yet another corner, which is worked out of the box for Ireland to smash onto net but his shot goes wide of the far post! This is truly exciting build-up play from the home side who look like a second goal is just a matter of time, now!
(27’) After a couple of minutes where neither side can seem to hold the ball, Arnautovic is once against set free down the left flank due to a fantastic pass - this time, a dinked ball over the top from Ireland. The wide man wins another corner for the home side, with the fans really being heard now.
(25’) OH AND NEARLY ANOTHER! Moses himself takes the free-kick and it's a truly inviting one, looking destined for the top corner before it bends just a moment too soon and fizzes away!
--- 24’ Yellow card Isla with a very poor challenge on Moses, sliding into the back of the player and missing the ball entirely just outside of QPR's box, and he's duly booked. ---
(23’) Stoke with a gorgeous play to nearly double their lead! N'Zonzi plays a fantastic through ball down the flank to Arnautovic, who's all by himself, races to the byline, and tries to cross it in for Walters, but Dunne rises high to get his head on it first!
--- 21’ Assist S. Ireland provided the assist. ---
--- 21’ Goal! GOALLLL WALTERS! STOKE ARE IN THE LEAD!!! And it's a howler from Henry, an absolute gift! Henry lets the ball run past him after failing to control it, just outside of his own box; Ireland steals possession and backheels it to Walters, who races into the box and confidently slots it into the far post! 1-0 to Stoke! ---
(20’) Bardsley plays a throw-in short to Whelan, who passes it back for his teammates to work around to the other side before quickly slotting it towards Walters, who was offside. Free-kick for QPR which Green is coming out of his box to take.
(18’) An excellent, driving run from Moses takes him deep into enemy territory and forces Fer to knock the ball out for a corner. He takes the corner himself, delivering it to the near post for Kranjcar to head clear.
(16’) Arnautovic finds himself up against Hill on the edge of the box after a fantastic pass from Wollscheid found the winger in some space. He confidently tries to dribble to the byline but his touch is poor and the ball drifts over the line!
(15’) The visitors now are trying to dictate the game on calmer terms, playing it around the back before seeing Begovic on the edge of his box to collect a stray forward pass sent the way of Austin.
(13’) The delivery is similarly disappointing, with Moses failing to beat the first man as his effort is cleared out of the box. QPR soon collect and Dunne launches it up towards Austin, but N'Zonzi's body gets in the way to give a throw-in to the visitors by the halfway line.
(12’) A fantastic pass from the spinning and falling Arnautovic to find Bardsley racing down the left flank. It's Kranjcar who soon fouls him, with the number 19 very involved in this opening spell, and now Stoke have a free-kick in a nearly identical manner as QPR had just a minute ago.
(11’) Hill and Arnautovic tangle arms on the side, just after the former sent in a solid cross that was cleared right back to him. It's a free-kick now to the visitors, who are going to send it directly into the box... but Kranjcar loops it far too high and it goes out of play on the other side of the goal!
(9’) Stoke are getting the ball forward well now in good areas, just outside of QPR's box, but are having trouble sending the proper pass in to penetrate the backline. Green is seeing more of the ball as well but mostly just in the form of goal-kicks.
(8’) Kranjcar waltzes forward, trying to break through Stoke's backline, but shows too much of the ball to his adversaries. Dunne is called into a smart clearance on the other side of the pitch that Moses slots forward for Isla to shepard out ahead of Ireland.
(6’) The home side now build down their left flank, flowing back and forth before Moses can't get on the end of a pass. QPR's throw-in is rendered useless almost immediately as Stoke collect and the midfield now is quickly becoming difficult for both sides to get past as Kranjcar shows Ireland with a well-timed sliding tackle.
(5’) Fer takes a QPR free-kick quickly, to the side's own detriment, as Stoke race to collect possession and race forward. In these opening moments the game has been frantic, with many pauses for goal-kicks and to allow the ball to come back in from out of play.
(3’) Dunne trundles over Walters, giving Stoke a free-kick from about halfway into QPR territory. Arnautovic decides to play a zippy ball, somewhere between a shot and a cross, right into the area, and it fizzes wide of teammates and the near post. A puzzling effort.
(1’) And we have kick-off! The visitors take a very early, very bold pass forward that goes right out of bounds, and soon Green has possession as the home men try something similar. An ambitious opening, if not slightly sloppy, form both sides.
Moses tries to launch a counter-attack but is determined to have fouled Dunne after the defender hooked the ball away from him. No card is given - luckily for the winger - and QPR now have a free-kick in their own half.
The teams are lining up in the tunnels about to come onto the pitch for the pre-match ceremonies! We're just three minutes away from kick-off now!
QPR's biggest problem right now might just be scoring goals. Not only have they notched just three in their last five league matches, but they have just five away from home all season! They seem to have found some consistency recently however, scoring once in each of their last three against Everton, Arsenal, Burnley.
Devastating as the loss and injury are for Stoke, QPR will be hoping to use the opportunity to break their run of 10 away matches without a single point so far this season. They haven't won at home since December 20th and have taken just two points from their last five matches in all competitions.
Even with Bojan, however, Stoke's home form has been indifferent at best. They've won four, lost four, and drawn twice at the Britannia this season, notching just twelve goals in the process. Bojan however has been a big part of Stoke's successes: he scored in four of the five matches they've won in the Premier League.
Of course, the biggest news in terms of this match is that it'll be Stoke's first without Bojan Krkic, who suffered a season-ending cruciate ligament injury during their last match in the F.A. Cup. It comes as a mighty blow to the home side who saw the former Barcelona man truly growing in confidence and stature throughout the season.
QPR (4-5-1): Green; Hill, Dunne, Onuoha, Isla; Fer, Henry, Kranjcar, Barton, Vargas; Austin.
Stoke (4-2-3-1): Begovic; Wilson, Wollscheid, Shawcross, Bardsley; N'Zonzi, Whelan; Moses, Ireland, Arnautovic; Walters.
Hello and welcome to our live match coverage of Stoke vs QPR! It's 11th against 19th in round 23 of the Premier League today for two teams in very different form. Full time at Stadium of Light. Sunderland secure a massive win against a relegation rival as they secure a relatively comfortable 2-0 victory against Burnley. Both goals came in the first half and came from the new striking duo of Connor Wickham and Jermain Defoe. Burnley were spirited at times but never really looked like mounting a comeback after the break. I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!

--- 90’ +3 Yellow card C. Pantilimon goes into the referee's book. ---
(90’) Three minutes of added time here and it doesn't look like we are going to see any sign of a miracle comeback from Burnley. They have looked well-beaten for much of this second period.
--- 89’ Yellow card S. Larsson gets yellow. ---
(88’) Arfield wins the ball back on the edge of his own box and looks to be the catalyst for a Burnley counterattack. In the end Larsson takes one for the team and commits the foul to stop the attack, earning a yellow card in the process.
--- 86’ Substitution A. Johnson is done for the day. R. Álvarez is his replacement. ---

(84’) A high ball is played up top and Vokes initially takes down with a nice touch before turning towards goal. The substitute lets himself down with is next touch though which allows O'Shea to come and make the interception.
(82’) Decent opportunity for Burnley! Wallace stands over a corner kick and swings a superb cross to the front post for Mee, who glances a lovely header towards the back post, but it just evaded the corner by a yard! Simple enough move, and it unluckily didn't come off!
(80’) Sunderland just need to keep concentrated as they have been doing for the remaining 10 minutes here. Tough to see where Burnley are going to muster a threat from though, as Jutkiewicz and Vokes haven't offered much since coming on. The latter was only just introduced a few minutes ago though so could still make a positive impact.
(78’) Burnley are quickly running out of time to salvage something from this Premier League clash. Sadly for them they just have not created a lot in the final third, and Sunderland have looked far too comfortable in this second period.
--- 76’ Substitution S. Vokes comes on for A. Barnes. ---
--- 76’ Substitution D. Graham enters the game and replaces C. Wickham. ---
(76’) A flurry of changes here! Wickham and Defoe are both coming off for Sunderland and they will be replaced by Danny Graham and former Burnley striker, Steven Fletcher. --- 75’ Substitution S. Fletcher enters play, replacing J. Defoe. ---
(74’) Sunderland get the opportunity to get a decent cross into the box here as Larsson stands over a free kick just to the left of the box. In the end the Swede opts to go for goal and it is a decent attempt, but never really poses a threat to Heaton. Bit of a waste really.
(72’) Keane bursts out of defence and darts forward before undoing all his good work with a poor pass to Barnes that goes out of play. However, the Burnley defenders makes up for his mistake by getting back a few moments later to dispossess Wickham, who was ominously driving forward.
(70’) Again van Aanholt opens up his stride on the left flank and latches on to a high ball to hit a first time volleyed cross into the box. Shackell's clearing header only goes as far as Defoe, but the former Toronto FC striker can't sort his feet out in time to get the shot away, which allows the Burnley defender to clear at the second attempt.
--- 69’ Yellow card A. Johnson is yellow-carded. ---
(68’) Jones swings a lovely diagonal out wide to Mee and the left-back powers forward. Jutkiewicz then picks out the former Manchester United man, who attempts to tee himself up for a volley, but it doesn't come off and Gomez clears.
(66’) Just over from Wickham. The Englishman shows good strength on the ball on the edge of the box and plays out wide to van Aanholt. He then receives the return pass and looks to divert a powerful strike towards the top corner, but the attempt goes over by a few yards.
(64’) Van Aanholt once again provides some width down the left-hand side and gets into a great position to the left of the box. He teases a brilliant cross into the box but none of his team-mates can make up the ground to convert it into a goal!
(62’) The Burnley supporters don't seem too pleased with their manager's decision to withdraw Ings. Judgement will remain until the final result, as if Burnley get at least a draw then it will look like a masterstroke. If not, he'll no doubt come in for some criticism.
--- 61’ Substitution L. Jutkiewicz enters play, replacing D. Ings. ---
--- 61’ Substitution G. Boyd is done for the day. R. Wallace is his replacement. ---
(61’) Sean Dyche makes his first two changes of the match, and it is a bit of an eyebrow raiser from the Burnley boss. His top goalscorer of the season, Ings, is coming off along with Boyd. Coming on are Ross Wallace and Lukas Jutkiewicz. Let's see if this gamble pays off for the visitors!
(59’) What is Arfield doing?! Ings does brilliantly to latch on to a pass down the wing and flick the ball into the path of his team-mate, who smashes a shot/cross miles over the bar with Barnes begging for the ball in the penalty area! Wasteful!
(57’) Much better from the Clarets in the last few minutes or so. Ings pops up inside the box to receive the ball to feet and tees up Barnes on the edge of the box, who looks to steer a strike into the bottom left corner. The attempt takes a deflection on its way through and Burnley get the corner.
(55’) Burnley mount an attack down the left wing and Mee eventually stands a decent cross into the box. Barnes fancies his chances with a header and rises high in an attempt to make a connection, but in the end the attempt goes harmlessly into the arms of Pantilimon.
(53’) Burnley need to get Ings into the game if they are going to get anything out of this. I mentioned before that this match could be decided by either he or Defoe, and it is the latter who has impressed so far. Ings hasn't received a lot of service to be fair though.
(51’) What a waste from Marney. The Burnley midfielder collects the ball from a quick free kick and makes a few strides forward before looking to try his luck with an attempt at goal from range. Unfortunately for him it goes near enough into row Z.
(49’) Boyd drifts inside from the left wing and receives the ball to feet before turning and darting towards goal. Looks a promising attack for Burnley but it fizzles out as Larsson commits the foul and the visitors get the free kick in a useful position.
(47’) CHANCE FOR DEFOE! Some lovely work from Johnson eventually sees van Aanholt collect possession in a dangerous area inside the box. He picks out Defoe with a cutback but Sunderland's new signing can't get enough purchase on the strike to grab his second goal!
(46’) We are back under way in this Premier League clash!
Half time at the Stadium of Light. Gus Poyet demanded a response from his squad due to their recent bad form and he has certainly got that in this opening 45 minutes. Wickham and Defoe both on the scoresheet and looking very dangerous in and around the penalty area. Burnley are notorious for not giving up though, so concentration still required in the second half from the hosts!
(44’) Sunderland are just professionally seeing out the remainder of this first half as they look to avoid any trouble at the back before the break. Two minutes of added time for Burnley to grab a goal and make Dyche's half time team talk a lot easier.
(42’) Burnley have just lacked some creativity in the final third in this first half. Too many times the wingers or full backs have received possession in good areas but opted to send an aimless cross into the box, with them being blocked more often than not.
(40’) There has been a very interesting battle developing in and around the Burnley penalty area between Wickham and Shackell. The Sunderland man probably has the better of the defender so far, as quite a lot of the home side's play has went through him in some fashion.
(38’) The visitors are just aiming to calm themselves down a bit with a period of possession and short stabbed passes. They have been under the cosh for most of this first half so they are taking this opportunity to regroup and make Sunderland do the running. Boyd attempts to get down the left wing but eventually has to revert back to Mee.
(36’) Burnley are sinking without a trace here. In their last Premier League match they surrendered a two-goal lead against Crystal Palace, and this time they are going to have to pull off a similar comeback if they are going to get anything out of this.
--- 34’ Assist P. van Aanholt provided the assist. ---
--- 34’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAAAAAALLLLLLL FOR SUNDERLAND! THE HOSTS DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! Jordi Gomez picks out a lovely pass down the left channel for van Aanholt, who drives forward before picking out Defoe for a signature close range finish! That's what he was brought in for! Two-nil! ---
(32’) Johnson receives the ball to feet 30 yards out and looks to tempt Jones into diving in with a couple of neat stepovers. He eventually gets the shot away but it is well-blocked on the edge of the box. Period of pressure from the hosts at the moment!
(30’) After that few minutes of quality from Sunderland the tempo of the game has just dropped slightly. It is a bit of a midfield battle at the moment with neither side enjoying a period of sustained possession.
(28’) Jordi Gomez receives the ball to feet in the No.10 role but just ponders in possession a little too long which allows Jones to pounce and reclaim possession for Burnley. Bridcutt ends up having to commit the foul to stop the counterattack of the visitors.
(26’) Johnson stands over a free kick deep in the opposition half and then swings the set-piece deep to the far post. Defoe retreats well to recycle the ball back into the danger area, but the former Tottenham striker is flagged as offside. Just as well for Burnley, as they were on the ropes there.
(24’) The goalscorer, Wickham, looks to turn provided this time as he pops up on the right flank to flash a teasing cross into the box, but Shackell is well-positioned to clear out of the danger area. Burnley just having to weather a bit of a Sunderland storm at the minute!
(22’) Before the match we probably would have been forgiven for thinking this would be a rather cagey affair, but both sides are showing attacking ambition that hasn't always been present at the Stadium of Light this season. Definitely more goals in this!
--- 20’ Assist A. Réveillère provided the assist. ---
--- 20’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAALLLLLLLLL FOR SUNDERLAND! AND THE OPENING GOAL COMES!! Reveillere bombs down the right-hand side to receive a pass and finds himself in acres of room. The Frenchman picks out Wickham, who bullets a header into the corner! Great goal! ---
(19’) Both sides looking much brighter in the last 10 minutes or so as we look to find the opening goal.
(17’) Barnes should be scoring!!! Jones whips a wicked cross into the box from a free kick and the Burnley striker manages to get on the end of it, but can only glance his headed attempt wide! Where was Pantilimon there? The attempt came from a couple of yards out!
(15’) Both goalkeepers haven't exactly inspired confidence with their commanding of the box from crosses. Both Heaton and Pantilimon have struggled to claim a couple of aerial balls into the box, so that should be something to take advantage of from an attacking point of view.
(13’) A small break in play at the moment as Ings is currently down injured after taking a small blow to the head in an aerial challenge with Bridcutt. There wasn't too much in it though and it looks like the striker just had his bell rung. He's back on his feet now and we can continue.
(11’) Well the Sunderland fans actually see the ball go in the opposition net but unfortunately a one-goal lead doesn't follow. Wickham latches on to a loose ball on the edge of the box and actually smashes a terrific finish home, but the referee brings play back for a foul on a Burnley defender.
(9’) It has been a relatively even opening few minutes or so at the Stadium of Light. Defoe has showed a couple of moments of class on the ball for the home side, but Ings hasn't really had a sniff as of yet for Burnley. Will this match be decided by either one of those predatory strikers?
(7’) Arfield collects the ball down the left and goes on a penetrating run alongside the touchline. The Burnley winger attempts to get the cross in but the retreating Reveillere does brilliantly to get back and claw the ball back for the hosts. Some impressive pace showed by both players there!
(5’) Trippier goes on his first marauding run down the right-hand side and looks to pick out Boyd with a flashed cross into the box. The former Hull man collects but is eventually dispossessed by van Aanholt, who looks to instigate a Sunderland counterattack.
(3’) Already some more positive aspects to Sunderland's play. It appears that Wickham is actually playing in a front two alongside Defoe rather than being deployed deeper or out on the wing. Be interesting to see if that duo can link up effectively today.

Sean Dyche, meanwhile, names the same starting XI for the ninth consecutive Premier League game.

Sunderland's form as a whole has been very poor. Gus Poyet's men have won just one game out of their last 12 in the league, although that solitary victory did come against arch rivals, Newcastle. The Uruguayan boss issued a rallying call to his squad this week and challenged them to claw themselves out of this downturn.
The Black Cats and the Clarets both suffered disappointing defeats in their last Premier League games. Sunderland went down 2-1 against Spurs thanks to a late Christian Eriksen winner and Burnley surrendered a two-goal lead to eventually be defeated by a spirited Crystal Palace side.
Both outfits certainly have creatively capable players in their ranks, but you get the feeling that today's match may simply come down to who wants it more and who works hardest.
To use an old cliché, this is what is known in the footballing world as a relegation six-pointer folks! Sunderland and Burnley currently sit perilously about the dropzone in 16th and 17th place with 20 points each taken from their opening 22 matches. If either side were to claim the win and avoid going down, they may indeed look back at today as a vital moment in their survival. Plenty of hard work in store before that can happen, though!

(81’) Chelsea are still pressing forwards for a sixth. They probe and work swift passing combinations, before Hazard's poor ball falls short of Ivanovic. Emnes carries it forwards but Swansea are forced to go backwards.
--- 79’ Assist Assist by B. Ivanović. ---
--- 79’ Goal! SCHURRLE! IT'S FIVE! Chelsea, so quick on the break, leave Swansea standing. Hazard and Ivanovic combine beautifully before the full-back cuts it back across Fabianski's goal and Schurrle cannot miss from two yards out. In truth, it had been coming. ---
(77’) Chelsea's work ethic is excellent as they continue to press and harry Swansea in possession. I've no doubt that with the top of the table as tight as it is, the visitors will want to score more to give their goal difference a healthier complexion.
--- 76’ Substitution A. Schürrle enters play, replacing Willian. ---
(76’) Oscar stabs a shot just wide even as it curled towards the goal. That came for Gomis being tackled well by Hazard. Chelsea still look hungry.
--- 75’ Substitution N. Dyer is done for the day. M. Barrow is his replacement. ---
--- 75’ Substitution Diego Costa is replaced with L. Rémy. ---
(75’) Taylor fires wide for Swansea because, frankly, he didn't have a better option. Willian is going off for Schurrle. The Brazilian had a good game, hitting the post once and the bar once, and contributing a lot in terms of passing and covering tackles.
--- 74’ Substitution Fàbregas is replaced with Ramires. ---
(73’) Costa is being replaced by Remy, having been quite brilliant today. That's 17 goals in 19 games for the striker in the league. Fabregas is off too, for Ramires. Barrow is on too, which is a gamble with Williams looking a bit tender.
(71’) Emnes tries to find Sigurdsson but his pass is to oheavy and runs straight out. He has been decent in a poor team performance, though, and should take heart from that. Mo Barrow is warming up, presumably as Monk again brings on a young player for experience.
(70’) FABIANSKI SAVES FROM HAZARD! The Belgian finds some space on the edge of the box and curls one towards the top left of the home goal, but the Swans' keeper does well. The football in the build-up to that was typically precise and lovely.
(69’) Taylor plays the ball into the Chelsea box after a good break from Emnes. There are no Swansea players in the area, though, so it all comes to nothing.
(67’) Fabregas wins the ball from Carroll after the Swans midfielder robs Oscar. Chelsea lose out though and Willian fouls Tiendalli as he looks to break.
--- 66’ Substitution Nélson Oliveira is replaced with J. Fulton. ---
(66’) Fulton will sit alongside Carroll and Sigurdsson will push up. The young Scot's first contribution is to give the ball away to Oscar, but Fabianski comes out to claim his pass as Costa looks to run onto it.
(65’) Oliveira again shoots wide from deep after a decent run. That's his last contribution, as young Jake Fulton comes on for the first time this season.
(64’) Cech restarts from the back. Williams looks very uncomfortable and is holding his right arm strangely. It's not looking good for the rugged Swansea defender.
(63’) Williams has been down on the floor for a minute or so now, which would just add to Swansea's already bad day. He is having his shoulder strapped up.
(61’) Oscar loses the ball sloppily and Swansea attack, Oliveira eventually shooting wide from 35 yards.
(60’) Swansea have had the ball for over a minute for the first time since the opening five minutes. Emnes has posed something of a threat and does well before Dyer eventually finds a bit of space in the box, but he is quickly closed down by Cahill, who clears.
(59’) Gomis carries the ball forwards having tackled Fabregas. Matic fouls him and Swansea have a chance to build from the free-kick. They too are forced to play it back, but at least they've kept the ball.
(57’) Fabregas shoots but it's straight at Fabianski. That came from a cross from Hazard, who left Tiendalli for dead there before cutting it back.
(56’) Hazard breaks at speed and finds Costa but he is forced to check his shot. Chelsea keep the ball and eventually play right back to the centre-backs. They are so adept at keeping the ball then springing forwards.
(55’) Oliveira makes a rare Swansea break after Oscar is tackled. He links with Dyer and Emnes, who finds Carroll. His touch is heavy though and Cahill clears.
(54’) Chelsea are dominant but Diego Costa and Ashlet Williams have continued their disagreements and the striker needs to be sure it doesn't boil over.
(52’) Swansea win a free-kick around fifteen yards from the Chelsea box. Sigurdsson bends it in but Ivanovic clears as far as Emnes. His cross is poor though and goes over Dyer's head.
(50’) Even when Swansea break up Chelsea's attacks, the visitors retain possession or win it back quickly. Willian bursts forwards on the right and tries to pull it back but it's put behind for a corner. Cahill heads wide for a goal-kick.
(49’) Cech rises easily to claim that corner. That was far too easy for the Chelsea stopper and now the Blues build again.
(48’) Swansea have a free-kick after a foul from Filipe Luis. Cahill clears for a corner, the first of the match.
(47’) Terry makes a fine challenge on Oliveira. The away centre-backs have had little to do but, one Cahill slip aside, have been faultless.
(46’) Diego Costa looks to squeeze a pass through with four Chelsea players ahead of him but it's been blocked. The visitors have started as they finished the first half: totally on top.
(45’) And we are off again. Can Swansea salvage anything from this game? I suspect not, but we shall see. And Williams and Costa are scrapping off the ball! The Swans defender dragged the striker down but they've been moved apart by the referee swiftly.
Join me, soon, for the second half of Swansea City 0-4 Chelsea LIVE!
It's seems impossible to conceive of Swansea getting back into this and the story may now simply be how many Chelsea score. They have been a real pleasure to watch so far.
The pick of the goals was Oscar's second, a sublime shot from just inside the box after a swift counter from the away side. When Jose Mourinho's side are in this kind of mood, there is hardly any stopping them.
Two goals for Costa and two for Oscar, and the visitors are in total control. Swansea gifted two of those goals to Chelsea, but that does not tell the full story. Fabregas has been exceptional as the Blues took the game by the scruff and have not relented.
(45’) And that's that and how the home side must be relieved! It's Swansea City 0-4 Chelsea!
(45’) Fabregas is on fire today and his ball finds Hazard, who just fails to create the room for a shot. The midfielder is running the show and Swansea are powerless to stop him.
(45’) Matic fluffs a shooting chance following another sublime ball from Fabregas. There will be two minutes of extra time.
(43’) WILLIAN HITS THE CROSSBAR! Diego Costa bursts through after a beautiful ball from Fabregas. He hares through and, one-on-one with the keeper, can't find a way through. He squares it to Willian, who hammers a shot onto the bar. Chelsea somehow fail to score.
(40’) Chelsea are in cruise control but Mourinho is still urging them on, possibly with the importance of goal diffference in mind.
(38’) Chelsea continue to press and Swansea look bereft of confidence now. They can barely string a pass together. Gomis tries to run through the Chelsea back-line on his own but Terry blocks.
--- 36’ Assist Diego Costa provided the assist. ---
--- 36’ Goal! Oscar has found the target for Chelsea! ---
(36’) AND THAT'S THE FOURTH! OSCAR SCORES AND THE BLUES ARE RAMPANT! Swansea barely have time to recover, as Willian storms through the middle. He spots and feeds Costa peeling away down the right, and the striker tees up Oscar for the smash home from just inside the box! What a counter!
--- 34’ Goal! DIEGO COSTA! Fernandez passes it back to Fabianski but doesn't look first and his pass finds the lurking, who coolly slots home past the stranded keeper. Chelsea are utterly on top now and the home side are the architects of their own downfall once more. ---
--- 32’ Substitution W. Routledge is done for the day. M. Emnes is his replacement. ---
(32’) Terry heads clear well from a Williams long ball and Chelsea attack immediately. Carroll has to hack down Fabregas to prevent the inevitable blue surge.
(31’) Monk has been giving instructions to Carroll and Sigurdsson during that break in play, presumably telling them to be less utterly woeful.
(30’) Routledge gives the ball away and Hazard surges forwards, but loses the ball with a poor touch. The Swans winger looks to have damaged his ankle and is going to be coming off, with Emnes likely to take his place.
(29’) WILLIAN HITS THE POST! A lovely interchange between Ivanovic and Fabregas allows the Spaniard to sneak a reverse pass into the path of the onrushing Willian, whose shot is driven high and onto the post with Fabianski beaten.
(28’) Fabregas and Hazard try to work a one-two but the ball is cleared on the edge of the box by Williams. Chelsea immediately win the ball back though, with Sigurdsson and Carroll totally unable to impose themselves on this midfield battle.
(27’) Chelsea are content to pass the ball around in the central third, looking for the overlap or the through ball. It is already nigh-on impossible to see the home side getting back into the game, although they will surely have chances.
(26’) Oscar, looking probably for the run from Filipe Luis, puts the ball straight out. A rare mistake from the men in blue.
(25’) Cahill puts himself under pressure with a poor touch after a bad header back to him from Matic. Gomis looks to sneak in but the Chelsea defender recovers in time.
(24’) Swansea actually get the ball into the Chelsea half for a period, but waste the chance with a shot that is wide.
(22’) Costa is adjudged offside in acres of space by the referee, who overrules his linesman, erroneously though. The ball had been passed back by a Swansea player and Chelsea are justifiably angry.
(21’) Costa goes close again, this time firing it narrowly over from the edge of the box. The Blues are so comfortable here and are treating us to a very stylish display.
--- 20’ Assist Fàbregas gave the assist. ---
--- 20’ Goal! DIEGO COSTA FROM CLOSE! Chelsea are running riot. A triangle of passes on the edge of the box between Willian, Fabregas, and Oscar, before the Spaniard slides a pass through to Costa. As the cliche goes, he doesn't miss from there. It's Swansea 0-2 Chelsea and we are only 19 minutes in. ---
(18’) Fabianski plunges low to his left to deny Hazard after Chelsea seize on another Swansea error in central midfield.
(16’) Oscar forces a shot just wide of Fabianski's left post after some lovely build-up. Chelsea's patience is perhaps their most devastating quality: they wait and wait and then thread the pass onto a runner having dragged the opposition this way and that.
(15’) Ashley Williams clears a Diego Costa cross and may just have turned his ankle doing so. Chelsea are now relentless in their patient, probing attacks. The ball is being moved around too quickly to mention everyone involved, but Matic and Fabregas are the fulcrum around which everything moves. It's quite superb.
(14’) When Chelsea are moving the ball around like this, it's almost unstoppable. The attack is only halted when Gomis wraps his legs around Fabregas' and brings him down. Chelsea take the free-kick short and retain possession.
(12’) Willian shoots over after Oscar has a shot well parried by Fabianski. The Chelsea build up was lovely, lots of swift, jiking interplay and passes. They can break so quickly and ably, that the lack of possession will not bother the visitors too greatly.
(11’) Swansea have had nearly 80% of the possession so far, but Terry steps out of the line and steals the ball well. He finds Willian, but the Brazilian is fouled. Chelsea build from the free-kick.
(9’) Routledge combines well with Gomis, who looks sharp, but Ivanovic is able to watch the ball out of play. There has been a really great tempo and energy to this game so far.
(8’) Ivanovic blocks a shot from Routledge, after a kind bounce from a Castro Oliveira cross finds the winger in a bit of space. Matic clears.
(7’) If there's a team who can sit and defend a lead, though, it's Chelsea. The home side are looking for width through the full-backs, especially Tiendalli, who is getting forward well.
(6’) Chelsea are struggling to get on the ball after that suberb start. Sigurdsson and Carroll are setting a good tempo in midfield, obviously keen to atone for the error that led to the goal.
(5’) Swansea look to push up against Chelsea, with new loan signing Castro Oliveira trying to get on the ball as much as possible. They are a patient side though and will probe consistently, looking for space and the final pass.
(3’) Hazard is down and holding his face. He's getting a lot of boos from the Swansea fans too, who have not forgotten his sending off a few seasons back for kicking a ball-boy.
(2’) AND SIGURDSSON HITS THE POST! Looking to make amends straight away, the Icelandic midfielder immediately tries to strike back, hitting a rising, curling shot which rattles the frame of the goal.
--- 1’ Goal! And we are off...! AND IT'S OSCAR! WHAT A START FROM CHELSEA! A sloppy pass from Sigurdsson puts Carroll under pressure and he miscontrols. Oscr pounces and takes a few touches before driving it low and hard to Fabianski's right. ---
It promises to be a tense affair at the Liberty, so join me shortly for Swansea City vs Chelsea LIVE!
In their last five games on the road, Chelsea have only managed five points from a possible fifteen, conceding eight goals in the last four of those matches. Jose Mourinho will hope that his team can arrest that slide and maintain their lead at the top of the table.
Swansea have not won an EPL game since Boxing Day but are on a good run of scoring, having netted in 11 consecutive games. However, Bony scored or created six of their last 11 goals, so it will be interesting to see how that affects the side.
Garry Monk and Swansea now face life after Wilfred Bony, following the striker's £30million move to Chelsea's rivals for the title. Bafetimbi Gomis, who has impressed when starting, comes in to fill his boots. Dwight Tiendalli gets a rare start and Jefferson Montero misses out through injury, forcing a slight reshuffle of the attacking midfield berths.
The main team news is that Petr Cech keeps out Tibaut Courtois, the latter having recovered enough from a thumb injury to make the bench. Otherwise, this Chelsea side looks familiar and settled, with solidity from Nemanja Matic, creativity from Cesc Fabregas, Oscar, and Eden Hazard, and goals from Diego Costa.
While Chelsea have been rampant for much of this season, Manchester City have slowly closing the gap on them and the Blues will look to maintain their momentum with what should be a fairly regulation visit to the Liberty.
Chelsea subs' bench: Courtois, Zouma, Ramires, Mikel, Schurrle, Salah, Remy.
Chelsea starting XI (4-2-3-1): Cech; Ivanovic, Cahill, Terry, Filipe Luis; Matic, Fabregas; Willian, Oscar, Hazard; Diego Costa.
Swansea subs' bench: Tremmel, Amat, Emnes, Rangel, Bartley, Fulton, Barrow.
Here are the teams. Swansea City starting XI (4-2-3-1): Fabianksi; Tiendalli, Fernandez, Williams, Taylor; Sigurdsson, Carroll; Dyer, Castro Oliveira, Routledge; Gomis.
I'm Alex Stewart and I'll be your host for this afternoon's encounter at the Liberty Stadium which pitches the league leaders against the side currently in ninth place, two points behind eighth and three above 10th. It's all very tight this season!
Good afternoon one and all and welcome to this LIVE coverage of Swansea City vs Chelsea!

As for Sunderland, they may feel hard-done by, nearly earning a point but undone with a moment of slack defending and a fantastic finish from Eriksen. They have their work cut out for them to avoid relegation this season but will be hoping a solid enough display today as well as the acquisition of Defoe will be enough to have them rise up the table. Thanks for joining us here today!
And that's the match! Tottenham have done just enough to win over Sunderland, showing good initiative in their play and keeping strong possession at home. Pochettino will want his side to work on creating chances and on finishing, but for the day, the job has been done.
(90’) Vertonghen scores a third but it won't count! The corner saw Pantilimon race into the box, but it's cleared by Spurs, who counter. Without the goalie in net, the ball is worked to the Belgian, who shoots from just above halfway and sees the ball go into the net, but he's judged to be offside!
(90’) LLORIS MAKES A SENSATIONAL SAVE ON GRAHAM! Sunderland looked to have nicked an improbably point here when Graham got in front of the defence with a smart turn to unleash a shot, but the French goalkeeper dived low in lightning-fast time to push the ball out for a corner!
--- 90’ +2 Substitution Spurs, unsurprisingly, playing with some swagger now, as Walker lets off a backheel on his own flank. Buckley comes on for Jones in a late roll of the dice from Poyet, who knows he has no choice but to do all he can for a late equalizer. ---
(89’) Seconds before that goal, Chadli went off fo Paulinho, who has been linked with a move away from Spurs in recent times. That goal may be tough on Sunderland, who have shown goalscoring threat when they've been in attacking positions, but Tottenham's tenacity and sheer amount of possession have earned them the lead here today.
--- 88’ Goal! Tottenham Hotspur score a goal through C. Eriksen! ---
--- 88’ Substitution N. Chadli is replaced with Paulinho. ---
--- 88’ Assist The assist came from A. Townsend. ---
--- 87’ Yellow card B. Jones receives a yellow card. ---
(87’) Sunderland keep the ball well as Larsson hooks a ball that was just about to go out of bounds into the path of Graham, who's cross from the right is blocked. Jones looks to have hit Rose without the ball but the referee saw the incident and decided just to talk to the player instead of booking him.
(85’) With Rose making an overlapping run to his left, Chadli decides to shoot with several bodies in front of him anyway; unsurprisingly, his shot is blocked and his teammate upset.
(83’) A free-kick now for the visitors, just on the halfway line, that Larsson sends deep towards Brown in the box. It's knocked out for a Sunderland throw-in, who are looking to work this carefully now, but van Aanholt loses possession and Spurs counter.
(81’) LLORIS WITH THE DOUBLE SAVE! From one end, breathlessly to the other; Wickham fails to give up on the ball, wins it in midfield, and passes it to Johnson, who unleashes a superb shot that forces Lloris into a first save before Graham's follow up can only find the goalkeeper from just yards out!!
(80’) A fantastic run from Rose sees him beat two defender and cut inside before unleashing a shot that's blocked! For a second it seemed destined to end up in the back of the net but it wasn't meant to be for Spurs.
(79’) Spurs fans rain whistles down on Townsend, who decided to shoot from outside of the box instead of passing it to Walker, who was making an unmarked run down the flank. His shot sails well wide of the post, in a move that sums up well how Spurs have done by and large this match.
(77’) An interesting statistic about Defoe: today was the first time he failed to score on his debut for any club that signed him. His current club still need a goal and have a deep throw-in, worked to Graham before Larsson whips it into the box for Wickham to head down to Johnson, but the play has drifted outside of the box.
--- 75’ Substitution Defoe's Premier League return ends after 75 minutes with Graham coming on in his place; Spurs also make a change with Townsend on for Dembele. ---
--- 75’ Substitution M. Dembélé is replaced with A. Townsend. ---
(74’) With little more than fifteen minutes plus injury tie here, Spurs continue to look the more likely of grabbing a winner. A fantastic cross from Kane is played into the onrushing Rose in the box, who sticks out a foot to shoot but watches the ball roll just too quickly before him!
(72’) Adebayor scoops the ball over to Kane, alone in front of the net, but before he can shoot the offside flag is up and the whistle is blown! He was offside there, and again, it's a close-but-no-cigar situation for Spurs.
(71’) Sunderland nearly - very nearly! - prod the ball into the net from a free-kick that arose out of seemingly nowhere, but the final touch that saw the ball go out of bounds is judged to have come off of Wickham, giving the home side a chance to regroup and breathe.
(69’) Sunderland meanwhile are growing into this now, no longer just sitting back and watching Tottenham dominate possession but pressing more effectively to try and nick the ball when they can.
(67’) Spurs are using their width more and more and it nearly pays off, as Adebayor knocks down a cross in the box that gets deflected to Chadli, who fires on goal. Somehow Pantilimon scrambles to the ground and gets a hand on the ball to keep it out of the net!
--- 65’ Substitution Following a Sunderland corner, Fletcher comes off for Wickham as Poyet looks to keep a lively and mobile attacking threat here despite this being a tricky away fixture for his side. ---
(64’) Jones halts Stambouli's progress down the pitch, causing Foy to whistle for a free-kick. Tottenham work it down the right, before crossing it to the left, and an excellent delivery from Stambouli is just hooked clear. The pressure from Spurs is mounting and they're certainly unafraid to shoot, though their shooting positions have often left a lot to be desired.
(63’) The first substitution of the game comes from the home side, with Adebayor coming on for Soldado, who's had a very anonymous match. Dier rushes in on Defoe to win the ball in midfield and get the ball to Kane, who takes a quick snap-shot that once again goes wide of the far post.
--- 61’ Substitution Soldado is done for the day. E. Adebayor is his replacement. ---
(61’) It's another poor corner from Eriksen, who's lofted balls into the box are only finding the heads of men in blue shirts. Seconds later, Tottenham counter with three of their men against just one of Sunderland's, but the pass to Kane is a second late and the striker's touch is too heavy, allowing van Aanholt to make a recovery run and knock the ball clear! That's a very good chance wasted terribly by the home side!
(59’) The set-piece resulting from that is well worked, as Kane gets on the end of it and smashes a shot towards goal from inside the box that van Aanholt scrambles to deflect out for a corner.
--- 58’ Yellow card Rodwell enters the book after taking down Eriksen from behind as the midfielder ghosted past him, with Tottenham streaking down the field on the counter. ---
(57’) From one end to the other as Dier is forced into a clearance on Defoe that results in a Sunderland corner, which Johnson whips in and watches it go just wide of Rodwell's head.
(56’) Dembele goes down in the box as he stretched to get the ball, but there was little in the challenge and no penalty is called. Tottenham keep possession and Eriksen fires a shot despite being under heavy pressure that ends up just inches wide of the far post!
(55’) Walker whips a cross into the box as Tottenham try to do something novel from out wide, but the delivery is poor and it's easily cleared.
(54’) Sunderland have a corner now as a rare foray forward ends when Fletcher's cross is knocked over the line. Larsson's delivery bounces over everyone and directly out of bounds, several yards wide of the far post.
(52’) A Tottenham corner goes to waste as Eriksen's high ball into the box is easily collected by Pantilimon. The opening spell of this half has seen Spurs continue as they were in the first; dominant in possession but lacking in ideas to turn this match on its head.
(50’) It's Chadli in the middle, who finds Kane, who sees Walker wide and alone in the box. He sends the ball to the full-back, and it's cleared but only back to the home side, who work their way into the box and see a pass deflected into the grateful hands of Pantilimon.
(48’) Eriksen is poking and prodding as usual, getting the ball just outside the box and trying to flick it in towards Kane. Sunderland have defensive strength in numbers, however, cutting out the cross and working their way slowly down the pitch.
(47’) Another nearly chance for the home side! Eriksen breaks into the box and gets the ball to Kane; the striker holds up possession until the midfielder is back onside, then returns the ball to him. He rifles a fast and pacy cross across the goal that Soldado just misses!
(46’) The second half is underway! No substitutes have been made for either side as Tottenham begin with the ball from kick-off, though it exchanges hands a few times before Stambouli and Eriksen control it in the middle and send it to Rose, who fires a low cross across the box that goes out for a Sunderland throw-in.
Sunderland, meanwhile, have equalized and threatened from nearly nothing today and have shown that they have the quality to steal something from this game, even with minimal possession. This is far from over and both managers will have his side believing they can take all three points in the second half!
Pochettino can be happy with how his side have dominated possession but certainly not with how they've created chances and finished. They have only one goal to show for their dominance and need to figure out how to be more creative in the final third.
(45’) Tottenham continue to press as much as they can but the first half ends in a draw as Kane's sensational effort from outside of the box hits the post and the follow up from Rose only finds Pantilimon!
(45’) The home side have a corner in the first minute of two extra-time ones. It ends with Kane in possession, outside the box, striking something fierce towards goal, though it bends towards Pantilimon who catches it in his midriff.
(44’) After seeing so little of the ball for so long, Fletcher gets it with space and plays it into Defoe in the box. The former Toronto man tries to stop and spin to make some space to shoot, but Walker recovers to steal it right off of his boot. Once again, Sunderland show their threat in a much more efficient manner than Spurs, and without a second goal, Tottenham continue to risk another concession.
(42’) Sunderland nearly make Tottenham pay, when out of nearly nothing, a backpass from Walker to Lloris is steps away from being intercepted by Defoe! Stambouli and van Aanholt tussle on the sideline after tangling legs though neither is booked after both just managed not to lose their temper.
(41’) Another attacking play from Tottenham but it ends once again with the ball behind the line and not in the net. They're having trouble creating genuine shooting chances now even if they're enjoying the vast majority of time spent in their opponents' half.
(40’) Jones makes his return to the pitch with his head bandaged, restoring numerical parity for both sides. He nearly immediately makes a clearance from a Tottenham throw-in though the home side are keeping the ball well in the visitors' half.
(39’) Rose dribbles into the box from his flank, working his way inside and out. He nearly does everything right but decides to snap a shot towards the near post with several defenders in front of him; his shot dribbles wide, ending the attack, which had several teammates around him.
(37’) Kane is doing his best to create chaos from a central position, just inches outside the box, as he first tries to charge his way into a shooting position before later trying to squeeze a pass wide to Chadli.
(35’) Eriksen's low corner is cleared by Rodwell at the near post, right back to the midfielder, who sees his second cross similarly cleared. On the follow-up corner, he plays it short to Walker, who loses out to Defoe and fouls the striker while trying to win the ball back. Sunderland have a free-kick now from just outside of their own box.
(34’) Jones is currently off the pitch, bleeding from his head, as he receives medical treatment. His absence has forced Johnson into the right wing-back position for the time being as Chadli's tame shot from outside of the box is deflected out for a corner.
(33’) Chadli prods his side forward, cutting inside near the edge of the box and sending in a cross that takes two different defenders in two different areas to clear.
--- 31’ Goal! AND THE FREE-KICK IS SCORED BY LARSSON! IT'S A FANTASTIC EFFORT! He runs up and strikes the ball beautifully, up and over the wall and smashing it almost exactly into the top right corner. Lloris had little he could do there, though he stretched as far as he could to stop it. That'll be controversial, with Defoe arguably offside in the build-up, but it's now tied at White Hart Lane! ---
--- 30’ Yellow card After a very dominating early spell, Spurs are struggling now as Vertonghen is booked for a very late challenge on Defoe, sliding into the striker after he had passed the ball. The home side are furious, arguing that he was offside to begin with and that the play never should have happened, but it stood nevertheless. Sunderland have a free-kick now from just outside the box, in a near central position. ---
(28’) HOW DID FLETCHER MISS THERE?! Jones sent in an inch-perfect low cross through Tottenham's box, which perfectly evades all of the defenders to end up right at Fletcher's foot, but he somehow fails to prod it into the net!
(27’) An absolutely fantastic strike from outside the box from Eriksen, who seemed to get tired of waiting for an opportunity to present itself, forces Pantilimon into an equally quality flying save! Spurs continue to flirt with a second goal here but have been unable to get the ball into the back of the net!
(25’) Another near chance for Tottenham! Vertonghen sends a high ball over the top of the defence that Soldado races onto; he's onside and just has Pantilimon to beat before the goalie slides low, makes himself big, and collects the ball from his feet!
(24’) Pantilimon scoops the ball up after Chadli's dummy in the box isn't enough for Kane to get possession. Sunderland counter quickly with O'Shea hoofing the ball up to Defoe, who is once again flagged offside, although the decision was very close this time as Dier nearly kept him in line.
(23’) Defoe underhits a pass for Fletcher that Walker can take for his own, though the game is becoming increasingly frantic and neither side are holding onto the ball well. It changes teams three or four times before Sunderland's defence can finally settle it for a spell.
(21’) Another offside flag is raised against Defoe, who's had limited involvement in his first 20 minutes back in the Premier League. Both he and Fletcher have been largely starved of possession with their midfield unable to get the ball up to them.
(19’) Rose is called into action again soon after, but this time defensively, as he is forced into a fast run to prevent Kane's poor pass from going out of bounds right around the middle fo the pitch. He keeps the ball in and sends it across field.
(18’) In a flash, Tottenham nearly double their lead! Rose rushes down the right flank and spot Eriksen unmarked in the middle. He sends the ball in, just outside the box, for the midfielder to run onto and fire a shot that forces Pantilimon into a diving save!
(17’) Chadli takes on a man too many out wide in the box and Sunderland break, with Larsson hoofing the ball up to Fletcher who tries to lay it off for the onrushing Defoe in the box but the Englishman can't get on the end of the overhit pass in time to get a shot off!
(16’) A poor pass from Eriksen is intercepted easily but Sunderland completely waste the opportunity as Brown's backpass to Pantilimon is undercooked and forces the goalie to rush and knock the ball out of play. The visitors are certainly not helping themselves, at the moment.
(15’) Kane spots Eriksen making a run in the box and sends a superbly weighted pass into the path of his teammate, who runs wide before turning to cross it to the byline. O'Shea clears it and for a second, it looks like Defoe is clear through on goal, but he's flagged offside!
(14’) Sunderland work the ball from Jones, through the backline, over to van Aanholt and into Johnson's path. By this point, much of the home side's midfield has pressed up to try and win the ball, forcing Dembele to commit a foul to prevent his side from being caught out at the back.
(13’) An excellent pass from Vertonghen sends Chadli racing to get past O'Shea in the box; the former Manchester United man uses all of his experience to shepard the ball out smartly before the wide player can cut inside with it.
(11’) Jones snakes his way down his flank and cuts inside before Dembele bundles him over. It's a free-kick now for Sunderland, from a wide position, that's looped into the box and eventually regained by Poyet's men, though it takes Pantilimon's involvement under some pressure to gain the ball back.
(10’) The visitors are looking to Rodwell, who's sitting deep and in a central position, to dictate the tempo of the game. Tottenham are doing all that they can to continually give the former Manchester City man no space whatsoever, often forcing him just to pass it right back to his centre-backs.
(9’) The visitors are trying to settle the play but Vertonghen is sharp to rise out of his line and intercept a throw-in. The home side press forward at every opportunity, though Stambouli's ambitious pass out wide towards Rose is underhit, allowing the visitors to recover the ball.
(6’) The home side work the ball down the left flank and a superb quick exchange between Kane and Chadli sets the latter free in the box, but as he goes to touch the ball around Pantilimon, he knocks it out of play! That could've been the second! Sunderland are looking very out of sorts at the back.
(5’) Sunderland seek an immediate equalizer from a corner as Rodwell rises high to meet the ball but can only get enough of his head around it to send it past the near post!
--- 3’ Goal! GOOOOOALLLL VERTONGHEN! That shot took an enormous deflection but the centre-back is taking all of the credit! After a failed clearance in the box following a Tottenham set-piece, the ball fell kindly for the Belgian, who set himself up for a shot that hit a defender and bounced around Pantilimon, leaving the goalkeeper with no chance. It's 1-0 to the home side in the opening three minutes! ---
(2’) And we have kick-off!!! The visitors, in their light blue away kits, begin with possession, and Defoe gets his first touch back in the Premier League as he sends the ball to Soldado to roll back to the defence. Rodwell is nearly caught in possession but manages to pass it to van Aanholt, though Spurs win it back near their own box. Dembele settles the ball after some back and forth to allow his side to press forward, but loses it moments later as his side tried to penetrate Sunderland's box.
We're just five minutes away from kick-off now, as the two teams prepare to walk out of the tunnel and begin the match!
There is, of course, very much on the line here today. A home victory could push Tottenham up to Manchester United, should Louis Van Gaal's men lose today, tying them on points. Sunderland may be able to go as high as twelfth and put several clubs and much breathing room between them and the relegation zone, which would be a very stable foundation from which to push on through the second half of the season.
In terms of head-to-head between these two sides, recent history is in favor of the home club. Tottenham haven't lost to Sunderland in five years and won this fixture last season in a thumping manner, with a 5-1 rout of Sunderland and Kane scoring his first ever goal for the club.
The big team news here, certainly, is the arrival and immediate start of Jermain Defoe against his former side, fresh from Toronto FC with Jozy Altidore heading in the opposite direction. Sunderland will need him to get off to a flying start, as the side have only scored 18 goals in their 21 games so far this season. Mason, Lamela, and Cattermole all miss out through injury as well as Bridcutt, who is suspended.

Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Walker, Dier, Vertonghen, Rose; Dembele, Stambouli; Chadli, Kane, Eriksen; Soldado.
