A bit of controversy at the end, as Newcastle see their appeals for a penalty denied, but they only have themselves to blame for this defeat. Up next for them is a trip to the KC Stadium to take on Hull City, while Southampton return home to take on a revitalized Crystal Palace side.
FULL TIME: NEWCASTLE 1-2 SOUTHAMPTON. There is just no stopping the Saints at the moment, who continue to march with yet another victory here today! A brace from Elia, his first two goals with the club, is enough to deal John Carver a second consecutive league defeat, while the visitors reclaim third spot with the win.
(90’) THAT WILL DO IT! A final chance for Sissoko is broken up by Fonte, and the final whistle sounds! Southampton hold on to claim all three points!
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card S. Long gets yellow. ---
(90’) The four minutes are up and Southampton have a free kick deep in their own end. Forster blasts the ball up the pitch, and still no whistle from Robert Madley. Perhaps time for one last chance?
(90’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY NOT GIVEN! Chaos atop the area and Riviere pounces on the loose ball, driving a half-volley towards goal. Jose Fonte gets his arm up and blocks the shot in the area, but nothing is given by the referee! Newcastle have every right to protest, as that sure looked like a strong claim for a penalty.
(90’) Haidara commits a foul at the halfway line, plowing through the back of Long. The substitute is down as the medical staff comes on, to run more precious time off the clock. Meanwhile, the fourth official has indicated there will be a minimum of four minutes of added time.
(88’) Time running out for Newcastle as the pressure is slowly relieved by Southampton. Pelle does some great work up the pitch to hold the ball and run time off the clock, as the hosts frantically try and get back in possession.
(86’) IMPORTANT BLOCK! The corner count rises steadily for Newcastle, but they have yet to find that elusive equalizer. This time Pelle clears the danger, but only as far as Cabella. The midfielder tries to drive a show through the mess of bodies, but Reed gets in front to turn the effort aside.
(84’) Wasted chance for Newcastle, who smartly work a short corner in for Cabella atop the area. The midfielder takes one touch too many, however, and sends his shot well wide of the near post under a bit of pressure from a defender.
--- 82’ Substitution E. Elia is done for the day. M. Targett is his replacement. ---
(82’) Southampton make their final change, and it is the hero of the night, Eljero Elia, who gives way for an extra defender in the shape of Matt Targett. There is a warm applause for the Dutchman from the traveling supporters, who show their appreciation for the impact he has had since arriving at the club.
--- 80’ Substitution M. Williamson enters play, replacing P. Dummett. ---
(80’) Cabella wins his side a free kick for his side near the touchline, from 20 yards out. Anticipation builds as players pack the penalty area, but the end result is a letdown as Colback's cross runs harmlessly behind for a goal kick.
(78’) OFF THE WOODWORK! Brilliant cross into the area from Clyne, and Pelle's header glances off the bar! That would have done it for Southampton, but the striker is incredibly unlucky not to have scored there. Pelle has now struck the woodwork six times this season, more than any other player, as well as a handful of clubs – including Newcastle (four).
(76’) Newcastle again have taken the game over, enjoying the bulk of possession and pushing high up the pitch. Southampton continue to defend well, however, blocking nearly every shot and cross, while preventing the hosts from finding any way through.
(74’) HOW HAS HE MISSED IT?! Another corner for Newcastle, but this time the delivery from Colback is a tasty one. Dummett rises to meet it, unmarked in the area, but sends his header wide of the far post! The whole of St. James' Park cannot believe it is not level.
(72’) STAT ATTACK: Southampton have the best defensive record in not just the Premier League, but all of England’s professional divisions, conceding just 15 goals through the opening 12 matches.
(70’) Good introduction by Ameobi, as he exploits the space on the left to win Newcastle a corner. Southampton deal with it well, however, as well as the ensuing pressure put on by Riviere, as the chance fizzles out.
--- 68’ Substitution Y. Gouffran is replaced with Sammy Ameobi. ---
--- 68’ Substitution V. Anita is replaced with E. Rivière. ---
(68’) Two substitutions made now by Newcastle, who are forced into a change here as they look to salvage something from this game. Emmanuel Riviere and Sammy Ameobi are introduced, as the hosts likely switch to a 4-4-2 formation, with Gouffran and Anita giving way.
(66’) There is a delay as Gouffran is down and in pain, landing awkwardly on his ankle. The medical staff it out to attend to him as a few substitutes begin to warm up for Newcastle.
(64’) It is deja vu for Newcastle, and John Carver will have to be wondering what he has done to deserve this. His side were starting to take control again and looking the likelier side to find a go-ahead goal, but a brief lapse in concentration is punished by Elia yet again, in a near replica of his first goal.
--- 63’ Yellow card S. Davis is yellow-carded. ---
--- 62’ Assist Assist by S. Long. ---
--- 62’ Goal! A lovely headed flick on from Pelle sends Elia in against Janmaat. The defender cannot usher the ball to safety, as the January acquisition gets a shot off from just inside the area. It takes a slight deflection off the right-back and beats Krul at the near post! ---
(62’) SOUTHAMPTON TAKE THE LEAD, AND ONCE AGAIN IT'S ELIA WHO SCORES COMPLETELY AGAINST THE RUN OF PLAY!
--- 60’ Substitution D. Tadić is replaced with S. Long. ---
--- 60’ Substitution J. Cork comes on for J. Ward-Prowse. ---
(60’) Koeman wastes no time, as both substitutes are introduced just a couple of minutes after taking off their tracksuits. James Ward-Prowse and Dusan Tadic are the ones to be replaced.
(58’) Shane Long and Jack Cork are both warming up on the touchline now, and either one or both of them are set to be introduced shortly. Koeman sees what we all do, with his side beginning to fade a bit, and knows he needs some fresh legs on there soon enough to spark a bit of life into his side.
(56’) There is a new sense of energy about this Newcastle side at the moment. Southampton remain calm and composed at the back, but they have had very little chance to grab a breather, as they struggle to break out of their own end in possession.
(54’) Purposeful passing from Newcastle, who are looking increasingly capable of finding a breakthrough. They still require a better final ball, but Southampton are starting to afford a bit more space than they would like in the final third.
(52’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle have not lost a league match at St. James’ Park this season in which they scored at least a goal. They were held scoreless in both defeats.
(50’) Newcastle are seeing more and more possession, but there is nothing amounting from it. They appear to have very little desire to push forward, but it certainly has not been easy for them either, with Southampton back in numbers.
(48’) Important intervention! Cabella is dispossessed far too easily by Davis near the halfway line. The midfielder breaks on a counter and lays it off for Pelle to his left, but the striker's final cross in broken up by Coloccini who prevents Ward-Prowse from running through on goal.
(46’) Newcastle get the second half underway at St. James' Park! No changes from either side at the break, as expected.
Both teams have viable options on the bench, but it is unlikely we will see any changes just yet. These sides are still feeling each other out, and both managers will feel they saw enough in that first half to believe they can go on and win this game.
HALF TIME: NEWCASTLE 1-1 SOUTHAMPTON. It was far from convincing from either side, and a draw is a very fair result as we enter the break. Eljero Elia gave the visitors the lead with his first goal since arriving at the club, though Tim Krul will be furious at himself for not keeping it out. The lead lasted just 15 minutes, as Southampton gifted Newcastle an equalizer after an ill-advised clearance by Florin Gardos. It is still all to play for in the second half!
(45’) There will be just one minute of added time, as indicated by the fourth official.
(43’) JUST WIDE! The noise is starting to build inside St. James' as Newcastle show signs of life. Cabella sends a sensational ball forward for Ayoze to chase, and the striker is able to direct a half-volley toward goal, only to see his effort trickle agonizingly wide!
(41’) STAT ATTACK: Southampton have lost just once from five matches against Newcastle since their return to the Premier League in 2012 (W3, D1).
(39’) Approaching half time now at St. James' Park, and it looks very unlikely that we will see the tie broken before the break. Neither side has been able to create much, and it just looks as though this game will be decided by whichever team makes fewer mistakes.
(37’) Newcastle are playing far too deep, which is playing into Southampton's hand. Their positioning has made it easy on the visitors to keep possession, while they struggle to get bodies forward themselves. The Magpies are just lacking a bit of inventiveness in their play, which has plagued them throughout this first half.
(35’) Elia is the latest to give the referee a piece of his mind, and rightfully so. A throw-in is played to him near the byline, and Gouffran virtually tackles the Dutchman to prevent him from breaking into the area, but no foul is given as Robert Madley awards a goal kick. The referee is just losing control a bit here and will have to regain control before things get out of hand.
(33’) John Carver is a bit unhappy here as he voices his displeasure with Tadic from the technical area, as the Southampton player goes down rather theatrically near the halfway line. Emotions are starting to run high now, in a game neither team can really afford to lose.
(31’) STAT ATTACK: Before today, Newcastle had scored just two goals in the opening half hour of their Premier League matches this season. They have the highest proportion of goals coming in the second half of games, at 76 per cent.
--- 29’ Goal! A ball through from Cabella looks quite tame, and Forster is off his line to collect. A lack of communication at the back, however, sees Gardos slide in carelessly and his scrambled clearance attempt bounces off Gouffran and into the back of the net! Extremely uncharacteristic from Southampton, who have it all to do again. ---
(29’) DISASTER FOR SOUTHAMPTON AT THE BACK, AS THEY GIFT NEWCASTLE AN EQUALIZER!
(26’) The visitors are taking control now, as the game just starts to open up a bit. Ward-Prowse is asking plenty of questions of the Newcastle defence with his passing, and nearly slips in Tadic, but Krul is alert and off his line to collect just ahead of the attacker.
(24’) NEARLY A SECOND! The Saints win a free kick along the right, from 35 yards out. Ward-Prowse sends in a sensational delivery and Newcastle fail to mark properly as Gardos gets a free header from five-yards out. The defender cannot keep it down, however, as it sails just inches over the bar.
(22’) Southampton have already started to clog the midfield and make life very difficult on Newcastle in possession. The hosts have yet to manage a real attack since Elia's opener, and they are in danger of letting this game slip away from them so early on.
(20’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle have now gone 10 games without keeping a clean sheet in the league for the first time since April to October of 2008. The last time they did not concede a goal was back on November 22, a 1-0 victory over QPR at St. James' Park.
(18’) It is incredibly cruel on Newcastle, who find themselves behind here despite controlling the game through the opening 15 minutes. As previously mentioned, Southampton so rarely give up leads this season which will make this task that much harder now for caretaker manager John Carver.
(16’) One thing which has to be said about Southampton is how comfortable they look in defence. Even without the protection from Morgan Schneiderlin and Victor Wanyama, the Saints are very calm and composed at the back. They keep their shape well, which makes it very difficult for their opponents to find a way through.
--- 14’ Assist The assist came from J. Ward-Prowse. ---
--- 14’ Goal! It is a simple long ball forward from Southampton, which Pelle does well to win and head down into the path of Ward-Prowse. The midfielder spots the run of Elia across the box, and the new signing slides the ball back across goal and into the far corner. One Dutchman outdoes the other, and Krul will be furious at himself for letting that one in! ---
(14’) COMPLETELY AGAINST THE RUN OF PLAY, ELIA GIVES SOUTHAMPTON THE LEAD!
(13’) THUNDEROUS VOLLEY! Newcastle win a corner and though the original danger is dealt with by Southampton, the ball falls to Gouffran from 30 yards out. (9’) Despite the hosts' best efforts to get on the front foot, they have posed little threat to Fraser Forster. John Carver will have to be pleased with the way they are knocking the ball around in attack, though he will be expecting a better end product.
(7’) It should hardly come as a surprise as to why Newcastle are pushing for an early goal. Southampton have dropped just two points from winning positions this season, the fewest in the Premier League. Only once this campaign did they fail to win when scoring the first goal, in a 1-1 draw with Chelsea.
(5’) It has been a rather timid start from Southampton, who have yet to string more than a few passes together in the attacking half. The visitors look eager to feel out their opponents early on, while Newcastle appear heart-set on trying to get an early goal.
(3’) Encouraging start from Newcastle as they break out of their own end wonderfully. Sissoko charges up the pitch and into the final third, before laying it off for Cabella. The midfielder does well to pick out Anita at the top of the area, but the end result is a letdown as he scuffs his shot well wide of the target.

Southampton continue to defy all odds under Ronald Koeman, with their 1-0 victory at Old Trafford last weekend proving the sky is the limit as to what they may accomplish this season. The Saints continue to reaffirm themselves as legitimate top four candidates, but can ill-afford to slip with the top of the table being as tight as it is. They face a tough test today after a long week of traveling, which took them from Manchester to Ipswich, and now Tyneside. This 1400-mile trek had to have been both physically and mentally draining for the squad – who are without four key members of the starting XI – and it will be interesting to see how they respond at St. James' Park just seven days after their emotional victory over Manchester United.
It has been quite the up and down season for Newcastle. Take out the five-consecutive wins they managed during October and November, and the Magpies have just two victories from their remaining league fixtures. Their search for a new manager looks like it will be dragged out longer than most fans would like, but they looked very good for extended periods in their 2-0 loss at Chelsea last weekend. Inconsistency has been their biggest issue all season and they will be undone by a tactically sound Southampton team if they are not at their best today.

It was a lacklustre first half for West Ham, who spent the vast majority of it on the back foot, but full credit to them for turning things around after the break, upping the tempo to great effect. Hull's task wasn't made any easier by disappointing injuries to Bruce and Chester, and they struggled against the pace and power of the hosts' in the second period, particularly when they broke away on quick counter attacks.
After failing to win any of their previous four Premier League games, the good times have returned to Upton Park for West Ham, who hold on to record a comfortable 3-0 victory against a Hull side that stay in the bottom three for another week. The Hammers, meanwhile, climb to seventh place, now equal on points with Arsenal, who are in action against Manchester City in half an hour's time.

Tony Pulis has enjoyed a perfect start with West Brom, following up a 7-0 victory in the FA Cup with a 1-0 success over Hull City. Baggies fans can finally see the light under new management, and all of a sudden their Premier League hopes do not seem nearly as bleak. They can jump all the way to 12th place win a win tonight, and need just a draw to move ahead of Aston Villa on goal differential. The Baggies have some important six-pointers against Burnley and Sunderland in February – but against all odds, their match tonight is shaping up to be one as well.
Everton are under far more pressure to pick up a victory tonight than their counterparts. Nothing has gone to plan for Roberto Martinez this season, whose side looked like legitimate top four contenders when the campaign kicked off in August. Fast forward half a season and run of five games without a win has left them just three points from safety. It is so shocking to look at the table and see their position, because they have looked nothing like relegation candidates. That is the reality of the Premier League, however, although it would be quite a surprise to see them in a similar position when the final month of the season rolls around.

As for Liverpool, the victory, their third in their last four Premier League games, temporarily moves them to within four points of fourth-place Southampton, and they next face Aston Villa at Villa Park in a week's time.
Despite the scoreline, it was a relatively straight-forward win for Liverpool, who always looked as if they were going to come away with all three points against a Sunderland side that struggled from start to finish. Despite looking more comfortable after being reduced to 10 men, the hosts never looked like they were going to cause the visitors' defence too many problems, and, as a result, they have now lost three of their last four league games heading into next weekend's tough clash against Tottenham.

Leicester continue to produce the best chances, while Benteke struggles to stay onside for the visitors. (80’) ANOTHER CHANCE GOES BEGGING! Simpson does well getting forward and picks out the run of Knockaert. The winger spots Nugent in the area, who turns and lays it off for Lawrence. The substitute fails to take the chance, however, as he scuffs his shot from in close high and wide!
(78’) STAT ATTACK: Leicester City have kept a Premier League low three clean sheets this season, while conceding at least two goals in six of their last eight matches.
--- 76’ Substitution K. Richardson enters the game and replaces C. Sánchez. ---
(76’) The substitutions have really taken the pace out of the match, which plays right into the hands of Leicester. The Villa fans are growing restless, with a "we don't know what you're doing!" chant directed at Paul Lambert. It will be a long trip home for the Villans if they cannot find an equalizer in these final 15 minutes.
--- 75’ Substitution D. Hammond is done for the day. A. King is his replacement. ---
(74’) The substitutions continue, as Andy King comes on to replace Dean Hammond, who has only just returned from injury. The visitors look set to make another change, with Kieran Richardson on for Carlos Sanchez, though it looks like they will hold off for a minute before introducing the midfielder.
--- 72’ Substitution A. Weimann comes on for J. Cole. ---
--- 72’ Substitution J. Vardy enters the game and replaces L. Ulloa. ---
--- 72’ Substitution T. Lawrence enters play, replacing M. Albrighton. ---
(72’) Leicester make a couple of changes as they try and see this one out through the final 20 minutes. James Vardy comes on to replace a fatigued Ulloa, while Thomas Lawrence, who should help defensively, is on in place of Albrighton, who had himself a tremendous game. Villa make one of their own, as well, with forward Andreas Weimann on to replace Joe Cole.
(70’) BUNDLED OVER! Willa win a corner and Cole's delivery falls kindly for Cleverley at the far post. The midfielder opts not to go for power and try and blast it past Hamer, instead trying to place it in the far corner. His effort sails over the bar as the chance goes begging.
(68’) Lambert looks nervous on the touch line as he consults with his staff about making a change. It should not be long now before we see a new face introduced for the visitors, who do not look like scoring at the moment.
(66’) STAT ATTACK: Since Paul Lambert took over as manager, Aston Villa have failed to score in 39 of their 96 Premier League matches – more than any other team over that span.
(64’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY NOT GIVEN! Knockaert does so well to make a run into the final third and cut inside, around Clark. He threads a ball across for Ulloa, who really needed to take the chance first time. The striker holds onto the ball too long and is eventually toppled over by Okore. Oliver immediately waves away claims for a penalty, and it does appear to be the right decision.
--- 63’ Yellow card C. Clark goes into the referee's book. ---
(62’) GUZAN AGAIN TO THE RESCUE! Okore gives possession away cheaply to Nugent, who lays it off for Albrighton. The winger gets into the area and unleashes a shot at goal, but again Guzan makes an acrobatic save to keep the game at 1-0!
(60’) Villa are lacking a great deal in confidence. The worst-case scenario for them is having to chase a game like they are forced to do now, and you can see in their play how uncomfortable they look having to press for an equalizer. It has left them stretched at the back and Leicester have plenty of space on the counter to try and double their lead.
(58’) This game has been sprung to life! Villa push forward and create a chance of their own, as Agbonlahor sends a teasing cross in from the right. Benteke is unable to bring it down, but Cole manages to keep it in. He drives a shot toward goal which Wasilewski does well to get in the way of before the danger is finally cleared.
--- 56’ Yellow card D. Hammond is yellow-carded. ---
(56’) Another giveaway! Villa try and play it out from the back and Sanchez puts his side under more pressure, giving the ball away carelessly with an ill-advised back pass. Nugent nearly gets on the end of it, but Clark manages to recover and clear the danger.
(54’) Guzan is keeping Villa alive! The visitors defending has been nothing short of abysmal and they are nearly made to pay again as Albrighton picks out Ulloa with a long ball forward. The striker beats his marker, but Guzan charges off his line to head it clear at the vital moment!
(52’) TREMENDOUS SAVE! That could prove to be a game saver by Guzan! Albrighton gets on the end of a long ball forward and does brilliantly to bring it down and get a cross in. Matty James runs onto the end of it, but his diving header is tipped over the bar by the keeper!
(50’) STAT ATTACK: Aston Villa have now gone 392 minutes and counting in league play without scoring a goal. Their last one was Christian Benteke’s Goal of the Month against Manchester United back on December 20.
(48’) The first chance of the second half falls for Villa as they win a corner. Joe Cole sums up the visitor's struggles in front of goal, however, as his delivery goes out of play, much to the dismay of the traveling fans.
(46’) Leicester kick-off and the second half is underway! No changes to tell you about at the break.
HALF TIME: LEICESTER CITY 1-0 ASTON VILLA. The hosts are deservedly in front at the break, and Nigel Pearson will have to be relieved. The Foxes had created the bulk of the chances throughout the opening 45 minutes, and were very unlucky not to be ahead. It was looking like another stalemate headed into the half, until a late surge of pressure finally resulted in the opening goal from Paul Konchesky. Villa have their work cut out for them now!
(45’) That is the final action of the first half as referee Michael Oliver sounds the whistle shortly after the restart.
--- 45’ +1 Goal! Scrambled defending by Villa, and Ulloa does so well to fend off Okore and loop a ball into the danger area. It bounces to Konchesky, who shows brilliant technique to strike a sensational half-volley past Guzan, off the near post and into the back of the net! ---
(45’) THERE IT IS! IT HAS BEEN COMING FOR SOME TIME NOW AND LEICESTER FINALLY HAVE THEIR LEAD!
(45’) The referee indicates one minute of stoppage time...
(43’) STAT ATTACK: Leicester City have won just one of their last 15 Premier League matches, picking up just six of a possible 45 points over that span.
(41’) SENSATIONAL EFFORT! Okore breaks up a cross and heads clear, but only as far as Nugent. The striker takes it beautifully and sends a half-volley towards the far top corner. It is wonderfully placed, dipping past Guzan, but striking the underside of the bar! It bounces on the wrong side of the line, and Ulloa is in a position to try and follow up, but his header falls onto the roof of the net! What a chance that was!
(39’) Villa are enjoying another lengthy spell in possession, but again they appear to have little intent on pushing forward, instead passing it around patiently in midfield.
(37’) No nonsense defending from Paul Konchesky. He reads the play well and does well to intercept Agbonlahor's through ball intended for Cole, and clears it behind for a Villa corner. The original cross takes a touch in the area and changes direction, falling kindly for Okore, though his shot is deflected well over the bar.
--- 35’ Yellow card J. Okore goes into the referee's book. ---
(35’) Successive corners for Leicester, and though they lead to some worrying moments at the back for Villa, neither results in a shot on target. After a bit of a lengthy goal-mouth scramble, the visitors clear and the pace is slowed again as they get back in possession. Hutton went through Hammond en route to getting that ball away, and it looked like the hosts had a strong appeal for a penalty turned aside there.
(33’) SUPERB BLOCK! Villa manage a bit of pressure of their own and after some pinball inside the area, the ball comes out for Cleverley, who lashes a shot towards goal. Morgan reads it wonderfully, throwing himself in the lane to get a vital block in, taking all the sting out of the shot for Hamer to collect.
(31’) STAT ATTACK: Only Manchester City (10 in 1995-96) and Derby (10 in 2007-08) have scored fewer goals through the first 20 games of a Premier League campaign than Aston Villa (11) this season.
(29’) With Villa's scoring troubles well-documented as of late, Leicester cannot afford to keep squandering these chances. Scoring the first goal would be so vital for them, as it would force Villa to get away from their game and really go after it, which works into Leicester's favour as there would be plenty of space for them on the counter.
(27’) ANOTHER SHOCKING MISS! Knockaert does very well to elude Hutton on the left, then send in a short cross. Ulloa flicks it on at the near post and Nugent runs onto the end of it. The striker is put under pressure by Clark, but gets his head to the ball from six-yards out, somehow putting his effort wide!
(25’) Much better from the Foxes! Leicester press much higher up the pitch now, which causes Villa all sorts of problems at the back. The defenders fail to deal with the pressure and possession is conceded in their own end, which earns a loud roar from the home supporters.
(23’) Confident defending from Wasilewski and Morgan, who deal with three successive balls played into the area for Benteke. They are doing a good job on the striker, though you can feel the tide beginning to shift a bit. The hosts have not mounted a counter attack in nearly 10 minutes now which has the crowd growing a little restless.
(21’) The visitors have settled down a bit and are enjoying the bulk of possession at the moment, though they have done little to penetrate Leicester at the back. The hosts are content at giving them space near the halfway line, but are pressuring the ball the moment it is advanced by a Villa player, which has forced Lambert's side to retreat on more than a few occasions.
(19’) OFFSIDE! Joe Cole wiggles his way through midfield and plays Benteke through on goal. The Belgian rounds the keeper and slots home, but the flag is up to indicate an offside. It was the right decision by the assistant referee, though only by a small margin, which should serve as a warning for the two Leicester centre-backs.
(17’) STAT ATTACK: By avoiding defeat today, Leicester City will extend their unbeaten run in all competitions to four matches for the first time this season.
(15’) The hosts look like they have come ready to play today! They are in dire need of three points and the urgency to their play early on is indicative of that. Villa, meanwhile, look sluggish and altogether a little disinterested through the first quarter of an hour.
(13’) ABSOLUTELY HORRENDOUS MISS! How it is not 1-0 is beyond me! Brilliant play from Albrighton who picks up the ball in midfield and streaks forward on a counter. He shows tremendous pace to break into the final third and thread a ball across goal for Nugent, but his redirection rolls wide of the far post! He has to be scoring there! If he left the ball for Knockaert, the Frenchman would have had an easy tap-in into an empty net.
(11’) GOOD CHANCE! Cole wins his side a free kick in a prominent position from 25 yards out, just to the left of goal after Albrighton was penalized for a foul. The delivery from Westwood is superb, but Leicester defend it even better, playing Benteke offside as the opportunity fails to come to fruition.
(9’) Aston Villa are trying to play their usual, boring, dreary possession game, but are not having much success keeping the ball through the opening stages of the match. Leicester have a spring in their step to start this game and are applying good pressure on the ball in midfield, wasting little time in winning the ball back.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: Aston Villa battled back from an early deficit to defeat Leicester 2-1 in the reverse fixture at Villa Park in December.
(5’) Magnificent cross! Marc Albrighton does incredibly well on the flank to fend off two defenders and send a superb ball into the box. Ciaran Clark just manages to head clear, but only as far as Dean Hammond. The midfielder keeps the pressure on and picks out Danny Simpson, who sees his cross met by David Nugent, though his shot is deflected behind for a corner.
(3’) Leicester manage a bit of good, early pressure. A poorly taken free kick and a strong bit of defensive play from Aly Cissokho, however, prevent the hosts from creating a chance. Leonardo Ulloa runs the ball out of play and the visitors can get back in possession.
(1’) Aston Villa kick-off and we are underway at the King Power Stadium! The visitors, moving right to left, are sporting their red tops and light blue sleeves, with Leicester sporting their blue and white home strip.
Paul Lambert's side were dealt a massive blow as Ron Vlaar was ruled out up to six weeks with a knee injury. Fabian Delph misses out as well as a result of a suspension. There is some good news, however, as Gabby Agbonlahor and Kieran Richardson return from injury.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Baker, Bacuna, Weimann, Richardson, N'Zogbia, Given, Lowton.
ASTON VILLA (4-3-3): Guzan; Hutton, Okore, Clark, Cissokho; Westwood, Sanchez, Cleverley; Agbonlahor, Cole, Benteke.
Mark Schwarzer is available, though he starts the game on the bench after arriving at the beginning of the transfer window. The club's record signing, Andrej Kramaric, has not arrived in time to take part. Electrifying winger Riyad Mahrez is away serving his country at the African Cup of Nations, while Esteban Cambiasso and Jeff Schlupp are injured. Danny Drinkwater also misses out as a result of a groin injury, though Dean Hammond and Andy King are fit and have returned, with the former slotting into the starting lineup.
LEICESTER CITY SUBS: Schwarzer, De Laet, Vardy, King, Lawrence, Moore, Wood.
LEICESTER CITY (4-4-2): Hamer; Simpson, Wasilewski, Morgan, Konchesky; Albrighton, Hammond, James, Knockaert; Nugent, Ulloa.
CONFIRMED TEAM NEWS:
Aston Villa are not in direct danger of dropping into the bottom three, but only as a result of their strong start to the season. They have just 12 points from their last 16 Premier League matches, and have had a harder time scoring than a sailor alone at sea. Their fans have made their discontent quite clear, with attendance dropping at a staggering rate. One goal in five matches is hardly acceptable, and barring a drastic change in their play, the Villans are putting themselves on the fast path towards relegation.
Leicester City sit bottom of the table entering the weekend – a place they have become all-too familiar with. They have already begun bringing in reinforcements, breaking their transfer record for yet another striker. Perhaps manager Nigel Pearson should shift his focus to the back line, where the Foxes are allowing the second most goals in the league this season. Leicester are four points from safety, which is not a great deal, but they have three teams to pass in the process. They have to start winning these games against the teams close to them in the table, as a few six-pointers could go a long way in salvaging their Premier League dreams.
Good day Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to East Midlands! The King Power Stadium is our venue today as Leicester City look to kick start their quest for survival as they play host to a struggling Aston Villa side. I am Alex Moretto and I will be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens!

Both teams contributed to an entertaining game this afternoon and perhaps a draw was just about a fair result. That's all from me today, I've been Chris Baker and thanks for stopping by. Enjoy the rest of your weekend.
Sam Allardyce wherever he was watching the match today will have been pleased my many aspects of West Ham's performance but ultimately he may feel frustrated that they didn't win this game. The Hammers dropped far too deep at the beginning of the second half and invited their opponents onto them. That said the claret and blues look like genuine contenders for European football next season on the evidence of today's display.
This was by no means a vintage display from Swansea but Garry Monk will be pleased with the battling qualities that his side showed this afternoon. They were on the backfoot for large spells but hung in there and probably deserved their equaliser at the time. City were missing some key player's today and it certainly showed.
After going ahead and then nearly going back in front you feel that West Ham will be the more disappointed of the two sides at full time. That said when Swansea did equalise you felt that the home team were the more likely to score the next goal. The Swans couldn't quite capitalise on that momentum and were hanging on in the final few minutes.
(90’) That's full time 1-1 here in South Wales. The points are shared at the Liberty Stadium.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card D. Poyet receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Now it's Swansea's turn to put some pressure on. Emnes and Barrow have made a real difference since coming on. Adding some pace and direct running to the City attack.
(89’) The away side looked up against it when Swansea got back on level terms but they have responded in an excellent fashion and will wonder how they aren't ahead in this match.
(86’) CHANCE! West Ham are so close to going back in front. Ashley Williams gives away a silly freekick that Aaron Cresswell takes. The left wing back goes for goal and Fabianski makes a bit of a mess of the save. The rebound falls to Andy Carroll but the Swansea goalkeeper recovers really well to stop the away team snatching all three points.
(85’) OFF THE LINE! Jenkinson's shot earned West Ham a corner that Downing delivered. On this occasion James Tomkins heads the ball towards goal and it is cleared from the goaline by Neil Taylor. West Ham are piling on the pressure but can they find a winner?!
(84’) From the resulting corner the ball drops to Carl Jenkinson who wastes no time in unleashing a fierce drive from the edge of the box. The ball is moving all over the place in the air but once again Fabianksi is up to the task and parries it away to safety.
--- 82’ Substitution D. Poyet enters the game and replaces K. Nolan. ---
(82’) SAVE! Fabianski makes a very good save to keep out a swerving shot from Stewart Downing. The West Ham winger picked up the ball in the inside right position and tried to bend the ball into the top corner with his left foot but the Swansea goalkeeper is equal to the effort.
(80’) The visitors make another change and Diego Poyet comes on in place of Kevin Nolan. It is worth pointing out that the West Ham skipper was on the receiving end of some boos from the travelling supporters as he left the field but he still applauded them anyway.
(78’) For a team that prides themselves on being defensively solid and well organised at set pieces West Ham will be bitterly disappointed to concede from a corner. The Hammers will point to the fact that James Collins was off the field receiving treatment when Swansea equalised.
(76’) In the aftermath of the Swansea goal Gylfi Sigurdsson has being substituted and Nelson Oliveira makes his debut in English football.
--- 74’ Substitution Nélson Oliveira enters the game and replaces G. Sigurðsson. ---
--- 74’ Goal! 1-1! Sigurdsson's inswinging corner is met by a great header by Gomis. The ball then seems to go in off a combination of the post and Mark Noble. I think that will go down as an own goal but Gomis will try to claim it no doubt. Game on. ---
(72’) Sigurdsson takes the ball out wide to the right wing before delivering a delicious curling cross towards Gomis in the area. James Collins however does brilliantly to head the ball away for a corner.
--- 71’ Substitution E. Valencia is replaced with M. Amalfitano. ---
(70’) Enner Valencia then takes the game to Swansea with a one man counter attack. The West Ham striker shows fantastic pace and dribbling ability to carry the ball up the pitch. His eventual shot is blocked and it turns out to be his final involvement in the match as he is taken off and Morgan Amalfitano comes on in his place.
(68’) Neil McDonald could really do with his player's pushing up the park a bit more as they dropping deeper and deeper which is inviting pressure. Barrow cuts in from the right and sees his shot blocked by Cresswell. The ball falls to Sigurdsson who's goalbound effort which is charged down in heroic fashion by Kevin Nolan.
(66’) The changes seem to have invigorated the home side and they are starting to put West Ham under some sustained pressure. Swansea will need to be at their intricate best if they are to break down the Hammers resolute backline.
(63’) OVER! Swansea put together their best move of the match together and the substitutes nearly made an immediate impact. Barrow fed the ball into Gomis who in turn picked out Emnes with a lovely pass but the sub lashed his shot wildly over the bar. That was a real opportunity for an equaliser there. More composure was required.
--- 62’ Substitution W. Routledge is replaced with M. Barrow. ---
--- 62’ Substitution M. Emnes comes on for N. Dyer. ---
(61’) Double chance for the hosts. Nathan Dyer makes way for Emnes while Wanye Routledge is replaced by the youngster Moudou Barrow.
(60’) Swansea are desperately looking for an out ball but the three West Ham central defenders are giving Gomis no room to work with and he is being massively outnumbered. Marvin Emnes looks set to join the action.
(57’) WIDE! James Collins rises unopposed at the back post from a Stewart Downing header but glances the ball wide of the post. The West Ham defender really should've hit the target there and if he had done it surely would have been 2-0. Big let off for Swansea.
(55’) Tom Carroll has been full of running this afternoon and the midfielder on loan from Spurs plays a nice one-two with Sigurdsson but he is then halted in his tracks by, would you believe it his namesake, Andy. Great work ethic from the West Ham centre forward.
(53’) West Ham are just dropping a little bit deeper and are prepared to wait for their opportunities to launch counter attacks. Jenkinson then makes a burst forward and puts in a great low cross which is met by man of the moment Andy Carroll who can only direct his effort wide of the goal.
(50’) Swansea are looking not only move the ball faster in this second half but to commit more players to their attacks. Rangel and Taylor didn't really contribute in an attacking sense during the first 45 minutes.
(48’) West Ham carry on from where they left off in the first half and quickly force a corner that Downing will go across to take. The former Liverpool defender looks to stand it up at the far post but it is comfortably headed away and Swansea look to counter attack.
(46’) Swansea get the second half started as they look to turn around this one goal deficit.
Swansea have got the likes of Emnes and Barrow on the bench. There is also Nelson Oliveira waiting in the wings to make his debut after joining on loan from Benfica. The big decision is does Garry Monk bring them on to join Gomis or in place of him?
Garry Monk's side have looked much more dangerous when they have moved the ball quickly from back to front. Swansea must get Dyer, Routledge and Sigurdsson into game in the second period. Gomis has worked hard up front but hasn't had a lot to go on so far.
After a shaky start to the match you have to say that West Ham have got their tactics just right so far. They have played a high line which has not allowed Swansea their usual room to pass the ball around. As you would expect from a Sam Allardyce team, the visitors have been well organised and physical when required. The wing backs have given them a great deal of width and City are once again struggling to deal with Andy Carroll.
Well, I'm just trying to get my breath back after a dramatic finale to the first half. Swansea were certainly the better side for the first ten minutes or so but then West Ham found their feet and began to dominate proceedings. Then just as the home team had created a couple of chances they were stunned by a fabulous goal by Andy Carroll just before the break. Despite scoring so late in the half, Swansea almost went into half time on level terms but they were denied by an excellent piece of defending from Jenkinson.
(45’) That's half time at the Liberty Stadium and West Ham lead 1-0 courtesy of a fantastic goal from Andy Carroll.
(45’) Routledge is picked out at the far post and looked set to make it 1-1 but the Swansea winger was denied by a superb block by Carl Jenkinson. That intervention from the West Ham defender is just as important as Carroll's goal.
(44’) Carroll is often labelled as a just a big target man who lacks technical ability but his goal was pure genius. He collected Stewart Downing's cross, worked the ball onto his favoured left foot and curled a beautiful shot into the top corner. Unstoppable.
--- 43’ Assist Assist by S. Downing. ---
--- 43’ Goal! GOAL! AND WHAT A GOAL! Andy Carroll gives West Ham the lead with an absolutely stunning strike. ---
(40’) Nathan Dyer has suddenly come to life in this match and Swansea are passing the ball around with their usual zip. The movement from the attacking player's has improved dramatically and West Ham look a lot more uncomfortable than they have done for much of this game.
(38’) CHANCE! Swansea really should be ahead. Dyer raced into space down the right wing between the centre backs and Cresswell at left wing back. The Swansea winger then cuts it back to Sigurdsson who can only side foot the ball straight at Adrian. You would expect him to do a lot better with that kind of opportunity.
(36’) SAVE! Sigurdsson tries to curl the ball into the bottom corner from the edge of the area but his effort takes a deflective and it is easy for Adrian to deal with. Much more like it from the home team though.
(33’) SHOT! Neil Taylor takes aim from 30 yards but his speculative effort was never in much danger of threatening Adrian in the West Ham goal. Crucially for Swansea - Gylfi Sigurdsson has been able to get on the ball a lot more in the last five minutes or so and as a consequence the Swans look more dangerous.
(30’) Gomis races onto a pass over the top and brings the ball into the West Ham penalty area. The Frenchman then shows a lack of conviction and loses the ball as he tries to cut inside on to his right foot. That was half a chance for the Swansea striker and he will need to be more decisive in future.
(28’) The away side are playing pretty high up the pitch and it is a deliberate tactic to minimise the amount of space Swansea have to play in. The City midfielders are being squeezed out of things at present. The home team will continue to play their passing game but they need to up the tempo.
(26’) The West Ham wing backs are seeing plenty of the ball and they are stretching the Swansea backline. Rangel and Taylor could do with a bit more support defensively from Dyer and Routledge to stem the flow of attacks.
(23’) SHOT! Another diagonal ball from Cresswell finds Carroll who brings the ball down well. Kevin Nolan then tries to take over but rather gets in the way of West Ham striker and Nolan's attempt sails over the bar.
(20’) OVER! Carl Jenkinson blasts the ball high over the bar after being icked out by Mark Noble. Swansea started brightly but it is now the away side who are beginning to get on top of their opponents. Britton and Tom Carroll are quite a lightweight pair in the defensive midfield area and they are being dominated at this moment in time.
(18’) Cresswell this time is spot on with his cross and he picks out Valencia from the left-hand side. The West Ham striker mistimes his jump and the ball flicks harmlessly off of his head. If Valencia had found the back of the net it wouldn't have counted as he had already been flagged offside.
(16’) Fabianski gets his first meaningful touch of the ball as he comes off his line to pluck Cresswell's freekick out of the air. That cross was far too straight from the West Ham full back, he never gave his teammates a chance to attack the delivery there.
(14’) The absence of Bony might be making all the headlines at the moment but Ki Seung Yeung being away the Asia Cup is also a big blow to Swansea. The South Korean midfielder is a bit of an unsung hero who covers a lot of ground and gives real energy to Garry Monk's team.
(12’) Ashley Williams and Enner Valencia have tangled with each other on the edge of the area. The City skipper appeared to pull Valencia to the ground and is perhaps a little fortunate not to be booked. Williams has been given the benefit of the doubt there from Mike Dean.
(10’) The West Ham midfield trio of Downing, Nolan and Noble are beginning to settle and are seeing more of the ball in central areas. Downing has been in fine form this season and the visitors will want him to become more involved in proceedings.
(8’) West Ham have been up against it so far but the Londoners have just managed to string a few passes together in the Swansea half for the first time. The Hammers have been fairly direct so far looking to go long towards Carroll at every opportunity.
(6’) Tom Carroll has been very bright in the opening exchanges and plays a neat one-two with Routledge who is tugged back by Mark Noble. Free kick to Swansea in definite Sigurdsson territory. The Icelander takes the shot on from all of 35 yards but it goes straight into the wall.
(3’) CHANCE! Gomis has begun this game with real intent and picks up the ball just inside the West Ham and drives forwards. The French striker then smuggles the ball out to the right to Nathan Dyer who fizzes a cross into the box and Gomis is just inches away from heading Swansea into an early lead.
(2’) Swansea have started the match in a positive fashion. Immediately trying to get into their usual passing rhythm early on. Andy Carroll then wants a free kick after a strong challenge from Fernandez but nothing doing from the referee.
(1’) Both sides are in their traditional strips. Swansea in all white and West Ham in their famous claret and blue. There is no Sam Allardyce in the du out for the visitors today as he is unwell. Neil MacDonald will be taking care of team affairs this afternoon. West Ham get us underway!
The players are just coming out onto the pitch. It's a sell out here at the Liberty Stadium and there is great atmosphere building here as kick off approaches. West Ham are looking for their first win in the Premier League at this ground. Can they do it this afternoon? We'll soon find out...
Swansea have been strong at home recently winning four, drawing two and only losing one of their last seven league games at home. The Hammers will arrive at the Liberty Stadium in confident mood as well, they are unbeaten in their last four games against the Swans. They've won three of those encounters.
Sam Allardyce has changed the shape of his West Ham side with the Hammers playing a 5-3-2 formation with Carl Jenkinson and Aaron Cresswell as the wing backs. Despite retiring from international football earlier this week there is no Alex Song in the squad today while Diafra Sakho misses out with a back injury. Cheikhou Kouyate has now joined up with the Senegal national team.
Swansea begin life without Wilfried Bony who is away on international duty with the Ivory Coast as they prepare for the African Nations Cup. In all likelihood though it seems that Bony has played his final game for the Welsh side as a transfer to Manchester City looks to be imminent. Garry Monk's side are also without Jefferson Montero through injury and Jonjo Shelvey is suspended. Bafetimbi Gomis will be looking to show that is a more than able replacement.
West Ham (5-3-2): Adrian; Jenkinson, Reid, Tomkins, Collins, Cresswell; Noble, Nolan (c), Downing; Valencia, A.Carroll. Subs: Jaaskelainen, Jarvis, Vaz Te, O'Brien, Amalfitano, Poyet and Cole.
Swansea (4-2-3-1): Fabianski; Rangel, Fernandez, Williams (c), Taylor; Britton, T.Carroll; Dyer, Sigurdsson, Routledge; Gomis. Subs: Tremmel, Oliveira, Emnes, Tiendalli, Bartley, Fulton and Barrow.

As for Stoke, they come into today's game in 11th place, seven points behind Arsenal and just one point behind Newcastle United after the latter side's defeat against league leaders Chelsea yesterday. It has been a good few weeks for the Potters, who are unbeaten in their last four games in all competitions, with their last defeat, their only one since the start of December, coming against Chelsea in the final game before Christmas. As a result, they are knocking on the door of the top half of the table, and a victory this afternoon will not only move them above Newcastle and into 10th place but will send them to within one point of ninth-place Swansea City ahead of back-to-back games against struggling Leicester City and Queens Park Rangers.
After embarking on a four-game unbeaten run, their longest since the end of September, in which they won three of their four Premier League clashes, Arsenal were sent crashing back down to earth by a revitalised Southampton side on New Year's Day, losing 2-0 to the Saints in a disappointing game for Arsene Wenger's men. As a result, they head into this afternoon's clash in sixth place in the table, three points behind Southampton, who are in action against Manchester United later today, and, crucially, one point behind Tottenham Hotspur. Their North London rivals' 2-1 defeat away to Crystal Palace yesterday evening means that either a win or a draw will move the Gunners above Spurs and into fifth place, but they will be well aware that a victory is vital if they are to keep the pressure firmly on Southampton and a Champions League qualification spot.

HALF TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-0 CRYSTAL PALACE. Both teams had their chances to break the deadlock through the early stages of the match, but Speroni denied Hutton at one end, before Bolasie and Palace were kept out by the crossbar. Chances were still hard to come by though the opening 45 minutes, and neither side will want to concede first with such an important three points at stake.
(45’) The half time whistle sounds with Aston Villa being jeered off the pitch by their own fans! Crystal Palace will be thrilled as frustration sets in amongst the home side.
(45’) There will be two minutes of added time as indicated by the fourth official.
(43’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace last scored an away goal in the league on November 29, a 1-1 draw at Swansea. They went the entire month of December without scoring an away goal, through three matches, and have now seen their drought extend to 380 minutes, unless they find one before the break.
(41’) With half time approaching, Palace are being very cautious at the back. They are focusing their efforts on keeping the clean sheet into the break, while waiting for a mistake from Villa to punish them on the counter. It has led to some good opportunities, but a lack of concentrated pressure on the hosts' goal has made life easy on them for extended periods.
(39’) SUPERB TACKLE! Crystal Palace strike on a quick counter, with Bolasie charging forward. He sends Kelly in along the left, and the defender delivers the ball into the path of Zaha in the centre. Clark does incredibly well to recover, however, sliding in from behind to break up the chance! It is a goal saving tackle from the substitute.
(37’) Villa have not got nearly enough movement from their front three. Benteke is playing very narrow, which is what you want from him, but Weimann and Agbonlahor are not nearly deep enough and have failed to make runs off the ball to try and open up space for the front-man, who has been held largely in check by the Palace defence.
(35’) The pace has really fizzled out of the match and neither team can find the right passes once in the final third. Space has been hard to come by in midfield, with the two sides seemingly more focused on not conceding than actually scoring.
(33’) STAT ATTACK: Since Paul Lambert took over as manager, Aston Villa have failed to score in 38 of their 95 Premier League matches – more than any other team over that span.
(31’) PENALTY APPEALS NOT GIVEN! Palace work the ball forward brilliantly. Bolasie takes a pass and fends off a defender before playing Ledley through on the left. The midfielder picks out McArthur in the centre, who goes to ground after nudging the ball forward. He was always looking for a penalty, as Okore made very little contact, proving referee Robert Madley made the right call.
(29’) Clever footwork shown from Puncheon to maneuver his way through a tight area atop the Villa box and get the ball onto his favoured left foot. He tries to curl a shot towards the far post, but his effort ends up sailing a couple of feet wide.
(27’) ROOF OF THE NET! Bacuna has had about enough of delivering good balls into the area, only for his teammates not to get on the end of them. He has a chance from a free kick about 30 yards out, and goes for goal himself. He gets plenty of pace and movement behind his shot, but it just doesn't dip enough as it skims the crossbar and crashes onto the roof of the net.
(25’) Crystal Palace are looking to use their speed to attack Villa, and it has worked for them thus far. A high, chipped ball forward gives Bolasie something to chase. Guzan comes out of his goal with Hutton beaten for pace, and is put into an awkward position as he is forced to leave his area and just head the ball away with the winger waiting to pounce.
(23’) STAT ATTACK: Aston Villa have scored a meager 11 goals this season, which is the fewest total among all 92 league clubs in England.
(21’) The hosts have been rather ineffective from set pieces, failing to capitalize on their chances. It appears at the moment that Palace want it more, getting to every ball first, while looking to press in possession. Villa have been more content on slowing the pace and trying to keep the ball away from the visitors.
(19’) Aston Villa did win the reverse fixture at Selhurst Park at the start of December, with Christian Benteke's glorious solo effort giving the Villans the first half lead. Lambert's side hung on for dear life after that, however, and Guzan proved to be the hero as they held on for a 1-0 victory.
(17’) HOW HAS HE MISSED IT?! Disbelief on the sidelines as Crystal Palace somehow fail to take the lead. Off the corner, Bolasie starts on a counter from inside his own half. He charges all the way up the pitch, showing great pace, beating two defenders. Finally through on goal, he makes quick work of Guzan, but his shot cannons out off the underside of the bar! He was already celebrating the goal, but it has not gone in! Unbelievable!
--- 15’ Substitution C. Clark comes on for R. Vlaar. ---
(15’) INCREDIBLE SAVE! Cissokho charges down the left with real intent, and passes across the area. His full-back partner, Alan Hutton, runs onto the end of it and looks to have a sure goal as he directs it towards goal. Speroni makes it across, however, and somehow gets his fingers on it to push the shot behind! Superb stuff from the keeper.
(13’) STAT ATTACK: The last five Premier League meetings between the two teams have seen just seven goals scored, and only on one occasion did both teams find the back of the net in the same match.
(11’) Concerning moments for both teams! Delaney seems to have picked up a knock following the challenge and makes his way off with the help of the training staff. Meanwhile, Vlaar's knee is in considerable pain. The Dutchman makes his way back out onto the pitch after getting a look from the training staff, but is limping considerably as he comes back onto the pitch. You can see the pain in his face! Surely he cannot carry on like this?
(9’) Palace win the first corner of the match following a free kick. Puncheon delivers but Villa deal with it and Bacuna starts on a quick counter. The Dutchman does well to fend off a defender and run the length of the pitch, but just as he gets set for a shot, Delaney slides in from behind to break up the move. Great hustle shown by the defender.
(7’) There is an incredibly subdued atmosphere inside Villa Park, as far from sellout crowds have become the norm for Aston Villa. It sounds more like a funeral than a football match, which should do wonders to help Crystal Palace's chances.
(5’) It has been a cagey start, as anticipated. While it is still early in the match, you can sense the nerves from both teams. These are two of the lowest scoring attacks in the Premier League and neither want to be the ones to concede the first goal, as it could spell disaster.
(3’) That didn't take long! After some good movement in attack, Andreas Weimann spots Benteke in the area, teeing the striker up for a shot. He makes good contact, but Julian Speroni is up to the task, keeping it out at the near post.
(1’) Aston Villa kick-off and we are underway in Birmingham! The hosts, moving left to right, are sporting their red tops and blue shorts, with Crystal Palace in their yellow away strip.
Alan Pardew is confirmed to be in attendance today at Villa Park, with his signing as new manager expected to be immenent. Keith Millen is expected to be in charge for the last time before handing over the reins to the ex-Newcastle boss.
The Eagles were dealt a big blow as Mile Jedinak left to join Australia for the Asia Cup, which is scheduled to take place over the next few weeks. He is replaced in midfield by Martin Kelly. Marouane Chamakh is the other absentee, as he continues to suffer from a lingering thigh injury. Caretaker manager Keith Millen has made no changes to his starting lineup otherwise, confident they can pick up a victory after drawing at Loftus Road on Sunday.

Paul Lambert has to make do without the suspended Fabian Delph, who is replaced by Leandro Bacuna in midfield. Gabby Agbonlahor had his red card revoked and returns to the starting lineup. Joe Cole also returns from a hamstring injury, but starts on the bench. The only other change comes at the back, where Jores Okore slots in alongside Ron Vlaar for the injured Ciaran Clark.

Crystal Palace begin their new year with a new manager. Alan Pardew has made his way over from Newcastle, and will take over for caretaker Keith Millen. The task is clear for the 53-year-old, who spent the greater part of his playing career with the Eagles – to keep them up in the Premier League. The London club enter 2015 in the third and final relegation slot, trailing Hull City on goal differential, yet their situation looks far less bleak than a few of the teams above them in the standings.
Aston Villa are struggling mightily at the moment, and not just in the standings. Villa Park has experienced a stark drop-off in attendance, which can be largely attributed to the fact that Paul Lambert's side are very hard to watch. Christian Benteke has an innate ability to spark the team with his moments of brilliance, but they have become far too dependent on the Belgian to create and score the goals. The Villans could desperately use some reinforcements with the transfer window now open, but Lambert will have to find a way to prevent them from dropping too much in the meantime.

Well that's all folks! I've been Patric Ridge, and it has been a pleasure to guide you through all the action today as Hull claimed their sceond home win of the campaign with a comfortable 2-0 victory over Everton, who had Antolin Alcaraz sent off late on. Join us next time!
It's been a torrid festive period for Evertonians, and that loss is the first time that The Toffees have suffered four defeats in a row since December 2005, while that is Hull's first home victory in over two months.
That loss means Everton slump down into 13th, while Hull move away from the relegation zone into 15th. Steve's Bruce men were in complete control for the majority of the game, and it is clear that Roberto Martinez has problems at the moment, with his side now just four points above the relegation spots.
(90’) FULL TIME: That's full-time here at the KC! Hull 2 - 0 Everton
(90’) Everton have shown a bit more in this second period, but The Tigers have never looked troubled. A deserved three points for the hosts.
(90’) A poor clearance from Jagielka lands at the feet of Meyler, but the Hull midfielder can't capitalise and Oviedo recovers. Naismith bursts forward but his pass is intercepted easily.
--- 89’ Yellow card H. Maguire gets yellow. ---
(89’) Hernandez races in behind The Toffees' backline once again, but his dinked effort is just wide of the upright. Still no action in regards to another change from Martinez. Poor stuff all-round from Everton.
--- 86’ Red card! Alcaraz sees red! The centre-back blocks off Jelavic, and the referee immediately reaches for his cards. It looks near impossible for Everton to get anything from this now! ---
(85’) CHANCE FOR EVERTON! Baines finds Lukaku with an inch-perfect pass over the top, but the Belgian can't direct his header on target.
(84’) More comical defensive work from Everton, who look unacustomed to playing with a back three. Oviedo finally breaks down the left and fires in a dangerous ball that Coleman recovers at the back post. The Irishman finds Barkley who twists out of trouble and chips a cross into the box, which is headed out by Chester.
(81’) Hernandez has tormented The Toffees all day, and he wins his side another free-kick after being brought down by Alcaraz. Brady floats in another superb cross which is destined for the head of Chester, but Jagielka rises well to head clear for a Hull corner.
(79’) CHANCE! The ball falls to Jelavic in the box after good play from Hernandez and Meyler. The Croatian swipes at it first time, but Barry is well positioned to stop a certain goal with a well-timed interception. Big chance to kill the game for the hosts.
(77’) Hull have only kept two clean sheets at home all season but, despite the pressure, Everton are toothless in attack. Martinez stiill has a third substitute left to use, with Koné having had a disapointing afternoon up top.
(75’) Good play down the left from the visitors as Oviedo whips in a cross, but McGregor is able to beat Koné to it. Hull counter again, with Barry catching Hernandez - and the experienced midfielder is perhaps lucky to escape a second booking.
(73’) This could be a crucial 20 minutes in Everton's season now. Another loss would almost certainly signal the end of their top-six hopes, while it will also plunge them closer to the relegation zone. They pile it forward once again, but Koné is easily dispossessed. Poor from the Ivorian.
(70’) Baines whips in yet another corner wasted for the visitors, who have had a decent spell of pressure in the last few moments. It is cleared well however, and Hull counter through Hernandez. The striker powers forward, but fails to find Livermore with his throughball.
--- 67’ Yellow card Booking for Alcaraz as the Paraguyan snaps at the ankles of Hernandez, giving Hull a free-kick in a dangerous position which Jelavic will take... and just over the top! Close to a second of the game there for the forward. ---
(66’) Teriffic play from Brady, who whips in a perfect cross into the danger area. It skids off the turf and into the grateful hands of Robles. Everton move out through Barkley, but The Tigers defence remains solid.
--- 65’ Yellow card G. Barry is yellow-carded. ---
(64’) Sloppy play from Koné who goes in high on Meyler, although Everton should have been awarded a free-kick beforehand for a foul on Barkley. Hull have lessened their attacks for now, but as soon as the ball is played into midfield they are able to win back possession with ease, with Baines looking lost in his new role.
(61’) Everton need more urgency in their game, as Hull are able to move forward without too much pressure. Koné and Lukaku are isolated up top, and Martinez needs to change it up if he is to avoid a fourth successive loss.
(58’) Barkley is the only bright spark for Everton at the moment as he drives The Toffees forward. His pass is blocked but lands at the feet of Lukaku, but the Belgian's shot is too tame to trouble McGregor.
--- 56’ Substitution That's it for Rosenior unfortunately, as he is stretchered down the tunnel. Hull move forward again, with Jelavic flashing a cross across the face of goal that somehow evades four players, allowing Coleamn to run it clear. Hull looking to wrap up the result with a third. ---
(54’) Rosenior is in big trouble now as he goes down without a player near him, clutching his hamstring. He falls off the pitch however, and Everton play on. Barkley picks it up twelve yards out, twisting and turning before drilling a shot at McGregor, who reacts well to parry away the strike. Better from Everton.
(52’) Everton have a free-kick in a promising position now, but it is wasted by Lukaku who drags his strike wide of the right-hand post. Martinez growing frustrated on the touch-line, with reason.
(49’) Hapless defending once again as the set-piece drops into the box, with Robles glued to his line. The ball eventually falls to Hernandez three-yards out, but the Uruguayan turns his effort wide.
(48’) Everton look to be setting up with a back-three now, with Baines moving into central midfield to accomodate Oviedo.But the backline still looks shaky, with Alcaraz being dispossesed by Jelavic with ease. Dour stuff here from The Toffees as Hull are awarded a free-kick for a foul on Brady.
--- 46’ Substitution K. Mirallas is replaced with R. Lukaku. ---
--- 46’ Substitution B. Oviedo comes on for M. Bešić. ---
--- 46’ Substitution R. Brady enters the game and replaces G. Ramírez. ---
(46’) Two changes from Martinez now as Mirallas and Besic are replaced by Bryan Oviedo and Romelu Lukaku respectively. Robbie Brady has been brought on by Bruce in place of Ramirez.
Everton have looked disjointed and sluggish in the first-half, and seem like a collective of individuals rather than a team at the moment. Steve Bruce, on the other hand, will be delighted with his side's performance so far, who have mustered 10 shots as opposed to Everton's two and have been in complete control. The Toffees look blunt going forward and defensively inept... the tide could start to turn against Martinez if they can't salvage something this afternoon.
HALF TIME - Hull 2 - 0 Everton: El Mohamady and Jelavic have given The Tigers a well-deserved lead at the interval. It's been a terrible performance from Martinez' lacklustre Everton, who only have themselves to blame for two basic defensive errors. The Spaniard has a lot of work to do in the dressing room!
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card Koné tracks back valiantly, but the Ivorian's challenge is lazy and mis-timed, earning him a booking. Hull find El Mohamady on the flank, but the Egyptian's cross is cleared away as the referee blows his whistle for half-time. ---
(45’) More terrible defending from Everton, who have been disapointing at both ends of the pitch so far. Baines whips in a free-kick from thirty yards-out, but it's comfortable for McGregor.
--- 43’ Assist The assist came from A. Hernández. ---
--- 43’ Goal! GOOALLL FOR HULL! Nikica Jelavic bags Hull's second against his old club. Hernandez hooks a pass over and behind the Everton defence which the Croatian latches onto before dinking a cute finish over the hapless Robles. ---
(40’) Coleman sprints down the right and earns Everton another corner. The delivery is again disapointing though, and Hull break swiftly, finding Hernandez 18-yards out, but the striker's effort soars over the bar.
--- 39’ Yellow card J. Livermore receives a yellow card. ---
(38’) Tight! Baines moves inside and plays through Mirallas, but the Belgian is given offside. Friend brings the play back however, with Livermore being shown a booking for a late tackle on Baines earlier in the move.
(35’) Another chance for Hull as Hernandez shanks his header wide as Hull exploit more amateur defending from Everton. The visitors manage to get it back however, and Koné wins a corner at the other end, but Baines' cross is blocked.
--- 33’ Assist The assist came from L. Rosenior. ---

(31’) Poor defending from Everton as Hull carve through their midfield with ease. Hernandez picks it up in the box and dances round Jagielka, before firing a powerful shot at Robles at the front post which the Spaniard deflects into the side-netting for a corner.
(29’) Good harrying by Naismith who wins the ball back off the tricky Ramirez. Hull get it back though and work it out to Meyler down the right, but Everton regroup and force the hosts backwards.
(27’) Barkley breaks superbly down the middle before taking a fall just outside the Hull area after being pushed by El Mohamady, but the referee doesn't award a foul. Controversial decision again by Friend.
(24’) Sustained pressure from Everton now, with Barkley pulling the strings in midfield. Besic does well down the right before finding Naismith, but Meyler tackles well.
--- 23’ Substitution Liam Rosenior is set to come on now for the hosts, with Andrew Robertson unable to continue after Besic's hefty tackle earlier on. ---
--- 20’ Yellow card Reckless tackle by Meyler here, as the Irishman dives in on Naismith. Thankfully for Everton the forward is unscathed. ---
(20’) Penalty shout from Everton now as Naismith takes a tumble in the box under pressure from Ramirez, but Friend waves away the appeals.
(18’) A lively start here, with both sides looking to get forward as much as possible, though Hull are seeing the majority of possession.
(16’) Hull are pegging the visitors back well here, but Coleman bursts well up the right before finding Naismith in the box, but the Scot's shot is blocked.
(14’) Hernandez gets in behind the Everton defence, but the Uruguayan is flagged offside. Risky defending from The Toffees.
--- 11’ Yellow card Late tackle from Besic on Robertson, and the Everton midfielder picks up a booking. He'll be suspended for The Toffees' next game. ---
(10’) El Mohamady picks up the ball on the edge of the box after Ramirez' corner is cleared, but the Egyptian's cross-come-shot sails just wide.
(9’) CHANCE! Barkley whips in a cross that deflects off a defender and falls to Mirallas on the edge of the area, but the Belgian blasts it high over the bar. Poor.
(7’) Promising build up play from Everton with Baines bursting down the left, but Mirallas can't find the full-back with a return pass. Hull pressing well here and Everton look uncomfortable at the moment.

(4’) Over! Jelavic steps up to take the free-kick, but he shanks the shot high and wide of the upright.
(3’) Big decision by Kevin Friend here, as Barry brings down Hernandez just inside the area, but the referee awards a free-kick rather than the spot-kick. Let off for Everton.
(2’) Hull have only won one game at home this season, and they could have been behind after just a minute when Everton broke through Besic. The midfielder played in Kone, but the Ivorian squandered his chance to get a shot off.

Leighton Baines struggled to settle in a central midfield role against Newcastle, and the England international has been moved back to full-back today.

Today's hosts earned a 1-1 draw in the reverse fixture at Goodison Park at the start of last month, and Steve Bruce will be confident that his men will be able to get a result against an Everton side that have lost four of their last six league fixtures.

As always, thank you for joining us for today's LIVE text commentary of the clash between Liverpool and Leicester City at Anfield. I'm Matthew Judge and it has been a great pleasure talking you through all the action. We hope to see you again very soon. Take care!
FA Cup action takes over now, with Liverpool travelling away to AFC Wimbledon while Leicester play hosts to Newcastle United. Next up in the league for both sides is a trip to Sunderland for the Merseysiders and a home visit from Aston Villa for the Foxes.
Leicester's point means they are still bottom of the table on 14 points, but they are now unbeaten in their last two games and in a good bit of form. Liverpool, on the other hand, have stayed eighth after throwing away a two-goal lead at Anfield.
With Burnley, Crystal Palace, QPR and West Brom all picking up a point apiece across the Premier League today - while Hull City managed to beat Everton 2-0 on home soil -  it was vital Leicester picked up something in the relegation scrap at the bottom of the table today.
While Liverpool entered the second-half with a two-goal lead, they simply never got started in the second 45 minutes and were caught cold by Nugent and Schlupp's strikes in a matter of minutes after the interval.
FULL-TIME! Leicester come back from two goals down to snatch a point in a 2-2 draw with Liverpool at Anfield on New Year's Day. Second half goals from Nugent and Schlupp cancel out a brace from Gerrard via the penalty spot.
(90’) Mahrez gives the ball away cheaply in the middle of the pitch and Liverpool break through Sterling, but De Laet comes across to clear the ball brilliantly. The Reds keep up the pressure and Cambiasso has cleared for a last-gasp corner for Rodgers' side.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card S. Gerrard is cautioned by the referee. ---

--- 89’ Yellow card M. James gets yellow. ---
(89’) Cambiasso and Ulloa play a great exchange of passes between each other to put Nugent in on goal, but the striker drives his effort straight at Mignolet. Leicester keep hold of possession and win a free-kick, which Mahrez is standing over.

Green should have been dismissed early on but somehow was allowed to stay on the pitch, and then Fer opened the scoring with a great goal. Nothing was given, and the Swans flimsy defence has been consistently put under pressure since.
(45’) After one minute of added time, the referee brings the first half to a close.

(43’) VARGAS HITS THE POST! Fer does brilliantly to move the ball down the left for Austin, whose cross to the back post is controlled by Zamora. It would have taken something special to find the net from there, mind.
(42’) Gomis gets in front of Dunne to receive a cross at the near post but the centre-back slides in to block his shot on goal. Another effort is intercepted by the QPR defence before a final strike from Routledge skids wide of the far post.
(40’) STAT: The Swans have won their last three Premier League encounters with the R’s, netting 11 times. They're going to have to come from behind in order to keep that record up today.

And so it finishes Southampton 2-0 Arsenal. Thank you for joining me, Alex Stewart, for this LIVE coverage. You can all go back to bed now.
Gardos was otherwise very good as was Wanyama and Harrison Reed, who came on for Mane when the goalscorer was injured. Davis also played well and the home team's tidy use of the ball and excellent pressing meant that their inability to convert chances did not cost them.
Arsenal's inability to defend has cost them dearly again, but Southampton were also very effective in stifling their creative attackers. Sanchez excelled again and Gardos should have been sent off for bringing the striker down.
Well, I said it would be good, didn't I? Sadio Mane's superbly struck shot from near the corner flag gave the Saints the lead after rash goalkeeping from Szczesny. Another defensive mix-up gifted Tadic the second from close and Southampton could have had more, with Ward-Prowse spurning four chances and Pelle hitting the post twice and having a shot cleared off the line.
(90’) Long tackles Gibbs deep in Arsenal territory, epitomising the home team's approach even as the final whistle nears. And there it is! Southampton have cemented fourth place with an emphatic 2-0 win over the Gunners!
(90’) Forster will take his time over this goal kick, I suspect. This is the first match in five when the Saints have managed to beat Arsenal at home, and, but for Ward-Prowse's profligacy, it could have been a shellacking.

(90’) Fonte clears as Gibbs is robbed in the box. Arsenal have an attacking throw though. Reed brings it away after tackling Sanchez well but Long is offside.
(89’) Southampton, with subsitute Reed at the fore, have not stopped harrying and hassling Arsenal all afternoon. They win the ball back but Arsenal then nab it back. They have nowhere to go though. There will be four minutes of extra time.
(88’) Coquelin's cross is so poor that it looks like a mis-hit shot. Arsenal are throwing everything at this, but they have lacked the quality to make it count.

(78’) Reed fouls Oxlade-Chamberlain to give Arsenal a free-kick. (77’) Cazorla finds a cross from nowhere and Oxlade-Chamberlain hoovers up the second ball, putting his laces through it from deep. Forster sees it all the way though, and gathers well.
(76’) Arsenal win a corner from Coquelin's good work. Alderweireld and Fonte combine to hammer it out.

(70’) Gardos is coming off for Yoshida. The Romanian has had a fine game but, in truth, should have been sent off for bringing down Sanchez with no cover.

(50’) Ward-Prowse lofts in a free-kick after Koscielny fouls. Szczesny gathers cleanly though.
