It's a completely different story for West Brom, however. The Baggies have only managed to win one of their last nine Premier League games, the last three of which all ended in defeat, leaving them just one point clear of the relegation zone in 16th place ahead of what is sure to be another tough clash this afternoon. Sunday's 2-0 defeat against Stoke City proved to be Alan Irvine's final game in charge, as the Scottish manager was given the boot on Monday morning. Former Stoke boss Tony Pulis has signed a two-and-a-half-year contract with the club but won't take charge until the weekend, meaning that joint-assistant head coaches Keith Downing and Rob Kelly will be in the hot seat for today's clash.
The latter stages of 2014 proved to be difficult for West Ham and West Brom, with both ending the year with a defeat after tough clashes on Sunday afternoon. Today's hosts were beaten 2-1 by Arsenal, meaning that Sam Allardyce's side have now lost back-to-back Premier League games for the first time since the end of last season. However, the Hammers have much to smile about, as the first half of this season has been an excellent one for a revitalised and confident team that have looked full of attacking flair and defensive discipline on the pitch. As a result, they start 2015 in a very respectable sixth place in the table, equal on points with seventh-place Tottenham Hotspur and just two points behind both Arsenal and Southampton, who sit in fifth and fourth place, respectively.

(66’) Bentaleb trips up Willian and gets booked. Surprisingly, given the cutthroat intensity of this game, that stands as the first yellow card issued by referee Phil Dowd, who has kept a good handle on things.
(65’) Now its Tottenham's turn to look rattled, as they suddenly have lost all motor coordination in the centre of the park. Chelsea are taking control of the midfield, and the hosts just need to settle down.
(63’) Now then, Kane's second goal is looking all the more crucial for Spurs. They still have a two-goal cushion, but Chelsea displayed in no uncertain terms during that last goal that they can carve anyone apart at will.
--- 61’ Assist Assist by Fàbregas. ---
--- 61’ Goal! CHELSEA ARE BACK IN THIS! Oafish play from Fazio, who ran right into a wall of blue shirts, sparking the visitors on the break. And what a tremendous break it was, executed at warp speed. Fabregas advances down the left and slides in the onrushing Hazard, who continues his momentum perfectly to stab a finish into the far side! ---
(58’) Kane comes up with the goods at the other end, getting first to a Fabregas free kick to clear ahead of a sea of blue shirts. Chelsea haven't had a good attacking idea for a good while now.
(56’) Chelsea are rocked to the core. Mourinho looks ready to wield his machete at full time. After such a promising start from his team, they have completely collapsed here!
(54’) Harry Kane hat-trick? Harry Kane for England? Anything seems possible for the striker at the moment here at White Hart Lane. He's now notched 17 goals in all competitions for Spurs this season.
--- 52’ Assist The assist came from N. Chadli. ---
--- 52’ Goal! INSANITY! SPURS ARE 4-1 UP! Another peach from Kane, who takes an otherworldly first touch to turn away from his man inside the box, freeing him to slide a finish into the bottom corner! Excellent goal! ---
(50’) End-to-end stuff at the moment as Cahill needs to step in to prevent Eriksen from advancing clean on goal. This second half has gotten off to a wonderful start. Both sides are fully up for this!
(48’) Chadli is quite happy to run at the defence all game long. He advances down the left but can't pick out the right cross into the area. Spurs are hungry for a fourth in the opening exchanges here!
--- 46’ Substitution Oscar is replaced with Ramires. ---
(46’) Here we go again!
Daniel Levy couldn't have cooked up a better start to 2015 for Spurs in a laboratory. This has been a stirring performance from the men in white, who shook off an early opener to respond with three goals, all of them deserved. White Hart Lane is rocking, but can they close out the job in the second half? Mourinho stormed straight into the dressing room after that penalty - he and his team have to put in some real work now, starting with what looks to be a dressing down at half-time. I'll be back with the second half in just a bit.
--- 45’ +4 Goal! NO MISTAKE FROM TOWNSEND! He places a penalty perfectly into the bottom corner. Courtois guessed perfectly well, but couldn't stretch enough to keep it out! ---
(45’) SPURS PENALTY! Kane was simply too quick for Cahill, nipping in ahead of the defender, who trod on his toes just inside the box. Now then, can the hosts go 3-1 up here?
(45’) Stirring comeback here from Spurs, but there's some trouble for the hero of the moment as Rose is being attended to by the physios. He's had a history of some vital goals in London derbies. Just ask Arsenal.
--- 44’ Goal! TOTTENHAM HAVE TAKEN THE LEAD! In a mirror image of the previous attack, except from the opposite side, Chadli steals through two defenders but his deft finish rebounds off the post. However, Rose is on hand to guide the rebound home! ---
(42’) Chadli squeezes in between two defenders and slides a finish through Courtois, only to see it rebound off the post. The flag is up, correctly, as the Belgian was an inch offside, but another warning shot for Chelsea.
(40’) Willian's shot takes the most awkward of deflections, and Hazard nearly latches onto it perfectly, but he can only head wide. A disappointing end there as Lloris was completely guessing.
(38’) Chelsea have been finding a lot of joy down the right flank. Almost everyone in blue has had a taste down that side. Ivanovic is the latest to get involved, but he's thwarted right on the byline by a splendid Dembele tackle.
(36’) Such an entertaining game of football, this. Both teams are fighting tooth and nail, and there's been generous helpings of quality all over the field. At this point it's impossible to call a winner.
(34’) Eriksen's corner gets a flick on at the near post, and Kane tries to hustle Terry into a mistake. However, the linesman flags for a foul as the striker went in too eagerly on a man 13 years his senior.
(32’) Renewed belief around White Hart Lane and that's an understatement. Chelsea looked to have a few more goals in them before the break but that moment of genius from Kane has put the cat right back amongst the pigeons.
--- 30’ Assist The assist came from D. Rose. ---
--- 30’ Goal! TOTTENHAM ARE LEVEL! A superb solo goal for Kane, who drives around the edge of the box, waiting for the exact moment to strike. He picks his spot excellently and fires a 25-yarder into the bottom corner! ---
(28’) Battle here between Hazard and Vertonghen as the former takes offense at a challenge from the latter. Chelsea's Belgian star has been tormenting the Spurs defence throughout this game!
(26’) Oscar is the latest player to have hurt himself in an attacking move. However, it doesn't seem serious enough to have him depart this match. And why would he, he's been on fire in this game!
(24’) SO CLOSE TO A SECOND! Oscar takes a page out of Hazard's book and goes on a sweeping run down the right-hand side. He squares to Costa inside the box, but his attempt to steer a finish home goes wide of the far post.
(22’) Nope, all is well with the world as the striker moves freely to aim a shove in the direction of Vertonghen.
(21’) Costa pulls up from that last move limping, and his hamstring looks to be in some distress.
(20’) Another magnificent ball from Fabregas puts Costa on the chase against a defender. However, the striker is clunky and can't maneuver past Fazio, who stands his ground well to block.
--- 18’ Assist Oscar provided the assist. ---
--- 18’ Goal! Chadli, ever the outlet for Spurs in the opening exchanges, attempts an overhead kick on short notice inside the box, but Courtois positions himself well at the near post to save. The rebound could have fallen anywhere but thankfully from Chelsea's perspective, it spilled to a blue shirt first. ---
(18’) CHELSEA LEAD! It's Costa who scores but all the praise must go to Hazard. The Belgian embarks on a mazy run that takes him past two players. He slides a finish to the far side, it rebounds off the base of the post and Oscar's attempted follow up is turned in by a barely onside Costa at the post!
(17’) It's turning into a real slog in midfield at the moment. Spurs are sitting deep, well aware of the threat of Costa and Hazard when they get space, with Fabregas pulling the strings in behind. So far, they've done well in rattling the visitors into a few poor passes in the final third.
(15’) For some reason Dembele needs a good three minutes to get prepped to come on and by the time his number is called, he still needs to rush to fit his shinpads and socks. The Belgian jogs on for the sadly departed Mason and Spurs have restored numerical parity.
--- 14’ Substitution M. Dembélé enters play, replacing R. Mason. ---
(13’) Oof. Mason has pulled up here clutching his hammy and you don't need me to tell you what that usually means. Mauricio Pochettino is already looking to his bench but for now, Spurs play on with 10 men.
(11’) Costa collects Oscar's pass at the top of the box and, facing a white wall of four players, attempts to bend one towards goal. It strikes Vertonghen and there are some appeals for handball. Replays show that the ball did strike the Belgian's forearms, but he made every attempt to keep his hands close to his body. Good call from the referee to allow play to go on.
(9’) It was so nearly a classic Chelsea goal. Fabregas spots that inch-perfect run from Costa and attempts to put a long ball on a platter for him. Stealing between two defenders, the striker stretches every sinew but he just can't bring that pass under his control!
(7’) A really swift buildup from Spurs has Chelsea guessing in midfield. Chadli is too quick for Fabregas and that burst of pace allows him to steal into a shooting position at the top of the box. He lashes one on goal, but it's a little too close to Courtois, who smothers confidently.
(5’) The fans are in full voice here for derby day. White Hart Lane is rocking as Spurs manage to orchestrate a few promising passing sequences in the opposition half. Kane is blocked from a threatening shooting position.
(3’) Chelsea are bossing the ball in the early exchanges, though a weak attempt at a cross from Costa halts a promising move in its' tracks. It will be interesting to see if the Spaniard continues to pull wide in this game, opening up space for Hazard and Co. centrally.
(1’) We're off!
Drogba will ride the bench for now, with Diego Costa chosen to lead the line against Spurs. Mourinho has selected Willian and Oscar to return to his starting XI, with Andre Schurrle and John Obi Mikel taking a backseat. Cesar Azpilicueta also slots in at left-back in place of Filipe Luis.
Harry Kane continues his line-leading exploits for the home side, while the trio of Kyle Walker, Danny Rose and Nabil Bentaleb have all been recalled to the Spurs XI, the only three changes after Tottenham's 0-0 draw against Manchester United last time out.
Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Ivanovic, Cahill, Terry, Azpilicueta; Matic, Fabregas; Willian, Oscar, Hazard; Costa.
Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Walker, Fazio, Vertonghen, Rose; Bentaleb, Mason; Chadli, Eriksen, Townsend; Kane.
Recent history in this fixture favours Tottenham. Tonight's hosts have lost only one of their last eight against Chelsea - the aforementioned 3-0 at the Bridge. In fact, Jose Mourinho has not won in his last two trips to White Hart Lane - though Didier Drogba has registered nine combined goals and assists in as many matches against the north Londoners.
Spurs have seen a recent upturn in their fortunes. Since Chelsea spanked them 3-0 at Stamford Bridge last month, the north London club have taken 11 points from 15 on offer in the league. Fifth place and a two-point gap on the top four beckons should they do the business here - which will also take them one spot above rivals Arsenal, who lost to Southampton today.
Chelsea have only failed to take maximum points from five league games this season - but those slip ups have all occured on the road. Four draws and one loss away from the Bridge has seen Manchester City creep up to level their 46-point tally - though this match marks the Blues' game in hand, one which they surely need to win to keep challengers at arm's length.
Happy New Year to you all. Let's get 2015 off on the right foot with our live coverage of a tasty Premier League clash between Tottenham and Chelsea from White Hart Lane. The league leaders have seen their gap at the top diminish in recent weeks, while Spurs have been tipping in and out of the Europa League places. I'm Keeghann Sinanan, your guide for all the action.

That is all we have time for today, though. Thanks a lot for joining me, Tom Webber, and have a great afternoon!
Spurs temporarily move above Arsenal and into sixth position, but the Gunners have a game in hand. United remain third, but the gap between them and second-placed Manchester City could widen if the Citizens defeat Burnely later today.
FULL TIME - Tottenham 0-0 Man United: Both sides retain their current unbeaten records, though Van Gaal may feel his side could have secured the win given their numerous first-half chances. The second half failed to live up to the entertainment provided by the first, as Spurs came into the game more but they ultimately both laboured to the final whistle.
(90’) There is the final whistle!
(90’) Young, who has been less involved in the second half, wastes an opportunity to create a late chance for his side by sending a cross straight out for a goal kick.
(90’) There will be three minutes of additional time at the end of this half.
(90’) Stambouli does well to break towards the byline before spinning back and teeing up Chiriches for a cross. The Romanian pings in a cross which is too high for Kane to attack! Time is running out for both teams!
(89’) Falcao charges down Fazio's attempted clearance but uses his hand to block it! United looked eager to capitalise on that, but the referee quickly pulled play back for a free kick to the hosts.
(87’) Eriksen's free kick is cleared by Rooney, but the Dane pops up on the right to put another cross into the box. Fazio is again the man on the end of it but he fails to hit the target!
--- 86’ Yellow card Rafael is cautioned by the referee. ---
(86’) Another free kick and another yellow card for United! Eriksen lets the ball roll across him and it draws Rafael in from behind with a clumsy challenge. Spurs are really putting the pressure on!
(85’) Eriksen flights the free kick in from deep on the right and Fazio meets it with his head, but he sends the ball high over the top. He claims to the referee that he was being held by Smalling.
--- 84’ Yellow card R. Falcao is cautioned by the referee. ---
(84’) Falcao goes into the book after a trip on Lamela as the pair chased a loose ball out on the right. It seemed accidental, but the referee clearly didn't view it that way.
(82’) MASON! The youngster misses a great opportunity to win it! Kane blocks Carrick's pass inside his own half and then races forward, holding onto the ball as he awaits support. He eventually spots his midfield team-mate surging up on the overlap and he puts him in behind with a great pass. Mason has the whole goal to aim at but blazes his shot over the top! What a chance!
(80’) It appears that United are still operating with three at the back, with Shaw playing on the left side of the trio and Smalling in the centre. Young remains at the left wing-back position.
--- 79’ Substitution E. Lamela enters the game and replaces N. Chadli. ---
--- 79’ Substitution M. Dembélé enters play, replacing A. Townsend. ---
(79’) Two changes from Pochettino now, with Erik Lamela and Moussa Dembele coming on for Chadli and Townsend.
(78’) ERIKSEN! The Dane whips the free kick over the wall with pace and it calls De Gea into action. He doesn't quite pick out the corner, though, so the keeper has a relatively simple save to make, parrying the shot aside.
(77’) Mata controls a looping ball out from the United penalty area but he loses his footing and Eriksen steals in. The Spaniard ends up pulling his opponent down with him, and Spurs win a free kick in a dangerous area.
--- 76’ Substitution L. Shaw enters the game and replaces P. McNair. ---
(76’) Another change from Van Gaal, with McNair being replaced by Luke Shaw. Will United stick with three at the back now?
(75’) As we head into the final 15 minutes the game remains all square. Both sides look capable of breaking the deadlock, and De Gea has to dart off his line to stop Chadli doing that from Chiriches' through-ball.
(73’) Van Gaal makes his second change of the game with Chris Smalling coming on to take the place of Evans.
--- 72’ Substitution C. Smalling comes on for J. Evans. ---
(72’) GOOD SAVE! De Gea gets down low to his left to make an important stop, keeping Fazio's efort out of the bottom corner. That looked to be sneaking in for the Argentine!
--- 71’ Yellow card P. McNair goes into the referee's book. ---
(71’) McNair earns a yellow card for catching Kane as the striker turned away from him 30 yards in goal. Spurs are awarded a free kick which Townsend flights into the box and Rooney heads it away.
(70’) Mata has been superb this afternoon, and he shows great speed of feet to get away from his marker in midfield and spread the play to Young on the left. The cross that comes in from the wing-back is deflected, though, and Stambouli clears with a header.
(68’) WHAT A MISS! United move the ball brilliantly from left to right, it culminates with Rafael rolling a bobbling cross into the box that Mata completely skies! The Spaniard didn't need to put so much power behind that.
(66’) TOWNSEND! Spurs are stepping up their high press now, and United are finding it difficult to get the ball clear of their half. Eventually the winger picks up possession and darts between Jones and Rooney. He finds himself in space so rifles an effort at goal from 25 yards which De Gea is equal to.
(64’) The second half has not had the same degree of openness that the first 45 minutes had, with neither team fully committing to opening the scoring. If it remains this delicately balanced then we can expect things to get more stretched in the final stages.
(62’) Woeful from Evans. The centre-back attempts to switch the play from left to right but miscues and kicks the ball out of play for a throw on the halfway line.
(61’) Davies absolutely flattens Falcao as the Colombian spins him to latch onto a throw. The striker stays down on the deck but the referee doesn't seem too interested and simply awards the free kick before moving on.
(60’) Van Persie and Vertonghen, who have been having a strong physical battle all afternoon, clash down near the corner. The Dutchman went in late but somehow avoids a yellow card that would keep him out of United's next game.
(58’) A long throw down the right drops for Van Persie beyond the back line. He stumbles as he tries to get a cross in and Lloris has the simple task of picking it up unopposed inside the six-yard box.
(57’) STAT: The Red Devils have won just two of their last 10 games on the road in the Premier League, losing three.
(55’) WHAT A CHANCE! Carrick releases Mata down the right with a brilliant pass, and the Spaniard spins to meet it at the byline. He centres the ball and Van Persie connects with a volley that sails over the top of the goal! He was leaning back as he connected there and could not test Lloris.
(53’) Claims for a penalty! The corner comes into Kane at the near post and his touch takes it away from McNair, who appears to catch the striker. However, the Spurs man is soon back to his feet to set up Eriksen who has a shot that pinballs around the box before being cleared.
(52’) Stambouli feeds Kane just inside the right-hand side of the box. He gets his head up and squares the cross into the centre, where Fazio attacks it. The centre-back cannot divert it on target, with the officials deeming Jones to have got the last touch.
--- 50’ Yellow card A. Young goes into the referee's book. ---
(50’) The hosts look to break and as Chadli knocks the ball away from Young he is caught by the wing-back, who earns a booking for the challenge.
(50’) Rafael pushes up for the first time this afternoon and attempts to whip a cross into the box which is diverted behind for a corner. Mata's delivery from the right is aimed towards Carrick, but a touch off the Spurs defence sends it out for another corner on the opposite side. This time Rooney delivers, but Lloris is off his line to claim it unchallenged.
(48’) United are retaining the ball in the opening stages, clearly not wanting Spurs to get into possession and build upon their first-half performance.
--- 46’ Substitution A. Valencia is replaced with Rafael. ---
(46’) We are back underway!
Welcome back! The second half is just a few moments away, and Rafael will be coming on to replace Valencia for the remainder with the Ecuadorian picking up a knock.
HALF TIME - Tottenham 0-0 Man United: The visitors have had the best of the chances, but it remains goalless at the interval. Pochettino will want more from his side after the break, though they have by no means been poor. It's been an exciting opening 45 minutes, and we should be set for another thrilling half shortly! Be sure to stick around.
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) There is to be just one minute of added time.
(45’) UNBELIEVABLE KEEPING! Young picks up the ball on the left and shifts it onto his right boot before curling a brilliant effort towards the top corner by the far post. Lloris shuffles to his left before leaping high into the air and clawing the effort around the post! A truly stunning stop from the France international, as that was heading in!
(44’) Townsend whips a free kick in from out on the right, and it looks to be swinging inside the far post. Kane fails to get a touch on the ball to guide it on target, though, and it bounces outside of the upright.
(43’) ROONEY! Young stands a great cross up on the penalty spot from the left, and his team-mate makes a late run into the box to connect with it. He sends his header down into the ground but it lacks the pace to beat Lloris, who dives to his left and holds it.
(42’) There are just a few minutes remaining until the interval, and Pochettino will be pleased if his side get their goalless given the number of chances United have had. Some more direction for the hosts could see them pose more of a threat in the second half.
(40’) WHAT A SAVE! Jones angles a fantastic ball up from the back and Van Persie controls it exquisitely in behind the defence. Lloris stays on his line though, allowing the Dutchman to take another touch to get it on his right foot. Only then does the keeper move, and he does enough to block the shot from the edge of the six-yard box and then recover to pluck the loose ball down from the sky!
(38’) Davies surges up from the back, darting beyond Mata before pulling the trigger from 25 yards. His shot flies across goal but keeps on going, bouncing wide of the far post. He would have needed something special to beat De Gea from there.
(36’) It's a delicately poised afternoon at White Hart Lane, which has provided for an intriguing, exciting game. There are still no goals but chances have been plentiful. United have perhaps shaved the first period so far, though.
(34’) FALCAO! Another chance goes begging for the Colombian, who is released down the left by another brilliant pass from Mata. He cuts inside of Fazio and attempts to bend a shot inside the far post with his right foot. He aims it close to Lloris and the keeper dives to his left to hold it at the first time of asking.
(33’) Spurs win another free kick out on the left and again Eriksen's delivery is disappointing. He sends it low to the near post, where Van Persie is back to hook it straight back out of the area. The hosts are enjoying more of possession now, though.
(31’) After that flurry of chances the tempo of the game has slowed in the past few minutes. The hosts are looking to find Kane in the box with crosses from the flanks, but the United defence are coming out on top more often than not.
(29’) STAT: United have not lost in their last 13 trips to White Hart Lane, winning eight.
--- 27’ Yellow card A. Townsend is yellow-carded. ---
(27’) Townsend is the next in the book for Spurs, and it is a rather cheap one for the winger.
--- 26’ Yellow card B. Stambouli is cautioned by the referee. ---
(26’) The game has really stepped up a gear in the last 10 minutes or so, with United certainly putting more of the pressure on. Stambouli puts a late tackle in on Carrick but the referee plays the advantage. Nothing comes of it for the visitors and Spurs break, with De Gea having to rush off his line to deny Mason a chane in a one-on-one. The referee then goes back to book the hosts' midfielder for his earlier challenge.
(24’) SO CLOSE! Another chance for United as Jones' header beats Lloris before being hooked off the line by Vertonghen. The visiting players appeal, but their hopes are dashed as play is pulled back for an offside decision against the England international. It was a brilliant spot from the official on the far side!
(22’) OFF THE POST! Van Persie wins a free kick 20 yards out from goal, and Mata and Rooney stand over it. The Spaniard is the man who takes it, though, and his effort takes a touch off the wall before coming back off the post. Davies deflects it back towards Lloris and Van Persie attempts to pounce, but somehow Chiriches manages to get it away before it ends in disaster for his side!
(21’) GOOD SAVE! Again Townsend receives the ball out on the right and this time, rather than cross, he goes for goal. His left-footed effort takes a deflection and fizzes towards the corner, but De Gea gets down to keep it out.
(20’) Kane is unable to divert a cross from the left on target, but his header drops to Townsend on the far side of the box. He twists and turns before dropping a fantastic pass in front of De Gea, which the Spurs striker just misses out on connecting with!
(19’) FALCAO! The Colombian has to do better in those situations! Mata is found in space in the centre of the Spurs half and he slides a great pass down the channel for Falcao. He takes a touch and lets the ball roll across to his left foot, which he uses to send a tame shot which Lloris holds comfortably.
(18’) Both the United wing-backs are pushing up high and offering plenty of width to their attacks. The ball is switched out to Young on the left again, but once more his delivery does not result in a chance to call Lloris into action.
(16’) Falcao falls to ground holding his face after a coming together with Vertonghen. The defender certainly caught the Colombian with a flailing arm but it hardly warranted such a theatrical reaction!
(15’) Pocchetino is not happy with that! Fazio tries to clip a long diagonal pass out to Chadli on the left but instead contrives to send it behind, far away from the Belgian!
(14’) Davies looks to cut inside from an advanced left position again, and he is brought to ground by Jones. Eriksen delivers it onto the penalty spot but Rooney is there to head clear. Not the best set piece from the Dane, there.
(12’) Davies comes inside from the left and flights a great cross towards the back post. There's slightly too much on it for Kane to make a run to get on the end of it, though, and it only results in a goal kick to the Red Devils.
(11’) United keep the pressure on the hosts by winning a corner after putting the ball back into play. Rooney's corner is headed away at the near post, though, and when he drops back to pick up the ball again his reverse pass to Mata was deemed illegal with the former Chelsea man in an offside position.
(10’) Vertonghen is deemed to be too physical with Mata out on the Spurs left, so the referee awards the visitors a free kick. The Spaniard clips it towards the back post where Lloris comes off his line to punch clear, conceding a throw in.
(8’) Mata launches a fantastic pass from inside his own half which Rooney springs the offside trap to latch onto. His touch lets him down somewhat, though, as he leaves the ball behind him at the top of the box. It allows the opposition defence to recover so he squares to Falcao, but the Colombian cannot create space to worry Lloris.
(7’) Kane does well to get win the ball from Rooney before spinning away from McNair, after initially being tackled by the centre-back. He then threads a pass behind the defence for Mason, but Jones gets just enough on it to stop the midfielder from converting.
(5’) Falcao releases Young by sliding a pass out to the left and he then surges towards the box. The wing-back cuts a ball back towards him at the top of the area which is intercepted by Mason.
(3’) The Red Devils look to break down the right but the eventual cross into the box runs all the way through to Young on the far side. He attempts to flight a cross beyond Chiriches, but the ball ricochets back off him and goes out for a goal kick.
(2’) Spurs have played some nice passing football in the opening moments, and Chadli then looks to open up the pitch by sending a pass down to the right corner for Townsend to chase. The winger stands up Evans and heads towards the top of the box where he stands a cross up for the Belgian, who continued his run, at the back post. He fails to generate enough power on the header and and United clear.
(1’) We are underway at White Hart Lane as United get the ball rolling!
There is a minute of applause beforehand for Ron Henry, the former Tottenham and England defender who has died, aged 80.
There are just five minutes to go until kick off in the first of the final round of Premier League fixtures of 2014. The teams are out on the field, so stick around for what is set to be an intriguing match!
That means Wayne Rooney once again operates in a central midfield role. Despite his change in position the England international is still managing to score, with 11 goals in his last 13 games for club and country. Louis van Gaal has decided to name the same XI that began the 3-1 win over Newcastle United just less than 48 hours ago, so it will be interesting to see how that impacts his team today. There aren't many options on the bench, which may have something to do with it, so tiredness could become an issue for them in the latter stages.
Tottenham unbeaten in their last four meetings with United, and if they are to maintain that record today they will need Harry Kane to continue his recent form. Ryan Mason is back in the starting line-up with Nabil Bentaleb out due to illness and Erik Lamela drops to the bench to make way for Andros Townsend.
After difficult starts to the season for both clubs, they have finally been gathering form and looking more like teams that could challenge for European competition come May. Today represents a real a test for the two teams. Spurs could move into fourth with a win, which would give them confidence going into the second half of the season. United, meanwhile, will want to keep pace with Manchester City and Chelsea, both of which sit above them.
Hello and welcome to today's LIVE commentary on this meeting between two of the Premier League's form sides as Tottenham Hotspur welcome Manchester United to White Hart Lane. FULL TIME! Southampton and Chelsea draw at St. Mary's, with the league leaders unable to break the resilience of Koeman's side! Mane's opening goal was cancelled out by Hazard, but second-half dominance couldn't be translated into more goals and three points for the Blues! The hosts hang on for a valuable point and that's good news for Man City fans! That's all that we have time for, I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again next time.
--- 90’ +5 Yellow card G. Pellè is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) Mane goes down under a challenge from Fabregas, with the referee not buying the goalscorer's theatrics. Long then breaks away down the left-hand side, with the former Salzburg man given the task of shielding the ball up near the corner flag.
(90’) Ivanovic floats in a cross from the right-hand side, which Fonte manages to clear into Wanyama's midriff. Fortunately for the Saints, the ball rebounds into the grateful arms of Forster.
(90’) We're into the first of four minutes of stoppage time at St. Mary's! Chelsea are looking for the winning goal that would keep them three points ahead of Man City. Drogba can't quite slide in at the near post to apply a finish to another Hazard cross.
(90’) Half chance for Drogba! Hazard flashes a cross in from the right-hand side, which the former Galatasaray striker fails to turn home with a cheeky backheel. It's all hands to the pump for Southampton, with Chelsea continuing to pile forward. Filipe Luis is denied by a good block.
--- 89’ Substitution L. Rémy comes on for Diego Costa. ---
--- 88’ Red card! RED CARD! Schneiderlin walks! Hazard concedes another corner, with the home fans really getting behind their side in the dying stages. Drogba is present to hammer a clearance away at the back post, before Chelsea break. As Fabregas looks to race into the Saints' half, the Frenchman makes a cynical tackle to earn his second yellow card of the afternoon. ---
(86’) A back-post delivery is looped in by Ward-Prowse, with Terry half-clearing with a header. Alderweireld takes a first touch to set himself, before volleying a powerful effort high and wide of the target. You have to admire his optimism!
(85’) Diego Costa is constantly playing on the last man, but the final ball is yet to be weighted as such that the Spain international can race in on goal and find the winner. Southampton finally break out of the Chelsea siege and earn themselves a corner.
(83’) Defending is becoming more and more last-ditch for the hosts, with plenty of red and white shirts surrounding the edge of the penalty area. Anywhere will do in terms of clearances, as Chelsea continue to be continually frustrated by the Saints' dense lines.
(81’) Drogba wins a corner from Gardos, allowing Chelsea to load the penalty area with bodies. Two deliveries are headed clear within moments of one another, but Chelsea recycle possession. Ivanovic tries to clip a cross back from the left byline, but Alderweireld gets a vital touch to deny Costa.
(79’) Diego Costa is nearly found by a pass from deep by Fabregas, but Forster is alert to the danger and comes off his line to smother the ball. The Southampton goalkeeper has been worried far more often in the second half, with Courtois presumably getting slightly bored.
--- 77’ Substitution S. Long enters play, replacing S. Davis. ---
(77’) Huge chance for Chelsea! An awful pass back from Ward-Prowse is intercepted by Diego Costa, before the Spaniard drives into the box and sets his sights. Just as he looked to shoot, however, the striker lost his footing and the opportunity dissipated. Moments later, Filipe Luis delivers a cross from the left, but Forster punches clear ahead of Drogba.
(76’) Drogba is involved straight away for Chelsea, but the substitute's second touch is a terrible attempted through ball which is intercepted easily by Wanyama. Southampton are maintaining their shape well, as Fonte is the next to deny a Drogba pass, as the Ivory Coast international looked unselfishly for Diego Costa.
--- 74’ Substitution J. Obi Mikel is replaced with D. Drogba. ---
(74’) Ivanovic unleashes a long-range effort, but his shot sails harmlessly high and wide of the target. Drogba is now introduced for Mikel, with the visitors switching to two up top. Fabregas is now asked to sit back slightly to partner Matic in central midfield.
(73’) All of the away side's play continues to come down the left-hand side, with Willian having no impact as of yet. Mourinho appears willing to continue to exploit the fact that Southampton have no orthodox right-back on the field. Drogba readies himself on the sideline, meanwhile.
--- 72’ Yellow card M. Schneiderlin is yellow-carded. ---
(71’) Chelsea only have 20 minutes left to translate their dominance into goals, with Koeman's system continuing to frustrate the Blues. Fabregas and Hazard are growing influences, who may have more opportunity to pull the strings when the Saints' midfield begins to tire somewhat.
(69’) The home side finally manage to break upfield for some brief respite, escaping from the Chelsea siege of the second half. Davis slides a pass through to Mane, who controls inside the opposition penalty area, but the Senegalese can't sort his feet out and is tackled.
(67’) Diego Costa and Hazard combine once again, but Southampton are holding their shape well and eliminating any opportunities to shoot from in and around the box. Fabregas then drives down the right and gets to the byline, but slips over as he attempts to centre a cross.
(66’) Fabregas curls a cross in from the right-hand side, but the hosts manage to clear at the second attempt. Chelsea are streaming forward and seeing all of the second-half possession, but the Saints are holding firm. There is a sense of inevitability that Mourinho's men will create some clear chances before the 90 minutes are up.
(64’) Hazard and Filipe Luis continue to combine well down the left-hand side. Diego Costa manages to wriggle free into a small pocket of space, before lining up a right-footed effort inside the box, but a combination of Fonte and Gardos makes an important block.
--- 62’ Substitution F. Gardoş enters play, replacing M. Yoshida. ---
(62’) Given his recent yellow card and Hazard's growing influence in the game, Yoshida is the next man to be withdrawn by Koeman. Gardos replaces the Japanese defender, with Alderweireld sliding over to the right-hand side of the back four.
(60’) Hazard flashes an effort wide! Fabregas scoops a delicate ball into his teammate, who controls before swivelling smartly to hook a shot goalward from 12 yards! Forster watches the ball zip off the turf and beyond the far upright.
--- 58’ Substitution D. Tadić is done for the day. J. Ward-Prowse is his replacement. ---
(58’) Yoshida picks up a yellow card for a clumsy hack at Hazard's heels, leaving the Japan international in a spot of bother in terms of committing future tackles. Koeman opts to make his first change of the game, with Ward-Prowse continuing his return from injury by replacing Tadic.
--- 57’ Yellow card M. Yoshida goes into the referee's book. ---
(56’) Fabregas goes down in the penalty area under pressure from Targett, though it appeared to be fairly innocuous from the youngster. The former Barcelona man, however, is absolutely apoplectic that he didn't get a penalty. His frustration shows, as the Spaniard kicks the ball away moments later, but the referee doesn't spot it.
--- 55’ Yellow card Fàbregas receives a yellow card. ---
(55’) Matic steps out to break up play, before feeding Hazard. The Belgian cuts a pass back for Willian to attack, but the Brazilian is quickly robbed of the ball on the edge of the area. Southampton remain very compact on the periphery of their 18-yard box.
(53’) Targett feeds Tadic down the left-hand side, before the former Groningen man whips in a cross. Mane allows it to flash beyond him, with Terry able to mop up the pieces and clear. A few half chances have been forthcoming, but clear-cut ones remain very, very elusive.
(51’) Fabregas is clipped by Wanyama when 25 yards from goal, earning Chelsea a free kick in a dangerous area. The Spaniard dusts himself down before whipping it in himself, but Fonte is able to send a header looping into the air which Forster catches easily.
(49’) Diego Costa switches play from left to right, picking out Ivanovic, but the Serbia international chops inside Tadic before fouling Targett. The away side have started the second half well and look composed on the ball.
(47’) Mourinho opts to make one change at the break, with Schurrle being replaced by Willian for the away side. After not having much of an impact on proceedings, the Germany international can't feel aggrieved to be replaced.
--- 46’ Substitution Willian comes on for A. Schürrle. ---
(46’) We are back underway in the second half at St. Mary's! The scoreline is level, with this game something of a hard-fought and tight contest between two very well-organised sides. This one could go either way!
HALF TIME! All square at the break in St. Mary's with the league leaders clawing their way back into the contest at the very death. Mane gave the hosts an early lead, which they defended fantastically until stoppage time, before Hazard burst inside to net an equaliser. Mourinho's men face a real test of their title mettle this afternoon, so be sure to stick with us for all of the second-half action!
--- 45’ +1 Assist Assist by Fàbregas. ---
--- 45’ +1 Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! BRILLIANT EQUALISER FROM HAZARD! The Belgium international is fed down the channel by a fantastic ball in behind, before chopping inside two challenges and firing a low finish into the bottom-right corner! Great individual goal! ---
(44’) Pelle fires wide! The home side work the ball well from left to right, before Yoshida battles his way across the face of the box. The ball bobbles loose, falling to his Italian teammate, but Pelle can only turn a shot on the turn way beyond the far upright!
(42’) Filipe Luis tries to make inroads down the left-hand side, but Davis comes across well to rob the Brazilian of possession and earn some applause from the home fans. It's hard to criticise Southampton's approach and collective commitment.
(40’) Forster remains untested, with Chelsea not being afforded the space to unleash efforts from range. Drogba is sent out to warm up on the sidelines, a possible sign that Mourinho is looking to change things at the break, perhaps?
(38’) Despite the break rapidly approaching, Chelsea aren't looking likely to find an equaliser before heading back to their dressing room. Costa is being kept quiet, with the Saints continuing to press well and prevent any joy in the wide areas. Koeman has his side set up excellently.
(36’) Less than 10 minutes remain until the break, with Chelsea's dominance waning somewhat. The Saints have seen much more of the ball in the last 10 minutes, with Schneiderlin and Wanyama able to control the centre of the park. Fabregas just isn't being given the space to manipulate the opposition defence.
(34’) Davis releases Tadic down the left-hand side, before Targett is able to overlap and take over, but Schurrle tracks back well yet again to snuff out a Saints' break. The home side are looking comfortable, with their counter attacks continuing to look very threatening.
(32’) Mane drives down the right-hand side, before earning a cheap free kick from the presence of Hazard. Tadic delivers, but curls the ball directly out of play for a goal kick - not exactly what the home fans were hoping for at all.
--- 31’ Yellow card N. Matić is cautioned by the referee. ---
(30’) Ivanovic wins a free kick from Tadic on the right-hand side, but Fabregas's delivery is headed clear. Chelsea recycle possession, but are unable to create any chances on the edge of what is a very congested final third. The Saints are staying compact.
(28’) Fabregas continues to look like the main source of inspiration for Chelsea, but the hosts are holding their shape well and remaining very tough to play through. Hazard has occasionally been able to isolate Yoshida on the left flank, but Southampton are defending well.
(26’) Chelsea continue to see more of the ball and dominate play, with Southampton are more than happy to sit back slightly before constricting space well. Pelle hasn't seen a great deal of the ball, but Tadic always has the ability to pick out the runs from deep by Mane.
(24’) Pelle backs into Terry, earning Chelsea a free kick, with the Italy international in something of disbelief. Fabregas ghosts in from the left-hand side with a lovely piece of skill, before clipping a pass across goal with the aid of a deflection, but Schurrle is unable to steer home the looping ball at the back post.
(23’) The Saints are working hard to close down in packs and shut down passing lanes, with Chelsea really struggling to make inroads. Fabregas hasn't had opportunity to pull the strings, with Koeman's set-up looking to have Mourinho's men stumped for the time being. A bit of quality is required to create something from nothing.
(21’) Hazard whips in a cross from the left-hand side, but Alderweireld gets in ahead of Costa to make a headed clearance which concedes a corner. The set piece is dealt with easily, with Mane breaking as a result, but Schurrle tracks back brilliantly to deny the goalscorer a chance to grab his second of the afternoon.
(20’) Schneiderlin unleashes an ambitious effort from all of 35 yards, but the ball dips some way wide of the target. The home crowd are in buoyant spirits, with their side looking easily able to compete with this strong Chelsea team. Diego Costa has barely touched the ball around the penalty area. The Spain international does manage to cut back a cross after outmuscling Fonte, but a clearance is made.
(19’) Hazard holds onto the ball well under pressure from Wanyama, before setting a pass back to Fabregas. The Spaniard finds Ivanovic in space, but the Serbia international is tackled well by Targett and the home side break again. Koeman's men have been combative and look a real threat on the counter.
--- 17’ Assist Assist by D. Tadić. ---
--- 17’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! MANE GIVES THE SAINTS THE LEAD! The Senegalese forward is fed in behind Terry, following a brilliant pass from Tadic. With Courtois racing off his line, the Southampton forward lifts a measured finish over the gangly goalkeeper and into the back of the net! An upset is on the cards! ---
(16’) Good interception from Cahill! Matic is robbed of the ball in the centre of the field by Tadic, before the Serbia international attempts to slide a pass into the path of Mane. The former Bolton defender stretches every sinew to ensure that the ball is knocked out wide towards Filipe Luis.
(14’) Mane is found on the right-hand side, but Terry comes across well to make a sliding challenge. After the throw in is taken, the former Salzburg man then manages to win a corner from Filipe Luis. The set piece is swung in, before being squared back across goal, but Terry slides in well to deny Fonte! Alert defending from the travelling captain!
(12’) Schurrle is fed in behind the lines, before trying to hook a clever finish over the onrushing figure of Forster, but the ball bobbles behind tamely for a goal kick. The league leaders are continuing to push on, with the Saints yet to worry Courtois whatsoever.
(10’) Terry goes down clutching his head, forcing the referee to halt play. The Englishman appeared to be caught by a stray arm from Pelle, but after some brief treatment the Chelsea captain is back to his feet. The home fans boo him from the field.
(9’) Close for Terry! The Chelsea captain is nearly found by a good corner delivery, but Forster gets the slightest of touches to divert the ball onto the top of his opponent's head, rather than his forehead. It loops clear of the penalty area, with the goalkeeper's intervention proving vital.
(8’) Diego Costa breaks into the penalty box, before hesitating as to whether to feed Hazard, before Fonte comes across well to hack behind for a corner. The delivery is swung in by Fabregas, who sees his cross rebound back out to him, before the Spaniard beats two men with some devilish footwork. His attempted cut back is cleared, however.
(6’) Filipe Luis slides a pass through Yoshida's legs for Hazard to chase, but Fonte mops up well to make a timely clearance. Chelsea are slowly creeping further into enemy territory, with Matic now ballooning a terrible effort high and wide on the turn, from a tight angle too.
(5’) Yoshida tries to clip a cross in towards Pelle at the back post, but Ivanovic does well to head clear instead. Mourinho's men continue to see more of the ball, but are yet to generate anything in the way of chances. Patient possession only, thus far.
(3’) The home side have looked to be direct in the opening few minutes, with Mane roaming freely in behind Pelle to try and use his pace to good effect. Chelsea aren't to be flustered, however, retaining the ball well and staying composed in possession.
(2’) Tadic shoots from 30 yards out, but sends an ambitious effort sailing way over Courtois' crossbar. Yoshida appears to be slotting in at right-back for the Saints, with Alderweireld taking to a more customary central role. Hazard may look to exploit the Japanese defender's inexperience in the position.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at St. Mary's! It's second against fourth in the Premier League's second kick off of the day, with the hosts keen to remain in the Champions League places, while Chelsea aim to widen the gap at the top.
Chelsea substitutes: Cech, Zouma, Ramires, Drogba, Remy, Willian, Azpilicueta.
Chelsea starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Ivanovic, Terry, Cahill, Filipe Luis; Mikel, Matic; Schurrle, Fabregas, Hazard; Diego Costa.
Southampton substitutes: Davis, Gardos, Long, Ward-Prowse, Isgrove, Reed, McCarthy.
Southampton starting line-up (4-3-3): Forster; Alderweireld, Fonte, Yoshida, Targett; Davis, Wanyama, Schneiderlin; Tadic, Pelle, Mane.
TEAM NEWS: Cesar Azpilicueta can only take a seat on the bench, as Branislav Ivanovic and Filipe Luis are Mourinho's preferred full-backs. John Obi Mikel partners Nemanja Matic in shielding the Chelsea back four, allowing for Cesc Fabregas to roam as a liberated playmaker. Andre Schurrle and Eden Hazard provide pace and trickery on the flanks, with Diego Costa leading the line.
TEAM NEWS: Ryan Bertrand is unavailable due to the terms of his loan deal from his parent club, meaning that young left-back Matt Targett slots into the back four. Toby Alderweireld is asked to ply his trade on the opposite flank in the absence of Nathaniel Clyne, while Steven Davis is deployed in midfield to provide some work rate and intensity. Dusan Tadic and Sadio Mane are the wide men, supporting the lone forward of Graziano Pelle.
I'm Simon Harrison and I will be keeping you up to date with proceedings from the south coast, as these two sides face off within 48 hours of their last outing. While it isn't ideal in terms of fatigue, this period offers real opportunity in terms of building momentum ahead of 2015. The visitors sit three points clear of second-place Manchester City, meaning that a win is required to keep the pressure on Manuel Pellegrini's side. Ronald Koeman, meanwhile, will target staying in the Champions League places.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of today's Premier League clash between Southampton and Chelsea, as two of the division's early front runners attempt to end the first half of the season in winning fashion. Jose Mourinho's men are on a fantastic run, but the Saints ended a poor stint with two consecutive victories in recent weeks, meaning that we should be in for some real entertainment at St. Mary's.

Sunderland, meanwhile, will see this as a missed opportunity, with a man advantage for so long and yet unable to put the ball into the back of the net, but certainly not for lack of trying. Thank you for joining us here for the match that ended in a 0-0 stalemate!
And that's the match! Aston Villa went down to ten men for the third time in their last four matches but did very well and nearly won the game regardless. The first half might have been dour but the action following the red card was often entertaining.
(90’) BENTEKE INTO THE SIDE NETTING! Pantilimon is completely caught out, throwing himself into Benteke and the ball after the striker sent a header from a cross towards goal. The header hits the side netting and Benteke can't believe it!
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card E. Giaccherini is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) A late, deep free-kick for Villa here, with the ball hoofed up to Benteke by Bacuna. He's watched closely by Brown so plays it to Hutton, who goes to Wiemann, as the side are forced deeper and deeper. Just one minute left now!
(90’) GUZAN SAVES WICKHAM'S SHOT! The forward gets the ball just outside of the box and tees up an effort that sails far too close to the keeper who makes the save! Two more minutes of injury time here - will it be enough to find a winner?!
--- 89’ Yellow card W. Brown receives a yellow card. ---
(89’) PANTILIMON SAVE! FROM ONE END TO THE OTHER! The tall goalkeeper is called into action after Weimann's shot was deflected and fell for Grealish! From the ensuing corner, Pantilimon twice comes out and fails to collect, but is let off the hook when Bacuna's cross is played directly out of bounds!
(88’) GOMEZ OFF THE POST! SO CLOSE FOR SUNDERLAND!!! It was all Buckley there, sending in a fantastic cross that was parried out for the midfielder to run onto and smack a shot off the woodwork!
(87’) O'SHEA MAKES A VITAL BLOCK ON BENTEKE! The target man took down Graelish's cross well in the box and as he went to shoot, the centre-back threw himself in the way!
(86’) Buckley gets the ball on the other flank and sends in a low cross that Vlaar hoofs out of his box. It's all Sunderland at the moment, with Giaccherini very involved in the buildup play that ends when Johnson gets the ball in an offside position.
(85’) Deep in Villa's half, Buckley tucks inside to get away from Cissokho, but Grealish races back to help his side and wins the ball. Soon it's with Johnson, who goes wide to Giaccherini, who's cross is knocked out of play by Okore.
(84’) O'Shea concedes a free-kick that his goalie collects easily when a high ball is lofted into the box. Time is running out here for the two sides to score but Villa have held their own well despite being down a man.
(83’) Sunderland huffing and puffing to find the opening goal here but Buckley's solid cross into Wickham isn't controlled well by the striker and he can't direct his effort onto target.
(82’) A late set-piece opportunity for Villa here that Bacuna whips into the box. Vlaar's header nearly goes out but Okore keeps it in play for the side to rebuild. Grealish has it now but loses out to Johnson who's racing foward.
(81’) Grealish spurs on a counter, leaving Cattermole in his wake with a crafty dribble and sending a very good ball into the box that Brown shuffles to hook out.
(80’) Vlaar, who's been involved in nearly everything this half, does well to keep Wickham from seeing the ball as it was heading back towards Guzan. Villa cannot get the ball out of their own area at the moment.
--- 78’ Substitution The frantic nature of the last 10 minutes or so has calmed somewhat now, as Vlaar sends a probing pass up to the right flank that no one can get to. Vergini comes off immediately after for Buckley. ---
(76’) Vlaar gets a powerful header off of the corner that forces Pantilimon into a fantastic diving save! This game is truly coming alive now, and though a series of corners comes to nothing, Grealish gets the ball again, sees his cross cleared, and Vlaar tries an audacious shot from 25 yards that goes well over the bar.
(75’) Grealish gets the ball in the box once again and does excellently to make it to the byline and send a fantastic ball across goal that leaves Pantilimon once again rooted and the defenders spawling to clear it!
(74’) Bacuna whips the ball into the box and it's cleared, but Villa get it back, Johnson commits yet another foul, and the home side take yet another free-kick. Grealish gets into the box and tries an audacious curling shot from a wide angle that leaves Pantilimon rooted and trickles wide of the far post!
--- 73’ Yellow card Cissokho relieves pressure for his side as he races forward and wins a free-kick when Johnson just pulls him down to prevent him from getting into the box. The winger is booked for that and Villa may not find a better opportunity to score all match! Bacuna is set to take this. ---
(71’) AND HOW DID THAT NOT GO IN?! Johnson slips the ball wide to Jones, who sends in a low cross that Guzan fails to collect. With the goal wide open and the ball pinging around the box, it eventually ends at the feet of Grealish who hooks it clear!
(70’) 20 minutes left to go here and though Sunderland have come awfully close at times, neither side has made the breakthrough. For the most part, Villa are defending wave after wave of crosses well, but Okore's clearances in particular look to be a weak spot for his side.
(69’) Lambert makes another change to his side, taking off the very disappointing Cleverley for the young Jack Grealish. The visitors, meanwhile, are dominating possession now as Giaccherini gets free on the right and fires in a cross that Hutton heads wide. The defender loses the ball to Jones soon after and breathes a sigh of relief as Johnson's very poor cross sails out of bounds.
--- 68’ Substitution J. Grealish enters the game and replaces T. Cleverley. ---
(68’) SOMEHOW THE VISITORS FAIL TO SCORE! It was really out of nothing - Cattermole takes a very poor shot from about 20 yards out that looks destined to trickle over the line, but Johnson races to keep it in play. He squares the ball which causes havoc in the box, with Wickham in particular shooting but seeing it go out for a corner!
(66’) Okore's heading once again nearly costing his side! That's the third time since coming on that he's played it directly to a man wearing blue. For him, luckily, Fletcher was offside - otherwise he would have raced into the box and been able to fire a shot without a defender remotely near him!
(65’) FLETCHER'S SHOT BLOCKED FOR A CORNER! Once again, Okore is called into action and his defensive header only finds his opponents in his own area. The number nine gets the ball and spins on the volley to shoot and it's cleared for a corner that calls Guzan into action after Johnson made some space to take the shot!
(63’) Jordi Gomez goes down just inside the box after Okore's header fails to clear the edge of his own area, but it's far too easily and no call is awarded to the visitors. Bacuna however fouls Jones with a slight shove moments later, near the centre-circle, and a foul is blown this time.
(62’) Ohh and there's nearly something for Sunderland! Vlaar tried to play a quick pass to Okore but severely underhit the ball, allowing Johnson to race in and steal it. The winger is unable to make it to the box and shoot, however, with the two centre-backs combining well to atone for the mistake and win it back for their side.
--- 61’ Substitution Another substitute from Lambert as Clark comes off for Okore just before Villa take a free-kick in the middle of the pitch. ---
(60’) Some excellent ball movement from Sunderland around the box, capitalizing on a very poor Bacuna pass out of the back to keep possession. They're unable to muster an opening to take a shot, though, and they have to play it all the way back to Guzan under some very heavy pressing.
(59’) Cissokho is down the wing but can't send in a cross, so he cuts it back for Cleverley to do so. The latter sends a looping ball in towards Benteke, but Brown is watching him closely and doesn't allow him to get close to it. The striker is furious with how physical the defender was but Atkinson has judged that to be a fair play.
--- 57’ Substitution Two substitutions make their way onto the pitch, with Giaccherini and Bacuna coming on for Larsson and N'Zogbia. The first substitute nearly makes an immediate impact, steering the side forward on the counter, but he hesitates in making a pass and Sanchez sneaks in to steal the ball. ---
--- 57’ Substitution L. Bacuna comes on for C. N'Zogbia. ---
--- 56’ Yellow card Cleverley is deep in hhis own box and heads out a cross, beginning a play that ends when the former Manchester United man is taken down by Cattermole, who's booked for his efforts. ---
(55’) Wickham is nearly through on goal all alone after a fantastic Johnson through ball but Vlaar makes a recovery run to cut out his shot at the last possible second! Absolutely vital interception from the captain!!
(54’) Villa have worked the ball down the right flank through N'Zogbia, send it back out wide to Hutton and whip a cross in for Weimann, who's header is weak and off-target. Still, signs of life for the home team!
(53’) Unfortunately for Villa, it comes to nothing, as the ball squared into the box takes a deflection, rises high, and is safely collected by Pantilimon. Lambert looks to be readying a substitute here.
(52’) Villa are picking their passes very carefully now, holding onto the ball but surely weary of spreading themselves too thin. They win a free-kick when a ball played down the wing hits Johnson's elbow. This is a fantastic opportunity for the home side!
(51’) Jones now gets the ball down the left and sends in another cross, but Vlaar is once again up to the challenge and sticks his boot out to send it clear. Unsurprisingly, the possession is all with the visitors now, and Sanchez nearly costs his side when he loses the ball deep but they press well to win it back and work it towards Sunderland's box.
(50’) Johnson whips in a cross into the box for Vlaar to head clear. The winger gets the ball again but loses it soon after, though his side collect it easily after N'Zogbia's terrible pass goes directly to the visitor's defence.
--- 49’ Red card! RED CARD!!! DELPH HAS BEEN SENT OFF! He slid in high with studs showing on Jordi Gomez just after the Sunderland man had gotten the ball from the throw-in. The players absolutely cannot believe it, and a yellow may have sufficed there, but it's yet another match where Villa are playing down a man and this can certainly give Sunderland the spark they need! ---
(47’) OHHH AND WEIMANN DRAGS THE BALL WIDE! A good spell from Villa and the number ten pounces on a very poor pass from out of the back, racing onto the ball in the box and sending his shot, from a wide angle, past the far post.
(46’) The teams are back from the interval and the second half is now underway! The home side now begin with the ball, playing it back to the defence and playing it down Cissokho's flank. They keep the ball well, switching sides as need be, though Sunderland's shape is preventing them from making it past the halfway line for the moment.
The silver lining here is that the second half surely couldn't be much worse (could it?!) so be sure to join us again in 15 minutes for the rest of the game!
The halftime speeches from the two coaches may not be drastically different; both sides' passing has been appalling at times with too many players not stamping their authority on the pitch, with Cleverley and Jordi Gomez in particular either uninfluential or simply not seeing enough of the ball.
(45’) Cissokho gets the better of Vergini on the flank to win possession back for his side. It ends up being the last meaningful event of a match largely devoid of them, with neither side providing much in the way of chances or quality.
(45’) Once again, another underhit pass from Jordi Gomez fails to beat Vlaar and the defender slides in to knock the ball out. Wickham and Jones combine in the box, and the latter's shot is deflected. The ball bounces around the box chaotically until Clark finally is able to hoof it clear!
(45’) Vergini, who hasn't often been involved offensively today, gets the ball down his flank and plays it back to his defence. Jordi Gomez sends a probing ball towards Johnson but it's underhit, much to the relief of Clark, who slides in and pushes the ball out just when the former Manchester City player looked to be clear through!
(45’) Larsson with a fantastic interception to nab the ball off of Cleverley in the heart of the midfield. The fourth official has announced four minutes of added time, which comes as no real surprise given the two injuries that Sunderland have suffered and the lengthy pauses in play that came about as a result.
--- 44’ Yellow card Vlaar enters the referee's notebook now after taking the ball from Fletcher though it didn't seem there was terribly much contact there, Luckily for the captain, the ensuing set-piece falls apart in the box and the home side look to build once again. ---
(43’) Johnson to Wickham, back to Johnson, who gets the ball to Jordi Gomez on the byline to whip a cross into the box. It's very close to Guzan, however, who collects it without much fuss. On the other end, Villa immediately get into the box but they can't find a way through via N'Zogbia.
(41’) N'Zogbia now is seeing more and more of the ball in the build up play now after a quiet opening spell of the game. Jones clears one cross out of his area but only to see Villa take back possession and work it down the left via Benteke, who loses the ball easily and Sanchez commits a foul, pushing Cattermole over in an attempt to try and win it back.
(40’) Pantilimon comes a long way off his line to collect the ball near the edge of the box but uses his height and hands to great advantage to relieve the pressure that was building on his defence. Johnson on the counter tries to hoof it up to Fletcher but Sanchez slides in the divert the pass to Guzan.
(39’) Delph sends the ball in only to see it come right back to him after Wickham cleared it. N'Zogbia collects on the right and plays Hutton through on the overlap, but Wickham is there once again to clear the ball out of his box.
(38’) Sunderland do get a shot nearly immediately after that, however, with Wickham firing a very tame effort to Guzan. Moments later, Benteke is fouled after collecting a poor goal-kick from Pantilimon and now Villa will look to send this directly into the box.
(37’) Delph is under pressure in the midfield and sends a high, looping ball back towards Guzan. It's poorly hit though and with Fletcher looming, Clark has to intercede and make a smart header back to his goalkeeper so that he can pick up the ball without giving the lurking striker a chance to shoot.
(36’) N'Zogbia gets the ball again and tries nearly the same exact move as before, cutting across Jones to shoot, but this time the shot takes a slight deflection that brings it closer to Pantilimon, who once again takes the ball with little fuss.
(34’) N'Zogbia loses out to Jones on the wing to concede possession back to the visitors. The full-back is having a tougher time today dealing with Hutton than the forward, but N'Zogbia shows what he's capable of by cutting in from the right past Jones and unleashing a shot that only finds the midriff of Pantilimon! It's the first real effort of the game though it's one that barely troubles the keeper.
(33’) Hutton races down the flank to cross the ball into the box. Weimann goes down, Atkinson refuses to acknowledge it, and the ball is cleared! No Villa players are arguing for a penalty but the player isn't booked for diving, either, and he's soon on his feet and rejoins the proceedings.
(32’) Very poor from Vergini, who takes a heavy touch and loses the ball just when Johnson looked to be in a fantastic position to slip the ball through to. Sunderland win it back and Brown draws a few questionable looks from his teammates when he sends a pass to no one in particular that dribbles out for a throw-in.
(31’) Larsson is off the pitch being evaluated but he was able to walk off himself and soon comes back on the pitch. Having already lost one player to injury, Poyet and his side will be hoping this is just a minor knock and that the player can go on.
(29’) Hutton sends a powerful cross in looking for Benteke that O'Shea stretches to get a foot onto and hoof it clear. On the counter, Johnson is flagged offside and Larsson is down holding his foot looking to be in some pain after sliding in on Delph, failing to get the ball, and then he seemed to twist his ankle as the Villa man raced by.
(27’) The game has a much more even flow to it now with both sides seeing plenty of the ball. Cleverly is caught late by Larsson and wins a free-kick in Sunderland's half, which he sends into the box for Pantilimon to easily collect. A disappointing effort.
(26’) A disappointing shot from Jordi Gomez, who got the ball with some space just outside of the box, takes two steps to get closer to goal, and tries an effort that sails very, very far wide of the far post. Guzan barely moved there and he didn't have to!
(25’) Wickham has been absolutely everywhere in this match so far and wins the ball for his side in midfield. Villa press, Sunderland play it back, and Cissokho rises high to head a long ball up to Johnson out for a throw-in.
(24’) Cleverly, who's had a quite match thus far, tries a quick ball over the top to Benteke on the left channel. O'Shea has read it well and heads it back to his keeper to cut out the danger.
(23’) Something from nothing there for the home side! N'Zogbia pounces on a loose ball after some sloppy possession from the visitors just outside their box; he lines up a shot after a couple of touches that deflects out off of Brown.
(22’) Wickham wins possession when the ball is chipped to him, passing it back and letting his defence play it back to him. Jones gets the ball in the box and lays it off once again for Wickham, who unleashes a curling shot from the edge of the box that goes past the far post!
(21’) Cattermole gets involved nearly immediately with a slide tackle that tries to win the ball, but Villa get it back and send it towards Hutton down the flank, only for Jones to intercept. Vlaar catches Fletcher with a kick through his legs to clear the ball and Atkinson duly whistles for a free-kick for the visitors, just on the Villa side of the halfway line.
--- 19’ Substitution Sad sights on the pitch as Bridcutt goes down holding his head. The substitution is now inevitable as Cattermole is sent on in his place, with Bridcutt surely on his way to be examined to ensure that his injury is not serious. ---
(17’) Gus Poyet will be keeping a very careful eye on his midfielder as play continues. Hutton tries to pry open the defence on one end but the ball is cut out by O'Shea; on the counter, Fletcher tries to send Wickham clear through but finds his teammate offside.
(16’) Four minutes after Bridcutt was knocked by Benteke, the game continues with the number four on the sidelines as he continues to be evaluated. For the time being, then, Sunderland are down to ten men, though it's a vert short spell as Bridcutt walks back onto the pitch less than a minute after play begins.
(14’) There's been a stoppage in play for the last couple of minutes as Bridcutt is down having been hit in the head by Benteke's knee as both went up to fight for the ball in the last play. Cattermole is warming up as a precaution, as it doesn't seem clear if Bridcutt can continue at the moment.
(12’) N'Zogbia and Hutton link up well down the right, forcing Jones to stick a foot in and concede a throw-in. Villa play it all the way back to Guzan, under immense team pressing from the visitors, thought Benteke's smart header for Weimann looks to have set the team free on the counter before the latter's very poor pass is played directly out of bounds.
(11’) The pattern here is quite evident: Sunderland are more than happy to let Villa into their own half before bolting down, trying to force an error, and racing on the counter. It looks to be paying off well but it takes a fantastic O'Shea interception on Weimann, who had just gotten the ball in the bo, to prevent him from firing into the net!
(9’) It takes Villa some time to work the ball into Sunderland's half but they finally doing, by quickly switching play from the middle out to the right. Sunderland give them absolutely no space and Delph responds by taking a shot from a long ways out that ends up nowhere near the target, much to Lambert's ire on the sidelines.
(7’) Wickham nicks the ball off of Delph in Villa's own half and races to the box, passing it wide to Gomez who sends a cross to the onrushing Fletcher, forcing Guzan off of his line to collect. It was a fast and direct attack from the visitors - a warning to Villa to be more careful in possession!
(5’) Cissokho tries a prying pass to Benteke in the box but Brown reads it well and cuts it out. The home side get the ball back and, entrenched in front of Sunderland's box, look to create something. Benteke takes a touch and tries a strike from outside of the box that goes over the bar but not by much!
(4’) Sunderland earn another corner here after a shot from Wickham takes a deflection. Larsson's effort this time is headed to the edge of the box where Johnson tries a volley on target but he miskicks it and Clark is eventually able to clear and send his team racing forward.
(3’) Very solid play by Villa now, controlling the ball well in midfield and getting it up wide to Sissokho. Vergini thinks he's cleared it but it finds its way up to Benteke, who tries to take a touch and race through the box but it's too heavy and lands kindly at the feet of Pantilimon.
(2’) Larsson's effort dips right in the centre of the box, forcing the Villa defence to clear it in two efforts.
(1’) AND WE HAVE KICK-OFF! Martin Atkinson gets the match underway with Sunderland, in their blue kits, taking the ball immediately up to Delph and taking a throw-in. It's worked up the pitch and out by Vlaar for another throw-in, deep in Villa's half, worked excellently by Jones to cross into the box and out for a corner.
The two teams are walking out of the tunnel now and we're just a few minutes away from kick-off!
Head-to-head history is kinder to the home side who have not lost in their last six meetings with the visitors, winning half of those and drawing the other half. On the other hand, Lambert's men have only one clean sheet at home all season and the Black Cats have recorded three of those in their last four away matches.
Villa fans will be keeping a close eye on how they team plays today. Coach Paul lambert said after their Boxing Day defeat that he was working on a new style for the club though it has not yet helped increase the amount of goals netted. The home side have scored just eleven in their eighteen matches so far this season.
Sunderland (4-1-4-1): Pantilimon; Jones, Brown, O'Shea, Vergini; Bridcutt; Wickham, Jordi Gomez, Larsson, Johnson; Fletcher.
Aston Villa (4-3-3): Guzan; Hutton, Vlaar, Clark, Cissokho; Cleverly, Sanchez, Delph; Weimann, Benteke, N'Zogbia.
There are quite a few absences for this match today. Agbonlahor is suspended following yellow card accumulation and Richardson is continuing to serve a suspension himself; on top of that, Villa will be without the injured Baker, Kozak, Senderos and Westwood. The visitors, meanwhile, will have to do without full-backs van Aanholt and Reveillere.
Sunderland's away form, meanwhile, has been excellent since their 8-0 thumping by Southampton. They beat Crystal Palace and Newcastle at tricky away grounds and tied both Liecester City and Liverpool. They'll need to keep that up today, given their spotty home record where they haven't won since defeating Stoke 3-1 back in early October.
The home side improved earlier this month to earn their first win since their 1-0 away victory over Liverpool all the way back in September, but their last three matches has seen them earn just a single point, off of Manchester United. They couldn't repeat that performance or result in a narrow loss to Swansea City last matchday.
Hello and welcome to our live match coverage of Aston Villa vs Sunderland! It's thirteenth hosting fourteenth in the Premier League today - two sides that have been seriously struggling with consistency and who know that just a couple of bad results could send them dangerously close to the relegation zone.
