FULL TIME - Hull 0-1 Leicester: The Foxes have their first Premier League victory in over three months thanks to Mahrez's first-half strike. They spent much of the second half clinging to the lead, with the Tigers hitting the woodwork twice. Both teams ended the match with 10 men, but it is the visitors that take all three points!
(90’) There is the final whistle!
--- 90’ +4 Red card! S. Quinn is sent for an early shower! ---
(90’) RED CARD! Quinn uses his hand to stop Nugent racing through on goal as he is the last man. Leicester have a free kick and the referee has no option but to send the midfielder off. Both teams down to 10 now, then.
(90’) Hull have a free kick in a great position, 25 yards out, following a foul on Elmohamady. Jelavic leaves it to Brady but the midfielder fires it straight into the wall! What a waste!
(90’) We are into the first of five additional minutes.
(90’) OVER THE TOP! The ball falls kindly for Hernandez just outside the six-yard box and he completely skies his effort. He cannot believe it, and nor can the fans!
(89’) Leicester are working so hard to keep this out! Brady's free kick is nodded over the top by a blue shirt for a corner, and it takes another clearance right in front of Hamer to stop that coming to anything!
--- 88’ Red card! RED CARD! LEICESTER DOWN TO 10 MEN! Konchesky blocks Elmohamady as he looks to break down the right but is blocked off. It's a second yellow card and Leicester's task just got harder. ---
(86’) Hull have looked a completely different beast since the introduction of Hernandez, and he comes inside from the right and bends a shot towards the far corner. It is kept out by Hamer, though, with a relatively routine stop.
(84’) THE POST SAVES LEICESTER AGAIN! Elmohamady's cross is met by a diving header from Hernandez and his header comes back off the upright. The rebound falls for Davies, whose shot on the half-volley is blocked on the line by Wasilewski!
(83’) WHAT A SAVE! A quick throw in catches Schlupp out, allowing Hernandez in behind. He shoots rom an acute angle but Hamer tips it behind for a corner!
(82’) Leicester eventually get the ball out of their half and Wood does well to hold up the ball and encourage his team to keep hold of it and alleviate the pressure on the defence. Eventually a long diagonal pass is pinged towards the right but McGregor is able to bring it in and restart the play.
(80’) The pressure continues to mount for the visitors! Leicester are clinging to their 1-0 lead, with Hull pinging crosses into the box continually in the hope of finding an equaliser.
(78’) OFF THE POST! Hernandez's cross is headed from the back post and into the danger area by Simpson, and it falls kindly for Livermore. He hits a volley which cannons back off the upright, and the follow-up effort is blocked by Morgan. Hull flight another cross to the back post which Jelavic nods wide!
(77’) Time is running out for the hosts as we approach the final 10 minutes of the game. Are they going to be able to salvage something from this?
(75’) Claims for a penalty as Hernandez flicks Elmohamady's cross on inside the area and it is blocked by Morgan. The Uruguayan suggests the centre-back used his arm, but play continues with the referee unmoved.
(73’) Quinn attempts a quick free kick down the right but Schlupp intercepts and then earns a free kick by knocking the ball past the Hull midfielder, who then blocks him off. The Tigers just cannot afford to waste chances like that.
(72’) One of the floodlights is completely out at the KC Stadium, but still the game is able to continue. Bruce won't want the momentum of his team to be broken up by an exogenous factor like that.
--- 71’ Substitution D. Drinkwater enters play, replacing E. Cambiasso. ---
--- 71’ Substitution R. Mahrez is done for the day. R. De Laet is his replacement. ---
(70’) Pearson makes two changes, with Drinkwater replacing Cambiasso and Ritchie De Laet taking the place of Mahrez. Both the Argetine and the Algerian have been brilliant today.
(69’) Leicester are looking to hold onto possession when they get the opportunity to move forward now. They are forcing Hull to chase the game, going back to their keeper before attacking down the left. Wood's effort on from a cross from the left loops narrowly wide of the far post.
(67’) Hull are cranking up the pressure yet again as a series of crosses come into the box but for the time being Leicester continue to repel them. The visitors are limiting themselves to playing on the counterattack now.
(65’) Hernandez tries to bulldoze his way into the area and he somehow gets to the byline and squeezes in a cross. There is no one gambling at the near post, though, and Hamer gathers.
(63’) The Tigers have controlled possession since the interval but Hamer remains untested. Will the pace of Ince and the striking instincts of Hernandez be enough to bring them back into this? Bruce has played all his cards now.
--- 62’ Substitution S. Aluko is replaced with A. Hernández. ---
--- 61’ Substitution D. Meyler is done for the day. T. Ince is his replacement. ---
(61’) Bruce makes a pair of changes now, with Ince and Hernandez coming on to replace Meyler and Aluko.
(60’) Elmohamady surges down the right, beating Konchesky for pace and putting a cross into the box. Morgan cuts it out at the near post and almost diverts the ball into his own net, but it goes just wide of the upright for a corner.
--- 58’ Yellow card P. Konchesky goes into the referee's book. ---
(58’) Konchesky is shown a yellow card for a poor challenge on Meyler in midfield. The left-back lost possession high up the pitch and clearly didn't want the opposition exploiting the space he had vacated.
(57’) Wood misses a great chance to go through one-on-one on the break as his touch deserts him on Nugent's pass out to the left!
(56’) Great challenge from Davies! The centre-back makes a superb sliding tackle just outside the six-yard box after Wood controlled a brilliant pass from Cambiasso.
--- 55’ Substitution L. Ulloa is done for the day. C. Wood is his replacement. ---
(54’) Nigel Pearson makes his first change with Ulloa coming off to be replaced by Chris Wood.
(52’) Leicester have not started this half with the same intensity that they did the first, and if they continue to invite Hull onto them then they will need to be completely concentrated at the back.
(50’) There is trouble with one of the floodlights at the KC Stadium, but both coaches are believed to be happy to continue.
(48’) Schlupp races away down the left, beating Bruce for pace, but his cross into the box is poor and Hull get it clear. He had other options there.
--- 46’ Substitution N. Jelavić comes on for G. Ramírez. ---
(46’) We are back underway!
There will be a change for the hosts, as Nikica Jelavic comes on for Ramirez.
The teams are back out, so the second half will begin in just a few moments.
HALF TIME - Hull 0-1 Leicester: The Premier League's bottom side are leading away at their fellow relegation candidates thanks to a brilliant strike from Mahrez. The visitors have pressed high and forced the Tigers into an uncomfortable long-ball game. It is all still to play for, though, so be sure to return for the second half shortly!
(45’) Hull take too long to get a throw in and once they put the ball back in play the referee brings the half to a close!
(45’) Aluko has gone down with an injury following that move, so we may have a few more added seconds.
(45’) WHAT A CHANCE! Quinn whips a fantastic cross into the box after pouncing on a weak clearance from the Foxes' defence. Elmohamady ghosts in at the back post to catch it on the vollye, but he fails to find the target! He was unmarked there and really should have tested Hamer at the very least.
(45’) There will be two added minutes at the end of this half.
(44’) The Tigers are starting to step up the tempo now, with Leicester abandoning their high press in the hope of soaking up pressure and frustrating the hosts until the break.
(42’) Leicester win the ball in midfield and suddenly break in a three-on-three situation. Mahrez attempts to thread a pass down the channel for Schlupp but it is intercepted. The Algerian puts his hands to his head, knowing that he's wasted a great opportunity there.
(40’) It's end to end stuff now! Mahrez creates space for another shot from the right, but this time he uses his right boot and McGregor gets down low to hold it. Hull break and win a corner which is put behind by the Leicester defence.
(39’) A chance for Ramirez! The Uruguayan finds space between Morgan and Wasilewski and he darts into it. Livermore spots his run and picks him out with a pass which draws Hamer from his line. The Southampton loanee gets a touch to poke the ball away from the keeper but he cannot stop it from going out for a goal kick. A lighter touch could have left him with a simple finish!
(37’) Ulloa has not seen much of the ball so far, but he is leading by example with his constant closing down of the opposing centre-backs. Hull are really struggling to play their game under this intense pressure, and yet another long diagonal ball is dealt with by the visitors' defence.
(35’) Ramirez picks up the ball on the right and spins inside. His pass is woeful though, finding neither Aluko or Brady and allowing Hamer to collect unopposed.
(34’) McGregor has not had an awful lot to do this afternoon, but there was little he could have done to keep out Mahrez's strike. It was a brilliant effort from the wide man, and it could prove to be a vital goal for the visitors' Premier League survival chances.
--- 32’ Assist Assist by D. Nugent. ---
--- 32’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAAAAL!! MAHREZ OPENS THE SCORING! Play eventually commences again and Alex Bruce jogs back into action, but moments later Hull are behind. Nugent finds the Algerian to his right, who cuts inside onto his left foot, beats Quinn, and then curls a fantastic shot beyond McGregor from 20 yards! ---
(30’) Hull put the ball out of play as Alex Bruce stays down following a late challenge from Simpson. The centre-back will now receive attention from the medical staff.
(29’) JUST WIDE! Meyler picks up the ball on the right and gets away from Cambiasso as he dribbles inside. He releases a shot from just over 20 yards which takes a touch that sends it narrowly outside of the upright! The resultant corner is punched away by Hamer.
(27’) Aluko drops deep and picks up the ball in space inside the centre circle. He sends a pass down towards the corner which Brady has absolutely no chance of reaching because he had not even set off on the run! Hamer has time to leave his goal and restart the play for the visitors.
(26’) Cambiasso cedes possession inside the Hull half and the hosts look to break. Aluko opens up his stride down the left wing but is stopped by a combination of Mahrez and Wasilewski.
(24’) Mahrez is shown down the outside by Rosenior and he earns a corner as his cross is deflected behind. The delivery is flicked on by Cambiasso at the near post before Livermore heads it away. Schlupp picks up the loose ball and looks to dart to the byline but his touch is too heavy and he fails to stop it from going out of play.
(22’) There's a confrontation between Mahrez and Brady after the Algerian shoved his opponent from behind as he looked to force him back inside his own half. As the Ireland international turned to face him he held up his hands apologetically, clearly not wanting to get involved.
(21’) Hull launch a free kick from inside their own half down the right wing, and Livermore comes in off the flank to nod it into a central area. Aluko looks to latch onto it but is unable to stop the ball from going out of play. There was no support in the box for him there anyway.
(19’) Nugent flicks the ball down the left-hand channel for Schlupp to chase, but he is adjudged overzealous in his attempts to get in front of Livermore inside the box and a free kick is awarded.
--- 18’ Yellow card D. Simpson is cautioned by the referee. ---
(18’) A free kick from deep on the right is bent into the box by Mahrez, but it is wasted as the first defender clears the ball before the visitors send it all the way back to Hamer.
(17’) Hull are continuing to look for the long ball due to the pressure being put on them deep inside their own half by the visitors. It will be interesting to see how long the Foxes can keep this intensity up, as it will only take one player to slacken off for the system to come crumbling down.
(15’) Brady has been drifting inside from the left frequently already in this first half, and he makes a run in behind to try and get on the end of Ramirez's clipped pass over the top. There's too much on it for him to beat Hamer to the ball.
(14’) Meyler is released down the right-hand channel but his cross is blocked by Wasilewski. Leicester fail to get the ball clear and Ramirez uses the opportunity to release a shot at goal. Again, it is fired straight at Hamer, though!
(13’) Ulloa has Schlupp overlapping to his left as he looks to bring the ball down 25 yards from goal, but he dawdles and is caught by Alex Bruce. Hull break and manage to force Hamer into a save, but it is a simple one from Brady's arrowed effort.
(11’) Leicester are struggling to get the ball down and play as they focus mainly on stopping Hull from opening them up through the middle.
(9’) Hull appear to have lined up with Rosenior at left-back and Elmohamady at right-back. Quinn is therefore in the centre of midfield with Meyler, and Livermore operating out on the right.
(7’) The Foxes' pressing forces Hull to play a long ball up from the back, and this time Aluko is offside. There's a huge gap between their defence and midfield so they cannot afford to get that wrong at all this afternoon.
(6’) Leicester are pressing Hull high up the pitch and looking to put them under pressure inside their own half. Eventually a long ball forward is picked up for the hosts by Aluko, and he cuts inside to create a shooting opportunity. He bends an effort around Morgan but sends it straight into the arms of Hamer.
(4’) Quinn gives the ball away cheaply under pressure from Nugent, and Ulloa picks it up before attempting to feed his team-mate. His pass is poor, though, and as Schlupp looks to dart into the box to keep the move alive he is brought to ground by a strong challenge from Alex Bruce.
(2’) A long ball up from the right-back position is flicked on at the top of the box by Ulloa, but Nugent had sat back to await the cushion. Therefore the ball bounces up for McGregor to claim it unchallenged.
(1’) We are underway!
We've got just a few minutes remaining before kick off at the KC Stadium!
The Foxes have lost all of their previous seven games on the road in the Premier League. They'll be bottom of the table at the end of the year regardless of today's outcome, but a positive result would keep them within touching distance of the likes of Burnley, Crystal Palace, and today's opponents, Hull.
Hull are looking to secure back-to-back victorories for the first time this season, but they have won just three of 17 Premier League games at the KC Stadium in 2014, losing 10. Still, Leicester's away record is hardly anything for them to worry about.
This is the first top-flight meeting of these two clubs, as all of their previous 68 league meetings have come in the second tier. It is a hugely important one, too, with both teams currently vying to avoid the drop come May.
Leicester bench: Smith, De Laet, Moore, Drinkwater, Knockaert, Hammond, Wood.
Leicester (4-4-1-1): Hamer; Simpson, Wasilewski, Morgan, Konchesky; Mahrez, Cambiasso, James, Schlupp; Nugent; Ulloa.
Hull bench: Harper, Figueroa, Maguire, Ince, Sagbo, Jelavic, Hernandez.
Hull (4-4-1-1): McGregor; Elmohamady, A. Bruce, Davies, Rosenior; Livermore, Meyler, Quinn, Brady; Ramirez; Aluko.
LEICESTER TEAM NEWS: Leicester are without Jamie Vardy who picked up his fifth booking of the season on Boxing Day. Kasper Schmeichel and Matt Upson also remain sidelined, but Esteban Cambiasso is recalled alongside Matty James as Danny Drinkwater drops to the bench and Andy King misses out through injury.
HULL TEAM NEWS: Tom Huddlestone and James Chester both miss out due to suspensions, so Jake Livermore, back after serving his ban, comes into midfield. Stephen Quinn subsequently moves to left-back with Liam Rosenior moving over to the right side of defence. It is Steve Bruce’s only change from the side that defeated Sunderland in their last outing just two days ago.
Leicester are currently on a run of 13 Premier League outings without a win, losing each of their last six. Their last victory was the 5-3 thumping of Manchester United back in September, and they desperately need a result today in order to avoid falling further adrift at the foot of the table.
Hull climbed out of the drop zone on Boxing Day following their 3-1 victory at Sunderland, ending a run of 10 games without a win. There is still plenty of work to be done for Steve Bruce's side, though, and he will be keen to build on that result against the Nigel Pearson's side today.

--- 81’ Goal! GOAL! Burnley have equalised! (78’) Great play by Burnley! Trippier sends a brilliant bouncing cross into the path of Arfield, who fires a first-time shot from the edge of the six-yard box that Demichelis stops from finding the back of the net with a great block.

(65’) Trippier tries to whip the free kick onto the head of Shackell, but, for the first time this game, it's poorly hit and is only able to find a blue shirt near the penalty spot.

(46’) City start the half in a sluggish manner and, as a result, Burnley earn themselves an early corner, which Kolarov is just about to clear away from danger with a deft header.

The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
Despite not playing as well as they have done at times this season, City head into the half-time break with a well-deserved 2-0 lead, one that is going to be incredibly difficult for Burnley to overturn. The visitors spent the vast majority of the opening 45 minutes on the back foot as they tried to deal with a strong Sky Blues side, who are on course for their eighth consecutive Premier League victory after two brilliant goals from Silva and Fernandinho.

(39’) It's all City at the moment as they pepper the Burnley penalty area with a plethora of dangerous crosses. They look determined to bag themselves a third goal before the half-time break.
(37’) Brilliant save by Heaton! Navas tests the Burnley goalkeeper with a rocket of a shot from 25 yards out, but the Englishman does well to deny the Spaniard with a great stop.

As for Burnley, a difficult week has left them second from bottom in the table, equal on points with 18th-place Crystal Palace after back-to-back defeats against Tottenham Hotspur and Liverpool. Their impressive 1-0 victory against Southampton two weeks ago is their only win in their last six league games, and today's clash against an incredibly strong City side is guaranteed to be another tough encounter in what has been a difficult month for Sean Dyche's side.

Full time at Loftus Road. It has certainly not been a Christmas Cracker of a match today as Queens Park Rangers and Crystal Palace play out a drab 0-0 stalemate in the Barclays Premier League. Keith Millen's outfit will be the happier side with the point and certainly can be proud of their defensive work, with QPR no doubt feeling mightily frustrated. I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
(90’) Palace almost grab a winner in the last minute as Puncheon runs through and lashes a strike towards goal, only to see the attempt saved. Meanwhile Campbell goes down under the challenge of Barton, but the ref doesn't blow for the penalty!
(90’) Only three minutes of added time here and it looks like it is going to be attack versus defence for the last few moments. Can anyone find the winner?
(89’) Redknapp is urging his players to get forward and find the winner here. The home side will still have to be wary though as we are all aware of the threat that Palace, and in particular Bolasie, can possess on the counterattack.
(87’) HOILETT! JUST WIDE! Barton sends a quality corner kick to the back post and Caulker sees his header cleared. The former Blackburn winger latches on to the loose ball and drills a half volley towards the corner, but it just screws wide of the post!
(85’) It looks like Palace may be settling for the point here as they have showed little attacking ambition in the last few minutes. QPR, conversely, are playing with a high defensive line and committing plenty of men forward. With the situation the visitors are in at the moment without a manager, this would be a great point.
(83’) Redknapp attempted to change the style of his team with his substitutes and the switch to a 4-3-3, but it has not really worked yet as Palace are sitting deep which means Vargas and Phillips can't utilise their pace to get in behind.
(81’) QPR send a variety of different crosses into the box but it is the same old story as Palace easily deal with the high balls. Dann and Delaney have been rocks at the back today.
(80’) 10 minutes to go now and there are still not many signs that either side is going to produce something to win this. The legs are starting to get tired though so if there is indeed a winner, it may come from a mistake.
(78’) Barton is again tasked with getting a decent delivery into the box from the halfway line from a set piece. The Englishman hits a deep cross to the back post but it is food and drink for Speroni who comes off his line to collect.
(76’) Another switch on the cards for QPR as Harry Redknapp continues to chase the winner. Zamora, who has been quiet today, comes off to be replaced by Matty Phillips, who will inject yet more pace into the attack of the home side. Looks like a 4-3-3 now.
--- 75’ Substitution M. Phillips enters play, replacing B. Zamora. ---
(75’) PALACE CLEAR OFF THE LINE! Barton swings a corner kick to the back post and Caulker rises high to head towards the corner, but McCarthur in on hand next to his goalkeeper to make the all important interception! Fantastic covering by the former Wigan man!
(73’) QPR are piling on the pressure with a succession of consecutive corner kick here, but Palace just are not budging in their defending. It is going to take something pretty special to break them down when they are in this kind of mood!
--- 72’ Yellow card J. Puncheon is yellow-carded. ---
(71’) Just under 20 minutes remaining here at Loftus Road. There has not been any lack of effort on show by either side, just a desperate lack of quality in the final third. Unless either side can buck up their ideas pretty quickly, the honours are going to remain even.
(69’) Palace follow suit and make their own opening change, and there is no surprises with this one. Zaha, who has failed to hold the ball up well in his central striker position, is coming off for a more recognised centre-forward, Fraizer Campbell.
--- 67’ Substitution W. Zaha is replaced with F. Campbell. ---
(67’) We've got our first substitution of the match now and it comes from QPR. Leror Fer is coming off despite nearly scoring on a few occasions, and he'll be replaced by Eduardo Vargas, in what is a positive switch from Harry Redknapp.
--- 65’ Substitution L. Fer is done for the day. E. Vargas is his replacement. ---
(65’) Bolasie latches on to a ball over the top and finds himself alone up against three QPR defenders. The winger keeps the attack alive with a few bouncing touches into the air and eventually looks to get the volley away, but the home side eventually smuggle clear.
(63’) Barton is the latest player to go into the book and it is for a rather naughty stud into the stomach of McCarthur. The QPR midfielder typically pleads his innocence, but he definitely knew what he was doing there. Deserved yellow card.
--- 62’ Yellow card J. Barton gets yellow. ---
(61’) What a clearance from Jedinak! Barton does brilliantly near the byline to dig out a cross to the back post, which Austin looks certain to head home, but the striker is foiled by the Palace captain who heads over the bar to save the goal! Superb defending!
(59’) FANTASTIC SAVE FROM SPERONI! Fer tees himself up for the half volley with a bouncing touch and drills a superb strike towards the top left corner, but his attempt is tipped over the bar by the diving Palace keeper! The Dutchman certainly has his shooting boots on today, but he is denied again!
(57’) QPR's usual prowess from set-pieces have just not been there today, and you have to hand it to the Palace defence as they have dealt with the threat excellently so far. Having said that, Austin only needs one chance to pop up with a goal, but we haven'r seen a lot of him so far.
(55’) It is all very scrappy at the moment as both sides are failing to instigate a period of sustained possession in central areas. Defences are on top, with far too many loose passes breaking down attacks.
(53’) QPR send a long ball up the park and Zamora takes possession into his chest before cleverly earning a foul out of Dann. The front two for the home side just have not received enough quality service to make an impact so far, but we still have plenty of time left.
(51’) Bolasie, who has moved into a more central position for the time being, receives the ball to feet and turns sharply before looking to get a shot away. The attempt ends up being disappointingly dragged wide whilst not posing any kind of threat to Green.
(49’) FER! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT! A cross is floated into the box and the Palace defence clear to the edge of the box. The Dutchman meets it with a terrific volley which looks in all the way, but ends up bouncing past the bottom of the post! Unlucky!
(47’) QPR get a set piece down the right-hand side early doors in this second half. Barton takes it but it is far too shallow which allows Bolasie to counterattack through the middle. In the end the home side retrieve possession and look to attack again.
(46’) We are back under way at Loftus Road!
Half time at Loftus Road. It has been, perhaps as predicted, a scrappy match between QPR and Crystal Palace so far as both sides attempt to gain dominance over the match. The visitors have been the better team in terms of attacking play and were unlucky not to take the lead when Puncheon hit the post, but the game has been bereft of goalscoring chances. Much better second half in store...hopefully!
--- 45’ +1 Yellow card C. Hill is cautioned by the referee. ---
(45’) Clint Hill is arguably lucky still to be on the park here as he goes in high and two-legged on the shinpad of Mariappa just outside the Palace box. The only saving grace for the QPR defender is perhaps that he got the ball first, but he is deservedly still given a booking by the ref.
(43’) Bolasie looks to link up with Zaha down this left wing once again as he fires a pass into the feet of his team-mate, but the latter can't get the ball out his feet which allows Isla to pounce and win possession. It has not been a good first half from the on-loan Man Utd man.
(41’) Zaha latches on to a pass down the left channel and finds himself in behind the QPR defence, but the home crowd breathes a sigh of relief as the resulting shot is dragged timidly wide. Considering the position he was in, he should be doing much better there!
(39’) Barton breaks ahead from his central midfield position and looks to make his way into the penalty area, but is just pipped to the ball slightly by McCarthy as the covering Scot puts out for a corner kick. Set piece opportunity for QPR once again.
(37’) Palace are playing pretty much without a recognised striker today as Zaha, who is usually a winger, is featuring in that position. It is certainly showing as much of their best play has came down the flanks, but with no real threat inside the penalty area.
(35’) Hoilett bursts down the left-hand side and typically looks to cut in on his right foot. He can't manage it though as Puncheon forces him down to the byline, which means the resulting cross in with his weaker foot is screwed behind the goal, much to the delight of the Palace fans.
(33’) Bolasie drops deep and rises high to meet a long ball to glance it down the wing for Zaha, but he can't manage to get possession out his feet which allows Isla to come in with another solid challenge. The visitors certainly getting a little bit of joy near that touchline.
(31’) You get the feeling that it may be a set piece which holds the key to a team opening the scoring here. We all know QPR's proficiency in the air with the likes of Austin and Zamora, but Palace certainly can be a threat in terms of delivery from Jedinak.
(29’) We are just about approaching the half hour mark and we are still to see too many out-and-out goalscoring chances here. Palace have been the better side in the attacking department and were unlucky not to score when Puncheon hit the post, but both keepers yet to be truly tested in between the sticks.
(27’) Hoilett, who has been quiet so far, gets down the left wing and cuts inside on his right foot before curling a teasing cross into the box. Austin and Zamora are interested but Speroni comes off his line and takes the pressure off his defence with an excellent claim.

(23’) McCarthur goes for the spectacular with a 25-yard half volley but the Scot's attempt was never going to bother Green in the QPR goal and ends up going well over. Palace very much on top at the moment!
(21’) PALACE HIT THE POST!!! Some brilliant interplay on the edge of the box from the visitors eventually sees Ledley tee up Puncheon, who bends a lovely strike towards the far corner, only to see his attempt crash off the outside of the woodwork! So unlucky!
(19’) BOLASIE! The DR Congo international received the ball to feet in the left channel and shifts inside on his right foot before firing an ambitious strike towards the top left corner. Green reads it well though and gets across goal to make the relatively comfortable stop.
(17’) QPR get the free kick deep down the left flank, which Barton will take. The former Marseille midfielder drops the set piece into the box which Speroni shakily manages to claim at the second attempt. No players from the home side waiting to pounce on the dropped save!
(15’) AUSTIN GOES CLOSE! We get our first real glimpse of QPR's top goalscorer as he latches on to a loose ball on the edge of the box to fire a volley towards the bottom right corner. In the end it is quite comfortable for Speroni but it was a decent attempt all the same!
(13’) Dunne gets let off the hook massively down the right wing as he basically falls over the ball under pressure from Zaha, only to be awarded a free kick by the ref as the Palace winger is penalised. Never a foul.
(11’) Very wasteful from Crystal Palace. The visitors have the opportunity to swing a corner kick into the box with plenty of attackers waiting to pounce, but opt to take the set piece short to Zaha. The Manchester United loanee attempts some trickery but ends up losing the ball rather easily.
(9’) Fer breaks forward through the middle and looks poised to get a shot away on the edge of the box, but just before he can he is hauled to the floor by McCarthur, who had gave the ball away a few seconds previously. QPR with the set piece opportunity 25 yards out here.
(7’) We are already seeing a pretty interesting feud develop down that right wing between Isla and the pacey Bolasie. The Chilean has defended solidly so far but he has his work cut out for him dealing with the sometimes mesmerising trickery of the Palace winger. Keep an eye on this one as it develops!
(5’) There is currently a round of applause coming from the crowd in tribute to former QPR player Clarke Carlisle who is currently in serious condition in hospital after a traffic accident. Nice touch from the Loftus Road faithful.
(3’) Bolasie moves into a deeper position down the left before looking to get in behind Caulker, but the pass from Zaha comes too late which means the former is offside.
(1’) We are under way at Loftus Road!

(66’) STOKE DOUBLE THEIR LEAD AND IT IS INCREDIBLY HARSH ON WEST BROM!

(51’) STOKE TAKE THE LEAD AS THE BRITANNIA PROVES FEARFUL ONCE AGAIN!
(50’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have won just one of their last 15 meetings with Stoke City in league play, losing 10 of those matches.
(48’) Tame start to the second half as West Brom do well to keep Stoke on the outside. Pieters and Arnautovic send crosses into the area, but Crouch can do very little to try and direct them on target before the ball finally runs safely behind for a goal kick.
(46’) West Brom kick-off and the second half is underway at the Britannia! No changes made by either side at the break.
HALF TIME: STOKE CITY 0-0 WEST BROM. There has been a few chances at both ends, but still no breakthrough to be had. The build up play from West Brom will have to please Alan Irvine, though they have yet to take one of their chances. Stoke look frantic in possession and, with the exception of Bojan, have yet to really trouble West Brom at the back.
(45’) A horrendous giveaway by N'Zonzi inside his own half allows Brunt to break on a counter. He is in all sorts of space in the centre, and again opts to have a go from distance, but his long-range strike again sails wide of the far post - and it wasn't nearly as close this time. That is the last action of the first half.
(45’) There will be just one minute of stoppage time added on at the end of this first half.
(43’) Stoke win a free kick from about 40 yards out, which gives them a chance to get some of the big bodies forward from the back. Pieters delivers a sensational ball into the area, but no one can get a head to it as it bounces just outside the six-yard box before running harmlessly out of play.
(41’) There have been very few talking points over the last 10 minutes, with a strike from distance producing the only real chance. At this point the teams seem content with playing out the final few minutes and heading into the break level.
(39’) Stoke are struggling to keep the ball, and their sloppy passing in the middle of the pitch has Mark Hughes stomping the ground in despair. The Potters have certainly not looked like the team targeting the top half of the table, and you get the sense that West Brom may be able to snatch all three points if they manage to take one of these chances and score the first goal.
(37’) HOW CLOSE WAS THAT! More great build up play from West Brom sees the ball come to Brunt from 30 yards out. He is more than capable of the spectacular, and opts to have a go from distance. (35’) STAT ATTACK: The 10 points picked up by Stoke City through their first eight league matches at the Britannia Stadium is their lowest-ever tally to start a Premier League season.
(33’) Important block! Arnautovic whips in a dangerous looking corner which West Brom fail to clear. It falls for Whelan at the top of the area, and he drives a shot toward goal. Lescott bravely throws his head in front of it to deflect the ball behind.
(31’) Good chance for West Brom! Lovely passing from the Baggies as Sessegnon and Gardner link up before Morrison is teed up for a shot from 25 yards out. He smacks his laces through the ball, but puts his effort straight at Begovic.
(29’) N'Zonzi has shown his capabilities in possession, but as has been the case for most in this game, the build up play has been great, with the end result lacking.
(27’) There is a certain lack of fluidity in the match which has prevented it from really flowing. The foul count is constantly rising, with the ball being contained primarily in midfield. Neither side has managed to take the reins, with the game up for grabs at the moment.
(25’) The pace has slowed significantly from the wide-open start we had. Stoke are looking to keep the ball for longer periods, while West Brom look disinterested in pushing up the pitch unless they are on the counter. Their pace up top has caused the hosts a few problems, but they have to find a way to maintain pressure while keeping possession.
(23’) Bojan looks threatening as he drifts in and out of the centre in attack. He is showing great skill on the ball, continuously trying to act as provider for his teammates. Here he finds a bit of space on the left, and sends a lovely ball in for Crouch, but the striker's lack of pace allows McAuley to intervene.
(21’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have kept four clean sheets in their eight away matches this season. Only Southampton have conceded fewer goals on their travels this season than the Baggies.
(19’) GOOD PATIENCE! West Brom look increasingly dangerous on the counter, with Ideye eager to run in behind the defence. This time he is sent through on goal by Sessegnon, and tries to outwit Begovic, but the keeper stays with him and gets down to keep the shot out.
(17’) NIFTY FOOTWORK! Bojan flashes a bit of skill as he dribbles his way through an incredibly tight area atop the West Brom box. He is finally dispossessed, but gets the ball back and again takes on defenders one at a time. He manages to slip in Cameron, but the defender gives it away at the vital moment.
(15’) Stoke are beginning to settle a bit, as their two centre-backs become more involved in the play. Shawcross is playing an important role in helping them keep possession, with the defender feeling a bit adventurous with the ball at his feet.
(13’) SMASHING START! Stoke look a bit stunned as West Brom pour on the pressure early on. They are passing it about wonderfully, and Brunt is doing a wonderful job of dictating the play in midfield. He gets around Whelan, but his shot is blocked. It rolls into the path of Sessegnon, but he cannot trouble Begovic with his shot.
(11’) Wasteful from Sessegnon! Ideye gets on the end of a long pass forward after some miscommunication between Muniesa and Begovic. The striker picks out the midfielder on the left, and waits for a return pass. Sessegnon holds onto the ball too long and tries to take on two defenders, though, as the chance goes begging.
(9’) Surprisingly enough, there is a brisk pace to this match early on. The teams are eager to get up the pitch, especially West Brom, who look to really be going for it. Ideye has made some teasing runs early on, causing one or two problems for the Stoke defence.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: The last two Premier League meetings between Stoke and West Brom at the Britannia have ended goalless. Graham Dorrans was the last player to score in a game between these teams in Stoke, securing a 2-1 Baggies victory back on January 21, 2012.
(5’) SHOCKING DECISION! STOKE DENIED A CLEAR PENALTY CLAIM! Arnautovic links up with Cameron along the right, before the defender sends a cutback pass to Muniesa. Gardner sticks out a leg and steps on the foot of the centre-back who goes to ground. Roger East is in a good position, and despite immense pressure from the home supporters, he waives away the claims!
(3’) The first chance of the game falls to Brown Ideye! Stoke win a free kick, but the Baggies are able to break after dealing with the threat. Chris Brunt sends a long ball forward for the striker to chase, and he does get there first, but skies his effort under pressure from Cameron.
(1’) Stoke kick-off and we are underway at the Britannia! The hosts, moving right to left, are in their red and white home stip, with West Brom sporting their blue and white stripes.
West Brom are given a boost as Alan Irvine welcomes Graham Dorrans and captain Chris Brunt back into the starting lineup. The skipper returned from his hamstring injury on Boxing Day, but only featured as a substitute. Their arrivals push Youssouf Mulumbu and Silvestre Varela to the bench. The manager has made two other changes, with the big Nigerian Brown Ideye replacing Sadio Berahino up top, while Chris Baird gets the start at left-back.
Bojan has recovered in time from a back injury picked up against Everton, and has been included in the starting lineup. Ryan Shawcross also picked up a knock against the Toffees, but much like the Spaniard, he is good to go. Phil Bardsley remains out with an ankle problem. There has been just one change employed by Mark Hughes, who has opted to rest Jonathan Walters, bringing Peter Crouch into the XI, while pushing Mame Diouf onto the wing.

West Brom are really struggling of late, and it is hard to look at any one aspect of their team and pinpoint it as the reason why they will stay up. They have lost six of their last eight games and to make matters worse, their defence appears to have started leaking goals. There can be an excuse made for the Baggies losing to Manchester City on Boxing Day, but blowing a 2-0 lead against QPR the week before and leaving Loftus Road empty handed is unacceptable. Alan Irvine has to demand a higher intensity from his players, because at the moment they hardly appear very motivated enough to stay up.
Stoke are in good shape headed into 2015, with a top half of the table finish looking like a realistic goal. The Britannia has not been its usual fortress of late, but Mark Hughes should see this as a very winnable game and a chance to build off their 1-0 victory at Goodison Park on Boxing Day. The pressure will be on their opponents today to pick up a result, but the Potters will not want to afford a slip up, either.

For West Ham, Adrian again excelled and Carroll worked hard, producing a few moments of quality. A thoroughly entertaining game finishes, then, West Ham 1-2 Arsenal.
Both teams threw everything they had at that game and Arsenal were indebted to the superb goalkeeping of Szczesny and the midfield work of Coquelin. Sanchez was again outstanding, and Oxlade-Chamberlain and Welbeck did well too.
While West Ham can have no complaints over the penalty decision, they will feel aggrieved that Song's first-half volley was chalked off for an offside.
Goals from Cazorla, who won the penalty he took after a clumsy challenge from Reid, and Welbeck, sliding in to tap home an Oxlade-Chamberlain cross, secured the win for Arsenal. West Ham got one back through Kouyate, heading in after Tomkins' clever cross.
And so, somehow, it finishes West Ham 1-2 Arsenal.

Szczesny has come to his team's rescue a few times, especially under the high ball, but West Ham will at least be heartened by the ease with which they have ruffled the feathers of the Gunners back-line.
Arsenal are shaky at the back, though, and Carroll's directness, Sakho's pace, and Downing's passing have all caused problems. Monreal and Debuchy look weak and Flamini has been utterly anonymous. Coquelin, however, has played well, and the front three of the away side have all impressed.
Football, eh? Arsenal, on the back foot for most of that game, go in at half-time winning 0-2 against home team West Ham. A Cazorla penalty and an excellent tap-in for Welbeck after great work from Oxlade-Chamberlain have put a very different complexion on the game after Song's early volleyed goal was disallowed.
(45’) The corner comes to nothing and it's half time. Arsenal go in two goals ahead, but the Boleyn Ground are all wondering how.

(90’) There are four minutes of stoppage time!

(82’) Newcastle are looking extremely comfortable, with Everton having absolutely nothing in the way of penetration. Without Naismith buzzing in behind the striker, there is nothing asking questions of the hosts' defence in terms of movement. It has been a rather gloomy Christmas for the Toffees.
(80’) Only 10 minutes remain for Newcastle to see out, with Alnwick hesitating with yet another set piece. Garbutt whips in a corner delivery, with the 21-year-old flapping a glove at the ball without success. Had there been an extra man in blue at the back post, the Magpies' shot-stopper might just have been in trouble.
(78’) Everton are being allowed to hold onto the ball, but only on Newcastle's terms, with the home side ceding some territory and allowing the away side to play in non-threatening areas. Martinez's substitutions haven't had any kind of impact yet.
(76’) Everton continue to look predictable and one-dimensional, attempting to intricately force their way through a very congested centre of the field. There isn't a great deal of width on offer, even with Coleman and Garbutt at full-back.
(74’) Newcastle are looking in complete control at this stage, despite the introduction of Lukaku. Alnwick has been a relative spectator in the second half, Pardew will be very pleased with how this match has panned out.
--- 73’ Substitution E. Rivière enters play, replacing P. Cissé. ---
--- 72’ Substitution A. Koné is done for the day. R. Lukaku is his replacement. ---
(72’) Sissoko requires a bit of treatment, after being clattered by Alcaraz in the build up to Cisse's latest opportunity. The Paraguayan defender picked up a yellow card for his troubles, with Martinez now opting to throw on Lukaku to save this contest.
--- 71’ Yellow card A. Alcáraz is cautioned by the referee. ---
(70’) The onus really is on Everton to stage a comeback now, but Martinez's men look void of any real ideas. Eto'o and Kone attempt to play a one-two on the edge of the box, but it's too congested and Newcastle clear. The hosts break upfield, with Cisse found on the right-hand side, but the goalscorer blasts directly at Joel!
--- 68’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! COLBACK EXTENDS THE MAGPIES' LEAD! Barkley takes an awful touch on the edge of his own penalty area from an early Newcastle cross, knocking it into the stride of Colback. (62’) Mirallas is thrown into the fray in place of McGeady, with the former Celtic winger failing to get into the game whatsoever since the break. Newcastle are looking confident and composed and continue to move the ball far better than their usually technically-impressive adversaries.

(45’) There are two minutes of stoppage time.

(36’) Baines and Garbutt combine down the left-hand side, before Coloccini clears the former's tame eventual effort. The home fans are responding to coming back onto level terms, making plenty of noise and urging the Magpies forward. Cisse and Gouffran both then fail to stretch to stab home a teasing cross.

Hello and welcome to St. James' Park, as Newcastle United host Everton. FULL TIME - Liverpool 4-1 Swansea: Rodgers' men end 2014 on a high with an emphatic victory over his former club in a scintilating game at Anfield. Moreno opened the scoring in the first half, and an electric second period followed. Lallana netted a fortunate second for the hosts but Sigurdsson immediately pegged them back. Welcome back! The teams are back out, so the second half will begin in just a few moments.
HALF TIME - Liverpool 1-0 Swansea: The Reds deservedly lead at the break thanks to Moreno's strike in the 33rd minute which rounded off a great team move. The hosts have dominated possession but the Swans began to show signs of life in the latter stages. Will they provide a resurgence in the second half or will Liverpool build upon their lead? Join me for the remainder in 15 minutes!
(45’) A corner from the right falls to Skrtel but his shot is blocked and the referee brings the first half to a close.
(45’) There will be just one minute of added time.
(45’) Sigurdsson clips a brilliant free kick to the back post where Fernandez attacks it. He attempts to cushion a header into the centre of the box but his connection is poor. Sakho is first to it, though his clearance drops for Dyer, whose volley is claimed by Mignolet. Liverpool quickly move up the other end and Coutinho pulls a save from Fabianski with a swerving drive from 25 yards.
(43’) The Swans put a series of crosses into the box, the last of which is controlled by the chest of Bony on the edge of the area. He rolls the ball out to the right for Richards to whip another one in, but his touch is poor and Liverpool manage to dispossess the right-back.
(41’) Can has stayed down holding his head following that challenge, and it seems he caught an elbow in the face from Shelvey. He's not happy with it, and, given the retrospective action taken against Papiss Cisse for his actions as the weekend, that may get looked at again.
(40’) Shelvey picks up the ball 20 yards out and he shows fantastic footwork to dribble into the penalty area. He knocks the ball beyond Can but lacks the strength to get around the German and Henderson kicks it off the Swansea man for a goal kick.
(38’) Liverpool are pressing very high, forcing Swansea to think quickly and rush their passes. Rodgers will be delighted with the intensity that his side are showing here.
(36’) Coutinho nearly makes it two! The Brazilian dribbles past Fernandez and Richards inside the box, getting to the byline before cutting back inside. He then fires a right-footed shot towards the near post which forces Fabianski to get down low and turn outside the upright.
(35’) There can be no denying that Liverpool deserve to be ahead this evening. They've been the more adventurous of the two sides, with Moreno earning his strike through his vibrant attacking play in this first half.
--- 33’ Assist The assist came from J. Henderson. ---
--- 33’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAL!! LIVERPOOL LEAD! Moreno initiates the move, carrying the ball down the left before moving infield and offloading to Lallana. The former Southampton man rolls a pass to the byline for Henderson, who cuts a square ball into the middle where the Spanish left-back supplies the finish! His shot was straight at Fabianski, but the keeper couldn't stop it finding the back of the net! ---
(32’) Bony tries his luck with a rasping effort from in excess of 25 yards, but it's a wild one that sails high over the top.
(31’) Taylor flights a cross in from deep on the left, which goes beyond Routledge but finds Dyer near the back post. He diverts his header on target but fails to generate enough power to worry Mignolet, who is left with a simple catch to make.
(29’) We've almost completed the opening 30 minutes and Liverpool certainly have the upper hand so far. Their back three have not been stretched at all so far, while Fabianski has had a couple of saves to make.
(27’) Swansea finally get a good spell in possession inside the Liverpool half but Shelvey's attempt to send Dyer down to the byline is cut out by Moreno. The visitors have been unable to get the best out of Sigurdsson so far this evening, who is being watched very closely.
(25’) Coutinho almost recreates his superb pass which assisted Sterling's goal in the previous outing against Burnley, but the England international did not have the strength to beat Fernandez to the ball and go through one-on-one with Fabianski.
(24’) Shelvey's poor control falls kindly for Routledge and he pounces to dart into the box from the left. He skips over one challenge but is unable to keep the ball in play. Had he gone down there the referee would have had a difficult decision to make. Credit to him for staying on his feet, though.
(22’) The Swans lose possession cheaply inside their own half and the hosts work the ball to Coutinho on the corner of the box. He searches out the far corner with a swerving drive that arrows just outside the upright. The Welsh side have been sloppy in possession so far.
(21’) Swansea finally get some relief with Routledge receiving possession wide on the left. He cuts inside to get the ball onto his right foot and overhits his cross! That is a real waste as the Swans had committed a number of men to provide options in the box for him.
(20’) STAT: Jonjo Shelvey has scored in both of his league appearances for Swansea against his former club.
(18’) Liverpool are monopolising possession now, forcing Swansea to sit deep inside their own half. The visitors have barely offered an attacking threat in the opening exchanges.
(16’) Henderson floats a diagonal pass towards the far side of the box for Manquillo, but his header back into the middle is nodded clear by Williams. Lallana keeps it alive and he picks out Coutinho at the top of the box, but his shot is a tame one which Fabianski welcomes into his arms.
(15’) Liverpool are looking to build on this momentum and the crowd are really getting behind their expansive, attacking play. Routledge attempts to initiate a counterattack for the visitors but he overruns the ball and cedes possession to Can.
(13’) STERLING! Moreno again finds acres of space out on the left, and the England international spreads the play to him before darting towards the box. The Spaniard returns the favour for Sterling, whose volley is pushed back into the danger area by Fabianski. Swansea fail to get rid and Lallana is offered a shot from 12 yards which he blazes over the top!
(12’) Moreno makes another late, surging run towards the byline and this time he manages to get a cross on. He fails to pick out a team-mate but Sterling and Lallana look to keep it alive with some intricate play on the edge of the box. Shelvey does well to intervene before Swansea clear.
(11’) Shelvey spots Routledge's diagonal run from the left wing towards the centre of the top of the box and he angles a clever pass over the top with the outside of his boot. It bends away from the winger at the vital moment, though, and it bounces into Mignolet's hands for a comfortable save.
(9’) Swansea are dropping both their wide players back into midfield when they are without possession in order to match Liverpool and cover against their wing-backs. It could be a rather cagey first half, you sense.
(7’) Moreno makes his first foray forward with an underlapping run on Coutinho, darting down the left-hand channel. The Brazilian rolls a pass into his feet which gets caught in his stride, leading to the wing-back kicking the ball out of play.
(6’) SKRTEL! The Slovakian is given space by Fernandez for a run-up to attack the resultant corner at the back post, but his powerful header is directed straight at Fabianski. The Polish keeper holds it at the first time of asking.
(5’) Sterling picks up the ball on the left and dribbles towards the area. He throws a stepover at Fernandez and beats him to the byline, but the covering defender sweeps in with a sliding challenge to send it behind for a corner.
(4’) Henderson switches the play with a raking pass out to Manquillo in an advanced position on the right. The wing-back had strayed into an offside position, though, so play is immediately pulled back.
(3’) Both teams are looking to play short, snappy passes in midfield in the early stages here, though neither have fully settled into possession with a number of stray balls from the pair.
(1’) We are underway at Anfield!
Simon Mignolet looked bereft of confidence after coming on in the game with Burnley so he will be desperate for a solid start to this evening's match.
The teams are out from the tunnel, so kick off will be upon us shortly!
Liverpool fans will be expecting more from their side tonight as the Reds have won just two of their last eight league games at Anfield. They did defeat Swansea here in the League Cup earlier this season, but they required two late goals to avoid elimination. It's far from convincing as Rodgers' men enjoy starkly contrasting fortunes to last season.
Just one goal was scored in the first three Premier League games between Swansea and Liverpool, but there have been 16 in the last three. Neutrals will certainly be hoping be more of the same tonight!
Swansea bench: Tremmel, Bartley, Rangel, Ki, Carroll, Emnes, Gomis.
Swansea (4-2-3-1): Fabianski; Richards, Fernandez, Williams, Taylor; Britton, Shelvey; Dyer, Sigurdsson, Routledge; Bony.
Liverpool bench: Ward, Toure, Gerrard, Markovic, Borini, Balotelli, Lambert.
Liverpool (3-4-2-1): Mignolet; Sakho, Skrtel, Can; Manquillo, Henderson, Lucas, Moreno; Coutinho, Lallana; Sterling.
SWANSEA TEAM NEWS: Monk makes three changes from the side he selected for the 1-0 win over Aston Villa. Jefferson Montero is unavailable following a hamstring injury picked up in that game, and Sung-Yueng Ki is replaced by Leon Britton. The final change comes in the right-back position, with Angel Rangel making way for Ashley Richards.
LIVERPOOL TEAM NEWS: Simon Mignolet continues in goal after replacing the injured Brad Jones in the 1-0 victory over Burnley on Boxing Day. Emre Can starts in the back three at the expense of Kolo Toure, while Steven Gerrard and Lazar Markovic drop to the bench with Spanish duo Javi Manquillo and Alberto Moreno coming in.
Brendan Rodgers guided Swansea into the Premier League in 2011 and left at the end of their debut campaign in the competition. The Welsh side are now under the stewardship of one of his former players in Garry Monk, and the coach has maintained the club's upwards trajectory. Tonight will provide the Swans with a big test, while Liverpool will be expecting to win these kind of games.
Hello and welcome to tonight's LIVE commentary on the final Premier League game of 2014! Liverpool, who currently occupy 10th position, welcome eighth-placed Swansea City to Anfield, with both sides keen to move closer to the European places with a victory. My name is Tom Webber and I will be guiding you through all the action.

Full time in Stamford Bridge. It has been as professional a performance as we come to expect from Chelsea these days as they run out relatively comfortable 2-0 winners over West Ham on Boxing Day. Some of the hosts play was scintillating in the final third and they grabbed two deserved goals through John Terry and Diego Costa. Chelsea have never lost the league when they have been leading on Boxing Day, so it looks like the rest have it all to do! I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
(90’) Only one minute of added time remaining now so it seems like West Ham's mini revival has came far too late. They certainly haven't gave up though so fair play to the Hammers.
(90’) West Ham are really upping their tempo in the latter stages here as they attempt to claw the ball back. Sakho gets down the right-hand side and swings a great cross to the back post, but Ivanovic is on hand to clear away. Song collects 30 yards out and recycles the attack.
(88’) WEST HAM HIT THE POST! Amalfitano, who has been very bright since coming on, twists and turns inside the box trying to find space and eventually does so before dinking a shot over the oncoming Courtois, but the attempt bounces off the inside of the woodwork! So unlucky!
--- 86’ Substitution Willian is done for the day. Ramires is his replacement. ---
(86’) It has took 86 minutes but finally we see Courtois slightly troubled in between the sticks. Amalfitano catches the goalkeeper off-guard with a header at the back post, which certainly has the Belgian scrambling, but in the end it goes just wide.
(84’) Chelsea make their third change in quick succession and it sees Ramires introduced to the action in place of Willian. Mourinho just adding some legs in midfield as they look to professionally see out the remainder of this match.
--- 83’ Substitution D. Drogba comes on for Diego Costa. ---
--- 83’ Substitution J. Obi Mikel enters the game and replaces Oscar. ---
(82’) First changes of the match from Jose Mourinho and it comes with just under 10 minutes remaining. Diego Costa is given a rest with Didier Drogba coming on, with John Obi Mikel also given a run out in place of Oscar, who has been terrific out there today.
(80’) Azpilicueta receives a lovely pass from Terry and then goes on a marauding run down the left before cutting inside. The Spaniard fizzes a cross into the feet of Diego Costa, who dummies for Willian, but Cresswell reads it well to make the interception.
(78’) Song once again finds Amalfitano down the right and the Frenchman cuts inside before returning the favour to the on-loan Barcelona man. Unfortunately for West Ham, the resulting strike on goal has plenty of power behind it but very little direction.
(76’) Song does well whilst under pressure from a few Chelsea players inside the centre circle to find Amalfitano. The substitute digs out a wicked cross into the box, which certainly interests Sakho, but it is food and drink for Courtois who picks the ball out of the air with ease.
--- 74’ Substitution M. Amalfitano comes on for S. Downing. ---
(74’) Third and final change from Allardyce now and it sees Downing coming off to be replaced by Morgan Amalfitano. The Hammers are running out of time to claw a goal back here and ensure a tense finish to the match for the hosts.
(72’) Incredible block from Winston Reid! Diego Costa tees up the ball superbly for Oscar who runs into the box and absolutely slams a strike towards goal, but the New Zealand international bravely charges down the shot with a brilliant challenge! That was definitely heading in before that interception!
(70’) West Ham get a rare corner kick opportunity now. It is a decent enough set piece but Courtois takes all the pressure completely off his defence by commandingly coming off his line to claim the ball out of the air. The Belgian has had very little to do today, but he is still as alert as ever.
(68’) Adrian again! The resulting corner kick from Oscar's saved free kick is swung into the box and Cahill glances to the back post. Matic just can't stretch out his leg enough to get a decent connection on the ball, which allows the Spaniard to make the block with his leg!
(67’) What a save from Adrian!!! In yet another Chelsea set piece 25 yards out, Oscar is given another chance for a crack at goal. The Brazilian fires the best free kick of the match directly towards the top corner but the West Ham keeper stretches out a fingertip to turn the strike over the bar!
(66’) Poor miss from Diego Costa! Hazard spreads the play with a wonderful pass down the right wing to Ivanovic, who swings an absolutely sensational cross to the back post. The former Atletico Madrid striker meets it but sends his volley miles over! That crossed deserved better; what a goal that would have been!
(64’) West Ham look to respond immediately as Valencia opens up his stride through the middle before making his way into the box. Courtois eventually does brilliantly to come off his line and claw the ball away from the feet of the Ecuadorian.
--- 62’ Assist E. Hazard provided the assist. ---
--- 62’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLLL FOR CHELSEA! THE BLUES DOUBLE THEIR LEAD!!! Kouyate gives the ball away poorly away in midfield and the home side pounce with a counterattack. Possession eventually finds Diego Costa and he takes on an couple of defenders before shifting the ball on to his left foot and smashing a strike into the bottom right corner! Two-nil! ---
(60’) Not the best first few touches from Song as the Barcelona loanee initially does well to hold off the challenge of Oscar, but then sends his attempted pass to Jenkinson straight into the stand.
--- 59’ Substitution A. Carroll is done for the day. D. Sakho is his replacement. ---
--- 59’ Substitution M. Noble is replaced with A. Song. ---
--- 58’ Yellow card W. Reid is cautioned by the referee. ---
(58’) Sam Allardyce makes his first changes of the match here and it is a double substitution. Mark Noble and Andy Carroll are coming off and they'll be replaced by Alex Song and Diafra Sakho. With the former Liverpool man now off, this may signal a change in tactic from the Hammers as they will want to utilise the pace they now possess in attack.
(56’) Brilliant defending from Terry. Carroll and Valencia finally manage to link up through the middle with the Ecuadorian latching on to a scooped pass through the middle. The West Ham man looks poised to burst into the box but the Chelsea captain is on hand to clear with a very brave header.
(54’) Hazard and Diego Costa link up once again on the edge of the box and the former's feet are just too quick for the West Ham defenders, which means Reid is forced into committing the foul 20 yards out. A very useful position for a set piece opportunity for Chelsea here.
(52’) SAVE FROM ADRIAN! Willian leads the Chelsea charge with a penetrative run through the middle and then slips a pass down the left for Hazard. The Belgian typically cuts inside on his right foot before slamming a strike at goal, but the West Ham keepers makes another solid stop!
(50’) Much, much better from West Ham now. The visitors are just beginning to press Chelsea's defence in advanced areas and as a result they are finally getting some joy in an attacking sense. It will still be worrying Allardyce as to how little Courtois has been tested, though.
(48’) We are only three minutes into this second half now but already we are seeing quite the feud developing between Valencia and Ivanovic down the left wing. The Ecuadorian has twice managed to get in behind the Chelsea man in the last few moments, but their was no end product on those occasions.
(46’) We are back under way in this London derby!
Half time at Stamford Bridge. So far it has been a Chelsea performance that will greatly satisfy Jose Mouinho. The home side have been completely dominant in possession and look dangerous whenever the have the ball in advanced areas. Their control of the match paid off just after the half hour mark when Terry scored from a yard out to make it 1-0. West Ham not out of the match due to the size of their deficit, but they'll need to buck up their ideas if they are to get anything out of this. Interesting second period in store!
(45’) Well we've got a bit of a melee at the moment as Ivanovic goes down far too easily inside the box under the challenge of Carroll. Both sets of players are involved in some pushing and shoving but the referee defuses the situation quickly and doesn't brandish a yellow. Sensible from Michael Oliver.
(43’) The home side really are playing some lovely stuff in and around the opposition box here. Every forward thinking player is getting involved in some way or another and the current move ends as Matic powers his way into the penalty area before winning the corner out of Reid.
(41’) Chelsea enjoy a period of sustained possession on the edge of the box and then Hazard eventually unlocks the West Ham defence with a lovely pass down the channel for Ivanovic. The right-back then fires a cross into the box which Diego Costa meets, but the resulting strike goes over by a few yards.
(39’) Diego Costa and Oscar link up on the edge of the box with a couple of neat passes and the former eventually bursts forward before getting a shot away. The strike takes a deflection on the way through and has Adrian scrambling across, but eventually goes out for yet another Chelsea corner.
(37’) One of West Ham's main problems so far has been their inability to get Carroll into the match in advanced areas. The former Newcastle man has been on the periphery of the action, with very little service being provided for him aerially or on the ground.
(35’) Hazard feeds the ball into the feet of Matic and the big Serbian tries his luck with a 25-yard strike. It is a decent attempt curled towards the bottom corner but Adrian gets across goal to tip it round the post, awarding Chelsea another corner in the process. Let's see if the hosts can be a danger from another set piece.
--- 33’ Yellow card A. Cresswell receives a yellow card. ---
(33’) West Ham are going to have to be careful not to lose their heads here, as there are definite signs of frustration out there. Cresswell is the latest Hammers player to go into the book and it is for an extremely late and potentially dangerous challenge on Oscar. Deserved yellow.
--- 31’ Assist Diego Costa provided the assist. ---
--- 31’ Goal! GOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLL FOR CHELSEA!!! THE HOSTS OPEN THE SCORING! A corner kick is sent into the box and Diego Costa rises high to glance a header to the back post, where Terry is on hand to smash in from a yard out! One-nil! ---
(29’) We get our first booking of the match now and it has to be said that Collins is very unlucky to be on the end of a yellow. Diego Costa runs through the middle and looks to be making his way into the box, before going down under the challenge of the Welshman, who actually takes the ball.
--- 28’ Yellow card J. Collins receives a yellow card. ---
(27’) Chelsea get the free kick opportunity around 30 yards from goal and Oscar is the man tasked with hitting it. The Brazilian curls the set piece up and down over the ball but the direction isn't totally there as it ends up flying wide. Not the worst attempt but Adrian had it covered.
(25’) West Ham enjoy a period of possession at the back and Collins finds Jenkinson with a pass out wide. The Arsenal loanee fires an excellent pass down the right channel for Downing, but the Englishman is well marshalled by Azpilicueta, who wins the ball.
(23’) Hazard picks up possession just outside the centre circle and dazzles the crowd with five or six completely scintillating touches of the ball. In the end it takes no less than four West Ham players to stop him, with Jenkinson eventually putting out for a Chelsea throw in.
(21’) What a fantastic save from Adrian!! A Chelsea corner is swept into the box and the ball drops kindly for Cahill, who slams a volley towards the top corner, but the West Ham keeper somehow gets across goal to make the block! Superb goalkeeping there!
(19’) Fabregas collects the ball on the edge of the box and dinks a pass through to find the run of Hazard, who probably could go down under the challenge of Reid but opts to stay on his feet and eventually winning the corner kick. Chelsea turning up the heat on the visitors!
(17’) Matic gets into an advanced position down the left wing and lashes a cross into the box, but Reid takes it off the head of Willian with a commanding clearance. West Ham counterattack with pace and the ball eventually comes to Downing, who earns a corner kick out of Azpilicueta.
(15’) Willian pops up through the middle this time and fires a pass into the feet of Diego Costa, who attempts to shift back on to his right foot in order to get a shot away, but the West Ham defence remains solid to make the important block.
(13’) Decent start to the match from Chelsea here as they assert their dominance over the ball in the early stages. Perhaps predictably, Hazard is the brightest player out there at the moment as he continually looks to break into spaces in and around the box.
(11’) Carroll receives a ticking off from referee, Michael Oliver, for going in with his studs up on Ivanovic. It actually looked like a pretty good challenge from the West Ham striker, but the ref deems it as a little too overly aggressive and blows for the foul.
(9’) Some lovely stuff by the home side at the moment. Willian once again bursts down the right-hand side but then leaves the defender for dead by shifting back on to his left. Matic collects possession at the edge of the box and clips a cross to the back post, which Cahill meets with a commanding header, but Adrian sees it over.
(7’) Hazard drops deep and fizzes a pass in behind the West Ham defence for Diego Costa. The Spain international does brilliantly to make up the ground to collect the ball near the corner flag, and receives an appreciative clap from the home crowd.
(5’) Whaaaaaat a miss from Oscar! Willian skips down the right channel and then reverses what looks like a nothing cross into the box. Jenkinson decides to leave it and Chelsea's No.8 collects before driving towards goal, but his subsequent shot is blazed over! The Hammers let off the hook massively there!
(3’) Some worrying scenes for Chelsea at the moment as Hazard is currently down injured after a collision with Kouyate. The Belgian was originally a doubt today with an ankle injury, only to eventually be passed fit. This looks like a hip problem, although he'll probably be okay to continue.
(1’) We are under way at Stamford Bridge!
The players have took to the field and we are almost ready for kick-off. Should be interesting to see West Ham's tactics today as they had success last season by being solid defensively and sitting back, but this campaign they have displayed some exciting attacking prowess.
Chelsea are currently the only team in English football to have a 100% record at home in the league, and Mourinho's men will be hoping to come out of this busy festive period unscathed.
The Hammers are flying in the Barclays Premier League at the moment and currently find themselves situated in the last Champions League position in fourth place. The signings of the likes of Alex Song, Diafra Sakho, and Enner Valencia have catapulted them into European contenders. Another success story coming out of Upton Park recently is the resurgence of Andy Carroll, who has been in superb form since returning from injury.
Rather infamously, this match last year between Chelsea and West Ham ended in a 0-0 stalemate, with Mourinho accusing Sam Allardyce and his men of playing "football from the 19th century". These comments resulted in a heated exchange of words between the two managers, so there is definitely an added air of tension about the clash today.
Jose Mourinho's outfit have the opportunity with this early kick off to open up a six-point gap on Manchester City at the top of the table. The Citizens don't play until 3pm today, so a victory today for Chelsea would certainly heap the pressure on their nearest rivals.
West Ham Subs: Jaaskelainen, O'Brien, Song, Amalfitano, Jarvis, Cole, Sakho.
West Ham (4-3-1-2): Adrian; Jenkinson, Collins, Reid, Cresswell; Noble, Kouyate, Nolan; Downing; Carroll, Valencia.
Chelsea subs: Cech, Zouma, Filipe Luis, Mikel, Ramires, Schurrle, Drogba.
Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Ivanovic, Cahill, Terry, Azpilicueta; Fabregas, Matic; Willian, Oscar, Hazard; Diego Costa.
