As always, thank you for joining us for today's LIVE text commentary of the clash between Burnley and Liverpool at Turf Moor. I'm Matthew Judge and it has been a great pleasure talking you through all the action. We hope to see you again very soon!
For Liverpool, they have moved up to ninth in the table thanks to Sterling's winner, with Tottenham and Swansea also picking up victories today to stop the Reds climbing even higher. Next up for Rodgers' men is a home clash against the Swans at Anfield next Monday.
Next up for Burnley is a trip to reigning Premier League champions Manchester City at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday, with the Clarets set to slip to 19th in the table as Hull City close in on a 3-1 win at Sunderland elsewhere in the top-flight today.
Sterling's sixth goal of the season in all competitions has ended Burnley's good run of form on home soil, with the Clarets' best chance of the game today falling to Ings, who saw a shot hit the post and bounce clear in the first-half.
FULL-TIME!! A second-half Raheem Sterling goal is enough to give Liverpool a 1-0 win against Burnley at Turf Moor on Boxing Day. The Clarets are left to rue a lack of cutting edge in the final third, having played so well for most of the match.
--- 90’ +3 Substitution B. Mee is replaced with L. Jutkiewicz. ---
(90’) 'We love you, Liverpool' is being bellowed out from the away stand as the travelling Merseysiders stand on the brink of a crucial away win. Burnley are throwing on Jutkiewicz with just minutes left.
(90’) The officials have indicated that there will be a minimum of three additional minutes added onto this second-half, with Burnley currenly in possession in Liverpool's half.
(89’) Mee breaks down the left hand side and drives a low cross towards Mignolet's goal, which Can converts behind for a Burnley corner. Trippier's resulting set-piece fails to pick out a target, though.
(88’) Henderson breaks down the left hand side and plays a reverse pass into the path of Sterling, who guides a right-footed effort just over Heaton's crossbar and into the stands. Still 0-1 to Liverpool.
(87’) Boyd comes off the right flank and latches onto Trippier's cross but fires wide of the post, with Arfield making a great dart just to his right.
(85’) We are just five minutes away from any additional time being heaped onto this second-half. Burnley are running out of time to score an equaliser.
--- 83’ Substitution D. Jones is done for the day. R. Wallace is his replacement. ---
(83’) Burnley are definitely tiring after putting in a colossal shift in terms of covering a lot of ground and putting Liverpool under intense pressure at times. Liverpool are starting to exploit that by finding more gaps to move into.
--- 82’ Yellow card Lucas Leiva is cautioned by the referee. ---
(81’) Liverpool play the ball out from defence and work possession to Sterling, who runs right at the heart of the Burnley defence before feeding an onrushing Lallana, who drives a shot straight at the diving legs of Shackell. Still 0-1 to Liverpool.
--- 80’ Substitution S. Vokes comes on for A. Barnes. ---
(78’) Trippier curls in a teasing corner which Mignolet parries straight to Mee, who guides a pass back to Marney lurking outside the box but Sakho does brilliantly to block his path before Henderson clears up the pitch.
(76’) Ings shifts the ball from his right foot onto his left foot nicely and beats Skrtel before driving a shot just wide of Mignolet between the sticks. One of Burnley's heroes from last season's successful Championship campaign, Vokes, is stripped and ready to come on.
(74’) NO GOAL!! Lambert latches onto Gerrard's brilliant first-time pass and fires the ball past Heaton to send Liverpool fans into rapture, only for the linesman on the near side to chalk the goal off for offside.
--- 73’ Substitution Philippe Coutinho is replaced with R. Lambert. ---
(73’) Barnes latches onto Arfield's pass and plays in Ings, only for Skrtel to come across and swipe away the danger. Burnley are starting to get more numbers forward now.
(71’) Trippier heads softly towards Markovic, who drives a shot straight at the left boot of Keane. Liverpool continue to pressurise Burnley's defence and Coutinho finds a bit of space to win a corner from a blocked effort.
(69’) It will be interesting to see what Burnley boss Dyche now does to try and see his side claw their way back into this game. They have played excellently for large spells and have a few options on the bench they can turn to if needed.
(68’) BIG CHANCE!! Mignolet gifts Burnley a golden chance to level the score by letting the ball run out of play for a corner. Trippier curls in a beauty, which Mignolet punched out well, but another cross from the Clarets' full-back was headed just wide by Shackell at the back post.
(66’) All the noise is now coming from the away end, with the travelling Reds not having a lot to sing about before Sterling's opener. Burnley have dominated this game for large spells but now look completely deflated since conceding against the run of play.
(64’) Henderson does well to bring the ball down from Shackell's header, but Coutinho's flicked pass, which baffled Burney's two centre-backs, to set Sterling off in his tracks was an incredible bit of skill. Game on here at Turf Moor.
--- 62’ Assist The assist came from Philippe Coutinho. ---
--- 62’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAALLLLLL!!! Liverpool take the lead after Coutinho plays a magnificent pass over the top of Burnley's defence for Sterling to run onto, with the forward taking the ball around Heaton to tap into an empty net. ---
(60’) Barnes brings down Jones' punt up the pitch but is barged down by Can towards the byline, with referee Taylor not interested in the home supporters' appeals for a free-kick.
(58’) Liverpool enjoy a rare spell of possession inside Burnley's half but Dyche's men soon put their foot on the accelerator to force the Reds back towards Mignolet. It's difficult to predict whether a goal will come today based on what we're seeing, in all honesty.
(56’) Henderson plays a long ball towards Lallana, who brings the ball down well and skips away from two Burnley defenders before Keane comes across to deflect the ball towards Heaton, who gobbles it up under no pressure.
(54’) Jones finds a bit of space in the centre of the pitch and sprays a great through ball to Mee breaking down the left, but the full-back's cross was well saved by Mignolet. The Belgian throws the ball out quickly and Liverpool win a throw-in deep into Burnley's half after some good work from Lallana down the right.
(52’) Liverpool win a free-kick in midfield and Gerrard plays it quickly to Lallana, who marauds through the middle and feeds Coutinho making tracks down the left, with the Brazilian moving just offside when the ball was played.
(50’) Burnley certainly haven't looked like a side scrapping near the bottom of the Premier League today. The Clarets have started the second-half the better of the two teams so far, with Liverpool struggling to get out of their own half.
(47’) It seems that, from first impressions, Can has come on as a like-for-like replacement for Toure. The youngster has so far slotted into Toure's right-sided centre-back position and has barely budged from it.
--- 46’ Substitution E. Can enters play, replacing K. Touré. ---
(46’) Welcome back! Liverpool get us underway for the second-half here at Turf Moor, with the only change being Emre Can has come on for Toure.
As things currenly stand in the Premier League at half-time, Burnley will move out of the relegation zones into 17th if results across the league stay the same at full-time, while Liverpool would also move up one place to ninth.
Reds boss Rodgers will surely have a lot to say to his players at half-time, with his side barely conjuring up anything positive to note. Liverpool turned up in first gear for the opening 45 minutes and while Burnley didn't allow them much time to play their game, the Merseysiders need to inject more urgency if they're to seriously threaten Burnley's untroubled defence.
HALF-TIME! Burnley and Liverpool head into the break with the score level at 0-0. The Clarets were comfortably the busier of the two sides but crucially couldn't manage to turn their dominance into goals.
(45’) The officials have indicated that there will be just one minute added onto this first-half. Burnley have been fantastic in the opening 45 minutes, with the only criticism being that they haven't manage to score while they've been so on top.
(43’) Trippier chucks in a lovely cross towards the back post, with Barnes knocking the ball down before Skrtel clears straight to Marney, but the Burnley midfielder could only fire wide of the goal.
(41’) Keane presses energetically to nick the ball off Lucas in midfield before feeding Arfield, who plays a lofted pass over the top of the Liverpool defence, with Mignolet getting to the ball just before Barnes, who was closing him down. It's all Burnley.
(38’) Barnes beats Skrtel in the air to knock the ball down to an onrushing Boyd, who drives a shot just wide of the post, with Mignolet at full stretch. Liverpool have been really under the cosh in the last ten minutes.
(36’) ALMOST! Burnley come so close to taking the lead, only for Lucas to get his side out of trouble. Trippier curls in a teasing corner which is unconvincingly punched by Mignolet straight to Arfield, who found his low shot fly just past the post thanks to a crucial block by Lucas.
(34’) Great spell of dominance from Burnley! Trippier curls in a dangerous cross which Sakho clears only to Marney, with the midfielder playing a lovely reverse ball to Boyd, who couldn't pick out a Burnley man inside the box before Skrtel clears for a corner.
(31’) Sakho clears Trippier's cross to set Liverpool off and running up the pitch but the Reds' move soon breaks down as Shackell beats Sterling for height with the ball up for grabs in the air. Liverpool could really do with a physical presence up top to compete against this Burnley defence today.
(29’) CHANCE! Gerrard plays a quality first-time pass to set Lallana off running down the left hand side, but the midfielder cuts inside only to drive a shot straight down the throat of Heaton in the Burnley goal.
(27’) Boyd carries the ball for a long distance through the middle of the pitch but Markovic does well to close him down and win possession back for Liverpool. The former Hull City winger has been very lively in this first-half.
(24’) Gerrard curls in a corner towards the back post, but Henderson can only drive his shot straight at Shackell as the danger clears. Burnley still remain on the front foot at the moment.
(21’) Mignolet almost comes in for a moment of madness after delaying his punt up the pitch before driving it straight at Barnes, which went wide of the goal. There is a real lack of urgency in Liverpool's game at the moment and they need to up their tempo.
(19’) Burnley boss Dyche will be delighted with the start his side have made to this game. Liverpool aren't putting enough pressure on the Clarets so far and are giving possession away too cheaply at times.
(18’) Boyd drifts in from the right hand side towards the centre of the pitch to play a neat one-two with Ings before playing a reverse cross towards the Burnley striker from the left, but Skrtel clears for Liverpool.
--- 16’ Substitution S. Mignolet enters the game and replaces B. Jones. ---
(15’) Liverpool are making an early change in goal as Jones is coming off for Mignolet after just 15 minutes, with the Australian shot-stopper understood to have picked up a thigh injury. Mignolet's first action will be to take a goal-kick.
(14’) CHANCE!! Arfield feeds Ings with a nice pass from the left flank before the Burnley striker spins onto his right foot and drives a low shot, which leaves Jones flat-footed between the sticks but strikes the post.
(13’) Coutinho and Sterling interchange nicely outside the box, with the Brazilian taking the ball forward before driving a low shot towards goal, which was gobbled up easily by Heaton.
(11’) Coutinho plays a quick one-two with Henderson down the right and switches possession brilliantly to Markovic, but the Serbian youngster fails to pick out any of his team-mates in yellow with his hanging cross. Good break from the visitors.
(9’) Sterling spins into space and drives forward towards Keane in the Burnley defence with little support from his Liverpool team-mates, with the Clarets man able to stop the Reds forward in his tracks and snuff out the danger.
(8’) Markovic breaks forward and plays a lovely chipped pass towards Sterling, who chests the ball down inside the box and feeds Lallana, but the former Southampton midfielder couldn't quite get possession under control as Burnley clear up the pitch.
(5’) Boyd thrusts forward down the right hand side before cutting a ball back to Marney, who curls his shot straight at Skrtel. A minutes applause is ringing around Turf Moor in honour of ex-Burnley defender Clarke Carlisle, who was tragically hit by a lorry on Monday.
(3’) Arfield latches onto Mee's pass down the left and beats Henderson far too easily at the byline before driving a low ball to Ings, who couldn't quite sort his feet out in the box before slicing a shot straight at Jones.
(1’) Burnley get us underway here at a lively Turf Moor. The man in charge of the cards today is Anthony Taylor.
TEAM NEWS: Liverpool manager Rodgers has named an unchanged starting eleven for the first time this season. Mario Balotelli returns to the squad, while 17-year-old talent Sheyi Ojo - who has impressed in recent weeks since being promoted from the Reds' academy - makes the bench.
TEAM NEWS: Burnley boss Sean Dyche has kept the faith by making no changes to his side which narrowly lost 2-1 to Tottenham in their last Premier League outing. Danny Ings, who has scored 50% of the Clarets' goals so far this season, starts up top in a 4-4-2 system, while Sam Vokes returns to the bench after a nine month lay-off with a knee problem.

LIVERPOOL (3-4-3): Jones; Toure, Skrtel, Sakho; Henderson, Gerrard (c), Lucas Leiva, Markovic; Coutinho, Sterling, Lallana.
BURNLEY substitutes: Gilks, Reid, Wallace, Kightly, Long, Jutkiewicz, Vokes.

This fixture was, of course, not contested last season as Burnley were in the Championship during the 2013/14 campaign, but Liverpool did win both Premier League matches against today's hosts 4-0 during the Clarets' only season in the Premier League in 2009/10.
The travelling Reds, who have previously lost both Boxing Day fixtures under Brendan Rodgers' tutelage, have, however, played well in their last two games against Manchester United and Arsenal, while Burnley are unbeaten in their last four home matches.
Today's match sees two teams looking to fix their patchy runs of form in the top-flight lock horns. Burnley, who have won just one of their last five Premier League games, will be hoping to move out of the drop zone with a positive result against Liverpool, who haven't won in their last three games.
Hello and welcome to our LIVE text commentary of today's Premier League Boxing Day clash between Burnley and Liverpool at Turf Moor. We hope you all had a great Christmas, I'm Matthew Judge and I will be your host for the match, which kicks off in 30 minutes time.

That's all from me, I've been Keeghann Sinanan and it's been fun!
The referee blows the final whistle and Southampton are heading back into the top four. A supremely professional performance from the visitors, who never looked back after that 17th minute opener from the impressive Mane. Bertrand and Alderweireld did the further damage, rendering Dann's late goal nothing but consolation.
(90’) McArthur takes aim with a curler but for the umpteenth time it's right at Forster in the Saints goal. He's not been critically tested often, but has made no mistake with the routine tasks asked of him.
(89’) Too little too late for Crystal Palace I'm afraid. It's not going to change this result. They almost get in again though, but Gardos is on hand to block. He's had an assured time in his first EPL start.
--- 87’ Substitution J. McCarthy comes on for N. Clyne. ---
--- 86’ Assist The assist came from M. Jedinak. ---
--- 86’ Goal! FINALLY SOME RELIEF! Jedinak launches the set piece into the box and Dann gets ahead of Wanyama to plant a header into the bottom corner. ---
(85’) Free kick coming up for the home side after Zaha uses his skill to trick Bertrand into a foul. Plenty of bodies forward and this may be a chance for them to get a goal back on the board.
(82’) Wanyama shows great poise to burst past four players with a marauding run from his own half. However, when it comes time to pick out a pass for Long, his ball is just off his run.
(79’) Ward-Prowse pulls out the Christmas crackers to flick a lovely ball into the path of Clyne. The full-back storms past multiple players before Delaney takes a chunk out of him. Yellow card.
--- 77’ Yellow card D. Delaney is cautioned by the referee. ---
(76’) Turning into a bit of a training-ground exercise as Palace's attempts to get back into the game are falling into a red-and-white wall. I'm afraid that they will be battling relegation all season with this kind of form.
(73’) Should this result and others around the Premier League hold till full time, then Southampton will be heading back into the top four. However, Palace will see themselves sucked into 18th place and the relegation zone.
--- 72’ Substitution M. Kelly comes on for Y. Bolasie. ---
--- 72’ Substitution S. Long enters the game and replaces G. Pellè. ---
(71’) Mane has been absolutely superb. We all know about his mobility and athleticism, but it's his deft touches on the ball and composure that have caught my eye especially. He's going to be a huge hit at the AFCON of he's in this kind of form.
(69’) MANE! What special play from the Senegalese, who leaves multiple men eating his dust once again before letting fly from a different zip code. However, Speroni watches it bend menacingly over the bar!
--- 67’ Substitution W. Zaha enters play, replacing J. Ledley. ---
(67’) Zaha comes on for Ledley in a change that's about 10 minutes too late in my opinion. The Manchester United loanee can at least be counted upon to stretch the defence with his speed.
(65’) Southampton have dealt with the huffs and puffs from Palace with supreme comfort. In fact, it looks more likely for them to grab a fourth on the break rather than the hosts getting a foothold in the game again.
(63’) Puncheon has had his moments breaking at pace today, and another determined run sees him cut onto his left foot and set Gayle up for a header, but Gardos is in position to divert the effort.
(61’) Pelle gives away a free kick after dallying on the ball, and Jedinak manages to get the ball back into the danger area, but the Saints defence can clear before any interested parties.
(59’) With the job seemingly done and dusted, Koeman decides to pull his captain Davis, who tosses the armband to Schneiderlin on his way off the pitch. Busy period on deck so smart to rest key men when you can.
(57’) Fair to say that a lot of the Selhurst Park faithful have had the stuffing knocked out of them after that two-goal Saints salvo. There's still a dedicated corner of the fans singing their lungs out, but it's not looking good for their team.
--- 56’ Substitution S. Davis is replaced with V. Wanyama. ---
(55’) It's really been pantomime defending from Crystal Palace at times. Practically each goal could have been stopped with some more dedication and awareness, not to mention communication between the defenders.
--- 53’ Assist Assist by J. Ward-Prowse. ---
--- 53’ Goal! ANOTHER FOR SOUTHAMPTON! Too simple as Ward-Prowse clips in a corner to the centre of the goal, and Alderweireld simply rises above his marker to plant a header home. ---
(50’) Now Crystal Palace really have a mountain to climb. Saints will most likely sit even deeper now, happy to invite the pressure on to them and pick the hosts off on the break whenever the opportunity presents itself.
--- 49’ Substitution D. Gayle enters the game and replaces F. Campbell. ---
--- 48’ Assist S. Mané gave the assist. ---
--- 48’ Goal! DIDN'T TAKE LONG! SAINTS TWO UP! Mane tricks his way into contention down the byline and decides to turn provider, sliding a low ball to the back post. From there, Bertrand arrives and cracks a lovely first-time effort into the back of the net! ---
(46’) We're back in action.
The first half ends with Southampton holding a narrow 1-0 lead. They took advantage of a defensive lapse as Mane stole in to score the opener. However, the game never kicked on from that 17th minute explosion, with the visitors' cautious approach proving an effective repellent to Palace's desire to get back into the game. I'll be back with the second half in just a bit.
(45’) Late free kick for Saints to end the half and they pile bodies into the box in a bid to steal a sucker-punch right before the break. However, the delivery from Ward-Prowse fails to trouble the opposition.
(43’) Not much happening in the final few minutes of this half. Southampton have wrangled a decent spell of possession as of late, but overall, they're not really making a dent in the Palace ranks.
(41’) Ward-Prowse takes advantage of Palace's hesitancy to clear a high ball, and guides a header towards goal. Speroni looks in trouble, but it bounces onto the roof of the net with an audible 'Oooh' from the crowd.
(39’) Southampton have switched to a 4-5-1 in the last few minutes, which is not surprising if you've watched the passage of play recently. It's been all about absorbing pressure inside their own half, but Saints have shown little desire to get back and counter.
(37’) Ward-Prowse misses the target, moments before Puncheon does the same down at the other end. The quality in this game has rather gone dry, and it's clear that Southampton, at least, are already looking towards half time.
(35’) After dominating the ball in the early exchanges, Southampton are playing most of the game off it. The stats tell the story, as they have only 33 per cent of the overall possession since the first whistle.
(33’) Puncheon sees a shot blocked as Palace continue to improve with every passing minute. Koeman will not be happy that his side have sat back this comfortably on a lead that is anything but.
(31’) Bolaise manipulates his way to the byline and has the position and space to angle in a cross. Campbell is aiming to get on the end of it, but Yoshida uses his body to block him - legally.
(29’) Ledley pulls the trigger with his left foot but sends the ball into the afternoon sky. Still, Palace are getting some shots away as of late, which must be encouraging for Neil Warnock.
(27’) Jedinak takes aim from the edge of the area but Forster, not for the first time, is honed into Palace's effort from long distance. The hosts may need to get closer to goal in order to really trouble the keeper.
(25’) It's taken only 25 minutes into his first Premier League start for Gardos to pick up a booking. He couldn't slow down in time to avoid clattering into Bolaise, and the referee makes a note of his name.
(23’) Just like that, Mane nearly acts on my words in the last post. He's too quick for Dann on a long punt, and with the defender and Speroni leaving the ball for each other, he nips between the pair to score again. However, the flag is up and that is a massive let off for Palace.
(21’) Mane's speed off the mark is incredible, and causing Palace all kinds of problems. Southampton can afford to sit deep and prevent the hosts from getting in behind, confident that they always have the outlet in the Senegalese.
(19’) The fans haven't been dejected by that opener too much, roaring their team on whenever they get back on the ball. However, this leaves them with all to do, especially considering their lack of goalscoring prowess at home.
--- 17’ Assist Assist by J. Ward-Prowse. ---
--- 17’ Goal! OPENER! SAINTS IN FRONT! That's exactly what Koeman was looking for. Crystal Palace are slow to move the ball through midfield, andWard-Prowse is presented with the chance to one-touch a pass behind the defence for Mane, who rounds Speroni and slots in from a tight angle. ---
(15’) A series of fouls in the middle of the park have broken up the flow of play. Koeman is bellowing instructions on the touchline, clearly wanting his team to keep pressing and getting men in advanced positions.
(13’) That last attack from Crystal Palace had some purpose, but generally, the visitors have been the side who have showed more danger and intent on the ball. Both teams have ramped up the intensity again.
(11’) CLOSE CALL FOR SOUTHAMPTON! A lightning-quick attack from Palace sees them advance through the centre with Saints always back pedaling. Puncheon gets the ball laid off for a shot from the top of the box and pulls the trigger, but it's right at Forster!
(9’) Not much of the play is being focused down the flanks, as the lack of movement off the ball from wingers and full backs has seen the ball worked centrally more often than not.
(7’) Southampton are holding a lot of the ball, daring Palace to commit men forward to press. The home side aren't biting so far though, and we're seeing a more cautious tone to play as a result.
(5’) Now back down at the other end, Campbell cracks an effort over the top of the bar after a good setup from McArthur. A lovely tempo developing to this game from the off, with both teams keen to get forward.
(3’) A really ingenious attempt from Alderweireld, who hooks a clearance from a corner back towards goal from at least 35 yards. He caught that with so much power and accuracy that it nearly catches Speroni off his line, but the keeper scrambles back in time to tip it over.
(1’) We're off!
Morgan Schneiderlin is back to man the midfield after shaking off a thigh injury in time to start. Florian Gardos is granted his initial start in the Premier League, while Sadio Mane is recalled. Meanwhile, Palace make two changes from the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City, with Adrian Mariappa and Damien Delaney replacing Brede Hangeland and Martin Kelly.
Southampton (4-3-3): Forster; Yoshida, Alderweireld, Gardos, Clyne; Schneiderlin, Ward-Prowse, S. Davis; Bertrand, Mane, Pelle.
Crystal Palace (4-3-3): Speroni; Mariappa, Dann, Delaney, Ward; Jedinak, McArthur, Ledley; Bolaise, Puncheon, Campbell.
Crystal Palace have lost their last five games in this fixture without scoring a single goal. That's been a general problem for the Eagles at Selhurst Park this season, with only nine goals in eight games. In fact, throughout the 10-game history of this fixture in the Premier League, the London outfit have never taken all three points.
Southampton just ended a five-match winless streak of their own recently, with a 3-0 win over Everton last Saturday getting things back to normal. Still, that questionable run of form has seen them surrender their place in the top four to West Ham, who they now trail by two points.
The home side haven't tasted victory in five games, a run which has seen them slip to one place above the relegation zone - only goal difference separates them from that particular black hole. However, the Eagles have only ever lost once in five Boxing Day fixtures.
Hello and welcome back to the Premier League. Hope you all ate and drank yourselves into enough of a stupor over the holiday to survuve our mini break without EPL football. Today we're in London as low-hanging Crystal Palace host high-flying Southampton. I'm Keeghann Sinanan, your designated scribe.

Boos ring around Goodison Park, with Stoke enjoying a solid performance, but plenty of the onus falls upon the referee! After failing to send off both Walters and Adam, the home fans have every right to feel slightly aggrieved. The Toffees continue their awful record without a comeback win! I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again next time!
FULL TIME! Stoke take a much-needed three points home from Goodison Park, courtesy of a fantastic defensive performance which gifts the Potters a rare clean sheet. A penalty conversion from Bojan proved to be enough for Hughes' men, with Everton continuing to really struggle in the Premier League. Another uninspiring performance from the Toffees.
(90’) Eto'o tries to whip a free kick goal ward, but it fails to clear the first man. Stoke break upfield as a result, but Crouch doesn't have the pace to penalise the home side. Adam then appears to kick the ball away to waste time, but the referee lets the Scottish midfielder off. I'm not too sure why, that should have been his second yellow!
--- 90’ +2 Substitution P. Crouch comes on for M. Diouf. ---
(90’) There are four minutes of stoppage time at Goodison Park. Adam has managed to hurt Mirallas, with the Stoke substitute clumsy clashing with the Belgian winger - but he gets back to his feet fairly quickly. Hughes opts to make his final change, with Crouch replacing Diouf for the dying minutes.
--- 90’ Yellow card C. Adam is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) Fantastic tackle from Pieters! That's saved the three points for Stoke! Naismith is picked out in a pocket of space deep in the away side's box, before looking to turn and shoot! As he draws back his boot, the Netherlands international slides in to make a fantastic sliding challenge!
(89’) Barkley tries to dance across the edge of the 18-yard box, but is promptly robbed of possession. The home side are maintaining their pressure but appear to have no means of penetrating the Potters' lines. Not long remains, but Stoke are tiring.
(87’) Walters hacks another clearance upfield, with Stoke having all hands to the defensive pump as we edge towards the 90-minute mark. There are some tired legs in red and white shirts, but they're dragging themselves towards the finish line. This would be a valuable three points for Hughes' men!
(86’) Less than five minutes remain before stoppage time, with the home crowd sitting very uneasily in their seats. Another free kick is flighted into the box, before Pieters heads clear. Stoke are sitting very deep in the dying embers of this game, with blue shirts streaming forward and populating the edge of the area.
(84’) Mirallas breaks to the right byline, before clipping a good cross into the box, but Naismith is unable to stretch enough to make contact! Everton are still trying to find the elusive equaliser, but Begovic has only been forced into pretty routine saves all afternoon.
--- 83’ Yellow card G. Cameron goes into the referee's book. ---
(83’) Barry clips a free-kick delivery into the Stoke box, but the away side clear once again. Cameron is then booked for wasting time with his throw in yet again, meaning that the American international can't be making any risky challenges in the last five minutes or so of normal time.
(81’) Mirallas whips in a corner, which Alcaraz is unable to turn towards goal. Naismith claims the rebound, but is robbed of possession in the box tidily by N'Zonzi. The Potters are looking well on course to a rare clean sheet. Adam shoots from the edge of the box, but Stones makes a good block.
(80’) N'Zonzi is back to his feet after receiving treatment in the wake of Barry's bookable offence. Lukaku unleashes a good effort from 25 yards out, but Begovic is able to make a save and then smother at the second attempt.
--- 78’ Yellow card G. Barry is yellow-carded. ---
(78’) Walters tries to go down claiming a foul on the right-hand side, but is quickly back to his feet after perhaps remembering that he's already on a yellow card. Narrowly over ten minutes of normal time remain, with Barry the latest man to pick up a yellow card.
--- 76’ Substitution M. Arnautović is replaced with O. Assaidi. ---
(76’) Assaidi is allowed to take to the field, with fresh legs high on the agenda for a Stoke side that have done a lot of good chasing - with Arnautovic the man replaced. The Morocco international looks a little bit cold as he jogs on, he will have to get moving and warm pretty quickly!
(75’) Coleman tries to overlap down the right-hand side and receives possession, but Arnautovic tracks back fantastically to deny the Irishman a chance to cross. This has been a team effort from back to front for Stoke this afternoon. Begovic then takes his time to take his goal kick.
(73’) N'Zonzi fires wide! The Frenchman drives from deep, with no blue shirt coming out to meet him, allowing him an attempt from range. Robles gets down to his right-hand side, but the ball zips beyond the far upright anyway, without the need for a touch.
(71’) Baines cuts inside once again, but the Englishman is halted by a solid tackle from N'Zonzi. Barkley is now sitting slightly deeper for the home side to allow Eto'o relative freedom. The substitute appears to be playing directly off of Lukaku.
--- 69’ Substitution S. Eto'o enters play, replacing J. McCarthy. ---
(69’) McCarthy is the deeper player sacrificed by Martinez, with Eto'o added into the offensive mix. If that isn't a clear sign of a side who are going on the prowl for an equaliser, then I don't know what is. The former Barcelona man is immediately involved, but Walters does well to intercept a through ball from the Cameroonian.
--- 67’ Substitution C. Adam enters the game and replaces Bojan. ---
(67’) Barry tries to stab a through ball between right-back and central defender for Mirallas to chase, but Shawcross reads the play well to intercept. Stoke opt to make their first change of the afternoon, with Adam replacing Bojan, perhaps showing Hughes' intent to make his side a tad feistier.
(66’) Pieters whips in a cross from the left-hand side, but it flashes beyond everyone and Robles is happy enough to let it zip out of play for a throw in on the opposite flank. Eto'o appears to be readying himself on the touchline for the home side.
(65’) Arnautovic and Walters are doing good jobs in wide areas to peg back Everton's fullbacks. The England international does manage to scamper inside, however, before trying to pick out a through ball to Naismith which is blocked. The former Wigan defender strikes the rebound first-time, forcing Begovic to parry, before Cameron coolly turns and clears Stoke's lines.
(63’) Lukaku tries to break down the right-hand side, but Muniesa marshals his man, before the Belgian misplaces his next pass. Stoke are looking incredibly comfortable, with Everton only mustering up attempts from range or set pieces. The former Chelsea man shoots from 20 yards, but it's straight at Begovic who collects.
(61’) Everton whip in a corner towards the near post, but Naismith and Lukaku are unable to turn the ball into the back of the net. The Scot's attempted header deflects wide, with the resulting corner headed high and wide of the target by Alcaraz. The away fans cheer sarcastically.
(60’) Stones is looking very uncomfortable on his feet, with Distin perhaps now being mustered to warm up on the sideline. Nothing is going right for the home side this afternoon and they just might rue the referee's decision not to send off Walters in the first half.
(58’) Baines clips a through ball over the top for Lukaku to chase, but Cameron tracks his man and Begovic is quick off his line to slide in and kick clear. Everton might just have to start looking longer to Lukaku, as their normal style of play just isn't getting any joy this afternoon.
(57’) Everton are not looking like a team capable of turning this scoreline around, with arguably their best offensive tools, Baines and Coleman pegged back too deep. Their confidence appears to be shot at, with the home crowd dissatisfied and the Toffees incapable of stringing more than three passes together.
(55’) Good clearance from Alcaraz! Walters sets the ball back to Cameron, who delivers a teasing cross which Diouf can only head downwards. Stones fails to clear his lines, leaving the half-time substitute to blast the ball away. Stoke are pressing forward!
(53’) Everton continue to enjoy the lion's share of possession, but the Toffees just aren't going anywhere with it. It's all well and good that Martinez's system helps retain the ball, but ultimately the hosts are producing nothing. Arnautovic flashes a cross in from the left, but Diouf heads over.
(51’) Bojan spreads play out to the right-hand side, but Walters' cross in towards Diouf at the back post is easily cleared. Stoke recycle the ball, with N'Zonzi delivering a low cross, but the Frenchman's pass deflects off Barry and behind for a corner. Muniesa receives the ball at the near post, but the former Barcelona man sends a drive high into the stands.
(49’) Everton control the ball in the opening exchanges, but Stoke are more than happy to stand off and sit deep to retain their shape. Hughes' men have remained very disciplined. Naismith is nearly picked out by a cross from deep on the right-hand side from Stones, but Begovic is quick off his line to smother the ball.
(47’) Martinez is forced into two changes at the interval, with Alcaraz replacing Jagielka and Joel Robles taking his place in between the posts instead of Howard. Not an ideal start to what needs to be a much-improved 45 minutes.
--- 46’ Substitution A. Alcáraz comes on for P. Jagielka. ---
--- 46’ Substitution Joel Robles enters the game and replaces T. Howard. ---
(46’) We are back underway at Goodison Park! There's a bit of snow in the air, with the home crowd giving the referee a rather frosty reception themselves! Everton need to change things around if they're to get three points today.
HALF TIME! Stoke head into the Goodison Park dressing rooms with a slender 1-0 lead, courtesy of a penalty converted coolly by Bojan. The Potters have looked dangerous on the counter, but the real talking point is whether Walters should still be on the field of play. The Republic of Ireland international hauled Baines down to deny a goalscoring opportunity, but only saw a yellow card brandished towards him by the referee! The home crowd aren't happy, that's for sure, so be sure to stick around for the second half!
(45’) Arnautovic tries his luck from distance, but the Austrian can't keep it down and that is that for the first half of play! Howard appears to have pulled a muscle in his leg and is helped to limp off the field of play.
(45’) Cameron looks to waste as much time as possible while taking a throw in on the right-hand side, infuriating the home fans even further. Stoke definitely aren't here to win any friends, merely points! Naismith picks out Mirallas at the back post with a wonderful pass, but the Belgian slides his finish into the side netting! That should have been the equaliser!
(45’) Arnautovic works his way down the left-hand side well, before looking to feed Diouf! Jagielka comes across well to pressure the former Molde striker, who is forced into blasting an improvised attempt well wide of the near post. Chants of "Arnie!" fill the air from the travelling Potters' faithful.
(45’) Stoke look to calm things down by retaining the ball at a slow tempo. Arnautovic is fed down the left, before Stones makes a good block to deny the Austrian winger a chance to deliver a telling cross. The resulting corner is headed clear by Naismith, of all people. A cross from N'Zonzi then takes a wicked deflection, but Howard makes the save, before Jagielka hooks the rebound away.
(45’) Barry and Bojan go down, with the former looking to turn his ankle, possibly adding further seconds onto this first-half marathon. Everton continue to press, with Lukaku and Naismith exchanging a one-two on the edge of the box, but Shawcross slides in brilliantly to make a vital interception!
(45’) Coleman tries to cut an pass back to Lukaku, but the Belgian has the ball robbed from his boot! The loose ball is recycled by Barry, before the former Man City midfielder curls an attempt towards goal that Begovic smothers with ease! The conditions aren't helping the Stoke goalkeeper here.
(45’) Begovic makes another blunder! The Bosnia international fails to make good contact with a punch, allowing for Naismith to head an effort goalward, but N'Zonzi is positioned well on the line to clear! Everton are turning the screw in this lengthy stint of stoppage time.
(45’) Barry breaks to the byline, before whipping a cross in towards the near post, but Lukaku is only able to send a looping header wide of the target. Begovic looks to claim, but spills the ball behind for a corner under no pressure. There will be TEN minutes of stoppage time.
(44’) Diouf tries to race in behind the hosts' back four, but the former Hannover man is caught narrowly offside - not that it would have mattered anyhow. The Stoke forward slipped over, losing a boot in the process, meaning that he receives rather negative attention from the home fans as he slowly puts it back on under the watchful eye of the referee.
(43’) The away fans are making plenty of noise and will remain in a jolly, festive mood should the scoreline stay the same. Everton attempt to break down the right, but Arnautovic tracks back brilliantly to defuse the situation. Both sides are enjoying counter attacks, but nothing in the way of maintained pressure.
(41’) Less than five minutes of normal time remain until the break, with Whelan managing to avoid a caution once again, despite clipping Naismith. This ground is a smouldering cauldron of unease, but Everton don't deserve to be ahead on the basis of play. Walters' possible red card is most definitely the talking point.
(39’) Bojan and McCarthy have something of a disagreement off the ball, with the two shoving one another! The Everton players are losing their focus somewhat, with the former Wigan midfielder absolutely incensed to have a penalty given against him! Stoke won't mind one bit, they're enjoying a solid away performance thus far.
--- 38’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAL! BOJAN MAKES IT 1-0 TO STOKE! The Spanish forward slides a finish into the bottom-left corner, as Howard guessed the right way but couldn't quite get there! The away side are ahead and Goodison Park is not happy with the referee whatsoever. ---
(37’) PENALTY FOR STOKE! Bojan beats McCarthy for pace down the left-hand side, before breaking to the byline. The Spaniard dances around his marker before appearing to have his heels clipped just inside the box. There was definite contact, but the home crowd aren't happy!
(36’) Walters picks up a yellow card, but Everton are claiming it should have been red! The Republic of Ireland international hauls down Baines as the Englishman looks to break through on goal and it's hard to argue that it wouldn't have been a definite goalscoring opportunity!
--- 35’ Yellow card J. Walters is yellow-carded. ---
(35’) Ten minutes remain until the end of normal time, but we could be playing here until next Christmas, if there are any more injuries! McCarthy tries to slot Lukaku in down the right-hand channel, but Pieters comes across well to put the ball into touch. The Belgian is then denied on the edge of the box by two good blocks in quick succession.
(33’) What a miss from Barry! The Englishman is picked out in plenty of space at the back post, but can only stab an attempt away from goal rather than trying to slot a finish beyond the helpless-looking Begovic! Two great chances in the past minute for the Toffees! The home crowd roar their encouragement!
(32’) Just wide by Mirallas! The Belgium international is picked out at the corner of the 18-yard box, before hammering a venomous effort at goal! It takes a nick off a defender and zips past the near upright and behind for a corner!
(31’) The opening half an hour has seen very little in the way of football, let alone chances. Bojan and Diouf have had the better of the limited opportunities, with Everton unable to get going offensively. Baines and Coleman just haven't got involved whatsoever.
(29’) Good effort from Bojan! Stoke work the ball from right to left smartly, before the former Barcelona man is picked out on the flank. He jinks inside Coleman and races inside, before unleashing a powerful strike from 25 yards out. It dips over the crossbar with Howard happy to watch it sail into the stand behind his goal.
--- 28’ Yellow card S. Naismith gets yellow. ---
(28’) Bojan is now caught by a very clumsy tackle by Naismith, with the Scotland international clattering through his man after the ball had zipped past him. The Everton forward complains, but that is a whole new definition of wasting your breath. A certain foul and a deserved caution.
(26’) Arnautovic is in some discomfort, after a rather naughty tackle from Barry, where the former England international got plenty of the ball but also plenty of the man. The Austrian winger is able to limp off under his own steam, but that's a couple of additional minutes to add onto the already gargantuan total.
(25’) Baines whips in a teasing corner delivery, but Naismith rises and is beaten to the ball! Stoke break as a result, but Bojan is quickly robbed of the ball by Barry, much to the delight of the home fans. Suddenly, the game springs into life with end-to-end action. Arnautovic now goes down! More stoppages.
(23’) Well, this definitely hasn't been a thriller so far! The ball has spent just as much time dead as it has live, with Stoke really able to disrupt Everton's usual possession-based style. The Toffees haven't been able to have a telling spell of pressure in an advanced area of the field.
(21’) Walters is given his final warning of the afternoon, with Jagielka now requiring treatment, as the flow of the game is fractured even further. The Stoke forward pushes his opponent to the floor and then falls onto the Everton defender. This game continues to be less about the football and more about clumsy challenges.
(19’) Jagielka is now caught by Whelan, with the Republic of Ireland international throwing himself into plenty of firm tackles in the opening 20 minutes. Everton are pushing players forward, meaning that interceptions in the midfield third are leaving two-on-two situations in the Toffees' back four. Coleman and Baines provide little defensive protection.
(18’) Neither team are building up any continuous pressure, with both sides giving away the ball in midfield far too cheaply. This game hasn't had anything of an ebb and flow, with both teams unable to retain possession for long enough to pose their opposition damaging questions.
(17’) Barkley now leads the field of play, with the young Englishman having continuous problems with a nosebleed. He is quickly patched up by a host of medical staff, but Everton are forced to continue with only ten men for the time being.
(16’) Stoke are clearly set up to play on the break, with Bojan already linking up with Diouf fairly well to set the lone striker on his way in behind the opposition defence. Lukaku, meanwhile, has seen very little in the way of service, with the Belgian pressing without reward.
(14’) Stones puts in two tackles in quick succession to deny Diouf and N'Zonzi, but Stoke keep on the pressure. Cameron drives down the right, before whipping in a decent cross, but Bojan is unable to crane his neck enough to steer a header on target.
(13’) The young centre-back appears to be willing to continue, who returns to the field with a slight limp - Everton fans will hope the Englishman can run off his knock. There will be plenty of stoppage time at the end of this half already, that's for sure. Both goalkeepers are yet to be forced into any kind of uncomfortable action, with possession being surrendered needlessly and with frequency.
(11’) After being firmly challenged by Whelan, Stones goes to ground and appears to be in some discomfort. The young Englishman has had his fair share of ankle and knee problems and it appears the former Barnsley man won't be able to continue. It was a fair tackle, but the physios are giving Stones a thorough once-over.
(10’) There have been no chances as of yet, with the majority of the action taking place in the midfield third. Mirallas is nearly able to drive in behind Pieters on the right-hand side, but the Dutchman intercepted. Stoke then break, but Diouf is unable to make the most of two gilt-edged chances after being set away by Bojan. Jagielka and Howard make timely interventions.
(8’) Both players rejoin the fray, with play finally back underway after a lengthy stoppage. Stoke get their foot on the ball for the first time of the afternoon, but Everton are keen to press high upfield and force mistakes. The Potters' back four don't look wholly confident in possession.
(6’) After liberal amounts of tape and bandaging, the Stoke player appears keen to carry on - he isn't one to feign injury. Martinez uses the break in play to call over a couple of players to give them further instructions. It appears that the Englishman wants to continue regardless.
(5’) There's now to be a break in play, due to a sickening collision between Shawcross and Lukaku, with the former back to his feet rather quickly. The Belgium international caught the defender accidentally in the temple, with a wound opening up immediately. The physios are straight onto the field.
(4’) Everton are enjoying the majority of possession in the early stages, with the tempo being kept rather slow and ponderous. Jagielka is forced into a hurried clearance after a cross in from the right-hand side, before the ball is recycled and Stones is made to hook a delivery clear of the danger area seconds later.
(2’) Everton claim for a penalty in the opening couple of minutes, but the referee isn't interested! Bojan is caught in possession high up the field by Mirallas, before the winger bursts into the box and gets the wrong side of Muniesa. Despite falling to the ground, there didn't appear to be much contact.
(1’) The ball is rolling in the first half! After a minute of applause things are ready to get underway! Everton are in their customary blue, with the away side in their red and white striped jerseys.
Stoke substitutes: Huth, Palacios, Wilson, Adam, Butland, Assaidi, Crouch.
Stoke starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Begovic; Cameron, Shawcross, Muniesa, Pieters; Whelan, N'Zonzi; Walters, Bojan, Arnautovic; Diouf.
Everton substitutes: Joel Robles, Eto'o, McGeady, Kone, Distin, Garbutt, Alcaraz.
Everton starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Howard; Coleman, Stones, Jagielka, Baines; Barry, McCarthy; Mirallas, Naismith, Barkley; Lukaku.
TEAM NEWS: Marc Muniesa partners Ryan Shawcross in the centre of the Potters' defence, with Geoff Cameron slotting in at right-back. Glenn Whelan and Steven N'Zonzi will look to break up play and feed counter attacks, with plenty of pace in advanced areas. Marko Arnautovic and Jonathan Walters flank the Spanish flair of Bojan Krkic, with the mobile presence of Mame Biram Diouf selected to lead the line alone.
TEAM NEWS: John Stones starts at centre-back alongside compatriot Phil Jagielka, with Sylvain Distin dropping to the bench. James McCarthy and Gareth Barry provide the defensive midfield shield, with Ross Barkley and Kevin Mirallas being given license to roam in wider areas due to the support of both Leighton Baines and Seamus Coleman from wing-back. Romelu Lukaku is the lone target man for Martinez's side.

Leicester 1-2 Tottenham: A hard-fought victory for Pochettino's Spurs. The London club were made to battle for all three points here, with the hosts dominating most of the second half and spurning several opportunities. Lloris was once again in fine form for the visitors, while the frame of the goal also denied Leicester on two separate occasions. Their winless run continues and they remain rock-bottom of the Premier League, even if there were some positives to take.
(90’) FULL-TIME!
(90’) Eriksen almost adds a third for Spurs as he shoots just wide from the edge of the area, but it matters not as the referee swiftly blows his whistle to end the match.
(90’) Time is almost up for Leicester. Spurs are clinging on.
(90’) Lloris appears to be in pain now. The goalkeeper rushed out to collect the ball as Vardy raced through on goal, chasing a bouncing pass. But the two collided and the Leicester man was given a yellow card as a result. The French keeper looks capable on continuing, though.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card J. Vardy goes into the referee's book. ---
(90’) LLORIS DENIES LEICESTER! The corner is fired in towards the back post and Morgan manages to get his head to it, with the goalkeeper tipping it around the post with both hands.
(90’) Vardy has been a threat since coming on and he is at it again here, racing on to a pass down the left and then drilling into the area. But his delivery is deflected behind.
(90’) There will be a minimum of four minutes added on here.
(89’) WHAT A LET-OFF FOR SPURS! Mahrez, who has been a constant threat, is once again given far too much space by Rose and he manages to flash a delivery right across the face of goal. Schlupp arrives at the back post with the goal at his mercy, but the ball gets stuck under his feet and Lloris pounces. That a lucky escape for the visitors.
(87’) More excellent defending from Vertonghen. Ulloa manages to bring the ball down inside the Spurs area, but he has the Belgian right on his back. The former Ajax defender gets a foot in to block the eventual shot and then clears.
(85’) LEICESTER CALLING FOR A PENALTY! Fazio is beaten far too easily by Vardy and the forwards get into the left side of the area. Vertonghen comes across and produces a strong challenge, taking the man and the ball, with the referee highlighting that very fact.
(85’) Decent delivery from Mahrez as the Algerian curls the ball over the Spurs wall and Drinkwater meets it with a flicked-on header. But his effort lands on the goal, rather than in it.
--- 84’ Substitution Paulinho comes on for H. Kane. ---
(84’) Free-kick to Leicester out on the right now. They are perhaps a little lucky to get that, as Vertonghen accidentally tripped Vardy while trying to clear the ball. Nevertheless, the hosts have themselves an opportunity.
--- 83’ Substitution A. Knockaert comes on for P. Konchesky. ---
--- 82’ Yellow card J. Vertonghen gets yellow. ---
(82’) Well, Leicester made nothing of the corner and Spurs subsequently get some respite before trying to start a counter of their own. But the move comes to an end as Chadli's cross is cut out by Wasilewski.
(80’) Corner on the right for Leicester now, after Mahrez saw his cross deflected behind by Rose. What can they make of this?
(79’) Leicester have just over ten minutes to go here. They are looking much brighter than Spurs at the moment, but how often this season have Pearson's men been unable to capitalise on positive play? A considerable number.
(77’) Leicester are piling the pressure on at the moment. Schlupp's cross from the left goes all the way through to Mahrez on the opposite side of the area. The Algerian takes a touch, cuts inside Rose and shoots over the bar.
--- 75’ Substitution J. Vardy enters the game and replaces D. Nugent. ---
(75’) That's another very good effort for Leicester. Drinkwater is given far too much space about 25 yards from goal and the former Manchester United youngster tries his luck, sending a low shot just wide of Lloris' right-hand post.
(73’) SPURS ESCAPE! Desperate defending from the visitors. A long ball is lofted into the area for Morgan. The defender fails to get a shot away, but the ball does land kindly for Schlupp, whose over-head kick is blocked by Rose. Leicester claim for a penalty, while Spurs clear the ball away. The passage comes to an end as James tries his luck from distance, drawing a simple save from Lloris.
--- 71’ Goal! Goal to Tottenham Hotspur, scored by C. Eriksen! ---
(71’) GOAL!!!! SPURS RE-TAKE THE LEAD! After a slight delay, Eriksen finally takes the free-kick and, instead of lifting an effort into the danger area for a team-mate, he goes for goal himself out on the left, squeezing his attempt just inside the post. Hamer really should have done better with that, but Spurs won't care!
(69’) Silly foul there by Leicester. Kane cuts in from the left and, after holding off the challenge of James, he is tripped over by Wasilewski. The visitors now have a free-kick in a good position out on the left.
(67’) LLORIS TO THE RESCUE! The Frenchman saves Spurs again, this time from the lively Schlupp. The Ghanaian latches on to a pass and drills a good effort towards goal after jinking past Walker. But the goalkeeper palms it away.
(66’) GOALMOUTH SCRAMBLE! Spurs manage to push Leicester back into their own area and the ball eventually falls to Eriksen in the left side of the box. He skips past one challenge and tries to squeeze the ball past Hamer, but he is ultimately crowded out.
(65’) Tottenham have had a couple of bright moments in this second half, but Leicester look far more likely of going on to win this at the moment. The Spurs attacks have generally lacked cutting edge, particularly since the break. Eriksen, Chadli and Kane have been very quiet.
--- 63’ Substitution Soldado enters the game and replaces N. Chadli. ---
(63’) Excellent play by Lamela as the Argentinian races down the right, shurgs off the challenge of Konchesky and then crosses into the danger zone. But his delivery is just a little too high for the lurking duo of Eriksen and Kane.
(62’) PENALTY CLAIMS REJECTED! The ball is lofted into the danger area from the deep position and Kane tries to get on the end of it at the back post, but he ends up on the ground after a bit of a nudge from Morgan. No penalty given, though.
(60’) Finally, some respite for the away side. Spurs have thsemlves a free-kick about 35 yards from the Leicester goal after Wasilewski brought Lamela down unfairly. What can they muster here?
(58’) Spurs haven't really come out for the second half. Leicester continue to keep their visitors pegged back and James is the latest to try his luck, though his attempt is deflected wide off Fazio and nothing comes of the corner.
(56’) The hosts remain on the front foot, though, and they win a free-kick about 30 yards from goal, as Vertonghen gets a little too close to Ulloa when challenging for an aerial ball.
(55’) Almost another opening for Leiester now Schlupp tries to race on to a long ball from the back, but Walker comes across and intercepts, clearing the danger in the process.
(53’) OFF THE BAR! Mahrez steps up to take the free-kick and sends a fine left-footed effort towards goal, but the crossbar comes to Spurs' rescue, with Lloris completely beaten. The visitors are really struggling now.
(52’) Free-kick now for Leicester just outside the Spurs area now. Wonderful opportunity for the hosts as they look to make the most of their brilliant start to the second half.
(50’) Wonderful start to the second half for the hosts. Ulloa has the goal to end his drought and Leicester have what their play towards the end of the first half deserved. Can they build on it, though?
--- 48’ Assist The assist came from R. Mahrez. ---
--- 48’ Goal! GOAL!!! LEICESTER ARE LEVEL! Brilliant play by Mahrez, who threatened a lot towards the end of the first half. The Algerian beats Bentaleb to the ball, skips past his compatriot and then plays a low ball in towards the near post for Ulloa, who gets across Fazio and steers home. ---
(47’) Both managers made changes at the break. For Leicester, King has gone off and been replaced by Matty James, while Mason has come on for Spurs' Stambouli.
--- 46’ Substitution M. James enters play, replacing A. King. ---
--- 46’ Substitution B. Stambouli is done for the day. R. Mason is his replacement. ---
(46’) Off we go for the second half.
Leicester City 0-1 Tottenham: Pochettino's side take a slender lead into the break thanks to Kane's early strike, but things could have been much different. The home side were very quiet for the first 30 minutes or so, but they really grew in confidence as the half progressed, with Mahrez going close, while Ulloa was denied only by the post. There is plenty more to come in this!
(45’) HALF-TIME!
(45’) JUST WIDE! The free-kick is whipped in by Eriksen from the left and Kane meets it with a fine glancing header, but his effort goes just wide of the right-hand post. That was very close indeed.
(45’) Eriksen's corner goes straight into the ball, but he wins a corner as a result. The Dane opts to play it low and back towards the edge of the box, only for Lamela's first touch to desert him. Eventually, Spurs win a free-kick out on the left as Simpson fouls Rose.
(43’) Uncompromising defending there from Morgan as he comes across and knocks Lamela over on the right flank. Free-kick to Spurs now, with Eriksen standing over the dead ball.
(41’) Pochettino is starting to look a little flustered in the Spurs technical area. The visitors generally had it very easy for the first 30 minutes or so, but Leicester are having all the meaningful possession at the moment, with the London-based club clinging on to their lead a bit.
(39’) OFF THE POST! Leicester have really come back into this! Once again Mahrez is decisive on the right as he lofts an early cross into the centre. Ulloa, who hasn't scored since the win over United, rises and meets the delivery with a powerful header, but it comes back off the post. Agonisingly close for the hosts!
(38’) MAHREZ DENIED! The Algerian winger has been quiet so far, but he comes to life finally in the Spurs penalty area. The tricky attacker cuts inside and on to his left foot, before curling a low shot past his marker and towards the bottom-left corner, but Lloris palms it away brilliantly.
(36’) ULLOA LOSES HIS FOOTING! Excellent play by Leicester. Drinkwater shows clever feet to beat his man just outside the Spurs area and he then plays the striker into the right side of the area. Ulloa strides past one defender, but he then slips while shooting and ultimately slices wide.
--- 35’ Yellow card K. Walker is cautioned by the referee. ---
(35’) Schlupp finds himself at the centre of things again on the left. This time he is able to burst away from Walker, who tries to take a chunk of his shirt. The Spurs man ultimately getting a booking for his troubles.
(35’) Lloris made to work there. Schlupp proves himself as a determined runner down the left and he manages to get a shot away from the edge of the area, but a deflection takes the sting out of it and the goalkeeper saves with ease.
(33’) HUGE CHANCE FOR SPURS! Once again Leicester are caught so high up the field, virtually on the halfway-line. Kane pokes a pass in behind Simpson, who was all at sea, and Bentaleb capitalises, marching through on goal. But his control of the ball is not great and Wasilewski makes an important intervention at the crucial moment.
(32’) That's not a particularly encouraging bit of goalkeeping from Hamer. The keeper receives a back-pass and his touch is heavy. Kane isn't quite quick enough to pounce, though.
(30’) What a waste for Leicester! Stambouli is caught out in his own half, giving the hosts the perfect opportunity to catch Spurs napping at the back. Drinkwater, who stole possession back from the Frenchman, charges towards goal with Nugent in support, but he opts to go it alone and his shot is terrible, scuffing well wide of the target.
(29’) Lovely move by the visitors. Chadli manages to cut a good delivery back towards the edge of the area and Kane meets it with a first-time pass into the box for Eriksen. The Dane then tries to square into the danger zone, but Wasilewski is there to intercept before Lamela can tap in.
(28’) Kane is involved again now, this time in the danger area. Chadli has been a nuisance out on the left and again he is able to get past Simpson and cross in towards the Spurs forward. His first-time effort and the front post goes wide, however.
(26’) HAMER SAVES LEICESTER! Eriksen cuts in from the left and manages to get himself into the hosts' area. The midfielder fires a right-footed effort at goal, though the goalkeeper palms it away, with Kane's attempt on the rebound blocked by a crowd of players.
(24’) Leicester have finally come to life! The free-kick delivery from King is excellent, but the ball only smacks into the back of Wasilewski. The hosts remain on the attack, though, and Mahrez bursts past Rose down the right. Again, though, Spurs hold firm as Stambouli blocks the eventual cross.
(22’) Free-kick out on the left flank for Leicester now. Nugent did well as he cleverly played the ball through Lamela's legs and then drew a foul. Can they make the most of this?
(20’) Tentative penalty claims there for Leicester as Ulloa goes to ground under the challenge of Fazio inside the area, but there was very little in that. Play goes on, as it should.
(18’) WONDERFUL SAVE BY LLORIS! Leicester catch SPurs napping at the back as Schlupp cuts across towards the left. He pokes a pass through to Ulloa on the edge of the area and, after his first touch sits up kindly, the forward unleashes a powerful half-volley. But the goalkeeper tips it over in acrobatic fashion.
(17’) The crowd is seemingly starting to get frustrated with the Leicester players now. They urge their men to put the Spurs defence under some pressure and Ulloa obliges with some half-hearted closing down.
(15’) Spurs are enjoying another spell in control of the ball, with Fazio and Vertonghen knocking it around unchallenged at the back. Nugent and Ulloa are not putting them under any pressure whatsoever, making it so easy for the visitors to move out from the back.
(13’) The home side really have to start not only using the ball better, but seeing more of it in general. Almost every time they find themselves in possession, Leicester have been too quick to surrender it back to Spurs. Mahrez appears too determined to find a defence-splitting pass, though he has not been accurate at all yet.
(11’) Leicester have been so poor on the ball so far. Again, Spurs keep the hosts camped in their own penalty area, stroking passes around them with ease, probing patiently. Eventually Kane's touch is heavy and the hosts are able to take possession back, but Stambouli swiftly sticks a foot in again.
(9’) Spurs are looking far more dangerous currently. An attack from the visitors comes to a premature end, but Spurs steal possession back swiftly as Leicester attempt to break. Stambouli is proving very effective out there at the moment, but on this occasion it is Bentaleb who comes across and halts King.
(7’) Corner now for Leicester. Mahrez fires the ball in from the right and, although Spurs' defending isn't particularly impressive, Eriksen manages to hook the ball away before a man in blue can get it under control.
(5’) Leicester are playing so high and, as a result, finding themselves looking increasingly vulnerable to Spurs. Again the visitors break through the middle and Lamela, who is finding joy in a central position, pokes a pass through for Kane. Luckily for Leicester, the forward is flagged offside this time.
(4’) Leicester have the opportunity to try and find an immediate response as they win a free-kick just outside the Tottenham area, though the chance is wasted, with the set-piece blasted straight into the wall.
(2’) GOAL!!! TOTTENHAM TAKE THE LEAD! Ferocious start to this match from the visitors. They catch their hosts on the break, as Lamela feeds Chadli into the final third down the left. The Belgian crosses low and Kane pounces on Morgan's hesitant defending, slamming past the helpless goalkeeper.
--- 1’ Assist N. Chadli provided the assist. ---
--- 1’ Goal! H. Kane has found the target for Tottenham Hotspur! ---
(1’) Off we go! Leicester start the action in the Midlands.
The players are now out on the pitch, with kick-off just a few moments away.
Leicester will be desperate to record a victory today. Pearson's men have not won at all since beating Manchester United 5-3 on September 21. That run has stretched to 12 matches, ten of which were defeats. The hosts undoubtedly go into this game in wretched form, though Spurs have not exactly been convincing this term. Even a win might not lift the home side off the bottom of the table, but they need to start picking up points if they are to avoid the drop.
Mauricio Pochettino, on the other hand, has no new injuries to take into consideration ahead of the clash. With just about everyone available, has the Argentinian finally been able to decide what is best starting XI is at Spurs? Well, the line-up includes Federico Fazio in at centre-back alongside Jan Vertonghen, while Danny Rose starts on the left. Bentaleb and close-season signing Benjamin Stambouli slot into the midfield, while Harry Kane starts again in attack.
Nigel Pearson has not had to contend with too many injury problems in the build-up to today's fixture. (52’) Gardner spings the offside trap and squares a pass from the right-hand side of the box. It's too close to Hart, though, who dives down and smothers the ball with Berahino and Varela lurking. City break with Navas surging into the area, but he fires wide!
(51’) Mulumbu spots Wisdom in space on the right wing and he picks him out with a great pass. The on-loan defender attempts to fizz a low cross into the centre but Clichy diverts it behind.
(50’) The snow is coming down even heavier now! The home fans may simply be worrying about the journey home before long unless their team pick up their display.
(49’) After both players receive treatment, the free kick is eventually taken by Gardner but he wastes the opportunity, firing the ball straight into the wall! The fans let out a huge groan!
(47’) Mulumbu does well to knock the ball away from Silva 25 yards from goal, and the Spaniard catches him. Both go tumbling to ground but it is the hosts who are correctly awarded the free kick.
(46’) We are back underway!
Welcome back! The teams are heading back out onto the field, so the second half will begin in just a few moments.
HALF TIME - West Brom 0-3 Man City: The Citizens take a three-goal lead into the interval. Fernando opened the scoring after hooking the ball home from inside the six-yard box after Foster had spilled, and Toure added the second from the penalty spot after Lescott felled Silva. The Spaniard then added the third following an incisive break, putting Pellegrini's men in a commanding position. It's difficult to see any route back into this for the hosts.
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) Berahino reveis the ball on the edge of the box and lifts it over the Hart, but he was in a clear offside position.
(45’) The snow is coming down at the Hawthorns, so the players may welcome the interval in a few moments. It isn't settling on the pitch, though, which is a relief for all at the stadium!
(45’) There will be three minutes of time added on at the end of this half.
(43’) Although West Brom haven't been convincing from set plays, City have hardly shown a rock-solid defence. Mangala and Demichelis are still showing frailties in the absence of Kompany.
(41’) City break at speed following the second corner, with Navas bursting down the right before passing inside. An opening for a shot doesn't open for anyone, though, and eventually the Baggies manage to work the ball clear of danger.
(40’) West Brom earn a couple of corners in quick succession but nothing is made of either of Pocognoli's deliveries. The hosts are going to have to make more of those openings when they come their way if they want any chance of recovering.
(38’) The visitors are now attempting to control possession with a series of short, calm passess around the halfway line. They don't want the hosts gaining any momentum before the break.
(36’) WHAT A SAVE! Berahino's pace causes problems for the City defence but his shot is blocked by Mangala. The loose ball sits up perfectly for Gardner, who thumps an effort towards goal which Hart manages to fling a hand in the way of! Another chance opens up seconds later, but Berahino pulls his attempt wide of the far corner.
--- 34’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAL!! CITY ARE THREE UP! Clinical stuff from Pellegrini's men! Fernando wins the ball on the halfway line and charges forward. He rolls a pass to the right for Navas, who then cuts it back for Silva. The Spaniard takes a touch before bending a low shot inside the far post! ---
--- 34’ Assist Assist by Jesús Navas. ---
(33’) City look to launch another quick counterattack, and as Nasri receives the ball inside the West Brom half he attempts to step across Mulumbu so that he cannot make a challenge. The midfielder is not worries about that, though, and makes a brilliant sliding challenge which sends possession back to his keeper.
(31’) Nasri is back on the pitch, and once more he is in the heart of the action. He slides a pass down the line for Navas who turns it inside for Silva. He takes a touch before releasing a shot which is blazed far over the top of the goal.
(29’) A cross from the left is not dealt with by Mangala, and his header falls to Mulumbu inside the box. The midfielder fires a shot at goal but he is unable to get enough power to worry Hart, and he also directed it straight at him!
(27’) The Frenchman got sandwiched between the two centre-backs there, but he has made his way off the pitch on his own. He looks keen to get back into the action as soon as possble.
(26’) Nasri has stayed down after contesting an aerial ball with both Lescott and McAuley. The referee quickly rushes over and indicates for the medical staff to enter the field and offer him treatment. Hopefully it's nothing serious.
(24’) Man City are unbeaten on their last four league visits to the Hawthorns. It's going to take a Christmas miracle for the hosts to avoid another negative result today.
(22’) Some lovely interplay between Silva and Nasri on the left wing nearly results in the Spaniard creating a chance for the latter, but the Frenchman gets the pass stuck under his feet and is dispossessed. The passing and movement there was an absolute delight.
(20’) West Brom have responded well to falling two goals behind so early in this game. They're continuing to press and probe for openings in the City half, but they don't really have a choice otherwise they've got no chance of salvaging anything from this game.
(18’) JUST WIDE! Berahino gets away from Demichelis, making a diagonal run to the right of the box. Morrison slides an intelligent pass into his path, and the striker flashes a shot slightly beyond the far post! That was a well-worked opening for the hosts.
(17’) STAT: City have won the last 18 Premier League games that Yaya Toure has scored in. It looks like that streak is going to be extended today!
(15’) The visitors are cutting apart their hosts at will! An almost identical chance to the one that fell to Milner earlier is forged down West Brom's left, but this time the final ball comes to Nasri and it is slightly too far ahead of him.
--- 13’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAL!! CITY GO 2-0 UP! Toure is given the responsibility of taking the spot-kick, and he puts a small stutter in his run up before firing it into the bottom corner. Foster went the right way but he couldn't get to it! ---
(12’) PENALTY TO CITY! Silva tries to slide a pass down the channel for Navas, but Lescott intercepts. The loose ball is pounced on by the Spaniard, though, and he knocks it aside before being felled by the former City defender! The referee is in no doubt, and points to the spot.
(11’) Sessegnon spots Gardner drifting into a pocket of space, 30 yards from goal in a central position. He sends a forceful pass to his feet but his team-mate is unable to bring it under his control, and the ball runs through for the Citizens' defence to clear.
(10’) The City fans are in good voice after taking an early lead in this one. After taking so long to break down Crystal Palace last week Pellegrini will be delighted to see his side go ahead inside the opening 10 minutes. Will West Brom's abysmal home form continue this afternoon?
--- 8’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAL!! Navas plays a give-and-go with Toure on the right of the box, and his cross takes a deflection which sends it looping to the back post. Foster goes to claim it but spills it, and Fernando hooks the ball over his head and into the back of the net from the edge of the six-yard box. Woeful keeping and City lead! ---
(7’) CHANCE! The corner is gathered by Hart and he launches City on a counterattack. Eventually a cross comes in from the byline courtesy of Sagna, and Silva flicks it behind him, teeing up Milner. The England international is falling but prods the ball towards the corner and Foster gets just enough on it to send it behind for a corner.
(6’) Silva slides a pass into the box for the diagonal run of Nasri, but Foster races off his line and beats the Frenchman to the ball. He sends it long and the hosts probe down the right, with Sessegnon eventually forcing a corner from Clichy.
(5’) Neither team has settled into possession yet, with a number of long, stray passes being played across the field. City took a while to get going in their last fixture due to the lack of a recognised striker. Will the same happen today?
(3’) Varela picks up the ball out on the left and cuts inside onto his right foot. He whips a low cross towards the near post which is too far ahead of Berahino, so Hart has a simple collection to make.
(1’) We are underway!
The teams are out on the pitch, so kick off will be upon us in a few moments!
Victory today would put City three points adrift of Chelsea, who were 2-0 winners against West Ham earlier. The Citizens are undefeated in their last nine Premier League games against West Brom, winning eight, so they fancy their chances of maintaining that three point gap from the league leaders.
Boxing Day form varies for both these sides. West Brom must dish out too much turkey at the training ground because they have won just one of their eight Premier League games played on this day, drawing two and losing five. City, meanwhile, have been victorious on five, and lost just one, of their last seven Boxing Day fixtures.
Man City substitutes: Caballero, Zabaleta, Boyata, Kolarov, Fernandinho, Lampard, Jovetic.
Man City (4-2-3-1): Hart; Sagna, Demichelis, Mangala, Clichy; Fernando, Toure; Navas, Silva, Nasri; Milner.
West Brom substitutes: Myhill, Gamboa, Dawson, Baird, Yacob, Brunt, Ideye.
West Brom (4-2-3-1): Foster; Wisdom, McAuley, Lescott, Pocognoli; Morrison, Mulumbu; Sessegnon, Gardner, Varela; Berahino.
MAN CITY TEAM NEWS: Sergio Aguero and Edin Dzeko remained sidelined through injury, and, although Pellegrini has Stevan Jovetic fit, Pellegrini has put the Montenegrin among the substitutes and lines up without a recognised striker. Vincent Kompany remains on the treatment table, but there are changes in both full-back positions as Aleksandar Kolarov and Pablo Zabaleta are replaced by Gael Clichy and Bacary Sagna. Fernando also comes into the starting line-up, with Fernandinho the man dropped.
WEST BROM TEAM NEWS: Chris Brunt is once again available for selection and he makes the bench, but Victor Anichebe is out. Brown Ideye is replaced by Saido Berahino in attack, while the only other change sees Graeme Dorrans make way for Youssouf Mulumbu.
With Chelsea on the brink of a 2-0 victory over West Ham United in the day's early kick off, the Citizens need to win at the Hawthorns in order to keep pace with Jose Mourinho's men. However, after surrendering a two-goal lead in their last league outing, the Baggies will be keen for a result today.
Hello and welcome to today's LIVE commentary on the Boxing Day meeting of West Bromwich Albion and Manchester City. Manuel Pellegrini's men will be eager to kick off their festive fixtures with a win at the Hawthorns today, and Alan Irvine's side have managed just four victories in front of their own fans in this calendar year. My name is Tom Webber, and I will be guiding you through all the action!
