Arsenal hold on for dear life to seal the points, and notch up Wenger's 40th EPL win, and 600th overall as Gunners boss. A breathless finish here at the Emirates, as QPR came mightily close to drawing level in the closing stages. The hosts were under a lot of pressure, but came through in the end.
(90’) Kranjcar hacks the free kick disappointingly over the top of the bar, and that's it!
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card F. Coquelin is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) Coquelin takes out Fer about 30 yards from goal and now, with the last kick of the game, QPR have a free-kick chance to seal the comeback. Now then, hold your breath folks...
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card N. Kranjčar goes into the referee's book. ---
(90’) How Arsenal could do with some of that possession they enjoyed earlier in the game. Anywhere will do for them now and they have a crucial respite as QPR have a man booked for a foul in midfield.
(90’) Back come QPR again and Arsenal are under real pressure! Vargas lets a great shooting opportunity pass him by with a poor first touch, and then Arsenal get away with a slight foul on Gibbs by Zamora in the box. Surprisingly, no appeals from the QPR players!
(89’) ISLA NEARLY! From a corner, the former Juve man gets a nifty little header in at the near post which has Szczesny guessing, but it's blocked and cleared before anyone of the Hoops can get to it.
--- 88’ Substitution D. Welbeck is replaced with F. Coquelin. ---
(87’) Kranjcar tries to angle himself for the shot from the top of the box, and manages to beat his man at that zone, but his left-footed drive doesn't come close to Szczesny. Let-off there.
(85’) Hoilett does excellently to get goal side of Chambers and free himself for the cross. However, having done that, his delivery is beyond terrible. Redknapp looks like he wants to throttle him. What a waste.
--- 83’ Substitution T. Rosický is replaced with C. Chambers. ---
(83’) Smart defensive change from Wenger, hauling off Rosicky for Chambers. The Czech Republic man was never going to complete the full 90, and the youngster that's replaced him will help shore things up at the back for the final stretch.
(81’) Martin Atkinson's two previous big decisions - the Sanchez penalty and the Giroud red card - were spot on. However, this last call will take some living down if Arsenal do not manage to close out this game. Then again, the Gunners will have no one to blame but themselves given their dominance of this contest.
--- 79’ Goal! No mistake from Austin! Szczesny guessed correctly, diving to his right. However, he went too far to the post, as Austin's penalty went in on his near side. Game well and truly on! ---
(77’) QPR HAVE A PENALTY! My word that's a tough one for Wenger and Co. to swallow. Hoilett squares up against Debuchy, who got his big toe on the ball before sending the winger to the turf. Looked a legit tackle to me but now, QPR have a great chance.
(75’) Very interesting time ahead in this game with Arsenal pressing forward. There's still enough time for QPR to grab two goals however, and perhaps it's a little too early for the Gunners to still be at full throttle.
(73’) Debuchy overlaps for the umpteenth time, and he squeezes a pass to Sanchez just inside the area. The Chilean, with a man in front of him, does the only thing that he can do, and tries to lift the ball into the top corner. Nothing doing though, as it goes just over the bar.
--- 71’ Substitution B. Zamora comes on for J. Mutch. ---
(71’) Hoilett grabs a handful of Debuchy's shirt and gets booked immediately. A good free kick chance for the Gunners that they can't pounce upon as the delivery from Cazorla goes off target.
--- 70’ Yellow card J. Hoilett goes into the referee's book. ---
(69’) Things back to normal for Arsenal and their fans, who can watch their side play their patient passing game without the need or urgency to turn it into goals. QPR have an almighty task ahead of them. even with the man advantage.
(67’) There was a slight deflection off Caulker on that Rosicky effort and it looked like that may have just put Green off making a more committed dive to his right. On first glance, it looked weak from the keeper.
--- 65’ Assist A. Sánchez gave the assist. ---
--- 65’ Goal! WITH EASE, THAT'S HOW! A tremendous run from Sanchez leaves three players as silhouettes, before he unselfishly slides the ball to Rosicky inside the area. Crucially, he doesn't wait to smash a first-time effort into the far side! ---
(63’) Hoilett and Fer both enter the fray as Redknapp goes on the offensive. This sets up an interesting last half-hour or so as the visitors have nothing to lose at this point. How will Arsenal fare?
--- 62’ Substitution A. Traoré is done for the day. J. Hoilett is his replacement. ---
--- 62’ Substitution K. Henry is replaced with L. Fer. ---
(61’) Redknapp has been hopping around with ants in his pants, ready to make some changes to react to the Giroud dismissal. However, the ball hasn't gone out of play yet for him to do so.
(59’) Gibbs sees a cross just about blocked before Welbeck as Arsenal push for that crucial second. it allows QPR to attack, but they can't do much more than Mutch's delivery straight down the throat of Szczesny.
(57’) Arsenal need that second goal more than ever now. Cynics like me would say that it wouldn't be a Gunners game without them shooting themselves in the foot. At least they keep it interesting.
--- 55’ Yellow card J. Mutch is yellow-carded. ---
(55’) Sanchez, as is his wont, has teased a few fouls from the opposition today. As he was about to skip towards the byline, he was tripped by Mutch, who is duly booked by the referee arriving on the scene.
--- 53’ Red card! GIROUD SENT OFF! What a dumb move from the Frenchman. After racing onto a back pass, he was felled in a crowd of players. Seeing blood, he got up and shoved Onuoha to the ground about two feet from the referee. Ferdinand leads the QPR protests and the red card is out! ---
(52’) It continues to be all Arsenal in terms of possession. The home side have a few gaps in front of them to exploit if they need to as QPR try to get bodies up front to get back into this game.
(50’) Debuchy gets down the right and squeezes a tasty ball across the face of goal, but no one in red and white is there to oblige with the final touch. There's the danger for QPR, because Arsenal have a lot of pace on the field to break if they need to.
(48’) Let's see what QPR have changed coming out of the break. It's clear that they needed a major overhaul in the way that they attacked - and I use that term loosely given that they barely crossed the halfway line.
(46’) Here we go again!
The referee signals for half time as Arsenal take a one-goal lead into the break. Shockingly, it's Sanchez who has scored, and he and his team could have had more if he had taken advantage of a penalty, which Green ended up saving. The Gunners have dominated possession and the chances but there's still only one goal in it. I'll be back with the second half soon.
(43’) Things just slowing down as we approach the end of the first half. Redknapp should have a list as long as Santa's of what was wrong with that first-half performance from his side. They've been trampled in every way but the scoreline.

(39’) QPR COME CLOSE! A free kick is not properly dealt with by Arsenal, and the visitors are allowed to recycle possession. The ball comes in for Caulker who makes contact, but Szczesny stretches out a long arm to push it wide.

--- 37’ Goal! ARSENAL LEAD! No presents for guessing who has taken the cake. Cazorla spreads the ball left to Gibbs, who hoists a cross to the far post. Sanchez is left criminally unmarked and cranes his neck to plant a header home! ---

(32’) Sanchez latches onto a quaint feed from Cazorla and tries to pick out a pass to one of Giroud or Welbeck, but Ferdinand uses his veteran savvy to put his body in the way of the delivery.

(28’) Ferdinand is booked for tripping Welbeck near the edge of the box. A rare yet clear yellow card for the veteran centre back. Now then, this looks as tasty as Christmas dinner for some of these players...
--- 27’ Yellow card R. Ferdinand gets yellow. ---
(27’) Moments after Giroud tried and failed to test Green from long distance, Sanchez takes aim from the top of the box after a defensive lapse, but meets a similarly wayward fate.
(25’) PENALTY? Giroud gets the luck of the bobble and plays a pass towards Welbeck. The lanky striker gets his tentacles tangled with Onuoha and goes down, but the referee rules it six of one, half a dozen of the other. Play on.
(23’) First action of the match for Szczesny, who rises highest to pluck a routine corner out of the air. He's been an absolute spectator back there but it's important for him to keep his concentration.
(21’) I barely need one hand to count how many sustained forays into the Arsenal half that QPR have made. However, we've seen this script before with the Gunners. Ruthlessness has always been one of their problems and with that Sanchez penalty snafu, the early signs are there.
(19’) The Chilean is fine to continue and Arsenal's dominance of the ball endures. QPR need a timely tackle from Isla to stop Welbeck from speeding in behind the defensive line.
(17’) Everyone inside the Emirates holds their breath as Sanchez goes down injured. Moments before his knock, Traore had made another good defensive play to stop him from finding space.
(15’) Traore reads the game well to stop Sanchez from escaping to the byline. Arsenal continue to probe patiently, but QPR know the drill at the Emirates and are holding a deep line, squeezing play wide.
(13’) The Traore-Sanchez battle is shaping up already as one that will define this fixture. The former Arsenal full back is no slouch, but he is up against it against one of the quickest men in the Premier League.
(11’) Arsenal didn't let that miss faze them, and they continue to keep the ball penned inside the QPR half. It will be a massive disappointment for Wenger and his team though, what a chance wasted.
(9’) Penalty saved by R. Green!

(5’) Arsenal are dominating the ball, and Cazorla works his way into a shooting position from just over 20 yards. However, his effort was blocked by the defence, but positive signs from Wenger's men.
(3’) Nice nippy start from Arsenal and Cazorla hasn't even let it slip yet. The Gunners are moving the ball quickly around their central players as ever and are keeping the visitors penned back.

Nacho Monreal comes back into the Gunners side, stepping into the centre of defence in place of Calum Chambers. There's also a rare start for Tomas Rosicky, who replaces the Ox. Charlie Austin starts for the visitors, he of the nine goals in his last eight appearances. Rio Ferdinand and Niko Kranjcar are also recalled.
QPR (3-5-2): Green; Onuoha, Ferdinand, Caulker; Isla, Mutch, Henry, Kranjcar, Traore; Austin, Vargas.
Arsenal (4-3-3): Szczesny; Debuchy, Mertesacker, Monreal, Gibbs; Flamini, Cazorla, Rosicky; Alexis, Giroud, Welbeck.
Arsenal have only ever lost one of six on Boxing Day, while QPR haven't won such a fixture in three attempts. In the last nine meetings between these two sides, the Gunners have scored exactly one goal in eight of them.
The good news for Wenger is that with West Ham's defeat to Chelsea, the Gunners can move to within two points of a top-four place with a win here. Southampton are the current incumbents of that prized position after their 3-1 win over Crystal Palace.
QPR have been terrible away from Loftus Road, losing every one of their eight road games since getting back into the top flight. They sit two points above the relegation zone though, and will be no worse off than that come the end of play today. They could move as high as 13th with a win.
Arsenal come into this game on the back of a 2-2 draw against Liverpool that saw them once again cough up a late, late goal to drop points at Anfield (Emmanuel Eboue says hi). This season has seen the vocal minority turn into a fuming majority as many fans have turned on Arsene Wenger and his methods, with the Gunners seemingly set for another top-four scramble.
Hello and welcome to the late Premier League kickoff today, as Arsenal host QPR in an all-London clash. The Gunners need to get their top-four chase back on track, while the visitors want to put some distance between themselves and the relegation zone. I'm Keeghann Sinanan, your designated scribe.

Palace wrongly had a goal ruled out when 2-0 down, so they may feel aggrieved with the defeat as it really could have changed the last 20 minutes. Still, their poor form continues and they could drop into the bottom three this weekend.

They played some scintilating football and were pushed hard by the visitors, but, in the second half, two goals from David Silva and one from Yaya Toure secured the victory.

Will Pellegrini introduce teenage striker Thierry Ambrose for a Premier League debut in the second half to provide a reference point up top?

Palace have not won at City since 1990, when Ian Wright was among the scorers in a 2-0 victory at Maine Road. That's almost 25 years ago now, and their recent record won't fill them with confidence. The Eagles have not won against the Citizens in their last six meetings in all competitions.

(79’) Again Hull send a free kick from just inside the attacking half into the penalty area. Maguire wins his header, flicking it towards goal, but it is far too straightforward for Fabianski. The debutant did well to win his aerial duel, but Hull cannot expect to score off these long balls forward.
--- 77’ Substitution C. Davies is done for the day. H. Maguire is his replacement. ---
(77’) The two sides make their second changes of the match with just over 10 minutes to play. For Swansea, on comes their leading scorer Wilfried Bony to replace Bafetimbi Gomis, while Harry Maguire, who arrived in the summer from Sheffield United, makes his Premier League debut, replacing Curtis Davies.
--- 76’ Substitution W. Bony comes on for B. Gomis. ---
(76’) Taylor is shown a yellow card as he takes out Aluko on the right. The ensuing set piece again results in disappointment for the hosts, however, as Swansea deal with the threat to head clear of danger.
--- 75’ Yellow card N. Taylor is yellow-carded. ---
(74’) OFF THE WOODWORK! Swansea again fail to put this game to bed as Hull still have life! Emnes delivers a brilliant ball into the area, which is met by Gomis. The striker hooks a half-volley back across goal, and McGregor can only watch as it rings off the upright!
(72’) Important defensive header! Meyley sends a clever ball over the top for Jelavic, but the striker's lack of pace allows Williams to recover and head the ball away from danger. Just half a step quicker and the Croatian would have been through on goal.
(70’) The stretcher is called on for Taylor who finally leaves the pitch. Less than a minute later, the defender trots back on with no one the wiser, which has done enough to tick off the home support, who are none too thrilled with the time wasted off the clock.
(68’) Worrying moments for Swansea as Neil Taylor is down and in a ton of pain after Aluko slid in from behind with a tackle. The left-back appears to have injured his ankle, as the training staff comes out to take a look. The substitute is lucky to only have been shown a yellow card.
--- 67’ Yellow card S. Aluko is yellow-carded. ---
(66’) Emnes is really stamping his name on the match as a substitute. The midfielder is looking confident in possession, winning consecutive free kicks to help keep Hull off the ball and relieve the pressure on his goal.
(64’) STAT ATTACK: Hull City have gone 275 minutes of play in the Premier League without scoring a goal, since Sone Aluko equalized against Everton early in the second half at Goodison Park.
(62’) The hosts are pressing the pace and taking a much more direct approach to their play, but it is still all too simple for Swansea to defend. They have committed numbers forward, but without any real creativity, Fabianski has hardly been troubled in goal.
(60’) Hull City make an important change, and it is a tactical one from Steve Bruce. On comes striker Sone Aluko, who replaces centre-back Alex Bruce. The Tigers will play with three up top now as they convert back to a normal back four.
--- 59’ Substitution S. Aluko enters play, replacing A. Bruce. ---
(58’) Just wide! Ki and Dyer link up well along the right, and the goalscorer sends a superb ball into the area. It is met by Marvin Emnes, who has just arrived on the pitch, but he hooks his volley just wide!

(56’) GAME SAVER! The game in really starting to open up now, as Hull press for an equalizer. This allows Swansea to break on the counter, and Routledge sends a ball across goal for Shelvey, who is in alone, but McGregor spreads himself to keep the midfielder's shot out! Absolutely brilliant stuff from the keeper!
(54’) FANTASTIC SAVE! El Mohamady makes a towering run along the right, before picking out Jelavic with a cross from 30 yards out. The striker gets his head to it, but Fabianski dives down to his left to tip it behind!
(52’) STAT ATTACK: Hull City have picked up just six points from their matches at the KC Stadium this season, the lowest total for any team at home in the Premier League.
(50’) Great chance for Hull City as Routledge is penalized for a foul on Meyler atop the area. The anticipation builds as the hosts are presented with one of their best chances of the match. Ramirez ends up being the one to take, but his left-footed effort does not dip enough as it sails just over the bar!
(48’) Robertson has done very well in dealing with Dyer in defence, and does so again early on, preventing the attacker from beating him for pace, before winning his side a throw as he ushers the ball out of play off the winger.
(46’) Swansea get the second half underway at the KC Stadium! There have been no changes made by either manager at the break.
HALF TIME: HULL CITY 0-1 SWANSEA CITY. A fortunate deflection has the visitors in front after 45 minutes, with the Tigers struggling to find a breakthrough. Shelvey has looked the most dangerous for the Swans, creating the first goal before nearly doubling their lead when he sent a shot off the post. Hull's best chance of the half fell for Robertson after a nicely-worked move, but the defender saw his shot cannon out off the bar. There is still everything to play for in the second half, but Steve Bruce will have to make some adjustments.
(45’) Into the final minute of stoppage time and Hull are trying desperately for a goal. A lack of creativity has the hosts sending long balls forward into the area forJelavic and Hernandez, but the strikers are isolated in attack, making it easy for Swansea to defend. Mark Clattenburg sounds his whistle as we reach the end of the first half at the KC Stadium!
(45’) OFFSIDE! Lovely, testing ball sent forward by Meyler to play Jelavic through on goal, and the striker has the ball in the back of the net! The flag was up long before that, however, as the striker is called for an offside. It is the right call, with the Croatian failing to time his run properly.
(43’) STAT ATTACK: Swansea City had lost each of their last three trips to the KC Stadium, across three divisions in England, while failing to score a single goal.
(41’) Jazz Richards is shown a yellow card for a cynical challenge, forcing himself to pull back the jersey of Ramirez to try and prevent the counter, after giving the ball away to the Hull midfielder along the near side of the pitch. The chance again comes to nothing, however, as the hosts continue to lack a good delivery from these set pieces.
--- 40’ Yellow card A. Richards gets yellow. ---
(39’) It is all a bit scrappy from the two sides at the moment. The match is being contained largely in midfield, as the Swans try and clog it up and get to half time with the lead.
(37’) Spectacular toss! Hull win a free kick from less than 25 yards out, along the far side of the pitch. The ball is delivered into the area, but again it is poor from Ramirez, as Fabianski comes out to collect. The keeper then throws the ball a good distance ahead for Routledge, sending him one-on-one into attack, but he cannot take advantage of the opportunity presented to him by his keeper.
(35’) This has been a good stretch of play for Swansea since the yellow card to Livermore. The visitors have slowed the tempo drastically and are in control of the ball, which has helped to provide them with a bit of relief at the back. Hull are beginning to grow a bit restless as they are forced to chase the game.
(33’) STAT ATTACK: Swansea have not managed to win away from home since their 2-1 victory at Old Trafford on the opening day of the season. They have two draws and four losses since on their travels.
(31’) EXQUISITE EFFORT! Shelvey takes a harmless looking pass in midfield, and finds himself in a bit of space for a shot as he turns forward. He guides a strike towards the far post, and it is superbly placed, beating McGregor, but cannons out off the inside of the post!
(29’) There is a lengthy delay, with Dyer down and in need of medical attention. The attacker picked up a knock on his head and is being looked at by the training staff. He is able to walk off under his own power and should be just fine to continue.
--- 27’ Yellow card J. Livermore is cautioned by the referee. ---
(27’) More bad news for Hull! The Tigers, who are already without the likes of Michael Dawson, Tom Huddlestone and Mohamed Diame, will now have to make do without Jake Livermore on Boxing Day, as the midfielder is shown a yellow card for an ill-timed challenge on Shelvey.
(25’) Wonderful build up! The hosts continue to control the tempo and take the game to Swansea. Livermore and Jelavic work a clever give-and-go in midfield, before the midfielder picks out Hernandez with his pass. The striker holds off Taylor and cuts into the centre, but his shot does not trouble Fabianski who makes a simple catch.
(23’) CANNONED OFF THE BAR! Absolutely sensational move from Hull! Robertson makes a superb run up the left, using his strength to keep Dyer away. The defender picks out Ramirez in midfield, who then slides a wonderful ball into the area for Hernandez. The striker fends off Williams, and lays it off for Robertson, who had continued his run, but the defender smacks his first-time shot off the crossbar!
(21’) Bafetimbi Gomis concedes a needless free kick as he slides in with a tackle on James Chester. The hosts have a chance to deliver another ball into the area, but instead play it short and have to settle for a throw. The crowd is starting to grow a bit restless as the Tigers fail to test Lukasz Fabianski in goal.
(19’) STAT ATTACK: Hull City have now conceded seven goals within the first 15 minutes of their matches. They were tied with Tottenham for the highest total in the Premier League entering today, but have now surpassed them with Ki Sung-yueng's opener.
(17’) Ki knew nothing about that shot, despite being credited with the goal. Hull manager Steve Bruce looks on in disgust, wondering how long his side's tailspin must continue. The Tigers started so strong, but the opening goal seems to have sucked the life out from inside the KC Stadium.
--- 15’ Assist The assist came from J. Shelvey. ---
--- 15’ Goal! Ki and Shelvey work a one-two in attack, with the former Liverpool midfielder taking a return pass and driving a shot towards goal. Ki continues to make his run, and the shot cannons off him and past a wrong-footed McGregor, into the back of the net. ---
(15’) IT'S GONE IN! A GENEROUS DEFLECTION HAS SWANSEA IN FRONT!
(13’) The Tigers are keeping the pressure on and possession has stayed with them for an extended period inside the attacking half. The fans like what they are seeing, but Hull are not posing a great enough threat on the ball. It is all a bit too comfortable for Swansea in defence thus far.
(11’) Horrendous deliveries from Gaston Ramirez, spurning successive corners with his crosses failing to elude the first defender at the near post. Hull have been struggling for goals of late and cannot afford to keep squandering these opportunities, especially against a Swansea side who have had a hard time defending set pieces in recent weeks.
(9’) Brilliant start! The opening few minutes have been wide open, with the two teams exchanging quick, potent attacks. Wayne Routledge spurns a chance at the far post for Swansea, sending an effort wide, while back the other way, Hernandez wins his side a corner as Williams blocks his shot behind.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: Wilfried Bony and Gylfi Sigurdsson have combined to score or assist 17 of Swansea's 21 league goals this season, and neither are in the starting lineup today.
(5’) THAT WOULD MISS THREE NETS! Abel Hernandez puts Ashley Williams under pressure and forces a turnover just outside the defender's penalty area. He picks it up and plays Nikica Jelavic into the area, but the striker sends an effort miles wide of the target with the outside of his foot.
(3’) Swansea are looking to try and control the tempo early on, keeping possession at the back as they play keep away. Hull are not content with letting them see the ball as often as they like, pressing high up the pitch to make life difficult on the visitors.

Despite this loss West Brom stay 14th in the table. However they have now taken just four points in their last six games. Things do not get easier for the Baggies as they host Champions Manchester City on Boxing Day.

West Brom Head Coach Alan Irvine will feel sick to his stomach after that result. His side took a commanding two-goal lead early on through Lescott and Varela and looked to be in complete control but the game was turned on its head by Austin who takes his tally to the season to 11.
FULL TIME: QPR 3-2 West Brom. That's it. It's full time at Loftus Road and Charlie Austin has single-handedly dragged QPR out of the relegation zone with a hat-trick.
(90’) There's three minutes of added time here and QPR are given a free-kick in West Brom's half after a foul by Morrison. Hoilett tried to take it into the corner but loses the ball. One last chance for the visitors to get it up.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution S. Pocognoli is done for the day. C. Gamboa is his replacement. ---
(90’) OFF THE WOODWORK!!! Berahino almost makes it 3-3 from the tightest of angles. He twists Caulker inside and out before swinging his left foot at the ball. Green breathes a huge sigh of relief as it comes out off the post.
(88’) West Brom are looking for a response now. Varela forces a corner as he tries to cross. The corner goes over everyone but another is awarded.
--- 86’ Assist J. Barton gave the assist. ---
--- 86’ Goal! It's heart break for West Brom. The corner is delivered by Barton and Austin gets up ahead of Pocogonoli, who really should have done better, and heads the ball back across Foster! Loftus Road erupts. ---
(86’) GOAL!!!! That's the hat-trick. Austin makes it 3-2.
(86’) Fer and Austin link well and the midfielder tries an effort from just inside the box which is blocked by McAuley and the visitors can clear their lines. Hoilett then attacks down the right and forces a corner off Pocognoli.
(84’) Berahino almost steels in to score. Gardner attacks down the right and his cross is deflected towards Green. However the striker doesn't give up on it and almost knicks it ahead of the keeper.
(82’) Fer plays a lovely flicked pass around the corner and sets Austin free but he is unable to control the ball and falls in a heap to floor as the ball bounces off him.
--- 80’ Substitution N. Kranjčar enters play, replacing B. Zamora. ---
(80’) FOSTER DENIES AUSTIN! It looked as though Austin would complete his hat-trick. He was played through by Hoilett and tried to slide it past Foster first time but the keeper stayed up well and kept his side level.
(78’) The pace is beginning to slow as we enter the final stretch. Fer almost finds himself through on goal but a last ditch challenge from Pocognoli stops the former Norwich man in tracks.
(76’) Another chance for the visitors. Berahino found space down the right and attacked Onuoha. He cut back and chipped a pass to Gardner at the edge of the box but last weeks goalscorer sliced his left-footed effort out for a goal kick.
(74’) A half chance for Sessegnon. Wisdom plays a low cross from the right to Gardner. He touches it up to the winger who strikes it first time on the volley but it goes harmlessly wide of Green's right hand post.
(72’) Berahino looked to break down the right but was pulled back by Caulker. It appears everyone in the stadium saw it except for the officials who gave a throw-in to the visitors. The likes of Hill, Dunne and Caulker will not want to get into a foot race with the young striker.
(70’) Barton has a corner for the home side but it is cleared easily by West Brom. England striker Berahino has been introduced for the final 20 minutes as he replaces the disappointing Ideye.

(68’) West Brom have responded well since conceding the second goal but QPR look dangerous when they go forward. It makes for a very interesting final 20 minutes.
--- 67’ Substitution J. Hoilett comes on for E. Vargas. ---
(66’) Some more passing from West Brom on the edge of QPR's box. Sessegnon and Ideye try to play a one-two but the striker may have been better off going on his own instead of feeding his team mate as his pass was blocked by Hill.
(64’) A nice sequence of play from West Brom. The ball was passed around the centre of the park before finding its way to Varela, he fed Pocognoli who was making a run inside but his cross was punched clear by Green. The ball came back and Varela picked out Gardner but his shot was blocked and easy for the keeper to collect.
(62’) Sessegnon almost carved an opening for the visitors as he ran at Hill but his pass was just behind Ideye. Vargas went up the other end and picked out Austin with a long pass. The striker took it on his chest and tried to feed Zamora but Lescott was able to clear.
(60’) Sessegnon is not happy with Hill. Having conceded a free-kick the QPR man kicks out at the former Sunderland player who is on the floor but referee Pawson sees no problem and keeps his cards in his pocket.
(58’) It's been another average display from Ideye today. Following his chance early on he has not been involved in the game and you wonder how long it will be before Irvine decides to introduce Saido Berahino to the action.
(56’) West Brom were in a good position as Varela received the ball wide left and played in a cross however referee Craig Pawson blows up for an off the ball foul. Gardner had impeded Vargas.
(54’) For a second Austin thought he was through to finish off his hat-trick. A long ball by Hill finds the striker who races through on goal but the assistant's flag is up for offside.
(52’) West Brom have a corner that Pocognoli takes. Green comes out to claim but lets the ball slip through his fingers for another corner. However it is cleared by Caulker who rises high in the box to head away.
(50’) Joey Barton goes down in the area under a challenge from Morrison but the appeals for a penalty are waved away. West Brom go up the other end and Wisdom has a chance to test Green but his effort is blocked by Hill.
--- 48’ Assist Assist by B. Zamora. ---
--- 48’ Goal! It all started with a corner. Dunne won the header and must have thought he'd scored but Foster tipped it on to the crossbar. The ball fell into the box where Zamora headed it across the face of goal for Austin to poke home. ---
(47’) GOAL!!! QPR are level and it's Austin again.
(45’) QPR get the second half started. There are no changes for either side following the interval.

The home side will be thankful for Green who has kept the score at 2-1. The goalkeeper has made two good saves to deny Gardner and Sessegnon.
It has been an entertaining first half at Loftus Road. The visitors stormed into a two goal lead after twenty minutes as Lescott and Varela grabbed their first league goals for West Brom. QPR got back into the game as Austin converted a penalty following a foul from Morrison on Fer.
HALF TIME: QPR 1-2 West Brom.

(44’) Austin fires over the bar. The ball was bobbling around outside the West Brom area and it fell to Austin. The Englishman allowed the ball to run across his body before trying to place in into the corner with his right foot. But it goes over the bar.

(40’) ANOTHER SAVE BY GREEN!!! The goalkeeper produces a fantastic save to stop Sessegnon making it three. The wide man collected the ball on the touch line and unleashed a fierce effort from the right side of the area. Green threw up his left hand and tipped it over.

(38’) It's been an entertaining opening half here at Loftus Road with both teams looking to pass the ball around. Richard Dunne gets booked for a late challenge on Varela and gives West Brom the chance to play another ball in to the box.
(36’) The visitors look to set up another quick counter however Morrison's pass was behind Varela and it allowed the QPR defence to regroup. The Portuguese player's cross was easily cleared by Caulker.
(34’) Save by Green. Gardner's free-kick took a deflection off the wall and almost wrong footed the English keeper. However he was able to readjust his feet and tip the ball over the bar.
(32’) Free-kick to West Brom in a dangerous area. Henry is penalised for a foul on Morrison, he had no intention of going for the ball as he grappled with the West Brom player just outside the box.

(26’) The volume inside Loftus Road has risen considerably as the home side get back into the game. There is an interesting ten minutes ahead as West Brom look to hold onto their slender one goal lead.

(24’) GOAL!! Charlie Austin converts from the spot to make it 2-1.
(23’) PENALTY TO QPR!!
(22’) The pace and trickery of Varela and Sessegnon has caused many problems for the home side and are the main reason for the Baggies having this early lead. QPR have a corner as they look to hit back.

(11’) QPR's passing has been very wayward early on and Harry Redknapp is far from happy. The visitors are looking very comfortable as they continue to pass the ball well and the home crowd are beginning to get restless.
--- 10’ Assist The assist came from S. Sessègnon. ---
--- 10’ Goal! You can't say it hasn't been coming. Joleon Lescott has got his first goal since his summer move from Manchester City. Pocognoli took the corner and Sessegnon, who has looked lively early on, got the flick on to the defender who thumped his header past Green. ---

FULL TIME - TOTTENHAM HOTSPUR 2 BURNLEY 1
(90’) The referee blows and Tottenham have held on for the win!
--- 90’ +3 Substitution D. Rose enters the game and replaces C. Eriksen. ---
(90’) Lovely play from Spurs as they execute some neat one-twos around the desperate Burnley players, and Eriksen has a snap shot that flashes just wide of goal. It's his last action as he goes off to be replaced by Danny Rose.
(90’) We're into the second of three added minutes here.
(90’) GREAT TRY FROM WALLACE! The Scot whips in a dangerous delivery that is creeping towards the far corner, and Lloris has to scramble across to push the ball away.
(90’) Burnley have a free kick in a dangerous position here. QPR have just completed an amazing turnaround against West Brom which means the Clarets will drop back into the relegation zone if they lose here.
--- 89’ Substitution L. Jutkiewicz enters the game and replaces A. Barnes. ---
(89’) Burnley are making their final change and Jutkiewicz is the man to come on for the visitors. Barnes makes way after scoring that wonder goal in the first half.
(87’) Now Spurs have gained a league-high of eight points from 85 minutes onwards so far this season, Burnley need to give them a taste of their own medicine if they are to take anything from the game.
(86’) This isn't the only entertaining game in the history of this fixture. Who could forget the League Cup semi-final in the 2008/09 season when Burnley overturned a 4-1 deficit from the first leg, before two late goals saw Spurs scrape through to the final.
--- 84’ Substitution H. Kane is replaced with Soldado. ---
(84’) And that is Kane's final involvement today. He has been a breath of fresh air yet again for Spurs with another goal and his work rate has been received very warmly by White Hart Lane. Soldado takes his place.
(83’) Spurs come forward once more on the counter and should have put the game to bed in all fairness, but Eriksen couldn't produce the worthy final ball with Kane and Stambouli to aim for across the box.
(80’) Dyche appears to be putting all of his eggs in one basket there. He will be hoping the fresh legs down the flanks will inspire his side, but he does still have Lukas Jutkiewicz on the bench if he wishes.
--- 79’ Substitution R. Wallace enters play, replacing S. Arfield. ---

(76’) More good link-up play from Spurs leads to Walker getting to the byline, but he pulls the ball behind the gambling Chadli and Kane in the area.

(72’) Ings looks to be struggling here for Burnley. He is holding the bottom of his back and replays show that he landed awkwardly after contesting an aerial challenge in the box.

(47’) IMPORTANT SAVES LLORIS! Bright start from Burnley! Ings gets away from Fazio and draws a good save from Lloris at his near post. From the resulting corner, Burnley's top scorer gets another chance from a tight angle but the Spurs skipper is once again equal to it.
(46’) HERE WE GO! Burnley get us back underway.

(45’) That's it for a very entertaining first half at White Hart Lane.
(45’) VERY SHAKY FROM BURNLEY! The visitors have conceded 10 headed goals in the league this season and five from corners and you can see why. They cannot clear as the ball pings around the area, before eventually going behind for a goal kick.

(11’) Burnley won the reverse fixture 4-2 at Turf Moor on the final day, though it had little significance as they were already relegated while Spurs had already sealed a place in the top four.

What a brilliant end to a tense Tyne-Wear derby clash! Sunderland, who were on the back foot for the vast majority of the game, leave St. James' Park full of joy and with all three points in the bag after a great goal scored by Johnson in the final stages of the game. The visitors sat back and defended well, soaking up the Newcastle pressure before hitting the hosts with well-timed, quick counter attacks. However, recent Premier League form is on Newcastle's side, albeit only just. After embarking on a fantastic five-game winning streak that saw them rocket up the table, Alan Pardew's men have won just once in their last four league games, although that victory did come against league leaders Chelsea. In stark contrast, Sunderland, who start the day just outside of the relegation zone in 16th place, have won just one of their last nine league clashes and only twice all season, a poor record that is matched only by Hull City and Leicester City, who sit in 19th and 20th place in the table, respectively. Recent form counts for little when it comes to the Tyne-Wear derby, however, as both sides are well aware just how vital a win today is.
So, here it is: the ever-fierce and always exciting Tyne-Wear derby is upon us once again! The last three league meetings between the two sides have presented us with nine goals in total, and today's clash is guaranteed to be just as action-packed. Despite coming into this afternoon's game seven points ahead of their rivals in ninth place in the table, recent derby history isn't on Newcastle's side; their bitter rivals have won all of the previous three meetings, with the last two clashes at St. James' Park ending in comfortable 3-0 victories for the Black Cats. In fact, Newcastle haven't beaten their neighbours at home since October 2010, when they won 5-1 thanks to a Kevin Nolan hat-trick and a Titus Bramble red card.

For City, the relentless march on Chelsea continues. They rarely sparkled, but have enough quality to beat run-of-the-mill teams without needing to push themselves. Lampard's goal was well worked and Toure was again strong. Injuries to Dzeko and Kompany will take the gloss off this three points, though, especially with Pozo far less convincing than he was last weekend.
Despite working tirelessly, Leicester seem bereft of the quality that keeps teams in the Premier League. Schlupp and Drinkwater played well and Ulloa caused problems with his bulk when he came on. While a solid performance from Hamer in goal was a bonus, the Foxes will see this as another game when they did well, but not well enough.
The final score at the King Power Stadium, then, is Leicester City 0-1 Manchester City. The defending champions rarely broke out of a stroll and the home side threatened on numerous occasions without ever really forcing a save from Joe Hart.

(90’) Valencia pops up at the back post and puts the ball back into the danger area with a header. Reid attempts to get on the end of it but ends up fouling Wickham with a shove in the back in the process. That has took the sting completely out the game so we may be destined to see a draw.
(90’) Well we've got a massive FIVE minutes of added time here at the Stadium of Light, which has gave both teams a massive incentive to go ahead and grab a winner. As I said earlier, it could STILL belong to anyone!
(89’) CARROLL!!! HE COMES WITHIN INCHES OF WINNING IT! The 25-year-old collects the ball on the edge of the box and attempts to pass a precision strike into the bottom right corner but it goes just the wrong side of the post! Pantilimon was definitely struggling to get there!
(87’) West Ham now looking dangerous! Downing clips a free kick to the back post aimed towards Carroll but Brown does brilliantly to head behind for a corner kick. Sunderland under the cosh a little bit at the moment. Can they weather the storm?!
(85’) WICKHAM!!! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT! Fletcher flicks the ball into the path of his striking partner who takes a touch past the defender before rifling a strike at goal. It looks in all the way but Adrian pulls off an incredible save to deny the home side!
(83’) Brilliant by Larsson! Cattermole loses the ball in a dangerous position in the middle of the park and Downing counterattacks at pace! Not once but twice however the Swede saves his side with well-timed slide tackles! The Sunderland fans loves that!
--- 82’ Yellow card C. Wickham is cautioned by the referee. ---
(82’) West Ham make a change and it sees Enner Valencia come on to replace Kevin Nolan.
--- 81’ Substitution E. Valencia comes on for K. Nolan. ---
(81’) That is swiftly followed by another yellow card and this time it is Wickham who comes on the end of the referee's wrath. The Sunderland striker just went in a little too hard in an aerial challenge with Tomkins ,and goes into the book, much to the annoyance of the home crowd.
--- 80’ Yellow card S. Downing is cautioned by the referee. ---
(80’) The latest player to go into the book is Downing and it is for a rather needless challenge on Reveillere near the touchline. The Sunderland defender was going nowhere on the wing but the home side now have a free kick as the West Ham midfielder sees yellow.
(78’) Cattermole finds himself down the right-hand side and has two bites of the cherry to get a cross into the box. The first is blocked and the second is drilled into the hands of Adrian. The West Ham keeper sends the ball straight out for an attack. It is end-to-end stuff at the moment!
(76’) Great work by Pantilimon. West Ham pile bodies into the box as they look to float a deep free kick into the danger area, but they are forced to retreat as the Sunderland keeper takes the pressure completely off his defence with a commanding punch.
(74’) Just about 15 minutes remaining here at the Stadium of Light and it is still unclear who, if anyone, is going to show the attacking ambition to go on and win this. It has been such an even half that it really could be anyone! Interesting climax in store for sure.
(72’) Penalty shout for Sunderland! Larsson curls a cross into the box and Reid meets it with what looks like the top of the shoulder! It is pretty inconclusive from what I can see, and the referee shares the same view as he waves play on!
--- 70’ Substitution A. Johnson is done for the day. R. Álvarez is his replacement. ---
(70’) Second change of the match from the hosts and fair play to Gus Poyet as it is a fairly positive change from the Uruguayan. Adam Johnson is the man coming off and he'll be replaced by Ricky Alvarez, who could add just a little more creativity for the Black Cats.
(68’) Song and Nolan exchange a lovely one-two in the centre circle and the ball eventually comes to Cresswell who curls a cross into the box. Carroll throws himself at it but O'Shea does well to stand tall but ends up conceding the corner.
(66’) Decent attempt from Reid. Downing drives a wicked corner kick into the box and the New Zealand international loses his marker before glancing a header towards the far corner. Pantilimon eventually sees it over but it wasn't too far away!
(64’) Carroll!!! Almost a goal from nothing for West Ham! Sakho goes down under the challenge of Brown inside the box and the ball falls to his striking partner, who attempts to dink the ball over Pantilimon. The whole stadium takes a breath but the shot goes just north of the bar!
--- 62’ Substitution S. Fletcher comes on for J. Altidore. ---
(62’) We've got our first substitution of the match and it is no surprise to see Altidore coming off. The USA international has once again had a poor games in terms of posing an attacking threat inside the box, and he'll be replaced by Steven Fletcher.
(60’) West Ham get some joy down the right wing and the ball eventually comes to Jenkinson who whips a teasing cross to the front post. It could potentially be awkward for the home defence but Brown listens to the shout from his keeper and plays it safe by clearing into the stand.
(58’) We are nearly 15 minutes into the second half now and unfortunately both sides have failed to replicate the flowing attacking display of the opening 45 minutes. Sunderland looking dangerous from set-pieces, but not much in terms of goalmouth action so far after the break.
--- 57’ Yellow card Jordi Gómez goes into the referee's book. ---
(56’) That is extremely cynical from Gomez. West Ham finally manage to weather the storm from the various corner kicks and Downing leads the counterattacking charge with a powerful run down the left, but he is eventually tripped up by the former Wigan midfielder, who rightfully goes into the book.
(54’) Later in his career Carroll may prove to be useful as a central defender! The former Liverpool man has been back helping out his defence for an array of Sunderland corner kicks and has cleared two of them with commanding headers! He'd probably enjoy a few more years up top right enough!
(52’) Larsson takes the corner kick from the left wing and Carroll clears out of the danger area. Sunderland manage to recycle the attack and eventually earn another free kick on the opposite wing. This little spell of pressure from the hosts has the home side cheering in anticipation!
(50’) Reid leaves the park for treatment but thankfully manages to re-enter the action apparently unscathed.
(49’) We've got a small break in play at the moment as Reid is currently down after taking a nasty blow to the head from Brown. It looked completely accidental but the Sunderland man just trod on him during a corner kick. The defender is currently down receiving treatment.
(47’) Jenkison collects the ball at right back and threads a lovely pass down the touchline for Sakho, who strides forward before attempting a cross inside, but the ball cannons off a Sunderland leg and West Ham get the corner kick early in this second half.
(47’) SITTER FROM ALTIDORE! The Sunderland man gets into a great position at the back post but can't sort his feet out to turn in a chance from a few yards out!
(46’) We are back under way in this Barclays Premier League clash!
Half time at the Stadium of Light. It has been a very entertaining clash so far here between Sunderland and West Ham. The home side took the lead in controversial circumstances when Johnson went down softly inside the box and a penalty was awarded. Jordi Gomez converted to make it 1-0 but the Hammers fought back to 1-1 quickly thanks to a deflected strike from Downing. An even clash so far so a very interesting second half in store!
(45’) Sakho steps up and fires the free kick towards goal but Pantilimon reads it and makes the save.
(45’) West Ham have the opportunity to get their noses in front just before the break here as they get a free kick around 25 yards out. There is only two minutes of added time so a goal now would see them take a lead into half time.
(44’) Sunderland take a quick free kick and Jordi Gomez collects just inside the box to the left. He fires a teasing cross along the six yard box but there are no takers for the home side! That was absolutely begging to be smashed home but West Ham are let off the hook!
(42’) West Ham are now the team who are on top of the possession and Song is at the heart of it as he pulls the strings in central areas. The attack of the visitors just breaks down though as the on loan Barcelona man's pass down the right for Jenkinson is intercepted.
--- 40’ Yellow card W. Reid goes into the referee's book. ---
(40’) We've got our first booking of the match and Winston Reid is the guilty party. Altidore cleverly flicks the ball round the corner for Larsson before being took out completely by the West Ham defender, who deservedly sees yellow.
(39’) The home side are just enjoying a short period of sustained possession in and around the West Ham penalty area here as they look to reclaim their lead. It is proving quite difficult to penetrate the visitor's sturdy defence though as Allardyce typically has them very organised.
(37’) Johnson attempts a daft pass across the field to Reveillere and Sakho intercepts before sliding a lovely pass into the channel for Downing. The West Ham winger cuts inside on his right foot and has a crack at goal, but Sunderland are back in numbers and manage to make the block. The Hammers probably could have made more of that chance!
(35’) Before this match many people would have been forgiven for suggesting it may be a cagey affair, but that is far from what we have seen at the Stadium of Light so far. Both sides impressively attempting to notch up some goals.
(33’) Well that goal has definitely gave West Ham a lot of confidence here. They certainly never give up when they go a goal down and the fact that they equalised so promptly has made them believe they can snatch a lead before the break. Sunderland, meanwhile, attempting to regroup.
(31’) Song wins the ball back in the middle of the park and sends Downing down the left wing as West Ham counterattack. There is only Sakho ahead of the play though which means the Englishman is forced to revert back to Nolan.
--- 29’ Assist K. Nolan provided the assist. ---
--- 29’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAAAAAAALLLLLL FOR WEST HAM! THE HAMMERS STRIKE BACK ALMOST IMMEDIATELY! Downing collects the ball in the right channel and cuts inside on his left foot before smashing at goal. The attempt takes a deflection on its route to goal which allows it to nestle right in the bottom left corner! One-one! ---
(28’) Altidore gets a pass to feet and holds off the challenge of Tomkins before attempting a strike at goal. Unfortunately for the USA international it takes a deflection on the way through which takes all the venom out of it, allowing Adrian to save comfortably.
(26’) Of course, West Ham did actually go behind to Swansea early doors last week only to impressively come back to win. Can Carroll and co. pull their side back from a goal down again?
(24’) Well, after a bright opening at the Stadium of Light, and although it was under rather controversial circumstances, we have our opening goal. It will be interesting to see Sunderland's tactics as they attempt to protect this lead. Will they sit back or will they show attacking ambition?
(23’) Sam Allardyce looks absolutely incensed on that touchline! He clearly feels that was never a penalty and he is getting the fourth official quite an earful! Sunderland won't mind though as they have the 1-0 lead!
--- 22’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLLLLL FOR SUNDERLAND!! Jordi Gomez steps up and confidently dispatches the penalty into the bottom corner! One-nil! ---
(20’) PENALTY KICK TO SUNDERLAND!! Johnson takes on the West Ham defence and eventually goes down under the challenge of Tomkins! There looked very minimal contact but the ref points to the spot!
(18’) Sakho receives the ball to feet and turns sharply before running towards goal. The centre forward tries to find room for a strike at goal and although he is outnumbered in that central area, gets an attempt away. It is never troubling Pantilimon though who sees it over.
(16’) Vergini drives up the right wing and cleverly cuts inside before losing the ball. The Argentine gets it back and attempts to lift a cross into the box, but his pass is cleared. Johnson collects and goes for a similar cross, but Adrian comes off his line to claim.
(14’) It is all a bit feisty in the early stages here at the Stadium of Light. Cattermole, perhaps unsurprisingly, is involved as he leaves the boot in slightly on Carroll just inside the centre circle. Expect bookings in this one if the same formula continues!
(12’) How has Nolan escaped a booking here? Vergini initially gets the better of the West Ham man, who takes exception to this as he comes in with a rather nasty tackle. The referee, Phil Dowd, lets him off on this occasion but he probably won't get away with another.
(10’) Carroll looking a real danger at the moment. Cresswell makes his way down the left and then reverts back to Downing, who looks for his team-mate's run inside the box. The resulting header goes just over the bar but Sunderland will still be wary of the threat posed by the big striker.
(8’) Carroll takes the ball down with an assured touch and looks to fire a strike at goal, but the attempt is too central and Pantilimon makes another save. The West Ham man is getting it tight from the home crowd, so it should be interesting seeing his celebration if he were to find the net today!
(6’) Saaaaaaaave by Pantilimon! The ball breaks kindly to Jenkinson at the back post and the on-loan Arsenal man sends a precision half volley towards goal, but the Sunderland keeper gets down to make the vital block! The Hammers nearly take the lead!
(4’) The home side have probably settled the better here as they look to get their passing game under way early doors. West Ham seem content to sit back and soak up the pressure for the time being, but they will always pose a threat with the attacking prowess they have up top.
(2’) Carroll gets his first touch of the match and as you may imagine he is met with a chorus of boos from the Sunderland crowd. West Ham's striker, of course, used to ply his trade for Newcastle. No love lost there!
(1’) We are under way at the Stadium of Light!
The teams have made their way to the pitch and we are almost ready for kick off!
West Ham (4-1-2-1-2): Adrian; Jenkinson, Tomkins, Reid, Cresswell; Song; Kouyate, Nolan; Downing; Sakho, Carroll.
Sunderland (4-4-2): Pantilimon; Vergini, Brown, O'Shea, Reveillere; Cattermole, Johnson, Larsson, Gomez; Wickham, Altidore.
TEAM NEWS...
Speaking of Andy Carroll, the former Liverpool striker is somewhat the man of the moment in the Premier League. A magnificent display last weekend against Swansea saw him claim two goals with two signature headers, a performance which has lead pundits and fans alike to suggest he is back to his best. How will he do against the Sunderland defence today?
The last time West Ham travelled to the Stadium of Light was in March. Goals from Andy Carroll and Mohamed Diame cancelled out Adam Johnson's strike on that occasion as the Hammers recorded a narrow 2-1 win.
West Ham, meanwhile, are absolutely flying in the league. The Hammers have defeated Newcastle, West Brom, and Swansea with three consecutive wins and are currently placed 4th in the Champions League qualifying spot. The likes of Southampton and Arsenal are hot on their heels though, so Sam Allardyce will be hoping to continue their good form today.
The home side can take heart from the fact that they have won points against Chelsea and Liverpool recently, but they need to start winning games if they are to avoid being clawed into the dropzone.
Today's match features two teams with rather contrasting form. Sunderland are without a win in five Premier League games and haven't actually recorded a win at home since the beginning of October. Winning games has indeed been the problem for the Black Cats so far this campaign, but thanks to a flurry of draws they are placed out of the relegation zone in 14th. However, with just a two-point cushion between themselves and Hull in 18th place, they cannot afford complacency.
I'm Martin Macdonald, and I'll be taking you through the action!
Good afternoon football fans! Welcome to LIVE coverage of the Barclays Premier League clash between Sunderland and West Ham from the Stadium of Light!

As for Villa, it's hard to not give them some credit, as despite being down a man for the majority of the match, they had several opportunities to score themselves. On a different day, Benteke may have even won the game! Thank you for joining us here!
West Brom have finally done it, securing their first win since November to create some breathing room above the drop zone. It was laboured and difficult but three points are three points and Alan Irvine surely won't mind how they've been won now that they have been won!
--- 90’ +5 Yellow card C. Gardner gets yellow. ---
(90’) Gardner is booked very, very late here for a handball in the midfield. Time is technically up but it looks like Villa will be allowed to whip this all the way into the box. It's headed into the box and nearly falls to Guzan, all the way forward to try and do something, as another cross falls to Vlaar who volleys wide! That's the final whistle and West Brom have hung on for the win!
(90’) AND HOW DID BENTEKE MISS THAT!?!? A long ball played up falls kindly to the forward after Weimann chests it down. On the run, he takes a shot from just inside the box but completely messes up the technique, slicing the shot well wide! A fantastic chance for the visitors absolutely wasted!!!
(90’) Okore races forward to win posession off of Idaye and tries to force a corner but Lescott smartly shepards the ball out over the line ahead of Weimann. Two minutes of injury time left!
(90’) A late free-kick around midfield is awarded to Villa, which Guzan comes up to take with nearly his entire team in the box. It comes to nothing however after a home player is fouled in the box and a free-kick is awarded the other way.
(89’) Berahino nearly does it all himself, completely ignoring Idaye on the right and trying to sensationally score a wonder goal, but he shows too much of the ball to Vlaar at the last moment for the centre-back to poke clear! That's far too selfish from the forward!
(88’) Pocognoli charges down the flank before releasing the ball to Varela. It's worked back and forth as Okore mistimes his challenge, allowing Varela to send in a cross that Vlaar clears. Villa send numbers forward to search for a goal, but their first two crosses are cleared before and Varela collects posession.
(86’) Wisdom slips a pass to Sessegnon down the right flank but the latter is closed down and the home side have a throw-in. There doesn't seem to be a tremendous amount of urgency to score again, with West Brom looking more cautious to not be caught out behind by Villa.
(85’) After all that, the corner really has not amounted to much, with West Brom keeping possession so deep that all of their players have retreated. They'll gladly take the 1-0 win now, with just five minutes left to go!
(84’) A corner for West Brom now. Berahino plays it short to Varela before working it to the other side of the pitch. Sessegnon and Okore collide on the right flank and though the defender stays down, play is allowed to continue.
(83’) Foster and Benteke collide just inside the box following the goalkeeper's save and rebound to the striker; luckily for West Brom, the whistle is up for offside as that could have easily been a penalty!
--- 78’ Substitution A. Weimann enters play, replacing A. Cissokho. ---
--- 78’ Substitution C. Sánchez is done for the day. R. Vlaar is his replacement. ---
--- 78’ Yellow card Silvestre Varela is cautioned by the referee. ---
--- 72’ Goal! GOOOALLLLL GARDNER! The deadlock is finally, finally broken after a slip-up from Guzan. He hopped out of his area to try and collect a cross and missed it. The ball bounced around before falling to Gardner who rifled it into the net and made no mistake! 1-0 to the home side! ---
--- 70’ Substitution S. Berahino enters the game and replaces G. Dorrans. ---
(66’) POINT-BLANK MISS! Ideye gets in position to connect with a cross almost inside the six-yard area, but he can't keep his attempt down! That should have bulged the back of the net!
--- 65’ Yellow card A. Hutton goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 63’ Yellow card S. Pocognoli is yellow-carded. ---
(63’) Pocognoli didn't even try to sell that one - he pulls off a shocker of a dive that is easy enough to see with your back turned. No surprise to see the yellow card pop out.
(51’) Hutton races down his flank to get behind his marker and send in a cross but he mis-hits it and it goes wide!
(49’) Benteke is fouled and Villa have yet another free-kick in a fantastic area, just outside the box, as Wisdom seemed to just bundle over the striker. Cleverley whips it into the box but it fails to beat the first marker as it's headed clear!
(48’) Villa's hard work is paying off when they're awarded a free-kick for a late collision on Hutton near the centre of the pitch. Okoe lofts it to the flank on the left but it's cleared away from Sessegnon for a throw-in.
(47’) Agbonlahor thinks he's slipped in clear on goal but he's offside as he gets the pass and the whistle is duly blown. Villa don't seem to be settling for a point here as they roam forward whenever they have a ball, despite being a man down!
--- 46’ Substitution The second half is about to kick off, with Delph on for N'zogbia as Aston Villa roll the dice here today. The visitors begin with the ball and Delph is involved immediately here in his first start in two months following a shoulder injury. ---
This is much better from West Brom now who are encamped in front of Villa's goal. They still are not getting real chances on target but they're keeping Guzan busy as he swarms around to collect passes and mis-hits.
VARELA OVER THE BAR! He gets the ball just outside the box after none of his teammates could get on the end of Wisdom's cross. His rifle of a shot sails just too high!
Berarinho is finally about to warm up for his side, with West Brom working down the left flank now as Cissokho smartly gets between Sessegnon and the ball to clear for a throw-in. It's been a busy night for the former Valencia man.
HUTTON BLOCKS A SHOT IN THE BOX! Varela contorted his body to get on the end of a cross and send his effort towards goal, but the defender gets in his way to knock it out for a corner!
The ball is comfortably in Guzan's hands now after a deflection in the box. West Brom aren't really applying the pressure like they'd like to be now and Irvine may want to think about making a substitution to let his side take control of this match.
As for Villa, they are by no means out of this and Lambert may want to see if his side can sneak through with a point or maybe even snatch a win under the unlikeliest of circumstances.
(45’) And that's the half! It's been a lot of one-way traffic for the home side after Richardson's red card but with few genuine chances on net. This is a golden opportunity for West Brom to get back to winning ways and Irvine knows he has 45 minutes to try and come up with something here!
(45’) Some late defending for Villa here as Sessegnin was taken down by Cissokho right near the corner flag. Dorrans whips in a cross that's cleared out to Pocognoli on the edge of the box. The full-back takes a step and sends in a chipped shot that goes just over the bar!
(45’) As Delph gets instructions from Lambert on the sideline, the match is becoming physical on the pitch. Sessegnon works his magic down the right but Cissokho races back to clear a ball in towards Varela.
(44’) Hutton whips in a cross that falls towards Agbonlahor, making a late run towards the box. The latter can't quite control it as he tries a looping chip over Foster that doesn't really pay off and the goalie easily scoops up the pass.
--- 42’ Yellow card Cleverley joins the bookings after sticking his leg out against Varela, just when the forward had slid away from him. ---
(40’) A great move from West Brom and a great save from Guzan! Hutton is once again beaten for pace by Pocognoli in the box and it falls kindly to Sessegnon, who forces a reactionary save from the American from just yards away!
(39’) From a deep throw-in, Varela dribbles towards the middle of the pitch before laying it off for Gardner, who takes his shot without any extra touch and sends it wide of the far post.
(38’) This is incessant pressure from the home side, as may be expected following the red, but Villa are getting more confident as time grows on. Benteke does very well to hold up the ball under pressure from a number of defenders and lay it off for Agbonlahor who's just outside the box, but it hits McAuley and bounces away from goal.
(36’) Gardner now down in the box after losing possesion but it was all too easily and Dean doesn't make a call. Agbonlahor gets the ball seconds after and gets knocked over by Lescott on the halfway circle, winning his side a valuable free-kick and a chance to relieve pressure off the defence!
(34’) West Brom with some fantastic interplay, with Sessegnon at the heart of it on the right flank. The forward's cross looks like it hits Sanchez in the box but Dean doesn't call a penalty and the home side are furious!
(33’) Agbonlahor presses Lescott high in his own half and forces an awkward back-pass to Foster which the goalie manages to send clear, under pressure himself from Benteke.
(32’) For West Brom though they're certainly becoming more aggressive and finding joy working the ball down the flanks, though the visitors' centre-backs are dealing well with crosses so far.
(31’) Idaye is down on the ground after colliding with Okore in the box following a cross from Wisdom but referee Mike Dean simply isn't buying it, with very minimal contact being made.
(30’) Dorrans nearly makes something out of nothing as he tries a backheel to Varela deep in Villa's half, on the left flank, but Hutton is positioned well to intercept.
(28’) West Brom are poking and prodding but simply cannot find a way through Villa's defence at the moment, which is bending but not breaking. Clark is coming forward at the right moments to cut out plays and the home side have not yet figured out a way to break through.
(27’) Somehow Villa get their bodies in front of Idaye and Gardner as both players were winding up shots just outside of the box.
(26’) West Brom defend well and counter as Sessegnon races all the way to the byline to win a corner off of Cissokho. Pocognoli whips it in though Guzan races off his line to collect it.
(25’) Lescott concedes a free-kick in his own half for a push on N'zogbia as both players rose to try and get the ball. With Villa down a man, an opportunity like this free-kick simply cannot be wasted and they have several players in the box.
(24’) Gardner has the ball at the heart of the box and tries to spray it wide for a teammate to run onto, but no one has read his intentions and it drifts out for a goal-kick!
--- 22’ Red card! A SENDING OFF FOR RICHARDSON! And what a silly challenge that was - Richardson decided to stray forward in midfield, but knocked the ball slightly too far in front of him. Sessegnon had just poked it towards a teammate, and in desperation to win it back, Richardson went through the back of the West Brom player absolutely recklessly with his studs up. Villa are down to 10 men! ---
(20’) The ball in is a solid one and knocked behind for a corner, but West Brom clear and quickly counter. Wisdom and Dorrans exchange passes just outside the box before the latter finds himself in some space, takes a step or two, and slices a shot very well wide of the far post.
--- 18’ Yellow card The first booking of the match has been awarded as Mc Auley rashly slides in on Agbonlahor and doesn't get the ball at all. The Villa man's pace has been causing issues for the home side and now his team have a set-piece that Cleverley will whip into the box. ---
(17’) Fantastic interception from Clark! He races is on Gardner after Sessegnon's pass nearly set the former free. From the corner, Guzan rises high to collect Morrison's cross into the box.
(16’) Richardson gets the ball in midfield, roams towards the box, spots Benteke on his left... and chips in a pass that Foster scoops up. It's end-to-end, with play going from one box to another, though the play breaks as Benteke's sideways pass fails to reach anyone and slowly drifts towards the line.
(15’) This is proving to be an absolutely fascinating battle down the flanks for both teams, with Agbonlahor and Idaye straying out wide on opposite ends of the pitch to stretch fullbacks and send crosses into the box.
(13’) Sanchez makes an excellent interception deep in his own half that sparks a counter. Agbonlahor runs deep into the box and looks like he'll take a shot on goal but a recovery run from Wisdom knocks the ball out for a corner!
(11’) OHHHH NEARLY FOR VILLA! Hutton whips in a fantastic cross from deep in his own half that nearly finds Agbonlahor. The forward needs to be at full stretch to try and bring the ball down, but it bounces off his foot and kindly for Foster to gather!
(9’) Everything is coming down the left for West Brom who now use Pocognoli as an outlet. He completely leaves Okore left behind as he surges forward and unleashes a powerful shot for Guzan to parry!
(7’) McAuley rushes forward to cut out the ball after Agbonlahor outmuscled Wisdom on the flank. From the throw-in, Lambert's men play it deep to their defence and try to build from the back.
(6’) Cissokho is looked at by the physios as he went down under Idaye's attempt to head the ball, though he appears to be fine and is about to walk back onto the pitch.
(5’) West Brom break quickly after N'zogbia loses the ball in his own midfield. Varela does well to get aroung Hutton down the wing and whip in a cross that nearly finds Idaye but for a powerful header clear from Clark!
(3’) Some spark from West Brom! Idaye skipped past Okore near the left side of the box and tried to get a shot on target, but it squirms towards Guzan for the American to collect easily.
(2’) Villa poking and prodding around West Brom's box, playing it back and forth as they look for an opening. A pass from Richardson to Cissokho is overhit and Wisdom collects to let his side build.
(1’) WE HAVE KICK-OFF! The home side immediately try to find Silvestre poking around Hutton but the pass is cut out and Villa take a near-immediate throw-in. Guzan is called into action early to scoop up a long ball played into Varela.
We're just minutes away from kick-off now! The last three matches between these two sides at this venue have all ended in stalemates and they'll both be looking to buck the trend today!
Today eyes will likely be on Irvine's team selection, with top scorer Berarinho on the bench with Varela and Ideye starting, with neither player really having been given a solid run-out during the season so far.
Quite a few injuries for the visitors today, with Baker, Kozak, Cole, Senderos and Westwood all missing the match. For West Brom, Brunt and Olsson won't take part of the game due to injury.
Aston Villa (4-3-3): Guzan; Cissokho, Clark, Okore, Hutton; Richardson, Sanchez, Cleverley; Agbonlahor, Benteke, N'Zogbia.
West Brom (4-4-1-1): Foster; Wisdom, Lescott, McAuley, Pocognoli; Dorrans, Gardner, Morrison, Silvestre; Sessegnon; Ideye.
