My name is Ben Cullimore and it's been an absolute pleasure describing all of action to you this evening. Until next time, goodbye!
As for Newcastle, their second defeat in their last four league games leaves them in seventh place in the table, although they could drop as low as ninth depending on tomorrow's results. They go on to face Sunderland next weekend in what is sure to be a fierce and exciting clash.
Arsenal record a badly needed win that not only takes some of the pressure off Arsene Wenger but also moves them equal on points with fifth-place Southampton ahead of next weekend's clash against Liverpool. Despite Newcastle's best efforts, they fully deserve the win after a fantastic performance all-round, particularly from Sanchez, Giroud and Cazorla, who caused the Newcastle back four plenty of problems from start to finish.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 4-1 NEWCASTLE UNITED
(90’) Newcastle are still pushing for a late goal, but they're unable to find a way past Arsenal, who are camped inside their own half of the pitch as we enter the final minute of the game.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution Arsenal have made their final substitution of the game, with Oxlade-Chamberlain making way for 17-year-old debutant Maitland-Niles. ---
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
--- 88’ Goal! GOAL! Cazorla sends a cheeky Panenka that catches Alnwick by surprise and restores Arsenal's well-deserved three-goal lead. ---
(88’) PENALTY! Welbeck is brought down clumsily from behind by Dummett, resulting in a chance for Arsenal to make it 4-1.
--- 87’ Substitution And now Arsenal have made another change, with Coquelin coming on to replace Sanchez. ---
(86’) The resulting set-piece is cleared well by the Arsenal defence but falls at the feet of Tiote. He immediately unleashes a rocket of a shot from 30 yards out but it flies well over the top of the crossbar.
(85’) Good play by Newcastle on the left wing allows Dummett to get a cross away, but it's deflected off Bellerin and out for a corner.
(84’) Armstrong picks up the ball on the left flank before darting towards the byline, but his run is slightly overzealous and he ends up sending the ball out of play for a goal kick.
--- 82’ Substitution Newcastle have made their final substitution of the game, with Armstrong coming on to take the place of Perez. ---
--- 82’ Yellow card Janmaat dives into Cazorla on the left wing, resulting in a yellow card that means the Dutchman will be suspended for Newcastle's next game. ---
(81’) It's all Arsenal at the moment but they seem content to hold onto the ball in the middle of the pitch as they look to hold on to their lead.
(79’) Newcastle lose possession in the middle of the pitch, allowing Sanchez and Welbeck to break away quickly. The Chilean burts forward before teeing up his teammate on the edge of the penalty area, but he stays too near to Coloccini and the centre-back is able to dispossess him with a great last-ditch tackle.
(77’) Bellerin darts down the right wing before whipping a quick cross towards the back post, but it's slightly too deep and Sanchez is unable to keep the ball in play.
(75’) Newcastle are enjoying a good spell of possession at the moment but they are finding it incredibly difficult to find a way past the hosts, who have the vast majority of their outfield players back inside their own half of the pitch as they look to hold on to their two-goal lead.
--- 73’ Substitution Giroud receives a standing ovation from the Arsenal fans as he makes his way off the pitch to be replaced by Podolski. ---
(72’) Welbeck and Oxlade-Chamberlain link up well on the byline before the latter tries to dart into the left hand side of the Newcastle penalty area, but his run is brought to an end by a good interception from Williamson.
(71’) Chance after chance for Arsenal! Coloccini tries to be too clever with the ball, allowing Welbeck to steal it from under his nose on the byline. First Sanchez shoots, then Cazorla, then Oxlade-Chamberlain, before, finally, Gibbs sends a low half-volley into the side-neeting. What a let off for Newcastle!
(69’) Sanchez muscles his way past two Newcastle midfielders before playing a lovely one-two with Giroud, but he ends up tripping Dummett from behind, resulting in a free kick for Newcastle deep inside their own penalty area.
(67’) Nervy moments at the back for Newcastle! Tiote is beaten easily by Sanchez before the Chilean cuts into the penalty area and fires a low cross towards the edge of the six-yard box, but Janmaat is there to clear the danger with a good sliding interception.
(65’) Welbeck, Giroud and Cazorla link up wonderfully well on the edge of the Newcastle penalty area before the Spaniard unleashes a fierce shot from the left hand corner of the box, but his effort ends up crashing into the side-netting.
--- 63’ Assist The assist came from J. Colback. ---
--- 63’ Goal! GOAL! Newcastle have pulled one back! Colback whips the free kick into the middle of the box where it finds Perez, who is easily able to peel away from his marker before sending the ball into the bottom right hand corner of the net with a deft header. Game on! ---
(63’) Colback is fouled by Giroud, resulting in a free kick for Newcastle 10 yards away from the left hand corner of the penalty area.
(62’) The corner is curled in by Sanchez towards the near post but it fails to beat the first man, who is comfortably able to clear the danger with a strong header.
(61’) The Chilean regains possession for Arsenal before being brought to the ground by the byline on the left flank, resulting in yet another free kick for the hosts. He whips it into the heart of the penalty area where Alnwick is just about able to get a hand on it to send the ball out for a corner.
(60’) Sanchez fires the resulting set-piece towards goal, but it fails to beat the wall of black and white shirts in front of him.
--- 59’ Yellow card Oxlade-Chamberlain is cynically brought to the ground by Tiote, resulting in a yellow card for the Ivorian and a free kick for Arsenal on the edge of the penalty area. ---
--- 58’ Assist Bellerín gave the assist. ---
--- 58’ Goal! GOAL! It's 3-0! Arsenal are cruising! The hosts break away quickly and Bellerin then sends a brilliant low cross into the heart of the penalty area where Giroud, who is completely unmarked, is easily able to side-foot the ball into the top right hand corner of the net. ---
--- 57’ Yellow card Cabella is almost immediately tripped over by a poor challenge from Oxlade-Chamberlain, resulting in a yellow card for the Arsenal midfielder. ---
--- 56’ Substitution Newcastle have decided to make a double substitution as a result of going behind. The first player to come on is Riviere, who takes the place of Cisse. ---
--- 56’ Substitution And the second is Cabella, who replaces Ameobi. ---
--- 54’ Assist The assist came from A. Sánchez. ---
--- 54’ Goal! GOAL! The birthday boy Cazorla doubles Arsenal's lead with a brilliant chip! Sanchez links up wonderfully well with the Spaniard before the latter lifts the ball over the top of Alnwick and into the back of the net from the edge of the six-yard box to make it 2-0. ---
(54’) Sloppy play at the back by Newcastle almost results in two chances on goal for Arsenal, but both times they are unable to make the mistakes count.
(52’) Giroud and Welbeck link up well just outside of the Newcastle penalty area, before the latter then flicks the ball back to Cazorla. The Spaniard tries to send it back to the Frenchman, who is on his way into the box, but the pass is poor and is intercepted easily by Williamson.
(50’) Perez loses possession midway inside the Arsenal half of the pitch, allowing the hosts to break away on a quick counter attack. Sanchez sprints through the middle of the field but is then brought down by a cynical shirt tug from Colback.
(48’) A bright start by Newcastle allows Ameobi to break away down the left flank before sending a dangerous cross into the heart of the penalty area, but it's only able to find Szczesny, who collects the ball comfortably.
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half-time break.
It's been a very good opening 45 minutes for Arsenal, despite the fact that Newcastle have slowly but surely got themselves back into the game after an encouraging display in the final 15 minutes of the half. Sanchez has been superb, linking up well with Giroud on several occasions, which was evident when the hosts took a well-deserved lead after just 15 minutes, but, to the visitors' credit, they have fought back extremely well, and Alan Pardew will be confident about their chances of finding that all-important equalising goal if they are able to start the second period in a similar fashion to the way that they finished the first.
HALF-TIME: ARSENAL 1-0 NEWCASTLE UNITED
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be one minute of added time.
(44’) Wonderful play by Sanchez! He picks up the ball on the right flank before chipping a brilliant cross towards Giroud, whose headed effort takes a slight deflection that sends it over the top of the crossbar.
(42’) Ameobi regains possession midway inside the Arsenal half of the pitch before attempting to send a through-ball into the path of Cisse, but the pass is slightly too heavy and the Senegalese striker is unable to make contact with it.
(40’) Sanchez cuts the resulting set-piece back to Cazorla, who then unleashes a rocket of a shot from just outside of the penalty area that is deflected out for a corner, which the visitors then deal with well.
(39’) Arsenal break away quickly through Sanchez, but the Chilean's darting run towards the Newcastle penalty area is brought to an end by Dummett, who brings the forward down with a last-ditch challenge from behind, which results in a free kick for the hosts.
(38’) The resulting set-piece is fired in well by Colback but Arsenal deal with the danger well, denying Perez the opportunity to get a shot away from the right hand side of the box.
--- 37’ Yellow card Bellerin dives into Dummett and trips the left-back over with a poorly-timed challenge, resulting in a yellow card for the Spanish youngster and a free kick for Newcastle on the left flank. ---
(35’) Great save by Szczesny! A brilliant cross is whipped in by Colback that fiinds Gouffran, who forces the goalkeeper into a great diving stop. The ball then falls to Cisse, who unleashes a half-volley from a few yards out, but again the Arsenal shot-stopper denies Newcastle the opportunity to equalise with another great piece of goalkeeping.
(33’) What a chance for Welbeck! Arsenal pass the ball around patiently before Sanchez scoops a lovely pass into the path of the Englishman, who then unleashes a fantastic scissor-kick from the edge of the Newcastle box that bounces just wide of the far post.
(31’) Colback whips a brilliant diagonal pass over the top of Mertesacker and into the feet of Cisse, but the Senegalese striker ends up miscontrolling the ball and sending it into the hands of Szczesny.
(29’) Wonderful play by Bellerin! The youngster sprints through the centre of the Newcastle midfield, beating two Newcastle players before being dispossessed by Janmaat just as he's about to shoot. The Dutchman's tackle results in a free kick for Arsenal, which the visitors deal with well.
(27’) The resulting set-piece is curled into the heart of the Arsenal penalty area, but Ameobi is unable to get any sort of decent contact on the ball and his effort bounces out for a goal kick.
(26’) Perez wins the ball for Newcastle midway inside the Arsenal half of the pitch before sending it out to Ameobi, who twists and turns around Bellerin before firing a low cross off the Spaniard and out for a corner.
(24’) Great play by Arsenal! Bellerin sends a lovely bouncing cross into the heart of the penalty area where it almost meets Welbeck in front of goal, but Colback is just about able to get a foot in to send the ball away from the striker and out for a corner.
(22’) Sanchez picks up the ball on the right hand side of the penalty area before cutting it back to Giroud, who is then sent crashing to the ground by what looks like a poor challenge from behind by Tiote, but, despite the Frenchman's pleas, the referee waves play on.
(20’) Oxlade-Chamberlain skips past two Newcastle midfielders before unleashing a fierce, Ramsey-esque shot from 35 yards out but, unlike Ramsey's effort during the week, it ends up flying well wide of the goal.
(19’) Giroud and Welbeck link up well in the middle of the pitch, with the two playing a wonderful one-two between one another, but the latter's final pass is slightly overhit and ends up in the hands of Alnwick.
(17’) Arsenal score again, but it's ruled out! Welbeck darts into the box and seemingly brings Janmaat to the ground before chipping the ball past Alnwick and into the back of the net, resulting in the goal being ruled out and Newcastle being awarded a free kick inside their own penalty area.
--- 15’ Assist A. Sánchez gave the assist. ---
--- 15’ Goal! GOAL! Arsenal take a well-deserved lead! Coloccini loses possession in the middle of the pitch, allowing the hosts to break away quickly. Giroud sends the ball out to Sanchez on the right flank, who steadies himself before whipping a lovely cross into the penalty area where it finds the Frenchman, and he has no trouble whatsoever beating Alnwick with a brilliant header. ---
(14’) The hosts break away on a swift counter attack though Oxlade-Chamberlain, but he ends up scuffing his attempted pass to Giroud, who was completely unmarked on the edge of the Newcastle box, bringing the move to a disappointing end.
(12’) Arsenal knock the ball around patiently on the edge of the penalty area before Sanchez tries to twist and turn towards goal, but his run is stopped by a good interception from Coloccini.
(11’) Welbeck lifts a lofted pass over the top of the Newcastle defence and into the path of Sanchez, but it's slightly overhit and ends up bouncing into the grateful hands of Alnwick.
(9’) Mertesacker hits the crossbar! The resulting set-piece is whipped towards the edge of the six-yard box where it finds the defender, and his backwards header beats Alnwick before crashing off the underside of the crossbar.
(8’) Giroud and Williamson battle for the ball near the byline, resulting in the first corner of the game for Arsenal.
(7’) Tiote and Sanchez clash going for the ball, resulting in the Arsenal forward receiving a boot in the stomach, but, despite the rash nature of the Newcastle midfielder's challenge, the referee decides not to show him a yellow card.
(6’) Again, Sanchez does well down the right flank before attempting to play a quick one-two with Giroud, but the Frenchman's pass is poor and is cut out comfortably by Williamson.
(4’) Oxlade-Chamberlain tees up Sanchez on the right hand side of the penalty area before the Chilean chips a lovely ball into the path of the on-rushing Bellerin, but Gouffran is there to shepherd the ball out of play for a goal kick.
(2’) Colback loses possession straight away, allowing Arsenal to break away on a quick counter attack, but the former Sunderland man is just about able to get back in time to cut out Welbeck's attempted low cross.

In stark contrast to Arsenal, last weekend proved to be a magical experience for Newcastle, as they became the first side to win against Chelsea in a competitive game since Atletico Madrid in April when they beat the league leaders 2-1 in a brilliant game at St. James' Park. The win, their third in their last five Premier League games, will no doubt have filled them with confidence ahead of today's game against an Arsenal side that have shown signs of weakness this season, and a victory here at the Emirates will see them leapfrog the North London side and climb up to sixth place in the table ahead of next Sunday's Tyne-Wear derby.
After picking up back-to-back wins against West Bromwich Albion and Southampton, Arsenal suffered another set-back last weekend when they were beaten 3-2 by Stoke City, with all three of the Potters' goals coming in a first half to forget for Arsene Wenger's men. As a result, they head into this afternoon's game with three defeats from their last five league games, leaving them in sixth place in the table and with an impressive Newcastle side breathing down their necks.

HALF TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 2-0 LIVERPOOL. The scoreline is flattering for the hosts, who have scored on their only two chances of the match. Much was made about Rodgers' decision to drop Mignolet for Jones, but after 45 minutes the keeper cannot be blamed for either goal, while having little else to do otherwise. Liverpool look threatening in attack, but the lack of a true centre forward has hurt them. They cannot afford to wait any longer before bringing on Mario Balotelli or Ricky Lambert... or both.
(45’) The halftime whistle from Martin Atkinson is met by a raucous applause from the Old Trafford faithful. The Red Devils are on their way to picking up all three points in Louis van Gaal's first derby as manager!

(38’) STAT ATTACK: There have been 15 red cards in the Premier League matches between Manchester United and Liverpool, the second highest total after the Merseyside Derby (20). Seven of those red cards have come in the last 13 meetings.

Brendan Rodgers says the reason is simple, he just felt they needed a change. It is quite a bold move in a match of this magnitude, and could do plenty to damage the Belgian keeper's confidence, but Jones has plenty of experience to his name. It does look like the Dutchman will employ a diamond in midfield, but the surprise comes up top where James Wilson gets the start alongside Robin van Persie. In his interview just a few short moments ago, Van Gaal said Falcao is fit to start, but he went with Wilson because his speed is needed in this match. The other noteable changes come at the back where Jonny Evans starts ahead of the injured Chris Smalling, while Phil Jones returns after a lengthy two-month absence on the sidelines. Swansea 1-2 Tottenham: Referee Martin Atkinson ends proceedings at the Liberty Stadium and the Swans' winless run against Spurs in the Premier League rumbles on. The hosts were the bigger attacking threat for much of this match and looked far more likely of going on to steal all three points after they drew level at the start of the second period. But the visitors, who have made late goals something of a trademark in recent weeks, claimed victory right at the end through Eriksen and they move up to seventh in the league table.

(77’) Shawcross does just enough to see the ball over the line after a dangerous pass was played into Welbeck for another goal-kick to his side. Arsenal are still pressing here but their ideas are coming up short now instead of looking dangerous.
(76’) Solid play from Stoke who are keeping the ball well and still going forward in search of another goal. They lose it however when Adams' chested pass is collected by Cazorla, though the pass to Welbeck down the flanks is overhit and Begovic has a goal-kick to take.
(75’) The home side are camped around their own box, pinned back into defending by relentless hounding from the visitors. Pieters is forced into heading a good cross out for a corner, and from the play, Sanchez is offside and gives Hughes' men a chance to breathe easily.
(74’) Podolski gets on the end of a cross in the box and his header finds its way into Begovic's hands, much to the relief of the home side who are now just trying to cling on for the win!
(73’) Absolutely breathless, this match, as Adam's delivery is a good one but no one can get onto it before it goes over the line for a goal-kick.
--- 72’ Yellow card A. Oxlade-Chamberlain is yellow-carded. ---
--- 71’ Yellow card K. Gibbs is cautioned by the referee. ---
(71’) Martinez now called into action on a free-kick to collect a rather routine ball into the box. All momentum with the visitors now who are playing with a swagger and belief, but Oxlade-Chamberlain is booked for taking down Pieters on an attack and now the home side have yet another free-kick they'll send into the box!
--- 70’ Assist The assist came from A. Sánchez. ---
--- 70’ Goal! ARSENAL SCORE AGAIN! WHAT A MAD, MAD GAME WE HAVE HERE! Following Begovic's fantastic save on Welbeck, Ramsey gets the ball from the ensuing corner and sensationally volleys it into the back of the net! 3-2 here and there's so much more to come!!!!! ---
--- 69’ Substitution Hughes makes a proactive change as he sends on Adam for Diouf in an effort to just hold the ball in the midfield more ---
--- 68’ Goal! Penalty goal scored by Cazorla! ---
(68’) AND CAZORLA MAKES NO MISTAKE FROM THE SPOT! 3-1 as he sends his low shot past Begovic, who angrily keeps the ball after conceding! There's over twenty minutes left here, and though some Stoke players are claiming Flamini made a meal of the challenge, there's a real sense now Arsenal could take something from this!
(65’) BOJAN SCORES AGAIN... no it's ruled out! The ball was in the back of the net but the referee spots an infringement in the build up and somehow Arsenal are off the hook!
(64’) Flamini is wide again down the flank but he's drifted offside as Welbeck tries to slip him the ball just on the edge of the box.
--- 63’ Substitution G. Whelan enters the game and replaces Muniesa. ---
--- 63’ Substitution Another roll of the dice for both managers, as Giroud comes off for Podolski and Muniesa, who's down injured, gets taken off for Whelan. ---
(62’) Welbeck and Cazorla combine well in the box to keep possession. It's played out wide to Flamini who's made an overlapping run and his cross/shot ends up being a bit of neither as it goes over the crossbar.
--- 61’ Yellow card Chambers is booked as he has his arm around Crouch and just pulls the striker back when the home side has the ball. ---
(60’) Diouf races into the box to get on the end of Walters' cross and sees his shot deflected wide pof the far post! The corner is of course played into Crouch who's some way from the net and his acrobatically volley sails harmlessly over the bar.
(57’) AND ARSENAL HAVE A PENALTY! WHAT A DRASTIC CHANGE OF FORTUNE! From Stoke scoring and being ruled out to Diouf taking down Flamini in the box seconds later to concede a penalty to the visitors!
(57’) A SENSATIONAL MOVE FROM SANCHEZ AND HE HITS THE POST! Was that the moment that would have turned this game around? The former Udinese man collected the ball from deep, skipped past Walters, Cameron and Muniesa, rounded the keeper and sent his finish off the near post and out for the home side to clear!
(54’) Stoke are now getting more and more into this, hounding Arsenal and cutting down their passing lanes. The longer this goes on the more desperate the visitors will become, and Hughes' men will want to take advantage of that.
(52’) Arsenal's shape now is interesting, with Flamini dropping in to occupy the space left by Bellerin's substitution whenever the home side have possession.
(51’) From a wide angle, Bojan goes directly on net and forces Martinez into a fantastic diving save to parry the ball out!
(50’) Tenacious defending from Shawcross who robs Giroud just outside the box and sparks a counter. Oxlade-Chamberlain thinks he fairly won the ball from Diouf just near the byline outside of his box on the left but it's judged to be a foul, and Stoke have another free-kick they'll want to whip onto Crouch's head.
(49’) This is the sort of start Wenger will have wanted for his side, with Welbeck immediately making an impact but the goals not having arrived just yet. Stoke are under immense pressure at the moment and the ball seems magnetically attracted to the feet of the players in yellow.
(48’) After Sanchez's cross is cut out, Gibbs gets on the end of the ball on the overlap and whips in a cross that forces Pieters into an awkward header. The visitors are surging forward here but simply cannot get a shot off.
(47’) Welbeck gets involved here almost immediately, smartly letting a pass roll past him before he can turn and shoot to win his side a corner. The ball played in is a poor one however and Begovic collects it without fuss.
--- 46’ Yellow card P. Crouch goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 46’ Substitution D. Welbeck enters the game and replaces Bellerín. ---
(46’) And the match is back! In the first minute two noteworthy things happen: Danny Welbeck comes on for Bellerin in a very attacking move from Wenger, who has nothing to lose at this point, and Crouch is booked for an elbow on Mertesacker.
As for Arsene Wenger's men, it's been a terrible day, with the offence making chances but not doing much with them at all and the defence exposed by two crosses and a set-piece. He'll need his side to come out roaring and score an early goal to have any chance of taking points here now!
That's the half! Stoke go into the break with a commanding lead over an Arsenal side that have been terribly exposed by Bojan's trickery and Crouch's height. It's been a fantastic performance from Stoke who look nearly certain to keep all three points today.
--- 45’ Goal! GOAL STOKE! THEY'RE TAKING A 3-0 LEAD INTO THE BREAK! It's an absolute calamity following the corner, where a ball headed downwards by Crouch falls kindly from a deflection into Walters' feet and he simply smashes it into the roof of the net! ---
(45’) Another excellent break from Stoke, who work the throw-in all the way down the pitch and force Bellerin into conceding a corner in the dying moments of the first half.
--- 44’ Yellow card And we have the first booking of the game after Muniesa tries to stop Sanchez from breaking free and clumsily misses the ball entirely, bringing down the forward. Instead of Cazorla taking this, it's delivered into the box by Sanchez but sails over everyone and goes out for a Stoke throw-in! ---
(43’) Neither side can get a grip on the ball at the moment as it pings back and forth in the midfield. Eventually, it ends up with Diouf wide, who squares it for Cameron to send back to his defence. Stoke are confidently working the ball up-field.
(41’) Sanchez is furious as he's penalized for a handball in Stoke's box as he argues the ball hit his side and not his arm. The call costs Arsenal possession just when they looked to be in a shooting position.
(39’) Stoke are insatiable today with Bojan switching flanks at will and causing Arsenal's fullbacks quite a few headaches in terms of marking him.
(37’) Arsenal surge forward in search of an equalizer and Sanchez's shot from outside the box is knocked out for a corner. Giroud gets his head onto it and Begovic is forced into an awkward clearance as he pushes the ball over the bar!
--- 35’ Assist The assist came from J. Walters. ---
--- 35’ Goal! BOJAN DOUBLES STOKE'S LEAD! OUT OF NEARLY NOTHING! Arsenal are in some serious trouble here after Walters' cross deep in the box found the Spaniard alone making a run onto it and he sends his first touch into the back of the net past Martinez! 2-0 to Stoke! ---
(33’) Cameron finds the ball with acres of space down the middle after some good work by his teammates down the right and he decides to take an effort on goal, though it, too, sails very high over the bar. Both sides have been happy to shoot today but neither have been terribly efficient at it!
(31’) Bojan stands over the ball and whips it into the far corner, where Diouf heads it back across goal towards Crouch. There's a mad scuffle to try and get the ball from both teams and the whistle is blown for a foul on Martinez, giving Arsenal a chance to breathe a sigh of relief!
(29’) The visitors try to ram their way down the middle of the pitch but find a sea of red in front of them that easily collects the ball when Giroud's first touch shows too much of it to Shawcross. As Walters counters down the left, Gibbs pulls him back and Stoke now have a free-kick just outside the box.
(27’) From the corner it comes as little surprise that Bojan looked for Crouch's head, and the striker once again made contact with the ball but once again could not direct his header into the net!
(26’) Bellerin tries a quick ball through to Giroud that bisects both midfields and most of Stoke's backline but Begovic races off his line to collect it. Stoke work it down the other end and N'Zonzi's shot is sliced out for a corner by Flamini.
(24’) Excellent movement from Arsenal as they work the ball down the left and cross it to the right before Gibbs sends it back into the box. Oxlade-Chamberlain, who's been very active this match, rises high to head it to goal but the ball once again goes over the bar!
(22’) Cazorla indeed goes right for net from about 25 yards away but overhits the ball, which sails harmlessly over Begovic's goal. He apologizes to his teammates as he knows he should've done better there!
(21’) Bardsley knocks over Sanchez and Arsenal take the free-kick quickly, but the referee isn't happy with the effort and calls it back to be taken again. Cazorla is now standing over it, ready to smash his effort towards goal.
(19’) Cazorla finds himself on the edge of the box with some space and takes a dipping shot that goes just over the crossbar!
(17’) The visitors' response to Crouch's aerial threat: don't let him get the ball. The full-backs and wingers are doubling up on Stoke's wide players now to prevent crosses from entering the box and it works well when Gibbs and Oxlade-Chamberlain combine to rob Bojan of the ball.
(16’) Another near chance for Arsenal! The side won possession deep in Stoke's half and raced forward. Oxlade-Chamberlain's cross nearly found the foot of Ramsey, attempting an overhead kick, but Shawcross got in the way to push it clear!
(15’) Tempers are starting to flair here as Crouch and Chambers pull each other to the ground. The striker has been giving Arsenal's new centre-back a nightmare of a start here with his height and is a continued threat on nearly every cross.
(14’) Bojan tries to force an opening into Arsenal's box as his pass fails to reach Crouch. At the other end, the visitors commit a similar mistake when a ball sent through for Sanchez to race onto is easily cleared by Begovic. Bojan makes up for it with a superb cross into Crouch's head but the tall striker diverts the ball wide!
(12’) Mertesacker steps up with perfect timing to intercept the ball during a dangerous Stoke attack, and though the home side wins back possession and crosses to Crouch to knock-down in the box, none of his teammates get on the end of the loose ball and Arsenal whisk it clear.
(10’) From one end right to another, as Walters sends in a cross that keeps Martinez on his toes. The visitors spring Bellerin free down the right and he just manages to keep the ball in with a sliding cross that finds Giroud but the Frenchman can't direct his header on target and it goes wide!
(9’) The visitors are starting to settle into a rhythm here and a quick passing sequence sets Giroud in the box with the ball. He's unable to beat either central defender and sends it wide for Gibbs to cross, but it's right into Begovic's grasp.
(8’) A brief, nervy moment for Arsenal as Oxlade-Chamberlain loses the ball after a reckless pass that sparks a counter and forces Bellerin to streak down the flank and clear off of Bojan just as the former Barcelona man was running into space!
(7’) Much better from Chambers now as he confidently heads a delivery out for Cazorla to orchestrate the counter. Oxlade-Chamberlain switches flanks and Grioud tries a backheel in the box to Sanchez but it doesn't fool Muneisa, who rushes to clear.
(6’) Arsenal win a free-kick about halfway into Stoke territory but Cazorla's effort into the box fails to beat the first man. In the follow up play, Sanchez and Bardsley tangle on the wing and the infringement is given to the Arsenal player, who's in much disbelief!
(4’) Immense pressure from Stoke here deep in Arsenal's half forces Ramsey to knock the ball out for a throw-in. The visitors are all over the place but get a break when Diouf's touch near the byline goes out for a goal-kick.
(2’) Needless to say, a nightmare start for Arsenal, who would have come into this match with a spring in their step after hearing that Jose Mourinho's men lost to Newcastle and therefore cannot emulate their famous Invincible season this year.
--- 1’ Assist Assist by M. Diouf. ---
--- 1’ Goal! GOOOALLLL FROM THE KICK-OFF! Crouch got on the end of a botched clearance from Chambers in the box, who totally missed a clearing header from the cross, to simply poke the ball into the net from point-blank range! What a howler and what a start we have here as Stoke lead 1-0! ---
Both sides are on the pitch lining up for their pre-match processions. We'll be underway in just a few minutes now!
The recent form between these two sides could not be more varied; the visitors have won each of their last three between the league and the Champions' League and the home side have lost each of their last three in the Premier League.
There's certainly been no love lost beween these two sides over the years, especially since Ramsey broke his leg following a terrible tackle from Shawcross four years ago. Both are in the starting eleven today, and Arsenal will need their midfielder to be in sterling form, with the visitors winning just once in seven trips to the Britannia.

Jedinak leads his team-mates over to the club's travelling fans and the Palace players are being clapped off after putting in a cracking display, which could have brought all three points had it not been for Lloris' heroics.

(77’) BIG CHANCE!! A moment of sloppiness by Dier gifts Palace a corner, and Puncheon from the resulting corner finds a bit of space and drives a shot off the underside of the crossbar.

(71’) Puncheon finds himself in a one-on-one situation with Davies, but the left-back again does well defensively to block the ball out for a corner to the visitors. The Palace substitute has looked strong since coming on.

(61’) It's the Palace supporters who are making all the noise inside White Hart Lane so far as their side continue to thwart Spurs from finding any joy in this second-half. The hosts have really struggled to get in-behind to cause Speroni enough problems.

(45’) The fourth official has indicated there will be one minute added onto the first-half, with Spurs currently on the break.

(30’) Spurs are momentarily down to ten men as Fazio is receiving treatment on a head injury sustained from an aerial tussle with Chamakh.

(11’) The game is still yet to settle as both sides are continuing to lose possession quite cheaply. Palace have come into it more in the last few minutes, though.
(8’) Palace are still finding it hard to pass their way out of their own half so far and are therefore being forced to thrust the ball long towards Chamakh.
(7’) CHANCE! Spurs make a break up the pitch through Eriksen and some neat work from the Dane saw him nutmeg Kelly down the left, but drag his shot into the side netting.
(6’) Everytime Palace are managing to nick the ball away from Spurs, they are being pressed by Pochettino's men and are being given little time to break on the counter.
(4’) It's been a very slow start to today's game, with Spurs seeing the majority of the ball so far as they look to patiently decide the best way to break down a sturdy Palace structure.

(90’) Everton win it back and this is going to be their last chance to mount an attack. Jagielka launches it long but Demichelis heads clear. The ball comes back inside and Eto'o has the ball stolen from his toe by the Argentine as he looks to get in a shot.
(90’) The big men of City combine again to win back the ball from Barkley, who has looked lively since his introduction. Time is running out for the Merseyside team now. Clichy has a throw-in in Everton territory.
(90’) Barkley tries to fashion a shooting chance for himself but is crowded out. Milner releases Nasri who is matched for pace by Distin. Everton win the throw-in. Hibbert brings it out on the right.
(90’) The ball pinged around in the City box there but Toure has the presence of mind to carry it clear.
--- 90’ Yellow card R. Barkley gets yellow. ---
(90’) Now Barkley is booked diving after Lampard's challenge. The game is getting rather fractious. Everton have a corner kick after Demichelis wastes a free-kick.
--- 88’ Substitution L. Osman enters the game and replaces K. Mirallas. ---
--- 88’ Yellow card Y. Touré gets yellow. ---
(88’) Barry did lead with his elbow in that challenge with Milner, though it would be hard to argue that was deliberate. Eto'o and Toure have a heated conversation about the fouls that led to the Ivorian's booking.
(87’) Toure is retrospectively booked for fouling Eto'o in the build-up to that cross. Osman is on for Mirallas. Milner is still down. He has been very good today.
(86’) Milner cannons a shot into Distin when a pass seemed like the wiser option. Everton cannot hold onto the ball at the moment though. Barkley carries it forwards and Eto'o finds Lukaku. His cross is forced out though. Milner is down with a head injury.
(84’) Milner's corner is cleared easily. City retain the ball, though. Their next attack is thwarted though, and Everton bring it forward. Leon Osman is getting ready to come on.
(83’) Both sides will have chances now, the game becoming more open as legs tire and space around the pitch increases. Hart plays it up to Dzeko who shields it well. He picks up a return pass from Milner but Jagielka blocks the Bosnian's shot for a corner.
(82’) Nasri wins a foot race against Hibbert and drags the ball inside before firing a shot straight at Howard.
(81’) JOE HART SAVES! Barry strides forward and plays it into Eto'o, who flicks it up into the path of Lukaku. The Belgian stiker volleys it and Hart pulls off an instinctive save with his left hand. The only winner there was football.
(80’) Lampard is indeed in the centre, with Nasri on the left and Milner on the right. City have retained their 4-2-3-1, though they have less pace out wide now.
(79’) Everton build well around the City box but Zabaleta steals the ball and Milner brings it out. They maintain possession with some neat interplays.
--- 78’ Substitution Jesús Navas is done for the day. F. Lampard is his replacement. ---
(77’) Lampard plays a lovely, deft reverse pass in to Dzeko, who heads it back inside into the path of Milner. The Englishman shoots first time on his weaker foot and puts it over, but that was sparkling football.
(75’) Eto'o blazes over after a good, cross-field run from Barkley. Lampard is going to come on for Navas. He will likely push Nasri out wide and operate in that central position before Dzeko. Unless City go to a 4-3-2-1, which would be festive.
(74’) Nasri wins a corner off Baines. Demichelis and Jagielka go for it and the Argentine heads weakly towards Tim Howard.
(73’) Seamus Coleman is incensed not to have won a free-kick after a clear trip by Milner. He has a point, too.
(72’) The corner from Baines is smashed out by Clichy but the away team retain possession. For a short while, anyway, before City steal it back. Milner plays a superb ball under pressure out towards Navas and Zabaleta, but the full-backs cross is poor and Everton win a goal-kick.
(71’) The free-kick is slightly to the right of Joe Hart's goal. Baines and Mirallas stand over it and the Belgian fires it into the wall, from which it loops over and out for a corner.
(70’) Everton are having a good go at this and City have had to retreat. Toure concedes a free-kick right on the edge of the box for a foul on Eto'o.
(69’) Hart gathers the high, looping cross under pressure from Distin, again looking assured under the high ball. That was good play from Everton though, with Barkley to the fore.
(68’) Eto'o is crowded out after a good run, Mangala eventually robbing him of the ball. Barkley then tees up Eto'o for another shot and it's deflected wide for a corner.
(66’) Nasri fires it in towards the back post and Distin's header is weak, but Milner cannot get any force onto his own headed effort and Howard gathers easily. Lukaku concedes a free-kick fouling Clichy.
(65’) Jagielka clears with ease but City win a free-kick as Mirallas tugs back Navas.
(64’) Dzeko plays in a cross and Distin just manages to force it out. Zabaleta and Toure combine well and win a corner.
--- 63’ Substitution José Ángel Pozo is done for the day. E. Džeko is his replacement. ---
(63’) City are all over Everton now with Milner to the fore. When the Sky Blues are in this sort of mood, they tend to score. Everton bring it out though but Zabaleta tackles Barkley well.
(62’) Milner again finds himself in space and pulls the ball back into the danger area. Nasri dallies on the ball, though, and cannot work a shooting opportunity before being crowded out.
(61’) Eto'o pirouettes and tries to find Hibbert but the full-back can't latch onto it and Hart gathers. Milner is left sprawling after a challenge and City use the interruption to bring off Pozo for Dzeko. The young Spaniard has does very well, moving nicely and only being denied a goal by a superb save from Howard.
(59’) Fernando blocks an Everton shot and Toure carries it out. Barkley has already offered more of an attacking threat for the away team but City do not look ruffled.
(58’) Nasri does brilliantly to shield the ball from Barry, before finding Toure, but Everton clear eventually. Barkley surges forward before laying it off to Eto'o. Clichy intervenes and plays it long but Pozo cannot gather.
(57’) The corner is too deep and Hart gathers with ease. One poor kick aside, he has looked comfortable without having much to do.
--- 56’ Substitution R. Barkley enters play, replacing M. Bešić. ---
(56’) Navas plays an angled ball into the corner for Pozo but Distin watches it cautiously and then clears off the striker, winning a throw-in. Fernando wins the ball well but Everton comes again and force a corner. Distin lumbers up.
(55’) Barkley will offer Everton more creativity but could well leave them a little less solid. Besic is the man to make way. Let's see what the young English midfielder can do.
(53’) Barkley is stripping off to come on. Eto'o tries an overhead kick and Hart saves with ease. Everton attack again but Mirallas fires it high and wide.
--- 52’ Yellow card G. Barry is cautioned by the referee. ---
(52’) Nasri looks for Navas with an angled cross but Howard gathers well. Everton need to keep the ball for a bit and regain their composure. Baines fires a cross into Navas and his second attempt finds Mirallas offside.
(51’) Barry is late and heavy on Milner and gets a yellow card, his 99th in the Premier League. That's some haul. He will miss Everton's next match.
(49’) HOWARD SAVES INCREDIBLY! Milner goes inside Hibbert and pulls it back swiftly. Pozo arrives and fires it in low but Howard, diving away from the ball, sticks his leg out and diverts it over the bar. Superb, instintcive keeping from the American.
(48’) Clichy brings it in-field and tries to play in Nasri but it doesn't come off and Everton bring the ball away through Eto'o. Demichelis wins it back well, though, and the home side can build again.
(47’) City are so swift and sure when on the front foot, but Navas gives away a free-kick against Mirallas. Everton can't hold onto it though and the home team attack again.
(45’) And they are off. Everton get us underway and hoof it forwards to Lukaku. City win it back swiftly though and attack with verve. Zabaleta is brought down but it's a goal kick.
Join me, Alex Stewart, shortly for the second half of this intriguing Premier League clash. It's Manchester City 1-0 Everton, LIVE!
Despite losing Aguero early on, City have been mobile and agile in attack, with the young striker Pozo impressing with his movement and positioning. One negative was Mangala's nasty challenge on Eto'o, for which he was rightly booked.
The home team are content to let Everton play the ball around from one side to the other, but as soon as they go for a more vertical ball, light blue shirts swarm in and press hard. City also look very swift and dangerous on the break.
A Yaya Toure penalty is the difference at half-time after Phil Jagielka's needless and clumsy challenge on James Milner. Both team's have played the ball around nicely, but City look significantly more likely to penetrate when they attack.
(45’) That's it! Half-time at the Etihad and it's Manchester City 1-0 Everton.
(45’) Everton have a little period of pressure themselves before the end of the first half. There are light blue shirts back in numbers though, and Clichy eventually thwarts a good attack. City are allowing the away side plenty of the ball but preventing them from passing it forwards that much, which is clever.
(45’) Coleman chests down the ball, which had looped up from a blocked Navas shot, and there were cries for handball. They would have been wrong, though.
(44’) There will be four minutes of extra time. Barry is caught offside and doesn't chase the loose ball, even though it had not been blown for. Hart gathers.
(43’) Fernando tries to play in Milner but his pass is too heavy. Toure is back on. Everton have a throw-in deep in City territory.
(42’) Toure is still down having twisted his knee and he looks to be in real pain. This would be a big blow after the loss of Aguero if the Ivorian has to go off. Lampard would be the natural replacement.
(41’) Toure carries it forwards and loses the ball in a coming-together with two Everton players. Milner tries to create a chance for Navas whose shot is deflected and loops over the bar.
(39’) Nasri fires a shot into Distin after good work from the Frenchman. Milner then drags a cross back and Pozo goes for it but the Everton centre-half blocks again.
(38’) Baines crosses but it's too high for Lukaku. Coleman gathers and tries to put it in again. Mirallas follows up the rebound and his shot is forced wide for a corner, which City clear with ease.
(37’) While City have looked excellent going forward, Everton have been good in possession too. Their final ball has let them down, however, and does so again as Coleman gives it away. The home team fail to break, though.
(35’) Everton concede a corner again. Fernando challenged Howard for it at the near post but the big American keeper did well to pluck the ball away. Pozo won that corner with clever movement and he has done well since replacing Aguero early on in the game.
(33’) Toure dinks a sneaky ball into the cross-field run of Zabaleta. Navas takes the ball and lays it off to Nasri, who has a shot blocked, before Pozo drags an effort just wide. Some of City's build-up play has been sparkling.
(32’) Besic and Barry combine to release Baines. The play is switched to Coleman and then back to Besic again, but his ball into Eto'o is too deep and slow and Hart gathers comfortably.
(31’) City are now controlling possession and look comfortable with the ball. Milner's pass into space has too much on it and Howard gathers.
(30’) There is a lovely ebb-and-flow to this game. Navas and Baines tussle and the City player concedes a free-kick.
(28’) Toure has a shot that cannons into Jagielka and out for a corner. Nasri's effort is cleared but he gets another go. Pozo shoots on the turn but it's knocked away. Jagielka scrambles to hoof it clear.
(27’) Everton are still playing with purpose and poise but City have the measure of control. This is an intriguing contest.
--- 26’ Yellow card Fernando gets yellow. ---
(25’) Manchester City 1-0 Everton, then, without either side dominating. Fernando gets booked for clattering Barry. The resulting free-kick goes into the wall and is cleared.
--- 24’ Goal! TOURE CONVERTS! Howard dives correctly to his right but Toure's spot-kick is hit too hard and low. It's difficult to say that had been coming, but both sides have played well enough to deserve a goal. ---
(22’) PENALTY! Jagielka goes in on Milner as they both chase Toure's through ball. That seemed like a fair penalty and Milner was running out of space.
(21’) So far, this game is well poised with both teams looking assured in possession, Everton arguably more so. Baines clears well from a cross with Navas lurking.
(20’) A very loose pass from Hart gives the ball straight to Mirallas but City are able to cover their keeper's error.
(19’) Intricate play between Navas, Nasri, and Zabaleta fashions a shooting chance for Toure but his shot is wide. That was nice from City, though perhaps they should attack with greater urgency.
--- 18’ Yellow card E. Mangala goes into the referee's book. ---
(18’) Eto'o will be able to continue but looks justifiably angry and in pain after that challenge from Mangala. City build from deep.
(16’) Zabaleta has a throw-in deep into Everton territory and City win a corner. Mangala and Eto'o contest the high ball and the centre-back appears to karate kick the away stiker right in the back. He gets a yellow card and that was a very, very stupid and malicious challenge.
(15’) City concede a free-kick after a series of challenges in a congested midfield area. Toure wins the ball though and releases Nasri.
(14’) Toure tries to play in Zabaleta from what looks like a training ground routine but his pass is behind the Argetine full-back and the momentum swings back to Everton.
(13’) City have some possession themselves now. Toure is brought down and the home team have a free-kick in a dangerous area.
(12’) Coleman is caught offside as Eto'o tries to play it to him. The Cameroon striker is working hard to close down City's midfield too.
--- 11’ Yellow card S. Coleman is cautioned by the referee. ---
(11’) The away team are in the ascendancy here and City's passing game is not working too well at the moment. There are dark blue shirts pressing every time they have the ball. Clichy produces a deep cross but the bearded Tim Howard claims well.
(9’) Demichelis clears after Lukaku had shouldered aside Zabaleta and produced a good, low cross. The away team retain possession and they look very solid at the moment. Coleman is booked for a shirt-pull on Clichy after the Irishman loses the ball.
(8’) Zabaleta challenges Mirallas well and City bring a good Everton passage of play to an end. Neither side is going hell-for-leather at the moment though, with the home team still settling after the Aguero injury.
--- 7’ Substitution S. Agüero is done for the day. José Ángel Pozo is his replacement. ---
(6’) Nasri takes and Zabaleta shoots wildly into an Everton defender. City keep the ball though, but a home player is caught offside.
(5’) Baines does well to intercept a through-ball and Everton attack through Besic. The away side keep the ball well but then Fernandinho steps in and steals it well from Mirallas. Aguero is coming off as City have a corner, but it's Pozo who is on.
(3’) Aguero looks to have over-extended his left leg, putting stress on his left knee. Dzeko is warming up just in case.
(2’) Aguero is down after a clash with Besic. He looked to have caught Coleman with a stray arm there as well.
(1’) And they're off, City in blue and Everton in darker blue. City get us underway and pass it back before looking to burst forward. Mirallas lumps Navas and Howard smothers a loose ball in his box.
It's Manchester City vs Everton, LIVE!
Join me in ten minutes for what promises to be an exciting encounter between one side looking to assert their domestic dominance and another looking to rescue a faltering season.
Mirallas will play in behind a strong front two for the away side, with Baines and Coleman looking to provide width in attack and force City's wingers to track back. Milner against Baines will be a great contest. Tim Howard will be looking to put some shaky recent performances behind him and will need to be at his best to thwart the in-form Aguero.
Mangala, the man sent off against the Saints, is in for the injured Kompany, and Milner comes in for Jovetic. City are on a good run and minor tweaks to the side are unlikely to upset them against the Merseyside team, who've won just one game in five in the EPL.
Manchester City looked superb in dismantling a strong Southampton side despite going down to ten men last weekend and are strong favourites against an indifferent and unpredictable Everton side.
Everton substitutes: Robles, Alcaraz, Garbutt, McGeady, Barkley, Pienaar, Osman.
Everton starting XI (3-5-2): Howard; Hibbert, Jagielka, Distin; Baines, Barry, Besic, Mirallas, Coleman; Eto'o, Lukaku.
Manchester City subs bench: Caballero, Sagna, Kolarov, Boyata, Lampard, Pozo, Dzeko.

FULL TIME: WEST HAM 3-1 SWANSEA CITY. Despite falling behind early, the Hammers battled back admirably to claim all three points in convincing fashion. Andy Carroll had a brace and Diafra Sakho added a third as West Ham win the game which they controlled from start to finish, to move them into third place in the Premier League.
(90’) West Ham pass the time off the clock with Swansea accepting the inevitable. That is the end of the match as Chris Foy blows his whistle for full time as 'I'm forever blowing bubbles' echoes through Upton Park.
(90’) STAT ATTACK: In his last two games against Swansea City, including today, Andy Carroll has two goals and three assists.
(90’) There will be five minutes of added time, for Swansea to try and erase this deficit.
(89’) Full of confidence now, West Ham are passing this game to completion. It's a party right now at Upton Park, which will surely add to the enjoyment of this monumental win for the Hammers, who are on their way to third place. Nobody is leaving as we approach the final minute, with the fans singing and dancing in unison.
--- 87’ Assist Assist by A. Carroll. ---
--- 87’ Goal! Carroll heads on a goal kick into the path of Sakho, who nudges the ball past Richards and Williams, before breaking into the area. The ball is bouncing, and he unleashes a cannon of a half-volley over Tremmel and emphatically into the back of the net! Sam Allardyce leads the applause, and you can see just how much this win means to them! ---
(87’) GAME OVER! DIAFRA SAKHO EMPHATICALLY STRIKES WEST HAM INTO THIRD PLACE IN THE PREMIER LEAGUE!
--- 86’ Substitution N. Dyer enters play, replacing Àngel Rangel. ---
--- 86’ Substitution C. Kouyaté is replaced with J. Collins. ---
(86’) James Collins comes into the match to replace Kouyate. It appears as though Allardyce will go with five at the back in the hopes of seeing this one out. It is a smart decision from the manager, but they cannot afford to just sit back here. They have shown their ability to take the game to Swansea and smother them in possession, which they should continue through the final minutes.
(84’) West Ham push forward again, but spend very little time in the attacking third before giving the ball away. Their reluctance to commit too many men forward is perfectly understandable, but there is no reason for them to strictly defend and let Swansea keep the ball while a man down.
(82’) WHAT A WASTE! Greay work from Ki, who picks out Sigurdsson at the top of the area. The midfielder sees his shot blocked by Reid, but it falls for Bony. The striker tries to nudge it into space, but Bartley runs onto it, firing his shot miles over the bar. Bony looks on in disgust at the wasted opportunity for Swansea.
(80’) Swansea begin to apply the pressure now, despite their numerical disadvantage. They win successive corners, but West Ham deal with it. Their clearances are not convincing, leading to a few moments of chaos inside the penalty area. Sigurdsson keeps it in, and his shot deflects behind for a corner.
--- 79’ Substitution J. O'Brien enters play, replacing C. Jenkinson. ---
(78’) OFF THE WOODWORK! So close to a third and decisive goal for West Ham, as Sakho does so well to get the ball past Williams and run clean through on goal. He has time and space, with Sigurdsson struggling to recover, but puts his effort off the far post! Carroll has something to say about that, as he was rushing on and appeared to have an easy tap in for the hat-trick had Sakho spotted him.
(76’) STAT ATTACK: Swansea have managed just one victory in their 23 league visits to West Ham all-time, which came back in the old Division Two in August on 1956 (D5, L17).
--- 75’ Substitution B. Gomis enters play, replacing J. Montero. ---
(74’) Swansea are forced into another change, as they bring on striker Bafetimbi Gomis to help try and chase an equalizer. Montero is the one to give way, though the Ecuadorian forward has looked very dangerous on the counter on the day.
(72’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY DENIED! There is an incredibly lengthy delay as Swansea ready their backup, Guy Tremmel. Play resumes, and West Ham continue to press. Another ball is played into the box by Jenkinson, and Williams pushes out at Carroll to prevent him from getting the header, but nothing doing says referee Chris Foy.
--- 71’ Substitution G. Tremmel enters play, replacing L. Britton. ---
(70’) There will be much controversy surrounding the decision to send off Fabianski and whether it was the right one. The keeper certainly tried to slow down Sakho, and was successful in doing so, but did not completely take him down. However, as the last defender, he did prevent a clear goal scoring opportunity, and to Chris Foy's credit, there was little hesitation in showing red.
--- 68’ Red card! FROM BAD TO WORSE FOR SWANSEA! Fabianski has been sent off! Sakho chases a ball forward, with the keeper well out of goal. The striker gets there first and nudges it forward. He is slowed down a bit, but keeps chugging forward. His hits the inside of the post from a tight angle, with the goal gaping, and referee Chris Foy brings it back for a foul, before giving the Swansea keeper his marching orders! ---
--- 66’ Assist S. Downing provided the assist. ---
--- 66’ Goal! It is a free header for Andy Carroll! Absolutely shocking defending from Swansea. West Ham win a corner and the ball is delivered in without any real pace to it. Williams fails to get position on the striker, who is able to guide the ball into the far corner! ---
(66’) A SECOND FOR ANDY CARROLL AND A LEAD FOR WEST HAM AT THE BOELYN GROUND!
(64’) Garry Monk looks like he is preparing his first change, as his side grow increasingly fatigued. Swansea have been under pressure for much of the match, which has mean a lot of running and chasing from their midfielders. They could use a change to help shore things up and ensure they come away with points.
(62’) West Ham have been a bit too predictable as they look to grab a winning goal. They are attacking the flanks well, continuing to find space, but their crosses into the area are not resulting in anything at the moment. Carroll is being held in check, and you just wonder if Sam Allardyce will make a few tweaks to his team's approach for the final 30 minutes.
(60’) OFF THE WOODWORK! West Ham are controlling play, much like the opening of the first half, and Swansea break on a counter. Montero sprints forward and picks out a pass for Bony. Routledge is making a run to his right, but the striker goes for goal himself, blasting a well placed effort off the bar!
(58’) SENSATIONAL RUN! Cresswell makes it look so easy along the left, fending off a defender before spotting a slight gap and darting through between two players. He cuts towards the centre, but rushes his cross just a bit, failing to pick out Carroll at the far post.
(56’) Panicked moments at the back for Swansea. West Ham have not carved out much in terms of chances, but their willingness to press high up the pitch and commit men into attack has made for some very uncomfortable moments at the back for the visitors.
(54’) STAT ATTACK: After winning their opening three league matches of the season, Swansea have managed just three wins from their 11 matches since (D4, L4).
(52’) There is a delay now as Kouyate and Bartley come together and clash heads. The Swansea defender appears to have got the brunt of it, as he is down with the medical staff out to attend to him. Kouyate does not appear any worse for wear, giving himself a little rub as he casually walks away from the scene.
--- 50’ Yellow card Wayne Routledge picks up the first yellow card of the match as he chases down a ball in his own end. Winston Reid is first to get to it, to keep the pressure on, but he is taken out by the attacker who rather cynically concedes a free kick. ---
(48’) Very positive start from West Ham as they continue to apply pressure on the Swansea goal. They win an early corner and keep the ball in the final third. They are quick to win the ball back after giving it away, which has provided the visitors with very little time to regroup.
--- 46’ Substitution D. Sakho enters the game and replaces E. Valencia. ---
(46’) West Ham get the second half underway, with a new look about them. Diafra Sakho, who has missed the last three games, has returned to the pitch, replacing Enner Valencia for the final 45 minutes.
Diafra Sakho is out on the pitch, warming up, which is a welcome sight for West Ham fans as their top scorer looks set to return from injury with a second half substitution.
HALF TIME: WEST HAM 1-1 SWANSEA CITY. The two teams head into the break all knotted up at one, in what was a very open and entertaining first half. Wilfried Bony put the visitors in front, completely against the run of play after 20 minutes, but the Hammers continued to apply the pressure and it finally paid off. Andy Carroll pulled them level with half time approaching, spectacularly heading home Carl Jenkinson's cross.
(45’) Nothing much doing in added time, as referee Chris Foy sounds his whistle to bring an end to this first half at Upton Park.
(45’) The medical staff is out to help Kouyate off the pitch, as he has picked up a bit of a knock. He has a bit of blood coming from his mouth, but it does not appear to be anything serious which would keep him from playing the second half. Meanwhile, the assistant referee has signaled for two minutes of stoppage time.
(43’) STAT ATTACK: Andy Carroll had not managed a goal or assist in 796 minutes of league play (including today) with West Ham, a dry spell that stretched out over his last 10 appearances. It is his first goal since March in the Premier League.
--- 41’ Assist C. Jenkinson provided the assist. ---
--- 41’ Goal! Credit to Jenkinson, who finds space on the right and sends a spectacular ball into the penalty area. Carroll has eyes for it, and times his run to perfection, getting there ahead of Rangel at the far post. He meets it with his head, and guides it back across goal and into the top corner! ---
(41’) ABSOLUTELY SUPERB HEADER FROM ANDY CARROLL! WEST HAM PULL LEVEL!
(39’) The Hammers are looking increasingly threatening yet again. Carroll has made himself a real nuisance in and around the penalty area, creating plenty of chances with his ability to win the ball in the air. Swansea are just barely holding out, and will be eager to get this game to half time.
(37’) BLOCKED BEHIND! Colossal error at the back as Williams' attempted clearance is sent straight off his defence partner and kept in by West Ham. Song picks out the run of Nolan, but his shot is just blocked behind for a corner, as he throws his arms up to pump up this Upton Park crowd.
(35’) Free kick awarded to West Ham on the left, and it is played dangerously into the area. Carroll meets it, heading it back towards Song, who scuffs his shot. The hosts keep the pressure on, and Jenkinson plays a brilliant ball in for Cresswell at the far post, but his header is straight into the waiting arms of Fabianski.
(33’) STAT ATTACK: Gylfi Sigurdsson has now created nine goals for Swansea this season, second only to Cesc Fabregas (10) in the Premier League.
(31’) INCHES WIDE! West Ham continue to keep possession well, but there is not as much pace or intent to them at the moment. Valencia gives the ball away in his own half and Sigurdsson pounces to set up Bony. The striker takes a shot from just outside the area, but it sails just wide of the far post.
(29’) Carroll chases down a long ball in attack and pushes Britton aside to concede a free kick. Frustration is beginning to kick in for West Ham, who feel they have been hard done by this early deficit. They will have to keep their focus and find the tempo that saw them put Swansea under considerable pressure through the opening 20 minutes.
(27’) Brilliant movement! Swansea are looking increasingly dangerous on the counter, this time Montero picks out Sigurdsson on the left. The midfielder cuts into the centre and drives a shot toward the near post, but Adrian is able to fist it away. Pressure stays on from Rangel, who crosses in to the danger area, but West Ham deal with the threat.
(25’) WONDERFUL DEFENDING! Cresswell floats a ball in toward the far post for Carroll, who heads it back into the centre. Valencia is there to meet it, but his half-volley is blocked by Williams and behind for a corner!
(23’) West Ham continue to press now in search of an equalizer, but it has left them susceptible on the counter. Carroll has options to either side, but gives the ball away at the top of the area. Routledge breaks and he has Bony with him, but an errant through ball runs into the waiting arms of Adrian. The hosts will have to be careful at it would spell disaster if they conceded a second.
(21’) STAT ATTACK: Swansea are winless in their last three meetings with West Ham (D1, L2), and have not managed to score over that span, a drought finally broken by Wilfried Bony.
--- 19’ Assist J. Montero provided the assist. ---
--- 19’ Goal! Spectacular ball from Sigurdsson to open West Ham up on the counter. He sends Montero into the area, and the forward cuts it back for Bony, who makes no mistake, putting his first time shot past Adrian and in at the far post. It comes completely against the run of play, as the Welsh side steal the lead at Upton Park! ---
(19’) SWANSEA OPEN THE SCORING COMPLETELY AGAINST THE RUN OF PLAY!
(17’) GREAT SAVE! Ashley Williams concedes a free kick along the right with a foul on Valencia. The delivery from Downing is superb, picking out Nolan at the near post, but his soft redirection is kept out by Fabianski! The pressure is kept on, and Tomkins goes for the spectacular, but a block from Williams sniffs out the chance.
(15’) Although he has not got on the end of a cross just yet, Carroll is doing a wonderful job of winning and holding up the ball in midfield. He brings a high pass down and starts West Ham forward on a quick break, which results in the first real chance as Jenkinson's cross in for Nolan is put just wide of the near post by the midfielder.
(13’) West Ham win a corner as Valencia gets the better of Richards near the corner flag. The delivery is dealt with by Swansea, but the pressure remains on. It is worked out to Cresswell on the left, but his cross just eludes Carroll in the centre, allowing Bartley to scramble clear.
(11’) Possession is all with West Ham through the opening 10 minutes. Swansea are not eager enough to close down on the ball at the moment, which has made life easy on the hosts. The Hammers high tempo and high pressure has made for a very bright start, with Cresswell and Jenkinson constantly joining the attack.
(9’) Incredible pressure from West Ham, who despite not cutting out a clear scoring opportunity just yet, are making it very difficult on Swansea to pass it out of their own half. The hosts have a fantastic tempo to their play and are closing the ball down magnificently well when they give it away.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: West Ham have picked up 24 points from their opening 14 matches, which represents their best ever start to a Premier League campaign. The last time they managed a better tally in the top flight was back in 1983, where they registered 29 points from 14 games.
(5’) The full-backs are getting in very advanced positions in the early going for West Ham. Swansea look a bit panicked when these high, looping balls are played into the box, as Andy Carroll is drawing plenty of attention, which creates space elsewhere in attack for the likes of Downing and Valencia.
(3’) West Ham apply some good early pressure, playing it around well in the final third. Alex Song looks up to the task already, getting himself on the ball and advancing it into some real attacking positions. Cresswell is eager to get forward, and he can promise to make life very difficult on Swansea, who have started off a bit timid at the back.
(1’) Swansea kick-off and we are underway at Upton Park! The visitors, moving left to right, are in their all white strip, with West Ham sporting their red tops with light blue shorts.
STAT ATTACK: West Ham have won both matches against Swansea City at Upton Park since the Welsh side’s debut in the Premier League in 2013, with the Swans failing to score in both of those games.
West Ham are surging towards the top four this season, with Swansea nipping at their heels. The two sides have a chance to gain important ground on both Liverpool, who drew yesterday, and Arsenal, who lost. In fact, West Ham would vault themselves into third place in the table with a victory today, ahead of Southampton and Manchester United who face off tomorrow.

SWANSEA CITY (4-2-3-1): Fabianski; Rangel, Bartley, Williams, Richards; Britton, Sung-Yong Ki; Routledge, Sigurdsson, Montero; Bony.

The duos return pushes Mauro Zarate and Morgan Amalfitano to the bench. Diafra Sakho also appears fit, but will be forced to begin the match on the substitutes bench.
