Pearson will no doubt suggest Konchesky should not have been sent off, but in truth his team left it too late to try and get back into it. He now faces an almighty battle to keep his job, but for now I've been Tom Maston and thanks for joining me.
The full-time whistle blows, and Aston Villa have recorded their second consecutive win. Overall they deserved victory, with Hutton's neat finish securing the points after Clark equalised Ulloa's opener early on.
(90’) JUST WIDE! So close to an equaliser for Leicester as Nugent holds the ball up in the area before Wood fires a shot in that flashes narrowly wide. That could be Leicester's final chance for an equaliser.
(90’) All the play is now in the Villa half but Leicester are struggling to create any opportunities. They are running out of time now as they look set to stay rooted to the bottom of the table.
--- 90’ Yellow card G. Agbonlahor receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Agbonlahor goes into the book for a foul on Cambiasso as we enter four minutes of added time. Leicester really going for this...
(88’) Villa waste another opportunity as Grealish feeds Richardson on the left-hand side of the area, but the midfielder can only slice his shot wide under pressure from James.
(86’) Leicester are throwing everyone forward despite their numerical disadvantage, but are struggling to find a way past Guzan. Villa holding firm.
(84’) GOOD BLOCK! Villa almost seal it as Grealish has time to pick his spot from the edge of the area, but Wasilewski throws his body in the way to keep it at 2-1.
(82’) Replays show Konchesky certainly caught Hutton but it was the Villa man's reaction that may have warranted a red card. Pearson will no doubt be complaining about that decision at full-time.
--- 81’ Yellow card A. Hutton goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 80’ Red card! RED CARD! KONCHESKY IS SENT OFF! Leicester are down to ten men, though this seems very harsh. The former Liverpool full-back catches Hutton with a late challenge before coming together with the Scotland international, and the referee decides that qualifies as a red card offence. Hutton is booked for his part in the incident. ---
--- 78’ Substitution M. Albrighton comes on for J. Schlupp. ---
(78’) Leicester make their third and final change as Schlupp is replaced by former Villa man Albrighton. He has 12 minutes to help find an equaliser.
(77’) GREAT SAVES! Schmeichel again to the rescue as he first keeps out Benteke's header after Grealish's cross before Clark is denied by the goalkeeper from the resulting corner.
--- 76’ Substitution L. Bacuna enters the game and replaces C. N'Zogbia. ---
(76’) N'Zogbia is replaced by Bacuna as Lambert looks to shut up shop. Villa still looking for a third though.
(75’) After Sanchez picks up a booking for a foul on Schlupp, James looks to cross the resulting free-kick into the box, but his ball is far too heavy and it drifts out for a goal kick.
--- 74’ Yellow card C. Sánchez is yellow-carded. ---
(73’) Leicester are throwing more men forward now, but Villa have suddenly found their groove on the break. Agbonlahor is coming into his own and you'd think a third home goal would seal it.
--- 71’ Yellow card M. Wasilewski goes into the referee's book. ---
--- 71’ Assist C. Benteke provided the assist. ---
--- 71’ Goal! GOAL!!! HUTTON MAKES IT 2-1! Villa take the lead with a fine counterattacking goal. Agbonlahor breaks down the left before feeding Benteke. The Belgian in turn plays in Hutton on the right-hand side of the area, and with time to pick his spot he finishes with ease. ---
(70’) Leicester are starting to threaten more, with Wood's presence meaning they are able to keep the ball int he final third much more.
(68’) BRILLIANT SAVE! Leicester finally create something as Nugent aims a volley from the corner of the area, and Guzan is at full stretch to tip the ball over as it headed for the top corner. Superb from the USA international.
--- 66’ Substitution C. Wood enters the game and replaces J. Vardy. ---
(66’) Leicester do, in fact, make a change as Wood replaces Vardy. That means its a totally different forward line for the Foxes now.
(64’) It's been all Villa since the break, with Vardy and Nugent having to feed on scraps in forward areas. Pearson may be thinking about an attacking change if his side can stay level heading into the closing stages.
--- 62’ Substitution J. Grealish enters the game and replaces T. Cleverley. ---
(62’) Villa make their second change of the afternoon as Grealish replaces Cleverley. The England international seems to be limping, and heads directly for the dressing room with the physio.
--- 60’ Yellow card J. Schlupp receives a yellow card. ---
(60’) Schlupp becomes the third Leicester player to go into the book as he catches Hutton with a late challenge, though the full-back does not require any treatment.
--- 59’ Yellow card E. Cambiasso is cautioned by the referee. ---
(58’) Cambiasso goes into the book as he cynically pulls back Agbonlahor in the centre circle and the former Inter man has no complaints about the referee's decision.
(56’) GOOD SAVE! Schmeichel is at it again as Agbonlahor gets in behind on the right-hand side before hitting an angled drive that the goalkeeper keeps out with his right foot.
(55’) Villa have certainly upped the tempo in this second half as they obviously feel they can get at Leicester and put them under increasing pressure.
(53’) GREAT SAVE! Schmeichel is keeping Leicester in this. Benteke is put through on goal and looks set to make it 2-1, only for Schmeichel to deflect it behind after rushing off his line. Superb goalkeeping.
(52’) GOOD SAVE! Agbonlahor uses his pace to get down the left-hand side for the first time, and his low cross looks set to be tapped in by Richardson, only for Schmeichel to dive at his feet and force it behind.
(50’) As with the first half, Cissokho is giving Simpson a torrid time, but this time his cross is too close to Schmiechel and the goalkeeper can catch.
(48’) JUST OVER! Villa have started brightly as Benteke drives to the edge of the area before finding Cleverley, but the Manchester United loanee can only fire over the bar. Decent chance for the hosts.
--- 46’ Substitution D. Nugent comes on for L. Ulloa. ---
(46’) Ulloa has not recovered from that Clark challenge late in the first half, and is replaced by Nugent as Villa kick off to get us back underway...
The players are making their way back out onto the pitch as both sides look to find a winner in the second half.
Ulloa's goal apart, Leicester have barely tested Guzan in the Villa goal, though Mahrez has been bright on the right-hand side. I'll be back in ten minutes to see if either side can find a winner.
After five minutes of stoppage time the half-time whistle finally goes, and we are all square at the break. After a frantic start the tempo has slowed down somewhat, though Villa have had the better of things and Benteke is proving a constant threat.
(45’) Ulloa is again down as Agbonlahor catches him in the centre circle. The striker is having a torrid time as the first half draws to a close.
(45’) Ulloa is able to get to his feet but he is still limping. The first half is far from over yet with that further stoppage in play.
(45’) Ulloa is now going to receive some treatment after a strong challenge by Clark. The defender got the ball but also took a piece of the striker on his way through. We will have a minimum of four minutes stoppage time before the break.
--- 44’ Substitution A. Westwood is done for the day. K. Richardson is his replacement. ---
(44’) Richardson is the man to replace Westwood, and it will be interesting to see if he goes into a central role with his usual position out on the left-hand side.
(43’) The stretcher is being called for with Westwood still stricken on the ground. After an encouraging showing, it would be a real shame if he was forced off after that needless foul by Vardy.
--- 41’ Yellow card J. Vardy receives a yellow card. ---
(41’) Vardy is given a yellow card after a cynical challenge from behind on Westwood. The midfielder will require some treatment after that poor challenge from the Leicester man.
(40’) Ulloa is penalised for leaning on Okore, but there is no booking for the Leicester goalscorer. He has been feeding on scraps since he opened the scoring early on.
(38’) Sanchez is seeing plenty of the ball at the heart of the Villa midfield but is unable to create anything of note with his passing game. Villa require a little more industry in midfield.
(36’) Leicester have begun to look far more comfortable on the ball in the last few minutes having held the hosts at arm's length. No chances for the Foxes though.
--- 34’ Yellow card C. N'Zogbia goes into the referee's book. ---
(34’) N'Zogbia becomes the first man to go into the referee's book as he catches James late with a high foot inside the Villa half.
(33’) Cissokho is still looking to cause Simpson problems whenever he can, but he is yet find a man in the middle despite delivering some dangerous crosses.
(31’) JUST WIDE! Schlupp does well to cut inside from the left-hand side before shooting with his right foot, but his effort is always heading wide. Ulloa wanted that in the middle, and the winger maybe should have looked to find him.
(30’) The game has entered a lull period, with Leicester happy enough to allow Villa to have the ball and look to create. The Foxes are defending well though.
(28’) Every Leicester player is having to retreat into their own half as Villa continue to patiently build towards creating a chance in the final third. Schmeichel yet to be tested since Clark's goal though.
(26’) Villa are starting to dominate possession in midfield and are always looking to find Benteke in the box. Moore and Wasilewski have just about kept him quiet so far.
(24’) PENALTY? NO! Vardy is able to get in behind the Villa defence, but Guzan is able to come off his line and get just enough of the ball before bringing down the striker. No real complaints from the former Fleetwood forward.
(22’) Neither team has really found a rhythm as we approach the halfway mark in the first period. Villa have had the better of things, but Leicester have caused problems on the break.
(20’) Mahrez is causing problems down the Leicester right as he again leaves Cissokho for dead before shooting from a tight angle. Guzan is again less than convincing, but is just about able to hold onto the shot at his near post.
(19’) All of a sudden the home fans find their voice after Clark's equaliser, and after some encouraging recent performances the Villa faithful will be confident of their side going onto win this.
--- 17’ Assist The assist came from A. Westwood. ---
--- 17’ Goal! GOAL!!! CLARK EQUALISES! Leicester's lead lasted four minutes, and it is far too easy for Villa to draw level. Westwood dinks a free-kick into the near post, and Clark escapes his marker to send a diving header into the top corner. Game on! ---
(15’) The away fans are in full voice following Ulloa's goal, and Villa Park has been stunned. The hosts had been on top in the early stages but one error from Guzan has seen them fall behind.
--- 13’ Goal! GOAL!!! ULLOA BREAKS THE DEADLOCK! Delight for Leicester but despair for Villa and Guzan. Mahrez breaks inside from the right before shooting. His effort gets a slight deflection, meaning the goalkeeper spills it, and Ulloa cannot miss from three yards out. ---
(12’) JUST WIDE! Best chance of the match so far as a long ball forward from Hutton eventually falls for Benteke driving into the box, but he hits the bouncing ball narrowly wide of the post with Schmeichel beaten.
(10’) Benteke is showing good strength already and creates a chance for himself as he turns around 25 yards from goal and fires well over the crossbar. That's a warning for Leicester from the Belgium striker.
(9’) Leicester have the first shot of the afternoon as James is teed up on the edge of the box but his left-footed drive is well wide of the post.
(7’) Leicester have their first chance to launch an attack as Ulloa robs Westwood in midfield, but Vardy and Mahrez get in each others' way around 25 yards out and Villa can win the ball back.
(5’) Cissokho is looking to get forward whenever he can, and he again tries to get to the byline after Agbonlahor's through ball. The pass is too heavy, however, and Simpson comes across to deal with the danger.
(3’) Early opportunity for Villa to get forward as Cissokho delivers a low ball across the edge of the six-yard box, but Benteke cannot get on the end of it and Leicester can clear.
(1’) The pre-match niceties are over, and Leicester kick off to get us underway...
The players make their way down the tunnel and out onto the pitch. As expected, there are plenty of empty seats, but those that are inside the stadium are doing their best to create an intimidating atmosphere.
There are now just five minutes until kick-off, and the Villa players will be hoping their fans come out in force for this Midlands derby. Villa Park has not been full in a long time, but the hosts need all the support they can get after a disappointing start to the season.
Foxes manager Pearson has come under increasing scrutiny this week after he was captured swearing at a supporter during the match against Liverpool. Though the former Newcastle coach brushed it off and claims he had been abused from the stands first, the pressure from unhappy fans will only intensify if he cannot find a first win in 10 matches.
Due to Leicester's prolonged absence from the Premier League, these two sides have not met in the league since 2004, though they have been drawn together twice in the League Cup since then. The Foxes triumphed on the second of those occasions as they ran out 1-0 winners at Villa Park, and Pearson will be hoping for a similar result this time around.
Leicester, too, make two changes, though only one of theirs is enforced. Captain Wes Morgan was sent off against Liverpool, meaning Liam Moore comes into the heart of the defence while Ritchie De Laet is dropped from the matchday squad entirely, which allows Danny Simpson to make his full Foxes debut at right-back. Manchester United loanee Nick Powell, who has struggled for opportunities and has been linked with an early return to Old Trafford, is handed a place on the bench.
Villa are forced into making two changes to the team that won at Selhurst Park in midweek, with Joe Cole injured and Andreas Weimann suspended. Back in come Carlos Sanchez and Charles N'Zogbia as Benteke again provides the focal point of their attack.
Leicester City subs: Hamer, Drinkwater, King, Powell, Albrighton, Nugent, Wood.
Leicester City (4-4-2): Schmeichel; Simpson, Moore, Wasilewski, Konchesky; Mahrez, Cambiasso, James, Schlupp; Ulloa, Vardy.
Aston Villa subs: Given, Lowton, Herd, Richardson, Bacuna, Grealish, Robinson.
Aston Villa (4-3-3): Guzan; Hutton, Okore, Clark, Cissokho; Sanchez, Westwood, Cleverley; N'Zogbia, Benteke, Agbonlahor.
Before we go any further, the two team line-ups have been announced ahead of kick-off in around 20 minutes...
Leicester, meanwhile, are in the midst of a horror run of results themselves having failed to win since their 5-3 triumph over Manchester United on September 21. Defeat to Liverpool in midweek left them rooted to the bottom of the table, and with Nigel Pearson coming under increasing pressure from supporters, he and the Foxes are desperate for a win over their Midlands rivals this afternoon.
Paul Lambert's Villa side have been in freefall after a bright start to the season saw them sitting in the Champions League places, though their win over Crystal Palace on Tuesday has lifted some of the gloom around Villa Park. With Christian Benteke back and leading the line, there is a belief they can start to climb the table again and push for a top-half finish.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League encounter between Aston Villa and Leicester City. (66’) Valencia comes across and ends up making a late challenge on Pelle. Southampton have a free kick in a great position out on the left, but the delivery to the back post from Davis isn't the greatest. It falls to a United head first and the hosts settle for a throw on the opposite flank.
(64’) United have won nine and lost just one of their last 12 league encounters with Southampton. It is the Saints, though, that look more likely to take all three points in this evening.
(62’) Pelle again receives the ball in a central area and he is given time to feed Mane on the left. The winger then looks to roll a pass to the back post for Long to tap home, but Young intercepts with a clearance.
(61’) Rooney has a woeful attempt at taking a corner. The ball bobbles up from a loose bit of turf, leading to the England captain launching it deep beyond all the bodies in the box.
(59’) ALMOST TWO! The Saints are pressing very high up the pitch, with Rojo losing possession this time. Tadic threads a pass through for Pelle as the hosts look to take advantage, but the Italian blazes his shot over the top!
(58’) Southampton have a chance to catch the visitors on the break but Pelle hesitates in possession, and when he eventually offloads to Tadic the Serbian has no options. He turns back on himself in order to find Bertrand on the left, but the defender fails to make anything of it.
(51’) Southampton are building upon their positive start to the half, with Wanyama getting away from Herrera to find Mane. The Senegalese comes back inside and is caught by the Spanish midfielder, earning his side a free kick. It is fired long to Pelle but the Italian fails to get on the end of it.
(49’) Pelle does well to rise above Fellaini and flick a free kick from deep on to Tadic. The Serbian then moves it on to Mane, but the winger sends a wayward pass to the feet of United's Belgian midfielder, and the move breaks down.
(47’) United fail to clear a corner, with Tadic beating Mata to the ball in order to feed Yoshida. The centre-back shows great agility to shift it into space, but he is closed by Evans before he can get a shot away. The ball seems to take a touch off the visitors' centre-back on its way out, but a goal kick is given.
(46’) We are back underway!
Welcome back! The teams will be returning to the pitch for the second half in just a few moments.
HALF TIME - Southampton 1-1 Manchester United: A nightmare moment for Fonte saw him gift Van Persie the game's opening goal, but the Saints responded positively and got themselves back on level terms through Pelle. The visitors have lost Smalling to injury, but Van Gaal will be expecting more of his side in the second half. Stay tuned for the second half!
(45’) VAN PERSIE! The Dutchman looses a ferocious shot from 20 yards that swings just wide of the post, crashing into the side netting. It is the last effort of the half, though, as the half-time whistle is sounded.
(45’) Pelle receives the ball from Mane and plays a give-and-go with Tadic at the top of the box. He then lets fly from 20 yards, completely scuffing his effort so it looks more like a pass for Long, though the Irishman was beaten to it by De Gea.
(45’) A good series of passes from the hosts earns them a corner on the right. Davis bends it into the box but Fellaini is first to it and he heads to safety. It has been indicated that there will be two minutes of added time at the end of this half.
(44’) Clyne flights a decent cross in from the right and Mane attacks it on the far side of the area. Valencia does just enough to distract the Senegalese, though, and De Gea has the simple job of picking a bouncing effort up from the deck.
(42’) Evans opens up his stride and surges into space down the centre of the park. He passes into the feet of Van Persie, who spins and spreads play out to Young on the left. The wing back cuts onto his right foot and attempts to find the Dutchman at the back post, but his cross is too high for him.
(41’) Davis holds the ball on the top of the box before flicking the ball out wide for the overlapping Long. His pass is just behind the forward, though, and Clyne's attempts to regain possession end with the visitors being awarded a goal kick.
--- 39’ Substitution P. McNair is done for the day. Ander Herrera is his replacement. ---
(39’) Van Gaal is going to shake things up with his second change of the game, as Herrera comes on for McNair. United may stick with the back three for the time being, though, as Carrick has dropped into the defence.
(37’) Fellaini looks to spread the play and feed Valencia on the right, but his pass runs out for a throw in on the near side for the hosts. That pass was nowhere near the wing back.
(35’) LONG! Tadic's cross is controlled by Mane, who then drops to ground under pressure from Carrick. McNair fails to clear it, though, and the ball drops for the Ireland international who hammers his shot over the top of the goal. That was a great opportunity for the Saints to go ahead!
(34’) Mata flights the ball towards the far post, with Fellaini looking to attack it. Forster comes off his line and collects it before the Belgian can connect, though.
(33’) That is a clumsy challenge from Wanyama! The midfielder tries desperately to get back in front of Van Persie with the Dutchman closing in on goal. He catches him from behind and United have a free kick in a central position 35 yards out.
--- 31’ Goal! G. Pellè has found the target for Southampton! ---
(31’) GOOOOOOAAAAL!! PELLE EQUALISES! The Italian striker scores his first Premier League goal since October 18! Long's cross is fired towards goal by Tadic, but a deflection off Carrick sees it drop perfectly for Pelle to lash a shot into the roof of the net! It's all square at St Mary's.
(30’) A good battle is developing in midfield between Fellaini and Wanyama. The pair are contesting every loose ball in a physical manner, but the Kenyan just seems to want it a little more than his counterpart at the moment.
(29’) A decent spell of possession for the hosts comes to a fruitless end as no one pulls the trigger from in shooting range. Koeman's men are guilty of trying to be a bit over-elaborate with the ball, and just need to focus on testing De Gea.
(27’) Yoshida plays a great ball down the left-hand channel for Tadic to latch onto. The Serbian cuts it back into the box for Pelle, whose rifled shot towards the near post takes a slight deflection. De Gea gets down to his right and gets his body behind it, ensuring the ball stays out of the corner.
(25’) McNair is caught in possession under pressure from Tadic and Mane, and the loose ball falls to the latter. He bears down on goal, cutting left and right to work his way onto the box. The Senegalese stumbles as he goes to pull the trigger, though, and United swarm upon the ball to remove the threat.
(23’) Southampton’s last win over the Red Devils came back in August 2003, with a 1-0 victory at St Mary’s. It's going to take at least two goals from them if they are to repeat that feat tonight.
(21’) The Saints are looking fairly rushed in possession when they move into the opposition half. A wayward pass from Pelle sees them lose the ball this time, and Rojo attempts to catch the hosts short at the back with a long pass up to Mata. He sends it too far beyond the Spaniard, though.
(19’) Mane uses his pace to get the better of McNair and dart to the byline, but he completely slices his cross and it swerves into the stand behind the goal.
--- 18’ Substitution J. Evans comes on for C. Smalling. ---
(18’) Van Gaal gets his team to kick the ball off so that Evans can finally be introduced. The Red Devils are back to their full complement, then.
(17’) The England centre-back has gone off the pitch, and play restarts with Evans waiting to make his entrance. United try to get Van Persie on the ball inside the box but the pass into him is slightly overhit and he fails to control it.
(15’) Smalling has dropped to ground in the centre of the United half with no one around him. That doesn't look good for the visitors. Evans is already preparing on the touchline and he may have to make an early appearance.
(14’) Mane rolls the ball down the left for Tadic and continues his run into the box. The Serbian plays a pass back into his feet but Carrick intercepts, having tracked his run from the centre of the park. The resultant corner is met by Pelle at the near post and his header arrows wide of the target.
--- 12’ Goal! Goal to Manchester United, scored by R. van Persie! ---
(12’) GOOOOOOOAAAALL!! UNITED LEAD! A calamity at the back for Southampton! Rooney looks to break down the left but his touch beyond Clyne is mopped up by Fonte. However, the Portuguese's attempt to roll the ball back to Forster is intercepted by Van Persie, and the striker takes full advantage by sliding a shot into the far corner!
(11’) The Red Devils are now beginning to have more of a say in possession, but they are yet to really push forward and threaten the hosts' defence.
(10’) Smalling follows Pelle as the striker comes short to receive the ball. The Italy international manages to hold off his marker and move possession out to Long on the right. A cross is then bent into the middle but there are no Saints players attacking it, leaving De Gea with a simple collection to make.
(9’) Rooney picks up the ball on the left and comes inside, seemingly trying to open up space for a shot. He takes too long in possession, though, and Davis speeds in to make a sly challenge and come away with the ball. He moves it on to Long and the Irishman soon surrenders it on the right.
(7’) McNair is doing a good job of sticking close to Mane, as the winger looks to make the most of the room in behind Valencia. Twice the young centre-back gets across quickly to block his attempts at playing a pass down the wing.
(6’) Southampton are controlling possession in the opening stages, launching long passes in behind the wing backs and looking to exploit the space. Mane fails to win one such pass but Wanyama is first to the follow-up, and he draws a foul from Fellaini as he shields possession from him.
(4’) Bertrand whips a deep cross to the back post from the left wing, and Long leaps above Young to connect with a header. He tries to loop it across goal and inside the far post, only to see his effort drop on the roof of the net for a goal kick.
(3’) Wanyama looks up for this. The Saints midfielder is coming out on top every time he challenges for the ball, showing great strength to win it and vision to distribute it accurately.
(2’) The home fans are in good voice tonight, and they've witnessed a positive start from their side. A long ball forward is knocked down in the box by Long and Pelle looks to bring it under control, but the ball doesn't fall for him and the United defence clear. They've shown good variety to their play already.
(1’) We are underway on the south coast!
The teams are out on the pitch at St Mary's. The Saints are in their traditional red and white stripes, while United don their alternate blue kits.
The Red Devils have not been particularly impressive on the road this season, with just one win from six attempts. Burnley have kick-started their season with a three-game unbeaten run and will be high on confidence to continue that tonight. Victories over Hull and Stoke could not be added to in their draw against Aston Villa over the weekend, but they did show spirit to claw themselves back into the game and almost steal the three points. A win could also see them move out of the relegation zone.
Newcastle's defeat to West Ham on Saturday ended a run of five straight league victories. A return to winning ways will be welcome tonight, particularly given their tough fixture list in December. They face Chelsea, Arsenal, Manchester United, Everton and local-rivals Sunderland in their next five games to mark a tricky festive period for the Pardew’s side.
Alan Pardew has been hit with suspensions to midfield duo Moussa Sissoko and Jack Colback, so brings in Papiss Cisse and Mehdi Abeid in their place. They are the only alterations from defeat to West Ham. Daryl Janmaat starts despite picking up a hamstring injury in that game. Massadio Haidara and Michael Williamson have pulled through from their respective injuries.

Liverpool now have a good opportunity to make it three wins out of three against Sunderland when the two sides meet at Anfield on Saturday, whilst Leicester, who stay bottom of the table for another week, face fellow strugglers Aston Villa in a must-win clash at Villa Park the following day.
After a nervy first half in which Leicester took the lead after 22 minutes through an unfortunate Mignolet own goal, Liverpool showed great grit and determination to fight their way back into the game, and they leave the King Power Stadium with a well-deserved, and well-earned, victory. It's their second in as many games, whilst the hosts are now without a win in their last nine league clashes, with seven of those ending in defeat.

FULL TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-1 ASTON VILLA. A thrilling game at Selhurst Park, as the hosts put forward a magnificent display, yet fall at the hands of Paul Lambert's side, as a result of Christian Benteke's solo effort. The Villans put everything they had into defending the advantage, and it paid off brilliantly for them, as the three points vault them into a much more comfortable position above the drop, while ending a nine match winless run in the Premier League.
(90’) IT'S ALL OVER! ASTON VILLA HOLD ON! Michael Oliver sounds his full time whistle, giving the visitors their first win away to Crystal Palace since September of 1980!
(90’) Villa players cramping up everywhere! They have put so much into defending this lead. Palace win a free kick and Guzan comes out to claim the cross. Into the final minute now!
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card A. Weimann goes into the referee's book. ---
(90’) Into the second of four minutes of added time, and Andi Weimann is down injured after a coming together with Jason Puncheon. The striker will be shown a yellow card for the incident, but not before he wastes precious second nursing what appears to be a hand injury.
(90’) IT SQUEEZES THROUGH! Magnificent stuff from Zaha, who dribbles his way through the defence to the byline. He sends a terrific ball across the face of goal, but Campbell and Bolasie both completely miss the ball! All it needed was a touch!

(88’) Still no way through for Palace! Villa are defending valiantly, throwing themselves in front of everything. Another cross is cleared out for a throw, which will allow both sides to make changes as we approach the 90th minute.
(86’) STAT ATTACK: Aston Villa have managed to tally a meager five points from a possible 48 against London clubs since their opening day victory at the Emirates to kick off the 2013-14 campaign.
(84’) Villa holding on for dear life! They have everyone back to defend, and are doing a great job keeping Palace out. There are moments of panic at the back, but the visitors are first to every ball in the area, as they desperately cling to this one goal advantage.
--- 82’ Yellow card C. Clark gets yellow. ---
(82’) Clark receives a yellow card of his own, as the intensity of the match picks up with time running out. Ward delivers the ensuing free kick into the penalty area from 35 yards out, but again no one attacks it, as it bounces harmlessly behind for a goal kick.
--- 81’ Yellow card Y. Bolasie is yellow-carded. ---
(81’) Bolasie is shown a yellow card, the second of the day for Crystal Palace, as he lunges in and ends up stomping on the leg of Hutton. The free kick again allows Villa to waste precious time off the clock, while relieving pressure on their goal.
(79’) Free kick now awarded to Palace, who have everyone forward in search of the elusive first goal. Ward delivers, and Hutton puts it behind for another corner. Michael Oliver blows his whistle, however, as Dann is penalized for a push in the back of the defender, awarding Villa a free kick.
(77’) Both teams growing increasingly desperate, as we approach the final 10 minutes. Villa are frantically trying to hold on and keep Palace out, while the hosts are throwing everything at them in search of a game-tying goal. You could cut the tension with a knife inside the ground!
(75’) Lovely pass from McArthur! The midfielder picks out Bolasie in attack, who then cuts into the centre and tries to curl a shot in at the far post. Okore gets a piece of it, forcing Palace to settle for yet another corner.
(73’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace scored three goals against Liverpool in their last home match. Since returning to the Premier League last season, they have scored three goals at Selhurst Park on three occasions before this, each time losing their next home match (0-2 vs Swansea, 0-2 vs Manchester United and 1-3 vs West Ham).
(71’) It is all boiling over now as Palace voice their frustration with referee Michael Oliver. Kelly's cross into the area is chased down by McArthur, with Guzan rushing off his line to collect. The two collide with each other, and a free kick is awarded to Villa. There was nothing in it from either player, as McArthur comes out worse for wear. The Palace players feel every decision is going against them, and have had about enough. Neil Warnock is livid, screaming at the fourth official from the edge of his technical area.
(69’) END TO END STUFF! Back come Villa on a counter of their own, and Weimann picks up the ball at the top of the area. His first shot is blocked by Hangelaand, but gets on the rebound from 15 yards out. It is a glorious opportunity, but Speroni is up to the task, making a fine save to deny the forward.
(67’) MAGNIFICENT DEFENDING! Villa win a corner, but Palace deal with it. They break on the counter, completely outnumbering the Villa defence. Campbell pushes forward in possession, but Hutton takes a chance, lunging forward with a superb tackle to dispossess the striker and sniff out the opportunity!
(65’) Agbonlahor drifts deep into his own end to get the ball, before starting Villa forward in attack. The visitors need much more of that, as it does wonders to help them escape being trapped at the back like they have so often in this match.
(63’) Villa again seem to have come out unscathed, as the tempo slows and pressure on their goal is relieved. They are experiencing their first spell in possession of this second half, which if not for anything, allows them to regain their shape at the back.
(61’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY NOT GIVEN! Bolasie at the heart of things again for the hosts, running into space on the left, before sending a sensational ball into the area for Campbell. The striker goes down, appearing to be toppled over from behind, but Michael Oliver is having none of it!
(59’) STAT ATTACK: Andreas Weimann’s goal in the first game of the season at Stoke is the lone second-half strike Aston Villa have registered this season. They have gone 12 matches since without scoring after the break, with all six of their goals coming in the opening 45 minutes. They have been held scoreless in the 51st minute and on through the entire season.
--- 57’ Yellow card F. Campbell receives a yellow card. ---
(57’) OUCH! Terrific clearance from Brad Guzan, who rushes well out of his area to clear a through ball which looked to have Campbell through on goal. The keeper gets to the ball first to clear, and in then taken out by the striker after a very hard coming together, which earns him the first yellow card of the match.
(55’) PRESSURE MOUNTING! Again Palace throw everything at the visitors, and have them scrambling to defend the lead. Bolasie looks incredibly dangerous along the left, sending another sensational ball in for Zaha, but the winger sends his header over the bar!
(53’) MORE SOLID DEFENDING! McArthur sends a ball through for Bolasie, who is in the midst of another one of his elegant runs forward. Okore spots the threat, however, and gets across, showing great pace and strength to fend off the forward without conceding a free kick. Important work from the Danish centre-back.
(51’) GREAT DEFENSIVE HEADER! Frazier Campbell makes a sublime run into the area, putting real pressure on the Villa defence. He turns and picks out Bolasie, who sends a teasing ball into the box, but Clark dives in to head clear just before Chamakh can get to it.
(49’) Jedinak takes the free kick, trying to loft a ball towards the far post, but his delivery is very poor, forcing Dann to concede a free kick and again the chance comes to nothing for Palace.
(48’) Wonderful run! Bolasie looks increasingly dangerous on the left. He is causing Hutton all sorts of problems, this time cutting it back into a dangerous area, but Westwood is back to clear the threat. The pressure remains on, and Okore gives away a free kick from 25 yards out.
--- 46’ Substitution F. Campbell enters play, replacing D. Gayle. ---
(46’) Crystal Palace kick off and the second half is underway at Selhurst Park. One change to tell you about at the break, as Frazier Campbell replaces Dwight Gayle. There are a massive three points up for grabs, who will claim them?
Frazier Campbell and Jason Puncheon are available from the bench for Crystal Palace, as they search for an all elusive equalizer. They have managed a ton of pressure, but need to be far more clinical with their chances, much like Christian Benteke, whose lone goal separates the two sides at the break.
HALF TIME: CRYSTAL PALACE 0-1 ASTON VILLA. Despite dominating the opening 45 minutes and creating a slew of chances, the hosts find themselves behind at the break thanks to Christian Benteke's wonderful solo effort. Brad Guzan recovered nicely from an early scare, making some fine saves to keep Palace out through the first half. There is still everything to play for in the final 45 minutes.
(45’) Referee Michael Oliver sounds his whistle, bringing an end to an electrifying first half at Selhurst Park!
(45’) There will be two minutes of added time at the end of the first half...
(44’) The pace has slowed a bit as we approach the break. Palace seem to have grown frustrated with their inability to capitalize on their chances, while Villa look eager to get to the break with their lead intact. The game is mostly being played in midfield at the moment, and possession being squandered on more than a few occasions.
(42’) STAT ATTACK: Aston Villa have been held without a goal in six of their last nine matches, conceding 17 goals while scoring just three times during that span. Their seven goals this season are the fewest in the Premier League, behind Burnley who have nine.
(40’) Incredible pressure from Crystal Palace, but somehow Villa again manage to have weathered the storm. They break out of their own half, if only for a moment, but seem to have escaped with the lead in-tact. The hosts have thrown everything at Villa, yet the first goal still eludes them.
(38’) APPEALS FOR A HANDBALL! Following a Palace corner, the ball comes out to McArthur at the top of the area. He drives a seeing eye shot towards goal, which appears to be blocked by a handball. They shout for a penalty, but have their claims immediately turned aside by Michael Oliver.
(36’) ANOTHER MAGNIFICENT SAVE! Lovely cross in from Zaha, which falls for Bolasie. The winger takes a touch before firing towards goal from in close. He strikes it with real power, but Guzan gets his body in front to make the save!
(34’) BACK COME PALACE! The hosts waste no time searching for an equalizer, throwing everything at the Villa goal. They commit men into the area, but Zaha sees his shot saved, before Bolasie's strike is blocked. Chaos in the area, but again Palace come away empty handed!
--- 32’ Goal! The Belgian striker shows great strength to dispossess Scott Dann near the halfway line. He charges forward with only Hangelaand to beat. (31’) ASTON VILLA OPEN THE SCORING THROUGH CHRISTIAN BENTEKE!
(29’) BRILLIANT SAVE! The first chance of the match for Villa, and it comes from nothing really. Sanchez sends an innocent looking pass forward to pick out Benteke, who has his back turned to goal. (27’) Disappointing from Zaha! After a Villa free kick, Palace win the ball and break on a threatening counter. The winger streaks up the right, with a few options in the centre. He tries to send in an early ball, but there is far too much behind it, as it runs past everyone and out for a throw.
(25’) Wilfried Zaha has posed a real threat for Palace through the opening 25 minutes, always looking to take on a defender, which has put some real pressure on Westwood and Cissokho. (23’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace are looking to win back-to-back home games for the first time since March-April of last season, where coincidentally, their second victory came against Aston Villa.
(21’) CLEVER! Palace win another corner, which Ward stands over to take. He tries to pick out Hangelaand with his cross, but the defender cannot get on the end of it. (19’) There is a spectacular pace to this match through the opening 20 minutes, with plenty of space being offered up by both sides. The teams look eager to push forward and get the all important first goal, which has done wonders to boost the entertainment value at Selhurst Park.
(17’) The visitors win a free kick along the right from 40 yards out after a handball by Chamakh. The ball is delivered into the area and cleared by Palace, but only as far as Sanchez. The substitute lets fly from 25 yards out, but horribly scuffs his shot, sending it high and wide of the near post.
(15’) Villa have yet to muster up a solid attack, but they seem to have tempered the early storm put forth by Crystal Palace. They are enjoying much more of the ball, with a change in shape appearing to be the reasoning behind it. Agbonlahor looks to have moved behind Benteke, with Cleverley shifting out wide to offer a bit more width in the middle of the pitch.
(13’) Important defensive work from Agbonlahor helps temporarily relieve the pressure on the Villa goal. The visitors push forward looking to counter, but a very poor pass from Benteke to Hutton on the right sees the ball run behind for a goal kick. Paul Lambert's side look in no way up for the match in the early going.
(11’) STAT ATTACK: Aston Villa are winless in their last nine Premier League matches, picking up just three points over that span, which comes after they managed three victories from four games to start the season. It is their longest winless run in the top flight under Paul Lambert.

Ciaran Clark is available after his scare against Burnley on the weekend, starting alongside Jores Okore at centre-back. There are no other changes to the team instilled by Paul Lambert, who will be hoping the return of his star forward will be enough to provide the Villans with the threat in front of goal they have been so desperately lacking.

(90’) West Ham are clinging on. West Brom are piling on the pressure and have even sent Foster forward in these desperate times.

(7’) Vertonghen and Cahill clashed heads going for the ball at the end of that previous Tottenham attack, leaving both on the floor and in serious discomfort.
(6’) Lamela's cross from the resulting set-piece is poor, and it misses all of the available white shirts in the middle of the box. Everton win a corner in the final seconds, but the delivery is poor and Hull can hang on for a deserved point. The hosts were off the pace for much of the night, and though their defence were rarely tested, Aluko's fine individual effort proved enough for the Tigers to move out of the relegation zone.
(90’) The latest Everton attack comes to nothing as Pienaar's pass into Baines comes to nothing and Hull are looking like they will claim a point. Not long left now.
(90’) Everton can barely get out of their own half as Hull pressure them in possession and make a number of key challenges. The home fans are urging their team on with time running out.
(90’) We are into six minutes of stoppage time, but that will be extended even further as Aluko stays down after a clash of heads with Distin. Both sides believe they can still win this.
(90’) Wasted opportunity for Hull as Brady skips past two challenges before getting to the edge of the area. He has time to play Jelavic in, but his pass is poor and Howard can collect.
--- 89’ Substitution A. Robertson comes on for S. Quinn. ---
(88’) Plenty of huffing and puffing from the home side but they cannot blow this Hull house down. The visitors, meanwhile, make their final change as Quinn is replaced by Robertson.
--- 87’ Substitution D. Meyler is done for the day. R. Brady is his replacement. ---
(86’) We've got another break in play here as Meyler stays down with an apparent knee injury before he is eventually replaced by Brady. We're set to have plenty of stoppage time at the end of this match.
(84’) Barkley looks to whip in a free-kick from the right, but after his cross is headed clear, McGeady's volley hits Pienaar and the Tigers can breathe again.
(82’) Everton throwing everyone forward now as Dawson makes a fine block to deny Lukaku before the Tigers eventually clear. Martinez does not want to drop any points tonight.
--- 80’ Substitution A. McGeady enters play, replacing M. Bešić. ---
(80’) Everton make their second change of the night as Besic is replaced by McGeady for the closing stages.
--- 78’ Yellow card L. Baines is cautioned by the referee. ---
(78’) Baines goes into the referee's book for a late challenge on Elmohamady, with the former Sunderland man staying down to receive treatment. He has been excellent tonight at both ends of the pitch.
(76’) Still no clearcut chances in the second half for Everton as we enter the final 15 minutes. If they cannot find a winner, they can have few complaints on the back of this showing.
(74’) Hull's period of dominance that brought about Aluko's goal seems to have come to an end, and Everton have lifted their own tempo again. It's the home team who are doing all the attacking now.
(72’) Pienaar's introduction has not had the desired effect for the hosts, with his lack of physical presence meaning he is struggling to create anything of note in the final third.
(70’) Barkley looks to skip past a couple of challenges on the edge of the box, but Huddlestone steps out to intercept and take control of the situation. No way through for the Toffees.
(68’) Hull aren't happy after the referee allows play to go on despite Livermore being down with a head injury. Eventually the visitors win the ball back and clear out of play so the midfielder can receive treatment.
(66’) Approaching the midway point in the second half and Everton seem to have run out of ideas. Their full-backs have struggled to get into the game since the break and Lukaku has seen little of the ball.
--- 64’ Substitution S. Pienaar enters play, replacing K. Mirallas. ---
(64’) Despite being excellent tonight, Mirallas is withdrawn early by Martinez, with Pienaar on in his place on the left-hand side.
(63’) Rosenior wins a corner on the left-hand side that is half-cleared by the hosts before Elmoahamady sends a shot into the stands behind the goal.
(61’) JUST WIDE! Aluko has brought Hull to life and he again does brilliantly against Distin to dig a cross out from the left-hand side. Jelavic is waiting in the middle, but his header drops just the wrong side of the post. Hull on top.
--- 59’ Assist Assist by N. Jelavić. ---
--- 59’ Goal! GOAL!!! ALUKO EQUALISES! Absolutely superb from Aluko as he picks up the ball from Jelavic before skipping past Distin and firing the ball past Howard from a tight angle. The goalkeeper will be disappointed to be beaten at his near post, but Hull won't care - they're level. ---
(58’) The ball is worked out to Rosenior in space on the left-hand side, but the full-back's inswinging cross is far too deep and Howard can catch under his own crossbar.
(56’) Besic has impressed tonight and he again tries his luck from distance as he curls an effort goalwards from 25 yards. McGregor is behind it all the way, however, and catches it well.
(55’) Baines has been patched up and is able to come back on. It looks as if he suffered a nosebleed following that challenge by Meyler, with tissue visible in his nostril.
--- 53’ Substitution S. Aluko comes on for M. Diamé. ---
(53’) Hull make the first change of the night as Diame, who seems to be limping, is replaced by Aluko. The former West Ham man seems to have a problem and goes straight to the medical staff on the bench.
(51’) Some concern here for Everton as Baines stays down after being caught by the arm of Meyler. Eventually he gets to his feet and heads down the tunnel, though it seems as if he will be back given his injury may only need stitches.
(49’) JUST OVER! Almost a brilliant goal from the hosts as Lukaku holds the ball up before feeding Mirallas in the middle. The winger looks to chip McGregor with the outside of his boot from 20 yards, but the ball drops just over the crossbar.
(48’) Everton living dangerously here as this time Barry looks to see the ball out of play, only for Meyler to nip in and square the ball across the box. Coleman is alive to the danger, however, and takes the ball off Diame's toes in the middle.
(47’) Early chance for the visitors as Distin and Baines get in each others' way on the left-hand side, but Diame's curled effort is well blocked by Jagielka on the edge of the box.
(46’) No changes for either side at the break and Hull kick-off to get us back underway...
The two teams are making their way back out for the second period, and Hull need their first second-half goal against Everton in Premier League history to get back into this one.
The Tigers worked exceptionally hard to inhibit their hosts in the opening stages, but they struggled to keep with the Toffees as the half wore on. As it stands they will remain in the relegation zone tonight. I'll be back in 10 minutes to see if they can turn things around.
Just a single minute of stoppage time passes without incident, and Everton go into the break with a deserved lead. Mirallas' direct running has been the difference as he created the opening goal for Lukaku, and Hull need some attacking inspiration from somewhere to get back into this one.
(45’) Barry plays a superb ball over the top of the Hull defence for Barkley to run onto, and McGregor has to be quick to get off his line and collect the pass on the edge of his own box.
(43’) Baines whips in a corner from the left-hand side that Jagielka meets above Jelavic, but his header is always heading wide of the post and McGregor is untroubled.
(41’) Huddleston, who broke up so many Everton attacks during the opening 30 minutes, is starting to be bypassed, meaning the hosts are looking much more threatening. Bruce needs some inspiration from somewhere.
(39’) JUST WIDE! Baines plays the set-piece into Osman, and after his shot is blocked, Besic curls a right-footed effort narrowly wide from 20 yards. Hull on the ropes after falling behind.
(38’) Meyler is all over Baines down the Everton left and is penalised for a push on the full-back. The hosts can look to get the ball into the box from here...
(36’) The hosts deserve their lead despite having few chances on goal, though Hull will feel slightly aggrieved after defending stoutly during this first half. They will need to be more expansive now if they are get anything from this one.

(23’) Diame is almost able to get a run on goal as Barry misplaces a pass in midfield, but Besic is alive to the danger and is able to step in and make the challenge.

(3’) Diame has started the match in a very advanced position almost alongside Jelavic for Hull while the hosts have started with Barkley on the left-hand side of the trio behind Lukaku.

(90’) The Sunderland fans still in attendance have three minutes of stoppage time to endure.
(89’) Navas has enjoyed a fine evening. He is unable to crown his performance with a goal, however, as he sends an optimistic effort well over the crossbar.

An astonishing number of Sunderland supporters have chosen not to witness the closing stages of this game, with an away victory a certainty. (79’) City appear hungry for a fifth goal as they swarm forward once again. Sunderland, meanwhile, appear to be waiting for the final whistle now. Perhaps their exertions against Chelsea have caught up with them.
(76’) The remainder of this match could well be played out at testimonial pace. With games aplenty in December, City might just be hitting form at the right time. After falling behind tonight, they have been terrific.

(74’) A host of Sunderland fans head for the exits. They have seen enough! Aguero, undoubtedly the man of the match, is given a rest as Frank Lampard comes on for the final 16 minutes.

(71’) Altidore comes close to collecting a ball over the top from Larsson, only for Joe Hart to get there first. A City break is then halted as Cattermole hacks down Navas with a cynical challenge, earning a yellow card in the process.
(69’) City look to have taken their foot off the gas here, somewhat surprisingly. A Sunderland goal would set up a very interesting finale, but for the time being Manuel Pellegrini has little reason for concern.

Milner and Santiago Vergini are involved in a tussle after the former fails to keep the ball in play on the City left. Referee Craig Pawson has a quiet word with both players before allowing the game to resume.
(61’) After a brief rally from the hosts, City are knocking the ball around with ease yet again. Sunderland's supporters make their frustration clear, but their side is simply being outclassed at the moment.
(59’) Sunderland have at least got on to the front foot since falling 3-1 behind, but they now face a mammoth task to get something out of this match.

(46’) We are back under way at the Stadium of Light. Part two of The Sergio Aguero Show to come, perhaps?

Sunderland fans seeking positives may wish to focus on the fact Pantilimon has not exactly been over-worked in goal. City have simply proved clinical when chances have come their way.

However, there was a late scare for City prior to the interval and they will know their work is not yet done.

(45’) Connor Wickham's goal seems an awful long time ago. We will have an additional two minutes at the end of this first period and Sunderland look as though they need half-time, having chased the ball for much of the opening 45 minutes.

(41’) Sunderland are in a real pickle now. City are a constant threat, epitomised by another attack that ends with Clichy heading wide. It's hard to see how Gus Poyet turns things around.
--- 39’ Assist The assist came from S. Agüero. ---
--- 39’ Goal! GOOOOAAAALLLL!!! CITY HAVE A SECOND!! Aguero turns provider on this occasion, with a glorious first-time flick finding Jovetic following Yaya Toure's ball into the area. The Montenegrin drills a shot through the legs of Pantilimon and you have to say City deserve to be in front. ---
(36’) City are not only looking good in possession; their players are working hard to force mistakes when the hosts have the ball. Navas forces Anthony Reveillere back towards his own goal before a foul on Fletcher allows Sunderland to take a breather.
(34’) Sunderland just cannot keep hold of the ball at the moment. However, City fans hoping for good news from Stamford Bridge will be disappointed to hear Chelsea lead Tottenham 2-0.
(32’) Poor old Steven Fletcher really isn't seeing too much action as his team-mates continue to come under pressure. That said, City are not exactly carving out chances at will. For the time being, they are content to stay patient and make Sunderland's defenders work.
(30’) After working so hard against Chelsea, you have to feel Sunderland could tire in the latter stages of this match if City continue to dominate possession. For the time being, Poyet's men are holding firm.
(28’) What a season Aguero is having. That's 13 Premier League goals this term for the former Atletico Madrid striker, who appears to be in the form of his life. (26’) Sunderland have hardly touched the ball since giving up the lead. City are controlling the tempo of the match and Nasri tries his luck from distance, but fails to keep his shot down.
(24’) Navas continues to offer a threat, firing wide from the right side of the box as City seek to build on Aguero's leveller.
(23’) It is safe to say this match has burst into life. Having lost 1-0 here on four successive occasions, City could have been forgiven for thinking 'here we go again' when Wickham opened the scoring. The talismanic Aguero had other ideas, though, and the visiting fans are now in fine voice.

Full time at the The Hawthorns. Arsenal make their way into the top four with a vital narrow 1-0 away victory against West Brom. A slow first half sprung into life after the break as both sides opened up and attempted to break the deadlock. The only goal of the match came on the hour when some great play down the wing from Cazorla enabled the Spaniard to set up Danny Welbeck for a bullet header past Foster. The Baggies rallied towards the end but the Gunners remained solid to claim all three points. I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card A. Oxlade-Chamberlain gets yellow. ---
(90’) Samaras drives down the left flank and reaches the byline before somehow digging out a cross into the box. Martinez takes the pressure completely off the Arsenal defence though as he comes off his line to commandingly claim out of the air.
(89’) GARDNER!! HOW CLOSE WAS THAT! The West Brom man latches on to a pass on the edge of the box and rifles a strike at goal which takes a deflection on its way through and flashes by the left-hand post! Corner kick to the home side!
(87’) Awful from Brunt. Arsenal are on the back foot slightly and the Irishman has the opportunity to pile on the pressure by lofting a free kick into the box, but instead sends the set piece straight to the feet of Welbeck, who takes the ball for a run down the left, thus taking the onus of his defence.
(85’) West Brom have Arsenal camped in their own half at the moment. Lescott and Dawson are as far up as the halfway line as they look to pin the visitors back, but they are leaving gaping spaces in behind in their own half if the Gunners can take advantage.
--- 84’ Yellow card C. Gamboa is cautioned by the referee. ---
(83’) Arsenal's tactics will be very interesting to see in these last few minutes. Wenger's men have been criticised recently for their inability to remain defensively solid in the last couple of minutes of games and that they still commit too many men forward. Well, they have the lead now, so let's see how they set out.
(81’) WEST BROM HIT THE BAR!! Arsenal fail to clear the ball out of the box and Berahino rises high in the air to guide a brilliant header towards goal, but his attempt crashes off the top of the woodwork! So unlucky! The Gunners living dangerously here!
(79’) VITAL block by Mertesacker! Samaras collects the ball on the left and then checks back before lofting a cross into the box. The cross is recycled back into the danger area and volley smashes a half volley towards goal, but the German defender stands tall to make the interception! That strike looked destined to find the net!
--- 78’ Substitution O. Giroud is done for the day. A. Oxlade-Chamberlain is his replacement. ---
(77’) Arsene Wenger follows suit and makes his second swap of the match. Giroud, who has did okay today in his first start since coming back from a leg break, is replaced by Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain, who was one of Arsenal's impressive performers against Dortmund midweek.
--- 76’ Substitution S. Sessègnon is done for the day. G. Samaras is his replacement. ---
(76’) That bit of action proves to be Sessegnon's last of the match as he comes off to be replaced by Georgios Samaras. The West Brom faithful don't seem to enamoured with that swap though as we hear a small chorus of boos!
--- 75’ Substitution S. Pocognoli is replaced with C. Gamboa. ---
(74’) Sessegnon is facing his own goal and is surrounded by Giroud and Cazorla as the duo attempt to hunt the ball down. The former Sunderland man shows excellent strength and eventually earns the free kick after a clip from Giroud.
(73’) Pocognoli has failed to shake off that injury and he'll be replaced by Cristian Gamboa.
(72’) Dawson gives the ball away poorly in a dangerous position in the middle of the park and Alexis gratefully collects before bursting ahead. To be fair to the West Brom defender though he manages to recover and puts in a great tackle to halt the run of the Chilean.
(70’) We've got a small break in play at the moment as Pocognoli is currently down after going down rather innocuously off the ball. Those are often the worst cases when in comes to injuries but the Belgian receives some treatment from the physios and thankfully manages to get to his feet.
(68’) Really important interception from Dawson! Alexis pops up down the left channel and then lays a ball into the path of Gibbs who darts ahead and smashes a dangerous cross to the front post. Giroud is lingering but the West Brom defender is positioned perfectly to clear behind for a corner.
(66’) Poor from Ramsey. Gibbs does well to reclaim possession near the West Brom box and the Welshman collects on the edge of the box, but he can only manage a weak, dragged shot wide. He hasn't scored since August in the league and it doesn't look like he has his shooting boots on today either!
--- 65’ Substitution Y. Mulumbu is replaced with V. Anichebe. ---
(64’) First change of the match from West Brom and it is an attacking change from Alan Irvine. Mulumbu is the man coming off and he'll be replaced by Victory Anichebe. That's a holding midfielder off for a striker then! Brave!
(62’) Koscielny gets into a bit of a pickle as he retreats towards his own goal whilst under plenty of pressure from Berahino. The West Brom man lets the Arsenal defender off the hook though as he pulls at his shirt, which there was no need at all to do. Daft.
--- 60’ Assist The assist came from Cazorla. ---
--- 60’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAAAAAAAAALLLLLL FOR ARSENAL!!! THE GUNNERS BREAK THE DEADLOCK!! Cazorla collects down the left wing and leaves Wisdom for dead before hitting the byline and chipping a cross into the box. Welbeck outjumps his marker to bullet a header past the desperate hand of Foster! One-nil! ---
(58’) Brunt gets into an advanced position down the left wing and looks to hit a signature whipped cross into the box. It cannons off Chambers and West Brom get the corner kick, which triggers an encouraging cheer from the Hawthorns faithful.
(56’) Much better, far more open match so far in this second half! Kibbs does brilliantly to hit the byline and dinks a great cross into the danger area. Cazorla leaves it for Alexis who looks poised to head home, but is foiled by Pocognoli who makes an important block! Great defending there!
(54’) BERAHINO! SIDE-NETTING ONLY! The West Brom man is called onside this time and bursts into the Arsenal box before cutting inside on his right foot. He looks to catch Martinez out at his front post but ends up sending his strike wide! He probably had better options inside!
--- 53’ Yellow card G. Dorrans receives a yellow card. ---
(52’) First booking of the match and it is a deserved one for Dorrans as the Scot cynically grabs the shirt of Alexis down the left-hand side. Probably a good free kick to give away though as Arsenal had committed plenty of men forward.
(50’) Arsenal just do not have a final product here! Welbeck is the latest guilty party as he gets into a great position inside the box and looks to bend a strike at goal. The Englishman takes far too much time to get the shot away which allows Dawson to make the block!
(48’) Good start to the second half from Arsenal. You can already see that the game is slightly more stretched after the break as West Brom maybe are set out to try and be more of an attacking threat. This may play into the hands of the Gunners though who usually thrive in open spaces. We shall see as the game develops.
(47’) Berahino collects near the halfway line and runs through on goal, only to be flagged as offside by the linesman. Well, that looks a terribly decision by the official; he was onside by a yard!
(46’) We are back under way between West Brom and Arsenal!
Half time at The Hawthorns. A decent display from Arsenal so far as they look by far the most likely team to open the scoring. Danny Welbeck and Santi Cazorla have tested Ben Foster with a one-on-one and a few long range strikes, but the deadlock remains as we go into the break goalless. The home side certainly need to improve in the second period of they are to get anything out of this.
(44’) There's no doubt about it, this game needs a goal. It has been a rather interesting clash so far and Foster has been kept busy in the West Brom goal with a few speculative shots and a great save from Welbeck, but the match has been bereft of out and out goalscoring chances. The former Manchester United man had the best one, but couldn't convert.
(42’) As West Brom lose the ball after an intercepted cross from Wisdom, Alexis bursts down the left-hand side before checking inside and looking to pick out Chambers with a diagonal, but the West Brom full back retreats well and combined with Mulumbu to reclaim possession.
(40’) In a rare West Brom attack in which Arsenal look shaky, Sessegnon powerfully runs at goal before passing out wide to Brunt. The Irishman then slides inside to Gardner, who attempts to lift a pass to the back post for the onrushing Wisdom, but the former Sunderland man's radar is way off and the visitors get the goal kick.
(38’) Koscielny lifts a pass into midfield and Cazorla turns sharply before driving through the middle and then into the right channel. He spots the run of Ramsey at the back post and curls a left-footed cross into the box, but it had just too much on it and Foster comes out to see it behind for a goal kick.
(36’) RAMSEY! How close was that?! Mulumbu initially does well to win the ball back on the edge of his own box, but then gives the ball away! The Welshman pounces and then dances into the box, but ends up dragging a strike just wide of the post! One of the better chances of the match so far!
(34’) A little too close for comfort for Pocognoli! Welbeck looks to latch on to loose ball inside the West Brom box but just, JUST, gets beaten to it by the Belgian, who would definitely have gave away a penalty kick if he was a second later. Ended up being a great challenge!
(32’) Much better from Cazorla this time as he shows quick feet in the middle of the pitch to get beyond the challenge of Mulumbu. The Spaniard then slides a pass into the channel for Alexis, but he Chilean's dinked cross into the box is easily collected by Foster.
(30’) Cazorla should be doing much better there. Some lovely interplay on the edge of the box from Arsenal with Giroud, Ramsey, and Alexis all involved. Once again the move ends with Cazorla, and once again the strike is too close to Foster. The Gunners have had plenty of shooting opportunities so far, but they haven't connected particularly well on most of them.
(28’) Almost from hero to zero for Foster! After saving brilliantly from Welbeck a few moments ago, the England international decides to dribble the ball out of his penalty area! Giroud intercepts but the angle is almost impossible and the Frenchman's strike goes beyond the goal! What was the West Brom keeper doing there?!
(26’) SAVE BY FOSTER!! Ramsey drifts into the pocket in between midfield and attack and threads a lovely pass in behind the West Brom defence for Welbeck, who lashes a strike at goal, but the goalkeeper rushes off his line and makes himself big to make the block!
(24’) There's a bit of a melee in and around the penalty area as Giroud goes down under the challenge of Mulumbu and then Gardner commits a foul 25 yards out. In the the end the free kick is given, but Alexis fails to get it over the wall despite a rather elaborate build up.
--- 23’ Substitution K. Gibbs enters play, replacing Nacho Monreal. ---
(22’) Well it looks like Monreal has indeed failed to shake off that injury he suffered in that tackle with Dorrans. The Spaniard is coming off and he'll be replaced by Kieran Gibbs, who should slot in easily at left-back. Like-for-like change then.
(20’) Berahino does well to get back into a defensive position but then gives the ball away cheaply to Ramsey, who gets beyond Dorrans with a lovely Marseille turn, but ends up being tripped by the Scot. Free kick to Arsenal in a useful position down the left flank.
(18’) That's great defending from Wisdom. Alexis finds himself in a deeper position this time and then drives forward before lofting a pass to the back post for Welbeck, who chests down before looking to get into the box, but the Liverpool loanee gets his body in the way before ushering the ball back to Foster.
(16’) Alexis gets into a central position 40 yards or so out and receives the ball to feet before turning sharply. He spots the run of Chambers as the Englishman gallops down the right channel, but the pass out doesn't have enough pace on it which allows Pocognoli to claim possession.
(14’) Pocognoli picks up the ball at left back and drifts past the challenge of Alexis before taking a few strides forward. He looks to exchange a one-two with Brunt down the wing but the Irishman's return pass is read well by Mertesacker, who makes the comfortable interception.
(12’) It looks like Arsenal may have yet another injury problem here as it looks like Monreal has picked up a knock after a collision with Dorrans. The former Malaga man is just receiving a bit of treatment on the touchline, but it seems as if he may be okay to continue. Watch this space.
(10’) Vital block by Dawson! A sweeping counterattack from Arsenal sees Cazorla drive a pass out to the right wing and then follow his run to the edge of the box. He receives a lay-off from Welbeck and hits a stinging strike towards goal, but the West Brom defender bravely makes the interception!
(8’) West Brom get their first corner kick of the match and take it short. Gardner collects 18 yards out and whips a cross to the back post for Lescott, who rises high to nod back into the danger area. Luckily for Arsenal, Koscielny is well-placed to clear away at the front post.
(6’) Great play by Alexis! The Chilean collects the ball on the halfway line and opens up his side through the middle with a driving run. He sees space on the edge of the box and lashes a strike at goal, but once again the shot goes straight at Foster. Easy save in the end.
(4’) West Brom have just managed to find their feet in the match now and are just enjoying a period of sustained possession inside Arsenal's half. The Gunners are sitting pretty deep for the moment but the hosts will need to be wary of the pacey counterattack their opposition possesses.
(2’) First decent move of the match and it comes from Arsenal. Alexis and Chambers link up well down the right wing and the ball comes in to Welbeck, who tees up Cazorla, but the Spaniard's drilled strike goes straight down the throat of Foster.

Arsenal's last two visits to West Brom have proved to be tough. In their past two games at The Hawthorns, they have only managed to come out with 1-1 draws, but one was indeed a League Cup encounter in which they prevailed 4-3 on penalties.
The last match at The Hawthorns saw Alan Irvine's men go down 2-0 to a resurgent Newcastle side; a result which saw the home fans air their grievances at full time with a chorus of boos. The hosts today will be hoping to give their supporters something to cheer about for the first time in a while.
West Brom are currently situated relatively safely in the table in 13th place, but the Baggies are on a bit of a torrid goalscoring run at the moment, having failed to score or claim a point in their last three league games.
Arsenal have been rocked by the news this week that Jack Wilshere could miss up to 3 months of football after picking up an ankle injury last week. However, they will be buoyed by the fact that Olivier Giroud is set to make his first start since returning from a broken leg.
Despite the London outfit's start to the season, they are still just two points away from the top four, and a victory today would see them preliminary move into the Champions League places.
Arsene Wenger's side have endured a poor start to their league campaign and have claimed just four wins from their opening 12 matches. The Gunners will be hoping that this result kick starts their season and sees them put together a decent run of form domestically.

The Potters leave Anfield without scoring again, though Mark Hughes will be gutted given how well his side played at times. Relief will certainly be the predominant emotion among home fans and the team itself, but they battled well despite lacking quality.
Liverpool finally found a way through though. Henderson's cross to an offside Lambert was headed onto the bar by the striker, and Glen Johnson did marvellously to stoop bravely and head in the rebound. Liverpool then held on despite sustained Stoke pressure.
The second half was wonderfully pulsating though, with great saves from Mignolet and Begovic, and Sterling on the line, keeping the game scoreless. Bojan came closest with a rasping shot onto the post.
Football, eh? Liverpool, woefully unproductive to start with, found Stoke obdurate and quick on the break in the first half. Only good defending from Kolo Toure prevented Stoke from fashioning good scoring chances.
(90’) And, finally, that's it. Well, well. After one of the worst first halves I've ever seen, Liverpool take it 1-0 against Stoke City.
(90’) Mignolet gathers really well under pressure. He then held it for around 20 seconds, which was a bit naughty. Mark Hughes is typically apoplectic.
(90’) Crazily, there are still three minutes to go. Lambert tries to hold it in the corner to waste time but gives up the goal-kick. Stoke win a corner and Shawcross has basically camped out in the Liverpool half. Begovic is up too.
(90’) Stoke have a corner. The pressure is intense for both teams now. Adam takes it and Shawcross just heads wide, with no-one on the post this time. This game is still bubbling like mad.
(90’) Bojan slips onto his posterior as he tries to bend in a shot at the edge of the Liverpool box. Stoke come again through Adam, looking for Crouch. Bojan incredibly volleys the rebound in and Mignolet may have got a touch.
(89’) Walters is bundled over but Stoke retain the ball and Crouch just misses a cross. There will be seven minutes of extra time. That seems a bit much, even with the Johnson head-patching.

(88’) Adam, the other ex-Red, dinks over a through-ball but there's too much on it and Mignolet gathers.
(87’) Crouch is on, the second former Liverpool player on the pitch for Stoke. This is tough on Stoke and it looked like Lambert was offside when he headed against the bar.
--- 85’ Goal! FINALLY! JOHNSON SCORES FOR LIVERPOOL! Henderson lofts in a cross and Lambert's towering header hits the bar. Johnson bravely follows up with his head at foot level and sneaks the ball over the line. It's been coming. Johnson is bleeding from a head-wound now. ---
(83’) Countinho, obviously trying to make a point, drags the ball back from the by-line and drives in a delicious cross but finds no-one there.
(82’) Shawcross and Countinho bravely contest the ball with diving headers in the Stoke box and Liverpool have another corner, which Gerrard wastes. (81’) DIOUF! SO CLOSE! Sterling does superbly to clear off the line from Diouf as Stoke come so close to breaking their set-piece duck. It was a neat turn-and-volley from the striker.
(80’) Shawcross heads clear under illegal pressure from Skrtel. Stoke have a good chance to clear their lines now.
(79’) The injection of energy and pace into this game has really enlivened it, but it's still hard to see which team will benefit. It's end to end now, but again a lack of quality in the box is preventing the goals from flowing. Allen forces a corner.
(77’) Gerrard looks for Lambert, whose control is clunky. Liverpool look most dangerous when they are running onto the ball at pace rather than trying to cross into a crowded, tall Stoke box.

(75’) Cameron stands up well to Sterling, who runs the ball out. The youngster is continually charging at the Stoke full-back though and has done a fine job without ever finding that extra bit of magic.
(74’) ADAM! The Scot forces a diving, slightly circus-y save from Mignolet, after he releases Arnautovic with a sublime ball and then runs onto the return pass.
(73’) Lucas is going to brought off for Gerrard. I'm not sure anyone will be overly saddened by this news, not even Lucas himself.
(72’) Toure defends well again, this time stealing it from Diouf, who has also been impressive, especially where his work rate is concerned. Stoke retain the ball though, pasisng it back and back again all the way to Begovic.
(70’) Shawcross touches Countinho in the box, who tumbles. The referee is not impressed though. At the other end, Stoke build well before Henderson knocks the ball out for a throw deep in Liverpool territory.

(66’) Lambert is well-found at the top of the box by Johnson but he side-foots it neatly to Begovic. A real waste of a chance by the English striker.
(65’) Stoke have a good passage of play which ends when N'Zonzi's pass is over-hit. Sterling brings it forwards but the Liverpool move peters out.
(63’) BEGOVIC SAVES! Lucas runs onto a ball from Henderson after Arnautovic gives it away. The big Bosnian stands up until the last minute and palms away a stinging shot. Lambert then wafts the follow-up wide.

(57’) N'Zonzi, not wishing to be left out, fires a shot into the behind of his own player from a similar distance when Cameron was overlapping wide right. Poor choice.
(56’) Lambert shoots from thirty-five yards and collectively, Liverpool fans shake their heads.
(55’) Begovic dives to grab a cross from Sterling, whose sheer pace is causing the now booked Cameron a lot of issues.
(54’) DIOUF! A lovely ball from Bojan is perfectly weighted for the rapid striker to run onto but Mignolet, who hesitated to start with, sprawls well to save. That was a great chance for the Stoke forward.

(49’) I say that, and then Toure passes it straight out under no pressure.

(46’) Johnson attacks well and Wilson scrambles it away. Liverpool have certainly begun with greater urgency this half and they've forced a throw-in deep in Stoke territory. Allen has a shot charged down on the edge of the box.
(45’) Liverpool get us underway. Stoke have brought on Charlie Adam for Glenn Whelan. He didn't last long. Must have been all that excitement.
