Hopefully the second half will pick up and, if Coutinho's excellent run is a precursor of anything, Liverpool will attack with renewed vigour.
Neither keeper have had a save of note to make though, and Liverpool have failed to capitalise of a number of set-pieces too. They seem frustrated and lacking both creativity and cutting edge, with Lambert cutting a lonely figure up front.
Both teams looks most dangerous down their respective left-hand sides, where for the home side, Luis Enrique has produced one superb cross and, for theaway team, Bojan, Arnautovic, and Pieters have done well.
The first half finishes Liverpool 0-0 Stoke City. It's been a difficult game to muster a great deal of enthusiasm about so far, though Sterling and Coutinho have had their moments, as have Bojan and Arnautovic.
(45’) The referee gratefully blows for half-time.
(45’) Cruelly, there will be at least two minutes of extra time.
(44’) Stoke are finishing the half on the front foot, but Countinho does create a beautiful, mazy run out of nothing before firing wide. That's a warning to the Potters, but it's the only one they've had, really.
(43’) Stoke have a corner. Toure and Skrtel have defended crosses well so far and the away team have yet to score from a set-piece this season. They don't manage now either, Bojan's ball easily dealt with.
(41’) Sterling is furious as he concedes a free-kick by fouling Cameron. Too many Liverpool moves have broken down due to imprecision, as much as a lack of numbers in the box.
(40’) Sterling does very well to create space for himself and fire in a low cross. He is certainly Liverpool's danger man. Stoke clear.
(39’) Lambert dinks in a cross but Pieters can safely chest it back to Begovic under no pressure at all. Whelan handles to prevent a Sterling pass from finding Henderson but oddly doesn't get booked for it.

(38’) Henderson sends in a woeful, low cross from the free-kick which Diouf leathers clear. There's some to-and-fro in midfield and then Liverpool come again but Stoke can clear. (37’) Wilson is booked for a silly foul on Lambert when he could simply have stood him up. Liverpool have a free-kick wide right.
(36’) Walters is tackled by Lucas as he lines up to volley a shot from Diouf's cross into the box. Good defending from the Brazilian.
(35’) Sterling is feeling his calf, which might be a worry. His pace has been a minor threat.

Stoke's record against the red half of Merseyside is poor though, having not netted in 21 years in the league at Anfield. Having said that, if there was a time to be playing Liverpool, it is now, and Hughes will hope that if his side can avoid the errors which tarnished their game against Burnley, the Potters can secure all three points.
Stoke City are a place and a point above their hosts and the Mark Hughes renaissance continues, albeit with a stutter after the loss to Burnley. But, the Potters have won away at Manchester City and Spurs this season and in Bojan and Arnautovic have two potential game-changers.
Liverpool have looked tired and lacking creativity and will be hoping that the movement and running of Sterling and Coutinho can fire them. The midfield trio looks solid but pedestrian.
Rodgers looks like a man under pressure and once again finds himself bereft of strikers, with none on the bench and an aging Lambert to lead the line. His height will be of use defensively though against a big Stoke side.

Unbelievable that it managed to stay out there!

And certainly, a point will be welcome for Palace on the road against an opponent who has proven to be very difficult to beat at home. That's all from us today. Thank you for joining us!
It was a breathless, open, and even affair in the latter stages today. Monk will be furious that his side have dropped points yet again from a winning position, but as Palace grew in composure following the penalty, a draw was about a fair result.
(90’) Bolasie tries to do it all himself, skipping in from the left, dribbling around several players and firing towards target, well wide over the bar. Zaha gets the ball seconds later and though Williams concedes a corner, the whistle is blown before it can be taken! It ends 1-1 with Palace's penalty enough to take a share of the spoils from the home side.
(90’) Nervy moments at the back for Swansea! Williams is nearly caught out against Campbell in a one-on-one scenario, but the defender really should have comfortably had possession and risked everything until Fabianski raced out.
(90’) Bolasie's been absolutely tireless for the visitors tonight and wins yet another throw-in for his side. It's worked to Kelly who takes a shot as he falls down on the flank, well outside the box, that ends up on target but comfortably so from Fabianski's point of view.
(90’) Four minutes of added time have just been announced by the fourth official in a game that at first seemed destined for an overwhelming Swansea victory though now seems fit to end in a draw. The home side continue to press with Montero central, finding Barrow on the right to send a cross into Gomis that he simply can't get on the end of. Gomis has not been on for long but he has not been running the show like Bony was, either.
(89’) Excellent from Montero on the left, who skips past Ward but is foiled by McArthur just seconds later, who concedes a throw-in. Taylor gets on the end of it and races into the box but his first touch sends the ball high for Speroni to collect. One minute plus stoppages now!
(87’) It's Ki again, who's really growing in influence as this team wears on, who dribbles his way into space and lays it off for Sigurdsson who draws a good save out of Speroni!
(83’) Gomis gives away a free-kick deep in Palace's half that Speroni is certainly in no rush to take.
--- 81’ Substitution It's another sub late on here, with Wilfred Zaha coming on as Warnock tries a late roll of the dice here to get all three points in a  very difficult venue. ---
(79’) SIGURDSSON JUST WIDE! Angel Rangel dribbled himself all the way to the middle, just outside the box, before laying it off for Sigurdsson; the former Spurs man takes the shot without stopping the ball and sees it go agonizingly wide of the far post!
(78’) Ki is crafting his way into the box, playing it deep but the cross is cut out. It gets back to Barrow who wins a throw-in off of Ward and soon Palace try to counter but Puncheon's pass in intercepted by Angel Rangel, who's having a simply excellent match.
(76’) Bartley makes an excellent block on the line to prevent Kelly's cross from reaching the box! Swansea break and are now in midfield, with Bartley trying to find a teammate before laying it off to Sigurddsson, who's pass to find Gomis is well overhit and trickles out.
--- 75’ Substitution Bony's match is over as Bafetimbi Gomis comes on for the forward, who has been in very good form today but looked knackered in these later minutes. ---
(72’) Less than 20 minutes to go here and neither side has been terribly convincing. They're both attacking at every opportunity but genuine chances are hard to come by now, as Sigurdsson's shot from outside the box is blocked.
(70’) Another chance gone absolutely begging for Shelvey but his miss this time is not as bad as the last two, as his first time shot from a clearance goes well wide of the far post.
--- 69’ Yellow card Ohh and there's some controversy now! McArthur is booked for taking down Barrow on the counter after a Palace corner was cleared out by Shelvey. There are some shouts for a sending off but a yellow seems fair and now Swansea have a chance to attack. ---
--- 66’ Substitution Campbell comes on for Chamakh now: the former Arsenal man has been lively and somewhat petulant, and Warnock may have been worried that his one booking could easily become two should he have stayed on for much longer. ---
--- 65’ Substitution Routledge comes off for Barrow as Monk tries to do something here to get his side to get all three points. As Swansea come up from the goal-kick, all of Palace's players are behind their own line. Taylor once again tries a high ball into Montero and once again, the latter can't reach it - it's becoming a predictable tactic and easy to defend against. ---
(63’) A throw-in in enemy territory for Palace, with Puncheon and Ki getting quite physical near the sideline. It's laid off to Jedinak to pass to Kelly and soon worked up to Chamakh, who's offside.
(61’) Bolasie goes down but it's a little too easily and Atkinson simply refuses to call for a foul, to Warnock's ire on the sidelines. The home side now work it to Shelvey, who sends a brilliant touch around Dann before findind Bony in the box, and though it's cleared, it's only to Sigurdsson who forces a smart save from outside the box!
(59’) Montero is trying to get onto the end of Taylor's high pass in the box but he just can't reach it in time. He's faded as this game has gone on and Monk will want him to get more involved, as his runs were causing issues at the back for the visitors during the first half.
(58’) Taylor and Puncheon are both fighting for the ball near the halfway line and the Swansea man wins out. Sigurdsson is deeper, trying to win the ball and make something happen but Ledley isn't giving him a second to think, forcing him to play it back to Fabianski.
(56’) A mistake from Hangeland now as he loses the ball deep in his own half but he's let off the hook as Sigurdsson's cross is easily cleared by Dunn.
(55’) McArthur tries an audacious chip down the left to send Bolasie racing free but he's asking far too much of the winger and Angel Rangel easily collects.
(53’) Wonderful play from Swansea, who have Sigurdsson running the engine but the cutback to Bony is just behind the striker. Shelvey then has the ball in the box and smartly holds it up to leave Dann rushing past him, but he cannot get it to a teammate! This is truly livening up now.
(52’) SHELVEY AGAIN MISSES A GOLDEN CHANCE! He gets the ball perfectly in the box, and takes it down wonderfully, but his shot is right at Speroni! Once again a chance presents itself and Swansea fail to take it!!
(51’) Chamakh has the ball in the box and tries to lay it off for Bolasie but it's too weak and Shelvey clears! It's played in again towards Chamakh but Fabianski has no issues jumping high to gather.
(50’) Bolasie's pace once again proves useful as he races in and has his shot deflected out for a corner. Ki heads it clear but only to the top of the box, sending Angel Rangel scrambling to clear it. Palace have the ball now, just outside of Swansea's box.
(49’) Angel Rangel tries to find Bony in the box with a long throw-in but Puncheon is there to clear. Palace races through the mdifield and Jedinak gets the ball abour twenty yards out to send a shot into the arms of Fabianski!
(48’) The intensity here is a lot slower than in the first half, which may have been expected. Both sides are setting up deep, in numbers, which is clogging the midfield more and reducing passing lanes. As always, however, Bony finds a smart pass to Routledge who wins a corner off Kelly, which gets headed out by Chamakh.
(46’) And we're back for the second half! It'll be fascinating to see how these two sides repond to a whirlwind of a first half. Ki is trying to dribble his way out of trouble but only finds Jedinak in his way. The visitors have the ball but nowhere to go with it, with a see of white in front of them.
Monk will simply need his side to settle back into their early game rhythm, though Warnock will want the exact opposite: for his team to keep interrupting Swansea's plans. The visitors need to find a way to keep Bony more quiet, however, as his every touch is finding little ways to expose them at the back.
That half was simply breathless. Swansea City looked to be well on their way to a routine win, even after taking the lead, until a old cliche reared its head and one moment changed everything. Now the game seems fairly even, with everything left to play for!
(45’) AND SOMEHOW SHELVEY MISSES NEARLY ALL BY HIMSELF! A fantastic ball finds the former Liverpool player about 15 yards from the goal, alone, without a defender around him, but his shot fails to even test Speroni! The whistle is blown immediately after and the sides head into the half tied at 1-1!
(45’) Bony and Sigurdsson combine well under pressure but soon they've lost the ball and a counter is led by Bolasie. He works the ball wide to Chamakh, who shows too much of the ball to Angel Rangel.
(45’) Two minutes have been added on here, in a half that has had nearly everything imaginable! The men in white are carefully playing with the ball now, keeping possession though looking to go forward when an opening is created through smart movement.
(44’) It ends up as a training ground routine from Monk's men, as Sigurdsson lays it off for the onrushing Shelvey to try and poke to net, but his attempt to divert the ball sees him fail to get enough of his foot around it, and it trickles wide of Speroni's near post!
(43’) Chamakh clears Sigurdsson's intitial corner right back out to the Swansea player. He sends in another cross that hits Chamakh's hand and Swansea are FURIOUS as they're awarded a free-kick, just outside the box! Fantastic opporrunity for the home side now!
(42’) Swansea have the ball and are interchanging very well down their right flank, with Sigurdsson at the heart of it with some deft touches. Their efforts win a corner when the ball deflects out off of substitute McArthur.
--- 40’ Yellow card Ward with an excellent defensive header to prevent the ball from getting to Montero. Seconds later, Chamakh goes in very harshly on a tackle into Taylor and earns a booking for that poor slide. He's arguing with Atkinson again over this call and must be careful not to be sent off! ---
(39’) Excellent defending from Taylor who wins the ball in his own box and springs out to set up his side to attack. The game has settled into an even rhythm now though there certainly seem to be more goals in this one, with each side looking more dangerous in attack than assured in the back.
(37’) Montero is down in visible pain, even with his side on the ball, but no one knocks it out! Ki plays it wide up to Routledge who plays the ball off of Kelly for a corner. Routledge gets the ball on the edge of the box on the play but can't get a shot off, committing a foul soon after to prevent a penalty.
(36’) That seems to have given the home side some confidence as they surge down the left but it's finally cleared by Dann in the box.
(34’) It's Swansea's best attack in quite some time here thanks to some smart link up from Bony. Sigurdsson plays an exquisite pass to send Routledge right through the centre-backs, and alone with Speroni, his weak effort off his weaker foot only finds Speroni! Monk will be wondering how they did not score there!
(33’) There's finally a moment to breathe for Monk's men when Chamakh slips and loses the chance to win the ball from a throw-in. He's talking to Taylor, perhaps even accusing him of pulling him down, but he's not complaining to Atkinson and Swansea have the ball.
(32’) This corner is defending much better from the home side, who whip it clear thanks to Bony. Palace have it again as Ward, Bolasie and Chamakh try to carve an opening down the right flank. It's worked to the other side and sent in well by McArthur, though it sails across the box before Bolasie can get it.
(31’) NEARLY A SECOND FROM BOLASIE! That's a simply sensational effort from the winger who cuts in from about twenty five yards out and just rips and effort on goal from a very wide angle that forces a jumping push over the bar from Fabianski, though the goalie is arguing he didn't get a hand on it!
(30’) On the other end, it's much less confidence goalkeeping as Speroni nearly loses the ball off a routine cross in from Sigurdsson, but is able to collect it on his second attempt. Ever since the goal, the fluidity in Swansea's play has gone and they are truly having trouble keeping the ball.
(29’) WHAT A SAVE FROM FABIANSKI! Palace's sequence of passing nearly pays off from a howler from Ashley Williams, who somehow only plays the ball into Chamakh in the box when trying to clear - the former Arsenal striker pounces and tries to prod the ball into the net, but the former Arsenal keeper races out to parry with his body!
(28’) Bony tries to win the ball for his side but now Palace are simply everywhere and he passes right to an opponent. Ward has the ball, playing it back to Jedinak, who goes wide to Puncheon, before going back to the defence. Palace refuse to lose the ball right now and are patiently building it up.
(27’) Jedinak wins the ball in midfield and Puncheon is charging forward. He's looking for Ward on the flank but Montero is all the way back covering for his side, winning back possession. Palace still have the ball, deep in their own half, and suddenly look a much better team.
(26’) Unfortunately for Monk, this is somewhat characteristic of his side. As it stands, they did not add to their tally when they could and in an instant, everything changed. They do have the bulk majority of the match to change things but they'll desperately need to hope this does not give Palace a confidence boost!
--- 25’ Goal! Shelvey had just bundled over Chamakh and Atkinson doesn't hesitate for a second to award a penalty! Jedinak steps up to take it... AND PUTS IT AWAY! SOMEHOW PALACE ARE TIED HERE DESPITE BEING DOMINATED FOR MOST OF THE HALF! 1-1!!! ---
(24’) Ward whips in the cross and Williams charges across his box to send it out for another corner. On the second CHAMAKH GOES DOWN IN THE BOX AND WINS A PENALTY! WHAT A MATCH WE HAVE HERE!
(23’) And just like that, Bolasie wins a corner. A poor pass from Ki is cut out and the winger gets it down to the opposition's box, sending his cross out off of Rangel for a set-peice opportunity.
(22’) With 70% possession, Swansea are in cruise control right now, but the side have dropped double digit points this season after taking the lead: Monk knows one goal may not be enough here and will be wanting his side to put this away while they can.
--- 21’ Substitution Palace have finally substituted Gayle, with McArthur coming on for the injured striker. He nearly gets the ball immediately from the throw-in but Bartley smartly ushers it out of bounds for a goal-kick to his own team. ---
(20’) Bolasie rips the ball off of Angel Rangel to try and launch a counter deep in Swansea's half, but Ashley Williams comes roraring out of defence to intercept the pass and win his side possession again. It comes to little, as a very ambitious pass from Montero ends up near no one in the box.
(19’) BONY JUST FAILS TO CONNECT WITH A CROSS FROM ROUTLEDGE! And Swansea are all over the box now, with Shelvey's shot from outside the area blocked and the play being worked down the other flank. Palace are down to ten right now with Gayle off injured and no substitute yet.
(18’) A rare foray forward from Palace ends as Puncheon's cross in the box is cleared by Bartley all too easily. As Bony tries to counter, Ledley bundles him over. Gayle is down once again, holding his thigh, and it looks like Palace may be forced into a very early substitute here.
(16’) Only 16 minutes have gone here but this is utterly dominant from Swansea. Jedinak takes down Shelvey in the midfield to gift another free-kick to the home side, who work it down the right by Routledge before Hangelaand can clear it. Ki tries a shot from a long ways out but it's wide. If anything, Swansea may be angry that they're only up by a single goal!
--- 15’ Assist G. Sigurðsson gave the assist. ---
--- 15’ Goal! BONY SCORES! SWANSEA LEAD 1-0! This is absolutely fantastic football from Swansea! Sigurdsson gets the ball to Bony in the box. Though Hangelaand is right behind him, Bony makes some space for himself and turns and shoots around the defender, slipping the ball into the far corner beyond Speroni! It's no less than the home side deserve!! ---
(14’) Ki wins the ball back in midfield and Montero switches field of play to pick out Routledge on the other flank. His cross is cleared but it's back with Taylor now.
(13’) WHAT A CHANCE! Seconds after a bad pass from Shelvey loses the ball, Swansea get it back thanks to Routledge's tenacity. He tries to play it into Bony deep in the box but Sigurdsson gets in the way and it's frantically knocked out for a corner by Hangeland! The corner is a poor one, easily collected by Speroni.
(12’) Scintillating from the home side! It's Montero once again who is simply giving the visitors all kinds of problems in the back, racing to the byline and crossing in for the onrushing Bony who's first time effort goes over the bar! Kelly absolutely cannot contain Montero at the moment!
(11’) Gayle goes off for treatment but comes on just seonds after, gingerly trying to see if he can play on. The home side once again have the ball and Rangel plays the perfect pass over the top for Routledge, but the midfielder just cannot find a teammate in the box with his cross!
(9’) Palace finally see some decent possession of the ball but a very fierce pass up to Chamakh is just too heavy for him to take under control. Shelvey soon cleans up the play and once again the home side are looking to build down the flank, though Gayle is down holding his thigh after a challenge with Williams and the ball is kicked out so he can receive treatment.
(8’) Who else but Sigurdsson, up to take the chance. He curves the ball marvelously but it lands just on the roof of the net, with Speroni racing across his goal-line just in case!
(7’) Six minutes in here and the visitors are nowhere to be seen. It's all Kelly can do to knock out a fantastic pass from Shelvey up to Rangel, but the home side skill have the ball and Chamakh takes down Ki from behind to give the home side the first free-kick of the game. The former Arsenal player is lucky not to be booked as he had thrown the ball away in clear dissention of Atkinson!
(5’) Insatiable from the home side! Montero gets the ball down the wing, cuts to the byline, and crosses for Bony. It's inch-perfect and the forward rises high to head the ball but his effort goes wide of the far post!
(4’) The home side continue to foray forward and it nearly pays off brilliantly, as Taylor roams all the way up to where Bony is, combines with the latter thanks to a cheeky backheel in the box, and then the full-back goes down in the box! It's a bit too soft however and Mark Atkinson refuses to blow for a penalty.
(3’) Williams, to Taylor, back to Fabianski, to Bartley... back and forth at the back, with Palace set up well and not giving them much room. The quick passes across the field work as Montero is played in behind Kelly and tries to slip the ball across to Bony but his pass along the box is cleared!
(2’) Montero rises high to head Speroni's goal-kick out of bounds and his teammates do equally well to intercept from the following throw-in. They seek Shelvey again to build for them but good pressing from the visitors has forced them to keep the ball amongst their defenders.
(1’) AND WE HAVE KICK-OFF! The visitors immediately look for a ball up to Bolasie but he loses out. The home side calmly takes control of possession as Shelvey begins to look for a rhythm. It's worked down the right into Routledge's path and his cross goes over the line on the far side of the box.
One more interesting tidbit before we get started here properly: Swansea have been defeated four times in the league this season but only one of those has been to a team below them in the table - their loss against Stoke.
The two teams are walking out of the tunnel and heading onto the pitch. Palace know their job today: their last win at Swansea was back in March 2009 when both teams were in the Championship!
Palace have a few more injury concerns, with Damien Delaney and Adrian Mariappa not called up for the match. And though confidence will be sky high following last weekend's win over Liverpool, recent history is not with the visitors; in the last six meetings between these teams, Swansea have won four times and drew the other two. Neil Warnock's men have just four points from the last 18 available and are two points above the relegation zone.
Besides defender Federico Fernandez, Garry Monk has a full squad available at his disposal today. The side, currently with 16 points, have done quite well during a grueling stretch in recent weeks, beating Arsenal and tying Everton in betweeen very narrow losses to Liverpool and Manchester City. They've shown that they're not afraid to go toe-to-toe with the biggest clubs in the league and Wilfred Bony and Gylfi Sigurdsson will be the danger men today as usual.
Crystal Palace (4-4-1-1): Speroni; Ward, Hangeland, Dann, Kelly; Bolasie, Ledley, Jedinak, Puncheon; Chamakh; Gayle.
Swansea City (4-2-3-1): Fabianski; Angel Rangel, Bartley, Williams, Taylor; Ki, Shelvey; Routledge, Sigurdsson, Montero; Bony.

Next up for Newcastle is a trip to Burnley and Pardew will be without Colback through suspension after he picked up a yellow card today, and also Sissoko after his sending off at the Boleyn Ground. For West Ham, they now travel to West Brom for their next fixture, with both of those games taking place on Tuesday.
The Hammers' victory also sees Allardyce's men put to bed a run of three games without a win, while Newcastle's five-game winning streak has come to an end. Pardew's side have dropped down to eighth in the table.
West Ham's win today sees them move up to fifth in the Premier League table on 21 points and just one point behind fourth-placed Manchester United, who picked up a 3-0 win against Hull City at Old Trafford.
Newcastle were equal to West Ham for large spells and will look back to Sissoko's sending off in the second-half as a key moment. The Frenchman picked up two yellow cards in the space of 45 seconds, and ensured his side would find it difficult to get an equaliser.
FULL-TIME!! WEST HAM PICK UP THE THREE POINTS! Cresswell's first Premier League goal in the second-half sees the Hammers edge past Newcastle by the narrowest of margins.
(90’) Newcastle have a corner late on. Surely this is the last chance of the game, with Toon goalkeeper Elliot going up for it.
(90’) Carroll controls the ball well and shifts it onto his stronger left-foot, but his shot goes well wide and out for a Newcastle throw in the dying minutes. Pardew is urging his players forward.
(90’) BIG CHANCE!! West Ham come so close to wrapping up the three points after Downing forced his way into the box, but the Englishman drove his shot agonisingly past the post.
(90’) The officials have indicated four minutes are being added onto the second-half. Newcastle still have time to claw back a late equaliser, but West Ham are looking good for their lead and have a one-man advantage.
(89’) Ameobi breaks forward on the counter-attack and has options left and right but the youngster decides to go on his own and loses possession to Collins just outside the box.
(88’) West Ham supporters are in full voice and are acting as the 12th man to get their side over the line late on, in what has been a very tight game at the Boleyn Ground. Still 1-0.
--- 87’ Yellow card M. Zárate is yellow-carded. ---
(87’) West Ham break forward again through Downing down the left-hand side and a switch over to Jenkinson saw the Arsenal loanee find Zarate with a cutback, with the Argentine driving a powerful shot towards Elliot, who made a great save! Corner to West Ham!
(86’) ALMOST!! West Ham come so close to doubling their lead after Zarate makes a great break through the middle and feeds Cresswell, who drove a low cross towards Carroll but Haidara done enough to clear. Corner to West Ham.
--- 85’ Substitution C. Kouyaté is done for the day. K. Nolan is his replacement. ---
(83’) Newcastle are the side doing all the pushing in order to try and claw their way back into this game. West Ham are holding firm at the back, though, and are making some changes to try and seal the three points.
(81’) CHANCE! Zarate breaks forward through the middle of the pitch and feeds Carroll with a great pass, but Dummett beat the gangly forward to the ball and cleared the danger brilliantly.
(79’) Pardew really must be cursing his luck as Sissoko's petulance results in his side going down to 10 men, while Haidara is now hobbling from a challenge by Amalfitano, having made all three of his substitutions.
--- 78’ Yellow card M. Amalfitano gets yellow. ---
(77’) Mike Dean is getting busy with the cards as the game is starting to get really tentative in the second-half and both sides are producing cynical fouls on one another.
--- 76’ Red card! HE'S OFF!! NEWCASTLE ARE DOWN TO TEN MEN!! Sissoko picks up a second yellow card in quick succession after pushing Carroll down to the floor, 45 seconds after receiving a yellow for kicking the ball away in frustration. Two crazy decisions from the midfielder have seriously dented his side's chances of getting back into this game. ---
--- 75’ Yellow card M. Sissoko receives a yellow card. ---
(75’) Newcastle get forward in numbers and Sissoko kicks the ball away in frustration after being judged to have pushed Jenkinson. The midfielder has received a yellow card.
--- 74’ Substitution D. Janmaat is replaced with S. Taylor. ---
(73’) West Ham have won a corner after Ameobi made a good block on Jenkinson's cross. Chance for the Hammers to double their lead as time ticks on.
(71’) Perez dances past two West Ham players to get in-behind their defence but his cross couldn't pick anybody out. The game here at the Boleyn Ground is starting to become a little stretched and both teams are having chances now.
--- 70’ Substitution M. Zárate comes on for M. Jarvis. ---
(68’) Pardew's substitutions have definitely seen Newcastle up the tempo since falling a goal behind. Haidara latches onto Cabella's pass and drives forward to win a corner for the Toon. Still 1-0 West Ham.
--- 66’ Yellow card M. Noble gets yellow. ---
(65’) Newcastle have a good chance to try and level the score after Jarvis brought down Cabella deep into West Ham's half. Perez, who has scored three Premier League goals so far this season, is standing over the ball.
(64’) ALMOST! Noble threads a phenomenal ball through to Carroll from the centre of the pitch and the West Ham forward controls nicely and feeds Amalfitano, but the Frenchman's cross can't get past Haidara to trouble Elliot.
--- 63’ Substitution Y. Gouffran is replaced with R. Cabella. ---
--- 63’ Substitution P. Cissé enters play, replacing C. Tioté. ---
(60’) Newcastle boss Pardew is lining up a couple of changes in a bid to get his side back level in this game. West Ham are definitely in the ascendancy since taking the lead and the Toon need to get more players forward to support Perez.
(58’) CHANCE! Newcastle almost get a quick equaliser after Janmaat surges forward from right-back and finds Perez with a bit of space inside the box, but the forward drove his shot too close to Adrian. Still 1-0 West Ham.
(57’) The Hammers fans have raised the atmosphere inside the Boleyn Ground after taking the lead through Cresswell. Both sides have started the second-half with great energy.
--- 56’ Assist C. Kouyaté gave the assist. ---
--- 56’ Goal! GOOOOOAAALLLL!!! WEST HAM BREAK THE DEADLOCK!! Kouyate's mis-hit shot slipped neatly through to an onrushing Cresswell from left-back, who guided the ball past Elliot very calmly. The ex-Ipswich man found himself in a striker's position, but showed great composure in a one-on-one situation with Elliot. ---
(55’) CHANCE! West Ham almost draw first blood after a long ball into the box wasn't cleared away by Elliot and narrowly went past the post. Corner to the Hammers.
--- 54’ Yellow card J. Colback gets yellow. ---
(54’) Colback's yellow card means he will now miss Newcastle's trip to Burnley next weekend. The ex-Sunderland midfielder has played well in this match so far, but will now have to be on his best behaviour for the rest of the game.
(52’) CHANCE! Perez breaks beyond the West Ham defence and plays a great ball back across the face of goal, but Collins done excellently to clear the ball away at the back post and prevent an onrushing Gouffran from scoring.
(51’) West Ham had the chance to pump the ball into the box from a free-kick, but Noble decided to chip it to Cresswell, who's hanging cross came to no avail.
(49’) Colback wins possession in midfield and feeds Perez down the right-hand channel, but the fleet-footed Spaniard couldn't get past Tomkins, who sees the ball out for a goal-kick.
(47’) CHANCE! West Ham break forward from a Newcastle chance and create one of their own. Carroll links up with his former Liverpool team-mate Downing, who drove a shot just over the crossbar. Lively start to the second-half from both sides.
(46’) Welcome back! Newcastle get us underway for the second-half here at the Boleyn Ground.
As things stand across the Premier League, both West Ham and Newcastle will remain in their places in the table before kick-off if the result stays the same here at the Boleyn Ground.
Perez's shot that went just wide of the post after the first two minutes of the game has been without doubt the best chance in the match so far. Both sides have deployed the same 4-2-3-1 formation and may be forced into a change at the break in order to try and break the deadlock.
HALF-TIME! Both sets of players head off towards the tunnel as the referee blows up for half-time. Neither side were able to really dominate in the opening 45 minutes and chances came few and far between.
(44’) The officials have indicated there will be one minute added onto the first-half as Downing whips in a great ball towards Carroll, but Williamson does well to head it away.
(42’) Sissoko is starting to get more involved for Newcastle and is so hard to stop when he gets into full steam and breaks through the middle of the pitch. The ex-Toulouse man is popping up everywhere as Newcastle's front four are interchanging between one another.
(41’) West Ham win a throw-in after some good work by Amalfitano to get away from Haidara down the right. Carroll was the obvious target to aim for but everytime the ball is coming in towards the striker, he is being surrounded by a number of Newcastle bodies.
(39’) Besides the odd half chance coming to fruition, both sides are still cancelling each other out and are struggling to impose themselves. Still 0-0 at the Boleyn Ground.
(37’) Great stuff from Perez! The ex-Tenerife forward latches onto a cross from Haidara and uses the back of his foot to angle the ball towards the West Ham goal, but his effort hit the side netting.
(35’) Tomkins receives some treatment after putting his head in where it matters to clear the ball from a fizzing Newcastle cross. The defender was caught in the face by a boot after Pardew's men whip in a fizzing ball from a free-kick.
(33’) BIG BLOCK! Newcastle break forward in numbers on the counter-attack through Sissoko and the Frenchman done well to feed Perez, before Collins done enough to snuff the ball away from his feet just inside the West Ham box. Fantastic block.
(31’) Neither Adrian or Elliot have had much to do between the sticks in the opening 45 minutes as both sides continue to hold onto possession for a few moments, but then give it away.
(29’) Colback done well to find some space in the pocket between Collins and Cresswell, but Hammers skipper Noble done an excellent job of sweeping up possession and clearing the ball up the field. Still 0-0, with the game in need of an injection of pace to get the fans going.
(28’) Newcastle clear a West Ham throw-in and break forward in numbers. Haidara launches a teasing cross towards the back post, but Cresswell done enough to get rid of the danger.
(26’) Newcastle win a throw-in down the right-hand side and after some good link-up play between Janmaat and Perez, the youngster found half-a-yard down the channel but he couldn't get a shot away.
(23’) Kouyate has been fantastic in the middle of the park so far and the West Ham powerhouse won possession brilliantly before feeding Jarvis down the left, but the former Wolves wide-man couldn't pick anybody out with his cross.
(21’) The Toon are starting to get more of a foothold in this game after a spell of pressure from West Ham. Other than Perez's chance inside the first two minutes, the match is lacking in clear-cut chances so far.
(20’) Newcastle are getting plenty of numbers back and are frustrating West Ham everytime they break forward. Pardew will be delighted with how organised and focussed his players are so far.
--- 19’ Yellow card M. Williamson gets yellow. ---
(17’) West Ham seize possession in midfield and make a great break forward through Downing and the winger found Cresswell marauding forward from left-back, but his cross was well blocked by Sissoko tracking back. The hosts are looking the more dangerous.
(15’) Kouyate shows his exuberance to get forward and links up well with Amalfitano down the right-hand side, but his cross was well blocked by Gouffran.
(13’) Carroll cuts inside from the left-hand side and drills a shot straight at Elliot from point blank range, but the ex-Newcastle striker was judged to have been offside. Replays show the officials were indeed correct.
(12’) West Ham get in-behind Newcastle's defence through Downing, who is interchanging from behind Carroll with Amalfitano and Jarvis, but his cross couldn't pick anybody out and is well cleared by Dummett. Still 0-0.
(10’) The first free-kick of the game goes to West Ham after Janmaat barged straight into Cresswell. Newcastle are definitely angling their play more towards the right flank in the opening stages.
(8’) Both teams are playing their way out of defence so far but are being rushed by one another when they reach the middle of the pitch. A clash of the same 4-2-3-1 formation is apparent.
(7’) West Ham find their rhythm for the first time and a nice burst down the left from Jarvis saw him pull the ball back to an oncoming Downing, who drove a shot straight at Elliot.
(4’) The visitors are having the better share of possession in the opening minutes and again found some joy down the right hand side as Sissoko played a cute cutback, but couldn't find anybody in the box before Collins cleared.
(2’) CHANCE! Newcastle have started the game very brightly and some nice work by Gouffran down the right hand side saw the Frenchman pick out Perez, who steered the ball just wide of the post.

Newcastle are also hoping to pick up three points on what has been a happy hunting ground for them in recent years, with the Tynesiders having won four and lost just one of their last eight games Premier League visits to the Boleyn Ground.
Today's match sees two of the Premier League's in-form sides lock horns as 6th-place Newcastle travel to 7th-place West Ham in a bid to extend their five-game winning streak. The Magpies have bounced back from a poor start to the season in fabulous fashion in recent weeks.

FULL TIME: SUNDERLAND 0-0 CHELSEA. It is a hard fought, well-earned point for the Black Cats, who remained disciplined through the 90 minutes. Chelsea had very little in terms of chances, and it was actually Sunderland who came close to snatching it late. It is the first time this season the Blues have failed to score, while Sunderland pick up their eighth draw from 13 matches.
--- 90’ +2 Yellow card Jordi Gómez is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) Jordi Gomez is shown the fifth yellow card of the match, as he commits a foul high up the pitch, pressuring Chelsea in possession. The visitors loft it forward, and the ball is eventually headed behind by Drogba, which prompts Kevin Friend to blow the whistle for full time!
(90’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY! Fabregas delivers a fine ball, which Terry rushes on to meet. He goes to ground, with Chelsea shouting for a penalty, but nothing is given by the referee. Into the first of two minutes of stoppage time now.
--- 89’ Yellow card S. Vergini goes into the referee's book. ---
(89’) Vergini commits a foul along the left, and then proceeds to slam the ball down in frustration, which earns him a yellow card. Real chance for Chelsea from the free kick, just a few yards from the byline to the left of the penalty area.
(88’) INCHES WIDE! It is all Sunderland at the moment! Johnson takes a pass and streaks through the centre. He has options to his left and right, but opts to have a go himself, perhaps catching Courtois off guard. He drives one towards the far post with his left foot, but it rolls agonizingly wide!
--- 86’ Yellow card N. Matić is yellow-carded. ---
(86’) BRILLIANT RUN! Wickham looks ever so dangerous when he gets on the ball, always looking to take on a defender. He darts up the middle of the pitch and gets takes out from behind by Matic, who is shown a yellow card. The forward takes the free kick, but lashes it against the wall.
--- 85’ Substitution A. Schürrle comes on for Willian. ---
(85’) JOHNSON PUTS IT WIDE! What a chance wasted for the Black Cats! Altidore drives forward and takes a shot from just inside the right of the area. It is blocked, falling kindly for Johnson in the centre, but he pushes it wide with his right foot! He really has to do better there!
(83’) SUNDERLAND COME EVER SO CLOSE! Spectacular counter from the hosts, who storm up the pitch. Altidore slides in Wickham, who bundles his way into the area. He eventually loses control, but the American picks up the lose ball. He cuts to his right and slides it under Terry, but Courtois sticks a leg out to make the save!
(81’) WIDE! Wasted opportunity for Chelsea. Fabregas sets up Drogba with a pass, who does very well to turn and create a chance for himself inside the area. He tries to drag a ball in at the far post, but scuffs it well wide!
(79’) Sunderland are keeping possession well themselves as we approach the last 10 minutes. They work the ball around well in the final third, but Chelsea are giving them very little room to maneuver. The fans are behind them in full force now, as they search for a winner!
(77’) Double substitution for Chelsea as Loic Remy and Didier Drogba are introduced, with Diego Costa and Oscar giving way. It is a positive change from Mourinho. The Ivorian has an impact just second after coming on, testing Pantilimon with his shot from distance.
--- 76’ Substitution L. Rémy enters the game and replaces Diego Costa. ---
--- 76’ Substitution Oscar is done for the day. D. Drogba is his replacement. ---
--- 75’ Yellow card J. O'Shea receives a yellow card. ---
(75’) Important defensive header from Matic! Sunderland win a corner, and Larsson delivers it in well. He sends it into a dangerous area, but Matic is back to head it away. Costa looks to break quickly, but gets taken down from behind by O'Shea, who is shown a yellow card.
(73’) The Sunderland fans are growing belief, as is the team! You can hear the anticipation building inside the stadium as they are less than 20 minutes away from stealing points from the league leaders. They will have to be on top of their game if they are to see this one out, as even a brief lapse in concentration could prove to be their undoing.
(71’) WONDERFUL SHOT! Wickham with more individual brilliance, as he dribbles his way towards the centre, and out of nothing, unleashes a drive towards goal. There is plenty of movement behind it, and some real power, but Courtois manages to knock it down before collecting.
(69’) STAT ATTACK: There have been 18 second half goals scored in the last six meetings between these two teams at the Stadium of Light, including eight in the last 20 minutes of those matches.
(67’) POWERFUL HIT! Matic collects a ball about 25 yards out, and immediately looks towards goal. He gets his powerful shot through the mess of bodies and forces Pantilimon into a rather uncomfortable save. Chelsea still cannot find a way through at the moment, with all their attempts coming from distance.
(65’) Free kick to Sunderland as Ivanovic is penalized for a foul on Wickham. The Sunderland forward's work rate has been exceptional, and he is causing Chelsea all sorts of problems. Encouraging stuff from him, which has earned a number of cheers from the home fans.
(63’) Sunderland make their first two substitutions, and it is Fletcher and Rodwell who will come off. On in their place are Jordi Gomez and American striker Jozy Altidore. He should provide the hosts with some much needed fresh legs in attack, helping to revitalize their play on the counter.
--- 62’ Substitution J. Altidore enters the game and replaces S. Fletcher. ---
--- 62’ Substitution J. Rodwell is done for the day. Jordi Gómez is his replacement. ---
(61’) The game is becoming incredibly stretched, which has made for some excellent viewing. Back and forth they go at the Stadium of Light, with an electrifying pace and wonderful atmosphere adding to the excitement. Into the final 30 minutes, who, if anyone, will find a breakthrough?
(59’) APPEALS FOR A PENALTY! Wonderful cross into the area by Wickham, which is met by Johnson at the far post. His header back across goal is blocked by Azpilicueta, and the Sunderland players are shouting for a handball. Nothing is given, and the replay shows it is the right call, as the ball never even struck the arm of the left-back.
(57’) The game is heating up now, as emotions run high. Chelsea are back in attack, working the ball around well near the penalty area. Fabregas gets on the end of a bouncing ball, but his half volley is stopped easily by Pantilimon.
--- 55’ Yellow card Diego Costa gets yellow. ---
(55’) Sunderland are furious with Kevin Friend, as Diego Costa is shown a yellow card for what they feel was an elbow to the face of Wes Brown. The Black Cats players are still perhaps upset over the kick back in the first half, but this time around there was little in the coming together. The contact appeared to be accidental. With the yellow card, Diego Costa will be suspended for the midweek clash with Tottenham.
(53’) STAT ATTACK: Chelsea have set a club record by remaining unbeaten through 12 league matches to start the season. They would equal a Premier League record for the best start to a campaign with a victory today.
(51’) THUMPING EFFORT! Oscar picks out Willian atop the penalty area. The Brazilian does well to elude his marker, Revelliere, and create space for a shot. He tries to pick out the near corner, but his effort squirts just wide.
(49’) NEARLY AN OPENER! Willian delivers the corner into a very dangerous area, and Cahill meets it. His header is directed towards goal with good power, but it is straight at Pantilimon who catches it on the line.
(48’) Chelsea get on the front foot and win an early corner. The Black Cats deal with the threat, but the pressure remains. Matic sends a fine ball through for Willian, with Revelliere intervening to nudge the ball it behind.
(46’) Chelsea kick off and the second half is underway! There are no changes from either side to tell you about at the break.
Chelsea need to bring more width to their game in the second half. They did well to attack the flanks early on, but it got away from them, as they started to stat in the middle of the pitch. Sunderland did a good job to take away space in the centre, with Chelsea failing to make an adjustment.
HALF TIME: SUNDERLAND 0-0 CHELSEA. We remain scoreless at the break, but it certainly has been an entertaining opening 45 minutes in Tyne and Wear. The sides exchanged chances, both being kept out by the woodwork. Poyet will have to be thrilled with his side's performance thus far, but it is all still to play for in the second half!
(45’) That will do it, as Kevin Friend sounds his whistle to signal the end of the first half at the Stadium of Light.
(45’) HOW IS HE STILL ON?! John O'Shea takes down Costa with a tug in midfield, and the striker kicks out at him from the ground. It certainly looked like he lost his head for a moment, but the referee does not think so, perhaps with his vision impeded by the angle he was at, as both players escape with only a warning. That could have been much, much worse for Costa.
(44’) The teams exchange free kicks in midfield, as the pace slows a bit with half time rapidly approaching. Chelsea are finding it very difficult to break into the final third at the moment, and when they do, there is little to no space for them to operate in.
(42’) STAT ATTACK: Sunderland have drawn seven of their 12 Premier League matches this season, two more than any other team in the top flight. Four of their ties have come at the Stadium of Light, compared to just one win and one defeat.
(40’) The corner is dealt with, but pressure is kept on by the Black Cats, as Johnson wins a throw near the corner flag. They give it away carelessly, however, and Cattermole is penalized for a foul on Hazard which helps relieve the pressure on the Chelsea goal.
(38’) Chelsea get back in possession, but they are experiencing much less time on the ball than they were in the early stages. A good interception wins the ball back for Sunderland, and Wickham again gets forward on the break, this time winning his side a corner.
(36’) Spectacular stuff from Wickham, who dances his way around near the corner flag to win the hosts a throw. He was lacking much in terms of support, but you can just see the tide turning a bit, as Sunderland begin to grow in confidence with 10 minutes to go until the break.
(34’) OFF THE BAR! Oh how close that was for Sunderland! The hosts win a free kick from 30 yards out, and though the original cross is dealt with, they keep the pressure on. Cattermole gets it on the right and sends a brilliant pass into the box for Vergini, who takes the chance first time, lifting it over Courtois but off the crossbar!
(32’) SPECTACULAR SAVE! Sumptuous build up from Chelsea, as Matic and Willian link up, with the latter sending a one touch pass in for Ivanovic. The defender is clean through on goal, but Pantilimon stretches himself wide to keep the game scoreless!
(30’) WONDERFUL CROSS! Wickham sends a splendid ball into the box, which Courtois can not deal with as he comes out to claim it. Fabregas tries to carry it clear, and Johnson wins it back with a handball, which brings the attack to an end, as Chelsea are awarded a free kick.
(29’) A chorus of boos is heard around the stadium as both Adam Johnson and Steven Fletcher are taken down in midfield, preventing Sunderland from hitting Chelsea on the counter. Neither are called, however, by referee Kevin Friend, which has Gus Poyet absolutely livid in the technical area.
(27’) STAT ATTACK: There have been 29 goals scored between these two teams in their last six league matches at the Stadium of Light, averaging just shy of five per game. Chelsea have 19 of those, compared to 10 from Sunderland.
(25’) Encouraging sign for Sunderland, as Rodwell finds himself a bit of space in midfield, driving forward before having a go at goal. He gets his shot on target from 30 yards out, but he will need something spectacular to beat Courtois from that range.
(23’) BRILLIANT CHALLENGE! Fabregas sends an exquisite ball forward for Costa, who looks to have a clear path towards goal. John O'Shea does incredibly well to make up ground, before sliding in to break up the chance. Great stuff from the centre-back.
(21’) Nemanja Matic looks to have picked up a knock after a coming together in midfield with Seb Larsson. The Sunderland player walks away with only a warning, but he has the right idea in trying to get close to the Serbian and make him feel just a bit uncomfortable on the ball.
(19’) Chelsea are queuing up now, as Sunderland play with fire. Their midfielders are not getting anywhere near close enough to Matic and Fabregas, who are keeping the visitors in possession, and starting them on the front foot. Oscar has a go again from just outside the area, as bodies pile up inside the box, but this time his effort is blocked by a teammate as the Black Cats scramble clear.
(17’) OFF THE WOODWORK! Fantastic strike by Willian, as Sunderland struggle to get back in defence and get their shape. Hazard tees up the Brazilian, who rings his effort off the post from 25 yards out.
(15’) Wonderful pressing from Wickham and Fletcher high up the pitch, which forces Courtois to put the ball out for a throw, earning quite the applause from the home supporters. That is what Sunderland have to do if they are to be successful today. They cannot afford to give Chelsea time and space in possession, or they will, at one point or another, be picked apart.
(13’) Costa does a wonderful job of drifting deep to get on the ball. He holds off Vergini to allow support to arrive, starting another Chelsea attack. Oscar weaves his way around the top of the area, eventually firing a shot towards goal, but Pantamilion is able to get across to make the save, with the aid of a slight deflection.
(11’) STAT ATTACK: Chelsea are unbeaten through 19 matches this season across all competitions, and have scored at least one goal in each of those games. They are the only Premier League team yet to lose so far this campaign.
(9’) A careless giveaway by John Terry puts unnecessary pressure on the Chelsea back line. Sunderland pounce on the mistake, working the ball to Wickham on the left, but his shot sails over the bar, much to the relief of the Blues' captain.
(7’) Great block! Chelsea win a corner, which Sunderland manage to clear, only partially. Terry rushes onto the loose ball just outside the area, and tries to drive a low shot through the mess of bodies in the box, but Lee Cattermole bravely flings himself in front of it to turn the chance away.
(5’) Lovely passing from Chelsea in the final third, as they wait for an opening. They are not rushing anything, but instead waiting for a Sunderland defender to fall asleep before taking advantage. Willian makes a smart run into the area, and Fabregas chips a ball over the top for him, but it runs to Pantilimon who relieves the pressure.
(3’) It has been a patient start to the match for Chelsea, as they try and feel the hosts out in possession. They are in no rush to push the ball forward into attack, instead getting everyone a touch on the ball in these early stages.
(1’) Sunderland kick off and we are underway at the Stadium of Light! The hosts, moving left to right, are wearing their red and white striped tops, with Chelsea sporting their classic blue kits.
The players have made their way through the tunnel and out onto the pitch. Handshakes are exchanged and the teams take their place, as we get set for kick-off.

Sunderland have been a bit of a hard team to beat this season, but have also found it quite difficult to win. The Black Cats are drawing games at a staggering rate, and while that is better than the alternative, they have to start picking up victories to distance themselves from the drop zone. Gus Poyet has earned a bit of a reputation of being able to beat the big teams since taking over as Sunderland manager, but Chelsea have been a whole other monster of late.
Chelsea are flying high as ever at the moment, holding a six point lead atop the Premier League, while clinching first place in the Champions League group with a 5-0 victory over Schalke in Germany on Tuesday. They have an impeccable record at the Stadium of Light in recent years, and with a full squad at Jose Mourinho's disposal, there is no reason for them not to continue that trend on the night.

And that's that in Southampton. Manchester City show Southampton that they still have much to learn as they bid to finish in the Champions League spots. Pellegrini's men produced an extremely professional display and deserve their victory, with Toure, Lampard and Clichy getting the goals. A red card for Managala had put their position in doubt, but Pellegrini's tweaks worked perfectly. City leap above Southampton and up to second.
(90’) FULL-TIME!
(90’) Southampton are throwing plenty of players forward at the moment, but these late efforts will prove to be futile. City have victory assured and any goal will be nothing more than a consolation.
(90’) There will be five minutes added on here.
(90’) This match does end on a slight sour note for City now as Kompany is forced off with a bit of a knock. He doesn't look too shaken, though. Nevertheless, the visitors are now momentarily down to nine men as they have used up all of their substitutions.
--- 88’ Assist The assist came from S. Agüero. ---
--- 88’ Goal! GOAL!!! GAME OVER! City finish this match off as Gael Clichy gets his first goal for the club! Lampard does well to play Aguero into the left side of the penalty area and his pass in towards the goalmouth is perfect, with the full-back arriving late to blast home. ---
(86’) SO CLOSE FOR SAINTS! Excellent play by Long as the forward exploits space behind Zabaleta and plays a fine pass into the danger zone with the outside of his right foot. Pelle can't quite reach it, though.
(85’) WHAT A CHANCE FOR CITY! Aguero races on to a hopeful ball from the back and he finds himself one-on-one with Forster, who had seemingly learned from his mistake against Aston Villa as he opted to stay in his area. The Argentinian attempted to knock the ball past the goalkeeper, but he does well to block the ball at the striker's feet.
(83’) Tadic's delivery is better than most of his previous attempts, but it is still too high for all of his team-mates, including Long at the back post. City, meanwhile, continue to look a threat on the counter.
--- 82’ Substitution E. Mayuka enters the game and replaces S. Davis. ---
(82’) On comes Mayuka now as Koeman throws on an extra striker. Davis departs.
(82’) Kompany is the latest to enter the referee's book as he fould long out on the left. This is a good opportunity for a Southampton attack here, though their set-pieces have hardly inspired much confidence today.
--- 81’ Yellow card V. Kompany is yellow-carded. ---
--- 80’ Assist The assist came from J. Milner. ---
--- 80’ Goal! GOAL!!! CITY GET THEIR SECOND! Southampton had been pushing men forward in a desperate attempt to find an equaliser and the visitors pick them off. Milner does well on the left and calmly squares the ball to Lampard on the edge of the area, and the former Chelsea man blasts low past Forster. Game over? ---
(78’) City not far off from getting a second goal there as Aguero picks out a clever pass to find Fernandinho in the right side of the Southampton area. His eventual shot crashes into the side-netting, however.
(77’) Southampton's immediate advantage is wasted as Tadic fires the free-kick straight into the wall, but the hosts remain on the front foot as they search a late equaliser.
--- 76’ Substitution M. Demichelis enters the game and replaces Jesús Navas. ---
(76’) Pellegrini responds to that sending off by introducing Demichelis. Navas is forced to make way.
(74’) Good play by Navas as he bursts inside Bertrand to beat the left-back to the ball, catching the former Chelsea man out of position. The Spanish winger gets a shot away from 20 yards, but he drags his effort wide of the far post. Shooting never has been his strong point!
(74’) RED CARD! Southampton have a lifeline! Managala is sent off for City! Toure is caught in possession about 35 yards from his own goal, playing his team-maes into a desperate situation. Managal is forced to barge Long to the ground and he is given a second yellow card. Off goes the Frenchman!

(72’) More poor defending from Southampton at a corner. For the second consecutive Milner delivery, City are able to produce a near-post flick-on. This time it is Mangala to nods the ball on into the danger zone, though City cannot capitalise.
(71’) City have done a very professional job since taking the lead. The introduction of Milner for Jovetic has helped the visitors become a little more secure in midfield and they have hardly given Southampton a sniff of a chance since going ahead.
(69’) SAINTS ESCAPE SOMEHOW! What a chance for City. Milner's excellent corner is flicked on by Kompany at the near post and, although Managala can't knock it in, Aguero is on hand. He, however, can't find the net either, though, with the Argentinian stabbing over from five yards.
--- 68’ Substitution S. Long comes on for S. Mané. ---
(68’) And now Southampton make a change, with Long taking the place of Mane, who has not been particularly effective today.
(66’) Here is Pellegrini's latest throw of the dice, as Lampard comes on for Nasri.
--- 65’ Substitution F. Lampard enters play, replacing S. Nasri. ---
(65’) There's another unimpressive set-piece delivery from Southampton. Davis' free-kick from the left does manage to beat the first man, but Nasri is right behind him and he heads clear. Another wasted opportunity.
(64’) Free-kick to Saints now out on the left. Mane is pulled back and dragged down by Zabaleta as he looked to race on to Pelle's first-time throughball, with the City man escaping a yellow card.
(63’) Well, not on this occasion. Tadic plays his left-footed delivery into the area, but it barely beats the first man and City clear their lines. The hosts' set-piece deliveries really have been exceptionally erratic today.
(61’) City clear the corner, but Southampton remain on the front foot and swiftly win another, as Davis' cross is deflected behind by a City defender. Can they make this pressure count?
(60’) Corner for Southampton! Tadic tries to make things happen as he comes in off the right. Kompany puts in a tackle on him, with the ball then flying up into the air. The Serbian knocks it through towards Pelle, but Navas nods behind.
(58’) Good play by Wanyama as the Kenyan gets possession in the midfield and charges forward. Fernandinho comes across in an attempt to clear the danger, but the Southampton man bursts past him anyway and sends an effort just over from 30 yards.
(56’) Managala meets Nasri's corner delivery at the near post and, although he does manage to get a header away, his effort ultimately rolls back out towards his compatriot, who can't avoid the ball going out for a goal-kick.

--- 84’ Substitution G. Dorrans is done for the day. J. Morrison is his replacement. ---

(82’) West Brom have did quite well to weather the Chelsea storm in this second half but they could make it a shaky last few minutes for the home side of they were to grab a goal soon. It all depends on how ambitious they want to be, but this afternoon could have went a lot worse.
(80’) Chelsea follow suit and make a substitution of their own; their first of the game. Oscar walks of the pitch to a warm applause from the home crowd and he'll be replaced by Loic Remy, who is given 10 minutes to get on the scoresheet.

(77’) We've got a little break in play at the moment as Costa is down after an aerial collision with Dawson. Looked like a sore one, but the Brazilian should be okay. Don't dish it out if you can't take it, Diego!
--- 75’ Yellow card Willian receives a yellow card. ---
(75’) That is such a silly booking for Willian. The Brazilian, who rightfully receives plenty of plaudits for his tracking back, earns a booking for a late challenge on Gamboa near the touchline. Completely needless.
(73’) Well we've got just under 15 minutes remaining here and it would be fair to say that both sets of supporters have the right to feel slightly aggrieved at the second half performance of their respective sides. West Brom have looked more solid but have showed zero attacking ambition, and Chelsea should have put on more of a show considering their scoreline and man advantage at the break.
(71’) Great save again from Foster! Fabregas pulls the strings again as he receives the ball on the edge of the box before threading a lovely pass through the middle for Hazard. The Belgian looks to lift the ball over the oncoming keeper, who ends up making another important block!
(69’) Ivanovic shows his attacking ambition once again as he drives into the final third and eventually into the box. On this occasion though he should be more selfish as he opts to pass inside to Costa rather than having a crack at goal. West Brom eventually clear the danger.
--- 68’ Substitution C. Gamboa enters play, replacing C. Baird. ---
(67’) First change of the match and it comes from West Brom. Baird comes off and he'll be replaced by Cristian Gamboa, who will come on at left-back, which will probably trigger Wisdom moving across to right.
(65’) Without putting down the performance of West Brom too much, it is rather incredible the amount of Chelsea possession we have seen in this second period. The Baggies may be a man down, but they are lucky if they have seen 20% of the ball since the break.
(63’) It looks as if Victor Anichebe may be entering the action. It is some rather unorthodox warming up by the former Everton striker though as he lies on the ground and moves his legs in the air. The West Brom fans will be needing a lie down too after this that's for sure!

(59’) Despite what they are up against, the West Brom players seem to be having a contest as to who can hit the highest row in the stand with a shot. The latest candidate is Brunt, who just about hits row Z with a strike from 30 yards.
(57’) Hazard drifts in from his position on the left in an attempt to find some possession. He ends up going beyond the West Brom defence, who trigger their offside trap. If the visitors had did that in the lead up to the first goal the game could have been different!
(55’) You wonder what kind of team talk Alan Irvine must have given to his players at half time, as they as stuck between a rock and a hard place at the moment. At 2-0 they have a small chance of getting something out of the game, but if they go forward they risk conceding further goals. A heavy defeat certainly wouldn't be great for morale, so is it damage limitations?
(53’) Ivanovic has been at his marauding best down the right-hand side today and once again he gets forward and hits the byline. He looks for Costa with a wicked cross inside but the West Brom defence do enough to smuggle behind for a goal kick.
(51’) Saaaaaaaaaave by Foster! Terry gets the better of his marker inside the West Brom box and rises high to power a header down towards goal, but the goalkeeper remains solid to beat the attempt away!
(49’) You have to feel for Berahino a bit. The West Brom striker looks to take the initiative by darting towards the Chelsea defence, but suddenly finds himself surrounded by FIVE opposition players, and eventually surrenders possession. He needs some support up top.
(47’) MATIC!! How has he missed that one! The former Benfica midfielder holds his position at the back post and latches on to a cross on the volley, but sends his attempt over the bar. He had bags of time to take the ball down and pick his spot! Dorrans completely left his man!
(46’) We are back under way in this Barclays Premier League clash!
Half time in Stamford Bridge. Chelsea would have been approaching the match today expecting a rather tough match against a usually rigid West Brom side, but they have split open the Baggies' defence time and time again and head into the break at 2-0. Diego Costa opened the scoring and Hazard made it two a few minutes before Claudio Yacob was sent off, further complicating the task for Alan Irvine's men. Expect Chelsea to go on and grab a couple more goals in the second half!
(45’) Dear, oh dear. Berahino somehow manages to top Gardner's poor shot a few moments ago by sending a strike even higher into the stand. Fair enough it was on his left foot, but he should be doing better than that. The Englishman cutting a frustrated figure at the moment.
(43’) Great goalkeeping by Foster! Hazard swings an excellent pass in between Dawson and Lescott and Costa run through on goal, but the Brazilian's shot is charged down by the West Brom keeper, who eventually pounces on the loose possession!
(41’) Chelsea should be three up! The home side split the West Brom defence open with a superb move and Ivanovic runs through on goal before unselfishly squaring for Azpilicueta, but the pass was just behind the Spaniard! The two full backs were the players furthest forward for the hosts!
(39’) Hazard strays in from the left wing and looks to make a run in behind the West Brom defence. Fabregas spots the run and attempts to dink a pass over the top, but is just intercepted by Dawson. Almost a brilliant move by Chelsea!
(37’) Well it has all been pretty grim for West Brom so far. Their performance so far is summed up by Gardner getting into a decent position on the edge of the box, only to slice a half volley way over the bar into the stand. Not his best.
(35’) Cheeky from Oscar! The Brazilian receives the ball to feet inside the box around 10 yards out and attempts to backheel a strike into the corner. In the end the attempt takes a deflection on the way through which makes it easier for Foster to get down and collect. An A for the idea!
(33’) Hazard goes on a signature run down the left-hand side as he twists and turns and looks to find a way into the penalty area. Dorrans is back helping out Wisdom at full-back, but ends up giving away a rather needless free kick.
(31’) This could prove to be a very, very long afternoon for West Brom if this keeps up. Two goals down and a man down with more than an hour to play! Chelsea smell blood...
--- 29’ Red card! C. Yacob goes off after a red card! ---
(29’) Yacob SENT OFF for West Brom! Chelsea enjoy a period of possession on the edge of the box and the ball comes to Costa, who is completely taken out by the Argentine, who comes in two-footed! Can't really argue with that one! Alan Irvine looks crestfallen on the bench!
(27’) Brunt looks to claw his side back into the match by collecting possession in midfield and driving forward. He spots a space in the left corner and attempts to curl a strike past Courtois, but the Belgian gets down to make the comfortable stop.
(26’) Really poor defending again from West Brom! Hazard had the freedom of the penalty box to take a touch and get his shot away!
--- 25’ Assist Fàbregas gave the assist. ---
--- 25’ Goal! GOOOOOAAAAAAAAAAALLLLLLL FOR CHELSEA!! THAT'S TWO!! Hazard latches on to a low corner kick to the front post and takes one touch before squeezing a left-footed strike past Foster! Two-nil! ---
(23’) Cahill and Terry's reading of the game has been excellent so far. Lescott in particular is aiming to come out of the West Brom defence to fizz passes into the feet of Sessegnon and Berahino, but the Chelsea duo intercept time and time again. No joy in the final third for the visitors as of yet.
(21’) West Brom just can't gain any ascendancy in their play at the moment. They are being allowed some room at the back to pop some passes around, but whenever possession comes into the middle of the park they lose the tempo and accuracy in their balls.
(19’) Costaaaaa! Chelsea should be two up! Ivanovic typically gallops forward down the right-hand side and teases a superb cross in to his team-mate at the front post, who can't get a good enough connection on a strike to turn the ball towards goal!
(17’) Perhaps predictably, that goal by Costa has gave Chelsea plenty of confidence on the ball. Fabregas and Matic are becoming more prominent in the middle of the park now and it is contributing to the hosts' domination of the ball.
(15’) A corner kick is cleared out of the box by West Brom but Chelsea manage to recycle back into the danger area. Cahill latches on to a loose ball on the edge of the box and looks to get a strike away, but he is put off slightly by the important challenge of Yacob. The shot goes wide in the end.
(13’) West Brom have prided themselves on their organisation so far this season but they just lost concentration at the vital moment, and Chelsea, to their credit, pounced. The Baggies will need to show a little more going forward now!
(12’) Slight suspicions of offside about that goal, but looking at it closely it seems as if Costa was played ONSIDE by Wisdom at right-back!
--- 11’ Assist The assist came from Oscar. ---
--- 11’ Goal! GOOOOOOAAAAAALLLLL FOR CHELSEAAAA! THE HOSTS TAKE THE LEAD! Oscar is involved positively once again as he collects the ball on the left wing and checks back before swinging a cross into the box. Diego Costa chests down before smashing a strike past Foster! Where was the West Brom defence there! One-nil! ---
(10’) Oscar has already sprayed one or two absolutely superb diagonal crosses to the advanced Ivanovic on the right wing. However, on this occasion the Brazilian gets his bearings wrong and screws the pass wayward.
(8’) Sessegnon collects the ball around 30 yards out and takes a few strides forward before lashing a right-footed strike at goal. It was struck decently, but ends up flashing by the post, not giving Courtois a problem. Positive play from the West Brom man though!
(6’) What a save by Ben Foster!!! A cross is floated in to the back post and headed back into the danger area by a Chelsea outside the six yard box. Terry looks to strike home from close range but the West Brom keeper somehow makes the block on the line! How did that not go in?!
(4’) Good defending from Lescott. The former Manchester City man certainly has his hands full with the powerful Diego Costa today, but in the first duel between the duo he comes out on top with an important interception inside the West Brom box.
(3’) It has been a tentative start to the match here in London as both sides just find their feet in terms of their passing. A few long punts up top but they have been successfully gobbled up by each defence.

(66’) CHANCE! James again gets in-behind Sunderland's defence and gets a shot away, but the ex-Manchester United man's drive went straight at Pantilimon.
(65’) BLOCK! Sunderland move the ball from one side to the other nicely before Gomez's shot was well blocked again by Morgan. The Leicester defender has put his body on the line for his side today.
(62’) Larsson is a very lucky man to have not received his marching orders after another cynical foul in the middle of the park. Sunderland need to calm down or they will be reduced to 10 men.

(61’) Cattermole picks up a yellow card and De Laet's deep free-kick comes to no avail.
(59’) Vardy and Cattermole are sharing a few words with each other after the Sunderland man catches Cambiasso with a dangerous tackle. The midfielder has only just returned from suspension for the Black Cats.
(57’) Sunderland have a free-kick from a similar range to the one Larsson scored against Everton in their last Premier League match. The Swedish midfielder and Johnson are both standing over it.

(53’) FOUL! Vardy catches Cattermole late with a nasty challenge. Free-kick to Sunderland, who have looked dangerous from set-pieces all afternoon.
(51’) CHANCE! James found himself with a bit of space just inside the box after Ulloa's knockdown and drove a shot right down the throat of Pantilimon. Corner to Leicester.
(50’) Sunderland again nick possession off Leicester in the middle of midfield and break forward in numbers, but Gomez's pass just couldn't find Fletcher.
(48’) CHANCE! Fletcher again heavily involved for Sunderland but the former Burnley forward couldn't sort his feet out inside the Leicester box.
(47’) Sunderland win an early corner in the second-half after Gomez broke through midfield and had his shot blocked by Wasilewski.

HALF-TIME! Leicester and Sunderland are both still level with the score 0-0 after a lively first 45 minutes from both sides. The Black Cats definitely had the best chances to break the deadlock.
(45’) The officials have indicated there will be one minute of stoppage time added onto the first-half. Leicester have had just one shot on target so far and Sunderland have had the better chances to draw first blood.

(43’) Leicester have started to get a foothold in the game once more after a spell of difficulty. Sunderland have a throw in with Reveillere.

(40’) Leicester whip in a corner and Ulloa heads just over the bar after Brown failed to clear the ball far enough.
(38’) Sunderland are turning the screw with seven minutes to play in this first-half. Leicester's early pressure has faded and they're struggling to keep hold of possession.
(37’) ALMOST!! Sunderland again come close to taking the lead after Fletcher latches onto a wonderful ball by Cattermole to feed Larsson, whose shot was well blocked by Morgan.
(35’) Wickham is causing Leicester's defence a number of problems in this first-half and wins a corner for Sunderland after some neat play down the left.
(34’) Rain is pouring down onto the pitch and players are starting to lose their footing a lot more often. Sunderland have a free-kick after Gomez was fouled. Larsson is standing over it.
(33’) The noise levels inside the King Power Stadium are still sky high as both teams continue to create openings to break the deadlock.

(31’) Larsson whips in a renowned clinical ball from the corner and Leicester's zonal marking was almost caught out, but Fletcher couldn't get any contact on the ball. Still 0-0.

(28’) CHANCE! Ulloa drifts out onto the left and floats a ball into Mahrez, who spins Brown and goes down inside the box under no contact.

(24’) FOUL! Sunderland have a good chance to float the ball into the box and test Leicester further after Morgan brought down Wickham.

(21’) HUGE SAVE!! Schmeichel keeps the scores level after making a brilliant save to deny Fletcher a fifth goal of the season inside the six-yard box. Corner to Sunderland.

(17’) Leicester are looking strong every time they manage to break beyond the middle of the pitch and into the attacking third. Mahrez and Vardy have both been dangerous so far.
