Thank you very much for joining me, Alex Stewart, for this LIVE Premier League encounter, which finished Manchester City 2-1 Swansea City. Until next time — have a lovely rest of the weekend.
City rode their luck at times, especially towards the end, when Swansea pressed hard for an equalizer. Serious credit has to go to Garry Monk's team for refusing to lie down and settle for the result, but City's superior class and physicality told in the end.
The Swansea goalkeeper was in excellent form, pushing a rasping shot from Clichy onto the post and saving well from Jovetic and Aguero too. He looked assured under crosses and could not be blamed for either goal.
City shot back through Jovetic's side-footed volley from a Navas cross, pretty much the only thing of merit the Spanish winger did all day, before Yaya Toure made sure of the points with a lovely, forecful run and finish under Fabianski.
Manchester City made life hard for themselves. Wilfred Bony scored a lovely goal to open the scoring for the Swans, with a sly sidefoot past Hart after a clever ball from Dyer.
(90’) And that's that. Manuel Pellegrini straightens his tie with some relief on the touchline. His team had some genuine scares towards the end but goals from Jovetic and Toure were enough. It finishes Manchester City 2-1 Swansea City.
(90’) The seconds are dribbling away now. City have had to fight long and hard towards the end of this game, having never managed to use their large passages of total dominance in the first half to real effect.
(90’) Gomis is caught offside at the other end. City come again through Toure and Milner. They manage to eat up valuable time before a Toure back-heel sets Milner free in the box. Fabianski gathers and tries to launch a counter.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card M. Demichelis is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) It's Shelvey and it's deflected horribly off the wall but just fails to creep into the goal past a stranded Hart. That was very unlucky for the away team.
(89’) Toure does well to bring the ball in from the right across the top of the box but fires his shot into the gut of Fabianski. There will be a minimum of four minutes of extra time. Swansea have a free-kick on the edge of the City box but no Sigurdsson to take it.
--- 88’ Substitution Fernando comes on for Fernandinho. ---
(88’) Barrow has bags of pace and energy but his end product comes to nothing. At the other end, Aguero uses his strength to hold off Williams and drives towards the goal, but flashes his shot high and wide.
(87’) Milner finds Navas well and the winger has time to pick a cross but, once again, fails to do so. Zabaleta tries a shot from the rebound but nothing comes of it. Fernando is coming on for Fernandinho which is basically swapping one lump for a slightly bigger lump.
(85’) City have a head of steam up now, though, and Milner has a good shot blocked. But, at the other end, Gomis is suddenly in space and, closed rapidly by Hart, pokes the ball wide. This game is at full tilt now.
(84’) You have to admire Swansea for still going after the result here. The pace of Barrow and presence of Bony and Gomis will ensure they get a couple of chances before the end of this game. Monk is such a positive manager.
(82’) FABIANKSI! Another superb save from the Pole, this time with his feet as Aguero combines with Navas to create a shooting chance for the Spaniard. That the away team are still in this match is pretty much solely down to their keeper.
(81’) A great, low, sweeping ball from Barrow should find Gomis charging in on it but the French striker decides to pull wide now rather than attack the box and nothing comes from it. Barrow is very quick. Shelvey wastes a shooting chance at the apex of the penalty box after a Gomis knock-down.
(80’) Gomis and Bony up front together is a pretty frightening prospect, it must be said. Kompany and Demichelis will have to be on their mettle, especially as they are both marking me now, rather than one being spare.
--- 79’ Substitution G. Sigurðsson is done for the day. B. Gomis is his replacement. ---
--- 79’ Substitution J. Milner comes on for S. Nasri. ---
(78’) Changes ahoy! Gomis is on for Sigurdsson to provide more of a threat up front and, for City, dependable James Milner is on for Nasri. Gomis got the winner for the Swans against Arsenal.
--- 77’ Substitution M. Barrow enters play, replacing N. Dyer. ---
(76’) Nathan Dyer, who provided the subtle assist for Bony's goal, is off for the young striker Barrow, about whom I know nothing. The corner comes to nothing, by the way.
(75’) Clichy crosses but it's just too high for Lampard. Ki and Bony try to break but Demichelis steps up confidently to intercept. Swansea come again though and Ki wins a corner as he aims for Bony.
(74’) For all City's dominance, they are still capable of rushing their play too much and giving the ball away cheaply. There is a fragility to the team that Swansea do have a sliver of hope of exploiting.
(72’) Sigurdsson has a free-kick in a dangerous position as a Swansea break is cynically stopped. He is a real danger from this range, but the ball wafts through the City wall and dribbles wide.
--- 70’ Substitution S. Jovetić is replaced with F. Lampard. ---
(70’) A lazy pass from Shelvey gifts the ball back to City. Lampard is playing off Aguero, it appears, so don't be surprised if he gets in among the goals. Zabaleta blazes over from wide right after a pass from Toure.
(68’) Jovetic slides the ball into Aguero who shows great strength and tenancity to drag the ball left and fashion a cross back inside. As has happened all too often, though, the move peters out with a poor Navas pass. Lampard is coming on for Jovetic. Dzeko aside, Lampard is City's supersub.
--- 67’ Substitution T. Carroll is done for the day. J. Shelvey is his replacement. ---
(67’) Aguero fouls Williams in the away team's box to reliev some pressure. Will Monk's change help too? That remains to be seen.
(66’) A rare period of Swansea possession here, interrupted by a foul which gives it back to City. Shelvey is on for Carroll.
(64’) Another fine block from Aguero's shot on the turn. Swansea are throwing themselves at this at the moment, hanging on for their lives. Monk is readying changes as he attempts to stop the City onslaught.
--- 62’ Assist The assist came from Fernandinho. ---
--- 62’ Goal! TOURE! He can turn it on like very few other players. From the resulting corner Bony clears it partially but City come again after Carroll's pass is intercepted. Toure swaggers past two white-shirted defenders and slides it under the onrushing Fabianski. He made it look very easy. ---
(62’) Who will Swansea adjust now? They've been under so much pressure they may have forgotten how to attack this City team, who they made look vulnerable for parts of the first half, let's not forget.
(59’) Fabianski saves well from Toure after some smart passing. The Pole almost spills the ball to Aguero but Bartley manages to smash it away.
(57’) Zabaleta makes room for himself in the box with a lovely first touch from Navas' pass and fires a half-volley over the bar. Swansea are barely in this game at the moment.
(56’) Montero concedes a corner from a Navas cross. The resulting set-piece is half-cleared but City come again. Swansea have no outlet even if they do win the ball back because everyone is currently back.
(54’) Swansea are again defending very deep and City have the freedom of the space in front of their penalty box. Navas makes a darting run and the Swans clear desperately.
(53’) Montero runs into the hulking frame of Toure and City attack. Swansea win it back though but Sigurdsson's pass is too heavy for Bony and the home side sweep up.
(52’) Jovetic should really have a yellow card for flopping tamely after a Williams challenge.
(51’) Sigurdsson stings the palms of Hart with a rising drive. At the other end Aguero forces a good block from Williams as the game opens up a bit.
(50’) After that small shock from Montero, City are exerting greater pressure once more. Swansea come back though, and now have a neat passage of passing.
(48’) Aguero flashes a shot hard and wide to the left as Fabianksi plunges to cover it. The Argentinian had far too much space there as the Swansea plays backed off him.
(47’) MONTERO! A fine, smothering block from Hart stops the dangerous left-winger from finding the net after a neat one-two with Bony. That was Swansea at their incisive, threatening best.
(46’) City have Swansea hemmed in already. Sigurdsson tries to clear but gives the ball back to the home team. That an attacking midfielder is back there defending shows just how deep the away team are having to defend.
(45’) And we're off for the start of the second half. City will be looking to use their first half momentum to put this game to bed. Swansea were grimly hanging on towards the end, but the away team look threatening on the break. This could go either way.
At half-time, then, it's Manchester City 1-1 Swansea City. Join me for the second half, LIVE, shortly!
Garry Monk will be grateful for the half-time whistle and the chance to regroup it offers. If he can get Swansea playing properly again then there's no reason why they cannot pose the home side problems. If Coty continue to hustle and disrupt, though, the Swans will find it very hard to get back into this game and City will use the momentum to score again.
The last twenty-five minutes of the first half saw Manchester City dominate but not manage to force in a second, largely due to the away team's Polsih keeper's excellent form.
City fought their way back and Jovetic scored with a close-range finish from Navas' cross. They've also forced Fabianski into a number of good saves, the fingertip turn onto the post from Clichy's fierce drive the pick of the bunch.
Well, well. Swansea started off with nothing of the ball but then worked their way into the game, scoring a beautifully deft goal through Wilfred Bony after Dyer's pass.
(45’) That's it for the first half, then. It's Manchester City 1-1 Swansea City!
(45’) Navas is knocked off the ball by Montero. One good cross aside, the Spaniard has been slightly off-the-boil today and dithers too often when in good positions.
(45’) Sigurdsson is a clever player but he is not strong enough to carry the ball against the City midfield. The Swans are not making enough use of Bony. Fabianski saves well, again, from a long shot from Nasri that dipped.
(44’) Jovetic heads into the arms of Fabianski after a short, quick cross from Zabaleta. There will be three minutes of extra time, which is actually less than I would have thought. Swansea try to break but Sigurdsson is forced off the ball again.
(43’) That short passage of play aside, it's been all City of late. Swansea will be plraying for the half-time whistle but with the Aguero clash, Taylor's injury, and the standard faffing about, there will be a fair bit of extra time.
(42’) This is better from Swansea. Carroll is the pivot for a series of good passes but the away side cannot find that incisive pass and it all peters out.
(41’) Swansea just aren't keeping the ball. Every time they try to break they find themslesv buffeted by the big men of the City midfield and back four.
(39’) GLICHY! So close for the Frenchman who leathers it against the left-hand post after a beautifully worked move. City broke swiftly and Aguero laid it out for the onrushing fullback who was only denied by the woodwork. From the replays it looks like that was a fantastic Fabianski save!
(38’) City have had over 60% of the possession in this game, and much of that will have been in the last twenty minutes. Since the Jovetic goal they've been almost totally in control and Hart has not had a save to make.
(37’) Dyer shows great strength and balance to take the ball down for such a small man. City press though and Ki eventually gets muscled off the ball. City counter but the move breaks down.
(35’) Sigurdsson is felled but doesn't win the free-kick. Swansea are on the back foot as City counter. They manage to force the home team back though and make time to regroup. Navas then crafts a great ball in for Aguero but Fabianksi does well to come out and block the shot. Good goalkeeping again.
(33’) Common sense appears to have prevailed there but Kyle Bartley needs to calm down a bit.
(32’) Aguero and Rangel clash off the ball. I have no idea what happened there but everyone seems very cross.Neil Swarbrick takes a conciliatory view and asks everyone to chill out a bit. He's right to. It appears that Aguero felt Bartley had knocked him down and Rangel ran over to argue with him.
--- 31’ Yellow card V. Kompany is cautioned by the referee. ---
(30’) Williams dinks the ball off Jovetic's foot as the goalscorer shapes to smash in a volley. That could well have been a second if he'd managed to connect. Kompany body-checks Bony as he looks to tear forwards and the Belgian is booked.
(29’) Toure wins a corner tussling with Ki. It's fed to the near post but cleared well. City retain possession and build from deep once more.
(27’) Ki and Dyer link well but Sigurdsson loses the ball to Clichy. Taylor is coming back on for the Swans, which will be a relief. Swansea desperately need to survive the next five minutes and then try to assert themselves a little. It's all City at the moment.
(26’) Fabianski gathers from Nasri's corner well. They need Taylor back on quickly as they are under the cosh.
(25’) Neil Taylor is bleeding heavily from a cut to his left eye socket. Kompany leapt into him to challenge for the ball but the contact appeared accidental and there was certainly no deliberate elbow. Taylor goes off to be patched up and City have a corner.
--- 24’ Yellow card K. Bartley is yellow-carded. ---
(24’) City have the resulting free-kick out wide on the left. It's taken short, possibly because City don't have much height up front at the moment. Swansea are able to break the attack down but give the ball away too easily.
(23’) Kyle Bartley knocks down Aguero needlessly and gets a yellow card for his troubles.
(21’) City are now able to play the high octane, physically aggressive style they're known for as Swansea drop back to regroup. Fabianski does very well to come out and claim a cross right on the edge of his box. No flappy hands there!
(20’) Nasri is now bustling around and there seems to be a greater energy about City after that goal. Aguero tries to streamroller though the Swansea back-line but they clear. This game is very much on.
--- 19’ Assist Jesús Navas gave the assist. ---
--- 19’ Goal! JOVETIC! Toure muscles in and releases Navas who delivers a teasing cross right across the front of goal. The Montenegran steals in and guides it past Fabianski. Very neat goal. It's 1-1! ---
(17’) Nasri does very well to find some space and then looks up to see no-one available for his cross.
(16’) The Swansea front four, especially Bony, work very hard to pressurise the City back four in possession. Bony does very well to win a throw, squeezing Zabaleta.
(14’) Dyer gives it away to Aguero but Carroll does well to disrupt the counter-attack and then tries to release Montero. Zabaleta hounds him and City win the ball back.

(11’) Swansea are playing with confidence and stroking it around. City really need to get a grip of this. Navas and Zabaleta try to give an attack some impetus but it peters out.
--- 9’ Assist The assist came from N. Dyer. ---
--- 9’ Goal! BONY! Oh that was a lovely, lovely goal. Dyer drifts inside and Bony times his run superbly, taking a lofted pass onto his chest then guiding the ball sweetly past Hart with his second touch. That was absolutely delightful. Manchester City 0-1 Swansea City! ---
(9’) Bony is just offside from Montero's through ball. City are just not working together at the back at the moment and Pellegrino must be fuming.
(7’) Aguero goes on a bullocking run but loses out. Swansea break quickly and Montero dinks in a cross towards Bony, but the ball is cleared.
(6’) Navas crosses well for Aguero but Williams clears. The home team are also playing very wide and getting into good crossing positions. Fabianski shanks out a clearance after a woeful back-pass.

(3’) Now it's Swansea's time to stroke the ball around. Bony holds the ball up well and looks to release Dyer. City interject through Kompany and Zabaleta though, and manage to clear. They can't old onto though, and Swanssea can build again.
(2’) Neither side have exactly settled into possession, but City start off better. Zabaleta finds Aguero wide right and the dangerman finds a sliver of space to fire wide.
(1’) And they're off! Both teams are in their standard kits and Swansea get us underway.

The Magpies have an outstanding head-to-head record having won five and lost none of the last six Premier League meetings with QPR. They will hope to continue that record today and pick up five consecutive victories for the first time since 2012.
Newcastle will need to be alert for Charlie Austin who is QPR's top scorer this season. The striker has scored five goals in his last six Premier League appearances including four in the last three.
Ayoze Perez is the man in form with three goals in the Premier League this season and each was a winning goal in Newcastle’s last three matches.
However, the away side will at least have been encouraged by their displays at home in recent weeks, beating Aston Villa 2-0 before then being unfortunate to only draw 2-2 with Manchester City in their last fixture.
The Magpies are looking to win five successive top flight games for the first time since April 2012 and Alan Pardew's side will be confident of achieving this against opposition that have really struggled on their travels. The west London club have the worst away record of any team in the Premier League, having failed to collect even a single point on the road so far this campaign and managing to score only two goals, while conceding 14 in five matches.
If Newcastle can win at home today it will be five Premier League victories in a row. Not even league leaders Chelsea have managed that this season. Joey Barton returns to St James’ Park with QPR as a resurgent Newcastle also aim to keep a fourth straight clean sheet.

Hi, good afternoon and welcome to our live text coverage of today’s Premier League clash between Stoke City and Burnley. I’m Kyle Hancox and I will be talking you through the action at the Britannia Stadium as both sides look to build on positive wins before the international break.

Despite being the better side for large periods, Arsenal fall victim to an efficient defensive performance from Man United, with De Gea in excellent form. Wenger's side continue to struggle slightly of late, while the Red Devils march on. That's all that we have time for from the Emirates, I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again next time.
FULL TIME! It's a very important win for Man United, who push up in search of European football, despite a poor start to the campaign. An own goal from Gibbs and a good finish from Rooney wrap up the three points, with a late Giroud consolation not enough for the Gunners.
(90’) Tempers flare once again, with the likes of Di Maria and Chambers getting involved in some bizarre off-the-ball antics. It appears to just be a ploy to waste time from the Argentine, but the referee will continue to keep an eye on his watch. Fellaini shoots from range, but Martinez collects.
--- 90’ +8 Yellow card O. Giroud gets yellow. ---
(90’) A nervy last couple of minutes for Man United now, with Di Maria taking the ball into the corner in an attempt to run down the clock. Had he managed to convert his earlier one-on-one opportunity, that would have been game over.
--- 90’ +7 Yellow card J. Wilson is cautioned by the referee. ---
--- 90’ +5 Assist Arteta gave the assist. ---
--- 90’ +5 Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! THEY'VE GOT ONE BACK! The former Montpellier man drives out to the left-hand side of the penalty area, before blasting a fantastic effort towards the near post! De Gea gets a hand to it, but can only push it into the top corner! ---
(90’) Man United are sitting very deep in their own half, with the vast majority of their personnel stationed in and around their penalty area. Sanchez whips in another corner delivery, but the visitors clear and break! Di Maria escapes and is in the clear, but clips a one-on-one effort way wide!
(90’) Despite the mammoth amount of added time, the Gunners look no more encouraged that they can get anything from this contest. Chambers breaks down the left and tries to deliver a cross, but it is hurriedly hacked away at the near post.
(90’) There are eight minutes of stoppage time.
--- 89’ Substitution D. Fletcher comes on for A. Young. ---
(89’) Young is substituted for the away side, with Fletcher brought into midfield to shore things up for the remaining minutes. Arsenal look entirely out of ideas, with Rooney's goal killing off any suggestions of a comeback.
(87’) Only a few minutes remain for Man United to see out, with the away fans delirious after Rooney's finish. It was a quick counter, but Arsenal have to really consider how easy it was for the Red Devils to exploit the space in behind.
--- 85’ Assist The assist came from Á. di María. ---
--- 85’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! ROONEY MAKES IT SAFE! The England international escapes on the break, as one of only two Man United players upfield, before clipping a finish over Martinez and into the back of the net! ---
(84’) Cazorla dribbles into the penalty area, before squaring a cross into Giroud! The Frenchman makes contact, but the ball ricochets into the air and clear! Man United are riding their luck tonight, that's for sure.
(82’) Things might be getting a little bit desperate soon for the Gunners, as the clock ticks down towards the 90 minute mark. Van Gaal's men are holding their shape and sitting deep, before allowing a select few to do their offensive running. It's all a matter of running down the seconds, now.
(80’) Sanchez uses quick feet around the edge of the box, before trying to clip a cross in towards the back post, but it is easily cleared. Arsenal are pressing forward in numbers, but Man United too have plenty of midfielders plugging the defensive gaps.
(78’) Giroud heads over! The former Montpellier man meets a corner delivery, but is unable to keep his effort down! The introduction of Giroud suggests that Arsenal are really going to go for it in the dying stages.
--- 77’ Substitution A. Ramsey is replaced with O. Giroud. ---
(76’) Less than a quarter of an hour remains for the Gunners to find an equaliser, with Wenger choosing to shuffle his pack. Ramsey is withdrawn, with Giroud thrown into the fray - which points towards a change of shape from the home side.
--- 75’ Substitution R. van Persie is done for the day. J. Wilson is his replacement. ---
(74’) Good tackle from Smalling! The Englishman tracks the run of Welbeck, before sliding in to dispossess the former Man United striker. Wilson is being readied on the sideline for the visitors, meanwhile.
(73’) Alexis lines up a free kick effort, but curls the ball high and wide of the target. It just hasn't clicked in forward areas for the home side tonight, they've seen more of the ball and have been stronger in midfield, but can't turn dominance into opportunities.
(71’) Fellaini is found by a looping back post cross, but the Belgium international can't steer his attempt the correct side of the upright! Arsenal then break, with Cazorla releasing Gibbs down the left, but the England international's square pass is deflected away for a corner.
(69’) De Gea makes another stop! Welbeck tees up Cazorla with a good header, but the Spain international can only place a shot within the reach of his compatriot in the Man United net. Arsenal have been extremely wasteful this evening.
(67’) Young escapes down the left-hand side, before whipping in a near post delivery, but Rooney gets the ball stolen from his boot as he attempts a volley. It's end-to-end stuff now, with every attack essentially being a counter attack.
--- 65’ Yellow card Cazorla gets yellow. ---
(65’) Cazorla picks up a yellow card for a very cynical tackle in the centre of midfield, with the Spain international preventing Young from breaking upfield. Since taking the lead, Man United have looked fairly comfortable.
(63’) Big chance for Sanchez! The Chile international gets the wrong side of Valencia, but can only cushion a close-range effort into the grasp of De Gea! Close, but not quite good enough for the Gunners.
(62’) Arsenal only have around half an hour to claw their way back into this game, with the away side essentially having a back five on show. Valencia and Young are tucking right in, making life difficult for Wenger's men when they approach the box - there are plenty of blue shirts in the way.
(60’) The change goes ahead, with Martinez taking to the hosts' net in place of Szczesny. The goalkeeper performed admirably in the Champions League recently, but this is arguably the bigger occasion now that the Gunners are behind at home.
--- 59’ Substitution D. Martínez enters the game and replaces W. Szczęsny. ---
(58’) Szczesny is hurt in the aftermath of Gibbs' own goal, with the stretcher readied for the hosts' goalkeeper. Martinez is quickly stripped off and ready to go on the sideline, with Arsenal forced to deal with two calamities in the space of a minute. The Polish shot-stopper may try to continue, however.
--- 56’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOOAL! MAN UNITED TAKE THE LEAD!! Fellaini is picked out at the back post, but the goalkeeper beats the Belgian to the delivery just about - thanks to the Poland international clashing with his defender. The rebound falls to Valencia, whose shot is deflected into the back of the net by the shin of Gibbs! ---
--- 55’ Substitution Cazorla enters the game and replaces J. Wilshere. ---
(54’) Wilshere is back on the field of play, but isn't moving well whatsoever. After walking around for a while, the Arsenal man goes to ground once again and Cazorla is readied as a replacement.
(53’) Wilshere is able to leave the field of his own accord, without a stretcher, but it doesn't look great for the Englishman. McNair is very lucky to escape without a booking, as the young defender slid straight through his adversary's ankle with his studs showing.
(51’) Fellaini gives away possession deep inside his own half, before Wilshere picks up the loose ball. He drives to the edge of the penalty box, before McNair slid in powerfully to try and deny him. He clatters through the Arsenal midfielder, who looks to be really hurt.
(49’) Great save from De Gea! Welbeck is released down the left channel, before breaking inside McNair and into the box. The England international tries to stab the ball home from a tight angle, but the goalkeeper spreads himself well to make another vital stop.
(48’) Arsenal earn an early corner, but Mertesacker fails to stoop and head home the first delivery, before the rebound is recycled and falls to the feet of Oxlade-Chamberlain. The England international forces another corner, which is volleyed wildly over the bar by Mertesacker.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half in London! The two sides have been relatively evenly matched thus far, but with so many high quality players on show, there have to be some goals in this contest somewhere!
After a poor opening 30 minutes, Man United improved somewhat, but still only Rooney and Di Maria appear to have anything up their sleeve in terms of grabbing a goal from nowhere. The hosts will feel aggrieved that they couldn't make their early pressure tell, that's for sure. Be sure to rejoin us in ten minutes time for all of the second-half action.
HALF TIME! It's goalless at the break at the Emirates, with Arsenal having the better of the opening 45 minutes. De Gea has been the Red Devils' best player, with some standout saves, but Welbeck just hasn't been able to punish his former club as of yet.
(45’) The final couple of minutes of the half are rather cagey, with neither outfit wanting to surrender their clean sheet. After a poor Chambers cross loops out of play for a goal kick, that should be that.
(45’) There are two minutes of stoppage time.
(44’) Arsenal win a corner on the left-hand side, which De Gea is able to bat half clear, before the rebound falls to Welbeck. The hosts' striker attempts a cheeky backheel, but fails to hit the target with his back to goal from 12 yards.
(42’) Smalling spurns a half chance for the Red Devils, slicing wide of the target from a close-range volley. It has taken Man United a long while, but they are suddenly competitive in this game, with Arsenal perhaps keen to head back into the dressing room and regroup.
(40’) After a long period on the backfoot, Man United enjoy a spell of pressure, earning a couple of corners in the process. Rooney and Di Maria continue to threaten around the periphery of the penalty area, but for the most part Szczesny has remained completely untroubled.
(38’) Great block from Chambers! The former Saints defender covers across brilliantly from right-back to slide in and deny a side-footed effort from Rooney! He concedes a corner, but that was a brilliant intervention from the Arsenal youngster.
(37’) Ramsey now tries his luck from range, but the Wales international blasts high and wide of the target poorly. Aside from the odd burst from Di Maria, Man United have been entirely predictable and continue to struggle at both ends of the field. Without De Gea, this could be any score.
(35’) Di Maria curls one wide! The Argentina international cuts in from the right-hand side, before letting fly from 20 yards out. It whistles just beyond the far upright with Szczesny stretching!
(34’) Di Maria whips a free kick delivery into a loaded penalty area, but Szczesny claims well to defuse the situation. With narrowly over ten minutes left to play until the interval, Arsenal continue to press for the opener, with Alexis forcing another comfortable save out of De Gea.
(32’) Wenger's men can feel very, very lucky to still have eleven men on the field of play. The England international lowered his head into his adversary, that should be a straight red card. He will have to watch his step now.
(30’) Tensions are rising and Wilshere and Fellaini clash! The Arsenal midfielder seems to lose his temper entirely, attempting to burrow his head into the Belgian's chest. The referee calls the pair over to him, but opts to only dish out a stern warning.
(28’) Another Arsenal set piece is wasted, with Wilshere curling the most recent directly out of play for a goal kick. As we reach the half hour mark, neither side have got anything to show for their respective pressure, though Man United have been mainly on the receiving end.
(26’) Sanchez whips a cross in towards the near post, but it is easily half-cleared and returned to the feet of the Chilean. He delivers a second, but nobody is able to turn the ball towards goal. Mertesacker tries a half volley, but misses it entirely, rather comically.
(24’) Young and Valencia gain possession in wide areas, but both waste their attempted crosses. De Gea is continuing to look rather uncomfortable in the Man United penalty area, which would only add to the visitors' current injury woes.
(22’) Another good save from De Gea! Oxlade-Chamberlain tries to take the ball around the goalkeeper, but the Spain international stays tall to make a great block. He gingerly gets back to his feet, which isn't a good sign.
(21’) Rooney blazes well over! The England international gets underneath the ball and sends it rocketing into the stands, just to compound the visitors' current misery. Things just haven't gone to plan for the Red Devils in the opening 20 minutes.
(20’) Di Maria is felled by a scrappy challenge from Ramsey, as the Argentine continues to be fairly anonymous tonight. Rooney is stood over the dead ball purposefully.
(18’) Man United are really struggling at the moment, with chance after chance falling to Welbeck - who just can't seem to punish his former club. Arsenal are maintaining the pressure and look the likelier side to find the breakthrough goal.
--- 16’ Substitution L. Shaw is replaced with A. Young. ---
(16’) After testing out his ankle for a few minutes, Shaw has decided that he is too injured to continue. Young is the man to be introduced at left wing-back, with Van Gaal really struggling for fit options.
(14’) Huge opportunity wasted by Wilshere! De Gea makes a bad clearance, which falls to the feet of the Arsenal midfielder and into his Chilean teammate's, but Alexis' stabbed pass into the path of Wilshere results in the Man United goalkeeper making a great save. From about eight yards out, he strikes the Spain international rather than the back of the net!
(13’) Good run from Wilshere! The Arsenal midfielder drives through the heart of the Man United defence, before seeing a 20-yard effort wickedly deflected off McNair and into the arms of De Gea. The away side are struggling to find a foothold in this game.
(11’) Monreal covers across to dispossess Van Persie and Di Maria in quick succession, with the natural left-back enjoying a rather good start to this game. Man United are looking flustered on the ball, with a not very assured back four. Shaw is still on the field, but doesn't look really comfortable.
(9’) Welbeck heads over! Oxlade-Chamberlain battles down the right once again, outmuscling Rooney and breaking to the byline well. His cross is reasonable, but the former Red Devil can't keep his header down! It loops into the stands, but the home crowd are encouraged. Shaw hobbles back onto the field.
(7’) Oxlade-Chamberlain is causing all kinds of problems down the right-hand side early on. The Englishman clashes with fellow compatriot Luke Shaw, but the former Southampton defender appears to turn his ankle. That did not look good.
(6’) Big chance for Welbeck! The former Man United striker is fed in behind the visiting back four, but McNair comes across brilliantly to block the Englishman's effort from a tight angle! Great work from Oxlade-Chamberlain in the build up, before Mertesacker heads wide from the resulting set piece.
(4’) Sanchez tries to race in behind Valencia and collect a diagonal pass, but the Ecuador international matches his marker stride-for-stride and allows for De Gea to sprint out and hoof clear.
(3’) Di Maria tries his luck down the right-hand side early on, but Monreal steps out well to rob the Argentine of the ball and clear up the line. Man United are indeed starting with three at the back.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at the Emirates, with Arsenal in their red and white home strip, while Man United are forced to change into their blue away kit.
Man United substitutes: Mata, Januzaj, Lindegaard, Young, Herrera, Fletcher, Wilson.
Man United starting line-up (3-4-1-2): De Gea; Smalling, McNair, Blackett; Valencia, Fellaini, Carrick, Shaw; Di Maria; Rooney, Van Persie.
Arsenal substitutes: Rosicky, Podolski, Giroud, Cazorla, Flamini, Martinez, Bellerin.
Arsenal starting line-up (4-2-3-1): Szczesny; Chambers, Mertesacker, Monreal, Gibbs; Arteta, Ramsey; Sanchez, Wilshere, Oxlade-Chamberlain; Welbeck.
TEAM NEWS: Injury woes mean that Paddy McNair and Tyler Blackett are called upon in defence once again, with Chris Smalling also involved from the start. Michael Carrick starts in holding midfield, with Marouane Fellaini providing some physicality alongside him, with Wayne Rooney, Angel di Maria and Wayne Rooney expected to provide some creativity. Van Gaal has the likes of Juan Mata, Ander Herrera and Adnan Januzaj on the bench.
TEAM NEWS: Nacho Monreal retains his place at centre-back in the absence of Laurent Koscielny, with Calum Chambers continuing at right-back for the hosts. Alexis Sanchez and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain provide the width for an interesting midfield for the Gunners, which is supporting ex-Red Devil Danny Welbeck. The script may already be written for the England international to find the net against his former club.
I'm Simon Harrison and I will be keeping you up to date with all of the action, as two big clubs who have suffered misfortune in seasons of late clash. There's plenty at stake in terms of points and pride, with several players absent which has made for interesting starting lineups from both bosses.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Manchester United's journey to the capital to face Arsenal, with Louis van Gaal's side searching for a result to kick start their season. Only two wins from their last five games isn't ideal form to enter the Emirates with, but Arsene Wenger's men themselves are without a victory in two games. This is an important clash in terms of who will finish in the European places come the end of the campaign.

Thank you for joining me today. I hope you have enjoyed the action. Until next time, farewell.
The referee blows his whistle to end the match and inflict more misery on Rodgers and Liverpool, who have now lost four in a row in all competitions. Palace claim all three points with their 3-1 win, coming from behind to claim victory after a magnificent performance. Lambert may have given the visitors an early lead, but goals from Gayle, Ledley and Jedinak gave Warnock's men a deserved triumph. The result will raise more questions about Liverpool and Rodgers as their Champions League challenge continues to dwindle, while Palace receive a major boost in their bid to avoid the drop.
(90’) FULL-TIME!
(90’) Not far from a fourth Palace goal! McArthur runs at Manquillo and produces a couple of stepovers. He cuts a pass back to the edge of the area for Ledley, who sees his first-time effort roll just wide of the right-hand post.
(90’) There will be four minutes added on here.
(88’) Liverpool are desperately trying to drag themselves back into this and they go close to scoring a second as a corner is hooked into the area and Skrtel slices over.
--- 86’ Substitution B. Bannan enters play, replacing Y. Bolasie. ---
(86’) Deserverd round-of-applause for Bolasie now as the winger goes off. Bannan takes his place.
(85’) Gerrard can't capitalise from the resulting free-kick, though. His controlled effort goes just over the crossbar, but Speroni never looked particularly worried.
--- 84’ Yellow card B. Hangeland gets yellow. ---
(84’) However, Liverpool do have a great opportunity now as Sterling wins a free-kick right on the edge of the Palace area after being tripped by Hangeland. The defender was also booked for his troubles.
(83’) What a kick in the teeth that goal will prove to be for Liverpool. At 2-1 they were very much in this going into the final 10 minutes, but that goal will surely give them too much to do now.
--- 81’ Goal! GOAL!!! WHAT A STRIKE! Palace open up a two-goal lead and in spectacular fashion. Jedinak steps up to take the free-kick and he curls a delightful effort into the top-right corner, giving Mignolet absolutely no chance. What a hit. ---
(81’) Free-kick now for Palace as Gayle is barged over by Skrtel about 25 yards from the Liverpool goal. The home fans are asking for a second yellow card, but the referee ignores their protests.
(80’) Few will argue that a win is more than Palace deserve. The hosts have been good today and their response to initially falling behind was excellent. Liverpool may have dictated much of the possession, but the home side have remained a constant threat.
--- 78’ Assist The assist came from Y. Bolasie. ---
--- 78’ Goal! GOAL!!! PALACE TAKE THE LEAD! Great wing play from Bolasie as the winger, just a few moments after switching to the right flank, flicks the ball over his head and races away from Lovren, who loses his footing. The DR Congo man cuts a low pass back towards the penalty spot and Ledley is on hand to knock past Mignolet. ---
(77’) Effective link-up between Bolasie and Ledley down the left and the Wales midfielder eventually manages to squeeze a cross into the danger area. Lovren heads clear, though.
--- 76’ Substitution J. Puncheon is replaced with J. McArthur. ---
(76’) Palace respond with a change of their own. Off goes Puncheon and McArthur enters proceedings. He will, in theory, help the hosts gain more of a foothold in midfield.
(75’) And Liverpool now make another change, as Emre Can takes the place of Joe Allen, who has had a good game today.
--- 74’ Substitution E. Can enters play, replacing J. Allen. ---
(73’) Off goes Lallana, who has been quiet for long periods. He is replaced by Borini.
--- 72’ Substitution F. Borini enters play, replacing A. Lallana. ---
(72’) WHAT A MISS! Liverpool really should be ahead again here. Coutinho does brilliantly as he dribbles through a crowd of players and finds Sterling in the area. The winger manages to pick out Manquillo arriving late and in acres of space, but his first-time effort from about 12 yards is terrible, ultimately going out for a throw-in.
(71’) Palace seemingly waste the counterattacking opportunity as Puncheon's forward pass to Gayle forces the attack out too wide. Nevertheless, he gets a cross into the centre, which is well held by Mignolet, with Bolasie lurking.
(69’) SPERONI ESCAPES! Lovely move from Liverpool as Lallana links well with Lambert, who lays the ball off to Allen. The Wales midfielder picks Johnson's run out and the left-back plays a teasing ball into the danger area. The goalkeeper pounces and spills the ball, but he manages to keep Sterling out on the follow-up.
(67’) More pressure from the hosts as Chamakh runs at the Liverpool defence and sees a shot blocked. The ball then drops kindly for Bolasie, but his cross is headed away. Palace work the move back out to the Congolese winger, though on this occasion he runs straight out of play.
(65’) Liverpool escape another Palace chance! On this occasion it is Puncheon, who has been rather quiet, causing trouble on the right flank. He cuts inside on to his left foot, crossing in towards the back post. Bolasie can't quite reach it, though.
(64’) Good play by Bolasie as he produces a clever turn and then releases Ward down the left flank. The full-back gets a cross in and, although it is partially cleared, Jedinak eventually gets a shot away. That, though, is blocked.
(63’) Well, they can't capitalise on this occasion anyway. The corner is lofted into the danger area, but Palace are penalised as Jedinak is adjudged to have fouled Mignolet.
(62’) Ledley lays the ball off for Jedinak, who sees his shot deflected over the crossbar for a corner. This is a good spell of pressure for Palace. Can they capitalise on it?
--- 61’ Yellow card Javi Manquillo goes into the referee's book. ---
(61’) Free-kick in a great position for Palace. Chamakh turns Manquillo on the left corner of the penalty area and is brought down just outside the box, with the Spaniard earning a yellow card. Some fans wanted a penalty, but the referee made the right decision.
(59’) Liverpool have so far managed to keep a lid on Bolasie in this second half. One suspects that Palace will need to get him involved again if they are to steal a win from this match.
(57’) Liverpool are slowly improving as this half progresses, dictating possession at Selhurst Park. They see another opportunity go begging as Gerrard races to the edge of the area to meet Coutinho's laid-off pass, though he scuffs his shot and misses the target from 25 yards.
(56’) Decent chance for Liverpool there as Palace fail to deal with the corner and the ball lands at the feet of Skrtel, who slices an effort across the face of goal and out of play.
(55’) Good move by Liverpool as Coutinho plays the ball into Lambert's feet. The forward plays a back-heel into the path of Sterling, inviting the winger into the penalty area, with his eventual delivery knocked behind for a corner.
--- 53’ Yellow card M. Škrtel is cautioned by the referee. ---
(53’) Palace look to catch Liverpool on the counterattack as Chamakh knocks the ball past Skrtel and attempts to chase it down. He is cynically brought down by the defender, though, who sees his name taken by the referee.
(52’) Clever footwork from Lallana on the right as he moves the ball on to his left foot, shapes to cross and then produces a Cruyff turn. He does then delivery with his right foot, but Dann nods clear.
(51’) There's Palace first attempt on goal of the second half, as Dann rises to meet Jedinak's lofted delivery from a deep free-kick after being fouled by Coutinho. His looping header is plucked out of the rather rather easily by Mignolet, however.
(49’) Gerrard blasts the ball towards goal with a powerful strike from the free-kick, though his attempt goes over the bar, causing Speroni few worries.
(48’) Good opportunity for Liverpool now as Sterling cuts in from the left and draws a cheap, needless foul from Martin Kelly. Gerrard walks over, as usual, and looks rather focused.
(47’) Encouraging start for the hosts. Bolasie almost immediately finds himself on the ball down the left and he skips away from the challenge of Skrtel before crossing. Lovren heads clear as far as Ledley, who cannot control the ball properly.
(46’) We are back underway for the second half.
The referee blows his whistle to end an entertaining first half at Selhurst Park, with 1-1 probably a fair reflection of the match so far. Liverpool started well and took an incredibly early lead as Lambert scored his first goal for the club within 90 seconds. The visitors continued to generally control possession, but Palace grew into the contest and levelled through Gayle, who inflicted such misery on Rodgers' men in this fixture last term. The hosts continued to threaten and through Bolasie they have caused numerous problems. More of the same in the second half, please!
(45’) HALF-TIME
(45’) There will be two minutes added on here.
(44’) Although Lovren appears to go in pretty hard on Gayle as the corner is delivered from the left, the referee sees nothing untoward and allows play to continue, with Liverpool clearing their lines.
(43’) SENSATIONAL COUNTERATTACK! Palace clear the Liverpool free-kick after a bit of a goalmouth scramble and Bolasie is released down the left. The winger highlights his fantastic pace as he charges into the visitors' half and gets into the final third. He cuts inside, plays a clever one-two with Gayle and ultimately sees his effort saved by Mignolet. Corner for the home side!
(42’) Clever use of his body from Coutinho there, as the Brazilian shifts himself between the ball and Jedinak to win a free-kick about 35 yards from goal. This is a good opportunity for the visitors.
(40’) For all the trouble Bolasie has caused, Puncheon has been rather quiet for Palace. Statistically the team's most potent attacking threat in terms of chances created this term, he has struggled to make much of an impact against Johnson and Allen.
(38’) Audacious attempt from Gerrard as the captain tries his luck from about 30 yards. But on this occasion he can't quite pull off a trademark piledriver, as his shot sails harmlessly over the crossbar.
(37’) Tentative penalty claims turned down for Liverpool. Sterling tried to chip a cross into the danger area after being halted by Kelly just inside the area. The ball does appear to hit the Palace defender on the arm, though the referee gives nothing.
--- 36’ Substitution B. Hangeland enters play, replacing D. Delaney. ---
(36’) That's a blow for the hosts. Delaney is being forced off with a rather innocuous-looking injury, with Hangeland coming on as his replacement.
(35’) LIVERPOOL WASTE ANOTHER CHANCE! Good play by Allen down the left as he looks set to attack Kelly down the outside, turns and then crosses in right-footed after cutting inside. His delivery picks out Lamber at the back post, but he fails to even hit the target. He has to do better there!
(33’) Lovely move by Liverpool. Sterling comes in off the right and plays the ball into a central position for Coutinho. The Brazilian hits a first-time pass into the area for Lallana, who tries to control on the turn. The ball just gets away from him, though and the attack peters out.
(31’) Puncheon's corner delivery is deep as it finds its way past the far post, though Liverpool are able to deal with it and clear relatively comfortably.
(30’) MIGNOLET SAVES LIVERPOOL! Everything from Palace's perspective is going through Bolasie at the moment. He cuts inside and on to his right foot again, jolting away from a couple of men after a standing-start, before unleashing a powerful drive towards the bottom-far corner. The goalkeeper turns it around the post, though.
(29’) LIVERPOOL GO CLOSE! Lallana drops deep and wins a free-kick from Dann, with Gerrard moving over to take the set-piece. His delivery, from about 35 yards, is an inviting one and Lambert manages to get his head on it, though his attempt goes well over the crossbar. He'll be disappointed with that.
(27’) That's a bit better from Sterling as he cuts in from the left, skips past one challenge and then chips a pass into the danger area for Lambert. His delivery is a little too high, though, as the forward can only flick the ball on with his head and Speroni collects with ease.

(37’) Aston Villa regain possession in the middle of the pitch before Cleverley sends the ball out to Cissokho on the left wing. The defender then curls a deep cross into the penalty area, but it's slightly overhit and ends up flying into the hands of Forster.
(35’) The visitors look visibly rattled after Agbonlahor's goal, and they're finding it extremely difficult to carve out any chances in the final third of the pitch.
(33’) Southampton win themselves a corner, which Tadic curls in towards the penalty spot. It pinballs around the penalty area before falling to Mane on the left hand side of the box, but the Senegalese midfielder ends up running the ball out of play for a goal kick.
(31’) Alderweireld is forced into launching a long ball forward in the hope of finding Pelle, but Hutton does well to intercept the pass before clearing the danger with a strong header.
--- 29’ Assist C. Clark gave the assist. ---
--- 29’ Goal! GOAL! Against all the odds, Aston Villa have taken the lead! Clark fires a lofted pass forward that Forster rushes out of his penalty area to deal with, but he's beaten to it by Agbonlahor, who then calmly slots the ball into the back of the empty net to make it 1-0 to the hosts. ---
(27’) Sanchez tees up Cissokho, who then sends a low cross in towards the six-yard box from the left flank, but it's unable to find Agbonlahor and instead is easily cleared away from danger by Alderweireld.
(25’) Westwood fires a shot towards goal from the resulting set-piece but it ends up bouncing off the wall and safely into the hands of Forster.
(24’) Great play by Agbonlahor! The striker picks up the ball on the halfway line and darts towards the Southampton penalty area before forcing Fonte into fouling him just a few yards outside of the box.
(22’) Hutton picks up the ball on the right wing before sending a great cross into the middle of the box, but it's easily cleared away from danger by Alderweireld.
(20’) After a period of Southampton pressure, Aston Villa break away on a quick counter attack down the left wing, but it's brought to an end by brilliant defending from Alderweireld and Fonte.
(18’) Bertrand and Pelle link up extremely well on the left hand side of the Aston Villa penalty area, allowing the former to dart towards the near post before cutting the ball back to Mane. The latter then unleashes a shot from eight yards out but he ends up badly scuffing his effort, sending it well wide of the far post.
(16’) Wanyama sprints past two Aston Villa players on the right wing before curling an absolutely wonderful bouncing cross into the path of Mane, but the Senegalese midfielder is just a few yards offside, bringing an end to another lovely Southampton attacking move.
(14’) The corner is initially dealt with by the Southampton defence but drops to Cleverley, who decides to volley the ball back towards goal from 25 yards out, but his shot is poor and fails to trouble Forster.
(13’) Aston Villa break forward down the left flank and Cissokho sends a dangerous cross into the box that almost finds Agbonlahor in front of goal. He's unable to get a head on it, however, and Fonte then fires the ball out of play for a corner.
(11’) Tadic sends the resulting set-piece into the heart of the penalty area, where it finds the head of Alderweireld. He's unable to direct his headed effort towards goal, however, and the Aston Villa defence deal with the danger well.
(10’) Mane bursts into the Aston Villa penalty area and twists and turns around two players before picking out Tadic at the back post. The Serbian side-steps around Cissokho before shooting but his attempt on goal takes a slight deflection that sends it out for a corner.
(8’) The resulting set-piece is well-worked and finds its way to Schneiderlin just inside the penalty area, but the French midfielder ends up firing his first-time shot a few yards wide of the near post.
(7’) Southampton patiently work their way towards the Aston Villa penalty area before Clyne curls a half-volleyed cross into the box. It's poorly hit but still ends up causing Guzan a problem, forcing the goalkeeper into tipping the ball out for a corner.
(5’) A lofted pass finds its way to Mane, who pushes forward down the left wing before firing a cross-cum-shot that ends flying well wide of the goal, leaving the Senegalese midfielder red in the face.
(3’) Agbonlahor picks up the ball just inside the Southampton half of the pitch and sprints through the centre of the midfield before unleashing a shot from 25 yards out, but Alderweireld is able to dive in the way to deflect the ball into the hands of Forster with a brilliant interception.
(1’) And we're off! Southampton get us underway, attacking from right to left.
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch, with just a few minutes to go until kick-off.
Meanwhile, Koeman has made just one change to the Southampton side that started the 2-0 win at home to Leicester City two weeks ago, with Shane Long coming in to replace the injured Steven Davis.
Aston Villa boss Paul Lambert has made three changes to the side that drew against West Ham United in their last Premier League outing, with Alan Hutton, Ciaran Clark and Jores Okore (the latter of whom is making his first appearance of the season) all coming in to the squad to replace Matthew Lowton, Ron Vlaar and Nathan Baker in a heavily changed defence.

There's just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let's have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this evening...
As for Southampton, they are flying near the top of the table, and another victory tonight, which would be their fifth in a row, would move them four points clear of third-place Manchester City ahead of the meeting between the two sides on Sunday afternoon. Ronald Koeman's men have only lost once in their last nine league games, conceding just three goals in the process, and the Dutchman will be expecting another impressive performance from his side tonight as they continue to go from strength to strength as the season unfolds.
It's been a tough two months for Aston Villa, who head into tonight's clash just one point clear of the relegation zone in 17th place after failing to win any of their last seven league games. Their hard-fought goalless draw away to West Ham United in their last clash before the international break was their first point since the middle of September when they beat Liverpool 1-0 at Anfield, and the joy surrounding the club in the wake of that impressive victory feels like it happened lifetime ago.

Chelsea are temporarily seven points clear at the top now, while Liverpool could drop into the bottom half by the end of the weekend. That is all we have time for today. Thanks for joining me, Tom Webber. It's been great!
FULL TIME - Liverpool 1-2 Chelsea: The Reds took the lead early on through Can but Cahill soon brought Mourinho's men back on level terms. The visitors pushed on and were far more convincing after the break, and they found the winning goal through Costa! The Blues remain unbeaten after 11 games this season.
(90’) Chelsea break and Willian closes Mignolet, who somehow kicks the ball out for a corner. The referee blows his whistle, though! It's all over!
(90’) Mourinho is complaining that the whistle is yet to go!
--- 90’ +5 Substitution Filipe Luis enters play, replacing E. Hazard. ---
(90’) Another change for Chelsea, now, as Hazard comes off for Filipe Luis. Mourinho just winding down the clock now.
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card T. Courtois is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) Courtois has been shown a yellow card for wasting time while taking his goal kick!
(90’) Lambert is released down the channel but the pass from Allen is too strong and it sends him down to the byline. He stands a cross up at the back post but it is too high for Sterling, who recycles the ball. A delivery is eventually sent in courtesy of Moreno but Borini's header sails over the top.
(90’) Johnson attempts to spin Azpilicueta and beat the Spaniard to the byline, but the Chelsea left-back defends brilliantly, blocking him off and taking nothing but the ball.
(90’) We are into the first of an additional FIVE minutes. Yes, five!
--- 90’ Substitution D. Drogba comes on for Diego Costa. ---
(90’) Costa walks off the pitch, and it looks like that will be the end of his afternoon. Drogba comes on to replace the scorer of the second goal.
(89’) Oscar kicks the ball out of play as Costa stays down following another coming together with Skrtel. The home fans aren't pleased, but the medical staff are on to tend to the striker.
(88’) PENALTY CLAIM FOR LIVERPOOL! Gerrard has a pop from 20 yards which is blocked by a diving Cahill. The Liverpool captain remonstrates with the referee, claiming it was a handball by the Chelsea centre-back. Nothing is given, but it certainly could have been awarded on another day.
--- 87’ Yellow card Diego Costa is yellow-carded. ---
(87’) Chelsea manage to win the ball down near the corner flag as Lambert stumbles when looking to latch onto a pass. The Blues look to counter but Azpilicueta gives the ball straight to Johnson, so Costa slides in with a rather poor challenge that earns him a booking.
(85’) There is not enough movement from Liverpool in the final third, so they keep shifting the ball across the halfway line without much penetration being offered. They need to step it up now, as there are only five minutes remaining.
--- 83’ Yellow card Oscar goes into the referee's book. ---
(83’) Oscar is the next player into the book for a clumsy, rather cynical challenge. Gerrard bends the free kick in from deep but the referee spots a foul in the box by Skrtel.
(82’) Good defending from Skrtel! Costa is left in space on the right and upon receiving the ball he drives to the byline. Hazard makes a near-post run and the striker picks him out. Skrtel tracks him, though, sliding in and deflecting the ball off the Belgian and out for a goal kick.
(81’) The Blues fail to make the most of a chance to get the ball down the other end, as a free kick near the halfway line is taken short and lost in a matter of seconds! Liverpool come forward again.
(80’) With 10 minutes to go Chelsea are struggling to get out of their own half. Options are limited when they look to get forward as they don't want to be caught short defensively.
--- 79’ Substitution R. Lambert comes on for M. Balotelli. ---
(79’) Here is the change, then. Not a poor performance by any means from Balotelli, who has worked hard for his side today. His replacement is another player searching for his first Premier League goal for Liverpool!
(78’) Lambert is being prepared on the touchline, and he will presumably replace Balotelli. The Italian has gone quiet after a bright start to proceedings.
(77’) Allen has been very lively since coming on, and again he causes Chelsea some problems over on the left. This time he uses the space he creates to tee up Gerrard for a shot from 25 yards, but Terry rushes out to close it down and make a vital block.
(75’) CHANCE! Allen makes a great run from the inside down to the left corner and is picked out. He then curls a cross to the back post for Henderson, whose volley takes a wicked deflection off Matic. Unlike Can's goal, though, it doesn't end up in the net, instead going out for a corner.
(73’) Henderson pulls out wide on the right and he drives a cross in towards the near post. Terry is first to it, though, making a block before sending the ball away from his goal.
(72’) The Blues will likely look to sit back and protect this lead for the remaining 20 minutes or so, now.
--- 70’ Substitution Philippe Coutinho is done for the day. F. Borini is his replacement. ---
--- 70’ Substitution J. Allen comes on for E. Can. ---
(70’) A pair of changes from Rodgers, as Borini and Allen come on for Coutinho and Can. Will they be able to spark the Reds back onto level terms?
--- 69’ Yellow card N. Matić gets yellow. ---
(69’) Chelsea are good value for that goal, as they have been far more positive than their opponents since the break. Liverpool do respond quickly, with Johnson coming inside from the right before being felled by Matic. The tackle earns the Serbian a yellow card.
--- 67’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAAALL! CHELSEA LEAD THROUGH COSTA! Willian picks out Azpilicueta on the left with a lovely, raking pass. The left-back beats Coutinho and races into the box, stabbing the ball into the middle with the outside of his boot. Mignolet and Moreno both get touches but they can't stop it reaching Costa, who rifles a low shot into the net! ---
(66’) Fabregas stands it up at the back post and Liverpool manage to head it away. The Blues keep it alive through Matic but they fail to put another cross into the box soon after.
--- 65’ Yellow card M. Balotelli is cautioned by the referee. ---
(65’) Balotelli is the next player to go into the book for an off-the-ball shove on Oscar, just outside the box on the near side. Fabregas stands over it once more...
(64’) The Serbian right-back is finally able to receive treatment and he returns to the pitch moments after play restarts!
(62’) Ivanovic stays down after challenging Moreno to a header, but the ball is not put out of play, with Cahill hooking it forward rather than kicking it into touch. The Reds subsequently continued but Balotelli was offside from Sterling's pass!
(60’) For large periods of the first half Chelsea sat back and absorbed pressure, while struggling to forge anything in the opposing half. The is how Liverpool have played since the break, and the tempo of the game is now starting to slow.
(59’) Hazard gets back to help mop up at the back as Johnson attempts to bring down Gerrard's excellent pass from inside the centre circle. The Belgian then takes a slight risk by looking to beat Coutinho just outside his own box, but he draws a foul to earn his side a free kick.
(57’) Costa shows great strength on the right to hold off Lovren before spinning the Croatian and running towards the box. He is forced down the line by the covering defender and thus passes back to Willian. The Brazilian immediately bears down on goal, cutting inside and back out before seeing his shot get blocked!
(55’) A long clearance up from the back is allowed to bounce by the Liverpool defence, and Oscar looks to capitalise. He pokes the ball away from Lovren but Moreno recovers to hook it clear.
--- 54’ Substitution Ramires is done for the day. Willian is his replacement. ---
(54’) Mourinho makes his first change of the game with Willian coming on in place of Ramires. A positive swap from the Portuguese.
(53’) GOOD SAVE! Liverpool finally work Courtois in this half as Sterling comes inside from the left, shifting the ball away from Ivanovic and lashing a shot at goal. It looks to be heading for the corner but the keeper gets down and parries it aside. Chelsea then counter through Hazard but the Belgian's effort is deflected out for a corner by Gerrard.
(51’) COSTA! Oscar lifts a lovely pass over the defence which the Reds fail to deal with. Costa attempts to punish them with an acrobatic overhead kick that flies just over the top of goal. Moreno had a firm grip on his shirt there and his compatriot now has a gaping hole on his back!
(50’) Chelsea have started the second half brightly, with some particularly impressive link-up play on the left between Azpilicueta, Hazard and Oscar. The trio combine again, with the latter cutting onto his right foot and bending a shot harmlessly wide of the far post.
(49’) Ivanovic picks up the ball on the edge of the box but doesn't quite know what to do with it and is quickly dispossessed. He grabs a hold of Sterling's shirt to stop him latching onto a pass and catching his team short, earning himself a yellow card.
--- 48’ Yellow card B. Ivanović gets yellow. ---
(48’) Some sustained pressure from Chelsea sees them win a corner. Fabregas whips it in from the left but his delivery is poor, and Balotelli clears it at the near post.
(47’) Matic plays a pass down the left-hand channel, looking for Costa, but Skrtel is across to it first in order to hook it out for a throw in.
(46’) We are back underway at Anfield!
Welcome back! We've got just a few minutes to go until the second half commences, with what is set to be another enthralling 45 minutes.
There was a confrontation between Skrtel and Costa as the players headed down the tunnel, there, with their team-mates having to intervene to stop things getting out of hand. It will be interesting to see how that develops after the break!
HALF TIME - Liverpool 1-1 Chelsea: The hosts got off to a great start as Can's deflected shot got the better of Courtois with just nine minutes on the clock, but their lead only lasted five minutes as Cahill's effort from a corner snuck over the line. There has been plenty of action so far, and we can expect more to come in the second half with the three points still very much up for grabs.
(45’) There is the half-time whistle!
(45’) There will be just one minute of added time at the end of this half.
(44’) Fabregas floats the free kick towards the far post but Lovren rises highest to head it away from danger. Johnson looks to ignite a counterattack by switching the play to Sterling, and the England international is held up by Fabregas before drawing a foul.
--- 43’ Yellow card R. Sterling is yellow-carded. ---
(43’) Livepool are being penned back by Chelsea here, and Sterling goes into the book for blocking off Ramires as the Brazilian attempted a one-two with Matic. A free kick in a dangerous area for the Blues now, then.
(41’) HAZARD! The Belgian waits for a space to open up just outside the box before looking to curl a shot across goal and inside the bottom corner. Mignolet gets down to it, keeping hold of the ball with Oscar chasing in to pounce on any potential spill.
(40’) Ivanovic bulldozes his way into the area, along the byline on the near side. He steams through a weak challenge from Moreno and then blocks Gerrard's clearance, but the ricochet is held by Mignolet at the near post!
(39’) The game is becoming quite stretched as we approach half time! Is there going to be another goal before the interval?
(37’) Chelsea push a few more men forward and look to capitalise on this spell of pressure, but they nearly leave themselves short moments later. Sterling breaks away down the left and squares a lovely cross into the middle, which Balotelli is too late to connect with.
(36’) Liverpool are opened up by another incisive Chelsea break, with Oscar releasing Ramires with a lovely pass, and his cutback rolls across to Hazard on the far side. He attempts to place a shot into the corner but again Johnson is in the way!
(35’) Things are getting quite heated between Skrtel and Costa! They've had a couple of collisions in the last few moments but it seems like healthy competition.
(34’) Important block from Johnson, stopping Hazard's shot, following a quick Chelsea break, from worrying Mignolet in goal. The visitors fail to make the most of their subsequent corner, though.
(32’) Nervy stuff from Mignolet! The keeper comes outside the left side of his box and produces a woeful kick that is controlled by Fabregas just outside the centre circle. Costa, coming back from behind the defence, is subsequently flagged offside incorrectly, but it's a Liverpool free kick.
(31’) The visitors have every man behind the ball, making the centre of their half very congested. Liverpool are thus to look to the wide areas where Sterling is found, but his cross evades its intended target of Balotelli at the back post.
(29’) Costa manages to hold off a couple of red shirts to fire an effort at goal from the left side of the box. It takes a touch off Skrtel and goes out for a corner, which Terry gets his head to at the back post once more. He fails to pick out a team-mate with his cushioned header, though.
(28’) The Blues are struggling to hold onto the ball inside the opposition half, and Ramires shows too much of it to Moreno, who makes a neat tackle. (26’) Coutinho picks up the ball inside his own half, darting past both Matic and Fabregas as he bears down on goal. He lets fly with a low effort from 20 yards out and Courtois is unable to keep hold of it. Ivanovic is first to the rebound, though, and he removes the threat.
(25’) Hazard dribbles down the left wing but he only has Costa up in support with him. The Chelsea players are outnumbered but Johnson races back and shoves the Belgian from behind, conceding a free kick. That was rather unnecessary!
(24’) The Reds have had an impressive 63% possession so far this afternoon, with Chelsea happy to sit back and look to stretch them on the counterattack.
(22’) Cahill hoofs the ball clear from the edge of the Chelsea box and Costa races Skrtel to get on the end of it. He pushes the defender in the back as they approach the edge of the box, and the referee awards a free kick. The Spain international then provokes his opponent with a few words afterwards, but the official cools the tempers with stern words for both.
(21’) PENALTY CLAIM?! The corner is only cleared as far as Sterling on the edge of the box, and the England international smashes an effort straight into the ground. (20’) Chelsea are sitting very deep at the moment so Johnson pushes forward to offer some width on the right. He receives a pass from Henderson and his cross goes out for a corner following an interception from Azpilicueta.
(19’) It's in the back of the net, but the goal is ruled out! The referee played the advantage as Coutinho shimmied away from a strong challenge courtesy of Ramires, but the Italian was in an offside position as he swept home his team-mate's pass!
(18’) Balotelli attempts to spin away from Matic on the near side but Ramires comes back to help his team-mate and catches the striker on the foot. He limps away from the challenge and the referee awards a free kick to the hosts.
(16’) Hazard comes inside from the right, getting the ball onto his left foot and then looking to sneak a shot from 20 yards inside Mignolet's near post. He doesn't quite hit the target, though, and the effort skids wide of the target.

Mignolet dives to his right to make a great save but, following a small touch from Matic, Cahill is first on the scene to fire a shot at goal on the follow-up. (13’) Chelsea win a corner as Ivanovic pushes forward before rolling a pass down the line for Hazard. Sterling is back helping out, though, and he sends it out for a corner kick!
(11’) Azpilicueta is allowed to stride forward down the left flank and he decides to slip a pass inside for Oscar. The Brazilian looks to angle a first-time pass into the path of Hazard, but he overhits the pass and it runs out of play for a goal kick.

The corner is whipped into the box and the keeper comes out to claim it confidently.
(1’) We are off!

Burnley's four point return from their first 10 games is worse than Derby's appalling start to the 2006/07 campaign. It is the fifth worst in Premier League history, better only than Swindon 1993/94, Everton 1994/95, Manchester City 1995/96 and Crystal Palace last season.
Burnley are the 10th team who have failed to pick up a win in any of their opening 10 Premier League matches of a single season, only three of the previous nine have survived the drop after such a poor start. Dyche's side will be aiming to overturn that record with a first season victory over Hull today and they have some reason to be confident having won four of the last five meetings.
It's been three games since Hull's last success and they have a particularly poor away record having won just one of their last 10 Premier League matches on the road, with four draws and five defeats. This fixture has always produced close encounters with four of the last five meetings between the sides having ended with a 1-0 scoreline.
Burnley have collected just four points so far this term, but remain only five adrift of safety and a progressive run of results would have them quickly climbing the positions in the table. It could be a timely period for them to be entertaining Hull, with Bruce's men hardly in dazzling form themselves at present. They have recorded just two wins and five draws so far.

FULL TIME: MANCHESTER UNITED 1-0 CRYSTAL PALACE. It was far from pretty from the hosts, but it is a massive three points for them nonetheless. The introduction of Juan Mata proved to be the difference, as his 67th minute shot just escaped Speroni, proving to be the winning goal, adding to Palace's misery.
(90’) IT'S ALL OVER! Chris Foy blows the whistle for full time, and United head into the international break on the back of a very important three points.
(90’) Wonderful work from James Wilson who kills time near the corner flag, before laying it off for Rooney. The captain switches the play, showing great vision, which keeps the hosts in possession as we enter the final minute of added time.

(90’) There will be three minutes of stoppage time at the end of this match...

Rooney and Van Persie pass it around in attack, with the skipper picking out Shaw on the left, but he is unable to pick out the Dutchman with his cross.
(87’) Possession stays with United as we approach the 90th minute. They pass it around comfortably in midfield, with Palace struggling to chase it down and win it back. Finally it is given away by Mata, but a wasteful ball forward gives possession straight back to the hosts.
(85’) STAT ATTACK: Crystal Palace have allowed a goal in the final 10 minutes of each of their five away matches in the league this season, four of which came in the 88th minute or later.

The ball comes to the top of the area, where Mata meets it with his left foot, but strikes it square off the woodwork! Van Persie is there to follow up, but his scrambled shot sails behind for a goal kick.

(77’) Palace win a ball back in midfield and push forward. They still have just four men committed to this attack, despite trailing. The ball comes to Delaney from 20 yards out, but his attempted placement shot barely trickles into the six yard box, as De Gea makes the easiest save he will ever have.

Speroni has no excuse to be beaten with that effort, even getting a hand to it, but not enough to push it onto the other side of the post. ---

The Foxes were resolute and hard to breakdown but never had enough of the ball to relieve the pressure on their back line. The best the visitors could hope for really was a 0-0 draw but Shane Long snatched that away from them. Chris Wood could have and really should've set up a grandstand finish but the striker put the ball wide when he had stuck the goalkeeper on his backside really encapsulated Leicester's lack of confidence in front of goal. They will need to use the international break well if they are to stop the rot.
Persistance certainly paid off for Southampton and just when you thought that the breakthrough might never materialise but then Shane Long popped up with not one but two goals after coming on as a substitute. It was an inspired change from Ronald Koeman, who must have been tempted to keep Sadio Mane on as well as his side looked for a winner but the Saints stuck to their guns and were ultimately rewarded. A hard fought victory that was well earned for the home team today.
(90’) Full time Southampton 2-0 Leicester City. The Saints go marching on.
(90’) SHOT! Shane Long nearly completes his hat-trick but his shot goes inches wide. That turns out to be the last kick of the game.

(90’) Another Southampton academy graduate enters the fray for the final few minutes in place of Morgan Schneiderlin and receives a very warm welcome from the Saints fans.
(89’) Southampton are quite happy now to keep the ball and run the clock down. Despite the home teams dominance it could have been a very different finale to the match if Wood had scored.

(85’) SHOT! Substitute Nick Powell tries his luck from all of 25 yards but the youngster on-loan from Manchester United only succeeds in finding the travelling Leicester City fans behind the goal.

Shane Long nearly bursts through again to complete his hat-trick but Wes Morgan puts in a crucial last-ditch tackle.

--- 80’ Assist The assist came from V. Wanyama. ---

(77’) What now for the Foxes? They have worked so hard but it has all been undone by some superb attacking play from Southampton.
--- 76’ Substitution A. King is done for the day. N. Powell is his replacement. ---
--- 75’ Assist G. Pellè gave the assist. ---
--- 75’ Goal! GOAL! Shane Long gives Southampton the lead with a fine finish. (73’) Southampton certainly aren't panicking and are sticking to their principles of patience possession football. The Saints are going to have to get used to visiting teams adopting similiar tactics to those that have been implemented by Leicester City this afternoon.

I don't feel Ronald Koeman will be overly concerned at this moment in time, if the pattern of the game continues into the second half without a breakthrough then he may look to someone like Shane Long to shake things up. Patience will be the key in the second period for the home team.
(45’) And there's the half-time whistle. Southampton 0-0 Leicester City. So far, so good for Nigel Pearson's men.

Leicester go into this game in the relegation zone and their recent defensive troubles will not give their supporters a huge amount of confidence against a free scoring Southampton side. The Foxes have conceded 16 goals in their ten matches while the Saints have scored 21 times already this season.
Ronald Koeman has been able to pick a very settled side all season which many believe has been key to Southampton's consistently excellent performances. Despite the many plaudits Saints have rightly received for their flair going forward, their defensive record has been absolutely outstanding. They have only conceded five goals in their ten matches so far.
Nigel Pearson's side were unfortunate to go down 1-0 at home to West Bromwich Albion last Saturday after Esteban Cambiasso's bizarre own goal. The Foxes are boosted though today by the return of Leonardo Ulloa, who is their top goalscorer so far this campaign. They will need the former Brighton striker to be at his very best if they are to come away from St.Mary's with a positive result.
Just the one change to the high flying Saints team that started away against Hull City last week with Shane Long dropping to the bench in place of Saido Mane. Southampton will be looking to continue their best ever start to a Premier League season against an out of form Leicester City side who are without a win in their last five matches.
