There's just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let's have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon...
As for Everton, they suffered a lacklustre start to the season, winning just one of their first seven league games, their worst run since December 2010, but have steadied the ship somewhat in recent weeks thanks to relatively comfortable back-to-back victories against Aston Villa and Burnley and a goalless draw at home to Swansea City last weekend. However, they currently sit in a disappointing 11th place, just three points clear of Sunderland, and they desperately need to keep their good form going ahead of tough games against West Ham United, Tottenham Hotspur and Manchester City all in the space of two weeks after the international break.
Today's hosts head into this afternoon's clash just two points clear of the relegation zone in 15th place after a tough start to the season, although last weekend's 3-1 win against fellow strugglers Crystal Palace will surely have given them confidence about their chances of coming away with something today. A win could move them as high as 11th, which shows just how congested the bottom half of the table is, whilst it would also set them up perfectly for their next game against 18th-place Leicester City, which is, even at this relatively early stage of the campaign, a must-win clash.

Stoke, meanwhile, have leapfrogged the likes of Liverpool and Tottenham themselves to launch into the top half of the table. Mark Hughes will take some pride from this performance and will certainly hope Bojan can use his fantastic goal to grow further in the league. Thank you for joining us here today!
The game, truly, had a little bit of everything, with three goals that were fantastic in their own ways. For Tottenham, their poor start to the season continues and they've now lost twice as many games at home as they've won in the Premier League this season.
(90’) Adebayor fluffs a great chance on a header and the referee blows the whistle for full time. Stoke hang on for the win and take all of the points away at Tottenham with a 2-1 win.
(90’) Barring a last minute surprise here, Stoke now look good for the win, doing well to keep the ball in the midfield and threatening Tottenham's diced backline when they foray forward. Just 2 minutes left at White Hart Lane.
(90’) It's a terrible effort from Kane, who fires directly into the bar for Stoke to clear. There are another five minutes added onto this half, exactly the same as last half.
(90’) Superb opportunity for Spurs here - Shawcross takes down Rose just outside of the line and the home side have a free-kick as close to the box as is possible. Can Spurs equalize here today against the most unlikeliest of circumstances?
(89’) With one minute plus stoppages left and Tottenham down both a man and a goal, you wouldn't really know it at the moment - they're all over Stoke in their own box but Fazio is caught in possession and it takes a good tackle from Rose to prevent a counter!
(88’) Shawcross and Kane tussle outside of the Stoke box, but the referee lets play go on and Tottenham earn a corner. Lamela goes down in the box but far too easily and the ball trickles out of play.
(86’) Fazio is having an absolute nightmare, with a poor header finding Ireland in the box that forces a superb save from Lloris!
--- 85’ Red card! NAUGHTON SENT OFF! He's been tormented all night down his flank by Moses and this time, their tussle turns into his final act: he roughly takes down the winger on the break and is duly red-carded. ---
--- 84’ Substitution Scorer of the first goal, Bojan, is coming off for Stephan Ireland ---
(83’) Tottenham are taking a measured appraoch now, trying to make every pass count, but an errant one sees Stoke win possession. The visitors lose it seconds later and it's back with the home side, though there's a major concern: Danny Rose looks to be in some pain but Pochettino has no more substitutions to make.
(81’) The visitors ride out the storm - at least for the moment - by seeing a Tottenham cross over the line for a goal-kick.
(79’) Stoke now need to hang on, but with 11 minutes plus stoppages left, Hughes' team are in for a rough task. Momentum is all with Tottenham now as well as a free-kick opportunity, which Shawcross heads out of the box and Mason volleys over the bar!
--- 77’ Assist The assist came from D. Rose. ---
--- 77’ Goal! WHAT A GOAL FROM CHADLI! TOTTENHAM HAVE HALVED THE LEAD! Chadli slices a shot into the net from a nearly impossible angle, practically perpendicular from the net while volleying a cross in first-time! GAME ON! ---
(76’) WHAT A SAVE FROM BEGOVIC! Lamela takes a superb free-kick that seems destined for the top right corner but Stoke's goalkeeper makes a flying save across the goal to tip it over for a corner!
(75’) Muniesa clips Kane just outside of Stoke's penalty area. This is surely a golden opportunity for Tottenham, who are running out of time here and desperately need to score twice to get something out of this match.
(73’) N'ZONZI JUST WIDE! An absolute calamity of a clearance from Fazio only goes as far as N'Zonzi, less than 10 yards away on the edge of the box. The midfielder somehow fires wide from such a close range!
--- 72’ Yellow card Kaboul goes in the book for a poor sliding tackle he went into immediately after he loses the ball to Walters while foraying forward. ---
(71’) Rose and Walters are in a heated argument after a scuffle by the sideline, where both acted quite physical to try and get the ball, and both have been pulled over the by the referee. He gives them a stern talking to but no cards are shown.
--- 69’ Yellow card R. Mason is cautioned by the referee. ---
(69’) Mason booked for a very poor challenge, sliding in behind Sidwell to take him down on the counter. Not much he can do to argue that one.
(66’) STOKE NEARLY WALTZING THROUGH TOTTENHAM'S DEFENCE! Somehow, somehow, Diouf gets the ball just inside the box and fails to unleash a shot, trying to step closer towards goal which creates chaos as defenders, goalies, and fellow forwards alike all scramble to get a foot on the ball. Eventually, the home side collects it and the chance has gone begging.
--- 65’ Substitution Pochettino makes his final substituion of the game, sending on Adebayor for Capoue in a rather attacking move - though, being two goals down at home, he doesn't really have much of an option. ---
(63’) From one side to another, from the middle out wide - Spurs are doing everything they can think of here to create an opening, but it's all for naught as Capoue takes a shot from a very poor position.
(61’) Another piercing run from Moses leaves Naughton looking quite foolish though his attempt at goal is poor - neither really a shot nor a cross, and Lloris leaves it alone to as it fizzles wide of everyone.
(60’) The past couple of minutes have been kinder for Stoke, who still haven't seen much of the ball at all since halftime but at least have Tottenham outside of their own box for the moment.
(58’) Lamela sends a fantastic delivery right on the head of Kane in the box but the striker's header goes agonizingly wide of the far post! Nearly someething there for Spurs, who keep knocking on the door of the goal.
(57’) Chaos in Stoke's box! Kane and Rose try to get on the end of a ball that spirals out of control in front of Begovic - Muniesa's interception is vital as he clears the ball seconds before the young striker could prod it into the net!
(55’) A good free-kick delivery from Moses into the box is headed out by Kane. The ensuing corner kick is taken by the same Moses, who seems to have recovered from his knock, and finds Shawcross who kicked it well wide.
(53’) Yet another injury for Stoke! It's been a terrible day for Hughes with these so far and now Moses is limping gingerly off the pitch. He may try to stay on before being substituted, especially since any change would be Stoke's last.
(52’) Stoke are not seeing much of the ball but they are doing very well to prevent this spell of possession from Spurs from turning into shots. Their pressing is closing down lanes and clogging up the middle, forcing Spurs out wide with only Kane to target in the middle.
(50’) Though it's very early here in the half, Tottenham are looking brighter than before the break. Mason streaks into the box and tries to pass it to an overlapping Lamela but his pass it cut out well by the defence.
(48’) Diouf is judged to have fouled Dembele and Spurs now have a free kick. It's not terribly deep in Stoke's half but it's whipped into Fazio in the box. There's some appeals after Begovic picks up the ball after Sidwell touches it, but it seems as though the defender miskicked it rather than passed it to his keeper.
(47’) Moses races down the heart of the pitch, blowing past Lamela, and unleashes a curling shot that seemed destined for just a second to ripple the back of the net, but Lloris snatches it out of the air. Kane whips a cross into the box on the other end but Muniesa chests it clear.
--- 46’ Substitution M. Dembélé enters play, replacing C. Eriksen. ---
--- 46’ Substitution A. Townsend is done for the day. E. Lamela is his replacement. ---
(46’) The second half is underway and Pochettino has sent on Lamela and Dembele for Eriksen and Townsend.
Unfortunately for Pochettino, his side truly are not doing much with the ball despite the majority of possession. Without cutting down on errant passing and some better movement up front, Tottenham look like they could be staring at yet another loss at home. There's plenty of time left for something to change but it may take some substitutions to give the home team a spark.
What more could Mark Hughes want? He's seen a superb individual goal from Bojan, a good team effort on the secodn to double his side's lead, and very few genuine chances if any from Tottenham. Stoke are not playing like an away side would, with the notable exception that Spurs are seeing more of the ball.
(45’) The final few minutes of added time occur without much incident, and Stoke head into the break 2-0 up over Tottenham at White Hart Lane.
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card Capoue booked for holding back N'Zonzi on the counter, summing up the home side's frustration well. Stoke carefully keep the ball though they'e looking to build down the flanks, and lose out when a poor pass fails to find Bojan out wide. ---
(45’) Stoke fail to make much of anything from a free-kick deep in Tottenham's half, and Tottenham fail to make much of anything from a free-kick deep in Stoke's half less than thirty seconds later. Five minutes of added time has been announced at White Hart Lane, taking into account the two substitutions and time wasting by Begovic amongst other factors.
(43’) Townsend tries a shot from outside the box but his effort is blocked. Tottenham then work the ball down the right and win a throw-in when Moses is unable to keep the ball in play while defending, but Kane commits a foul in the box just moments later and Stoke can breathe easy with a free-kick.
(42’) Cameron, very high up the pitch, plays a fantastic pass to set Diouf free in the box, but the latter is just offside and the whistle is blown as he readies himself to take a shot.
(41’) Tottenham are keeping the ball now but cannot find a lane to press forward through, as they pass the ball from side to side in the midfield with a sea of red-and-white shirts in front of them.
(39’) Another half-chance for Spurs, with Chadli intercepted in the box so the ball could be cleared for a corner. Eriksen whips it in and it's headed very powerfully out of the box and all the way back to Mason.
(38’) Kaboul whips a cross in from a throw-in, deep in Stoke's half, but it's cleared. Kane thinks he's raced through the defence moments later but he's offside and fails to hit the target regardless. Either way, there are some signs of life here from Tottenham, but they simply need to be much better in possession.
(36’) Pochettino looks to be regretting his risky starting eleven as he already has several players warming up, with Adebayor leading the charge and stretching on the sidelines.
(35’) On a counter Diouf nearly adds a third, racing down the pitch and taking a shot that Fazio slides to deflect out for a corner. Tottenham must be careful now before this game evades them entirely, with the visitors well and truly in better form now.
--- 33’ Assist M. Diouf gave the assist. ---
--- 33’ Goal! STOKE DOUBLE THEIR LEAD! Shawcross is at the heart of this, winning a header over Rose that ends up beautifull in the path of Diouf to cross to a completely open Walters, who makes no mistake from nearly point-blank range. This is a nightmare start for Spurs but a fantastic one from Stoke, who truly deserve their lead. ---
(32’) The visitors are doing tremendously well at the moment, keeping the ball under pressure and winning it very easily whenever they do lose it. Moses races down the left and whips in a cross that sails just over Diouf's head.
(30’) Eriksen sends a flying pass into the middle of the box to find Rose, but the striker just cannot control the ball and loses out. It's good pressure from Spurs deep in Stoke's half but a poor challenge from Mason on Sidwell sees the visitors given a free-kick.
(29’) A few promising forays forward by Stoke in the last couple of minutes, but without any shots at the end of them. Kaboul, however, concedes a corner under pressure, and Shawcross's little flick fails to divert the ball into the net.
(27’) The corner is taken once the substitution happens, with the first one cleared out for another corner, and the second one ending with Bojan winning a free-kick about halfway down the pitch as he's pushed down by Kaboul.
--- 26’ Substitution Stoke will be absolutely rueing their luck today, as Wilson is down holding his knee in visible discomfort. Not even a half hour has been played and yet Hughes is forced into a second defensive substitution as Marc Muniesa is about to come on in his place. ---
--- 24’ Yellow card It seems nearly unbelievable but Begovic is indeed booked for time wasting - halfway through the first half! The goalkeeper was simply taking far too much time to play a free kick, faking one way before backing up and trying another. ---
(23’) Clever from Mason! Stoke were expecting a ball crossed in from Eriksen, but he plays it short to the midfielder, who rifles a shot in from a very long ways out that just barely skims past the near post of Begovic's goal.

(17’) Walters does well on the other end of the pitch, using his body to sheild the ball from Rose who was making a high overlapping run.
(15’) A simply excellent play from from Stoke sees them go from their own box to winning a corner with just three passes, as Moses' shot is deflected out in the box. The ball falls to Wilson in the box but he has his back to goal and can only manipulate it well wide of the post.

(10’) Cameron's substitution comes with Jurgen Klinsmann, coach of the United States Men's National Team, watching on from the stands. Though truly unfortunate for Bardsley, Cameron may be able to seize the opportunity to impress the manager of his national side.

(8’) From one end to the other, as Tottenham now have a free kick. Townsend's initial effort was cleared but only right back to him, and after interchanging passes with Kaboul, he takes a shot on target that goes well over the bar.
--- 6’ Assist The assist came from S. N'Zonzi. ---

(2’) Mason concedes a throw-in that Tottenham quickly regain possession from. As Kane rushes onto a long ball, Shawcross ends up acting too indecisive and concedes a rather cheap throw-in to the home side.

We're less than 3 minutes from kickoff now in what looks to be a very intriguing tie. A minute's silence is just about to take place in honor of Remembrance Day.
It is, however, no surprise to see Harry Kane finally get a start in the Premier League, having scored in the Europa League midweek and opening his account in England last gameday.
It perhaps is not terribly surprising to see Pochettino rotates his side heavily given their Europa League match just three days ago, but there are substantial changes from the team that defeated Asteras Tripolis 2-1 on November 6th: Vertonghen, Lamela, Dier, Dembele, Stambouli and Vorm all drop to the bench today.
Stoke (4-2-3-1): Begovic; Bardsley, Shawcross, Wilson, Pieters; Sidwell, N'Zonzi; Walter, Bojan, Moses; Diouf.
Tottenham (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Naughton, Kaboul, Fazio, Rose; Mason, Capoue; Townsend, Eriksen, Chadli; Kane.
On the other hand, Stoke have only won two of their last five matches in the Premier League, with just one away win out of five this season. What a victory it was, though, as they went to the Etihad Stadium and stunned Manchester City 1-0.
Mauricio Pochettino's men have struggled at home in the Premier League this season, winning just twice out of five matches. Liverpool, West Brom, and Newcastle have all taken maximum points on their travels to the Lane - something that will surely give Mark Hughes inspiration today.

(90’) That will do it! The referee blows the whistle for full time, and Newcastle enjoy a fourth consecutive league win!

(90’) There will be three minutes of stoppage time added on...

(45’) Craig Pawson blows his whistle and that is the last action of the first half!

(27’) STAT ATTACK: Newcastle's victory over Tottenham in their last away match in the Premier League ended a nine match league winless run away from St. James' Park. They were held scoreless seven times over that span.
(25’) GREAT BLOCK! More delightful passing from the hosts, as Morrison picks out Berahino, who links up smartly with Anichebe, playing the striker through on goal. He takes a quick shot as he breaks into the area, but Dummett rushes across to slide in and get an all-important block in.
(23’) Great run forward from Colback, who gets near the top of the area before trying to slip in Sissoko. The midfielder takes the pass, but opts to stop his run and play it back for Ameobi. The move loses its pace, and West Brom get back in numbers to sniff it out.
(21’) The pace has not really been allowed to develop in this match so far, with a plethora of stoppages interrupting the flow. Neither team is keeping possession for extended periods here, looking to break forward soon after they win the ball, without a very high success rate.
(19’) West Brom have really taken the game over now, since the early surge from Newcastle. A quick throw in deep in the attacking half comes to Dorrans, who nudges forward and sends a cross into the centre. Brunt does very well to meet it, but his header glances narrowly over the bar.
(17’) WONDERFUL BUILD UP! Brunt and Morrison prove vital in keeping the hosts in possession in the attacking half, with the latter picking out Anichebe at the top of the box. The striker lays it off for Berahino, who hits it first time and forces an uncomfortable save from Krul, who tips it over the bar for a corner.
(15’) STAT ATTACK: With three wins, three defeats and four draws from their first 10 matches, West Brom have the exact same record they did at this stage last season. They also have the exact same goal differential, of zero.
(13’) Much better from the hosts! Mulumbu and Wisdom link up well along the right wing, with the midfielder taking a return pass, and beating Colback to the byline. He sends a wonderful cross in towards the far post, but Pocognoli arrives just a second too late, failing to make contact with the ball before Newcastle scramble it clear.
(11’) OFF THE BAR! Magnificent attempt from Sammy Ameobi, as he drifts into the centre and takes a pass at the top of the box. He turns and squares up towards goal, and has Krul beaten with his shot, but strikes it off the crossbar!
(9’) Another free kick for the visitors, in a virtual identical position, as Ameobi shows some wonderfully quick feet to force Dorrans into a tackle. Cabella delivers, but it is put behind at the near post for a corner. The Frenchman delivers again from the set piece, but some good defending from Pocognoli eventually sniffs out the chance.
(7’) Another promising chance for Newcastle comes from a set piece. Cabella takes a free kick to the left of the penalty area and sends a wonderful ball into the box, which Dummett manages to meet at the far post, but heads over the bar.
(5’) Colback takes the free kick, but a strong defensive header sees Dorrans clear the danger. The visitors get back on the ball, keeping possession nicely in midfield, passing into space which has caused the hosts some problems early on.
(3’) The two teams feel each other out in the early minutes, with possession changing hands often. Mulumbu concedes a free kick as he takes out Remy Cabella, which gives the visitors their first chance of the match from a set piece situation.
(1’) West Brom kick off and we are underway at the Hawthorns! The hosts, moving left to right, are in their white tops and blue shorts, with Newcastle in their dark blue shirts with light green bottoms.
Steven Taylor is a late injury absentee for Alan Pardew, which brings Frenchman Massadio Haidara into the starting line-up. Remy Cabella replaces the injured Gabriel Obertan in midfield, while Ayoze Perez gets the start over Papiss Cisse, who is fit, but will start on the substitute's bench.
NEWCASTLE SUBS: R. Taylor, Williamson, Anita, Cisse, Gouffran, Elliot, Armstrong.
NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Krul; Janmaat, Coloccini, Haidara, Dummett; Colback, Abeid; Cabella, Sissoko, Ameobi; Ayoze Perez.
Coach Alan Irvine has to make due without the injured Silvestre Varela and Jonas Olsson, while Craig Gardner misses out due to suspension, being replaced by Youssouf Mulumbu. The most interesting change comes up top, where Victor Anichebe gets the start at striker, with Saido Berahino slotting in behind, being asked to work off the Nigerian striker. The move pushes in form midfielder Stephane Sessegnon to the bench.
WEST BROM SUBS: Baird, Yacob, Myhill, Gamboa, McAuley, Sessegnon, Samaras.
WEST BROM (4-2-3-1): Foster; Wisdom, Dawson, Lescott, Pocognoli; Mulumbu, Morrison; Dorrans, Berahino, Brunt; Anichebe.
The teams have been announced, so let us have ourselves a look at the starting line-ups:
It is amazing what a difference a few weeks can make. Alan Pardew was left for dead a month ago, with fans calling for his head. Fast forward to today, and Newcastle have won four straight matches in all competitions, which includes impressive victories over Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester City in the League Cup. As they get set to take the pitch at the Hawthorns, Pardew's job seems secure for now, ironically enough, as it was a 3-1 loss away to West Bromwich four years ago that got Chris Hughton fired. The rest is history, as they say.
Alan Irvine has turned West Bromwich into a very hard team to beat. The Baggies stumbled through the first month of the season, but have lost just once since then. It remains essential for them to turn the Hawthorns back into the fortress it once was, after winning just four games in front of their fans last season. They have only managed one home victory through the first quarter of the campaign, and with matches against Chelsea and Arsenal looming, it will be very important to pick up three points over a resurgent Newcastle team today.
Good day Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to West Midlands. The Hawthorns is our venue today, as West Bromwich host Newcastle, with both teams hoping to move into the top half of the table. I am Alex Moretto and I will be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens!

That's it for me then on what turned out to be a gripping night in Wales. I've been Keeghann Sinanan and it's been fun!
Sanchez appeared to have dragged Arsenal over the line with his 63rd minute opener, but once again this week, the Gunners drop points from a winning position. Wenger's side are in sixth, staring down a gap of 12 points on league leaders Chelsea.
A massive, massive result for the home side, who leapfrog Arsenal by a point to move into fifth place. They fully deserved this win, defending doggedly and ruthlessly exploiting Arsenal when the opportunities presented themselves. What a turnaround for them!
(90’) THERE WAS A CHANCE! Oxlade-Chamberlain skins his man on the right, and plays a ball into Wilshere inside the six-yard area...but he can't make contact on the ball. And that's it! Swansea win!
(90’) Free kick given after a failed Arsenal corner. The Gunners also had an appeal for a handball rightfully go uncalled. Swansea will reset with the set piece, and they're clearly in no hurry.
(90’) Into the third of four added minutes, and Arsenal win a corner, which goes absolutely nowhere. Ki hacks it clear, and Swansea are so close to a vital victory against the Gunners!
(90’) In his final roll of the dice, Wenger throws on Yaya Sanogo for Chambers. And his first contribution is to bowl over his marker and concede a foul. Time is not on Arsenal's side.
--- 90’ Substitution Y. Sanogo enters play, replacing C. Chambers. ---
--- 90’ Yellow card M. Barrow is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) YET ANOTHER yellow card here, as Barrow is booked for dissent. That takes the number of bookings in this game into double figures. I guess the rain does that to people.
(89’) Lovely pass from Sanchez. The Chilean lifts the ball over the defensive line for Walcott to chase, but the lack of game time clearly shows with a rusty first touch that sees the chance collapse.
--- 87’ Substitution L. Britton enters play, replacing T. Carroll. ---
(87’) There's going to be a yellow card for Alexis for dissent. He went down enthusiastically looking for a free kick, but the referee waved play on, to his fury. Swansea earn an opportunity to milk the clock.
--- 86’ Yellow card A. Sánchez is yellow-carded. ---
(86’) The ball has been camped in the Swansea half since the Gomis goal, but the home side are defending in great numbers. Arsenal are struggling to find a way through the walls of white.
(85’) On the flip side, Arsenal have recovered the most points in the league from losing positions this season. There's some resilience in there, but why do they need to have their backs against the wall to perform? Can they do it again in the last five minutes plus stoppage time?
(84’) Wenger will again face criticism of his side's display. And to be honest, if this result holds, or if they drop points from a winning position for the second time this week, he will deserve every word of it. It boggles the mind how fragile this side can be.
(82’) And what about the substitutions by Monk? Two strokes of genius. Barrow won the free kick for their equaliser, and now Gomis, barely a minute off the bench, struck the go-ahead goal.
(80’) I'm sorry, but Chambers has been roasted on a spit in this game. Forget the multiple skinnings by Montero - he was lucky not to concede a penalty and nearly coughed up a one-on-one with a poor back header. Wenger throws on Wilshere and Walcott as his side chase a way back into the game.
--- 79’ Substitution M. Flamini is replaced with J. Wilshere. ---
--- 79’ Substitution T. Walcott enters the game and replaces A. Ramsey. ---
--- 78’ Assist The assist came from J. Montero. ---
--- 78’ Goal! SWANSEA HAVE ANOTHER! WHAT A TURNAROUND! Montero leaves Chambers for dead once again, and clips a lovely cross into the box. No one in a yellow shirt bothers to defend it, leaving new introduction Gomis with all the time in the world to rise and plant a header home! ---
(77’) Gibbs was the one who gave up that set piece, and he was booked for his troubles. Impactful debut for Barrow too, whose speed through the centre forced the concession of the free kick. Meanwhile, Gomis cones on for Bony.
--- 76’ Substitution B. Gomis enters the game and replaces W. Bony. ---
--- 75’ Goal! MAGNIFICENT GOAL! SWANSEA LEVEL! A free kick from at least 25 yards is curled over the wall and into the top corner by Sigurdsson. He has had a mixed afternoon, but he won't forget that goal in a hurry! ---
--- 74’ Yellow card K. Gibbs receives a yellow card. ---
(72’) Swansea waste a corner, which falls right to the Arsenal defence. The Gunners have shipped league goals left, right and centre from set pieces, so the hosts really need to be doing better with those opportunities.
(70’) This game is so finely poised at the moment. Sanchez's goal is the best thing that could have happened, since it forces Swansea forward to get back into the contest. That will leave opportunities for the Gunners to counter again. We may be in for a cracking final 20 minutes.
(68’) First substitution of the game from either manager, as Emnes departs for Barrow, who makes his Swansea debut. The dreadlocked winger was occasionally able to use his speed to good effect out wide in this match. Barrow will be more likely to cut inside, given that he's a left footer playing on the right.
--- 67’ Substitution M. Barrow enters the game and replaces M. Emnes. ---
(67’) So, if you're counting, that's eight goals in as many Premier League games for Alexis, and 12 in his last 14. Definitely getting some Suarez in 2013-14 vibes from the Chilean in the way that he's carrying his team.
(65’) NEARLY AN INSTANT RESPONSE! Montero skips past Chambers again, and squares to Bony who is in almost an identical position from which Sanchez scored moments ago. However, his finish lacks the conviction of the Chilean's and it bobbles wide.
--- 63’ Yellow card T. Carroll receives a yellow card. ---
--- 63’ Assist The assist came from D. Welbeck. ---
--- 63’ Goal! ARSENAL LEAD - AND GUESS WHO SCORED? Bony coughs up the ball and the Gunners are devastating on the break. Welbeck speeds down the right and cuts back on the byline once again. This time, he has plenty of options to pick out, and he squares for Alexis, who sweeps it home! ---
--- 62’ Yellow card C. Chambers receives a yellow card. ---
(62’) Yet another booking here, and it unsurprisingly goes to Flamini. For better or for worse, the midfielder has been very busy in this game, and one of his traditional two-footers is immediately penalized.
(60’) The rain continues to fall over the Liberty Stadium, and Cazorla attempts to manipulate the conditions to his advantage with a low drive that skids off the turf and is saved by Fabianski. Crucially, the Polish keeper smothers the loose ball before Sanchez can follow up.
(58’) Opportunity for Welbeck to make inroads into the box after he pivoted away from Taylor on the byline, but his attempted cutback is too predictable. Sometimes, the Arsenal striker is too passive.
(56’) Mertesacker goes in late on Bony and gets booked. The giant German doesn't pick up too many bookings - this is his second of the season. The yellow cards starting to pile up in this game.
--- 55’ Yellow card P. Mertesacker receives a yellow card. ---
(54’) Both sides have been dependent on their wing wizards for the majority of their attacks this evening. Montero and Oxlade-Chamberlain have both not shied away from taking on their man, but the end product has been lacking.
(52’) Swansea come close to carving Arsenal apart on the break, as the Gunners are caught short at the back following a failed corner. However Montero, leading the charge, is unable to pick out his man.
--- 50’ Yellow card A. Williams receives a yellow card. ---
(50’) Cazorla and Williams go down in a heap after a challenge. Replays show that the Swansea defender was the aggressor with a bad challenge and to add insult to injury, he's booked.
(48’) Chance right from the off! Oxlade-Chamberlain picks up where he left off, taking an Alexis feed in stride but firing his effort right down the throat of Swansea keeper Fabianski.
(46’) Here we go again!
So, goalless at the break here at the Liberty Stadium. Arsenal began to force more and more pressure in the Swansea half towards the end, but they have still struggled to fashion any real chances. Swansea have defended well, but their attacking endeavour has dried up as the half progressed. Let's hope for more goalmouth action in the second half. Stay tuned.
--- 45’ +1 Yellow card A. Ramsey is yellow-carded. ---
(45’) Ramsey shows splendid technique to volley a high ball towards the bottom corner, missing by inches. He's not been near his form of this time last season, the Welshman, but the ability is clearly still there.
(44’) Welbeck flicks a header to the far side, and Chambers is racing to get on the end of it. However, he can't get any purchase on the shot thanks to the defensive attention of Montero.
(42’) Half time is moments away. Wenger should be wanting his team to show more fire and directness - perhaps pointing to Oxlade-Chamberlain as an example. Monk will be satisfied that they've managed to stymie Arsenal, but he'll surely want his side to push forward more, given that the points are very much there for the taking.
--- 41’ Yellow card Sung-Yong Ki gets yellow. ---
(40’) Welbeck uses his hand to control a long pass from Monreal. Not pretty stuff from Arsenal, but then again, there's been nothing in this game that would ever make it on a highlight reel.
(38’) Taylor slides in late on Oxlade-Chamberlain, and is promptly booked for his challenge. Now he has to walk a tightrope against a player that will keep running right at him.
--- 37’ Yellow card N. Taylor goes into the referee's book. ---
(37’) Swansea have a 53-47 per cent edge in possession, an encouraging statistic for Monk and his side, given that they were virtually starved of the ball in the opening ten minutes of this game. Now, if we could have a chance or two...
(35’) SZCZESNY SAVES! Montero wriggles his way past his man after a mistake from Chambers, and he feeds Emnes down the right. The winger has the space for the shot and lets fly, but it's right down the throat of the Pole, who still can't hold onto it!
(33’) Second penalty shout for Swansea in the first half. Emnes fires a cross into the hand of Gibbs on the edge of the box and though the appeals go up from the stands, Phil Dowd is unmoved once again.
(31’) The game is momentarily delayed as Cazorla is tended to by the physios for an injury picked up. Arsenal will wait to take a corner, won by the persistence of the Ox on the right-hand side.
(29’) Arsenal are showing more purpose in their buildup, but it's still a little too intricate from them. Oxlade-Chamberlain at least is attempting to take players on, and Arsenal would do well to feed him at the moment. He looks hungry.
(27’) Ramsey wins a corner thanks to a deflection, and Fabianski shows good command of his area to nab the ball from the resulting delivery, before he is fouled by Chambers. Some fire to this game now.
(25’) Taylor gets the better of Chambers out wide and spots Rangel making a move infield. He feeds the Spaniard who takes aim from the top of the box, but he can't get his shot through a sea of yellow shirts.
(23’) That's the second nervy moment for Chambers in this match. There's a reactionary side to his game that sees him occasionally concede mistakes like that and rack up yellow cards like they're going out of style. Perhaps just the impetuousness of youth though, and there's a lot to like about the aggression and versatility that the former Southampton man brings to the table.
(21’) WAS THAT A PENALTY? Bony controlled Emnes' cross inside the box and Chambers barged into his back. Phil Dowd waves play on though, to the fury of the home fans. That was a really close call, and I would not have faulted the referee if he had signaled a spot kick!
(19’) There's been a consistent rain over South Wales, and it has made the pitch very slippery, but not soggy. In theory, this should help the ball zip along the surface but at the moment, it only looks to be stunting the chance creation from both sides.
(17’) The quality in the final third is really lacking from both sides. Arsenal and Swansea are, on reputation at least, two of the Premier League's best exponents of passing football. It's lead nowhere so far though.
(15’) A weak back header from Chambers almost leaves Szczesny stranded against Montero, but the Arsenal defence manages to recover just in time to ward off the fleet-footed Ecuadorian.
(13’) Cazorla fakes a shot and instead feeds Gibbs on the overlap. The England left back drills in a low cross for Sanchez, but the Chilean can't find the goalscoring position that he needs amongst a sea of bodies.
(11’) Swansea are starting to explore their attacking options more now, and are forcing Arsenal to organise defensively. There's always the risk of the Gunners pushing too high up and getting caught on the break.
(9’) Some caution there for the Arsenal defence to deal with as Oxlade-Chamberlain gives away a careless free kick, which Sigurdsson swings into a dangerous area. Chambers heads away with authority.
(7’) Arsenal have been camped in the opposition half for almost the entirety of this game, but they've not created anything meaningful with the ball. Swansea are biding their time for the moment.
(5’) Williams has seemingly shaken off that knock, but Monk will be keeping an eye on him. Arsenal resume the game as they started it, in complete control of possession, playing patiently.
(3’) Already some problems for Monk to ponder in defence. Williams has pulled up in pain, and he may not be able to continue. With Bartley already making a rare start, the Swansea boss will not want to be forced into another alteration at the back.
(1’) Here we go!
Only one change from Wenger following the Anderlecht game, and it's an enforced one. Mikel Arteta's injury means that Mathieu Flamini comes in to assume the deepest midfield position. Surprising that there weren't other alterations, but Arsenal did play well for the best part of an hour against the Belgians and in Alexis Sanchez, they have one of Europe's most in-form players.
Lukasz Fabianski starts as expected in goal against his former club. Monk also makes three changes to his XI following the 0-0 draw against Everton, with Kyle Bartley, Tom Carroll and Marvin Emnes coming in for Federico Fernandez, Jonjo Shelvey and Wayne Routledge.
Arsenal subs: Martinez, Bellerin, Rosicky, Wilshere, Podolski, Walcott, Sanogo.
Arsenal (4-1-4-1): Szczesny; Chambers, Mertesacker, Monreal, Gibbs; Flamini; Alexis, Ramsey, Cazorla, Oxlade-Chamberlain; Welbeck.
Swansea subs: Tremmel, Tiendalli, Amat, Britton, Fulton, Barrow, Gomis.
Swansea (4-3-3): Fabianski; Rangel, Bartley, Williams, Taylor; Ki, Carroll, Sigurdsson; Emnes, Montero, Bony.
Swansea have not won agains Arsenal in five games, but their home form has been strong this season. They've taken 10 points from 15 on offer and their defensive record at the Liberty Stadium is the joint second best in the league, with only three goals conceded.
The Gunners boss is facing all of the usual complaints - tactics, injuries and transfers. There's a growing disillusionment among Arsenal fans that the side's ability seems to yet again be capped at a top-four finish. All of their four league wins this season has come against sides currently in the bottom six of the table - though Arsenal have recovered seven points from losing positions this season, a league high.
Meanwhile, Arsene Wenger has been forced to step into the ring to defend himself against more criticism after another baffling performance from his side. The Gunners coughed up a three-goal lead to draw 3-3 at home against Anderlecht midweek in the Champions League.
Under Garry Monk, Swansea have made their best-ever start to a Premier League season, with 15 points from their opening 10 games. It could have been even better for the Swans, given that they've dropped eight points from winning positions this season, joint most in the division.
Hello and welcome to the Liberty Stadium, as Swansea host Arsenal. These two sides are separated by only two points in the table, and have had contrasting fortunes this season. I'm Keeghann Sinanan, your guide for this afternoon's action in Wales.

My name is Ben Cullimore and it's been an absolute pleasure describing the action to you today. Until next time, goodbye!
What a win for Newcastle! It's their first against Liverpool in over two and a half years and temporarily sends them into the top half of the table. They are the deserved winners too, after another lacklustre display from the visitors left them with little chance of leaving St. James' Park with all three points. They struggled in the final third of the pitch, with poor passing letting them down from start to finish. Newcastle defended incredibly well, sitting back before embarking on swift counter attacks that Liverpool found hard to deal with.
FULL-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 1-0 LIVERPOOL
(90’) Cabella and Sissoko link up well on the left wing before the latter cuts inside and into the Liverpool penalty area, but Skrtel is there to make an important interception to deny the French midfielder the opportunity to get a shot away on goal.
(90’) Lovren loses the ball near the halfway line, gifting possession back to Newcastle. They head towards the corner flag but are unable to keep the ball in play and end up sending it out for a goal kick.
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
--- 89’ Yellow card Abeid dispossesses Moreno deep inside the Newcastle half of the pitch before setting up Cabella down the right wing, who sprints forward before being brought to the ground by a poor challenge from Lovren near the corner flag. ---
(88’) Balotelli whips in a lovely cross from the left wing that finds Moreno on the edge of the penalty area. The left-back tries to pull off an acrobatic scissor kick but he ends up missing the ball, allowing Krul to collect it comfortably.
(86’) After receiving medical attention for a few moments, it seems as if Sissoko is going to be able to continue.
(85’) Sissoko and Borini clash as they battle for a high ball, leaving the Newcastle man in a heap on the floor and in some discomfort.
(83’) Fantastic play again from the hosts! They break forward through Sissoko, who plays a great one-two with Cabella before firing a shot from a tight angle that Mignolet is just about able to save with one hand.
(81’) Great play by Newcastle! Perez sprints down the right flank before sending a deep cross that finds Cabella on the edge of the Liverpool box. He sets himself up before firing a fantastic shot that only just clears the top of the crossbar by a few inches.
--- 80’ Substitution Brendan Rodgers has decided to make another attacking change for Liverpool as we enter the final 10 minutes of the game, with Lambert coming on to replace Coutinho. ---
--- 79’ Yellow card Colback goes flying into Gerrard near the halfway line, resulting in a yellow card, which is Newcastle's fourth of the game. ---
(77’) What a chance for Newcastle! Liverpool are caught in possession and the hosts are able to break away on a swift counter attack. It's two against one with Perez and Cabella in the visitors' half of the pitch, and they play a nice one-two between one another before the latter bursts forward and fires a low shot that is brilliantly tipped around the post by the feet of Mignolet.
(75’) Gerrard sends a great lofted pass over to Sterling, who bursts into the Liverpool box from the right wing before Krul flies out to parry the ball out for a corner.
--- 73’ Goal! GOAL! Newcastle have finally gone ahead thanks to a defensive mistake from Liverpool! The hosts break away down the left wing through Dummett, who cuts inside before teeing up Sissoko inside the penalty area. He turns before sending a deft pass towards Perez, which is cut out by Moreno, but the left-back fails to clear the ball, allowing the striker to steal it from under his nose and fire it into the back of the net. ---
--- 72’ Yellow card J. Henderson receives a yellow card. ---
(72’) Henderson cynically pulls Coloccini to the ground as is shown a yellow card by the referee, much to the annoyance of the Liverpool midfielder.
(71’) Sterling brings down a lofted ball wonderfully well on the edge of the box and chests it into the path of Borini, who fires a low first-time shot that only just misses the far post by a few inches.
(70’) Countinho finds himself in space down the left wing and cuts inside towards the edge of the Newcastle box before teeing up Gerrard, but his pass is poor and ends up going behind his captain, gifting possession back to the hosts.
(68’) Dummett darts down the left flank before attempting to whip a low cross into the Liverpool penalty area, but it's comfortably volleyed away from danger by Skrtel.
--- 66’ Substitution Liverpool have decided to make their first substitution of the game, with Borini coming on for Allen. ---
--- 66’ Substitution Newcastle have also decided to make an attacking change, with Ameobi making way for Cabella. ---
(64’) Colback and Sissoko play a nice one-two between one another 25 yards out before the latter darts towards the edge of the penalty area, but Johnson is there to cut out the danger with a great tackle.
--- 62’ Yellow card It's all getting rather heated! Abeid and Balotelli clash before Janmaat decides to bring the Liverpool striker crashing to the ground with a terrible high challenge that earns himself a yellow card. ---
(60’) Newcastle push forward down the left flank but find each of their attempts to penetrate the Liverpool penalty area stopped by a plethora of red shirts camped in front of them. Dummett finally finds himself in space on the edge of the box and decides to fire a rocket of a shot towards goal, but it ends up clearing the crossbar by a foot or so.
(58’) What a save by Krul! Gerrard picks up the ball on the right hand side of the penalty area and whips in a lovely cross that finds Coutinho on the edge of the six-yard box. His headed effort looks to be heading for the top corner of the goal but he's denied by a fantastic save from the Newcastle goalkeeper, before the linesman raises his flag for offside.
(56’) Balotelli finds himself in space just outside of the Newcastle box and decides to fire a curling shot towards goal, but it's saved comfortably by Krul.
(54’) Balotelli sends a great ball out to Sterling on the right wing, and the youngster tries to twist and turn his way into the Newcastle penalty area but he finds himself outnumbered by black and white shirts and ends up losing possession.
(52’) Both sides are battling for possession in the middle of the pitch, with neither able to fashion a chance on goal due to poor passing from all involved.
(50’) Balotelli fires a bouncing shot from the resulting free kick but it's dealt with well by Krul.
--- 49’ Yellow card Sissoko flies into Allen with his studs showing, resulting in a yellow card for the Newcastle midfielder. ---
(48’) Johnson loses the ball on the edge of the Liverpool penalty area and gifts possession to Perez in a dangerous position. He tries to thread a pass into the path of Aarons but Lovren is there to cut out the danger with a great tackle in front of goal.
--- 46’ Substitution Newcastle have decided to make a substitution during the half-time break, with Perez coming on for Cisse. ---
(46’) And we're underway once again!
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half.
It's been a very subdued first half in which neither side have had too many chances on goal. Liverpool have enjoyed the vast majority of possession but are finding it difficult to penetrate a resolute and well-organised Newcastle defensive line, whilst their passing in the final third of the pitch has let them down on several occasions. Both sides will have to up their game in the second half if they are to come away with all three points today.
HALF-TIME: NEWCASTLE UNITED 0-0 LIVERPOOL
(45’) After plenty of pushing and shoving and arguing with the referee, the free kick is finally taken by Cisse but he ends up blasting it over the top of the crossbar and out for a goal kick.
--- 45’ Yellow card Steven Taylor tries to put off Mignolet by standing in front of the Liverpool goalkeeper to block his view but ends up earning himself a yellow card as a result. ---
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be two minutes of added time.
--- 44’ Yellow card Sissoko breaks away through the middle of the pitch and embarks on a driving run forward. He makes it to the edge of the penalty area before he is brought to the ground by Skrtel, who is then awarded a yellow card by the referee. ---
(42’) Again, Liverpool try to push forward down the right wing through another lofted ball forward, but the pass is poor and gifts possession back to Newcastle, who are finding it easy to deal with the visitors in the final third of the pitch.
(40’) What a header by Skrtel! Liverpool push forward and earn themselves a corner, which is curled into the penalty area by Gerrard. His cross finds the head of the Slovakian defender, who is completely unmarked on the edge of the six-yard box, but his effort ends up flying just wide of the near post.
(38’) Great chance for Newcastle! The hosts win a corner and it's fired in towards the back post where it finds Cisse, who is just about able to get a touch on the ball. His shot seems to be heading for the back of the net but it's headed away off the line by Johnson.
(36’) Abeid decides to fire a shot from the resulting set-piece, but his effort is blocked by the Liverpool wall and goes out for a corner. The Algerian youngster then sends the corner in low but his cross is poor and it's cleared away by Gerrard.

The recapturing of Sigurdsson has been a crucial influence in Monk's strong start to his first season as full time Swansea manager. The Icelandic midfielder struggled to make an impression after leaving Wales in 2012, but having already made seven assists this term, the 25 year old has wasted no time in settling back into familiar surroundings.
A victory over Swansea, a team that has never beaten them in a league match, will give the home side their third win in a row. However, under Garry Monk's rule the Swans have earned plenty of plaudits for their free-flowing attacking football, a style which Martinez will undoubtedly appreciate.
Martinez's men have made an uninspiring start to the campaign, the defence has struggled the most with 13 goals already being shipped in Everton's first five games of the season, as an aged backline looked extremely vulnerable.

It's all over and City are derby winners for the fourth time in a row thanks to a superb goal from Aguero midway through the second half. Despite Smalling's red card at the end of the first period, today's clash was an incredibly close encounter, with United's makeshift defence putting in a fantastic shift to deny the hosts the opportunity to further their lead. The visitors then became the better side as the game wore on but, despite their best efforts, City's strong and disciplined defence were just too strong for them to deal with.

After a disappointing start to the season in which they only won one of their opening five Premier League games, the United ship has been steadied somewhat in recent weeks, and the Red Devils now find themselves with the opportunity to extend their unbeaten run to five league games if they avoid defeat here today. They showed grit and determination to come from behind to draw against both West Bromwich Albion and Chelsea in their last two league games, and a win today will move them up to sixth place in the table, just one point behind their local rivals.
It's been a mixed start to the new league campaign for the hosts, who head into today's clash in a respectable third place but already nine points behind leaders Chelsea. After going three games without a win a month ago - a run that was kick-started by a poor defeat at home to Stoke City - Manuel Pellegrini's men bounced back in fine fashion by winning three league games on the trot, but last weekend's 2-1 loss against West Ham United showed that there is still a lot of work to be done if they are to catch such an impressive Chelsea side. The injury that David Silva picked up whilst on Capital One Cup duty during the week rubbed salt in their wounds, and the Spaniard's absence today is guaranteed to be noticeable.

Thank you for joining me, Alex Stewart, for this afternoon's LIVE coverage of Aston Villa 1-2 Tottenham Hotspur. Enjoy the rest of your weekend!
The game threatened to boil over at several points, but it was Harry Kane who kept his cool and found the net to give Spurs a vital away win that relieves some of the pressure on manager Pochettino.
Weimann had opened the scoring for the home team, their first goal in over nine hours of play, but Chadli grabbed one back from a corner after Benteke had been sent off for slapping Mason.

We could see the net bulge a few times this evening, if history is anything to go by. The last three Monday night Premier League games involving Palace have yielded 17 goals. Palace drew one and lost two of those, while Sunderland haven’t won any of their last 20 Monday night matches in the top flight.
This is not a happy hunting ground for the Black Cats - they have only won one league game away to Palace in 33 years, and are without a win in their last five clashes against the Eagles.
Palace, meanwhile, went the whole of October without a win, losing to Hull and Chelsea before throwing away a 2-0 lead over West Brom last weekend as the game ended 2-2.
Sunderland’s only victory of the season already feels like a long time ago. Since their 3-1 win over Stoke they’ve been humiliated 8-0 by Southampton and lost 2-0 at home to Arsenal thanks to some defensive howlers.

Hull defended admirably, and third choice keeper Eldin Jakupovic helped keep them out long enough to secure a second away draw in as many weeks.
