(56’) The defender makes his way off the pitch and looks to be alright. Play finally resumes with a goal kick, and less than 30 seconds later Bruce goes down after Balotelli catches him with a high forearm, the striker lunging in as he tried to win a ball in the air.
--- 55’ Yellow card R. Sterling is yellow-carded. ---
(54’) Hull have pressed incredibly well and Liverpool are completely out of answers at the moment. There is a stoppage in play now, as Sterling catches Brady late. The defender is down in pain and the training staff is out onto the pitch to take a look.
(52’) At the moment, Liverpool appear to be plagued by a lack of movement up front. They seems to have figured out a way to pass their way into the final third, but there is no one making themselves available for a pass when they get there.
--- 50’ Yellow card H. Ben Arfa goes into the referee's book. ---
(50’) The hosts are keeping possession much better, and look to be much more patient in their build up as opposed to throwing every ball forward in the hopes of getting a goal. Hull are pressing high up the pitch, and Ben Arfa slides in to try and win a ball, earning himself a yellow card.
(48’) Superb defending! Much better from Liverpool in their build up, as Allen sends a ball through for Sterling. Bruce stays with him stride for stride, careful not to concede a penalty and gets a vital block on the winger's shot.
(46’) Mario Balotelli strolls out late for the second half, but we are finally back underway at Anfield.
Hull will be content with their performance in the first half. They have essentially asked Liverpool "can you break us down?" So far, the answer is no. The hosts have plenty of players on the bench to counter with, including the likes of Coutinho, Markovic, Henderson and of course, Lambert is waiting in the wings with Balotelli again struggling to make an impact.
HALF TIME: LIVERPOOL 0-0 HULL CITY. It has been an unimaginative first 45 minutes at Anfield, with nothing much to cheer about for fans from either side. There has been little pace to the match, which has made for difficult viewing. A goal would really do wonders to help open things up, so hopefully it comes sooner rather than later.
(45’) Liverpool do take the corner, but Jakupovic is able to collect and referee Neil Swarbrick blows his whistle to signal the end of the first half.
(45’) Liverpool win a corner off a free kick, courtesy of a lovely delivery from Gerrard. We have played the two minutes of extra time and Steve Bruce is livid with the referee, arguing that the corner should not be taken.
(45’) DEFLECTED JUST WIDE! Hull are taking over these final minutes, with some more exquisite build up play. Ben Arfa picks out the run of Livermore, who lays a pass off for Hernandez. The striker sends a clever back heel pass to El Mohamady on the right. His cross in is partially cleared, but only as far as Huddlestone, who sees his shot deflected inches wide at the near post!
(43’) ALMOST AN OPENER! Incredible stuff from Ben Arfa who breaks into the area and slides to keep the ball in play. From the ground, he cuts it back for Livermore in the centre, showing some wonderful inventiveness, and the midfielder hits the shot first time, but straight at Mignolet who makes a comfortable catch.
(41’) Lallana is growing into the match now. He picks up the ball in midfield and darts forward. He looks to chip a pass through for Balotelli, and the idea is strong, but the execution fails him as Bruce is in a good position to head clear.
--- 40’ Yellow card T. Huddlestone receives a yellow card. ---
(39’) There have been a few flashes of trickery from Liverpool, but aside from that it has all been very straightforward for Hull in defence. There has been little threat posed by the Reds going forward, and even less so from the visitors who have not possessed the ball in the final third for quite some time now.
(37’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool beat Hull City 2-0 in Anfield last season, both goals being scored by players no longer with the team – Daniel Agger and Luis Suarez.
(35’) CLEVER! Much more like it from Liverpool. Lovely build up play as Lallana and Moreno link up on the left. A nifty one-two sees them break into the area, and the midfielder chips a cross into the danger area with the outside of his foot. Again it is not attacked well, however, and the ball is scrambled clear by Hull.
(33’) There has been no steady flow to this match, which has made it near impossible for either side to generate any momentum in attack. The lack of pace as a result has made for some uninspiring attacking play in the opening half hour.
(31’) Chester commits a foul which gives Liverpool a free kick along the left from 35 yards out. Gerrard takes, and sends a terrific ball into the area for Lovren. The defender looked to have escaped his marker but just does not attack the ball anywhere close to well enough as it runs behind for a goal kick.
(29’) NEARLY DISASTER! Alex Bruce does not get nearly enough behind his back pass, giving Balotelli a real chase. The striker lunges towards the ball, but Jakupovic slides in just ahead of him to clear the threat. Liverpool keep possession, until Joe Allen's shot flies wide at the near post.
(27’) This is a game in desperate need of some more imagination in attack. There is plenty of quality in both sides up top, but it just is not showing at the moment. Can gets forward on the ball as Liverpool are up in numbers, but a poor pass for Balotelli sees the striker's touch run safely into the hands of Jakupovic.
(25’) Brilliant one touch passing from Hull City as the trio of Diame, El Mohamady and Ben Arfa work the ball up the pitch along the right. The latter gets on the end of a return pass behind Moreno, but some good defensive work by Liverpool sees the attack fizzle out.
(23’) STAT ATTACK: Liverpool have not had a scoreless draw in 48 Premier League matches, the longest current streak of any side.
(21’) Balotelli drops into a deeper role in order to see a bit more time on the ball. He takes a pass and sends a long, searching pass forward for Sterling, but it runs far too close to Jakupovic who collects with ease. Liverpool are doing a splendid job of winning the ball back, but it is all breaking down at the moment in the final third.
(19’) The visitors are struggling a bit at the moment to transition into attack, while Liverpool cannot find a way through themselves. Both midfield groups are doing very well to prevent a quick break, which has made for a cagey start to this match.
(17’) Relentless pressure on the ball applied by Liverpool in midfield has the fans buzzing! Hull keep possession well and look to push forward. Huddlestone can barely pass the ball off before Diame is swarmed by three Liverpool players, eventually giving the ball away. A poor pass forward by Allen sees the chance come to nothing, however.
(15’) Hull manage to get themselves into attack, looking for a bit of a response, and Ben Arfa does well to hold off a defender and slide in El Mohamady on the right. His cross in nearly picks out Diame, but some good defensive work from Skrtel sees that the danger is cleared.
(13’) SUPER MARIO! Balotelli makes a wonderfully timed run behind the defence and a splendid ball from Sterling sends the striker in on goal at a bit of a difficult angle. The Italian forward squares up to goal and forces a fine save by Jakupovic at the near post, as he punches the ball behind for a corner.
(11’) STAT ATTACK: In 18 all-time meetings between the two teams in competitive matches, Hull City only have one win, which came last season at the KC Stadium, while Liverpool have 13.
(9’) OFF THE LINE! Liverpool have a chance from the corner, and Gerrard's delivery is met by Lovren. The central defender's header is very strong, as he beats Jakupovic, but not El Mohamady, who heads clear at the near post.
(7’) Anfield shouts for a penalty as Gerrard picks out the run of Sterling. The speedy winger puts pressure on Chester, who looks to push out into the back of the forward on the edge of the penalty area. Sterling goes to ground and grabs the ball looking for a foul, but the assistant referee calls for a free kick the other way for a handball.
(5’) We have our first lengthy stoppage of the match as Can is down in significant pain as Huddlestone slides in to win a loose ball and catches the Liverpool player on the follow through. The medical staff is out to take a look, as Can gets to his feet quite gingerly, limping over to the touch line.
(3’) Hull have begun the game quite well, moving the ball about with confidence. They stretch Liverpool at the back, but a good outlet pass relieves the pressure. Mario Balotelli does very well to hold the ball up, beat a defender and look to push forward, but Emre Can gets in his way as some miscommunication sees the hosts relinquish possession.
(1’) Abel Hernandez and Hatem Ben Arfa get the match underway as Hull City take the opening kick-off. The visitors, moving left to right, are sporting their white tops and light blue shorts, with Liverpool in all red.
The players get themselves readied on the pitch, as "You'll Never Walk Alone" is so beautifully sung by these Liverpool faithful. It's hard not to get goosebumps when these fans put their singing caps on.
Hull have been dealt a massive blow after Nikica Jelavic and Michael Dawson picked up injuries last weekend at the Emirates, which will see the duo sidelined for up to six weeks. Allan McGregor and Steve Harper are also both injured, forcing third choice keeper Eldin Jakupovic into action. El Mohamady and Brady will have their work cut out for them on the flanks, with Tom Huddlestone and Jake Livermore providing defensive support in a deeper lying role in midfield, while Mohamed Diame plays in a more attacking position behind the strikers.
HULL CITY SUBS: McShane, Rosenior, Quinn, Meyler, Ramirez, Aluko, Watson.
HULL CITY (3-5-2): Jakupovic; Bruce, Davies, Chester; El Mohamady, Huddlestone, Diame, Livermore, Brady; Ben Arfa, Hernandez.
Well, well, well... Despite yet another uninspiring performance on Wednesday, including swapping jerseys with Real Madrid defender Pepe at half time of their match, Mario Balotelli has controversially kept his place in the starting XI today. There have been a chorus of claims from fans and pundits alike to drop the Italian for the much harder working Ricky Lambert, but Brendan Rodgers is having nothing to do with it. The manager has made just three changes to the team that took the pitch on Wednesday, with Javier Manquillo, Emre Can and Adam Lallana replacing Glen Johnson, Jordan Henderson and Philippe Coutinho in the starting line-up.
LIVERPOOL SUBS: Henderson, Coutinho, Markovic, Johnson, Jones, Lambert, Toure.
LIVERPOOL (4-3-3): Mignolet; Manquillo, Skrtel, Lovren, Moreno; Allen, Gerrard, Can; Sterling, Lallana, Balotelli.
The teams have been announced, so let us have ourselves a look at the starting line-ups:
Hull City have been buoyed by new signings early in the season, with Abel Hernandez and Mohamed Diame combining to score seven league goals in their first five matches. The Tigers have netted twice a game in each of their league matches since the arrival of these new faces, which has them looking down at the table as opposed to up, early in the season. They came close to picking up three points at the Emirates last weekend, and will be hoping to carry that momentum into their battle with Liverpool here today.
As Liverpool's Premier League form picks up slightly, they continue to struggle in Europe. A 3-0 dismantling at the hands of Real Madrid on Wednesday followed up a 1-0 loss away to Basel. The Reds did manage to pick up three points in a wild and wacky game at QPR last weekend, courtesy of two own goals, but the loss of Luis Suarez appears to be bothering them more than ever. Daniel Sturridge remains out, while the indolent Mario Balotelli is failing to fill the massive void left by the Uruguayan striker.
Hello Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to Merseyside! Anfield is our venue today, as Liverpool look to claw their way back into the top four when they host a resurgent Hull City squad. I am Alex Moretto and I will be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens!

Well that's all from me today folks. I've been Chris Baker and thank you very much for joining me. Enjoy the rest of your weekend.
Southampton have been rightly lavished with praise for their attacking swagger this season but Ronald Koeman must be delighted with the grit and determination his side showed today. They were far from their fluent best in the second half but they were defensively solid and ground out what must be a very satisfying victory. Miserly in defence and flamboyant upfront - in anyone's book that is a winning combination.
Mark Hughes can be proud of his player's efforts, particularly in the second half. They were very much on the ropes in the first half but they refused to lie down in the second. If Stoke could have taken a bit more care in the final third then they might have been able to nick an equaliser. On the balance of play though it is hard to argue that Southampton weren't good value for their victory. These sides meet again on Wednesday in the League Cup at the Britannia stadium. The Potters will have revenge on their minds no doubt.
Would you believe it - Southampton move into second place in the Premier League after this hard fought victory. Many tipped them as outsiders to possibly get relegated after their summer sales and managerial departure but the only place Saints are looking at this moment is up. if they can maintain this sort of form surely European qualification of some kind can be achieved this season.
(90’) And that's it! The referee's whistle is greeted with an enormous roar as Southampton hang on to win this contest 1-0.
(90’) Mane leads a Southampton breakaway after being expertly played in by Pelle. Mane races into the Stoke area but is rather caught in two minds and his cross-cum-shot flashes across the face of Begovic's goal. Surely no time left now for Stoke?
(90’) SHOT! The ball drops to the talented Marko Arnautovic who doesn't need any invitation to shoot. The Austrian was well within his rights to take the shot on but he can only drag his effort wide of Forster's goal.
--- 90’ Substitution S. Davis is replaced with F. Gardoş. ---
(90’) There will be four minutes of time added on here. Koeman has thrown on Gardos to bolster the Southampton defence and secure three precious points. Stoke continue to pump the ball forward in search of a late equaliser.
(88’) Pieters swings a cross into the Southampton box, which looked threatening but the giant figure of Fraser Forster comes flying off his line and plucks the ball out of the sky with great confidence. That was exactly what the Saints defenders wanted to see from their goalkeeper.
(86’) SHOT! Pelle yet again tries his luck but he slices his shot way over the bar. Southampton almost caught Stoke out on the break but Steven Davis delayed his pass and the momentum of the move broke down.
(84’) Southampton could desperately do with a spell of possession to take the pressure off but Stoke aren't giving them any breathing space to do so. Pelle on this occasion is guilty of holding onto the ball too long and he is dispossessed.
(82’) Stoke force another corner but it comes to nothing as Peter Crouch is blown up for a foul on Fonte. For such a tall player, Crouch needlessly gets involved in holding and shirt pulling at corners and free-kicks. It must drive Mark Hughes and his countless other manager's over the years absolutely mad.
--- 81’ Yellow card M. Wilson gets yellow. ---
(80’) If Saints can hang on to this and claim the three points it will be a massive victory for Koeman's men. They have had opportunities in the second half but haven't taken them. Stoke haven't thrown the towel in  and are pressing for an equaliser.
--- 79’ Substitution O. Assaidi comes on for V. Moses. ---
(78’) CLOSE! Diouf is inches away from connecting with Bardsley's cross from the right. Any contact from the ex-Manchester United striker would surely have levelled the scores here at 1-1. Southampton are getting a bit edgy now.
(76’) WIDE! Pelle heads wide from about 12 yards out after being picked out by Tadic's corner. By anyone's standards that is a poor effort but it is especially surprising given Pelle's form this season. Saints can't kill this match off. Will these missed chances come back to haunt them?
(74’) Diouf goes down just outside the box after racing onto N'Zonzi excellent flighted through ball under the challenge of Clyne. Stoke to the amazement of everyone inside the stadium aren't given a free-kick. Mark Hughes is understandably furious.
(72’) Southampton's passes in the final third are continually probing the Stoke backline. Looking for a chink in the armour. Davis and Schneiderlin have tried to play the ball forwards at every available chance. Davis this time nearly releases Tadic but it is just too heavy and Begovic can sweep up.
(70’) 'Oh when the Saints go marching in!' reverberates around St.Mary's as Stoke look to put some passes together but Wanyama wins the ball back and Southampton charge forward in search of this elusive second goal that would surely put this match to bed.
--- 69’ Substitution M. Arnautović comes on for J. Walters. ---
(68’) Stoke will be kicking themselves after they waste a free-kick opportunity by getting caught offside. Moses had put in a dangerous looking cross that Crouch headed across the area but Diouf had gone too early and was correctly flagged by linesman.
(66’) Mark Hughes will be very pleased with how his side have not only kept themselves in the game but are going into the final period of this match with a realistic chance of salvaging something from this entertaining contest.
(64’) SHOT! Pelle spanks a half volley over the bar after Mane had cushioned the ball into his path. The Senegalese winger had been excellently picked out by a long pass from Steven Davis.
--- 62’ Substitution J. Cork is done for the day. V. Wanyama is his replacement. ---
(61’) Ronald Koeman has looked visibly unhappy with how his side have started this second half and has reacted by making a substitution. Southampton have beefed up their midfield by sending on Victor Wanyama in place of Jack Cork. The Kenyan midfielder will relish the physical battle with Stoke in the middle of the pitch.
(59’) There has been a great noise all afternoon inside the stadium and right now the Saints faithful are sensing that their team need their support and they raise the volume as Nathaniel Clyne earns Southampton a corner. yet again the home side take it short but it comes to nothing as Tadic's cross is headed down by Fonte but it only goes as far as Pieters who hacks it clear.
(57’) Stoke are noticeably playing a bit higher up the park as a team and that is putting the Southampton midfield under more pressure. As a result Jack Cork and Steven Davis have been guilty of giving the ball away too easily.
(55’) At the moment it is Southampton that are struggling to get a hold of the ball which will be of great encouragement to Stoke. With Crouch, Walters, Moses and Diouf all in the side the away team should pose more of a threat as this match develops.
--- 53’ Substitution M. Diouf enters play, replacing C. Adam. ---
(53’) Mark Hughes has seen enough from his side in these opening minutes of the second period and has decided to make a change. Charlie Adam is replaced by Mame Biram Diouf. Stoke seemingly deciding that attack is the best form of defence against Southampton.
(50’) Stoke win their first corner of the game but Charlie Adam's delivery is emphatically headed away by Jose Fonte. This is probably the visitors best spell of the match so far, as they are beginning to build some attacking momentum.
(48’) OFF THE BAR! Pelle gets on the end of Tadic's cross from the left and his header rattles the frame of Begovic's goal. So nearly 2-0 to Southampton. Stoke had actually started the second period in much more positive fashion, looking to get on the front foot and take the game to the opposition.
(46’) No substitutions at the break for either side. The first thing Stoke need to do in this second period is get more of the ball. They have had such little possession it is almost impossible for them to trouble the Southampton backline.
The players are back out and we are all set for the start of the second half. Southampton will get us restarted.
Both sides have plenty of decent options to call upon from the substitutes bench this afternoon. You would think that it would be Stoke that would make the first change in an attempt to alter the pattern of the match and get back into it. Victor Wanyama will probably be a bit frustrated to be watching this match from the sidelines after scoring in the rout last weekend.
Stoke haven't been able to contain this rampant Southampton side so far or impose themselves on the match at all really. A Peter Crouch header and a pretty weak effort from Victor Moses is all they have to look back on from an attacking perspective. That said, it is only one-nil and the visitors should take some heart from that fact. Despite being dominated they are very much still in this game.
Ronald Koeman will be delighted with the intensity that his side have shown so far. There have been no signs that the 8-0 to Sunderland and all the plaudits that Southampton are getting at the moment are going to their heads at all. It has been a very confident performance from the home team. The only disappointment from a Saints point of view is that they are only one goal in front.
(45’) That's half-time! 1-0 to the Saints. Southampton have been too hot for Stoke to handle so far. Mark Hughes will be relieved that it is only 1-0 at the break and he has plenty to ponder in the next 15 minutes.
(45’) Tadic has been fantastic in this opening forty-five minutes. The Serbian has absolutely tormented the Stoke City defence to the point of cruelty. Erik Pieters and Phil Bardsley have had a torrid time against the fleet-footed attacking midfielder.
(42’) Stoke can't clear their lines at the moment and it leads to another Southampton free-kick in a dangerous position. Bertrand has a go this time but his effort is a tame one that goes straight into the wall.
(40’) WIDE! Tadic absolutely ties his marker in knots before flashing the ball across the Stoke backline but no-one can get on the end of it and the visitors can breathe a little bit easier now. You feel it is vital for the away side not to concede again before half-time or it might be game over.
--- 39’ Yellow card R. Shawcross receives a yellow card. ---
(38’) Stoke need to keep their cool here - Cameron, Adam and Pieters are rather fortunate not to be in the book already and they are certainly testing the patience of the referee Jonathon Moss. Pieters brings down Pelle this time and Tadic takes the resulting free-kick but he fires his effort high, wide and not very handsome.
(36’) The dubious goals panel took a goal away from Saido Mane last weekend but there is no doubt about this one. It's Mane's first goal for Southampton. Mark Hughes will be annoyed by the manner of Stoke's defending in the build-up to conceding. City are so well known for their strength at set pieces.
(34’) Tadic whipped in a pretty poor free-kick into the Stoke penalty area the ball was headed into the path of Graziano Pelle who half-volley's the ball against the post. The rebound falls kindly to Saido Mane who lashes it high into the roof of the net.
--- 33’ Goal! GOAL! Southampton take the lead! Mane opens the scoring. ---
(31’) SHOT! Schneiderlin sends his shot over the bar after Southampton worked the corner short. The French international was in a good position there and perhaps should've made Begovic work there. You feel a goal is coming for the home side if the pattern of the match continues in this fashion.
(29’) SAVE! Asmir Begovic gets down low to his near post sharply to turn away Tadic's low drive. The Southampton winger cut inside from the right wing and smashed the ball at goal with his left foot but the Bosnian goalkeeper was equal to the effort.
(27’) Pelle almost gets a shot away inside the area being played in intelligently by Tadic but he is snuffed out by Ryan Shawcross. The movement of the Southampton front three has been a joy to watch so far this afternoon. Stoke are doing well just to stay in the game at the moment.
(23’) Southampton have the best defensive record in all four professional divisions which is just as impressive as their attacking prowess at the other end of the pitch this season. Nathaniel Clyne and Ryan Bertrand have got forward at every opportunity and that has been a feature of their play so far in this campaign.
(20’) It has been a very competitive opening to the game with plenty of strong challenges going in. On this occasion Peter Crouch is on the receiving end of a robust tackle from Saints captain Jose Fonte. Stoke look up for the fight this afternoon. After what happened to Sunderland last weekend they know that they have to be at their best to get a result against Southampton.
(17’) CHANCE! Mane jinks down the left wing and cuts the ball back to Pelle who arrives at just right time but the in form striker can't keep his shot down and rather lashes the ball over the crossbar from about six yards out. That was a decent opportunity for Southampton to take the lead.
(15’) Moses creates a great opportunity for himself by dancing past two Southampton challenges but his eventual shot is a weak one that is straight at Fraser Forster. There was a bit of contact on Moses has he got into the area but to his credit the winger stayed on his feet. Did the events of last week mean that he didn't want to go to ground?
(12’) A good battle is developing in these early stages between Saido Mane and Phil Bardsley. Mane has looked to take the Stoke right back on at every opportunity but the former Sunderland man has stuck to his task well and has put in some excellent tackles.
(10’) CHANCE! Peter Crouch meets N'Zonzi's cross from the right wing but the Stoke striker can't get his header on target. That's the first meaningful attack that the visitors have had so far. That will encourage the travelling fans from the Potteries.
(8’) SHOT! Steven Davis drags his shot wide after being teed up by Pelle. The Northern Ireland international will be a bit disappointed that he has not hit the target there but more good attacking play from the Saints.
(6’) Stoke can't get anywhere near the ball at the moment as Southampton string the passes together. Mark Hughes will be keen for his side to maintain a good shape and not let Southampton get an early goal.
(4’) CHANCE! Mane cuts in from the left-hand side and looks to curl his shot into the bottom corner and he doesn't miss by much. Pelle almost got a toe on it which would surely have put Saints in front if he had been able to connect.
(2’) Southampton have started very brightly as you migh have anticipated and have won their first corner within 90 seconds of kick off. Tadic already looks very sharp. Cork's set piece is a poor one and Stoke easily clear the danger.
(1’) And we're underway Southampton playing in their traditional colours of red  and white striped shirts, black shorts and red socks. Stoke are in their away kit which is a light blue shirts, navy shorts and socks. The visitors kick off.
As usual the playing surface at St. Mary's looks absolutely immaculate as the players come out onto the pitch. There's a very decent atmosphere in the stadium and kick off is just a couple of minutes away. Can Graziano Pelle continue his goalscoring exploits or will former Saint Peter Crouch spoil the party?
What more can you say about Southampton at the moment? They are absolutely flying right now. Confidence must be sky high in Ronald Koeman's dressing room after the Saints recorded their biggest ever Premier League victory last weekend against a hapless Sunderland side. The Dutchman has done an outstanding job since taking over from Mauricio Pochettino in the summer and he'll be looking for another three points today.
It will be interesting to see how Victor Moses reacts to all of the negative attention he has been given in the press this week since he was accused of simulation against Swansea City last Sunday. You suspect that the Saints crowd may give the on-loan Chelsea player a hard time this afternoon. Mark Hughes has fiercely defended the integrity of his player and will be hoping that Moses can repay the faith shown in him today.
As for Stoke they make two changes to the team that beat Swansea in such controversial circumstances last Sunday with Mame Biram Diouf and Stephen Ireland being replaced in the starting lineup by Geoff Cameron and Jonathan Walters.
Only one change to the Southampton side that demolished Sunderland last week with Shane Long dropping to the bench in place of Saido Mane. Mane came on as a substitute and scored in the 8-0 thrashing.
Stoke City: Begovic; Bardsley, Shawcross (c), Wilson, Pieters; Cameron, N'Zonzi; Walters, Adam, Moses; Crouch. Subs: Sorensen, Huth, Arnautovic, Diouf, Sidwell, Assaidi, Bojan.
Southampton (4-3-3): Forster; Clyne, Fonte (c), Alderweireld, Bertrand; S.Davis, Cork, Schneiderlin; Mane, Pelle, Tadic.Subs:K.Davis, Yoshida, Gardos, Long, Wanyama, Mayuka, Reed.

Good afternoon and welcome along to St.Mary's for this Premier League clash between Southampton and Stoke City. I'm Chris Baker and I'll be guiding you through the action today.

Sunderland may officially be in crisis now, with confidence surely low after the individual catastrophes in the last few games. That's all from us here today - thank you for joining us!
Arsenal were lively but far from convincing, needing two huge mistakes to score and failing to truly carve up the defence. The team may not care today, as they earned a precious win and an equally-precious clean-sheet, but Wenger will want his side to be far better up top.
(90’) What a game we've had today. Sunderland nearly clawed their wy back into this but two terrible mistakes from Brown and Mannone have condemned them to defeat at home against Arsenal as the full-time whistle rings out.
--- 90’ +2 Goal! WHAT A MISTAKE FROM MANNONE! AND FOR THE SECOND TIME, SANCHEZ CAPITALIZES! 2-0 ARSENAL!!! Van Aanholt rolls the ball back to his goalie under pressure, but Mannone hesitates, miscontrols the ball completely, and Sanchez merely has to tap it into an empty net! ---
(90’) Into the second of four added minutes here, and we may likely see a finale where Arsenal win but Wenger isn't happy anyway with how many fantastic chances his side failed to finish, as Cazorla somehow skies another chance from just yards out!!
--- 90’ Substitution A. Oxlade-Chamberlain is replaced with T. Rosický. ---
(90’) Two shots blocked in a row for Arsenal on the edge of the box and Sunderland have a throw-in deep in the visitor's half. Rosicky comes on for Oxlade-Chamberlain, who has faded quite a bit in this second half.
(89’) Cazorla skies his effort well over the bar after an excellent layoff from Welbeck!
--- 88’ Substitution A. Ramsey comes on for Arteta. ---
(87’) Bellerin floats a cross in that's far too close to Mannone and either side looks likely to score every time they have the ball! It's simply breathless at the moment.
(86’) Another chance gone begging for Sunderland as Wickham fails to get a shot off in the box - Poyet will be furious with how many chances his side have not turned into genuine efforts on target.
(84’) Van Aanholt does everything right, racing through Arsenal's defence, but scuffing his shot at the very end! The ball is immediately worked down the other side and Cazorla's shot is saved by Mannone! Truly end-to-end stuff now.
(83’) Sunderland plying pressure on Arsenal but it ends with no free-kick is awarded to a Wickham that goes down. These final few minutes look to be incredibly even and scrappy.
(81’) Szczesny races out of the box to head the ball clear, but its right to van Aanholt - with no goalie in the net - albeit a difficult, tight angle - van Aanholt hits it wide! Arsenal will take a big sigh of relief there as their keeper nearly cost them.
(79’) Monreal with an excellent run down the wing to chip the ball in the box for Welbeck, but from very close range the English international heads it over the bar!
(78’) Sunderland are looking better in these early minutes since the substitutions, with more focus in attack and really taking the game to the visitors. Altidore ends an attack with a very, very poor shot that's hit so weakly the defence can actually clear it!
(76’) Altidore nearly gets on the end of a cross but Mertesacker's physicality did enough to prevent the American's header from being a clean one.

--- 74’ Substitution J. Rodwell is replaced with Jordi Gómez. ---

(74’) Sunderland make changes as well, with Jozy Altidore making a rare appearance for the side as well as Jordi Gomez.
(72’) The visitors working the ball very well in possession but once again, unable to find a way to break through a Sunderland side sitting very deep without the ball.
(70’) Mannone eventually gathers the ball played in by Sanchez, but Oxalde-Chamberlain gets it back, races down the line, and crosses for Vergini to head clear.
(69’) Very, very scrappy now as Rodwell takes down Arteta with a tug. Arsenal with yet another free-kick, further up the pitch.
--- 68’ Yellow card Wickham again with a poor challenge, taking down Chambers and this time being booked for his efforts. He's been lively since coming on but perhaps not in the ways Poyet would have liked! ---
(67’) Wickham frustratedly takes down Arteta from behind and Arsenal have a free-kick in their own half. The visitors are playing very good, free-flowing football but need to be wary of Sunderland on the counter.
(65’) And that's not a bad shot at all from Larsson, who picks out his chance from outside the box for Szczesny to save.
(64’) Cazorla leads the charge forward, finding Oxlade-Chamberlain and the winger crosses into the box. Mannone collects before Welbeck can get on the end of it.
--- 63’ Yellow card Rodwell goes down just outside the box and the Sunderland players are furious that no call is made. Cattermole is booked seconds later to prevent Oxlade-Chamberlain for getting down the flank, much to the ire of the crowd. ---
(61’) An increasingly scrappy match sees both sides lose the ball, before Brown makes a vital interception on Oxlade-Chamberlain who was nearly racing free in the box.
(60’) It's a good spell for Arsenal who are suffocating Sunderland near their own box, but Sanchez's shot from outside the box is far too close to Mannone to trouble the keeper.
(58’) Very, very nearly a good chance for Arsenal but Sanchez's ball to Flamini in the box is just slightly overhit for the Frenchman to reach.
(57’) Buckley lively again but with a poor cross this time that fails to find Wickham in the box. Sunderland, however, are looking bright at the moment.
(56’) Smooth defending from Arsenal to take over Buckley's pass in the box and win a throw-in further down the midfield.
--- 55’ Yellow card That's a very poor play from Arteta, who gets booked for kicking Rodwell in the chin. The midfield did not even seem to see Rodwell while he was raising his leg, but he's booked for a dangerous play nevertheless. ---
(54’) This half has begun much more brightly for Sunderland than it started. The home side looks like they're ready to fight for something here and are not pegged back in their box like they were for extended periods in the first half.
(52’) Wickham with an immediate impact, as a focal point for a cross that Mertesacker awkwardly clears. It's played back in and Rodwell's good effort towards goal forces a quick save out of Szczesny!
(51’) Wickham comes on for Fletcher, who looks to have pulled up with an injury and goes straight into the tunnels. It's a like-for-like change but Sunderland surely won't want to see Fletcher sidelines for any extended period of time.
--- 50’ Substitution C. Wickham enters the game and replaces S. Fletcher. ---
--- 50’ Yellow card Danny Welbeck booked for diving as he's adjudged to having anticipated a challenge from O'Shea in the box and going down a little too easily. Not many complains from the Arsenal players on that one. ---
(49’) An excellent interception from a charging Mertesacker, who reads the play smartly and cuts out what would have been a perfect through ball to Fletcher.
(47’) Sloppy from Wenger's men, passing the ball directly out of bounds in their own half while trying to switch sides of possession, but they do well keep Sunderland bottled up from the throw-in.
(45’) The second half is now underway with no changes for either side. The visitors play it from the back, losing it right in the centre-circle, and Szczesny needs to make a smart save on Rodwell who muscled his way into the box. Ultimately, however, it was a rather tame effort.
Arsenal, meanwhile, have been comfortable but lacking a cutting edge; playing down the wings to send in crosses is something that Sunderland's defence are dealing with very well for the most part. Wenger will want to see a quicker build-up and more creativity up front.
Poyet's team were nearly doing everything they needed to in order to at least get a point, but with an individual error like that against a player like Sanchez, they now have it all to do in the second half, and will surely need to risk more in order to score.
(45’) That turns out to be the last meaninful action of the half as the whistle is blown after a minute of extra time. It's 0-1 to Arsenal at the half, thanks to an awful mistake by Wes Brown.
(43’) Gibbs trying to charge his way into the box but loses out under a number of defenders. Soon after, Monreal jumps over Fletcher to head the ball clear, knocking the forward down and Gus Poyet is furious that no card is given.
(42’) Absolutely superb work from Welbeck to take the ball from a sea of defenders in Sunderland's box, but nearly every home player is back there and there's no room to shoot. Arsenal win a corner when Welbeck's header is deflected out.
(41’) Oxlade-Chamberlain goes down just outside the box but advantage is played as Welbeck collects it. Unfortunately for the visitors, they may have been better off with a free-kick, as the possession ultimately comes to a poor cross that Mannone easily collects.
(40’) Arsenal are flirting with the goal with solid possession around the box. Gibbs has a cross that's immediately cleared and the visitors' defence is quickly bale to mop up any danger. The Gunners are simply cruising at the moment.
--- 38’ Yellow card Sanchez is cynically taken down by Larsson during a good team move from Arsenal, with the Sunderland player just raking the back of the forward's leg, though he's arguing it was not intentional. Nevertheless, he's booked and Arsenal take the free kick quickly, as usual. ---
(36’) A game that was stretched at times is more contained now, with Arsenal being a little bit more conservative with building up in the midfield. Mannone makes a solid save off his line on Chambers, racing down the right side of the box.
(34’) A poor, weak shot from Arteta ends a good spell of Arsenal possession, with the midfielder picked out from deep by a Welbeck under pressure in the box.
(33’) Buckley tries to do it all on his own and nearly does, dribbling his way into the box before getting to the byline and crossing, only for Szczesny to collecyt. Immeiately after, Cazorla takes a shot that dribbles agonizingly wide of Mannone's far post!
(32’) Arsenal foaming at the mouth now and pouring forward looking for the second, but the cross to Welbeck is just ahead of the striker. Sunderland's mistake on the goal was entirely avoidable and they must immediately find ways to ensure it does not begin a downward spiral.
--- 30’ Goal! ALEXIS SANCHEZ SCORES!!!! 1-0 TO ARSENAL! And it's a disastrous goal for the home side to concede; Brown fails to control a high ball played up from Mertesacker and tries a backpass but it's woefully short and easy for Sanchez to steal. The Chilean races forward unopposed and makes not mistake to coolly slot into the net. ---
(29’) Johnson whips the ball into the box but it's a poor delivery, being cleared by the first man it passes in Welbeck. Sunderland still have the ball but they won't have many chances in areas that good.
(28’) Monreal jumps into the back of Buckley just as the home player was getting the ball, duly conceding a free kick in a fantastic area: roughly seven meters outside of the box, on the right.
(27’) Chambers concedes a corner, Larsson plays it into the box, Mertesacker clears. The home side re-groups and looks to play it from the back now.
(25’) An end-to-end spell here ends with a perfect challenge from Mertesacker to clear the ball off of van Aanholt who was racing through in the box!
--- 24’ Yellow card Arsenal's turn to feel angry, with Oxlade-Chamberlain going down just as he was going into the box under pressure from Brown. No call is made and Gibbs retailiates in anger by pushing over van Aanholt to quickly get the ball, earning him the first booking of the game. ---
(23’) The free kick comes to naught and Welbeck thinks he's about to spark a counter when he wins the ball in midfield but he loses it immediately after. Sunderland wanted a penalty when they think Mertesacker hit the ball with his hand during the free kick but it was his shoulder and nothing comes of it.
(21’) Arsenal decide to play it quickly which turns out to be a mistake, as Sunderland hound them all the way back to Szczesny, forced to clear it quickly. Fletcher goes down shortly after the win the home sided a free kick and Flamini was at fault there, pulling his shoulder back.
(20’) Saved by the whistle: Arteta loses the ball after a very poor pass but Arsenal win back possession when Rodwell slides in far too harshly on Chambers during the counter. No cards given but no doubt that's a foul.
(19’) An absolutely brilliant slide from Vergini prevents Sanchez from getting the ball after a quick give and go, allowing Cattermole to clear!
(18’) Arsenal win a free-kick when Monreal is taken down by Fletcher on a counter-attack. The visitors are playing with verve up front though the home side might take heart with how solid the defence has looked, Mannone's slip-up aside,  in these opening 18 minutes.
(16’) Johnson does immensely well to keep the ball after Flamini nipped it off of the feet of Fletcher but his teammate Buckley is offside near the box.
(15’) Sanchez spots Welbeck's run into the box and plays it smartly into the forward, but the former Manchester United player is too wide and plays it back. He gets it again and decides to have a go from just outside of the box on the left, with a whipping shot that dips just after the bar.
(14’) It's a manic corner, played short before crossed into the box and headed by seemingly everyone on Sunderland before Arsenal finally put it behind for another. Gibbs collects and leads the counter, but it loses momentum when the full-back pulls up to look for teammates.
(12’) Excellent defending by Monreal in his own box to cut out the ball from reaching Fletcher and shielding it for Szczesny to clear. The pressure from Sunderland continues and they currently have a corner.
(10’) What a miss by Mannone! The goalie flies out to collect Gibbs' cross but spills it, forcing O'Shea to clear it quickly with Welbeck set to pounce. After last week's performance and a nervy moment like this, Mannone certainly isn't inspiring much confidence.
(8’) Immense pressure from Sunderland is forcing Arsenal deep to keep the ball, and any attempts to bypass the midfield aren't paying off in these early moments. Sanchez tries a shot from about 30 yards, drilling it wide.
(7’) Brown rises high to head a crafty Cazorla pass out for a corner ahead of the lurking Welbeck. The corner is very poorly worked, play out on the edge of the box to a Gibbs under pressure that can only fire well wide.
(5’) The visitors are trying to build a way into the box mostly using Cazorla and Arteta, but the home side are sitting very deep with numbers and giving them very little. Arsenal dominating possession early here.
(4’) Sanchez will be thanking Flamini there, after the Chilean lost the ball far too easily deep in his own half; the Frenchman was able to clear it before a breakaway could start.
(3’) Controlled, measured play by Arsenal in the midfield. Quick passes work their way to Welbeck near the box but the pass is played in just behind him.
(2’) The first chance of the game comes from the home side, capitalizing on a poor Monreal clearance to cross one into the box that Fletcher fails to control. Play races down the other end as Chambers sends a cross from one wing directly out of bounds on the other.
(1’) And we have kick-off at the Stadium of Light! The home side immedately play a ball towards the box that Nacho heads clear, and Szczesny is called out of his area soon after to deal with another long pass.
As the two teams walk out of the tunnel, there's some good news for Arsenal, with Theo Walcott back on the bench and looking to be re-integrated back into the team after some time on the sideline.
Sunderland: Mannone, Vergini, van Aanholt, O'Shea, Brown, Cattermole, Larsson, Rodwell, Buckley, Johnson, Fletcher.
Arsenal: Szczesny, Chambers, Mertesacker, Monreal, Gibbs, Arteta, Flamini, Oxlade-Chamberlai, Cazorla, Alexis, Welbeck.
Arsenal meanwhile are missing a rash of names as well: Mathieu Debuchy, Olivier Giroud, David Ospina, Abou Diaby, Laurent Koscielny, Mesut Ozil, and Yaya Sanogo are all injured today, and Jack Wilshere suspended.

Arsene Wegner noted earlier this week that the visitors simply must improve defensively, having kept merely a single clean sheet this entire season! With Sunderland struggling to score this season - they're tied for the leagues 4th worst offence with eight goals in eight games - Wenger knows this is a vital moment to have his defenders gain some confidence.
Of course, last weekend, Gus Poyet's men were torn to shreds by Southampton, who put 8 past them during a performance that captain John O'Shea stressed was incredibly important to put behind them today. Arsenal, meanwhile, have just one win in their last five Premier League matches, defeating Aston Villa 3-0 away but tieing Manchester City, Tottenham and Hull as well as losing to Chelsea.
Hello and welcome to our live match coverage of a mouthwatering match between Sunderland and Arsenal! The hosts are coming off of their worst ever defeat in the Premier League; the visitors, from a late win in the Champions' League but desperate for points after a slow start to life in England this campaign. A cracking game at The Hawthorns today, Neil Warnock's team looked to be heading for their first away victory of the season before Jedinak conceded a penalty in stoppage time which Berahino converted. Jedinak had scored a penalty himself in the first half after Hangeland had given Palace the lead. Substitution Anichebe bagged a controversial goal before Berahino levelled things from the spot.
(90’) FULL TIME AT THE HAWTHORNS! Berahino's stoppage time penalty wins West Brom a point after Palace were unable to hang on to a slender advantage! The game ends 2-2!
(90’) What a game this has been, Palace unable to hang on to their lead. Still time for West Brom to maybe steal a winner as Anichebe breaks forward!
--- 90’ +3 Goal! GGOOOOAAAAALLLLLLL FROM THE SPOT! Berahino levels the game in stoppage time with a lovely spot kick into the bottom left corner! ---
(90’) PENALTY TO WEST BROM! Anichebe is brought down in stoppage time after a clumsy tackle from Jedinak!
(90’) STOPPAGE TIME! We're into the dying embers of this game now as Palace hold on to a slender one goal lead! Warnock cuts a nervous figure on the touchline as Hangeland clears an attempted cross from Berahino towards Anichebe.

(78’) The home side still have possession as the crowd urge their team forward in search of an equaliser. They seem to have lost that spring in their step after a dominant spell after half time! Morrison with the ball in midfield.
(76’) GREAT CHANCE! Morisson's effort on the edge of the box is blocked down by the towering figure of Hangeland after a great one-two down the left wing between Berahino and Brunt.
(74’) Campbell is unable to find a way through the West Brom defence as he tries to dance between Dawson and Lescott, a pass to Puncheon was the better option but the striker didn't get his head up!

(62’) Zaha tries to take on too many defenders and loses out gifting West Brom with the chance to break! He is replaced by Jason Puncheon shortly afterwards. The home side now pushing for an equaliser as we reach the final 30 minutes of the game.
(60’) West Brom look like a different side in this second half since the arrival of Anichebe, the striker is providing them with a new dimension up top. Hennessey is forced into action for the first time since coming on after a quick free kick which led to a shot from Dorrans!
(58’) IMPACT! Anichebe has made a brilliant impact on this game since coming on at half time! He drills another cross across the face of the Palace goal but it finds nobody in the end.
(56’) Zaha can't get on the end of a long cross from Bolasie on the left. West Brom have the momentum now following the contraversial goal!

(50’) GOAL RULED OUT! West Brom have the ball in the net for first time in this game but the referee blows for a foul on the goalkeeper. Speroni came out to try and punch the ball clear but got taken out by Dawson!
(49’) BERAHINO EFFORT! The striker finally makes some space for himself and gets his shot away, forcing a great save from Speroni.
(48’) Lescott concedes a silly free kick a few yards away from his own penalty area but the away side are unable to punish the defender as the attacks breaks down.
(47’) Campbell finds himself one on one with Speroni but is caught offside!

Hangeland's goal gave the Eagles the lead before Jedinak doubled the advantage from the penalty spot on the stroke of half time. Plenty of time for more entertainment in this enjoyable Premier League clash!
West Brom have a big task ahead of them in the second period, Warnock's defence have been extremely solid! Join me again in seven minutes for the second half of this interesting encounter!
A lively first half at The Hawthorns with the away side securing a two goal advantage thanks to a well taken penalty from Jedinak just before the break after Hangeland had sent the Eagles ahead with a close range effort.
--- 45’ +3 Yellow card S. Sessègnon goes into the referee's book. ---

(45’) PENALTY TO PALACE! This time the away side get the decision! Bolasie is taken down by Pocognoli.
(43’) West Brom runnig out of ideas in the final third as we approach half time at The Hawthorns, Brunt is forced to attempt a very long range effort which is sent well wide of the goal.
(41’) HEAD INJURY! Play is stopped as Campbell is down holding his head after a strong challenge in the air from Lescott. The forward gets to his feet and is met with jeers from the Hawthrons crowd!
(39’) Brunt wastes a left sided corner, the winger attempts another in swinging ball but it's overhit and Palace now break from the goal kick with Bolasie on the right. Lescott concedes a throw in.

(36’) Zaha goes down in the box but there is a lack of appeals for a penalty from the Palace players!

(17’) At the other end the goalscorer helps defend a corner, Bolasie breaks from the clearance and wins a free kick. West Brom win possession in the centre of midfield with Morrison.

(2’) An early offside given against Chris Brunt as he marched forward trying to get on the end of Sebastien Pocognoli's lofted ball towards the corner. The home side keeping possession well in the early stages.
(1’) We are underway here in the first half at The Hawthorns! West Brom are donning their white away strip while Crystal Palace are in their customary red and blue stripes.
Less than 15 minutes to go until kick-off at The Hawthorns. West Brom will be very confident coming into this fixture having only lost two of their last 13 Premier League games against London sides.
Warnock's men will need to be on red alert for Baggies striker Berahino. The in-form forward has scored seven goals in 10 appearances this season with six of these coming in home games. He's on his way to becoming the highest goalscoring Englishman in the league so far.

West Brom almost toppled another one of the 'big' teams last week, they were leading Manchester United 2-1 at home before Daley Blind popped up with a nicely finished late equaliser. (48’) Rangel brings down Mahrez and Leicester are awarded a free kick in a dangerous position on the left wing. The Algerian whips the ball into the Swansea penalty area but his attempted cross is poor and it's easily dealt with by Fabianski.
(47’) It's been an excellent 45 minutes for Swansea, and they head into the half time break with a well deserved 1-0 lead. Sigurdsson and Bony have been fantastic, and that was evident in the build up to the goal, in which both showcased great understanding and awareness to penetrate the Leicester defence in such impressive fashion. The hosts have bossed possession too, leaving the visitors increasingly frustrated and unable to cause too much trouble in the final third of the pitch.
(46’) And we're underway once again!

The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch ahead of the start of second half. Neither side have made any substitutions during the half time break.

(44’) Swansea seem comfortable to keep possession in the middle of the pitch as they look to go into the half time break with their 1-0 lead intact.

(36’) Leicester are trying their hardest to find an equaliser by sending a plethora of long balls into the final third of the pitch, but all of their attempts are being comfortably dealt with by the impressive Swansea back four.

There's just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let's have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon...
As for Leicester, they too have been finding points hard to come by in recent weeks, with two defeats from their last three league games - against Crystal Palace and Newcastle United, respectively - leaving them just outside of the relegation zone in 15th place heading into today's clash. Their last victory came at home to Manchester United over a month ago, and they will also be desperate to pick up three points today to stop them from falling further down the table.
After impressive starts to the new campaign, both Swansea and Leicester have struggled in recent weeks, with today's hosts in particularly poor form at the moment. Three wins from their first three games of the season saw Swansea rocket to the top part of the table, but since their comfortable 3-0 victory at home to West Bromwich Albion at the end of August they have only managed to pick up two points, with both of those coming against sides that sit near the foot of the table. With games against Everton, Arsenal and Manchester City coming up in the next few weeks, today's clash really is a must win for Garry Monk's struggling side.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live text commentary of today's Premier League clash between Swansea City and Leicester City. My name is Ben Cullimore and I will be keeping you up to date with all of the action from the Liberty Stadium.

Burnley huffed and puffed but remain without a win and second-bottom in the table. They struggled to trouble Howard and need to find a cutting edge if they are to climb the table. For now, I've been Tom Maston and thanks for joining me.
The final whistle blows and Everton have done enough to record back-to-back league wins for the first time this season. Eto'o showed his class with two fine finishes and the Toffees fully deserved their victory as they climb back into the top half.
(90’) OFF THE POST! So close to a hat-trick for Eto'o as he nips in and takes the ball around Heaton. The angle is very tight, but the forward does brilliantly to hit the post with his placed effort. He has been excellent today.
(90’) Into four minutes of stoppage time and Sordell cuts inside before driving straight at Howard. Burnley have put in plenty of effort but have not quite had the cutting edge in the final third.
(89’) GOOD SAVE! Naismith has been quiet this afternoon but almost finds the net as he skips past two challenges before going for goal. Heaton does well to tip the ball behind at his near post.

--- 86’ Substitution N. Chalobah comes on for G. Boyd. ---
--- 85’ Assist S. Pienaar gave the assist. ---

(84’) The first of those Burnley changes is made as Sordell replaces Kightly for the last few minutes. The home side may well go with three up front in pursuit of an equaliser now.
(83’) Arfield finds space around 25 yards from goal but the midfielder rushes his shot and drags it well wide of the post. Still no clearcut opportunities for the home side.
--- 82’ Substitution L. Osman is replaced with S. Pienaar. ---
(82’) Everton make their second change of the afternoon as Pienaar replaces Osman for the closing stages. Burnley are readying some changes themselves.
(81’) Arfield looks to drive the home side forward before feeding Barnes, but the striker runs straight into Alcaraz. The Everton defender holds firm to win the ball back.
(80’) As the game enters the final ten minutes of normal time, much of the play is now taking place in the Everton half. The Goodison Park outfit could yet pay for not putting this game to bed.
(78’) Boyd wins a free-kick on the right-hand side as Burnley look to create something in this second half. Howard has not been tested since Ing's equaliser after 20 minutes.
(76’) Barry has returned to his feet and Everton are back to 11 men after a brief period of having a numerical disadvantage. The visitors have done well to stay as solid as they have in the second period.
--- 74’ Yellow card A. Barnes goes into the referee's book. ---
(74’) Barnes is the fourth Burnley player to go into the book as he catches Barry in the middle of the park. The former Manchester City man will need some treatment after that.
(72’) Naismith looks to create some room for himself on the edge of the area but his shot is deflected and has all the power taken out of it for Heaton to save.
(71’) The home fans have raised the volume as they look to inspire their team towards an equaliser in this second half. They have struggled to get going in the second period.
(69’) Barkley manages to get Baines in behind on the left-hand side, but the defender's cross is a poor one and is cleared at the near post. The Toffees have not been as threatening in the second period.
(67’) We are into the final quarter of the game as Burnley begin to enjoy a little more possession. Dyche's team will have to throw more men forward, you feel, if they are to get anything from this game.

(64’) GOOD SAVE! From the resulting free-kick, Baines curls in a cross from deep that evades everyone, with Heaton having to be aware enough to turn it behind.

(63’) Coleman is able to get forward on the right-hand side after a quiet first hour, and Ward goes into the referee's book for a pull on the Ireland full-back.
(61’) Jagielka has been excellent today and again gets the better of Ings as the striker looked to take advantage of a poor touch from Alcaraz. No way through for Burnley as yet.
(59’) Eto'o and Lukaku combine for the first time in the second half as the latter's lay-off is struck goalwards from 20 yards by the former Barcelona man, but his effort is straight at Heaton who holds on well.

(54’) Little goalmouth action as yet in the second half, with both teams looking to keep the ball in midfield and build patiently. Not quite the tempo of the first 45 minutes as yet.

(50’) Not quite the same start to the second half from Everton as they made in the first, but the Toffees are looking to control possession and slowly make their way into Burnley territory.
(48’) Alcaraz is very lucky to get away with a mistake inside his own area. The former Wigan defender miscontrols Kightly's left-wing cross, but Jutkiewicz's subsequent header is straight at Howard and easy for the goalkeeper.
(46’) No changes for either side at the break, and Burnley get the second half underway...
The two teams are making their way out onto the pitch as the second half approaches. Everton were not totally convincing in the first period, but have the lead and will be looking to put the game out of sight after the break.

(44’) Eto'o eventually gets back to his feet and looks as if he is ready to continue. The former Cameroon captain has shown plenty of nice touches in this first half to go with his early goal.
(42’) Both teams are beginning to spring counterattacks with the half-time break approaching. Eventually the game is halted as Eto'o receives some treatment after a challenge from Duff.

(26’) Lukaku does well to dig out a cross on the right-hand side of the box, but the ball is behind Eto'o at the back post and flies out for a throw-in to the home side. Burnley looking comfortable at present.

(22’) JUST WIDE! Burnley have been lifted by that goal and go close to taking the lead as the ball falls for Arfield on the edge of the box, but his controlled volley skids narrowly wide of the upright.

(16’) Burnley have begun to get a foothold in this game, and Naismith does well to throw himself in front of Jones' long-range effort to block. Everton not having it all their own way.
(14’) Trippier and Boyd combine well down the right-hand side, and Barry has to track back to win the ball off the former as he looked to put the ball into the box.

(7’) Burnley are struggling to get out of their own half and keep hold of the ball for any period of time. The Everton fans are in full voice with their side dominating proceedings.
