(79’) Tottenham finally make the change with Aaron Lennon coming on for Erik Lamela, while Newcastle's hero Ayoze Perez gives way for defender Massadio Haidara as the visitors look to see this one out.
--- 78’ Substitution A. Lennon enters play, replacing E. Lamela. ---
(77’) Pochettino has to make a substitution here. Dier is not getting forward with any effectiveness, while Lamela seems altogether disinterested. They are posing no threat along the right, which does not have to be the case with Aaron Lennon sitting right there on the substitute's bench just waiting to hear his name.
(75’) STAT ATTACK: None of the last 17 meetings between these two teams at White Hart Lane have ended in a draw. The last time they settled for a share of the points in London was back on October 29, 1995.
(73’) The difference in Newcastle's attacking play is worlds different than it was in the first half. They are passing it around with much greater confidence in the final third, and their moment off the ball is significantly better. Tottenham are forced to defend this patient build up play, when all they want to do at the moment is push for an equalizer.
(71’) Ayoze is down injured which brings a much needed stoppage in play for Newcastle as Tottenham are coming on strong. Pochettino, for some strange reason, is reluctant to make a second substitution, despite Lamela and Chadli's ineffectiveness throughout much of the match.
(69’) HOW HAS HE NOT SCORED THAT?! Great build up from Tottenham. Eriksen picks out Rose along the left, and the defender sends a superb low cross into the area. Newcastle cannot defend it as it comes to the feet of Harry Kane, but the substitute lashes it back across goal straight at Krul! He had the entire near side of the net gaping.
--- 67’ Substitution E. Capoue is replaced with H. Kane. ---
(67’) TOTTENHAM GOAL DISALLOWED! Eriksen's corner is delivered in and bounces along the byline. Gouffran cannot deal with it at the near post and it bounces off the chest of Krul and into the back of the net. Tottenham are confused by the referee's decision, but it was the right one as the ball bounced out of play on its way to goal.
(66’) Better build up from Tottenham but they do not get in behind as Capou takes a shot from long range, that takes a deflection off Colback and behind for a corner. That will be the last contribution from the French midfielder who is about to give way for Thursday's hero Harry Kane.
(64’) CABELLA! Terrible defending from Tottenham, as Ameobi makes a fine tackle and starts Newcastle on a break. Colback nudges the ball forward for Cabella who beats Kaboul far too easily inside the area. He approaches the byline and tries to poke a shot past Lloris who parries behind for a corner. Perez was waiting in the middle, all the substitute had to do was square it up.
--- 63’ Yellow card E. Capoue is yellow-carded. ---
(62’) What a difference in play now, as Newcastle have a spring in their step. Tottenham look frustrated, forcing play forward, but the visiting players are pressuring the ball extremely well. Sissoko, who has done it all for Newcastle here today, runs back to dispossess Eriksen, which elicits a groan from the home supporters.
(60’) Pochettino looks on in disbelief, as his side, despite leading by just a goal at the break, hardly looked like giving up their lead. But some fine substitutions from Pardew, who elected not to waste any time, have made all the difference here.
--- 58’ Assist R. Cabella gave the assist. ---
--- 58’ Goal! Tremendous build up play from Newcastle, started off by Sissoko, who makes a sensational run up the pitch past three defenders before laying it off for Cabella. The substitute takes one touch before sending a marvelous cross in for Ayoze, who glances his header past a diving Lloris at the far post for his first Newcastle goal! ---
(58’) NEWCASTLE HAVE TAKEN THE LEAD EMPHATICALLY!
(56’) STAT ATTACK: At this stage last season, Tottenham had 16 points, five more than they do currently. This is their worst start to a Premier League season since 2008.
(54’) Tottenham have it all to do again, and Newcastle are falling into their shell. The early goal does not appear to have boosted their spirits, but rather give them an excuse to sit back and let Tottenham come after them. They have plenty of attackers on the pitch now, so there really is no excuse for them not to go searching for a second.
(52’) AGONIZINGLY WIDE! Rose provides Totteham with great width, and sends a fine ball into the area for Eriksen. The midfielder surely has to score, but his shot from in close is partially deflected by Coloccini before bouncing wide at the far post!
--- 50’ Yellow card J. Colback is cautioned by the referee. ---
(50’) Jack Colback is shown a yellow card for a pull back on Lamela, giving Tottenham a free kick from 40 yards out. Eriksen delivers into the area and Newcastle clear. The hosts keep the pressure on, but some good defending by Dummett forces Lamela to run it behind for a goal kick.
(48’) That goal should prove absolutely vital for Newcastle, not just pulling them back into the game, but giving them the confidence to feel like they can actually take something from this match.
--- 46’ Substitution R. Cabella enters the game and replaces V. Anita. ---
--- 46’ Assist ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE! Newcastle kick-off and immediately Ameobi runs forward. A brilliant pass forward from Colback catches Dier sleeping as the substitute runs in behind to get on the end of it and blast home past Lloris with his first touch! ---
--- 46’ Goal! Sammy Ameobi has found the target for Newcastle United! ---
--- 46’ Substitution G. Obertan is done for the day. Sammy Ameobi is his replacement. ---
(46’) NEWCASTLE ARE LEVEL AFTER JUST SIX SECONDS!
(46’) Newcastle get the second half underway, with two new faces as Sammy Ameobi and Remy Cabella are introduced at the expense of Vurnon Anita and Gabriel Obertan.
For Newcastle, they are in dire need of help going forward, which could come through Remy Cabella, Sammy Ameobi or Facundo Ferreyra who has yet to make his Premier League debut. Ayoze Perez is not getting the job done at the moment, and you just have to wonder how much longer Pardew will wait before making a change.
HALF TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-0 NEWCASTLE. Neither team looking very inspired through the opening 45 minutes, but the hosts have added to Alan Pardew's misery as Emmanuel Adebayor has Spurs in front at the break.
(45’) Sissoko tries to get through everyone as he makes a run forward and is dispossessed by a strong tackle from Danny Rose. Eriksen starts on a break for Tottenham with plenty of options in support. He picks out Mason, who crosses in for Adebayor, but the striker tries to bring it down which allows Coloccini to clear. That is the last of the action in this first half.
(45’) Two minutes to be added on at the end of the first half...
(44’) WHERE IS THE DEFENDING?! Tottenham win a free kick from 40 yards out and Eriksen delivers towards the far post. The Newcastle defenders are all caught ball watching, as it falls for Chadli at the far post, but the Belgian's volley is skied over the bar.
(42’) Back the other way come Tottenham after dealing with the threat, and Eriksen sends a nice cross into the area that forces Taylor to usher behind for a corner. Lamela's delivery is poor and Newcastle clear, but Perez is far too weak on the ball as he fails to take advantage of an opportunity to break.
(40’) This is much better from Newcastle! Sissoko, back out on the pitch, picks up a ball with pace to draw defenders towards him before laying it off to a teammate. A cross is sent into the area and Dier heads behind for a corner.
(38’) Sissoko is down injured for Newcastle, a worrying sight for them. He appears to have picked up a knock after making a strong run forward, cutting across the top of the box. He showed some hesitation on the ball, however, never getting a shot off to threaten Lloris in goal.
(36’) There is nothing to Newcastle's play in this first half. Pardew's side have lacked any sort of desire to push forward which has made life incredibly easy on Tottenham. The hosts' defence has shown they are vulnerable under pressure, but Newcastle are doing nothing to try and take advantage of that so far.
(34’) Ryan Mason squeezes a pass through to Lamela on the right, who subsequently wins a corner. Newcastle deal with the threat, but Spurs keep the ball and immediately look to get back forward. There is a real intent to their play now, but it has yet to result in many chances, with Krul having far less to do early on than he did in this fixture last season.
(32’) STAT ATTACK: A Loic Remy goal gave Newcastle a 1-0 victory in this fixture last season, with Tim Krul standing on his head to secure the three points.
(30’) Newcastle look completely out of ideas on the ball. They are incredibly lacking in confidence, with the early goal seemingly removing any momentum they may have picked up with last weekend's victory. It is all too unimaginative from the visitors at the moment, who are showing no signs of getting themselves back into this game.
(28’) Ryan Mason has been incredibly bright for Tottenham in the opening half hour, seeing plenty of the ball and passing it about smartly from midfield. He drifts to the right here and plays Lamela in behind the defence, but the Argentine just mistimes his run, resulting in an offside.
(26’) Chadli picks out the run of Danny Rose, who streaks into space along the left. He gets past Obertan and into the area, but falls flat on his face after losing his balance, putting the ball behind for a goal kick. That was a real chance for Tottenham had Rose stayed upright.
(24’) Scary moments for Tottenham as Emmanuel Adebayor pulls up after seemingly rolling his ankle. There was no one within five yards of the striker and he just came up lame. He is trying to walk it off, and hopefully for Tottenham's sake he will be alright to continue.
--- 23’ Yellow card Y. Gouffran receives a yellow card. ---
(22’) Alan Pardew looks on, disgusted, as his side again fall behind on the road. They have not won away from St. James Park since March, a run of nine Premier Matches on the road that have seen them pick up a meager two points.
(20’) The early goal has done plenty to lift the spirit of these Tottenham players. They have grown increasingly frustrated with their inability to find the back of the net with any consistency of late, so Adebayor's opener should do wonders for their confidence.
--- 18’ Assist The assist came from R. Mason. ---
--- 18’ Goal! The striker tries to pick out a pass, and a deflection sends it straight onto the feet of Chadli. The winger is into the area but sees his shot blocked. Eriksen picks up and Coloccini gets to his effort as well. Mason picks up the ball, and instead of thrashing it at goal, he sends a wonderful chipped pass to the far post that Adebayor heads past Krul! Tottenham in front! ---
(18’) TOTTENHAM TAKE THE EARLY LEAD THROUGH ADEBAYOR!
(17’) WHAT A MISS! Gouffran sends a cross into the area that Lloris punches away unconvincingly. It falls to Colback at the top of the box with the keeper in no man's land, but he scuffs his shot horribly, putting it wide of the target! He has to do better there.
(15’) Ayoze does well to win a free kick after a careless giveaway by Lamela. The striker nudges the ball past Kaboul who is beaten for pace, forcing himself into a tackle. The visitors play it short, and Dummett strikes from 40 yards out, again a wasteful effort from a defender, as the ball never threatened to hit the target.
(13’) STAT ATTACK: Tottenham have scored just one goal in their last three Premier League matches at White Hart Lane, after scoring four in their first home game of the season against QPR. If they are held without a goal today, they would have one goal from four home league matches for the first time since November-December 2008.
(11’) Newcastle win a free kick along the right from 40 yards out. Dummett comes across to take, delivering a ball in along the near side for Coloccini. The defender is always going to win his battle with Lamela, but his header back into the danger area is collected easily by Lloris.
(9’) Extremely wasteful from Vertonghen. He picks up the ball from 40 yards out, with teammates in space in front of him. As opposed to picking out a pass, the defender tries a shot from distance that sails well over the bar, never troubling Krul in goal.
(7’) After plenty of time on the ball early, Chadli finally ups the tempo, with some more direct play down the left to win a corner. Lamela delivers but his cross is very poor, sailing over the heads of his teammates, allowing Newcastle to take over possession. It is all a bit too straightforward from the hosts early on.
(5’) Eriksen takes a pass and runs past Janmaat with ease along the left. Stephen Taylor rushes across to slide in and send the ball out for a throw, but you can already see Tottenham eager to attack the Dutch right-back, who has been struggling defensively of late.
(3’) Newcastle happy to give Tottenham early possession, as it has been quite a positive start to the hosts. Spurs have done a good job of keeping the ball against teams lower than them in the table, but they have still struggled to turn it into goals early on in the season.
(1’) Tottenham kick-off and we are underway in North London! The hosts, moving right to left, are in their white tops, with Newcastle in their blue and green away kits.
White Hart Lane is buzzing with anticipation, perhaps spurred on by their victory here just a few short days ago, and augmented with the club honoring former player and manager Bill Nicholson, who died 10 years ago this week. His family are in attendance, and the minute of applause from these faithful fans has created some wonderful scenes ahead of kick-off.
Cheick Tiote, Mike Williamson and Emmanuel Riviere all remain injured for Newcastle after missing last week through injury, while Papiss Cisse is a new absentee and will be replaced by Ayoze Perez up top. Sammy Ameobi returns to the bench, as does Ryan Taylor after more than two years absent with a knee problem.
NEWCASTLE SUBS: R. Taylor, Ferreyra, Haidara, Cabella, Elliot, Sammy Ameobi, Armstrong.
NEWCASTLE (4-2-3-1): Krul; Janmaat, S. Taylor, Coloccini, Dummett; Anita, Colback; Obertan, Sissoko, Gouffran; Ayoze Perez.
Nabil Bentaleb and Kyle Naughton faced late fitness tests and have been deemed unfit to return just yet. Federico Fazio is suspended after picking up a red card against Manchester City, paving the way for Jan Vertonghen to return to the starting line-up. The only other change instilled by Pochettino is at striker, where Emmanuel Adebayor is back in the XI, while Roberto Soldado joins Harry Kane on the bench.
TOTTENHAM SUBS: Chiriches, Lennon, Soldado, Vorm, Kane, Dembele, Davies.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Dier, Kaboul, Vertonghen, Rose; Mason, Capoue; Lamela, Eriksen, Chadli; Adebayor.
The teams have been announced, so let us have ourselves a look at the starting line-ups:
Protests from Newcastle fans to fire Alan Pardew have subdued with recent results, but only slightly. A 1-0 victory over Leicester City last weekend, their first of the season, was massive for them. The points will need to keep coming, however, for the manager to feel any sense of security. Their road struggles have been well documented, and another loss here today would keep the Toons in the bottom three, putting Pardew's future with the club in serious doubt yet again.
Tottenham continue to struggle against the top teams, which makes games like this even more vital for Mauricio Pochettino's side in their quest for a top four finish. The North London club have been struggling in attack this season, but an emphatic attacking display in the Europa League on Thursday could be the breakout they needed. Erik Lamela's highlight reel rabona goal was one of two for him on the night, while Harry Kane added a hat trick of his own, yet still cannot get a league start ahead of either Emmanuel Adebayor or Roberto Soldado, both of which have been relatively ineffective up top this season.
Hello Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to London! White Hart Lane is our venue today, as Tottenham look to build upon Thursday's Europa League victory when they play host to a struggling Newcastle side. I am Alex Moretto and I will be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens!

Chelsea remain unbeaten but their lead over Southampton is now only four points. They put in an excellent away performance and deserved at least a point. It will take a fine performance to beat them this season. For now, I've been Tom Maston and thanks for joining me.
And that is the final moment of note, with Manchester United stealing a point right at the death. Courtois was superb but was powerless to keep out Van Persie's late equaliser, and the hosts just about deserved a point for the way they kept going after Drogba's opener.
--- 90’ +5 Yellow card R. van Persie is yellow-carded. ---
--- 90’ +4 Goal! GOAL!!! VAN PERSIE EQUALISES! Di Maria's ball into the box is a good one, and though Courtois makes a great save to deny Fellaini with the original header, Van Persie cannot miss with the follow-up. Old Trafford erupts as the skipper removes his shirt in celebration. Mourinho cannot believe it on the sidelines. ---
--- 90’ +3 Substitution K. Zouma enters the game and replaces Willian. ---
--- 90’ +3 Red card! RED CARD! IVANOVIC IS SENT OFF! Chelsea will play the final few seconds with ten men as Ivanovic is shown a second yellow for a trip on Di Maria. Free-kick in a dangerous area on the left-hand side... ---
(90’) Di Maria looks to be the hero as he hits a swerving effort from 30 yards that skids along the turf. Courtois is right behind it though and holds on. Mourinho makes his final change as Willian is replaced by Zouma for the final few seconds.
(90’) There will be four minutes of stoppage time at Old Trafford. As it stands Chelsea are going six points clear at the top of the Premier League table.
--- 90’ Substitution E. Hazard is replaced with A. Schürrle. ---
(89’) Some fine hold-up play from Drogba eases the pressure on Chelsea and they are able to make their second change of the evening. The impressive Hazard is replaced by Schurrle for the closing stages.
--- 88’ Yellow card E. Hazard goes into the referee's book. ---
(87’) Still Manchester United push for an equaliser, but they have not tested Courtois nearly enough. Van Gaal has two changes left if he wanted to throw on anymore attack-minded players.
(85’) Chelsea continue to stand firm as the hosts bring the ball forward through midfield yet again. No real cutting edge though and the visitors are comfortable at present.
(83’) Di Maria looks to send a long ball into Van Persie, but the United captain is penalised for a foul on Cahill as he chested it down. Time beginning to run out for the home team.
(81’) The home side are starting to bombard Chelsea now as a ball comes into the box from the right-hand side that Wilson looks to divert goalwards with a header. Unfortunately for the youngster his effort is too high and loops onto the roof of the net.
(79’) GOOD SAVE! United at last threaten the Chelsea goal as Shaw feeds Van Persie in the area, but his effort from a tight angle is kept out by Courtois. The ball is cleared but Januzaj is able to cut inside from the right. The youngster's shot screws wide, however.
--- 77’ Yellow card M. Fellaini receives a yellow card. ---
(77’) Fellaini is the latest player to be booked as he pulls back Hazard on the left wing. The Belgium star was away then, so that foul may well have saved the home team.
(75’) Chelsea are sitting back much more now with Mikel on the field, but they will still carry a threat on the counterattack if they can get the ball forward quickly.
(73’) No real chances for United in the second half as they look to get back into this game. Wilson's appearance has brought about a change in system but the youngster has struggled to get involved so far.
(71’) Januzaj looks to put the ball into the box from the right-hand side after a decent spell of possession from the hosts, but Courtois rises highest in the middle to catch and fall on the ball.
(69’) SO CLOSE! Ivanovic does brilliantly to skip past two challenges before looking to shoot from a very tight angle. His effort is a good one but only slides across the face of goal.
--- 67’ Substitution Mata is replaced with J. Wilson. ---
--- 67’ Substitution J. Obi Mikel enters the game and replaces Oscar. ---
(67’) Mourinho makes his first change of the afternoon as Oscar is replaced by Mikel while United also make a substitution with Wilson coming on for Mata.
(66’) Di Maria looks to whip the ball in but he cannot beat Fabregas the near post. The winger has been poor today and has now been switched to the left-hand side.
--- 65’ Yellow card B. Ivanović is yellow-carded. ---
(64’) Di Maria does well to get around the outside of Ivanovic and wins a free-kick on the left-hand side of the area. The Serbia defender goes into the book to become the fifth Chelsea man to be yellow carded.
--- 62’ Yellow card Oscar goes into the referee's book. ---
(62’) Oscar goes into the book as he loses the ball to Smalling before bringing the defender down from behind. No complaints from the Brazil international.
(61’) The home fans are beginning to get very frustrated as Chelsea keep possession with ease in midfield. Mourinho will be very happy with how this is panning out.
(59’) GOOD SAVE! Chelsea again make their way forward through their attacking players before Willian unleashes a powerful drive from 30 yards that De Gea does well to hold onto. The visitors have their tails up now.
(57’) Drogba had previously scored just once against Manchester United before today, but that came in a Chelsea win at Old Trafford. At present history looks set to repeat itself today.
(55’) United all of a sudden look shell shocked by that Drogba goal. They have been as good as Chelsea this afternoon but will now have to produce something special to get back into this one against the league leaders.
--- 53’ Assist The assist came from Fàbregas. ---
--- 53’ Goal! GOAL!!! DROGBA OPENS THE SCORING! Just seconds after De Gea makes a brilliant save to deny Hazard, Chelsea take the lead. The resulting corner is played into the near post, and Drogba nips in to head home. Van Persie gets a touch on the line but he cannot keep it out. The Blues have the lead. ---
(52’) JUST WIDE! Chelsea are unable to clear a corner, and after Van Persie brings the ball down on the edge of the area, Fellaini fires narrowly wide from 20 yards.
--- 50’ Yellow card Fàbregas goes into the referee's book. ---
(50’) Good again from Chelsea as Drogba feeds Ivanovic who crosses into the middle. Oscar flicks the ball on for Hazard, but the winger cannot turn and Fabregas picks up a booking for a foul as United brought the ball out.
(48’) Bright start to the second period from Chelsea as they slowly make their way to the edge of the area before Smalling's clearance ricochets off Hazard and out for a goal kick.
(46’) No changes for either side at the break and Chelsea get us back underway for the second half...
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch as the second half approaches. United are still well in this and could yet become the first team to down Chelsea this season.
Neither team has a raft of attacking options on the bench, so it may need some tactical innovation from either Mourinho or Van Gaal to win this game. We could be in for quite the second half, and I'll be back in ten minutes to see if either team can secure a victory.
The half-time whistle goes and we are still waiting for the deadlock to be broken. Van Persie and Drogba have both been denied by the respective goalkeepers, but shots on goal have been few and far between in the opening 45 minutes.
(45’) We are into the second of two minutes of stoppage time at the end of the first half with both sides still going all out to break the deadlock. Surely they cannot keep up this energy for the whole of the 90 minutes?
(45’) The dead ball is played low into the box where Mata has pulled away from his marker, but the former Chelsea man hits his shot high into the stands. Wasted opportunity for the hosts.
(44’) United win a free-kick right on the edge of the box to the left-hand side of the area. Can they find a way through in the final seconds of the half?
(42’) Plenty of chances all of a sudden as Januzaj runs at Ivanovic before unleashing a drive from the edge of the area that hits the side-netting. He could have brought that ball into the box and made his life much easier there.
(41’) GREAT SAVE! Superb from De Gea as Chelsea break and almost take the lead. Oscar finds room on the right after an error by Rojo before pulling the ball back for Drogba. The striker's shot is a good one but the Spain goalkeeper does well to save with his feet.
(40’) Still no way through for either side as we approach half-time. Manchester United have had the better of things in the last 10 minutes and will be hoping to make their dominance count before the break.
--- 39’ Yellow card N. Matić goes into the referee's book. ---
(38’) Rafael wins a free-kick in a dangerous area on the right-hand side, but Di Maria's delivery is too close to Courtois and the goalkeeper holds on with ease.
(36’) PENALTY? NO! Big appeals from Chelsea for a spot-kick as Ivanovic goes down under a challenge from Smalling as Fabregas chips in a free-kick from the left. No reaction from Dowd despite the vociferous shouts from the visitors.
(34’) Decent opportunity for the visitors as the ball falls kindly for Willian on the halfway line and he can bring the ball forward. Eventually he looks to take the ball around Smalling and into the box, but the England defender chases well to win it and clear up field.
(33’) Drogba does well to intercept Mata's crossfield pass inside the centre circle, but the striker has no support and Smalling is able to clear up the danger with no trouble.
(31’) No goals in the first third of the game but it is not for a lack of effort. Van Persie has gone closest but the United striker really needs to offer more if the hosts are to win this one.
(29’) Some concern for both teams as Matic and Di Maria stay down after a good challenge from the Chelsea man. Referee Dowd signals both will require treatment and we will have a short stoppage.
(27’) Shaw does well to tackle Willian after originally being left for dead by the winger, and the Brazilian stays down clutching his Achilles. Eventually, though, he gets back to his feet and is able to continue without treatment.
(25’) Fabregas concedes a free-kick on the left-hand side, but Di Maria's delivery is too close to Courtois and the goalkeeper opts to punch clear. Good few minutes for the young Belgian.
(23’) GOOD SAVE! United threaten Courtois' goal for the first time, but the Belgium goalkeeper is there to halt them. Shaw plays Van Persie in behind the defence, but the former Atletico man spreads himself to parry the shot away from danger.
--- 22’ Yellow card D. Drogba goes into the referee's book. ---
(22’) Drogba becomes the first Chelsea player to go into the book for a cynical pull as the home side looked to build a counterattack. The striker is not happy.
(21’) Little in the way of goalmouth action as yet with both sides happy to build with patience. The high-tempo opening has made way for a midfield battle with the flair players on the periphery thus far.
(19’) Di Maria does whip the ball in towards the back post where Smalling meets it, but he cannot control his header as it flies into the stand behind the goal.
(18’) Di Maria shows some quick feet to win a foul from Matic around 35 yards from goal, and the Argentina international will look to swing this into the box. He scored from a similar position against QPR earlier in the campaign...
(16’) Chelsea are having the better of things in terms of possession and territory, but Smalling especially is standing firm and keeping the Premier League leaders at bay.
(14’) Chelsea win a succession of corners, but they are unable to create anything as Drogba heads the final set-piece well over the crossbar. The Ivorian has made a quiet start.
--- 12’ Yellow card Rafael is cautioned by the referee. ---
(12’) Rafael becomes the first man to go into the book as he pulls back Hazard on the Chelsea left. It could now be a long afternoon for the full-back up against the Belgium winger.
(10’) Courtois and De Gea are yet to be really tested as yet as the two teams play out a midfield battle. Both sides have looked dangerous when coming forward but Drogba and Van Persie have struggled to get involved.
(8’) Fellaini has been tasked with sticking tight to Fabregas in midfield while Di Maria is being utilised on the right up against Filipe. Van Gaal is certainly looking to win the tactical battle.
(6’) The game has begun at breakneck speed, with both sides looking to get on the front foot from the outset. With plenty of attacking talent on show, there should be goals in this one.
(4’) Better from the hosts as they work the ball on the edge of the areas before Di Maria is found on the right-hand side of the box. The former Real Madrid man looks to control his volley but it instead flies well over the crossbar.
(3’) Chelsea make a bright and start and are almost able to capitalise on a poor pass out of defence from Rojo. Oscar picks up the ball, but his effort from the edge of the box is well blocked.
(1’) The usual pre-match niceties are over, and Manchester United kick off to get us underway...
The two teams make their way out onto the pitch as Van Gaal waves to the fans. Will Manchester United continue their fine home form, or will Chelsea move further clear at the top of the table? We're about to find out...
The two teams have made their way into the tunnel and they will be greeted by a wall of noise when they enter the stadium. This is the biggest game at Old Trafford this season, and the fans will look to give the players as big a boost as possibly by creating an imposing atmosphere.
There are now less than ten minutes until kick-off in Manchester, and while there is set to be a great atmosphere inside the stadium, some Chelsea fans with tickets will not be there. A number of fans have been stranded in London after a trains to the North West were cancelled this morning, so expect there to be some gaps in the away end.
The two managers today know each other very well after Mourinho worked under Van Gaal during their time at Barcelona. The pair have already embraced in the tunnel prior to kick-off, and expect there to be plenty of respect shown in today's enocunter.
Chelsea are dealt a huge blow with news that Diego Costa has not made it, meaning Didier Drogba starts up front with Loic Remy also absent. Elsewhere, Filipe Luis comes in at left-back for the suspended Cesar Azpilicueta after the latter's red card against Crystal Palace last week.
Radamel Falcao misses out through injury for the hosts, with Robin van Persie again leading the line on his own. Adnan Januzaj retains his place on the right wing while Marouane Fellaini is rewarded for a fine showing at West Brom with a place in the line-up at Ander Herrera's expense. Chris Smalling comes into the defence with Phil Jones out injured.
Chelsea subs: Cech, Zouma, Ake, Mikel, Baker, Salah, Schurrle.
Chelsea (4-2-3-1): Courtois; Ivanovic, Cahill, Terry, Filipe; Matic, Fabregas; Willian, Oscar, Hazard; Drogba.
Manchester United subs: Lindegaard, Blackett, Fletcher, Carrick, Herrera, Pereira, Wilson.
Manchester United (4-2-3-1): De Gea; Rafael, Smalling, Rojo, Shaw; Blind, Fellaini; Januzaj, Mata, Di Maria; Van Persie.
Before we go any further, the two team line-ups have been announced ahead of kick-off in around 20 minutes...

Sergio Aguero looks unstoppable, and the team looks incredibly dangerous as a whole with their quick transition play.

HALF TIME: MANCHESTER CITY 2-1 TOTTENHAM. There has been a stunning flow to this match through 45 minutes, with both sides causing quite a stir in attack. Sergio Aguero opened the scoring early on with a brilliant individual effort, only for Eriksen to pull the visitors level almost immediately. The Argentine was back at it shortly after, putting City ahead after Lampard won a penalty, and then nearly doubled the hosts lead from the spot yet again, but Lloris was up to the task.
(45’) NEARLY IN! City break again with incredible pace through Navas. The Spaniard picks out Fernandinho, who instead of having a shot, lays it off for Milner. The midfielder pushes it forward and sends a cross back into the centre, with Lloris caught out at the near post. Aguero is waiting in the middle, but cannot get his head to it as Tottenham clear!
(45’) Into the second of three minutes of added time, as a Chadli cross runs behind for a goal kick. City push forward one last time before the interval, but Navas is manhandled along the right, running the ball out of play, with no foul given.
(45’) Milner does incredibly well to track back and slide in to dispossess Capoue in midfield. He starts City forward in numbers, with Navas streaking into the area. The Spaniard strikes towards goal, but his effort needs to be better, making for an easy save by Lloris who tips over for a corner.
(44’) Eriksen making some wonderful runs forward, proving a handful to deal with for these City defenders. Tottenham are mustering one final push before the break in an attempt to pull themselves level.
(42’) SAVED AGAIN! Eriksen breaks into the are and cuts it back for Lamela. Kompany slides in to clear, but it falls for Mason at the top of the box. The midfielder smacks a half-volley towards goal, but Hart gets across to keep it out!
(40’) ERIKSEN! The Danish midfielder runs at the defence with real intent, stepping to his right and unleashing a drive from 30 yards out. Hart is never really tested, but is forced to push it behind for a corner. Lamela delivers, and again the keeper is out to punch clear.
(38’) The game has started to get a bit chippy now as Capoue makes a harsh tackle on Silva. It certainly looked like a lazy challenge, with no intention on getting the ball, but Moss has not seen it as such as the midfielder escapes without a caution.
--- 37’ Yellow card E. Dier goes into the referee's book. ---
(36’) Eric Dier becomes the second Tottenham player to be booked as he tugs on the shirt of Clichy, who was through into space along the left. It is a cynical challenge from the right-back, but an important one to keep City from catching Spurs at the back yet again.
(34’) WONDERFUL STOP! Aguero looks unstoppable at the moment! He takes a pass and breaks into the area one-on-one against Kaboul. He makes quick work of the defender, but cannot beat Lloris with his shot, the Frenchman getting down to his right to keep it out!
--- 33’ Yellow card R. Mason is cautioned by the referee. ---
--- 32’ Missed penalty ---
(32’) LLORIS SAVES! Aguero hits it low and down the centre, with the keeper diving to his left. Lloris does incredibly well to keep a foot in the middle, and is strong enough to keep it out! The rebound comes back to Aguero, but he lashes it over the bar.
(32’) ANOTHER PENALTY TO CITY! This one is a much easier call for Moss to make. City break with such pace, leaving Tottenham stretched at the back. Silva takes a pass in the area and Kaboul slides in, making no contact with the ball. He knew he was in trouble there.
(30’) Kompany lunges into the back of Chadli, who did well to turn and shield the ball. It is a needless foul from the City skipper, who concedes a free kick 30 yards out. Eriksen takes, but from a difficult angle, his effort sails high and wide at the near post.
--- 28’ Substitution F. Lampard is replaced with Fernandinho. ---
(28’) Lovely applause from both sets of fans as Lampard is taken off on a stretcher. With his loan deal set to expire in the winter, one has to wonder if this is his last contribution to a Premier League match. Fernandinho is on to replace him.
(26’) City put the ball out of play as Frank Lampard is down, clutching his left thigh. He looks in some real pain, trying to get back up, unsuccessfully. The training staff come out and this one does not look good for the former Chelsea midfielder.
(24’) NEARLY THREE! Again Navas does well to create space on the right. He eludes Fazio and sends a fine ball in for Aguero, but the strikers first time shot is straight at Lloris, who denies the Argentine a hat-trick... at least for the time being.
(22’) Looking for a third goal, City get right back into attack. Aguero makes a nice run through the heart of midfield, but cannot pick out a good enough pass for Silva, in yards of space in the area, as Tottenham manage to clear.
--- 20’ Goal! GOAL! Sergio Aguero makes no mistake, sending Lloris the wrong way, slotting home confidently in the bottom left corner and City have their lead restored after just five minutes! ---
(19’) PENALTY TO CITY! Lamela lunges into the back of Lampard, who goes to ground immediately, and referee Jonathan Moss does not hesitate to award the hosts a spot kick.
(17’) It would have been all too easy for Tottenham to crumble after the early Aguero goal. They could have cowered after shades of last season, but a stunning response, in the home of the defending champions, has them right back in this match!
--- 15’ Assist Soldado gave the assist. ---
--- 15’ Goal! Fernando is far too casual with the ball in his own end, as Lamela slides in to dispossess. Soldado picks up the ball and runs into the area, laying it off for Eriksen who blasts it home past Hart. It is a vital response from the visitors! ---
(15’) TOTTENHAM RESPOND WITHIN A MINUTE!
--- 13’ Assist The assist came from F. Lampard. ---
--- 13’ Goal! Lampard picks out Aguero to his left. The striker stops the ball and looks to take on Kaboul. He pauses for only a moment, before nudging the ball to his right and picking out the far corner. It is as easy as it gets for the Argentine. Top stuff from a top class striker. ---
(13’) JUST LIKE THAT, CITY ARE IN FRONT!
(11’) Lovely work by Navas in the area as he gets by Fazio with some clever footwork and sends a teasing ball across the face of goal. It is not attacked by City, however, as Lloris is able to collect and sniff out the danger.
(9’) OFFSIDE! City push forward looking for a response. Aguero makes a towering run into the box and cuts it back for Silva. The Spaniard is in prime position for a shot from in close, but opts to try and pick out a return pass. He does find Aguero, but the flag is up for offside as Lloris makes the save anyhow.
(7’) IMPORTANT SAVE! Tottenham can be very encouraged by their start here today. The visitors look to have a spring in their step, with City yet to wake up. Soldado sends a lovely ball through for Mason, who cannot beat Hart with the goal at his mercy. Hart makes a fine save, but the youngster really needs to be finishing there.
(5’) Sagna gets forward and he is picked out by Navas. Rose manages to sniff out the danger and clear, but Fernando wins the ball back in midfield. The hosts concede possession and Chadli breaks. He cuts back for Mason, but the midfielder shoots well wide from outside the box.
(3’) The Citizens were up 1-0 at this stage last year, so the start from Tottenham has, according to the numbers, been better. They have yet to really secure possession as the hosts push forward on two separate occasions, only to see their final ball cleared by Lloris and Fazio respectively.

As a result, Arsenal are now without a win in their last three league games heading into next weekend's must-win clash away to Sunderland, whilst Hull, who are unbeaten in their last two, face Liverpool in what is bound to be a tough game at Anfield on Saturday.
What a fantastic end to a fascinating game! Arsenal, who were on the front foot from start to finish, finally found the goal that they were looking for with just five minutes left to play, but they still leave with just a point after an excellent performance from the Hull defence. The visitors frustrated the hosts from the first whistle, allowing them to attack in waves, each time calmly dealing with the threat before regaining possession and pushing forward on counter-attacks of their own. It looked as if they might end up leaving the Emirates with what would have been three well-deserved points, but, in the end, they didn't have enough in the tank to do so, as Arsenal picked apart their well-disciplined defence with one of the last moves of the game.
FULL-TIME: ARSENAL 2-2 HULL CITY
(90’) Great save by Jakupovic! A fantastic curling pass is sent to the back post where Gibbs, who is completely unmarked, meets the ball with his outstretched foot, but his shot is tipped around the post by a fingertip save from the Swiss goalkeeper.
(90’) Cazorla unleashes a shot from 25 yards out that takes a slight deflection before being unconvincingly parried away by Jakupovic. --- 90’ +1 Assist A. Sánchez gave the assist. ---

(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be six minutes of added time.
(89’) Every outfield Arsenal player is camped inside the Hull half of the pitch as they push for a late equaliser. However, no matter how hard they try, the Hull defence, who now seem to have at least seven players as part of it, are keeping them at bay.
(87’) Great save by Jakupovic! A fantastic cross is sent into the heart of the box and it meets the head of Sanchez, but his diving effort on goal is wonderfully saved by the Hull goalkeeper, who tips it over the top of the crossbar.

(83’) Again, Dawson throws himself in front of a shot on goal, this time from Sanchez, and this one seems to have finished his game, as once again he is lying in a heap on the floor in considerable pain.

--- 80’ Yellow card Cazorla leaves his leg out and ends up clipping El Mohamady on the edge of the Hull penalty area, resulting in a free kick for the visitors and a yellow card for the Arsenal midfielder, who was visibly angry with the Egyptian's decision to go crashing to the ground so heavily. ---
(78’) After a few moments on the sideline, Dawson looks as if he is going to be able to continue, although he is still walking rather gingerly.
(77’) It looks as if Hull have another injury to deal with, as Dawson seems to be in serious pain after accidentally clashing with El Mohamady in front of his own goal.
(75’) Arsenal are pushing as many bodies forward as possible in an attempt to find an equaliser, but the Hull defence remain firm and well-disciplined. (73’) Hull deal with the corner well and break away on a quick counter-attack, but Ramirez isn't as fast as he would like to be and ends up being dispossessed midway inside the Arsenal half of the pitch.

(58’) Sanchez clips Chester from behind near the halfway line and Hull are awarded a free kick and, more importantly, an opportunity to breathe after having to deal with a plethora of Arsenal attacks. The visitors seem content to sit back and hold on to their one-goal advantage, even at this relatively early stage of the game.
(56’) Oxlade-Chamberlain wonderfully twists and turns around three Hull defenders down the left flank but ends up running out of pitch before he can get a cross away, resulting in a goal kick for Hull.
(54’) A poor pass from Huddlestone gives the ball away in the middle of the pitch and Arsenal are able to break away on a quick counter-attack. A fantastic ball is sent through by Wilshere to Welbeck, but the striker is dispossessed by a wonderful, perfectly-timed sliding tackle by Dawson.
(52’) Sanchez pushes forward and tries to chip a pass into the path of Welbeck, but Dawson is there to cut out the danger with a strong header on the edge of the Hull penalty area before a poor Oxlade-Chamberlain pass ends up gifting the visitors with a throw-in near the halfway line.
(50’) Davies brings down Sanchez and Arsenal are awarded a free kick midway inside Hull's half of the pitch, but they are unable to make the set-piece count and the visitors easily regain possession.
(48’) Like in the first half, Arsenal seems to be trying to patiently pass their way through the middle of the Hull defence, but, as was the case in the opening 45 minutes of the game, they are finding little luck in the visitors' half of the pitch.

--- 46’ Goal! GOAL! What a start for Hull! Hull's defence looked shaky and ill-disciplined in the opening stages but were far more impressive as the game wore on, and they now seem content to sit back and allow Arsenal to come at them before regaining possession and breaking away on swift counter-attacks. So far, it has worked, and Arsenal desperately need a change in tactic if they are going to find the back of the net again in the final 45 minutes.
Arsenal go into the half-time break deeply disappointed to not be at least a goal ahead, which is clear from the looks of frustration on the faces of the players and fans, not to mention Wenger, who is stood shaking his head on the sideline. The hosts have bossed possession from start to finish and have easily been the better of the two sides in front of goal, but are continuously letting themselves down with poor passes in the final third of the pitch.

(67’) West Ham win successive corners and Cole is getting his head to nearly everything at the moment! He turns it wide, however, as the chance goes begging. The Hammers have scored six goals from set-piece situations this season, the highest tally of any Premier League side.

(65’) Burnley make a switch, in an attempt to get some more pace up top, with Ashley Barnes replacing Lukas Jutkiewicz, who has been unable to convert his chances today.
(63’) OH MY! INGS NEARLY LEVELS THINGS! Trippier gets forward again and sends a wonderful ball of his own in for Ings. The striker meets it well, but his header glances inches wide of the far post! Turf Moor is shaking with all the noise now!

(60’) BURNLEY ARE BACK IN THIS WITH A GOAL!

(58’) Enner Valencia gives way for West Ham in the first substitution of the match. The second goalscorer, who had a lengthy travel itinerary during the international break, comes off to a rowdy applause from the visiting supporters.
(56’) It is incredibly harsh on Burnley who could have been up 2-0 themselves at half time. They failed to convert their chances and now have been made to pay. The atmosphere at Turf Moor has changed drastically, as the traveling supporters from East London are the ones making the noise at the moment.
--- 54’ Assist The assist came from C. Jenkinson. ---

(54’) ABSOLUTELY INCREDIBLE! WEST HAM DOUBLE THEIR LEAD!
(51’) STAT ATTACK: Diafra Sakho has now scored in five consecutive league matches for West Ham, tying Carlton Cole as the only player in Hammers history to do so.
--- 49’ Assist The assist came from A. Cresswell. ---

(49’) WELL THERE'S NOTHING CAGEY ABOUT THAT! SAKHO GIVES WEST HAM THE LEAD!
(48’) It has been a much more cagey start to this second half, a polar opposite from the wide open match we saw in the opening 45 minutes. Both teams looked to be going for it in the first half, but it appears now as though neither want to be the first to concede.
(46’) West Ham get the second half underway! No changes to tell you about at the break.
STAT ATTACK: Burnley's last two home matches resulted in 0-0 draws. They have not had three scoreless top flight matches in a row at Turf Moor in their history.
HALF TIME: BURNLEY 0-0 WEST HAM. Plenty of chances for both sides, but this one remains scoreless as we head into the break. The hosts have been the better side thus far, creating opportunities for themselves as a result of some wonderful build up play, but West Ham have threatened on the counter.
(45’) ARFIELD! Lovely build up from Burnley! It has been a real joy to watch through the first half. The Scotsman takes a pass and cuts into the centre, letting fly from the top of the box, but a deflection takes the sting out of the shot and Adrian makes a comfortable stop.

(41’) Amalfitano returns the favor! The West Ham midfielder shows some skill of his own, sending a back heel flick on for Sakho. The striker has Valencia to his right, but tries to take Duff on himself. A heavy touch allows the centre-back to recover as the chance goes begging.
(39’) Lovely vision from Boyd! He is causing all sorts of problems down the right, this time cutting it into the middle before sending a back heel pass through for Jutkiewicz. Cresswell recovers, however, showing his strength to shield off the striker and win a goal kick.
(37’) STAT ATTACK: The last time these two played a Premier League match at Turf Moor was back in February 2010, where the hosts came away with a 2-1 victory thanks to goals from David Nugent and Danny Fox.
(35’) Winston Reid with a very cynical challenge on George Boyd, as the midfielder had him beat, looking to break on a real promising looking counter. The foul earns the centre-back a yellow card, the first of the match handed out by Kevin Friend.

(27’) SO CLOSE TO THE OPENER! West Ham attack well down the left, as Cresswell makes a fine overlapping run. He sends a fantastic ball in for Sakho, but the striker heads wide from just a few yards out at the near post.
(25’) Boyd does well to win and keep possession for Burnley along the right. He switches the play and Kightly tries to thread in a pass for Ings, but some tough defending from Collins sees him clear the danger away.

(21’) Another strong move from Burnley, and the ball is played into the box, but it just will not sit still for a shot from Jutkiewicz! The hosts keep possession and Kightly wins a free kick to the left of the penalty area.
(19’) Back come West Ham and they get men forward in numbers. Enner Valencia, certainly never lacking for confidence, lashes a shot from 40 yards out, which sails well over the bar, earning a teasing applause from the Turf Moor crowd.
(17’) Boyd makes a nice run into space along the right and sends in a cross for Jutkiewicz. The striker makes muffed contact, under pressure from Collins, and the effort loops over the bar.

(11’) Important tackle from Collins! Jutkiewicz gets on the end of a pass and looks to split the defence and run in on goal, but the centre-back lunges in well to dispossess.
(9’) BURNLEY LEAD! But the flag is up for an offside, so it will not count! Absolutely sublime run from Danny Ings, who beats two defenders on his way into the area, before cutting onto his right. West Ham look an entirely different side to the one that nearly had Sam Allardyce sacked last season. Some shrewd summer signings have really added tooth to an otherwise lifeless attack, averaging barely over a goal per game last season. The potential of this group knows no limits, it will just be a matter of winning the games they are supposed to, and avoiding any prolonged poor runs of form. But it really is shocking what a difference a year makes – last season at this time, the Hammers looked like early candidates for relegation, whereas now, a top 10 finish is not so much as a possibility, but an expectation.
The spirit of this Burnley team is rivaled only by that of their manager, Sean Dyche. Unfortunately for this irrepressible bunch, that is not enough to keep them in the Premier League. Just seven games into the new season and their deficiencies have jumped to the forefront. Goals have been about as rare as a solar eclipse, and the return of last season's leading scorer Sam Vokes cannot come soon enough for the Clarets. They are up against quite a fight to remain in the top flight, and points will be at a premium in every match from here on out.

Thank you for joining us here for our live text coverage of Crystal Palace - Chelsea!
The match had a little bit of everything, with individual brilliance from set-pieces, red cards, beautiful attacking plays, and even some dull periods. It wasn't always fantastic from Chelsea but it was effective. On Palace's part, they'll be able to take some pride away from the showing and proved that they'll be able to take on other teams should they play with just a little more verve.
(90’) And that's the match! Despite a late goal here, Chelsea hang on for the win and emerge as 2-1 victors over Crystal Palace to keep their brilliant start to the season alive.
(90’) Zaha pulls down Felipe Luis as he goes to race down the flank, and Chelsea have a free-kick that they'll be in no rush to take, despite the protestations of the fans in the stands.

(90’) In the first of four minutes of added time now, and Mourinho has thrown on Drogba in a surprising move, perhaps hoping the presence of the club legend will lift his team and inspire fear into the home side.

(76’) Palace are doing better not to keep possession - perhaps the effect of having used all three substitutes and having fresher legs than the visitors - but they just cannot find a way into the box.
(75’) Oscar's turn now to go close-but-not-quite, as his shot towards the far post is too close to Speroni and the goalkeeper smothers it.

(31’) Matic creates space for himself and then takes a shot from about 15 yards outside of the box, but his shot goes well wide.

The players make their way on to the pitch for this delayed match between Newcastle and Leicester. Under fire manager Pardew will be hoping for a fast start from his players to ensure the atmosphere inside St James' Park does not turn sour.
Anita steps in to the starting line-up to make his fourth start of the season in midfield, it will the former Ajax man's 64th league game for Newcastle. Ferreyra is still waiting for his first appearance for the Toon Army since joining on loan from Shaktar Donetsk.
LINE UP CHANGE: Cheick Tiote has picked up an injury in the warm-ups so will be replaced by Vurnon Anita in the starting XI. Facundo Ferreyra steps up to the bench.
Kick-off is just 20 minutes away at St James' Park. It is a tale of two in-form strikers today. Papiss Cisse, who looked to be surplus to requirements this season having scored just 10 goals in his last 50 league games, has rediscovered his scoring form in the early part of this campaign, bagging four in three with a brace against Hull City and Swansea City. Leonardo Ulloa has been one of the bargains of the summer for Leicester, since his club record £8 million move from Brighton and Hove Albion, notiching five in seven including a double against Manchester United and the winner against Stoke City.
Nigel Pearson, who had two stints as Newcastle caretaker manager in 2007 and 2008, has succeeded in making Leicester difficult to beat this season. Especially at the King Power Stadium where they are unbeaten in four games, including that 5-3 win over Manchester United. Away from home they have found it more difficult, losing 2-0 at Chelsea and Crystal Palace, however they did claim a 1-0 win against Stoke at the Britannia Stadium on 13th September.
Having played three home games this season, conceding seven goals, Newcastle will be looking for a much improved performance in defence. The return of local boy Steven Taylor to partner Fabricio Collocini in defence will be a welcome sight for the Toon Army as they look to tighten up their back line. Daryl Janmaat continues his record of starting every game this season at right-back, but the former Feyenoord man has been put under pressure to improve his defensive performances this season.
It has been announced that kick-off in the North East has been delayed until 4pm.
Kick-off at St James' Park has been delayed after an electronic scoreboard came loose in the blustery conditions. We will have more on the revised start time soon.
Nigel Pearson makes three changes to his Leicester side that drew 2-2 at home to Burnley. In come Marc Albrighton, Esteban Cambiasso and Matty James replacing Dean Hammond, Jamie Vardy and Riyad Mahrez.
The Foxes currently sit 12th in the table and have adapted well to life in the Premier League, much of this is down to the goals of Leonardo Ulloa who has scored five goals in his seven appearances since joining from Brighton. He starts up front today with his usual strike partner David Nugent settling for a spot on the substitute’s bench. Having scored for England u-21's in their 2-1 second leg win against Croatia, Liam Moore starts today in a defence that has been ever present this season.
Newcastle continue to search for their first win of the season and manager Alan Pardew makes a single change to the side that drew 2-2 at Swansea before the international break. Steven Taylor comes in to the centre of defence, for just his second appearance of the season, replacing Mike Williamson. Papiss Cisse reclaims his place up front after scoring four goals in the last three Premier League matches. Emmanuel Riviere is out injured so 17-year-old Adam Armstrong is on the bench. Having been brought in from the cold to start against Swansea, Gabriel Obertan keeps his place on the right wing and Yoan Gouffran starts on the left, still looking for his first goal in 2014.

Vargas popped up again to bring the match level but in the fifth minute of added time Steven Caulker sent the ball into his own net! The R's remain bottom of the table, while Liverpool rise to fifth.

(19’) Some nice interplay between Johnson, Henderson and Balotelli sets the Italy international away down the left flank. He loops the ball over the head of Yun but is closed down by Caulker on the edge of the box as he looks to continue his run into the area. The centre-back makes sure of the clearance with a powerful scissor kick!
(17’) Lallana goes in late on Zamora and the referee awards the hosts a free kick. The England international complains to the official, and he may have a point because he certainly looked to have taken the ball.
(15’) STAT: Zamora has failed to score in any of his previous 12 Premier League starts for QPR. He's looking in the mood today, though!
(13’) Sterling slides a brilliant pass in behind the defence for Balotelli to run onto. The Italian's run is timed to perfection but it doesn't stop him from only reaching the ball at an acute angle. He turns and faces up Caulker but shows too much of it to the centre-back, who comes away with it.
(12’) Yun initiates a quick one-two and breaks into the box from the byline. However, Sterling is back chasing and tracks him all the way to knock the ball out for a corner.
(11’) This has been really positive from Rangers so far. Are they going to be able to keep this up all afternoon, though?
(9’) AUSTIN! HE SHOULD SCORE! The striker wins a 50-50 with Johnson and then Skrtel fails to clear the danger as he dives in at the top of the box. Austin pokes a shot at goal which Mignolet blocks, but the ball deflects off Skrtel and back to the striker. He attempts to slot it in on the spin from an acute angle but he only finds the side netting.
(8’) QPR are doing well to pen Liverpool back inside their own half here. They are frequently finding Zamora and the striker is doing a good job of holding up possession and encourage his team-mates to make runs off the ball.
(6’) Can slides the ball out to Henderson on the left and he drives a great low cross into the box. It finds Balotelli but the Italian is unable to control it well enough to get a shot away.
(4’) Onuoha's free kick from deep on the left is flicked into the box by Caulker, but none of his team-mates are able to beat Mignolet to it! The keeper gathers the ball up calmly.
(3’) Yun flights a great ball up from the back and Zamora holds off Lovren to cushion it down with his chest. He tees it up for Austin at the top of the box but the former Burnley man cannot get his foot over it enough to stop his strike from sailing over the top.
(2’) Yun sends a long thrown down the left flank and as Johnson attempts to hack it clear he misses the ball and smashes his foot into Austin's shin. He goes down in paid, but Austin didn't seem to feel it at all!
(1’) We are underway at Loftus Road!
The teams are out on the pitch now, so kick off will be upon us in just a few short minutes.
Redknapp has won just five of his 32 Premier League games in charge of QPR. It is probably the best time to play Liverpool, who are usually so intense and exciting under Rodgers, as they currently sit 10th in the table with 10 points from their opening seven games.
Liverpool substitutes: Jones, Toure, Manquillo, Allen, Markovic, Coutinho, Lambert.
Liverpool (4-2-3-1): Mignolet; Johnson, Skrtel, Lovren, Jose Enrique; Gerrard, Can; Sterling, Henderson, Lallana; Balotelli.
QPR substitutes: Murphy, Ferdinand, Traore, Kranjcar, Phillips, Hoilett, Vargas.
QPR (3-5-2): McCarthy; Onuoha, Dunne, Caulker; Isla, Sandro, Fer, Henry, Suk-Young; Austin, Zamora.
