(75’) A quarter of an hour remains for the away side to find that all-important goal, with the Citizens going much closer over the last ten minutes or so. Silva has been in unstoppable form, but even with the Spanish maestro pulling the strings, Aguero hasn't been able to capitalise.
(73’) Very close for Man City! Kolarov drives to the left byline, before firing a low delivery across the face of goal! Senderos stretches to turn the ball behind for a corner. The set piece is swung in and Mangala meets it, but Guzan gets all of his body behind the effort to smother it well.
(72’) Aguero fires straight at Guzan! Silva plays a lovely ball through for the Argentine to run onto, before the former Atletico forward places a well-struck finish directly down the centre of the goal. Man City are looking threatening, but haven't forced the goalkeeper into too much work.
--- 71’ Substitution J. Grealish comes on for K. Richardson. ---
--- 71’ Substitution L. Bacuna enters play, replacing C. N'Zogbia. ---
(71’) Bacuna and Grealish come into the fray in place of N'Zogbia and Richardson, as Lambert looks to freshen things up and keep his options ready for counter-attacks. As Man City start to dominate again, they might just leave some gaps in behind for Villa to exploit.
(70’) Villa are camping deep in their own half now. Milner cuts back a fantastic ball to the edge of the six-yard box, after being released by Silva, before the former Valencia man steers a close-range finish just wide of the far post! Guzan might not have got there, had it been on target!
(68’) Silva dances into the penalty area, but the Spaniard's eventual shot is tame and heads straight at Guzan. Man City are starting to get back on top, but Pellegrini's men are running out of time to take the lead in this contest.
(67’) Villa are continuing to look resilient, frustrating the away side. Toure tries to scoop a pass over the hosts' back four, but Baker hoofs clear. The Englishman has been key to Lambert's men keeping the scoreline goalless.
(65’) Fernando replaces Dzeko for the away side, which might lead to Yaya Toure having more license to get forward, as the former Porto midfielder can break up play and provide a foundation for the Citizens to build upon. Milner plays a great one-two with Lampard, but Delph tracks back and makes an important challenge.
--- 64’ Substitution Fernando enters play, replacing E. Džeko. ---
(64’) Man City win a free kick on the periphery of the penalty area, which Silva stands over intimidatingly. The former Valencia midfielder curls a right-footed effort towards the top right corner, but the ball whistles narrowly over the crossbar.
(62’) Less than half an hour remains for Man City, with Villa taking belief from the introduction of talismanic striker Benteke. The Belgian forward gets in behind immediately and breaks to the byline, but Mangala intercepts the former Genk man's cut-back well.
--- 61’ Substitution C. Benteke enters play, replacing A. Weimann. ---
(60’) Weimann heads wide! Hutton picks out a near post cross, before the Austrian striker diverts an effort beyond the far upright! That might be the last contribution of the evening for the lone striker, who hasn't had the rub of the green.
(59’) Benteke is warming up for the home side, which has given a lift to the atmosphere inside the stadium. The longer this match goes on without Man City finding an opening goal, the more confidence will be instilled in Lambert's side. If it stays goalless, Villa could nick three points late on.
(57’) Despite a fierce and high tempo start to the second half, Villa are still holding out for the moment. By staying compact and narrow in defence, Dzeko and Aguero are having problems finding sufficient space in and around the box to truly test Guzan.
--- 56’ Substitution F. Lampard enters play, replacing Fernandinho. ---
(55’) Fernandinho receives some treatment after landing awkwardly following an aerial challenge with Weimann. Lampard is warming up on the sidelines for Man City as a result and looks likely to replace the Brazilian.
(53’) N'Zogbia goes on a brilliant run, ghosting past two challenges, before failing to poke a pass out wide to the left for Richardson to run onto! Westwood manages to strike the rebound towards goal, but Hart claims under pressure from Weimann.
(51’) Great ball in from Kolarov! The Serbia international arrows a powerful delivery through the corridor of uncertainty, with Dzeko unable to poke home a close-range finish! Guzan was at full stretch, he thought that cross might creep in!
(50’) Delph drives through the centre of midfield, before the England international sees a strike deflected wide of the target! He wants a corner, but the referee awards a goal kick - a very tight call indeed!
(48’) Great save from Guzan! Silva swivels and shoots from 15 yards out, with the Spaniard's effort taking a profound deflection off the knee of Senderos! The American goalkeeper readjusts brilliantly to push the danger away!
(47’) Aguero strikes the post! Villa then break and Hart denies Richardson! Milner slides a great pass into the path of the Argentine striker, who places a finish onto the upright! The hosts counter, finding Richardson in space down the left, but the England international goalkeeper makes a top save!
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! No goals were forthcoming before the interval, but there's bound to be continued entertainment as Man City look for the points required to maintain pace with Chelsea.
Dzeko and Aguero have had half chances, but Guzan remains largely untested. Milner and Kolarov have hit the woodwork, while Weimann has had the odd glimmer of hope at the other end. Be sure to rejoin us in ten minutes for all of the second half action.
HALF TIME! It remains goalless at the break at Villa Park, with Man City going much the closer to taking the lead. Corners aplenty for the reigning champions, but resilient hosts' defending has frustrated the away side thus far. Baker, in particular, has been a vital piece of Lambert's defensive jigsaw.
(45’) Another corner is floated in, which Baker clears. The resulting set piece is swung to the back post, which Dzeko meets, but Cissokho gets a vital touch to turn it wide! Several set pieces in quick succession for Man City, but no luck for the Citizens!
(45’) Milner hits the side netting! Hutton holds Dzeko up well, forcing the former Wolfsburg striker to look backwards. The former Villa midfielder is picked out, before his first-time effort is deflected narrowly wide of the near post. The away side win the corner, which is used to pick out Kolarov, but the Serbian left-back drills a shot wide!
(43’) Pellegrini's side are starting to take real control, pressing forward with intent constantly. Villa are dropping deep and plugging gaps, leaving the lone running of Weimann to be their sole outlet to break upfield. Baker makes a great intervention to rob Aguero of possession as he looked to pivot just inside the 18-yard box.
(41’) Dzeko is denied by Senderos! Silva finds Milner at the right byline, before the former Villa midfielder pulls back a clever cross. The Bosnia international controls well and spins, but Senderos is on hand to make a good block. Less than five minutes until the break for Man City to find an opening goal.
(39’) Milner is found offside! The midfielder is set on his way in behind the Villa defence, before he hooks a clever touch over Guzan and places his finish onto the foot of the near post from a tight angle. Fortunately for the England international, the linesman's flag was raised anyhow.
(38’) Weimann spurns a good chance! Delph wins the ball back in the middle of midfield, before feeding his lone striker. The Austrian forward tries his luck from the edge of the box, but Kompany and Mangala recover well to make a timely block between them.
(37’) Just wide from Kolarov! The left-back sends a 30-yard free kick zipping off the turf and past the upright, with Guzan scrambling! The Villa goalkeeper hasn't had a great deal to do thus far, to say that the away side are trying to push to find the game's elusive first goal.
(36’) Fernandinho finds Silva in the hole, but Baker comes through the back of the Spain international to surrender another free kick. Rash decisions such as that from the Aston Villa defender could prove much more costly later in the contest.
(34’) Baker does well to rise in between Aguero and Dzeko to head clear, as Villa continue to defend fairly solidly. Zabaleta then breaks down the right before cutting a pass back inside to the Bosnia international, but the Man City striker balloons his strike horrifically over the crossbar.
(32’) Great interception from Kompany! Westwood tries to pick out Weimann, who makes an intelligent run in behind for the home side. Just when the Austrian striker looked to be through on goal, Man City's captain slid in to defuse the situation.
(31’) Hutton tries to flight a cross into the penalty box from 35 yards out, but gets his angles all wrong. Instead of finding the head of Weimann, the Scotland international sees his delivery loop onto the roof of the net!
(29’) Dzeko breaks to the left byline, before cutting a ball across the penalty area - but Villa clear. Kolarov then delivers from the same flank, finding the head of Aguero, but the diminutive striker's glancing header whistles just wide of the far post!
(27’) Silva delivers a free kick from the left-hand side, but Senderos is able to half-clear at the back post, before Man City work all the way back into their own half. Pellegrini's men are struggling to peg Villa in their own half and exert dominance.
(25’) N'Zogbia blazes wide! The former Wigan man drives through the middle of the field, before shifting the ball onto his left foot. He lets fly from 30 yards, with Hart diving full stretch to ensure that the effort doesn't creep inside his far post.
--- 24’ Yellow card A. Kolarov is yellow-carded. ---
(24’) Aguero has gone on several driving runs through the heart of the Villa defence, but it isn't quite happening for the Argentine international yet. The odd poor touch is letting him down. Kolarov picks up a yellow card for a poorly timed tackle, as Man City look lightweight down their left.
(22’) Weimann goes close to opening the scoring, but would have been offside! N'Zogbia whips in a teasing back post cross, but Kompany steps up to catch the Austrian the wrong side of him. Hart manages to gather, despite a touch from the Villa striker, at the second attempt.
(21’) The home fans are actively urging their side on, probably buoyed by the fact that Man City's defence look rather uncertain while on the ball. Mangala and Kompany have made a couple of nervy decisions already. The away side break, before Baker makes a brilliant challenge to dispossess Dzeko.
(19’) Man City are settling into this one, but Villa are keen to constantly press and harry, with Weimann leading the charge as their lone striker. Pellegrini's side are retaining possession, but haven't been able to hurt the hosts as of yet.
(17’) Silva releases Aguero down the right-hand side, before the Argentine sets it back to Toure. The Ivory Coast international plays a ball to the right channel, when the former Atletico Madrid striker darts inside and looks for a positive one-two. Clear miscommunication and Toure raises an apologetic hand.
(15’) The opening quarter of an hour has proved threatening for Man City, but Guzan has been equal to everything the Citizens have been able to throw at him thus far. Senderos has thus far been able to keep close tabs on Aguero.
(13’) Richardson clips a ball forward for Weimann, which Kompany needs two attempts to clear upfield. The away side are having the more telling pressure early on, with Yaya Toure seeing plenty of the ball already for the reigning champions.
(11’) Kolarov strikes the post! The Serbia international is found on the edge of the penalty box, before hitting a ferocious strike towards goal! It deflects slightly off the boot of Hutton, before kissing the woodwork and bouncing clear for a throw in!
(9’) Toure looks to split the Villa defence with an early pass, trying to slide the ball into the path of Aguero, but Senderos just about makes an interception. Things are fairly open for Man City in the opening minutes, with Lambert's side not looking as solid as they have done with Vlaar marshalling the back four.
(7’) Mangala nearly makes a costly error in defence, with Weimann snapping at the Frenchman's heels. The Austrian forward is a late switch, with Agbonlahor being taken out of the matchday squad in favour of Jack Grealish late on.
(5’) Zabaleta looks early from the right, looping a cross in towards the back post for Dzeko, but Senderos makes an important defensive header. Moments later, Man City throw another ball into the area, before Yaya Toure's effort is blocked by Baker on the edge of the area.
(3’) Milner tracks back and dispossesses Richardson, with the former Aston Villa midfielder presumably keen to impress this afternoon. Westwood looks to find the former Fulham man once again moments later, but his pass is woefully inaccurate.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at Villa Park, as Man City look to continue their title charge at the expense of stuttering Aston Villa. The home side are in their traditional claret and blue, while Pellegrini's men line up in navy.
Man City substitutes: Sagna, Fernando, Caballero, Navas, Lampard, Demichelis, Jovetic.
Man City starting line-up: Hart; Zabaleta, Kompany, Mangala, Kolarov; Milner, Fernandinho, Yaya Toure, Silva; Dzeko, Aguero.
Villa substitutes: Clark, Bacuna, Weimann, Bent, Benteke, Sanchez, Given.
Villa starting line-up: Guzan; Hutton, Senderos, Baker, Cissokho; Delph, Westwood, Cleverley; N'Zogbia, Agbonlahor, Richardson.
TEAM NEWS: Aleksandar Kolarov starts at right-back for the away side, with Eliaquim Mangala continuing in the heart of defence at the expense of Martin Demichelis. Fernando misses out, as Fernandinho and Yaya Toure make up the central midfield duo for Pellegrini's eleven. Edin Dzeko and Sergio Aguero make up what is a formidable front two, with the likes of Stevan Jovetic and Jesus Navas on the bench.
TEAM NEWS: Nathan Baker and Philippe Senderos are the central defensive partnership for the hosts, with Ron Vlaar sidelined through injury. Tom Cleverley starts in midfield, with Kieran Richardson and Charles N'Zogbia asked to do the running in wide areas to support the lone striker of Gabby Agbonlahor. As always, it looks like a counter-attacking 4-3-3 from Villa. Star striker Christian Benteke is among the substitutes.
I'm Simon Harrison and I will be keeping you up to date with all of the action from Villa Park, as Lambert's outfit attempt to right their faltering form, following a brilliant opening few games in their domestic campaign. After a slightly disappointing 1-1 draw midweek against Roma in the Champions League, the Citizens will want to get back on track with victory today.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Premier League action between Aston Villa and Manchester City in the English top flight's late kick-off. There hasn't been an away win all day in the division, a theme that Paul Lambert's side will be hoping continues until the end of play this evening. Manuel Pellegrini's men have only one thing in their sights, three points.

After struggling in their opening fixtures of the season, Manchester United go into the international break in a buoyant mood and looking in great attacking form. Everton, meanwhile, could drop into the relegation zone if QPR beat West Ham today, and are in desperate need of some of their key players regaining fitness. For now, I've been Tom Maston, and thanks for joining me.
The full-time whistle blows and Manchester United have recorded back-to-back wins for the firs time this season. Falcao's goal secured the points, though De Gea was the hero with a penalty save and two world-class stops in added time at the death. Van Gaal's side into the top four.
(90’) After Stones is stretchered from the field Everon eventually take their corner, and though Lukaku wins it at the near post, his header is wayward and flies into the stands behind the goal.
(90’) We've got a delay here as Everton wait to take their corner. Stones won the original header from that corner and has landed awkwardly. The Toffees look likely to end this game with 10 men.
(90’) WHAT A SAVE! De Gea is in quite ridiculous form. Barry's original shot is blocked by Blackett before Oviedo hits a half-volley that is destined for the top corner, only for the goalkeeper to pull off possibly the best save you'll see all season.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card J. Wilson is cautioned by the referee. ---
(90’) Everton win a free-kick right on the edge of the box as Wilson brings down Baines on the left-hand side of the area. The full-back will look to whip this into the box...
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card T. Howard receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) BRILLIANT SAVE! De Gea has been outstanding today and for the second time in quick succession he denies Osman. The midfielder pokes a powerful effort towards the corner from the edge of the box but the goalkeeper dives at full stretch away to his left to tip it behind.
(90’) Howard picks up a booking for taking exception to Van Persie, and we are into four minutes of stoppage time...
(89’) Lukaku, who has been poor today, looks to carry the ball into the box but the linesman's flag is up. Replays suggest the official got that right following Osman's lobbed pass.
(87’) Everton work the ball nicely down the right-hand side and Browning floats in a dangerous cross that Naismith heads against Rafael and out for a corner. Baines whips the dead ball in from the left, and after some pinball, Osman strikes a low effort through a sea of bodies that De Gea does well to hold onto.
(85’) Manchester United are not sitting back and Di Maria thinks he should have a corner after taking on Browning. The referee disagrees and Everton have a goal kick.
(83’) The home defence is yet to be tested as Everton's persistence in playing through midfield is slowing the tempo of the match. Osman and Oviedo have struggled since coming on.
(81’) Into the final 10 minutes now, and Naismith seems to have moved up front alongside Lukaku having been withdrawn for much of the match. We could be in a for a fantastic end to this game.
--- 79’ Substitution And United follow their visitors in utilising the last of their substitutions as Valencia is replaced by former Everton man Fellaini. ---
--- 78’ Substitution T. Hibbert is done for the day. T. Browning is his replacement. ---
--- 77’ Substitution In fact, we are not going to see Eto'o as Martinez makes his final two changes of the afternoon at the same time. Osman and Browning are the men coming on with McGeady and Hibbert replaced. ---
(75’) Everton are increasingly looking for Lukaku as they chase the game, but misplaced passes are letting them down. Surely Eto'o would be a good option for Martinez off the bench now.
--- 73’ Substitution One recent United academy graduate follows another onto the pitch as Wilson replaces the man whose goal separates the sides; Falcao. ---
--- 71’ Substitution United waste no time in making that change as Blackett replaces the England full-back for the final 19 minutes. ---
(70’) Shaw has been limping for some time now as well as clutching his knee and he may well be forced off here. He heads off the field for treatment with the club physio.
(68’) The air of nervousness around Old Trafford has certainly lifted since Falcao's goal, and as we enter the final quarter of the match the hosts look comfortable in possession. They would certainly like one more to probably make the game safe.
(66’) Valencia loses the ball on the edge of the Everton box which allows Barry to look for the run of Lukaku. The striker is beaten to the ball by De Gea, though the offside flag had already gone up.
--- 64’ Substitution Everton react to that goal by making a change with Pienaar replaced by Oviedo. The Costa Rica international scored the winner here last season but has barely played since following a broken leg suffered in January. ---
--- 62’ Assist Á. di María gave the assist. ---
--- 62’ Goal! GOAL!!! FALCAO MAKES IT 2-1! Against the run of play the Red Devils take the lead. Di Maria drives in a low effort from 30 yards that Falcao reads and stabs past Howard. Stones was playing him onside, and the former Atletico striker has his first goal in English football. ---
(61’) Manchester United could do with a period of possession to compose themselves following Naismith's goal. Everton are looking dangerous whenver they carry the ball forward.
(59’) OFF THE LINE! Suddenly Everton are all over United and almost take the lead through Jagielka. The defender meets Baines' corner at the near post and Falcao is in the right place to head away the goalbound effort.
(57’) Di Maria sends in a cross from the left as United look for an immediate response, and Jagielka does well to head over his own crossbar from inside the six-yard box. The resulting corner is then collected by Howard.
--- 55’ Yellow card Some concern here for Everton as Lukaku stays down after being caught late by Valencia. The winger is booked for the foul and the Belgium striker is eventually able to get up and continue without treatment. ---
--- 55’ Assist The assist came from L. Baines. ---
--- 55’ Goal! GOAL!!! NAISMITH EQUALISES! From the resulting free-kick Baines and Barry trade passes before the former whips in a superb ball to the far post from the left and Naismith dives in to he head home the equaliser. Toffees back on terms. ---
(53’) After four bookings in the first half, McGeady is fortunate to avoid becoming the first player to be yellow carded after the break after catching Rojo with a late challenge.
(51’) Shaw is having plenty of joy against Hibbert in an attacking sense and he is able to get to the byline this time before pulling the ball back for Falcao. The striker takes a touch before shooting, and though his effort is off-target it deflects behind off Stones.
(49’) Everton have begun the second half in an imposing manner but some sloppiness in the final third has meant the United defence has been comfortable.
(47’) SO CLOSE! After a Manchester United corner is cleared back out to Di Maria, the winger drives in a superb low cross from the right-hand side and Falcao is inches away from making contact at the far post.
(46’) No changes for either team and Everton kick-off to get us back underway...
The players are making their way back out onto the pitch at Old Trafford ahead of a crucial second half. That De Gea save, by the way, has ended Baines' 100 percent penalty record for Everton in the Premier League to an end. The full-back has scored his 14 previous efforts from the spot.
Everton have had plenty of possession, but until the penalty have struggled to get into the United area with any regularity. I'll be back in ten minutes to see if the Toffees can make amends for that penalty miss and get back into the game.
And with that the whistle blows for half-time, and De Gea's name is sung loud by the home fans as the players head for the dressing rooms. Di Maria's goal separates the sides with United deserving of their lead.
--- 45’ +4 Missed penalty ---
(45’) SAVED BY DE GEA! The left-back goes to the goalkeeper's right and De Gea gets down to push the ball away from a dangerous area. Brilliant from the Spain star.
(45’) PENALTY TO EVERTON! Right on the verge of half-time, Everton have a lifeline. Pienaar finds Hibber breaking into the box with a fine backheel, and Shaw dives in on the full-back. Friend has option but to point to the spot, and Baines will step up...
(45’) As we enter two minutes of stoppage time, United are enjoying a sustained period of possession. They have had much of their joy on the break today, but are now happy to keep the ball and not let this lead slip before the break.
(43’) Rafael is having a good game in an attacking sense and his ball creates another half-chance for the hosts. Van Persie looks to head the ball into Falcao's path but the strikers are not on the same wavelength and Everton can clear.
(41’) United win successive corners but from the second Falcao makes contact with Di Maria's cross, but his volley is timed incorrectly and eventually flies out for a throw-in.
(39’) Finally Lukaku manages to get away from McNair after a fine ball forward from Baines, but the striker's shot is not controlled and he slices it wide of the post. Everton's best chance of the game.
(37’) The Toffees continue to put pressure on the home goal as they win a free-kick in a good position on the left-hand side, but Baines' ball in is headed clear by Rafael. Another wasted opportunity by the visitors.
(35’) Everton win a corner on the left-hand side and Lukaku almost gets on the end of Baines' cross. Eventually Manchester United clear through Van Persie after some pinball in the box.
(33’) Despite falling behind, Everton are continuing to have the better of things in terms of possession, but they are yet to even create a half-chance in the final third. Lukaku is seeing less and less of the ball.
--- 31’ Yellow card Yet another booking, this time for Blind, as he goes in late on Naismith. The Scot is not happy about the challenge but replays suggest there was minimal contact. ---
(30’) GOOD SAVE! The Argentine's free-kick takes a slight deflection off the wall and Howard does well to sramble across his goal and tip it behind. That was destined for the top corner.
(29’) Manchester United win a free-kick around 30 yards from goal as Van Persie is barged to the ground by Barry. Unsurprisingly, Di Maria is lining it up with the ball slightly to the right of the goal.
--- 27’ Assist The assist came from Mata. ---
--- 27’ Goal! GOAL!!! DI MARIA OPENS THE SCORING! Manchester United take the lead, and though they have played most things down the left it is from the right that they find the net. Rafael's cross is cleared to Mata, and the midfielder tees up Di Maria, with the British record signing able to curl home from the edge of the box. ---
--- 26’ Yellow card Pienaar picks up the third booking of the afternoon as he loses the ball to Rafael before tripping the full-back as he looks to break forward. ---
(24’) Di Maria gets the ball on the left-hand side and lines up a shot from 25 yards that takes two deflections before swerving narrowly over Howard's crossbar. The resulting corner eventually comes for Blind on the edge of the box but his shot is a wild one and flies over the crossbar.
(23’) Everton have had the monopoly of possession in the first quarter of the game but are yet to have a shot on goal. They need to start moving the ball quicker in midfield.
(21’) Lukaku is causing the home defence problems as he looks to play with his back to goal. Rojo is looking to come across and help McNair out with the former Chelsea forward.
(19’) United yet again work the ball down the left-hand side as Shaw finds Di Maria, and the former Real Madrid player flicks a delightful pass into Falcao's path, but the striker can only drag his shot well wide of the post.
--- 17’ Yellow card Besic get his name taken by the referee after he trips Falcao on the halfway line as United looked to launch a counter-attack. McGeady's misplaced pass caused the problems for the visitors. ---
(15’) Lukaku uses his pace and strength to win a corner from McNair on the Eveton left, but Baines' ball is cleared by Shaw under pressure from a number of blue shirts.
(13’) Di Maria is having a fine game and again troubles the Everton defence with a brilliant ball into the box. The cross evades Baines but Mata cannot control it before Blind fires over the bar from long-range.
(11’) With Mata unable to stay tight to the Everton midfielders, Barry and Besic are able to pick their passes at will and control the pace of the game. Martinez will be pleased with the way his team has started.
--- 9’ Yellow card Referee Friend shows the first yellow card of the day as Van Persie is penalised for diving in on Barry and bringing the England international down in the centre circle. ---
(7’) United are getting plenty of joy down the left-hand side and this time it is Di Maria that whips in a quality cross into the box. Van Persie is the man on the end of it as he gets in front of Stones but the captain's volley flies well over the crossbar.
(6’) Everton are looking to play through midfield, with Piennar's quick feet winning two free-kicks in the space of a minute. Lukaku is holding the ball up well as he continues to keep McNair on his toes.
(4’) Manchester United create the first opportunity of the match as Shaw runs at Hibbert before crossing from the left-hand side, and Howard does well to hold onto Falcao's downward header.
(3’) Plenty of early possession for Everton in the opening stages, with Lukaku trying to put the inexperienced McNair under pressure. The Belgium international is back in a central role with Naismith behind him.
(1’) Manchester United kick-off and we are underway in the first Premier League match of the day...
The sides make their way out onto the pitch, and once we have had all the pre-match niceties we will be ready for kick-off. Can Manchester United make it three successive home wins or can Everton continue their good run against the Red Devils? We're about to find out...
The two teams have made their way into the tunnel and the atmosphere inside Old Trafford is at fever pitch. This should be a fantastic encounter between two teams who still have plenty to prove this season.
If recent history is anything to go by, Everton can be confident ahead of kick-off in under ten minutes time. The Toffees have lost just one of their last five meetings with Manchester United, and did the double over the Red Devils last season after Bryan Oviedo's late goal sealed a first win at Old Trafford since August 1992. The reverse fixture ended in a 2-0 win for the Goodison Park outfit and turned out to be David Moyes' final game as United manager.
As kick-off draws ever closer, those already inside Old Trafford are treated to the rare sight of Sir Alex Ferguson back out on the pitch. The former Red Devils manager is reintroducing Ji-Sung Park to the United fans after the former South Korea international was announced as the club's latest global ambassador earlier this week. Unsurprisingly the ovation was fantastic for both.
Roberto Martinez makes four changes to the Everton side that drew in Krasnodar as Romelu Lukaku and Steven Naismith unsurprisingly return. Muhamed Besic comes back in with James McCarthy out with a knock picked up by Liverpool while Steven Pienaar makes his first appearance since August 23. Seamus Coleman remains on the sidelines along with Kevin Mirallas and Sylvain Distin.
Van Gaal makes just two enforced changes from the team that played West Ham, with the suspended Rooney and injured Ander Herrera replaced by Juan Mata and Antonio Valencia. Paddy McNair, who made his debut against the Irons, continues at the heart of the defence despite Tyler Blackett again being available while Robin van Perise takes the captain's armband in Rooney's absence. Meanwhile, former Everton star Marouane Fellaini is on the bench for the first time since the opening day of the season.
Everton subs: Joel, Browning, Alcaraz, Oviedo, Gibson, Osman, Eto'o.
Everton: Howard; Hibbert, Stones, Jagielka, Baines; Besic, Barry; McGeady, Naismith, Pienaar; Lukaku.
Manchester United subs: Lindegaard, Thorpe, Blackett, Fletcher, Fellaini, Januzaj, Wilson.

Before we go any further, the two team line-ups have been announced with just over 20 minutes until kick-off...
Everton, meanwhile, have also had a disappointing start to the campaign and find themselves in 17th at kick-off today. The Toffees have won just two of their nine competitive outings this season but have taken points off both Arsenal and Liverpool. Their powers of recovery will be tested this afternoon after travelling back from Russia following their Europa League tie against Krasnodar on Thursday.
Louis van Gaal's side battled to a 2-1 victory over West Ham last time out, and though captain Wayne Rooney saw red in the second half, the confidence gained from that win will surely aid the hosts today. When the fixtures originally came out, many saw today's match as the first real test of the new-look Manchester United. Obviously they have already struggled against lesser sides, but with others faltering, they are far from out of the title race yet.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League encounter between Manchester United and Everton. FULL TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-0 SOUTHAMPTON. Christian Eriksen's goal proves to be the difference as Pochettino defeats his former team at White Hart Lane, to claim an important three points ahead of the international break. The visitors had their chances to pull level, most notably of which fell for Mane from five yards out, but the forward could not convert.
(90’) Bertrand wins a free kick just across the half-way line, as we reach the 93rd minute. They loft it into the box, and it is unconvincingly flubbed behind for a corner. Mike Jones blows his whistle, however, and there will be no time to take it!
(90’) Lloris boots the ball forward and it results in a throw for the hosts, which they are in no rush to take.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution H. Kane comes on for E. Lamela. ---
(90’) Tottenham run the first minute off the clock with a substitution, as Erik Lamela gives way for Harry Kane. Finally play resumes with Southampton taking the throw, but Schneiderlin's eventual through ball for Pelle is collected by Lloris.
(90’) Three minutes to be added on at the end here as the visitors pass it around in the attacking third...
(88’) Time running low for Southampton now as Spurs do well to keep the ball and string a few passes together. The visitors win it back and Capoue slides into the feet of Mane, conceding a foul just inside the Tottenham half.
(86’) Southampton really applying the pressure now, but Tottenham keep their shape well. Dier does well to escape a challenge from Bertrand and push up the pitch, however, a poor final ball runs to Forster, giving possession right back to the visitors.
(84’) MANE MISSES A SITTER! Lovely move from Southampton, as Bertrand gets possession in space on the left after Long does well to hold it up and pick out a pass. He sends a sensational ball across the face of goal into the feet of Mane, who simply needed to pass it into the back of the net. He makes a real meal out of the chance, pushing it wide. He really should have made it 1-1.
(83’) Forster inexcusably spills a cross, as it rolls behind for a corner. Nothing comes of it, much to his relief, but it needlessly wastes more time off the clock. The visitors have to start getting forward in numbers and putting pressure on this Tottenham defence like they have in spells thus far.
--- 82’ Substitution M. Dembélé enters the game and replaces C. Eriksen. ---
(81’) STAT ATTACK: Dating back to his time with Feyenoord in the Eredivisie, Graziano Pelle has scored 54 goals in his last 63 league appearances, including four in six matches with Southampton. Can he find an equalizer here today?
(79’) Kaboul does well to win Tottenham a corner, earning a roar from the home supporters. Eriksen delivers, but cannot get it past the near post as Long puts it behind for another, before finally clearing the second time.
--- 77’ Yellow card D. Tadić is cautioned by the referee. ---
(77’) Dusan Tadic commits a foul on Rose, after being taken out by the left-back on several occasions, with no yellow card being shown. Mike Jones sees this one as worthy enough for a booking, however, rather ironically showing a card to the Serbian winger.
--- 76’ Substitution V. Wanyama is replaced with S. Long. ---
(76’) Great defending by Alderweireld! Adebayor is sent through on goal, but the centre-back sticks his foot in from behind, stepping on the ball to sniff out the chance. The visitors look to break but a foul is committed, allowing Southampton to make their first change of the match.
(74’) Tadic delivers in well towards Schneiderlin at the far post, marked by the much smaller Rose. The Frenchman misjudges the cross, however, failing to get his head to the ball as it goes behind for a goal kick. Another wasted opportunity for the visitors.
(73’) Wanyama and Mane linking up along the left to put pressure on Tottenham. The winger loses his footing, but does well to keep the ball, forcing Capoue into a foul at the edge of the area, in a real promising position for Southampton.
(71’) Southampton are passing the ball around nicely. Schneiderlin switches play for Davis, who is subsequently taken out by Capoue, giving the visitors a free kick in a threatening position for a cross. Tadic over hits, however, sending the ball safely behind for a goal kick.
(69’) Now Danny Rose commits a foul on Tadic, yet another by the defender, who still has not been booked. The left-back is struggling to deal with the Serbian winger. This game is screaming out for Shane Long, who really could pose the defender a threat with his lovely combination of strength and pace.
(67’) Lamela is shown a yellow card for a soft challenge. We have seen much worse here today that has gone unpunished. Southampton restart play quickly, and Schneiderlin sends a ball forward for Mane, but Kaboul does well to shield him off, allowing Lloris to come off his line and collect.
--- 66’ Yellow card E. Lamela is cautioned by the referee. ---
(65’) BRILLIANT SAVE! Shocking defending by Spurs, as Kaboul scuffs his clearance. It falls kindly for Wanyama at the top of the area. He smacks a shot towards goal, but Lloris is up to the task, diving across to push the ball behind for a corner.
(64’) WHAT IS DAVIS DOING?! The midfielder makes a lovely run into the area and Tadic picks him out well. He gets into a shooting position, but slows the attack and tries to cut it back for Pelle, however, his pass is quite poor. Far too indecisive by Davis who should have done much better there.
(62’) Tottenham clear the corner and get forward quickly. Eriksen picks out Chadli who breaks into the area, but his shot is blocked and send behind by Bertrand. Lovely defensive work from the left-back, with Southampton stretched at the back.
(60’) Southampton win a throw in the attacking half, and Tadic does well to send Clyne in along the right. He delivers a good ball into the area, but Kaboul heads behind for a corner.
(58’) Well it is all breaking down in the final third early on in this second half, with neither side able to pick out a much needed good final ball. The field is being stretched well, but some important interceptions have proved timely.
(56’) STAT ATTACK: Southampton have won just two of their 15 matches at White Hart Lane in the Premier League.
(54’) Real sloppy couple of minutes as the teams fail to string more than a few passes together before conceding possession. There is a lovely flow to the match, but neither side is able to take advantage, with the ball exchanging hands at a rapid pace here.
--- 53’ Yellow card Y. Kaboul is yellow-carded. ---
(52’) Wonderful through ball by Pelle to send in Mane, putting plenty of pressure on Kaboul. The centre-back topples over the forward, which is a foul in the eyes of the referee, who shows him a yellow card. You have to wonder, with Mike Jones seeing it as a foul, Kaboul is extremely lucky not to have been sent off considering he was the last defender by quite a distance there.
(50’) Rose is taken down after a cynical challenge from Schneiderlin in midfield. The left-back is down and in pain, but again the leniency of Mike Jones comes into play, as the Frenchman escapes with only a warning. He will have to start putting players in the book or these challenges will no doubt continue.
(48’) Encouraging start from the visitors who win back possession and push up the pitch. Bertrand tries to pick out Mane, forcing Kaboul into a clearance that gives them a throw near the corner flag.
(46’) Tottenham kickoff the second half, as we get back underway at White Hart Lane!
Southampton have had an innate ability to grow into games this season, scoring eight of their 11 goals in the second half of their matches. They have plenty of quality in the final third, and Tottenham's defence is of course very susceptible to conceding goals.
STAT ATTACK: Tottenham have lost their last two Premier League matches at White Hart Lane – against Liverpool and West Brom. The last time they suffered three defeats in a row at their North London fortress was back in September of 2008.
HALF TIME: TOTTENHAM 1-0 SOUTHAMPTON. The hosts have really come on in the final 15 minutes, after a very timid start to the match in which Saints were the ones asking the questions. Tottenham found their breakthrough just a few minutes before the break off a lovely finish by Christian Eriksen, and Chadli was unlucky not to double that lead just a few minutes later.
(45’) Southampton have had their share of possession in the attacking third, and have asked questions of the Tottenham defence, however, they cannot find that final ball at the moment. An errant Tadic pass runs behind and that is the last of the action in the first half.
(45’) Into the first of three minutes of added time, and Lloris produces a fine save! Tadic strikes a free kick from 25 yards out, and his effort takes a slight deflection off the wall. It looks to be headed in at the near post, but the French keeper scurries across to make the save.
(44’) OFF THE POST! A lightning quick break from Tottenham, with Adebayor and Chadli linking up. The Belgian, who already has four goals this season, is through on goal, but rings his shot off the woodwork! What a massive goal that would have been on the stroke of half time.
(42’) Southampton get forward quickly, eager to try and get level before the break. Pelle picks up a pass from 25 yards out, and has options to his left, but opts to have a shot, producing a simple save from Lloris.
--- 40’ Assist N. Chadli gave the assist. ---
--- 40’ Goal! Tottenham Hotspur score a goal through C. Eriksen! ---
(40’) Well-worked move by the hosts. Adebayor finds Chadli, who lays it off wonderfully for Eriksen. The midfielder takes a quick first touch to stretch Alderweireld, his former Ajax teammate, and send his shot through the defenders legs and past Forster at the near post.
(40’) GOOOOOOAL! ERIKSEN PUTS TOTTENHAM IN FRONT!
(39’) STAT ATTACK: Southampton have conceded just four goals this season, fewest in the Premier League ahead of five teams tied with seven.
(37’) WONDERFUL STRIKE! Eriksen picks up a pass and immediately cuts towards the middle. He darts forward through the heart of defence, and lets fly on his left foot. It is a stinging shot that Forster gets his hands too, but a wicked backspin nearly takes the ball into the net, rolling just wide.
(35’) The game is starting to tilt again in the favor of the hosts this time. Southampton are on the back foot after dominating possession for a lengthy period. Wanyama commits a foul with a challenge on Lamela, giving Tottenham a free kick from jut inside the attacking half.
(33’) Rose wins a free kick for the hosts, and the stoppage allows Tottenham to make a substitution, with the injured Naughton giving way to Eric Dier. The free kick is played short, but Kaboul lacks the creativity to convert it into a scoring chance, as the opportunity goes begging.
--- 32’ Substitution E. Dier enters play, replacing K. Naughton. ---
(31’) Another clumsy challenge! Ryan Bertrand and Kyle Naughton both try and run onto a loose ball. The Southampton defender is second to it, sticking out a foot to try and make a challenge, but goes over top the ball and catches Naughton with his studs. Very dangerous, that, and he as well is extremely lucky to not be shown yellow... or worse.
(29’) YIKES! Danny Rose is extremely lucky not to find his name in referee Mike Jones' book. The left-back slides in very late with a challenge on Tadic, taking the attacker out with his trailing leg. He gets a stern talking to, but no action taken for the tackle which happened directly in front of the two managers on the touch line.
(27’) NEARLY AN OPENER! A chance materializes from nothing, really, as Lamela darts through the middle and lets fly with his left. The shot appears to be going in at the near post, but Forster dives across to get fingertips on it, pushing it behind.
(25’) STAT ATTACK: Tottenham managed just 31.2 per cent possession against Arsenal last weekend, their lowest total since 2006.
(23’) Tottenham finally get up the pitch and win their second corner of the match. It falls kindly for Kaboul at the top of the area, but he tries to pass it back into the danger area as opposed to swinging his foot through the ball, and his pass goes astray, as Southampton clear the threat.
(21’) Nathaniel Clyne makes a strong run of his own down the right and wins a throw following a tackle by Danny Rose. The ball comes in and is passed around the area nicely. Mane finds it with space inside the left of the area, cutting it back for Schneiderlin, but the midfielder is not quick enough to react as the opportunity for a shot is wasted.
(19’) Play resumes and Wanyama wins a throw deep in Tottenham territory. Tadic sends a strong ball into the area but Vertonghen clears. The hosts subsequently boot it up the pitch, allowing the visitors to remain in possession. Lovely spell from Saints, who have hardly squandered the ball in the last 10 minutes.
(17’) We have a bit of a delay now as Mane is down and in need of treatment after extending to try and run onto the end of a long ball forward. The medical staff is out and you have to hope this is nothing serious for the Senegalese winger, who is making just his second Premier League start today.
(15’) Nervy moments at the back, and quite a disgruntled start from Tottenham. The hosts try and pass their way out of danger at the back, but Kaboul feels the pressure of Schneiderlin, with Lloris urging him to act quickly, and he blasts the ball out of play to give the visitors a throw.
(13’) Great interchange amongst the forwards. Mane and Pelle swap positions which allows the winger to get on the end of a through ball. He tries to cut it back for Davis in the centre, but Naughton gets there first to clear.
(11’) Southampton pressing well in midfield, which has left Tottenham struggling to break out of their own half at the moment. The visitors are passing it around well, and wasting very little time winning the ball back when they squander possession.
(9’) VITAL BLOCK! Fantastic break from Saints who get up the pitch with such precision. Pelle and Tadic work a one-two, with the striker picking out Mane with his pass across the face of goal. The winger tries to finish from in close, but Naughton gets an all-important block in.
(7’) STAT ATTACK: The two matches between these sides last season proved to be quite the entertaining fixtures – both ending in 3-2 victories for Tottenham. A Christian Eriksen brace and a 92nd minute Gylfi Sigurdsson winner helped erase a 2-0 deficit, earning Tottenham three points when Southampton visited White Hart Lane.
(5’) There has been a real lively start to the match, with the sides exchanging time in attack. The intent is clear for both sides early on. Tottenham need three points, while Southampton's strong start to the season has them flowing with confidence, while awarding them the opportunity to take a few risks.
(3’) CLOSE! An early scare for Southampton off a Tottenham corner won by Danny Rose after a splendid run. Vertonghen meets the cross with his head, looping it towards the far post, but Bertrand is there to cover his keeper and clear off the line.
(1’) Southampton kickoff and we are underway at White Hart Lane! The visitors, moving right to left, are in their red and white striped shirts, with Tottenham sporting their white tops and navy shorts.
The players are out on a wonderful, sunny day in North London, as we get set for the start of the match.
As expected, Ronald Koeman has named an unchanged team, as his side beat QPR last weekend earning a fourth consecutive Premier League victory. Florian Gardos has recovered from injury and is amongst the substitutes today.
SOUTHAMPTON SUBS: K. Davis, Gardos, Long, Cork, Mayuka, Reed, Targett.
SOUTHAMPTON (4-3-3): Forster; Clyne, Fonte, Alderweireld, Bertrand; Davis, Wanyama, Schneiderlin; Tadic, Mane, Pelle.
Hugo Lloris is the only Tottenham player who started midweek, with Pochettino opting to rest a slew of starters. All of today's starters had the night off on Thursday, with the exception of Emmanuel Adebayor who came on as a late substitute. TOTTENHAM SUBS: Soldado, Vorm, Dier, Townsend, Kane, Dembele, Fazio.

Southampton have enjoyed a stellar start to the season under Ronald Koeman, having not lost a match since opening day. The Dutchman, graced by the fine play of two former Eredivisie stars in Dusan Tadic and Graziano Pelle, has guided the Saints to their best Premier League start since 1983-84, a season in which they finished second. Many had Southampton pegged for relegation at the start of the campaign, but after picking up 13 points from their first six matches, the sky is the limit for this entertaining outfit.
Life under Mauricio Pochettino has not gone according to plan quite yet for Tottenham. Goals have been incredibly hard to come by through the first two months of the season, however, a hard-fought 1-1 draw at the Emirates last weekend should give the Argentine something to build off of. Spurs are still in desperate need of a convincing win, having failed to pick up maximum points from a league match since the second week of the season. It will be interesting to see how the players respond for their manager, who for a variety of reasons, is in dire need of a victory in front of his new supporters here today.
"I love Southampton. I love a lot of people. That year and a half in my life was an amazing period and I left, but this is another thing. I have amazing memories from Southampton. I am happy they are having a great season, but it is a game that we need to win the three points. We need to fight with Southampton on Sunday, but it is emotional. Football is emotional and Sunday is emotional for us too.” These were the words Tottenham boss Mauricio Pochettino echoed to reporters ahead of Spurs' massive match against his former team. He did a lot of good for the club, and should no doubt receive a warm welcome from the travelling fans, who have no reason to be bitter with the success their side has experienced under new boss Ronald Koeman.
Hello Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to London, where Mauricio Pochettino's new team, Tottenham, take on his former side, Southampton, at White Hart Lane. I am Alex Moretto and I will be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens!

So, six wins out of seven for Chelsea while Arsenal have now only registered one victory in their last six in the Premier League. Contrasting fortunes for the London sides, but they produced a very entertaining game of football. That's all from our live coverage - thanks for joining us, and goodbye for now!
Arsenal will have a lot to think about after not really troubling the Chelsea defence all afternoon. Wilshere was one positive as he was the fulcrum of most of the Gunners' moves forward, but they just couldn't produce in and around the opposing box.
The difference, in the end, was the quality in the final third. Hazard was a menace throughout while Fabregas showed his quality with yet more excellent passing. Costa was quiet, but when he got his chance he took it.
That's FULL TIME at Stamford Bridge and Chelsea have beaten Arsenal 2-0 as Diego Costa netted his ninth Premier League goal of the season, after Eden Hazard opened the scoring from the spot. That's seven unbeaten for the hosts, who now lead at the top by five points.
(90’) We're just seeing out the final few moments here, now. The result is beyond doubt, surely. Arsenal are inside the Chelsea half but anything would be a consolation.
(90’) COSTA MISSES AN OPEN GOAL!! It's another cutting move from the Blues as Ivanovic races on to a loose ball before squaring to Costa, who only needs to tap in from two yards, but spoons it over! Luckily for him, the flag is up, slightly sparing his blushes.
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card D. Welbeck is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) Oof, that's a strong challenge from Welbeck! The striker goes in on Fabregas with two feet right on the touchline and ends up with a booking. Silly, really.
(90’) PODOSLKI DENIED!! The substitute gets in behind as he latches on to Ozil's chip, which Mikel swings at and misses before Cech comes out to smother the German's effort at goal.
(89’) Oxlade-Chamberlain looks to move into the Chelsea box but soon finds the door closed before he drills in a cross which Terry clears comfortably. Arsenal have just not been threatening enough today.
(88’) Costa receives the ball out by the touchline but is swiftly surrounded by red-and-white shirts, eventually conceding a throw. Time is rapidly running out for the Gunners, though.
--- 87’ Substitution Willian comes on for Oscar. ---
(87’) Oscar is the latest player to leave the pitch as he is given a standing ovation from the Chelsea fans. The Brazilian has been tireless this afternoon, and is replaced by compatriot Willian for the final few minutes.
--- 86’ Yellow card Oscar is cautioned by the referee. ---
(86’) Oscar goes into the book - probably far later than he should have - as he fouls Rosicky inside the Arsenal half. At the other end, Cech does really well to come off his line to cut out Podolski's low cross at the near post.
(85’) Chambers cuts in from the left but meets Mikel, who slides to win it before Fabregas flicks it nonchalantly out to the wing for Hazard.
(84’) Danger for Chelsea as Arsenal win a corner and it's fired into the box, but Mertesacker can't quite get there as Terry eventually hacks the ball clear before Ozil sums up his day by running it out of play.
--- 83’ Substitution T. Rosický enters the game and replaces J. Wilshere. ---
(83’) Arsenal have the ball inside the Chelsea half as Tomas Rosicky looks for fellow substitute Lukas Podolski, but his pass is poor and easily cut out. That's been the story of the Gunners' afternoon.
(82’) Hazard forces a throw off Oxlade-Chamberlain on the near side as the Chelsea fans sing the praises of their manager. He looks to have beaten Wenger yet again.
(80’) That's nine goals in his first seven Premier League outings for Diego Costa. A superb introduction to life in England. Chelsea are in control now, keeping possession well while the noise levels have shot up too.
--- 79’ Substitution A. Sánchez is replaced with L. Podolski. ---
(79’) Is that game over for Arsenal? The deadly combination of Fabregas and Costa strikes again and could have fired Chelsea to a five-point lead at the top of the Premier League.
--- 78’ Assist Fàbregas gave the assist. ---
--- 78’ Goal! COSTA DOUBLES THE LEAD!! He's been quiet today, but that's what he can do! Chelsea pick the ball up in midfield and it's that man Fabregas again. The midfielder lifts it forward to meet the run of Costa, and the striker volleys over Szczesny who can only watch as it bounces into the empty net. ---
(77’) Hazard is again involved as he picks the ball up on the left, but Chambers presses him well to force Chelsea backwards before Costa is penalised for a foul on Flamini.
(76’) HAZARD FIRES OVER!! It's a wonderful move, made by Costa. The striker is on his own in the Arsenal half but moves into the box before delaying his pass to meet the run of Hazard, who skips past a challenge before firing just over the bar from a tight angle.
(75’) Wilshere and then Ozil work it out wide to Sanchez, who looks to cut inside before he is quickly closed down by Matic and again the door closes for Arsenal.
(73’) Wilshere nearly finds Gibbs with a slotted pass but Ivanovic cuts it out. The ball eventually comes to Chambers, who steadies it with a touch before trying his luck from 25 yards, firing it well over Cech's crossbar.
(72’) Arsenal are moving the ball around and keeping it well, but they aren't really going anywhere. Mikel closes Ozil down after a poor touch from the German, but he challenges the Arsenal man illegally and the Gunners have a free kick on halfway.
(71’) Hazard is on the deck again as he is fouled once more, this time by Gibbs out on the far side near the halfway line. Things have gone a little quiet on the pitch and in the stands, here - someone needs to liven the game up again.
(70’) Hazard collects a throw from Ivanovic and looks to flick the ball through the defence for Oscar, but Szczesny is out quickly to smother it and avert any danger.
--- 69’ Substitution A. Schürrle is replaced with J. Obi Mikel. ---
--- 69’ Substitution A. Oxlade-Chamberlain enters the game and replaces Cazorla. ---
(69’) Wenger decides it's time to make a change, and it's Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain who replaces Cazorla. Chelsea, meanwhile, throw on John Obi Mikel in place of Schurrle as they look to see out the victory.
(68’) Hazard wants a free kick as he cuts in from the left-hand side and goes down under Flamini's challenge, but nothing is given and Arsenal move into the Blues' half.
(67’) Chelsea are being pressed hard by the visitors, and Ivanovic gives it away as Schurrle can't reach his pass down the right-hand side. Arsenal are doing well with Chelsea in possession but not as well when they have the ball themselves.
--- 66’ Yellow card A. Schürrle is yellow-carded. ---
(66’) The stoppage gives the referee time to book Schurrle, who had fouled Sanchez when he cut out that earlier pass from Fabregas.
(65’) Wonderful defending from Oscar, who races across to block Flamini's shot from outside the box and divert it away from danger. The Arsenal man landed on the Brazilian's hand as a result and Chelsea's midfielder is off for treatment.
(64’) Chelsea clear the corner and break into the Arsenal half through Fabregas, but the Spaniard's square ball for Schurrle is uncharacteristally poor and Sanchez is there to cut it out.
(63’) Gibbs sprints past his man and fires it into the box. Welbeck collects it with his back to goal and lays it off for Wilshere, whose shot deflects behind off Fabregas. The visitors scream for handball but it's only a corner.
(62’) With under half an hour remaining, Chelsea look reasonably comfortable as Arsenal have failed to keep their passing accurate in the final third. They are definitely still a threat, though, so the Blues will have to stay tight.
(61’) More wonderful skill from Hazard as he skips past Cazorla, before his pass to Schurrle is followed on by a ball through for Ivanovic to chase. The Serbian just about gets to it but can only fire a cross out the other side before Schurrle gives it away and Hazard concedes a free kick as he tries to win it back.
(60’) Real chance for Chelsea as Matic latches on to a loose ball and evades the challenge of Koscielny before sliding it through to Schurrle. The German spots the checked run of Costa but can't find the striker and Mertesacker cuts it out.
(58’) ALMOST AN OWN GOAL!! Hazard is the one to benefit from the Chelsea counter and he races down the left before firing it into the box. It hits Flamini and looks bound for the net but somehow it hits Szczesny's arm and goes behind. The goalkeeper didn't know much about that!
(57’) Oscar cuts out Cazorla's pass and Chelsea have a chance to break. That's happened far too often for Arsenal this afternoon.
(56’) Chelsea have it back and Fabregas lifts it up for Costa, who nods down for Hazard. He loses out to Ozil but the German is quickly caught out. Thankfully for him, he is backed up by several team-mates and Arsenal are able to get rid of any danger.
(55’) Chelsea have done well to slow things down, here, as they try to control the tempo and stifle Arsenal's pace. They surrender possession as it's aimlessly hacked forward, though.
(54’) SZCZESNY ESCAPES!! Ivanovic blasts the ball forward and Costa chases it down with the Arsenal goalkeeper sprinting out, and the shot-stopper's clearance hits the striker. Luckily for him it goes into the path of a team-mate and not Costa, but that was very risky.
--- 53’ Yellow card B. Ivanović gets yellow. ---
(53’) As Arsenal clear through Sanchez, Ivanovic tugs the Chilean back and promptly earns himself a booking. Some of these yellows have been quite unnecessary this afternoon.
(52’) Hazard and Azpilicueta exchange passes on the left before the Belgian works some space and whips it into the box. Costa goes up for it but Mertesacker is there to head away - the German has looked good this afternoon.
(51’) Gibbs fouls Oscar out wide and Fabregas whips it into the box. The ball zips out the other side and Matic retrieves before his own cross does the same. Fabregas works it back to Cahill, who tries a long-range effort which he doesn't properly connect with and Arsenal clear.
(50’) CAZORLA FIRES WIDE!! That's Arsenal's best effort of the match as it's played in from the left and Wilshere produces a lovely dummy, leaving it for Cazorla who drills it wide of goal from the edge of the box.
(49’) Welbeck is almost in again but is quickly closed down by Azpilicueta, who lofts it back to Cech. The goalkeeper fluffs his clearance, though, and Arsenal have possession again. Slightly dodgy opening from the substitute.
(48’) Wilshere steals possession in midfield and helps it on to Welbeck, who is forced to check back but is almost in again as he looks to meet Ozil's ball through the defence. He can't quite reach it, though, and Chelsea have another goal kick.
(47’) Cech is almost caught out by Welbeck as he receives a pass from Azpilicueta. The Chelsea goalkeeper takes his time over a clearance and it's blocked by the Arsenal striker, going behind for a goal kick.
(46’) It's KICK-OFF at Stamford Bridge once more as Arsenal get things moving again for the second half, with no changes made at the break.
Can Arsenal work their way back into this one? Or are Chelsea going to stretch away and extend their lead at the top? Be sure to stick with us when we resume commentary for the second half.
With a few yellows already we may see some early changes after the break. Ozil looks very out of sorts for Arsenal and they need to stop losing the ball in dangerous positions. For the Blues, Hazard is causing havoc for Chambers, but Costa has been kept fairly quite so far.
A thoroughly entertaining 45 minutes in west London, there. Chelsea have had the better of the territory but Arsenal are matching them in the middle and could have threatened with their pace if their passing was more accurate. It's finely balanced, this one.
That's HALF TIME at Stamford Bridge and Chelsea lead 1-0 thanks to Eden Hazard's cool penalty after the Belgian won it with a lovely run. It's been a fiery affair on and off the pitch, with strong challenges in midfield and strong words exchanged by the managers.
(45’) That's stupid from Oscar, who makes no attempt to play the ball as he slides in on Wilshere's legs, but somehow he escapes a booking. That's very lenient from Martin Atkinson.
(45’) Ozil loses out and Chelsea sprint forward with Fabregas, who looks for Hazard to his left but it's well cut out. There are a lot of counters this afternoon and I wouldn't be surprised to see someone score that way today.

The two teams are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off. As expected, the atmosphere at Anfield is absolutely electric, with flags and scarves flying in the air and both sets of fans in fine voice.
As for Everton, boss Roberto Martinez has decided to make four changes to the side that lost against Crystal Palace last weekend, with the most notable inclusion being Tony Hibbert, who makes his first Premier League start since December 2012 in place of Seamus Coleman, who misses out due to injury. The most notable problem for the two sides is at the back, where both have struggled in the opening five games of the season. Liverpool's current defensive sloppiness - which has resulted in them conceding seven goals in their last four league games, three of which ended in defeat - has echoes of their struggles last season, when they conceded almost twice as many goals as Chelsea, whilst Everton have already let in 13 goals after a poor start to the season in which they have only won once, leaving them in 14th place in the table with just five points. With these defensive problems in mind, today's game is guaranteed to be both very interesting and extremely exciting, with, fingers crossed, a plethora of attacking action at both ends of the pitch.
The Merseyside derby is always one of the most anticipated games of the Premier League season, and today's clash is no different. Whilst these historic derby games never fail to deliver in terms of intensity and excitement, today's 223rd meeting between the two sides comes at a time when both are struggling, with hosts Liverpool facing their fierce local rivals after disappointing back-to-back league defeats against Aston Villa and West Ham United, whilst Everton travel to Anfield on the back of an equally frustrating 3-2 loss at home to Crystal Palace.

Manchester City looked on course for an emphatic victory after a brilliant opening 11 minutes saw them hit the back of the net twice through Aguero and Dzeko, but terrible defending from Mangala has seen Hull make it 2-2, first through a poor own goal and then through a penalty from Hernandez after the Uruguayan was brought to the floor in front of goal by the high boot of Mangala. Mark Clattenburg is the referee today. It’s his first visit to St. Mary’s in nearly two years and the Saints have failed to win on the eight previous occasions he’s officiated them, including their 2-1 defeat at Liverpool on the opening day of this season. His last appointment was Leicester City’s classic victory against Manchester United last week, and he’ll be hoping for an equally entertaining afternoon today.

The clubs are walking out of the tunnels and we're five minutes away from the kick-off here!
Swansea's defeats in the last two matchdays were not enough to scar the fact that they're currently enjoying the best start to the season in club history - needless to say, confidence is high with the visitors and they may well see the home side today as the perfect opportunity to bounce back to winning ways.
One of the men to watch today is surely Gylfi Sigurdsson, who's having a superb adjustment to life at Swansea since transferring back to the club where he spent 2011-2012 after a spell with Tottenham. His four assists in the league are bettered by only Cesc Fabregas!
Swansea (4-4-1-1): Fabianski; Angel Rangel, Fernandez, Williams, Taylor; Dyer, Sung-Yong Ki, Shelvey, Routledge; Sigurdsson; Gomis.

Mauricio Pochettino's side were well organised at the back and survived a late siege on Hugo Lloris' goal and, on the balance of play, a point is probably a fair result.

(77’) That goal has given Arsenal a renewed sense of confidence and they are roared on by their fans. Ozil and Gibbs take turns to deliver teasing crosses into the box but on both occasions Kaboul is in the right place to head clear.
(75’) STAT: Oxlade-Chamberlain has won every Arsenal game in which he has scored. Can he keep that run going?

This isn't a happy hunting ground for the visitors. Their last victory at the Hawthorns was way back in 1969, and since then the Clarets have lost seven of their last eight league visits to the Baggies.
The Baggies are yet to win at home this season and Morrison’s goal last week was their first in four league games. Burnley, meanwhile, have drawn their last three games 0-0 and have only netted once so far this season. On paper this one doesn’t promise too many goals…
West Brom and Burnley are both founder members of the original Football League, having first met in 1888, but this is actually the first time the two have clashed in the Premier League.
Sean Dyche makes three changes from the draw with Sunderland as Steven Reid starts against his former club, while Michael Kightly and Ross Wallace also come into the Clarets’ starting line-up this afternoon.
