Hello and welcome to LIVE coverage of the Premier League clash between West Brom and Burnley at the Hawthorns. The hosts got their first win of the season last weekend, but can they make it two in a row?

Stoke just about deserved their win given the chances they created, with Moses very impressive. It was his cross that found Crouch for the winner, and the Potters are up and running at the Britannia Stadium. For now, though, I've been Tom Maston and thanks for joining me.
One last spell of pressure from Newcastle comes to nothing, and it is a first home win of the season from Stoke City. Newcastle remain winless and second from bottom, with Pardew's job certainly hanging in the balance. Will Ashley keep his word? We will probably find out in the next couple of days.
(90’) A poor cross from Dummett flies straight out for a goal kick as another opportunity goes begging. Time running out for the Magpies in Staffordshire.
(90’) Chants of 'Sacked in the morning' are coming from both sets of fans as the match enters the final seconds of normal time. Pardew's job hangs in the balance with four minutes added on.
(88’) Newcastle lose possession and yet again Arnautovic can run towards goal and get a shot in. Coloccini does well to stand his ground and block.
(86’) Stoke break yet again as Ireland feeds Arnautovic on the right, but Tiote does brilliantly to get back and win the ball back. The Ivorian has been excellent this evening.
(84’) OFF THE BAR! All of a sudden Newcastle come to life through Obertan on the right. The winger's cross is a good one into the six-yard box where Colback is waiting, but the midfielder can only turn his effort onto the crossbar. Let-off for Stoke.
--- 82’ Substitution V. Moses is replaced with O. Assaidi. ---
(82’) Moses' race is run following a fine performance, and he is replaced by Liverpool loanee Assaidi for the closing stages.
(80’) Newcastle look to work a free-kick routine on the edge of the box as Tiote tees up Sissoko. The France international's low effort is a powerful one but Whelan does well to charge it down and neutralise the danger.
(78’) Stoke break at lightning speed following a Newcastle corner, with Moses yet again the architect. He finds Arnautovic who runs in on goal before poking wide, though the offside flag had already gone up.
(76’) Sissoko looks to work some room on the right-hand side before crossing towards the back post where Ameobi is waiting. The winger's header is a weak one though and is picked up by Begovic.
--- 74’ Substitution Sammy Ameobi comes on for R. Cabella. ---
(74’) Pardew makes his third and final change of the night as Cabella is replaced by Ameobi for the closing stages.
(73’) This has been a very poor second-half showing from Newcastle. They have never looked like threatening Begovic and are struggling to control the game as they did in the first 45 minutes.
(71’) PENALTY? NO! Appeals from Stoke fans as Crouch is tripped on the edge of the box by Williamson. Pawson waves play on, but Krul is quickly out of his goal to confront the striker. Fortunately for the goalkeeper none of the officials seemed to see that.
(69’) Newcastle have had 53 percent possession in the second half but have done very little with it. Pardew has 20 minutes to turn this match around and possibly save his job.
--- 68’ Substitution G. Obertan comes on for Y. Gouffran. ---
(67’) Finally the visitors create something in the final third but Dummett's long-range effort flies well wide. Meanwhile Pardew makes his second change of the night as Obertain replaces Gouffran.
(66’) Arnautovic breaks through the middles of the pitch as the Newcastle defence backs off. Eventually Williamson dives in, but the ball falls for Ireland on the edge of the box. His curled shot is poor though and drifts well over the crossbar.
--- 64’ Yellow card G. Whelan is cautioned by the referee. ---
(64’) Whelan becomes the first Stoke player to go in the referee's book for a foul on Cisse in the middle of the pitch. The Magpies have not got going in this second half as yet.
(62’) GOOD SAVE! A comedy of errors in the Newcastle defence almost allows Moses to double Stoke's lead. Janmaat tries to clear his lines, only for the ball to bounce back goalwards off Williamson. Moses has plenty of space to find the net, but Krul does well to save with his feet from close range.
--- 61’ Substitution C. Adam is done for the day. S. Ireland is his replacement. ---
--- 60’ Yellow card P. Cissé receives a yellow card. ---
(60’) Cisse drops deep to try and pick up the ball but he can only be shown a yellow card as he catches Adam late. That is the Scot's last action as Ireland comes on in his place.
(58’) N'Zonzi wins a free-kick around 25 yards from goal that Adam lines up with his left foot. His curling shot is on target but Krul is always behind it and can hold on at the second attempt.
(56’) Little in terms of goalmouth action since Arnautovic hit the post early in the second period. Stoke will be happy enough given the fact that they have the narrow lead.
(54’) Despite Cisse's introduction Newcastle have struggled to get anything going in the final third. Only Janmaat's long-range effort has tested Begovic despite all their possession.
(52’) Bardsley is not pleased after he is pulled up by Pawson for a trip on Cabella. Tiote comes to get involved but the referee quickly diffuses the situation.
(50’) Despite that early chance for Stoke, they again look happy to sit and allow Newcastle to have plenty of possession in their half. Hughes knows his team can cause problems on the counter attack if they are solid in defence.
(48’) OFF THE POST! So close to a second for Stoke as Muniesa crosses from the left towards Crouch. Williamson does brilliantly to head away, but Arnautovic is there to strike a low effort against the upright. Krul was well beaten.
--- 46’ Substitution Pardew has opted to make a change at the break, with Cisse, who scored twice against Hull City last time out in the league, replacing Riviere. Stoke get us underway for the second period... ---
The two teams are making their way back out onto the pitch as both teams chase an important victory. Arguably Pardew needs a win more than Hughes, with possibly 45 minutes to save his job.
The hosts have struggled to control the game, but Moses has been superb on the counter-attack. Newcastle need to contain the winger if they are to get back into this one. I'll be back in ten minutes to see if Pardew can inspire a comeback.
The half-time whistle blows, and after a frenetic first 45 minutes it is Stoke who have the lead through Crouch's header. The 'Sack Pardew' banners are out in force again, and the Magpies boss needs a turnaround here.
(45’) We are halfway into four minutes of stoppage time at the end of the first half, and it is Newcastle looking to put pressure on the Stoke goal. Pardew can certainly be happy with how his side have controlled this match thus far.
(45’) Moses has been the best player on the pitch in the first half, and he creates yet another chance for the home side. The Chelsea loanee skipped through two challenges on the left before finding Arnautovic, but the substitute's effort is well blocked by Dummett.
(44’) GOOD SAVE! Newcastle's best moment of the game as Janmaat lines up an effort from 25 yards. The Netherlands defender has to find a way through a sea of bodies, but his shot is a good one and Begovic has to get down well to his right to push the ball away.
(43’) Moses, yet again, finds space to run at the heart of the Newcastle defence. He looks to feed Crouch in the box but the ball is too heavy, and though the striker looked to work space for a cross, he ran out of room.
--- 41’ Yellow card Colback picks up the first booking of the match as he cynically takes out Moses on the far touchline. No complaints from the former Sunderland midfielder. ---
(39’) Dummett has certainly been keen to get forward, and he looks to test Begovic after cutting inside on the edge of the area. His effort flies over the bar, though it was deflected off Shawcross.
(37’) This game is very open now, and Newcastle are able to launch a counter-attack through Sissoko. He finds Cabella, who in turn looks to return the ball to the France international at the back post, but Muniesa does well to head away.
(35’) Stoke's counter-attacks are causing Newcastle all sorts of problems. This time Muniesa crosses in from the left, and only a Coloccini header stops Crouch from doubling the lead inside the six-yard box.
(33’) Riviere just has not got into the game in his role as a lone striker while Gouffran and Sissoko are also struggling behind the former Monaco man. Stoke's defence are fairly comfortable despite the pressure.
(31’) The rain is absolutely pouring down now, but Pardew is happy to stand out with no hood and get absolutely soaked. The weather no doubt matches his mood as he looks to possibly save his job.
(29’) Tiote looks to find Dummett making a run down the left-hand side bu the diagonal ball is too heavy for the full-back. Despite some good play in midfield the Magpies have struggled in the final third.
(27’) After a period of Newcastle pressure they lose the ball in the Stoke half and all of a sudden Moses is away down the middle. As he reaches the edge of the area he feeds Crouch, but the England forward's effort is sliced horribly wide.
(25’) Despite holding the lead, Stoke have not really managed to get their passing game going. Moses' pace is causing problems but the likes of Adam and Whelan have struggled to control the game in midfield.
--- 23’ Substitution Arnautovic is the man who has been called up from the bench to replace Diouf. The striker has headed straight down the tunnel to receive more treatment. ---
(22’) Play has now been halted as Diouf seemed to injure his hamstring during that Stoke break. The former Manchester United striker does not look as if he will be able to continue.
(21’) The free-kick is headed away by Crouch and Stoke can launch a counter-attack. Diouf carries the ball forward before finding Moses, but he is unable to keep hold of the ball under Gouffran's challenge. Referee Pawson waves away the appeals for a penalty, and suddenly at the other end Sissoko drives wide after cutting inside from the left.
(19’) Newcastle are working the ball well down the flanks, and they win another free-kick in a dangerous area as Wilson trips Dummett on the left-hand side of the area. Cabella will look to find a team-mate this time.
(17’) As the thunder and lightning begins in Staffordshire, Cabella picks out Coloccini on the edge of the box from a corner, but the Newcastle skipper's controlled volley flies well over the bar.
--- 15’ Assist V. Moses gave the assist. ---
--- 15’ Goal! GOAL!!! CROUCH OPENS THE SCORING! All of a sudden Stoke lead as Moses finds space on the left before whipping in an inch-perfect cross for Crouch to leap and head past Krul. The goalkeeper never moved as the Potters find the net at home for the first time this season. ---
(14’) Better from Newcastle as Cabella skips past two challenges as he cuts inside from the right before feeding Riviere, but the former Monaco man can only lash his effort over the crossbar.
(12’) Little goalmouth action in the opening stages, with neither side able to find the space to get their creative players into the game as yet. These two teams tend not to play out cagey encounters, though, so expect plenty of action to come.
(10’) Colback's cross is a poor one and Whelan can head away at the near post. The home side then look to break but Whelan's ball into Moses is too heavy and Krul can collect.
(9’) Riviere wins a free-kick in a dangerous area on the right-hand side as he is caught by Wilson as he looks to cross into the box. Colback will look to whip this in with his left-foot.
(7’) Adam looks to be fine to continue after some lengthy treatment. It looks like little more than a hefty knock on the shin.
(5’) Newcastle certainly look comfortable in possession, but there are some worries for Stoke as Adam goes down after limping away from a strong challenge with Cabella in the second minute. He will need some treatment.
(3’) Stoke have started brightly, and N'Zonzi has the first shot on goal of the evening as he picked the ball up around the halfway line before breaking goalwards. Eventually he opts to shoot from 30 yards, but his effort is a poor one and dribbles wide of the post.
(1’) Newcastle kick-off and we are underway in the final Premier League match of the weekend...
Unsurprisingly, much of the attention is on Pardew, with almost every camera snapping away at the Newcastle boss. Meanwhile, we are ready to get going on the pitch.
The teams make their way out onto the pitch, and after all the usual pre-match niceties and handshakes we will be ready to get underway...
The two teams are in the tunnel as we approach kick-off, with the atmosphere certainly building inside the stadium. After two home defeats, the Potters' supporters will certainly be up for this one.
There are a number of 'Pardew Out' banners on show within the away end, with the Newcastle fans keen to make their feelings known. After Ashley's comments earlier this weekend, they may well get their wish after this evening's encounter.
There are now under ten minutes until kick-off in Staffordshire, and there could be a brisk pace to this game given the fact that there has been heavy rain prior to the match getting underway. Despite the weather, there should be a great atmosphere inside one of the Premier League's loudest stadiums.
Newcastle's recent record at Stoke is not great, with the Magpies having won just once in five Premier League visits to the Britannia Stadium. Pardew will be keen to improve that record, especially since anything short of a win could signal the end of his time in the North East.
Newcastle, meanwhile, are unchanged from their 2-2 draw against Hull City, meaning the hero of that match Papiss Cisse must make do with a place on the bench. Emmanuel Riviere is retained up front after netting twice against Crystal Palace in the League Cup while young striker Adam Armstrong is named among the substitutes.
Hughes makes just one change from the Stoke side that drew with QPR as Marc Muniesa, who scored twice against Sunderland in the Capital One Cup, replaces Erik Pieters at left-back. Otherwise they are unchanged, meaning Bojan Krkic remains on the bench as he searches for his first Premier League goal.
Newcastle United subs: Elliot, S.Taylor, Anita, Obertan, Ameobi, Armstrong, Cisse.
Newcastle United: Krul; Janmaat, Coloccini, Williamson, Dummett; Tiote, Colback; Sissoko, Cabella, Gouffran; Riviere.
Stoke City subs: Sorensen, Pieters, Huth, Ireland, Arnautovic, Assaidi, Bojan.
Stoke City: Begovic; Bardsley, Shawcross, Wilson, Muniesa; Whelan, Nzonzi; Diouf, Adam, Moses; Crouch.
Before we go any further, the two line-ups have been announced ahead of kick-off in around 20 minutes time...
Stoke, meanwhile, have fared little better so far this season, with Mark Hughes' side having only registered one victory from their opening five matches, though that was away at Manchester City. They are yet to score at home as yet and were twicve pegged back to draw 2-2 at QPR last time out in the Premier League. The Potters sit 17th in the table and would drop into the relegation zone with defeat this evening.
Much of the attention this evening is on Newcastle boss Alan Pardew, with his job seemingly hanging by a thread. The club's owner Mike Ashley was quoted on Saturday that a defeat to Stoke would signal the end of Pardew's reign, and though he has since admitted he only said that as a joke, this may well be the former West Ham boss' final game as Magpies boss. His team is yet to register a league win this season and currently sit 19th in the table.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of the Premier League encounter between Stoke City and Newcastle United. Neither team has really set the world alight yet this season, but after cup victories there is hope that their league form will in turn pick up. I'm Tom Maston and I'll be guiding you through all the action from the Britannia Stadium.

Kranjcar was the star man for QPR, bailing his side out despite a disappointing offensive performance. Stoke held firm for long periods and will be disappointed to head back to the Britannia Stadium with merely a point. That's all we have time for, I've been Simon Harrison and I hope to see you again next time.
FULL TIME! All square at Loftus Road, in an entertaining 2-2 draw at the bottom end of the embryonic Premier League table. Goals from Crouch and Diouf looked to be enough for Stoke, but a late Kranjcar free-kick salvaged a share of the points for Redknapp's men.
(90’) Kranjcar shoots from 25 yards once again, but Begovic is easily able to gather up a trickling effort. It's all open once more, with both sides searching for the winning goal - a point isn't ideal for either club.
(90’) We're into the first of four minutes of stoppage time.
(90’) Well, that goal has changed the complexion of the game somewhat! Loftus Road suddenly has its atmosphere back, with the home fans urging their side towards a much-needed three points. Sidwell almost has the chance to bundle home a third, but the ball ricochets off the midfielder's shin and heads into the grateful grasp of Green.
--- 88’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOOAL! KRANJCAR EQUALISES FROM THE FREE-KICK! The Croatian midfielder dips home a fantastic effort, which gets up and over the wall beyond rasping beyond the despairing reach of the goalkeeper! He's been QPR's main threat all game! ---
--- 88’ Yellow card S. Sidwell receives a yellow card. ---
(87’) A few minutes of normal time remain, with QPR exerting all of the pressure and seeing more of the ball - but Redknapp's men look a little lost with what they're trying to do with it. Sidwell receives a booking for a poor tackle on the edge of the box, giving the hosts a brilliant chance from a dead ball situation.
--- 85’ Yellow card L. Fer is yellow-carded. ---
(85’) Begovic gets across well to deny Fer! The Dutchman nearly managed to bundle home a back post cross, but the Bosnian shot-stopper covered his upright well! That's the closest QPR have come to equalising for a while!
--- 84’ Yellow card R. Shawcross is cautioned by the referee. ---
(84’) Tempers flare, with Fer and Shawcross clashing as a result of a poor tackle on Kranjcar. The referee awards the Stoke defender a yellow card for his involvement in the latter, as he clattered through the back of the former Portsmouth midfielder horribly.
(82’) Less than ten minutes remain, with QPR looking very low on ideas. Hughes' changes have freshened up his side, who continue to look comfortable while sitting deep and in numbers. Diouf is a constant threat on the break too.
--- 81’ Yellow card M. Diouf goes into the referee's book. ---
(80’) Diouf tries to hook a cross-cum-shot towards the back post, but the former Molde man can only float his heavy attempt out of play for a goal-kick. QPR break upfield, with Phillips again delivering from the right byline, but his cross doesn't reach its intended target.
--- 79’ Substitution V. Moses is done for the day. M. Arnautović is his replacement. ---
(79’) The impressive Moses is withdrawn for Arnautovic, giving Hughes a chance to show that his squad does have some quality outside of the starting eleven.
(78’) Kranjcar jinks past N'Zonzi and onto his left foot brilliantly, but his eventual strike is deflected behind for a corner - which Stoke deal with. Phillips picks up the ball in a deep area as a result, but lasers a 25-yard shot across goal and wide.
(77’) Diouf goes down asking for a penalty, but the referee isn't interested whatsoever! it appeared that Traore robbed the Stoke forward of the ball fairly, so it's a good decision from the match official.
(75’) Austin picks up possession from deep, before looking to spin off into the right channel, but Moses tracks back to good effect. Stoke's wide men have worked incredibly hard for the cause this afternoon, with the Nigeria international in particular contributing moments of real quality.
--- 74’ Yellow card A. Traoré is yellow-carded. ---
(73’) Phillips breaks to the right byline before crossing, but the delivery is far too close to Begovic, who claims. QPR just can't find that little bit of quality to unlock a plucky Potters defence.
(72’) Time is running out for the home side, with less than 20 minutes on the clock to find a way back into the game. QPR are beginning to push forward and dominate, but only due to Stoke's willingness to sit back and draw Redknapp's side in.
--- 70’ Substitution B. Zamora enters play, replacing E. Vargas. ---
--- 70’ Substitution C. Adam is replaced with S. Sidwell. ---
(70’) Henry blazes over! The midfielder sidesteps a challenge to make some space for himself, before ballooning the ball over at the near post. Stoke ready a substitute, with Sidwell replacing Adam. Zamora is thrown into the fray in place of Vargas.
(68’) Phillips now shoots from range, but the ball heads behind for a goal-kick. QPR have upped the tempo in the last five minutes, but Vargas and Austin's involvement in and around the box remains minimal.
(66’) Good defensive work from Bardsley at the back post! The former Sunderland man manages to protect his goal well, with Vargas threatening. The loose ball is contested by Begovic and Phillips, but the Bosnia international claims.
(64’) Ferdinand and Caulker look frustrated due a lack of options ahead of them, as Stoke continue to look very comfortable. QPR just aren't threatening whatsoever, with long-range efforts from Kranjcar just about the best the hosts can muster.
(62’) Less than half an hour remains for QPR to get back into this game, but Stoke are looking far more dangerous offensively at the moment. Moses has been excellent down the left, with Isla having a fairly difficult afternoon. Diouf and Crouch nearly combine to goalscoring effect, but Green smothers the ball at the latter's feet.
(60’) Kranjcar fizzes wide of the near post! The Croatian midfielder turns smartly before firing a left-footed effort towards the bottom corner, but it thuds into the advertising hoardings! Begovic was at full stretch and perhaps had his angles covered regardless.
(59’) Shawcross isn't endearing himself to the home fans, with the Stoke defender grabbing hold of Caulker at every corner. It's a clear foul, but the referee continues to ignore the actions of the Englishman.
(57’) Austin fires over! The QPR striker shoots from 25 yards, sending a dipping effort off-target under heavy pressure from Wilson. The former Burnley man thinks that it took a deflection before heading behind, but the referee isn't interested.
(56’) N'Zonzi fires wide! Stoke enjoy success down the left yet again, before Adam sets a pass back to the edge of the box for the Frenchman. He runs onto the ball and strikes first time, but balloons it high and wide!
(55’) Pieters goes close! The left-back breaks beyond Moses, before being fed in behind by the Nigeria international. Isla fails to clear, but the Dutchman's eventual close-range effort is scuffed horribly wide. He knows that was a huge chance!
(53’) Phillips shoots from 30 yards out, but the former Blackpool winger sees his effort blocked easily. After regaining the lead, Stoke are content to sit back in numbers and continue to purely counter-attack.
--- 51’ Assist The assist came from V. Moses. ---
--- 51’ Goal! GOOOOOOAL! CROUCH MAKES IT 2-1! The physical striker comes back to haunt his former coach, with good work down the left from Moses proving key again. The Nigeria international cuts back a pass to Crouch, which Ferdinand should perhaps cut out, but the English striker makes no mistake! He sweeps home a powerful finish. ---
--- 50’ Substitution K. Henry enters play, replacing J. Mutch. ---
(50’) Mutch takes a knock and is replaced by Karl Henry, with the former Wolves midfielder offering some additional tenacity - which QPR have lost out on in the absence of Barton. It isn't an offensive change, however, that's for sure.
(48’) No clear chances in the opening stages of the second half, with neither side willing to concede the first goal since the interval. The third goal in this contest could prove decisive.
(46’) We are back underway in the second half! Both teams are targetting three points here today, as they attempt to pull themselves clear of the relegation zone - despite it being so early in the season.
Kranjcar went close with a long-range strike, but otherwise the Potters have frustrated their adversaries effectively. Diouf and Crouch have spurned good opportunities on the break for Stoke, which could prove costly come 90 minutes. Stick with us for all of the second half action in ten minutes time!
HALF TIME! The two sides go in level at the break, with goals from Diouf and Caulker at Loftus Road. Stoke looked able to hold out until the interval, but a late header from the QPR defender robbed Mark Hughes' men the chance to regroup. The hosts have seen more of the ball, but haven't impressed.
--- 45’ +2 Yellow card E. Pieters receives a yellow card. ---
(45’) There's only one minute of stoppage time at the end of the first half.
(44’) QPR are right back in this game, with Crouch's recent miss looking all the more glaring now! Not a good time for Stoke to concede, as the Potters looked set to weather the storm to make their way back to their dressing room ahead.
--- 42’ Assist The assist came from J. Mutch. ---
--- 42’ Goal! GOOOOOOOAL! CAULKER HEADS HOME FROM A CORNER! The former Spurs defender manages to prise himself free of Shawcross, before heading the ball back into the mix. Adam and Crouch attempt to hack clear, but the latter puts his sliced clearance into the back of the net! That should be an own goal! ---
(41’) Diouf almost manages to break in behind the QPR back four, but Ferdinand comes across well to rob the Stoke striker of the ball following a slip from the former Hannover man.
(39’) Crouch is picked out at the back post by a corner delivery, but is only able to loop a header into the six-yard box. Green claims almost under his own crossbar.
(38’) Slightly under ten minutes remains for QPR to get back into the game, as Stoke continue to defend efficiently and limit the home side to long-range efforts. However, missed chances from Diouf and Crouch could prove costly later in the game.
(36’) The atmosphere has gone rather flat at Loftus Road, with the hosts' performance not quite living up to expectation. Isla has offered some pace and crosses down the right, but the introduction of Phillips might limit the Chilean's desire to get forward.
--- 34’ Substitution M. Phillips enters play, replacing J. Barton. ---
(34’) Matt Phillips is brought on in place of Barton, with the former Blackpool winger presumably key for offering the width which QPR have been solely lacking thus far. The Scot has ten minutes to settle into the speed of the game before the interval.
(33’) Barton makes his way down the tunnel, as it appears he's pulled something. Kranjcar blasts an effort at goal from 30 yards, but the Croatian's strike dips narrowly over the top right-hand corner! That was mightily close.
(31’) Crouch fires narrowly wide! Ferdinand is beaten for pace again by the former Portsmouth striker, who cuts onto his right foot. The Stoke forward lets fly, with Green beaten, but the ball zips wide of the upright. Barton goes off briefly to stretch his hamstring.
(30’) Half an hour has passed without Begovic having to do more than make a couple of routine saves. QPR have seen a little bit more of the ball and have exerted pressure throughout, but a lack of invention is playing into Stoke's hands. It's incredibly narrow at the moment, testament to Redknapp's team selection.
(28’) Half chance for Adam, but Fer tracks back well! Diouf is released down the left by a quick throw-in, before cutting a pass back to the edge of the box. The Scotland international looks to take the ball in his stride, but Fer gets a toe in to deny the Stoke midfielder.
(27’) Austin sees an acrobatic effort deflect wide! Fer sets up his teammate with a smart header, which the former Burnley forward tries to fire home with an overhead kick. QPR are being routinely denied by a resilient Potters' defence thus far.
(25’) The tempo is still high, but QPR are looking very hurried on the ball rather than purposeful. Barton delivers a free-kick delivery, but Bardsley rises well deep in his own penalty area to clear. It may be entertaining for the neutral, but certainly frustrating for home fans.
(23’) Stoke are standing firm despite QPR enjoying a fair amount of possession. Redknapp's men are trying to force play through their two central forwards, when the likes of Isla and Traore have acres of space on the flanks.
(21’) Diouf wastes a counter-attacking opportunity! The Stoke goalscorer cuts inside a challenge before shaping to shoot at the edge of the penalty area, but is robbed of possession! The rebounding ball bobbles out to N'Zonzi, but the Frenchman sees his first-time effort blocked!
(20’) QPR are approaching the penalty area rather well, but aren't able to convert their early build-up play into clear cut chances. Mutch tries to loft a through ball beyond Shawcross, but the English defender heads behind for a corner to prevent a two versus one situation at right-back.
(18’) Vargas receives the ball with his back to goal, before trying to hook a pass beyond the last defender for Barton to chase. Pieters manages to get the right side of the ball, shepherding it back to Begovic. Moments later, Austin drags a shot wide of the target from 20 yards out.
(17’) Diouf recovers well to dispossess Traore on the Stoke right flank, putting the ball behind for a QPR corner. Kranjcar delivers, but Adam rises brilliantly to head the danger clear.
(15’) Traore blasts over! The former Arsenal left-back is presented with a half-chance on the edge of the box, but is always leaning back! QPR won't be discouraged with some of their build-up play, but they're still looking rather merciful in front of goal.
(14’) Barton and Adam make a couple of scrappy challenges in the centre of midfield, as tempers rise somewhat. The former still isn't happy with the Stoke goal - he believes that Crouch fouled Ferdinand in the build-up. There could definitely be some cards today!
(12’) Moses tests Green! The Chelsea loanee races down the left before cutting inside, eventually letting fly at the near post! The former England international goalkeeper is able to get his body behind the powerful strike to defuse the situation.
--- 11’ Assist P. Crouch gave the assist. ---
--- 11’ Goal! GOOOOOOOOAL! DIOUF BUNDLES HOME THE OPENER! Moses whips in a cross from the byline, which Crouch nods back across goal after climbing over Ferdinand! The former Man United striker is able to knock a close-range finish beyond Green to give Stoke the lead! ---
(10’) Isla delivers a cross into the near post for Vargas to chase, but Begovic is able to race off his line and claim. The Bosnian goalkeeper takes a knock in the process, but is quickly back to his feet - despite possibly being a tad winded.
(8’) High on effort but low on quality is probably the best way to summarise the opening minutes. Both sides are hell-bent on starting well, but this contest needs settling down for high quality opportunities to be created. In trying to force the issue, there's been plenty of turnovers of possession. Crouch drives down the right before angling a cross towards the back post, but the Englishman's delivery heads behind for a goal-kick.
(6’) It's a fairly hurried start to proceedings, with both respective sides giving the ball away needlessly in midfield. Barton takes aim from 30 yards, but his long-range shot sails harmlessly wide of the far post, with Begovic a content spectator.
(4’) Adam tries to put a well-weighted ball in behind Ferdinand, who gave away possession cheaply, but Traore comes across smartly to ease the chasing Diouf off the ball. The former Hannover striker wants a free-kick, but the referee isn't interested.
(2’) Vargas records the first shot of the game, as Barton slides the Chilean through on goal. He tries his luck from a tight angle, but Begovic is easily able to smother at the near post.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at Loftus Road! QPR are in their blue and white stripes, while Stoke boast a similar design but in red and white.
Both teams have taken to the field for the Premier League's early match, meaning that kick-off is imminent! Stay with us for all of the action.

The home side have plenty of new additions involved, with Stoke opting to keep the main spine of last season's impressive eleven intact.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Queens Park Rangers versus Stoke City, as Mark Hughes returns to Loftus Road with a view to stealing three points from his former employers. Harry Redknapp's men have only managed one win from their last five games, with the Potters taking four more points than their adversaries in the same period of fixtures. For the hosts, whose target is Premier League survival, victory would be most welcome.

Up next for the Gunners, they return to the Emirates to take on their North London rivals, while Villa travel to Stamford Bridge to take on Chelsea. I am Alex Moretto and I would like to thank you all for joining me today. Good bye!
FULL TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-3 ARSENAL. Three minutes in the first half were enough to decide the match well before the break, as Mesut Ozil, Danny Welbeck and an Aly Cissokho own goal distanced the Gunners enough for them to coast through the second half.
(90’) It's all over at Villa Park! The Gunners pick up their second win of the season and continue their unbeaten start.
(90’) Arsenal milking away this stoppage time with some more quick passing moves. The ball is worked out to Gibbs on the left, in a surprising change of tempo, but the defender can only send his cross into the arms of Guzan.
(90’) The minutes mercilessly added on by the assistant referee...
(88’) Drifting into the final moments of the match now as Aston Villa muster up their first real possession since the break. Arsenal have kept 80 percent of the ball throughout the second half, a staggering number when you consider which side needed the goals.
--- 86’ Substitution C. Sánchez is done for the day. L. Bacuna is his replacement. ---
(86’) It is a night where the 'what ifs?' will reign supreme for Paul Lambert. Clark nearly gave the visitors the lead in the first half, if not for a fine save from Szczesny. The match would have played out incredibly different no doubt had the hosts taken an early lead.
--- 84’ Yellow card J. Wilshere goes into the referee's book. ---
(84’) Perhaps in retaliation, Jack Wilshere picks up a yellow card of his own for a similar tackle. The midfielder coming to the defence of his teammate, just minutes later.
--- 83’ Yellow card C. Clark receives a yellow card. ---
(82’) Nasty tackle from Clark. There looked to be some real intent to injure Podolski there, as he came sliding in to clean him up with no eyes for the ball. Mike Jones may have had half a mind to send him off there. Hardly an apologetic response from the Villa man, either.
(80’) Arsenal have hardly conceded possession in the last 10 minutes and do not look like giving it away any time soon. For the time being, the substitutes have done nothing to liven up the match, which has become incredibly tedious.
--- 78’ Substitution L. Podolski comes on for D. Welbeck. ---
--- 78’ Substitution T. Rosický enters play, replacing A. Oxlade-Chamberlain. ---
--- 78’ Substitution A. Ramsey is replaced with J. Wilshere. ---
(78’) The stoppage allows for a flurry of substitutions, with Lukas Podolski, Tomas Rosicky and Jack Wilshere entering the match in place of Welbeck, Oxlade-Chamberlain and Ramsey. Charles N'Zogbia is also introduced by the hosts.
--- 77’ Substitution K. Richardson is done for the day. C. N'Zogbia is his replacement. ---
(76’) Grealish concedes possession in his own end and concedes a free kick, much to the delight of the visiting supporters, who have been in full voice throughout this match.
(74’) Incredibly disappointing from Paul Lambert's side, who had a real opportunity to take advantage of Arsenal's mid-week journey across Europe and steal something from this match. They haven't looked like a top table team here today, laying down without so much as a whimper.
(72’) The hosts are hardly going down with much of a fight. All 11 players waiting in their own half as Arsenal pass it around amongst their defenders. No pressure on the ball carries has made life incredibly easy for the Gunners, who remain reluctant to give up possession.
(70’) Any semblance of pace has been sucked out of the match as we enter the final 20 minutes. With the result already all but finalized, both teams appear content on getting this over with.
(68’) STAT ATTACK: Only Chelsea had more than the 17 clean sheets Arsenal kept last season, however, the Gunners are one of just three teams yet to keep one this season, along with Sunderland and West Ham.
(66’) Villa are getting their chances to push forward and search for a consolation goal, but it is all going wrong for them in the final third. This may have been a long time coming for the hosts, who had scored four goals on just six attempts on target coming into the match.
(64’) Successive corners for the Gunners, who are begging to take the game to Villa now. Cazorla delivers and it is met by Koscielny, but referee Mike Jones blows the play dead for a foul in the area. Pressure relieved, for now.
(62’) Lovely one-two from Arsenal as Chambers and Oxlade-Chamberlain link up along the right. The defender sends a teasing ball into the box, but Senderos does well to beat Ramsey to the ball and push it behind for a corner.
(60’) Risky challenge by Chambers who gets a stern talking to from the referee. The right-back is already on a yellow card and that should serve as his last warning. Wenger may be wise to use his first substitution to find a replacement for the defender.
(58’) Ramsey gives away a cheap corner and it nearly results in the opener for Villa. Clark gets on the end of the cross at the far post, brings it down and looks to have a go. Oxlade-Chamberlain courageously dives in and gets a vital block to sniff out the chance.
--- 56’ Yellow card A. Ramsey is yellow-carded. ---
(56’) Agbonlahor certainly appears to be up for this match still. The forward does well to beat Mertesacker and force Ramsey into a tackle which earns him a yellow card. The ensuing free kick is delivered into the area well. Cleverley cuts it back, but Koscielny is there to deal with the threat.
(54’) STAT ATTACK: Arsenal are unbeaten in their last nine Premier League matches (W6, D3). The last time they went 10 matches unbeaten was to close out the 2012-13 season.
(52’) Villa extremely hesitant on the ball. Ozil and Ramsey commanding play in midfield. The hosts win it back on a couple of occasions, but are immediately caught out from behind, allowing Arsenal to keep the ball. The traveling supporters are in full voice, delighted by the play of their team on this sunny this afternoon in Birmingham.
(50’) The home fans growing restless with Sanchez, who is caught in possession and then concedes a foul in midfield. Arsenal flowing with confidence at the moment, passing it around nicely, forcing Villa to chase the game.
(48’) Arsenal keeping possession well early on. Villa's spirits are down quite a bit, and understandably so. Carlos Sanchez has had a difficult go in midfield. The hosts really do seem to be missing the services of Westwood who was a late scratch for this one.
--- 46’ Substitution J. Grealish enters play, replacing A. Weimann. ---
(46’) Jack Grealish is on to start the second half in an effort to get Villa back into this game. The 19-year-old enters in place of Andreas Weimann as the hosts get this final frame underway.
STAT ATTACK: Mesut Ozil scored and assisted a goal in the space of one minute and 19 seconds in the first half.
HALF TIME: ASTON VILLA 0-3 ARSENAL. After 30 minutes, it was the hosts who looked the likelier team to break the deadlock. However, three goal in four minutes after some wonderful build-up play and clinical finishing, the Gunners have stormed out to a commanding lead at the intermission. Villa's undefeated start looks to be in jeopardy, unless they can pull off something of a miracle in the final 45 minutes.
(45’) Villa deliver in the free kick but it is dealt with well by Arsenal. The hosts keep possession, but cannot find a way through and we head to the break in Birmingham with Arsenal well in front.
(45’) Two minutes to be added on as Fabian Delph is attended to after picking up a knock.
(43’) Arsenal keep possession well here. It looks like Villa are trying to just ride this wave out until half time where they can regroup. Will they even be up for the second half? It will be a real test of their character to see how they perform in these final 45 minutes.
(41’) STAT ATTACK: Only Sunderland and Fulham (11) lost more home matches than Aston Villa (10) last season. Their minus seven goal differential at Villa Park was also worst among teams above the drop.
(39’) The hosts are completely shell shocked! Their flawless start to the season has been undone in less than four minutes! It was all going quite well for Paul Lanbert's team, who did not look at all like conceding. But credit to Arsenal who were absolutely clinical in the build-up to those goals.
--- 36’ Goal! Gibbs picks up a loose ball atop the area after a deflection, and pushes forward. He blazes it across the box, and whether the intent was a shot or a pass is irrelevant at this point. Cissokho sees it running to Oxlade-Chamberlain at the far post and tries to turn it behind, but instead puts it into his own net! Three goals in less than four minutes for the Gunners! INCREDIBLE! ---
(36’) IT'S ALL FALLING APART FOR VILLA! ARSENAL TAKE A 3-0 LEAD!
--- 34’ Assist The assist came from M. Özil. ---
--- 34’ Goal! Another brilliantly worked move as Welbeck lays off for Ramsey, who picks out Ozil along the left. The German slides a sensational ball across the face of goal that the striker turns in. Two goals in 79 seconds for the Gunners! ---
(34’) DANNY WELBECK MAKES IT 2-0 JUST A MINUTE AFTER OZIL OPENED THE SCORING!
--- 32’ Assist The assist came from D. Welbeck. ---
--- 32’ Goal! Lovely passing move from the visitors. Mertesacker picks out Ramsey, then a string of one-touch passes by the Welshman, Oxlade-Chamberlain and Welbeck send Ozil through on goal. The German has the goal at his mercy, and puts the visitors in front with one of the calmest finishes you will ever see. ---
(32’) OZIL HAS HIS GOAL AND ARSENAL HAVE THEIR LEAD!
(31’) STAT ATTACK: The Gunners' 11 victories away from home were most in the Premier League last season.
(29’) Arsenal are getting their fair share of possession, but as Liverpool found last week, it is not an easy task to break down this Villa defence. The hosts are playing this like they are away from home, sitting back and staying disciplined in defence, while looking for a quick strike on the counter.
(27’) Welbeck looks to take on Senderos, with a turnover allowing Arsenal to break in numbers. The striker spots the run of Ozil, who is calling out for a pass, but the German is lined up in an offside position. Needs to be smarter there, does Ozil, who has not had the best of starts to the new season.
(25’) Arsenal seem to be mounting a bit of pressure on the Aston Villa goal, but Cazorla just takes his eyes off the ball, gets dispossessed by Weimann, and the hosts break on a counter. Koscielny gets back well, however, to deal with Agbonlahor.
(23’) BRILLIANT SAVE FROM SZCZESNY! A wonderful delivery towards the far post is met by Clark. The defender gets his head to it, but Szczesny scurries across and makes himself big, somehow managing to keep the ball out!
--- 22’ Yellow card C. Chambers is yellow-carded. ---
(22’) Dangerous tackle from Calum Chambers, who earns the first yellow of the match. Agbonlahor beats the right-back with his pace, forcing him into a rash challenge. Free kick to the hosts from 30 yards out along the left.
(20’) RAMSEY! Another corner for Arsenal, this one is cleared, but falls kindly for the Welshman atop the area. He unleashes a drive, but narrowly misses at the near post. Better, that, from the visitors.
(19’) Gibbs wins the visitors a corner after Cleverley's back-tracking was able to sniff out the run of the left-back. The ball is delivered in, and falls to Welbeck who tries a rather acrobatic volley which sees the chance go begging.
(17’) STAT ATTACK: Arsenal are unbeaten in their last 15 matches at Villa Park. Their last defeat came back in 1998, when they squandered a 2-0 half time lead thanks to second half goals from Julian Joachim and a Dion Dublin brace.
(15’) Ramsey gives it away now and Gibbs just manages to bail him out! The Welshman passes straight to Delph at the top of the Arsenal area. The midfielder crosses into the box, but a fortunate bounce for the visitors allows the left-back to clear. Wenger will not be happy with his side's performance early on.
(13’) Important intervention from Koscielny! Another giveaway by Arsenal in midfield allows Villa to break on a counter. Richardson gets up along the left and tries to thread a pass in to meet the run of Agbonlahor, but the centre-back reads it well as he rushes across to clear the danger.
(11’) Cagey start to the match with both sides failing look very convincing on the ball. A number of stray passes in midfield have created a bit of a pinball effect, with possession being wasted at an alarming rate early on.
(9’) TEAM NEWS: Ashley Westwood was a late scratch from the Villa line-up as a result of a bug rumored to be going through the team. He is replaced in the starting XI by Carlos Sanchez.
(7’) Arsenal win a corner now as Oxlade-Chamberlain gets into a threatening position along the right. Cazorla delivers, but Clark makes a strong headed clearance to sniff out the danger. They break on a counter, but Weimann's pass for Richardson runs too far and Szczesny comes out to collect.
(5’) Welbeck! He really has to hit the target from there. The deadline day addition takes a pass from 25 yards out, finds space and tries to curl a shot inside the far corner, but misses by quite a few feet.
(3’) AGONIZINGLY CLOSE! Szczesny does a horrible job with his pass from the back, giving it straight away to Villa. Delph charges forward, works a one-two with Weimann, then unleashes a wrong-footed shot from the top of the box. Atoning for his earlier miscue, Szczesny dives down to his left and knocks the ball behind. Fine save from the Arsenal keeper.
(1’) Arsenal kick-off and we are underway at Villa Park! The visitors, moving right to left, are wearing their yellow tops and blue shorts, with Aston Villa sporting their classing dark red with light blue sleeves.
UPDATE: After originally appearing on the team sheet, Alexis Sanchez has been scratched from the XI and will be replaced by Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain.
Ron Vlaar and Joe Cole have not recovered in time, thus have been left out of the squad for today by Paul Lambert. Ciaran Clark slots in for Nathan Baker at the back, who did so well at Anfield last weekend. Other than that, no changes to Paul Lambert's side who beat Liverpool 1-0 a week ago.
ASTON VILLA SUBS: Okore, Bacuna, Sanchez, N'Zogbia, Given, Lowton, Grealish.
ASTON VILLA (4-2-3-1): Guzan; Hutton, Clark, Senderos, Cissokho; Cleverley, Delph; Weimann, Westwood, Richardson; Agbonlahor.
Encouraging news for Arsene Wenger as Calum Chambers and Mikel Arteta have been deemed fit enough to start, the former slotting in for the injured Mathieu Debuchy. In midfield, Arteta will take up a deeper role in the centre, between Santi Cazorla and Aaron Ramsey, with Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain and Mesut Ozil on the wings. Danny Welbeck plays as the lone striker up top. Arsenal look to be hitting Villa with their own game, crowding midfield and looking to make them pay on the counter.
ARSENAL SUBS: Sanchez, Ospina, Coquelin, Diaby, Rosicky, Wilshere, Podolski.
ARSENAL (4-5-1): Szczesny; Chambers, Mertesacker, Koscielny, Gibbs; Oxlade-Chamberlain, Cazorla, Arteta, Ramsey, Ozil; Welbeck.
The teams have been announced, so let us have ourselves a look at the starting line-ups:
Aston Villa sits in second place in the Premier League as we enter week five, despite recording just six shots on goal, the fewest in the top flight. Their defence has been impeccable, however, carrying the side to three victories and a draw from their opening four fixtures and keeping a league high three clean sheets. A 1-0 win at Anfield on the last match day legitimized their superb start, but it begins to get a whole lot harder for the Villans who take on Chelsea away, Manchester City and Everton at Goodison Park following today's date with the Gunners.
Arsenal are in need of a bit of a boost today having picked up maximum points just once from their opening four fixtures. The Gunners have yet to lose a Premier League match, however, three draws from four has them sitting seventh entering the weekend, behind North London rivals Tottenham, who have been anything but impressive to start the season. Arsene Wenger's men were defeated by Dortmund midweek in their Champions League opener, and with injuries beginning to pile up yet again, points are at a premium today at Villa Park.
Good afternoon Premier League fans around the world, and welcome to Birmingham, where two of the three unbeaten teams remaining in the top flight get set to do battle at Villa Park. I am Alex Moretto and I will be your in-game host, guiding you through the match LIVE as it happens!

That's all from me folks! I'm Chris Baker and thanks very much for joining me this afternoon. Enjoy the rest of your weekend.
The sooner Danny Ings returns the better for Sean Dyche as serious question marks remain over whether Jutkiewicz, Sordell and Barnes can cut it at Premier League level. The Burnley manager will be happy with the commitment and organisation his team showed but they need to win games at home against teams like Sunderland if they are to survive.
Adam Johnson looked less than impressed when substituted and his withdrawal to a lot of impetus out of the Sunderland attack. Jozy Altidore continues to not be a goal threat which makes the exclusion of Steven Fletcher from the squad look even more strange. Connor Wickham could definitely do with more support upfront.
Dyche and Poyet will be reasonably satisified with a point in the end as both teams defended pretty well over the 90 minutes. What will be a concern is the lack of invention and cutting edge in attacking areas. Neither side look like scoring a lot of goals this season and that could develop into a problem in the coming months.
(90’) That's it full time 0-0 here at Turf Moor! Both sides hit the woodwork in the closing stages but ultimately a draw is a fair reflection as neither team did quite enough to claim all three points.
(90’) It is end-to-end stuff now. Wallaces manages to smuggle a cross into the box from the right but Sunderland clear. The ball comes back into towards Mannone, who rather unconvincingly punches the ball into the air but Wes Brown helps out his keeper and heads away.
--- 90’ +2 Substitution G. Boyd is replaced with S. Reid. ---
--- 90’ Yellow card D. Marney is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) SHOT! Jordi Gomez takes the free kick short to van Aanholt who unleashes a thunderous drive from all of 30 yards which flies past a helpless Heaton and cracks the post. The ball then rebound off the goalkeeper but doesn't bounce into the net. How close can you get?!
(88’) It would have been a fortunate way to take the lead but it would have been a pricless goal for Burnley. Dean Marney then goes into the referee's notebook after a pretty untidy tackle on Vergini. Can Sunderland make anything of this set piece?
--- 86’ Substitution D. Jones is done for the day. R. Wallace is his replacement. ---
(86’) OFF THE BAR! Big deflection on Arfield's shot and his effort loops up and onto the Mannone's cross bar. So close to the opening goal. Agonising for Burnley.
(84’) Vergini is played in well by Buckley but the Sunderland right back can't find a teammate with his cross. All a bit too slow and ponderous in possession for the visitors at present. Ross Wallace has come on to replace David Jones in the Burnley midfield.
(81’) Since the Sunderland substitutions it has actually been the Clarets who have improved. Sean Dyche will feel that this game is there for the taking if they can put a move together of real quality. It has all got a bit disjointed for the Black Cats over the last ten minutes or so.
(79’) O'Shea is not a popular man at Turf Moor at the moment. The experienced Irishman bundles Jutkiewicz over about 25 yards from goal. David Jones takes the resulting free-kick but his shot can't beat the Sunderland wall.
--- 78’ Yellow card J. O'Shea gets yellow. ---
(77’) John O'Shea is playing a very dangerous game at the moment. He is getting far too tight to the Burnley strikers. The veteran centre back was retrospectively booked for his tug on Jutkiewicz. For such an experienced player he is being rather rash. The last thing Gus Poyet needs is a red card during this pivotal point in the match. The result could go either way. A moment of madness or inspiration looks the most likely means of separating the sides.
(76’) Mee is fine to continue. The match is starting to get stretched. Can anyone find an elusive goal? Jutkiewicz breaks clear of O'Shea who then pulls back the Burnley striker, who still manages to get a shot on target but it is at a good height for Mannone to parry away.
(74’) Clash of heads here as Altidore clashes with Mee. The big American centre forward has certainly been putting himself about since coming on. The last five minutes or so have been a bit disjointed which may help Burnley as it has disrupted Sunderland's rhythm.
--- 73’ Substitution W. Buckley comes on for E. Giaccherini. ---
(72’) Burnley have only scored one goal so far this season and on the evidence of today it is easy to see why. It's certainly not for the lack of trying but they look short of ideas when going forward. They are struggling to get in behind Sunderland's deep defensive line.
(71’) Another change for Sunderland as Buckley comes on in place of Giaccherini who was on the receiving end of a strong challenge by Jutkiewicz a few moments ago and has been unable to run off the knock. Poyet will be looking for his side to go a bit more direct with the physical presence of Wickham and Altidore up front.
(69’) There was some good movement and link up between Arfield and Jutkiewicz to create space on the left wing a few moments ago. It's something that hasn't been seen enough this afternoon. Both sides have been too static in possession and need to give the man on the ball more options. Player's seem too reluctant to make a run or risk losing the ball with a forward pass.
--- 67’ Substitution J. Altidore enters the game and replaces A. Johnson. ---
--- 67’ Substitution S. Larsson is replaced with Jordi Gómez. ---
(67’) SAVE! Arfield is played in down the left hand channel by Jutkiewicz and the midfielders cross come shot needs to be turned away at the near post by Vito Mannone. Finally some signs of life from the home side as we head into the final quarter of the game.
(65’) The crossing from both teams has left a lot to be desired this afternoon. Changes are afoot for Sunderland as Jordi Gomez readies himself to come on. Trippier meanwhile takes on his man and sends a low ball into the area but not for the first time it doesn't beat the first man.
--- 63’ Substitution A. Barnes comes on for M. Sordell. ---
(63’) Good hold up play there from Wickham who receives the ball on the edge of the area from Larsson. The striker manages to work half a yard for a shot but can only drag his effort wide.
--- 62’ Yellow card J. Rodwell is yellow-carded. ---
(61’) Ashley Barnes is stripped off and ready to enter the fray. Will it be a straight swap or a change in shape for Burnley? Rodwell receives the first yellow card of the game as he hacks down George Boyd. Very easy decision for the referee there.
(58’) Burnley have hardly had a kick since the second half started. It's important for Sean Dyche's men to reassert themselves and not drop too deep which will invite pressure. Crucial for the home side not to concede during this period. Sunderland on the other hand are building up a head of steam.
(55’) CLOSE! The visitors almost take the lead on the break. Johnson releases Giaccherini down the left and the winger fires the ball across the six yard area before it is scrambled away by Jason Shackell. Larsson looked set for a tap in at the far post there.
(53’) SHOT! Rodwell stings the palms of Tom Heaton with a decent drive from the edge of the area. The Black Cats midfielder is wonderfully two-footed and on this occasion he works the ball from his right onto his left before shooting. Sunderland's good start to the second half continues.
(51’) Johnson pops up on the right wing and drives into the Burnley penalty area with a typically jinking run. The winger goes down as he shoots but there is no suggestion of a penalty apeal from Sunderland. That run from the winger was reminiscent of the dribble that lead to his goal last weekend against Spurs.
(48’) Giaccherini and Johnson have reverted to their natural flanks at the start of this second half with the Italian on the right and Johnson on the left. Sunderland are looking a bit more composed on the ball at the start of this half. Passing the ball with a bit more intent rathering than keeping possession just for the sake of it.
(46’) Sunderland get us restarted, they'll be attacking the end of the ground where their supporters are gathered in the second half.
There has been a slight sense of both teams not wanting to lose this match rather than going all out to win, which is perfectly understandable as a defeat today would be a massive blow. Burnley seemed to be set up well to counter attack but Sunderland haven't given them any space to exploit in behind.
There has been plenty of effort and endeavour during the first 45 minutes but quality has been lacking in attack. Sunderland have some good options on the bench in the form of Jozy Altidore, Will Buckley, Jordi Gomez and Danny Graham who are all waiting in the wings. Michael Kightly, Ross Wallace and Ashley Barnes could certainly make an impact from the Burnley bench as well.
(45’) There's the half time whistle 0-0! Dyche and Poyet will have plenty to think about during the interval and it wouldn't be a surprise to see some of the substitutes introduced in the early part of the second half.
(44’) Just one minute of time to be added on at the end of the first half here at Turf Moor. Burnley will feel that they can create further opportunities in the second half if their decision making in the final third improves. Sunderland on the otherhand need to have possession in better areas if they want to make the breakthrough.
(40’) As half time approaches both managers will be pleased and disappointed in equal measure. Both teams have decent spells in the match without either goalkeeper being seriously tested. Defences have been on top for the most part this afternoon.
(37’) Almost a horrific moment for Wes Brown who massively underhits a back pass to Mannone. Fortunately for Sunderland their goalkeeper was alive to the situation and raced off his line to smash the ball out of harm's way.
(35’) CHANCE! Rodwell sets up at counter attack by bursting forward from midfield. The former Man City midfielder plays a crisp pass into the feet of Connor Wickham who takes one touch before firing the ball straight down the throat of Heaton. A wasted opportunity there for the visitors.
(32’) Sean Dyche will be slightly concerned that Sunderland's more creative players are beginning to find more time and space in the middle of the park over the last few minutes. Rodwell and Cattermole are dominating the midfield areas and spray the ball around.
(28’) The Sunderland supporters are rather ironically cheering their teams string of passes at the moment. Vergini eventually gets his head to Larsson's low cross but the defender's effort flashes wide of the post. Gus Poyet's side are just starting to find their feet in this match.
(24’) Another shot from Jutkiewicz but the Burnley striker only finds Row Z! The centre forward is almost trying too hard at the moment to get off the mark.
(22’) CHANCE! Larsson's dangerous cross is headed back across goal by Wickham into the path of Jack Rodwell who nods towards goal but his header harmlessly loops into the arms of Heaton. Better from Sunderland.
(19’) SAVE! Great football from Burnley. Scott Arfield played the ball into George Boyd who has his back to goal just inside the Sunderland area. Boyd holds the ball up well before laying it off to Jones who fires a low shot in on goal but it was straight at Vito Mannone. Jones perhaps will feel that he should've done better there. Excellent approach work to create the chance though.
(17’) Ben Mee fouls Sebastian Larsson out on Sunderland's right wing. Johnson whips the ball in but Wes Brown is penalised for a push in the box and Burnley can start again with a free-kick that goalkeeper Tom Heaton will take.
(14’) Johnson tries to play in Connor Wickham over the top but Sunderland's lone striker fouls Michael Duff. Wickham has not been involved at all so far. Gus Poyet will want to see a bit more from his big no.10.
(12’) Adam Johnson and Emmanuele Giaccherini have switched wings as the away side try to get a foothold in this match. All credit to Burnley they have simply not allowed Sunderland to settle into any sort of rhythm in these early exchanges.
(9’) Sunderland enjoy their first spell of possession but it doesn't last long as Jones wins the ball back. The Burnley midfielder feeds Jutkiewicz but the striker's shot is deflected and doesn't trouble Mannone.
(7’) John O'Shea gives away a cheap free-kick by pulling back Jutkiewicz. David Jones will swing this into the box with his left foot. It's a decent delivery but Patrick van Aanholt heads away the danger.
(4’) There is a great atmosphere inside the stadium and Marvin Sordell really should've opened the scoring for Burnley. Lukas Jutkiewicz raced down the left-hand channel and cut the ball back to his striker partner Sordell who completely missed his kick when he should really have given his side the lead. Let off for the Black Cats.
(2’) Promising start from Burnley with George Boyd forcing an early corner for the home side. It comes to nothing as Sunderland clear their lines. Trippier regains possession and tests Mannone from 25 yards out but it is easy for the Sunderland keeper to deal with.
(1’) We are underway at Turf Moor! Both teams wearing their traditional colours.

Of course, there's immense pressure on Newcastle manager Alan Pardew, who most fans feel is simply not up to the task. Many of the fans have been openly protesting against the manager, who has described the situation as "mass hysteria." Anything less than a win today could finally spell the end of his time at the club.
Some interesting facts about the recent form and head-to-head between these two sides: Newcastle have just one win in their last six home games, none of the last six competitive meetings between these two sides has ended in a home win, and both sides have only won one of their last nine games in the league.

Last gameday was one that both sides will be hoping to put quickly behind them. Newcastle were picked apart 4-0 by Southampton and Graziano Pelle, and Hull twice led at home against West Ham before conceded each time and taking away just a point.
Hello and welcome to our pre-match coverage of Newcastle vs Hull City! It's only the fifth match-day in the Premier League and yet both of these sides will be desperate for a win. The home side have yet to secure three points this season whereas Hull's only victory was away at QPR on the opening day.

Today's game truly was a tale of two halves. Swansea easily looked the better of the two sides during the first period, with Routledge, Dyer and Sigurdsson running rings around the Southampton defence, but Bony's dismissal after two poor challenges was the turning point, and from then onwards the hosts could only hope for a point. It looked as if they were going to achieve that after great defending during the second half, but a wonderful goal by Wanyama with just 10 minutes left to play cruelly ended their hopes of coming away with anything.
