(34’) And now Di Maria is down on the floor injured. De Laet and the Argentine come together near the touchline, leaving the latter holding his wrist in a heap on the ground.
--- 33’ Yellow card R. De Laet receives a yellow card. ---
(32’) Cambiasso's pass to Hammond is cut out by Falcao and Manchester United break away on a quick counter-attack. Di Maria picks up the ball 25 yards out and tries to send a curling cross into the middle of the Leicester penalty area, but it's only able to find the head of Cambiasso.
--- 30’ Substitution Evans has been struggling for the last 10 minutes or so with what looks like a nasty injury, and he's eventually replaced by Smalling after deciding that he's unable to continue. ---
(29’) Blackett and Vardy wrestle for the ball near the byline, but the Manchester United youngster comes out on top and is able to shepherd the ball out of play for a goal-kick.
(27’) A heavy touch from Konchesky gifts Manchester United a corner. It's whipped into the box by Di Maria but Moore is able to chest the ball away at the near post.
(25’) Blackett and Ulloa clash on the edge of the Manchester United penalty area, resulting in cries for a penalty from the Leicester fans, but referee Mark Clattenburg shakes his head and waves play on.
(23’) Di Maria is brought to the ground by Hammond and Manchester United are awarded a free-kick 35 yards out. Rooney takes it short and Di Maria tries to cross towards Falcao at the far post, but the effort is poor and the ball sails out for a goal-kick.
(21’) After a frantic few moments, the pace of the game has slowed down somewhat, but both sides look hungry for more goals. The question is, who is going to strike first?
(19’) Van Persie almost re-establishes Manchester United's two-goal lead with a fantastic volley from just inside the Leicester box, but it rolls just wide of the far post before the Dutchman is eventually flagged offside.
--- 17’ Assist The assist came from J. Vardy. ---
--- 17’ Goal! GOAL! From one club record signing to another! Leicester are right back in this game thanks to a bullet header from Ulloa after a brilliant Vardy cross. That's four goals already for the Argentine striker this season. ---
--- 16’ Assist The assist came from W. Rooney. ---
--- 16’ Goal! GOAL! A world-class strike from Di Maria doubles Manchester United's lead! The visitors break away through the middle of the pitch and Rooney sets up Di Maria on the edge of the box. Spotting Schmeichel off his line, the club record signing decides to send a beautiful chipped shot over the Dane's head, leaving him rooted to the spot and giving the Red Devils a well-deserved 2-0 lead. ---
(15’) Cambiasso and Drinkwater link up well on the right wing after patient build-up play from Leicester, but Blackett is there to cut out the danger on the edge of the penalty area and fire the ball out of play for a throw-in.
--- 13’ Assist The assist came from R. Falcao. ---
--- 13’ Goal! GOAL! Manchester United take an early lead after fantastic play down the left flank. Falcao finds himself in acres of space before chipping a beautiful cross right onto the head of Van Persie, and the Dutchman is easily able to nod the ball into the back of the net. ---
(12’) Manchester United break away again, this time down the left wing through Falcao, and the Colombian finds Van Persie in the centre of the box with a low cross, but the latter's first touch is poor and the Leicester defence are able to clear the danger.
(11’) That's much better from Manchester United! Di Maria threads a beautiful through-ball into the path of Van Persie, but the Dutchman's deft shot is saved brilliantly by Schmeichel.
(9’) Manchester United haven't started the game particularly well, with Leicester certainly looking the most dangerous of the two sides, particularly in the final third of the pitch.
(7’) Great play by Leicester! The hosts regain possession in the middle of the pitch and break away on a quick counter-attack. Nugent spins around Blind on the edge of the penalty area before teeing up Ulloa, but the striker's first touch is too heavy and Rafael is able to win the ball back.
(6’) Rojo accidentally handles the ball near the halfway line and Leicester are awarded another free-kick. It's taken quickly by Cambiasso and he finds Nugent, who darts down the right flank before sending a dangerous cross towards Ulloa at the back post, but Evans is there to cut out the danger before the Argentine striker is able to get a head on the ball.
(4’) Leicester are awarded a free-kick after a poor challenge by Blackett and Cambiasso sends it in towards the edge of the six-yard box. The set-piece seems to be heading for the head of Morgan but it's slightly too heavy and the ball ends up going out for a goal-kick.
(3’) Herrera wins a header in the middle of the pitch and sets up Rafael on the right wing, but the Brazilian's cross is poor and it sails into the hands of Schmeichel.
(2’) Leicester immediately break away down the left wing from the kick off, but Ulloa is halted by Rafael before he is able to send a cross into the Manchester United box.
(1’) And we're off!
The two sides are making their way out onto the pitch ahead of kick-off. The atmosphere at the King Power Stadium is fantastic, with the home fans in particularly fine voice.
As for Manchester United, Van Gaal has made just one change to the side that started last Sunday's victory against Queens Park Rangers, with Radamel Falcao coming in to make his first start for the club in place of Juan Mata, who drops to the substitutes' bench.
Leicester boss Pearson has decided to make four changes to the side that won 1-0 against Stoke last weekend, with Kasper Schmeichel, Danny Drinkwater and Jamie Vardy all returning to the starting line-up to replace Ben Hamer, Riyad Mahrez and Jeffrey Schlupp. Meanwhile, Andy King makes way for Argentine veteran Esteban Cambiasso, who makes his first start for the Foxes since his summer move from Inter Milan.
Manchester United substitutes: Lindegaard, Shaw, Smalling, Fletcher, Valencia, Mata, Januzaj.
Manchester United XI (4-1-3-2): De Gea; Rafael, Evans, Blackett, Rojo; Blind; Herrera, Rooney, Di Maria; Falcao, Van Persie.
Leicester City substitutes: Hamer, Wasilewski, King, James, Schlupp, Mahrez, Wood.
Leicester City XI (4-1-4-1): Schmeichel; De Laet, Morgan, Moore, Konchesky; Cambiasso; Nugent, Hammond, Drinkwater, Vardy; Ulloa.
There's just over 15 minutes left to go until kick-off, so let's have a look at how the two teams will be lining up this afternoon...
It won't be easy, however, as today's hosts have marked their return to the Premier League after a 10 year absence by putting in a string of fantastic performances. Spirited displays against both Everton and Arsenal earned Nigel Pearson's side vital draws, and last weekend their hard work was rewarded with a 1-0 win against Stoke City thanks to Argentine striker Leonardo Ulloa's third goal in four league games. Manchester United's makeshift defence have looked poor this season, and the former Brighton & Hove Albion man will be hoping to increase his goal-scoring tally today in what is sure to be an extremely interesting game.
Life under Louis Van Gaal continues to throw up surprises, but his new-look Manchester United side finally seem to be finding their feet after a turbulent opening few weeks under the Dutchman. The Red Devils were given a boost of confidence last weekend when they comfortably thrashed Queens Park Rangers 4-0 at Old Trafford to pick up their first league win of the season, and Van Gaal will be hoping that his side can build on last week's victory by seeing off another newly-promoted side in Leicester this afternoon.
Good afternoon and welcome to our live text commentary of today's Premier League clash between Leicester City and Manchester United. My name is Ben Cullimore and I will be keeping you up-to-date with all of the action from the King Power Stadium.

Joleon Lescott was terrific on his West Brom debut and he epitomised the Baggies' performance with his determination and organisation in defence. Alan Irvine's side will look to make it successive league wins when they take on Burnley at home next weekend while Tottenham will aim for their first victory in four league games when they make the short journey across North London to take on Arsenal. That's all from me, Max Bentley, on this live commentary. Until next time, goodbye.
FT: Tottenham 0-1 West Brom. The boos ring out for Mauricio Pochettino's side as they suffer back-to-back home league defeats for the first time since November 2012. James Morrison's second-half header was the difference and on the balance of play, you have to say that the visitors deserved it. The Baggies have finally ended their seven-game winless streak in the Premier League, earning their first victory at White Hart Lane since 1984.
--- 90’ +4 Yellow card B. Foster receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Tottenham continue to pepper the West Brom box with crosses but Lescott and Dawson are in no mood to concede a late equaliser and they head clear for the umpteenth time. Eriksen then delivers a corner from the left but Dier's header deflects narrowly wide of the target. Time is running out for the hosts.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution V. Anichebe comes on for S. Sessègnon. ---
(90’) Tottenham launch another attack on the West Brom goal in the first minute of four added on. Lamela picks out Lennon with a clever pass on the right but the former England winger's cross is well cleared by Brunt. Lennon then has a second chance to pick out a teammate as he bursts beyond Pocognoli and his inviting cross is fired over acrobatically by Soldado.
--- 90’ Yellow card Soldado is cautioned by the referee. ---
(89’) The West Brom midfield have worked tirelessly all game and they continue to force Tottenham into mistakes high up the pitch with their intense pressing game. Victor Anichebe is preparing to come on for the visitors, presumably to hold the ball up in the closing stages and assist with defending late set-pieces.
(87’) Lennon has struggled to make the desired impact since coming off the Tottenham bench and he fails to pick out a white shirt in the box after bamboozling Pocognoli down the right. Alan Irvine is looking at his watch, can the Baggies hold on for their first victory at White Hart Lane since 1984?
(85’) Tottenham have just five minutes to find an equaliser to deny Alan Irvine his first league win as West Brom manager. A Spurs goal would be harsh on the Baggies who have defended magnificently and who have proved a threat to the opposition goal on numerous occasions.
--- 83’ Yellow card S. Sessègnon is yellow-carded. ---
(83’) As I mentioned earlier, Tottenham's deliveries from set-pieces have been poor today and Eriksen is the latest to frustrate the White Hart Lane faithful as his free kick goes wastefully into the gloves of Foster. Mauricio Pochettino is pacing up and down the touchline and he does not look happy.
(81’) Soldado has certainly given Tottenham more of a focal point up front but the service to the Spaniard has not been good enough and it has all been too easy for West Brom. Adebayor clips a cross towards the back post for his strike partner but it is too high and the ball goes out of play.
(79’) Tottenham are frantically searching for an equaliser but Eriksen's through pass, intended for Soldado, is well intercepted by Lescott. It's been a common feature of Spurs' game today and as it stands, they are staring at back-to-back home league defeats for the first time since October-November 2012, when they were beaten by Chelsea and then Wigan.
(77’) West Brom look to put the game beyond Tottenham as Sessegnon produces a splendid turn to get away from Chiriches before driving towards the opposition box. The former Sunderland attacker shapes to shoot and is tugged to the ground by the Romanian defender. However, the referee somehow decides to wave play on.
--- 76’ Substitution A. Lennon enters the game and replaces E. Capoue. ---
(75’) STAT: That was West Brom's third league goal of the season and their first in 360 minutes.
--- 74’ Assist C. Brunt gave the assist. ---
--- 74’ Goal! WEST BROM TAKE THE LEAD! James Morrison is the goalscorer as he is in the right place to head in Brunt's teasing corner from the right. The Scotland midfielder had all the time in the world to finish from close range but where was the Spurs marking? ---
--- 73’ Yellow card D. Rose receives a yellow card. ---
(72’) West Brom have stepped up a gear in the last couple of minutes but there is no red shirt to meet Wisdom's low cross into the box. Tottenham then break down the other end but Soldado's pass to Lamela is too heavy and a good opportunity breaks down, much to the frustration of the home support.
(70’) CHANCE FOR WEST BROM! Sessegnon has worked hard for the Baggies today and he cuts infield from the left before picking out Morrison outside the box with an accurate pass. The Scotland midfielder looks to drive his shot into the bottom left corner but Lloris dives down low to make a good stop.
(69’) STAT: West Brom are winless in their last 13 Premier League games on a Sunday (D6, L7) since beating Liverpool in April 2012.
(67’) West Brom are on the back foot at the moment and they are struggling to earn possession in the final third. It's all gone flat for the visitors in attack and I suspect Alan Irvine may be contemplating some changes of his own.
(65’) Play finally resumes after a brief spell of treatment to Foster. Eriksen is looking the most likely to make things happen for Tottenham and with Soldado now up alongside Adebayor, he may have more joy picking his passes.
(63’) Eriksen nearly unlocks the West Brom defence when he clips a clever ball over the top for Adebayor. The Dane's pass ricochets off of Foster but he reacts well to prevent Soldado poking in the rebound. The West Brom goalkeeper picked up a knock but he should be alright to continue.
--- 61’ Substitution Soldado comes on for N. Chadli. ---
--- 61’ Substitution Paulinho enters the game and replaces M. Dembélé. ---
(61’) Mauricio Pochettino has seen enough of his side's performance and he decides to make two changes, with Roberto Soldado and Paulinho replacing Nacer Chadli and Moussa Dembele. Can the Argentine's substitutions make the desired impact?
(59’) West Brom threaten when Pocognoli makes a clever run down the left to advance into the box unmarked. However, Brunt cannot execute the pass to perfection and Kaboul makes a vital interception.
(57’) Tottenham continue to enjoy plenty of possession in the opposition half but they cannot find that killer pass, with Adebayor easily contained by Dawson and Lescott. Mauricio Pochettino must be thinking of shaking things up here, with an injection of pace needed from the bench.
(55’) WEST BROM GO CLOSE! Berahino is involved once again as he latches onto Morrison's slipped pass down the right before easily jinking past Chiriches. The 21-year-old lets fly with a left-footed effort from just outside the area but Lloris gets across his goal quickly to punch it clear. Another warning sign for Spurs.
(53’) West Brom threaten for the first time in the second half when Brunt's corner is headed towards the edge of the box to Kaboul. Gardner is there to meet it on the half volley but his effort slices wide of the target.
(52’) Tottenham have started this second half the brighter of the two sides but they are still lacking that cutting edge in the final third. Lamela escapes from his marker down the right but his cross is too close to Foster who makes an easy catch.
(50’) Christian Eriksen scored in both of Spurs' games against West Brom last season but he cannot provide the opening goal here as his incisive pass is just too heavy for Lamela who had a made a clever run infield from the right.
(48’) Tottenham make a bright start to the second half, with Rose steaming forward down the left. The full-back delivers a deep cross into the box but Lescott is there to beat Chadli in the air and clear the immediate danger. Lamela picks up the ball on the right-hand side but a series of stepovers cannot deceive the West Brom debutant who again stands firm to turn the ball behind for a corner. However, Tottenham cannot take advantage from the resulting set-piece and the visitors hack clear.
(46’) The teams re-emerge from the tunnel for the second half, unchanged. West Bromwich Albion, looking for their first win of the season and their first goals since the opening day, get the game back underway.
HT: Tottenham 0-0 West Brom. It's been a frustrating first half for Mauricio Pochettino's side who have looked sluggish in possession and who have been second-best for large periods. West Brom have been well-organised and have enjoyed the best chances of the game, with Saido Berahino a lively presence in attack. The Baggies have had the game's only shot on target and they can feel aggrieved that they did not have a penalty when Craig Dawson's header clearly struck Emmanuel Adebayor's outstretched arm in the box. However, it is goalless at the break.
(45’) CHANCE FOR TOTTENHAM! Eriksen is slowly starting to grow into this game and he delivers a peach of a cross into the box which Adebayor somehow fails to get his head on. That really should have been the opening goal for the hosts.
(43’) Both sides have been disappointing from set-pieces today and Brunt sees his delivery easily plucked out of the air by Lloris. Tottenham then attack down the other end as Dier feeds a pass down the right for Chadli who in turn finds Eriksen on the edge of the box. However, the Dane's effort is deflected behind for a corner which Kaboul then heads over the bar.
(41’) Lamela has endured a frustrating afternoon for Tottenham so far and he attempts to burst his way beyond Lescott down the right, only to see the centre-half outmuscle him and regain possession for his team. Mauricio Pochettino has plenty to ponder with half time fast approaching.
(39’) Rose has been a good outlet for Tottenham on the overlap but on this occasion he fails to beat the first man with his cross and it goes behind for a corner. Eriksen delivers the resulting set-piece into the box but Lescott is again in the right place to head clear.
(37’) West Brom have the ball in the net but it won't count. Berahino is the danger man again as he peels off Chiriches to control Dorrans' pass before coolly slotting past Lloris. However, the England youth international is denied his third league goal of the season as the linesman adjudges that he was marginally offside.
(35’) Eriksen finally makes an impact on the game as he threads an incisive pass through for Adebayor. The Togo striker has just Foster to beat, but Lescott races back to make another timely challenge.
(34’) EXCELLENT DEFENDING FROM LESCOTT! The former Manchester City and Everton centre-back has been superb on his Baggies debut so far and he produces another last-ditch clearance to prevent Adebayor from meeting Dier's cross from the right.
(33’) Tottenham are looking sluggish in possession, with their midfielders taking too many touches in the opposition half. West Brom's pressing game has worked to perfection so far and Alan Irvine might be feeling that his team deserve to be in the lead.
(31’) We've played just over half an hour at White Hart Lane and you have to say that it is West Brom who have enjoyed the best of the game so far. The visitors scream for a penalty when Dawson's header appears to strike a Tottenham arm, but the referee waves play on. Adebayor certainly had his hand raised and that should have been a penalty for West Brom.
(29’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have failed to score in their last three top-flight matches and have now gone 315 minutes without scoring. The only previous time they failed to score in four successive Premier League matches was between March and April 2003.
(27’) West Brom enjoy an impressive spell of passing inside the Tottenham half but Sessegnon misplaces a pass to Morrison, allowing the hosts the chance to regain possession. The home crowd are starting to become a little restless here as it is West Brom who look the most likely to break the deadlock.
(25’) Chiriches has looked shaky in the Tottenham defence today and Berahino once again nips in behind the Romanian defender but cannot divert an effort on target. That partnership of Chiriches and Kaboul looks far from solid.
(23’) STAT: The Baggies' most recent win against Spurs was a 2-0 victory at The Hawthorns on 28 December 2008 thanks to goals from Roman Bednar and Craig Beattie. Can they bring their nine-game winless streak to an end today?
(21’) Tottenham enjoy a patient build-up but once again the move breaks down in the final third as West Brom regain possession. Spurs are finding it difficult to break down the opposition's organised banks of four and Adebayor has hardly been involved. Alan Irvine will be very happy with his side's performance so far.
(19’) Tottenham are struggling to penetrate the West Brom defence at the moment, with Adebayor and Eriksen both losing possession on the edge of the box. Mauricio Pochettino is up from the bench and barking instructions to his players - he clearly wants to see more from his side in the final third.
(17’) STAT: Last season Tottenham lost six of 12 Premier League games immediately after Europa League matches. Will they suffer from a continental hangover today?
(15’) GOOD SAVE FROM LLORIS! It's end-to-end stuff at White Hart Lane and this time it is the Baggies' turn to attack. Gardner latches onto a loose ball outside the box before letting fly with a powerful effort and Lloris reacts superbly to palm the ball away from safety. That's the best effort of the match so far.
(13’) Rose marauds forward excellently from left-back, playing a neat one-two with Chadli. The England international curls an inviting low cross into the box but Lescott does superbly to clear on the stretch, with Foster nowhere to be seen.
(12’) Lamela has made a lively start for Tottenham and he shows his fancy footwork before delivering a teasing cross from the right. However, Dawson anticipates the danger excellently and gets ahead of Adebayor to head clear.
(10’) Berahino is causing Tottenham plenty of early problems with his clever movement and quick runs into wide areas. He once again gets in behind Chiriches but he has no support in attack and a promising attack breaks down. Lescott then goes close to scoring on his Baggies debut as he executes a half volley towards goal from a corner, but his goalbound effort strikes Dawson and Tottenham scramble the ball to safety.
(8’) Chadli has enjoyed a bright start to the season, scoring three times already. The Belgian cuts inside from the left and floats a teasing cross towards the back post, but it is too high for Lamela and the move breaks down. Tottenham are beginning to stamp their authority on this contest now.
(6’) Tottenham threaten for the first time in the game when Rose gets forward from left back. He delivers a dangerous cross into the box but Adebayor cannot direct a header towards goal and Brunt concedes a corner. West Brom defend well from the resulting set-piece and Foster is then called into action for the first time as he and Gardner work well to bring a halt to Lamela's jinking run.
(4’) Alan Irvine will be delighted at how his side have settled into this game and they continue to do the early pressing. Berahino latches onto a long ball over the top of the Spurs centre-backs but the England youth international can only fire into the side netting. Early warning signs for the hosts.
(2’) CHANCE FOR WEST BROM! The Baggies win the first corner of the game after sloppy play between Chiriches and Kaboul. Morrison delivers the set-piece from the left but it is headed clear at the front post by Rose. The danger is not over for Tottenham as Pocognoli marauds down the left and his teasing cross is headed narrowly over by Dawson.
(1’) The referee blows his whistle and Tottenham, in their traditional white shirts, get the game underway. West Brom are in their alternative red strip.
The teams emerge from the tunnel to a great reception from both sets of fans. Captains Younes Kaboul and Chris Brunt begin the handshakes between the respective sides. Today's referee is Kevin Friend.
West Brom subs: Myhill, Baird, McAuley, Mulumbu, Gamboa, Anichebe, Ideye.
WEST BROM (4-4-1-1): Foster; Wisdom, Dawson, Lescott, Pocognoli; Dorrans, Morrison, Gardner, Brunt; Sessegnon; Berahino.
Tottenham subs: Vorm, Naughton, Vertonghen, Bentaleb, Lennon, Paulinho, Soldado.
TOTTENHAM (4-2-3-1): Lloris; Dier, Kaboul (c), Chiriches, Rose; Capoue, Dembele; Chadli, Eriksen, Lamela; Adebayor.
WEST BROM TEAM NEWS: Alan Irvine makes two changes to the side which were defeated 2-0 by Everton last time out. Joleon Lescott has recovered from injury to make his debut alongside Craig Dawson in the Baggies defence with Jonas Olsson dropping out, while Stephane Sessegnon is preferred to record signing Brown Ideye in attack. Youssouf Mulumbu is only deemed fit enough for the bench after his hamstring injury while Victor Anichebe is also a substitute after recovering from a hernia problem.
TOTTENHAM TEAM NEWS: Mauricio Pochettino recalls a number of players after rotating his side for the 0-0 Europa League draw against Partizan Belgrade in midweek. Newly-appointed captain Younes Kaboul starts alongside Vlad Chiriches in central defence, with Eric Dier and Danny Rose once again occupying the full-back roles. Nacer Chadli and Erik Lamela will be tasked with providing creativity and pace from their wide midfield positions, with both players beginning to showcase their true potential this season, while Emmanuel Adebayor leads the front line.
As for West Brom, they currently sit bottom of the Premier League and are one of five teams - alongside Burnley, Sunderland, Crystal Palace and Newcastle - yet to win a game this season. Alan Irvine signed 11 players in the summer but the Baggies are yet to gel and only Saido Berahino has scored for them in the league this campaign. West Brom have drawn on three of their last four visits to White Hart Lane but they are winless against Tottenham in their last nine matches.
Tottenham currently sit seventh in the Premier League but a win today could take them up to as high as second. Mauricio Pochettino has enjoyed a respectable start as Spurs coach though a heavy 3-0 home defeat to Liverpool followed up by a 2-2 draw at Sunderland has raised a few eyebrows. Can they return to winning ways today?
Hello and welcome to this live Premier League commentary between Tottenham Hotspur and West Bromwich Albion. The Baggies are yet to win in the league since Alan Irvine took charge and today they will be attempting to earn their first victory at White Hart Lane since 1984. I'm Max Bentley and I'll be keeping you informed with all the action as it unfolds.

The Premier League never ceases to amaze, does it? Everton will hope to bounce back to winning ways when they make the short trip across Merseyside to take on neighbours Liverpool next weekend while Crystal Palace will be seeking back-to-back league triumphs when they host Leicester City. Thanks for joining me, Max Bentley, on this live commentary. Until next time, goodbye.
FT: Everton 2-3 Crystal Palace. Neil Warnock enjoys his first win since being reinstalled as Eagles boss thanks to goals from Mile Jedinak, Frazier Campbell and Yannick Bolasie. It looked like it would be a difficult afternoon for Palace when Romelu Lukaku put Everton ahead early on but they responded brilliantly, taking advantage of the Toffees' continental hangover to dominate the midfield battle. Leighton Baines' late spot kick set up a frantic finale but Palace held on to secure their first league victory of the season, lifting them off the foot of the table.
(90’) Everton bombard the Palace box with a series of crosses but Dann and Delaney stand firm again to head clear. The referee looks at his watch and blows the final whistle!
(90’) WHAT A SAVE FROM SPERONI! The Argentine has produced many special stops for the Eagles in the past and he makes an excellent reflex save here to deny Dann turning Lukaku's dangerous low cross into his own net. Mirallas kicks the post in frustration.
(90’) Palace have all 11 men pegged back inside their half and Everton are resisting the urge to pump the ball into the box, wary of the tall Palace backline. Can they find a late, late equaliser?
(90’) Neil Warnock has made several changes in an attempt to stop the Everton flow and add more stability to the Palace rearguard. However, Roberto Martinez's side continue to pour forward and the Goodison Park faithful applaud loudly as the fourth official signals SIX minutes of stoppage time.
--- 89’ Yellow card J. Speroni is cautioned by the referee. ---
(88’) DELANEY TO THE RESCUE! Everton are pursuing the equaliser and they nearly snatch it as Mirallas escapes down the left before feeding his countryman Lukaku with a low cross. The Belgian striker thinks he's going to score but Delaney bravely gets across to deflect his strike over the crossbar. Superb defending.
--- 87’ Substitution E. Fryers enters the game and replaces Y. Bolasie. ---
--- 86’ Substitution F. Campbell is done for the day. K. Doyle is his replacement. ---
(86’) SO CLOSE TO 3-3! Everton work the short corner again with Baines and Osman combining to good effect. The England left-back cuts the ball back to Jagielka inside the box but his shot goes inches past the post. If only that had fallen to Lukaku or Eto'o!
--- 84’ Substitution A. Guédioura enters play, replacing J. McArthur. ---
--- 84’ Substitution S. Distin is replaced with D. Gibson. ---
(84’) STAT: That penalty means that Baines has now scored from all 14 attempts from the spot.
--- 83’ Goal! BAINES PULLS ONE BACK! Everton win a penalty when Dann is harshly adjudged to have tripped McCarthy in the box. Baines steps up to the spot and he keeps his composure to send Speroni the wrong way. ---
(81’) Dann has proved insurmountable in the air today and he rises above Osman to prevent the midfielder from turning in Lukaku's knock-down. Can Palace hold on?
(79’) There is a stoppage in play here as Delaney lands awkwardly and receives a spell of treatment. The Republic of Ireland centre-back has been terrific today and it is Palace's strong defensive foundations which look set to earn Neil Warnock his first win in his second spell in charge of the Eagles.
--- 77’ Yellow card S. Naismith goes into the referee's book. ---
(77’) Mirallas springs to life as he dribbles down the left wing before feeding Lukaku outside the box. The former Chelsea striker attempts to curl a shot into the top corner but Jedinak gets his body in the way to deflect it behind for a corner.
--- 76’ Yellow card J. Puncheon receives a yellow card. ---
(75’) Everton are upping the tempo here and Osman looks to atone for his error as he lets fly from outside the box and sees his effort well parried by Speroni. Mirallas and Naismith have struggled to make the desired impact off the bench.
(73’) Lukaku has struggled to test the Palace goal since his ninth-minute strike though he does well to peel off his marker at the back post to meet McCarthy's cross before diverting a header on target. However, Delaney reads the danger and produces a brilliant header to prevent Speroni from being forced into a save.
(71’) It looked like being a long afternoon for Crystal Palace when they went behind after just nine minutes but Neil Warnock's side have responded brilliantly and deserve their lead. Fingers may be pointed at Howard after his two errors but Everton simply have not been incisive enough in the final third and have looked lacklustre in midfield.
--- 69’ Assist The assist came from J. Puncheon. ---
--- 69’ Goal! BOLASIE MAKES IT 3-1! Everton have been second-best in midfield since going ahead and Osman has his pocket picked by Puncheon all too easily. The former Southampton winger coolly picks out Bolasie on the left corner of the box and the Democratic Republic of Congo man makes no mistake, steering his effort into the bottom corner. ---

Although Jose Mourinho may have some concerns over his defence, Chelsea look simply unstoppable going forward with Costa's clinical finishing complementing Hazard's dribbling and Fabregas' vision. It's going to take something very special to stop Chelsea!

A John Terry own goal gifted the visitors the lead before a Diego Costa hat trick put the Blues in firm control. Loic Remy capped his debut with a well-taken goal before Jonjo Shelvey pulled one back late on for Garry Monk's side. A thrilling afternoon at Stamford Bridge!

The two sides emerge from the tunnel to a good reception from both sets of fans. Captains John Terry and Ashley Williams lead the handshakes between the respective sides. Today's referee is Kevin Friend.

Swansea have not beaten Chelsea in a league game since 1981, though they did win in west London in the Capital One Cup in January 2013, en route to their famous cup success.

Leon Britton faces a month on the sidelines through injury.

When the fixture list was released in June, Chelsea manager Jose Mourinho is unlikely to have foreseen this game being a top-of-the-table battle. For Burnley that is two draws in three games since their return to the Premier League and they occupy 18th place at the moment. That is also two clean sheets on the bounce for Sean Dyche's men after their 0-0 home draw to Manchester United. It could have been a win but a point away from home is always good for a team battling relegation. Dyche will be sweating on the injury to Danny Ings as that will mean both parts of his 40 goal strike partnership from last season will be out with injuries. Sunderland travel to Turf Moor next weekend as Burnley continue the search for their first win.
It is early days to be looking at the league table but after Newcastle's 3-0 defeat to Southampton, Crystal Palace are out of the relegation zone. Neil Warnock is still looking for his first league win as manager having draw both his games so far. However he will be happy with a point after Jedinak gave away a penalty in the final ten minutes of the game. Next up for them is a trip to Goodison Park, to face Roberto Martinez and his Everton side.

(90’) Lamela's free kick is flicked towards goal and is the last action of the match. The game ends 2-2 as Spurs twice let the lead slip and will have to settle for a point. Neither side will be thrilled about their defending but there was some superb individual quality from Adam Johnson in what may very well be a goal of the week candidate. Thank you for joining us here for this match!
(90’) It's a poor free kick from Lamela and Sunderland race forward. Giaccherini slips and falls down before Kaboul plays a wild pass back to his goalie, forcing Lloris to wace before letting it go out for a corner. Brown slides into Lamela incredibly harshly and it's a booking for the former Manchester United defender.
--- 90’ +3 Yellow card Jordi Gómez receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) Yet another free kick to Spurs as Lamela goes down after a rough challenge. This is further outside the box but his teammates are all forward, waiting to get on the end of it.
(90’) Sunderland are furious with that decision as it seems Rose dived to win that free kick without being touched at all. Justice is done as Lamela skies his shot and the game remains tied.
(90’) In the first of four minutes here and Cattermole wins the ball back before giving it away to Chiriches, who presses forward and passes it wide to Lamela. Rose goes down just outside the box and wins a free kick!
--- 90’ Yellow card C. Wickham is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) AND SUNDERLAND'S CHANCE GOES BEGGING! Buckley turns his body to get his foot on the ball for a shot after some fantastic work from Giaccherini. His shot looks good but loops over the bar! Seconds later, Wickham is booked for a challenge from behind on Rose.
(89’) One minute plus stoppages here as Tottenham press forward but lose the ball far too easily. Sunderland smell blood now and look like they might just be able to win this one but time is not on their side.
--- 88’ Yellow card S. Vergini is cautioned by the referee. ---
(87’) The game is becoming quite physical now as Poyet is madly barking out instructions on the sidelines. Vergini is getting a booking from the ref for shoving down Stambouli.
--- 86’ Substitution Lennon comes on for Eriksen right after a booking on Sunderland for dissent and kicking away the ball after disagreeing with the referee's decision to award a free-kick to the Spurs. ---
--- 85’ Yellow card P. van Aanholt gets yellow. ---
(85’) Dier conceded yet another corner and Sunderland take it short. Johnson whips it into the box as Kaboul races to head it clear but the home side still have possession. Can they win the game in these remaining minutes?!
(84’) Kaboul is forward and trying to play a cross in, but his ball hits Brown, before hitting himself and going out for a goal-kick. Nothing going right for Spurs at the moment!
(83’) That's unfortunately a comedy of a goal to concede for the visitors, who manage to bundle it into the net with three defenders surrounding the lone attacker. The final touch may have just been off of Kane.
--- 82’ Goal! SUNDERLAND TIIIEEEEE! 2-2!! Gomez makes an immediate impact as he's taken down by Capoue on the left side of the box, gifting a free kick to the home side. Gomez himself swings it into the box, and it deflects off of Chiriches into the back of the net! ---
(81’) The corner is cleared once and then twice after being played in again, but Sunderland now are the ones pressing and look more likely to score the goal. Their effort today has been fantastic but they simply have not given themselves enough chances to score.
--- 80’ Substitution Jordi Gómez enters play, replacing J. Rodwell. ---
(80’) Giaccherini takes Dier on in the box to win a corner when the defender kicks the ball out. Johnson stands ready to take it.
--- 79’ Substitution Brown's clearance ricochets off of Lamela and into the thankful arms of Mannone before the former Roma player could shoot. Adebayor, who looks quite tired, is off for Kane as Poyet sends on Gomez for Rodwell. ---
(78’) Adebayor again has the ball in the box but still cannot get his shot off, as he tries to dribble an opening his way but falls over. The visitors continue to press here but there are some tired legs on show.
(77’) Spurs take a corner short, with Lamela and Eriksen keeping the ball before playing it back to their defence. Chiriches looks for Dier down the flank but looses the ball before winning it back and charging forward. He gets it to Adebayor in the box but O'Shea stands firm and pokes the ball loose.
(75’) LAMELA OFF THE CROSSBAR!!!! Ohhhh and that was VERY, VERY good from the Argentine, who showed persistence just when he was about to lose the ball to beat his man and send a shot in from just outside the box that absolutely had Mannone beat!
(74’) Chiriches with a superb tackle on Wickham, sticking a leg in on the edge of the box to prevent the player from getting into a shooting position.
(73’) Brown beats Adebayor to the ball and launches his side forward through Buckley. The latter tangles with Dier on the edge of the Spurs box and the free kick is awarded to the visitors, to the chagrin of the home fans.
(71’) Spurs with the ball now about halfway in Sunderland's half, looking for a piercing through ball to send someone forward. Poyet's men have the channels closed well but Lamela plays Adebayor in quickly and Mannone races out to prevent the shot!
--- 70’ Substitution Chadli off for the debut of Stambouli as Pochettino looks to get some fresh legs on the pitch in an effort to counter the drive that Giaccherini has shown since coming on. ---
(69’) Lamela ghots by one player and goes down as he collides with Cattermole on the edge of the box but nothing is called! In fairness, it looks as though Lamela ran into Cattermole rather than the other way around, but Pochettino is furious on the sidelines!
(68’) And that's a SCREAMER of a shot from Johnson, who strikes from ten yards outside the box and watches his effort sail just wide of the far post!
(67’) It's one dribble too many for Capoue, who tries to beat an extra man instead of taking a shot from a good central position. His wastefulness costs him the ball and Sunderland counter.
(66’) There's just an extra spring here in the step of the home side, who aren't playing like theyr down a goal and short of confidence. Spurs are currently in possession but are having a tough time advancing it beyond their midfield.
--- 65’ Substitution W. Buckley enters play, replacing R. Álvarez. ---
--- 65’ Substitution Larsson, who has put in a superb shift today, goes off for Giaccherini and the new boy Alvarez is off for Buckley. ---
(62’) Vergini does just enough to stop the ball from getting to Lamela in the box. The chances have evened out here as both sides look lively up top.
--- 61’ Yellow card A rare booking finally comes as Dier slides into the side of Alvarez and catches the on-loan winger on his shin without touching the ball. It's the first booking of the match and Dier can really have no complaints about it. ---
(60’) Ooh and a chance from Wickham goes wide! He races down the right flank and whips a ball into the box that goes past Lloris and fails to reach any of his teammates! It was a delightful pass but to no one, ultimately.
(58’) Another penalty shout! Dier goes down under a rough sliding challenge from Cattermole from behind but again, the referee does not blow his whistle. It looks as though Cattermole may have just knocked the ball before taking the full-back down but it was surely a debatable call!
(57’) The fans at the stadium today are really growing into the match, applauding loudly every time their side completes a pass as they sense that there's more life to this yet. Adebayor drops very deep to get the ball but the spell of possession ends when Eriksen's shot from outside of the box is blocked.
(55’) Chadli goes down on the counter, on the right edge of the box but outside of it, as Larsson takes the ball but no call is made. In truth he went down a little too easily there and the ref simply wasn't fooled. The visitors are struggling a little bit now to keep the ball.
(54’) Odd corner from Sunderland who try something from the training ground that doesn't quite work out. From the corner, Larsson plays it vey wide to Johnson, near the edge of the box. Johnson tries to take two touches and shoot but fails to control the ball and has to lay it off deeper.
(53’) A brief respite for Spurs as Rodwell has a high foot on Kaboul, who lunged with his head to clear the ball in the box. Free kick to Spurs.
(52’) From the throw-in, the home side win a corner as Rose deflects a cross into the box. Johnson plays it high to the near post but Adebayor smacks it clear. Sunderland still have the ball in Spurs' half.
(51’) Sunderland are looking lively now, trying to keep the ball deeper in their opponents' half, but are leaving Wickham too isolated to really do damage. Alvarez wins a throw-in in enemy territory.
(49’) Sunderland once again behind and once again looking for an immediate answer. Wickham takes a shot that gets deflected out for a corner, that's played in by Larsson and cleared by Capoue.
--- 48’ Goal! SPURS SCORE!!! The finish is scrappy -Eriksen poking it over the line from very close range after some confusion - but the buildup was beautiful, with Adebayor and Lamela exchanging passes as they raced forward. The final ball in from Chadli takes two deflections before landing at Eriksen, who rises from a prone position to get his toe on it and poke it in! ---
(46’) And the second half is now underway! The effect of the locker room talks will be evident soon enough, with neither side surely looking to settle for a point here. The game is picking up from where it left off, with Spurs immediately deep in Sunderland's half. Adebayor's long cross nearly finds Chadli on the other side of the pitch but Mannone collects.
For the second half, Spurs will need to convert their possession deep in Sunderland's territory into actual shots, which they began the game doing well enough but eventually became hesitant to do. Sunderland, meanwhile, just need more possession period and have to hope that they can turn momentum around to create a few chances of their own.
The half began relentlessly, with Chadli pouncing on a clearance and Johnson responding moments later with a superb solo goal to give us two goals in the opening four minutes. The game settled not too long after that, with chances much harder to come by.
(45’) Dier throws his arms all over Larsson and the referee awards yet another free kick to the home side. It turns out to be the last meaningful action of the half as the whistle is blown and the teams march into the locker room tied, 1-1.
(45’) Fantastic persistence from Chadli in the box who refused to give up on the ball in the box. He played it to Eriksen, continued his run, and tried to receive the return ball but lost out at the last second.
(44’) Free kick to the home side as Rodwell goes down about five yards from the box under a challenge from Dembele.
(42’) IS THAT A HAND BALL? Lamela tries to play it through to Adebayor in the box but it looks as though the ball his O'Shea's hand and bounces away. The referee doesn't make a call and it looked as though it hit his torso instead of his arm.
(41’) Lamela tries to work the ball into Chadli on the edge of the box but the pass is played just behind him. The Argentine has been lively today but Pochettino will want him to work on his passing in the final third.
(39’) Kaboul is down holding his back after rolling over Wickham while going up for the ball. With not long left until half-time, Pochettino has to make a decision here about a substitute, but it seems likely that he'll see if Kaboul can carry on at least until the break.
(38’) DEMBELE OFF THE BAR! The midfielder sees Mannone too far to his left and rips a shot towards the top righ corner that absolutely thhumps off the crossbar and bounces off! That's surely a wake-up call to the keeper!!
(37’) Sunderland want a penalty! Wickham goes down in the box after Rose comes in from behind to strip him of the ball in the box, but it looks as though Rose plays the ball fairly and no call is made.
(36’) Lamela tries a pass over the top for his teammate, but it's overhit and Mannone intercepts it before Adebayor can get onto it. Spurs are trying new ways here to breach the defence but the game is much different now than it was in the opening spell when Sunderland's backline was chaotic.
(35’) Nevertheless, after the free kick, it's business as usual for Spurs. Sunderland are totally pinned back in their box and simply cannot find a way to get the ball - but in fairness to them, are restricting Spurs from taking any shots.
(33’) This is a fantastic spell of possession from the visitors, who even have Ricky Alvarez back on defence to try and contain Dier and Lamela. It's the Sunderland man who collides with Capoue and goes down, winning a free kick.
(31’) Cattermole easily intercepts a poor pass from Lamela. The Argentine is all over the pitch today, swapping flanks as needed but to diminishing effect right now.
(29’) Immense pressure from Tottenham right now, as the visitors win yet another corner. Lamela swings it in this time instead of Eriksen but it's cleared centrally, only for the visitors to win it back.
(27’) Spurs are taking their free kicks quickly, as Lamela is fouled and one is awarded before being taken almost immediately. It's clear that the visitors want to use their creativity to pull players out of position and then pounce with a shot.
(26’) Some silky moves from Lamela leads a counter down the pitch, which results in a corner when Chadli's cross is poked out. Rodwell heads it up and Mannone collides with Kaboul as he reaches for it. Free-kick to the home side with neither player looking worse for the wear.
(25’) A bit of a half-chance for Spurs, as Dier has possession centrally near the box and tries to play it in for Rose, but there's a sea of bodies in front of him and the pass is deflected out.
(23’) Larsson catches Rose's foot off a poor tackle and thus gives away a free-kick to the visitors. Spurs are working the ball deep in Sunderland's half as the home side's pressing is not giving them much time on the ball.
(22’) The two sides are trading possession in the middle but failing to make inroads with the ball. The defences seem to have figured out how to contain each other's offence - at least for the moment - as chances are becoming increasingly speculative.
(20’) A poor clearance from Chiriches gifts the ball to Rodwell, but luckily for the defender, the midfielder plauys a poor pass that is intercepted. The tempo of this game has settled.
(19’) Larsson whips the ball into the box and Adebayor rises high to head it away. Sunderland are starting to control the match more, doing well to stop losing possession so easily.
(18’) The difference in possession thus far is staggering, with Tottenham holding over 70%! Nevertheless, Poyet's men now have a corner after Kaboul is forced to play a dangerous pass out of the box.
(17’) Sunderland have a shot blocked in the box as Wickham can't turn around quickly enough and Rose falls over before he can take his own shot moments later. Dier and Adebayor both tackle Johnson and a free-kick is awarded to the home side.
(15’) Another fantastic passing sequence from the visitors, involving Lamela on a quick turn and a fast pass from Eriksen. Pochettino's men are getting the ball down the byline and into the box but are having trouble converting that meaningful possession into truly meaningful chances.
(14’) A very well worked team move from the visitors ends as Rose goes goes in the box easily, and Larsson is asking for his opponent to be cautioned for diving but the referee is having none of it. No call is awarded and Mannone takes a goal kick.
(13’) Alvarez's first real involvement is to keep the ball high down the right flank for his side, but shortly thereafter, Sunderland lose possession anyway. The visitors are playing like the home side, ferocious in their attacks and gripping in their possession.
(11’) Mannone races to heave clear a ball played in towards Adebayor, poking it down the field to give his defence a chance to regroup. The striker has been immensely influential thus far.
(10’) Chadli does well to wrap his foot around the ball and pry it off of the home side without committing a foul. The past few minutes have all been down the home side's left channel, giving Dier quite a bit of work to do at the moment.
(9’) Wickham is fouled by Kaboul, giving both sides a much needed break in the middle of the pitch. Sunderland look to build from the back as Johnson races down the byline, but Dier covers his well and manages to clear.
(7’) From the ensuing corner, the ball lands at Kaboul who sticks a leg at it but finds his shot blocked! Absolutely breathless, this match, with neither midfield anywhere to be seen.
(6’) AND NEARLY A SECOND FOR SPURS! Eriksen lifts a peach of a ball over to Adebayor after the give-and-go; he gets to it, onside, and fires straight at Mannone for a corner!
(5’) Wickham gets down the byline and crosses well but Totenham's defence clears. Straight away the ball gets to the other box and Mannone is forced into a diving save! The tempo of this game is purely outrageous at the moment!
--- 4’ Assist The assist came from S. Larsson. ---
--- 4’ Goal! AND WHAT A RESPONSE!!!! SUNDERLAND EQUALIZE IMMEDIATELY! That was ALL Adam Johnson in the box, who dribbles and jinxes his way through the defence after picking up the ball wide. The shot takes the slightest of deflections off Kaboul which sees the ball dribble past Lloris and into the net! 1-1!! ---
--- 2’ Goal! GOOALLL CHADLI! WHAT A START FOR TOTTENHAM! Dembele picks up the ball in the midfield and ushers it forward. Adebayor gets the ball central and drills a powerful shot to Mannone. The former Arsenal keeper parries it to his right - directly into the path of Chadli who slots it into the far post! ---
(1’) AND WE HAVE KICK-OFF! The visitors, in their yellow aaway kit, immediately press forward, with Eriksen looking for Adebayor. They play it back and wide, keeping the home side pinned back. Eriksen plays a smart ball on the edge of the box to Rose, who shoots and forces Mannone into a save almost immediately!
Both teams are walking out of the tunnel and we're just minutes away from kick off now!
Recent history between these two sides heavily favours the visitors. In the last 8 matches, Tottenham have won 6 and drew 2, and Spurs scored more against Sunderland last season than any other other side with 7. Poyet's men have won only 3 of their last 14 games at home.
Not many injuries tonight, with Spurs missing out on Roberto Soldado and Kyle Walker. Otherwise, both coaches have a full team at their disposal, with Ricky Alvarez immediately slotting in for the home side and the red-hot Erik Lamela looking to play from the first minute as well.
Tottenham: Lloris, Dier, Kaboul, Chiriches, Rose, Dembele, Capoue, Lamela, Eriksen, Chadli, Adebayor
Sunderland: Mannone, Vergini, van Aanholt, Brown, O'Shea, Cattermole, Larsson, Rodwell, Johnson, Alvarez, Wickham.
What's on the line here today? With so few points available yet this season, either side could rocket up the table with a win. The home team could go from 13th up to 7th, even above Arsenal, should they manage all three points. For Spurs, it's a chance to get themselves in the top 3, and could even go top should they win by a five goal margin.
Gus Poyet's side has become a bit more interesting in recent weeks, having taken Sebastian Coates on loan from Liverpool in an effort to keep out the goals at the back and bringing in Ricky Alvarez on loan from Inter to provide a spark of creativity up front.
Before those defeats however, both sides have had matches they could be proud about. The visitors had a flying start to the season, winning 4 matches between the league and the Europa League, before the 3-0 loss to Liverpool at home. Sunderland have not been quite as good but still managed to draw Manchester United and defeat Birmingham in the League Cup.
Hello and welcome to our pre-match coverage of Sunderland vs Tottenham! It's match-day 4 of the Premier League, coming off an international break that both of these sides may have welcomed, having suffered defeats against Queens Park Rangers and Liverpool, respectively.

Full time at the Hawthorns. Everton go back to Merseyside with the three points today after brushing aside West Brom with a relatively routine 2-0 victory. A terribly uninspiring performance from the home side came after conceding just two minutes in thanks to a terrific finish from Romelu Lukaku after a poor mistake from Jonas Olsson. A slight improvement thereafter was hampered when Ben Foster allowed Kevin Mirallas speculative strike to creep into the corner. Everton record their first win of the season, meanwhile it is doom and gloom for the Baggies! I'm Martin Macdonald, thanks for joining us, see you next time!
--- 90’ +1 Yellow card M. Bešić receives a yellow card. ---
--- 90’ Yellow card A. Wisdom is yellow-carded. ---
(90’) Superb double save by Howard! The Everton keeper, who has barely had anything to do today, denied Samaras and Berahino in quick succession! Looks like there wont even be a consolation for the Baggies today!
--- 88’ Substitution A. McGeady is replaced with M. Bešić. ---
(88’) SAVE FROM FOSTER!! The Englishman looks to atone for his previous error and does so to some degree as he denied Osman with a terrific palmed block to the right-hand side! Almost a third for Everton!
(86’) Martinez just looks to take the sting out of the game totally as he introduces Muhamed Besic in place of McGeady. Hopefully the Bosnian does better today than he did on his debut; a horrible touch which allowed Samuel Eto'o to run through and score for Chelsea!
(84’) The West Brom fans have had enough and are now leaving the stadium in their droves. You can't blame them really, there team has put in a pretty dire performance. Samaras and Blanco have been decent after coming on, but Everton have been solid.
--- 81’ Yellow card S. Naismith receives a yellow card. ---
(81’) Naismith is the latest player to go into the book here as he cynically breaks down a West Brom attack with a trip on Gamboa. There's no need to get a yellow at this stage when you're two goals up. Daft!
(78’) Everton have been excellent since going two goals up as they completely dominate possession in the middle of the park. The Hawthorns crowd is flat, and that'll not do wonders for West Brom's attempts to claw a goal back!
--- 77’ Substitution C. Gamboa enters play, replacing S. Pocognoli. ---
(76’) Final throw of the dice from Alan Irvine as he introduces Cristian Luna for Pocognoli. Hardly the most positive of changes, so there must be an injury involved with the Belgian!
(74’) There just is no sign at all of West Brom mounting any kind of comeback here. They have been desperately poor up top with Tim Howard barely being called into action this afternoon.
(72’) McGeadyyyyy! How close was that?! The Republic of Ireland international, who scored a brace for his country during the week, almost rounds off a perfect few days as he flashes a shot at goal from 25 yards out. No goal today yet though as they attempt goes a whisker by the post! Unlucky! Foster was beaten!
--- 70’ Substitution G. Samaras enters the game and replaces B. Ideye. ---
--- 70’ Substitution C. Brunt is done for the day. S. Blanco is his replacement. ---
(70’) Alan Irvine finally decides the time is right to make some changes, although it is probably too late now. Chris Brunt and Ideye Brown are replaced by Sebastian Blanco and Georgios Samaras. Going for it then, but they are sure to leave some space in behind as they chase the game!
--- 68’ Substitution L. Osman comes on for R. Lukaku. ---
(68’) Roberto Martinez reacts quickly to going two goals up as he withdraws opening goalscorer, Lukaku, in favour of Osman. A fairly conservative swap you'd have to say, so it looks like Everton are happy with what they have, and no wonder, they look really comfortable now.
--- 66’ Assist L. Baines gave the assist. ---
--- 66’ Goal! GOOOOOOALLLLLL FOR EVERTON!! A calamity from Foster! Mirallas bursts down the left-hand side before drifting inside hand having a crack with a speculative effort from 25 yards. It looked like a routine save for the goalkeeper, but the Englishman lets the attempt creep under him! Two-nil Everton! ---
(64’) West Brom have two bites of the cherry within a minute as Ideye and Dorrans both have attempts in quick succession. The former sees his attempt blocked before the Scotsman blazes over the bar from 25 yards. They have had plenty of shots, but Howard has been barely worked in between the sticks!
(62’) Just over an hour played at the Hawthorns and West Brom aren't really looking any more likely to equaling the game than they did in the first half. They have looked a danger on the wings, but the crosses into the box are being easily gobbled up by the Everton defence.
(60’) Wisdom gets down the right-hand side on the overlap and teases a cross to the front post. Ideye is lurking and looks poised to have a crack at goal, but Howard is alert to the danger and steps out of goal to palm away the cross. Good goalkeeping there from the American!
(58’) Berahino has probably been West Brom's brightest player so far. He has lead the line well but with Ideye sees as the most central forward, he has been forced out wide to try and affect the play. The hosts need to get the Englishman in and around the penalty area, as this is where he can be a danger.
(56’) Ideye Brown, who has been quiet so far, attempts to grab a goal back for his side as he collects the ball inside the box before attempting a curler into the top corner. It ends up taking a deflection on the way through and West Brom get the corner. They need to make more of their set pieces, and here is a chance!
(54’) Baines stretches his legs down the left flank before shifting the ball out wide to McGeady. The former Celtic winger gets to the byline before coming back inside and whipping a cross into the box, but Olsson is on hand this time to head away from the danger area. He should have been as decisive that clearance two minutes in which lead to the goal!
--- 53’ Yellow card J. McCarthy goes into the referee's book. ---
(52’) An aspect of Everton's play in the first few minutes of this second half has been their pressing high up the pitch. The latest example comes as Olsson collects the ball midway through the half and is forced to retreat all the way back to Foster after some intense pressure from Lukaku and McGeady.
(50’) Whaaaaaaat a miss from Naismith!! Ben Foster initially makes an excellent save from a Lukaku strike, but the block falls perfectly to the feet of the Scotsman, who blazes over from six yards out! You'd have put your house on the in-form striker putting that away!
(48’) Everton begin the second half impressively as they pop the ball around for at least 20 passes before an attacking move breaks down through a poor touch from Lukaku under pressure from Dawson. West Brom still in the dressing room it appears!
(46’) We are back under way in this Barclays Premier League clash!
Half time at the Hawthorns. West Brom are met with boos are they walk off the pitch as they head into the break 1-0 down against Everton. It was a horror start for the hosts as they conceded with just two minutes on the clock thanks to a lovely finish from Lukaku. A spirited comeback looked on the cards as Alan Irvine's men dominated thereafter, but no goals and a desperate lack of creativity up top. They'll need to improve massively in the second period if they are going to get back into this!
(44’) McGeady gets down the left wing and shifts back inside before sliding a pass square to Lukaku. The goalscorer looks to double his tally with an attempt from the edge of the box, but it ends up going high and wide over the bar.
(42’) Both sets of players get involves in a melee just outside the West Brom box as Naismith and Dawson instigate the mini-brawl. The former Rangers striker was guilty of kicking out at the defender slightly, but escapes punishment from the ref. He paints a relieved picture as he walks away from the drama!
(40’) The fans at the Hawthorns are getting frustrated with their players here as we approach the last five minutes of the half. The frustration stems from a lack of options from the man on the ball, which is hampering any kind of creativity in the final third.
(38’) Mirallas almost scores a screamer! Everton almost double their lead against the run of play as the Belgian picks up the ball 25 yards out and decides to have a crack from distance. The attempt looks destined to nestle in the top corner but just rises at the last minute before going north of the crossbar! Unlucky!
(36’) Baines looks to open up his stride down the left-hand side and get into the final third, but ends up being scythed down cynically by Wisdom. The Toffees get the free kick just inside the opposition half a yard or so in from the halfway line. Predictably, they take in quickly and pop the ball around in midfield.
(34’) The tactics of Everton are pretty clear at the moment. They have sensed that West Brom have grown in confidence since conceding and they are simply attempting to take the sting out of the match by keeping the ball for extended periods. As I mentioned before though, they have plenty of pace going forward though Lukaku, McGeady, Naismith, and Mirallas.
(32’) West Brom pile on the pressure with two consecutive corner kicks after some good work by Berahino inside the opposition box. The second set piece is swung in but Everton are let off the hook as Olsson is penalised for pushing inside the six yard box.
(30’) BRUNT!! How close was that?! The Irishman latches on to a loose ball in the inside channel and looks to catch Howard out with a drilled strike to the near post. It certainly had the keeper scrambling, but ends up slamming into the side netting! The hosts go close!
(28’) The game has been pretty scrappy in the last few minutes as both teams struggle to keep possession. Plenty of hard tackling in midfield, but not much creativity. You get the feeling this would probably favour Everton, as they certainly have the pace to hurt the hosts on the counterattack.
--- 26’ Yellow card C. Gardner gets yellow. ---
(26’) This time it is Everton who get the free kick and Gardner rather stupidly gets himself involved in the melee, resulting in the first booking of the match. West Brom will need all their players if they are going to get back into this, so everyone needs to keep their heads!
(24’) Dorrans gets down the right-hand side and looks to clip a cross into the box, but ends up on the end of a foul by Jagielka. The resulting free kick comes straight off the wall though. Disappointing.
(22’) West Brom continue to press forward for the equaliser now as they enjoy a period of sustained possession in the final third. However, the Everton defence haven't been particularly stretched as of yet and they are looking relatively comfortable, despite the hosts current domination of the ball.
(20’) Berahino collects the ball down the right-hand side and skips past a couple of challenges before attempting to find his strike partner, Ideye, inside the box. The final ball was just lacking in quality though and Everton clear.
(18’) Martinez's men just attempt to halt the ascendancy of the home side as Barry and McCarthy instigate a keep-ball session in the middle of the park. A clever plan to quieten the crowd back down.
(16’) Everton may have took the early lead , but it is West Brom who look the more likely to score at the moment. They could have easily folded after conceding after just two minutes, but they have displayed some grit to claw themselves back into contention. No goal yet though!
(14’) A stroke of luck for Everton here! Brunt whips in a wicked corner kick and the ball bounces dangerously off Lukaku towards goal, but it ends up fortuitously floating straight into the hands of the grateful Howard. Almost an OG for the Belgian.
(12’) Great block by Stones! Some lovely build up play be West Brom eventually sees the ball come to Berahino at the back post, who takes down before having a crack at goal. The Everton defender sticks out a leg and deflects the strike over the bar!
(10’) The Baggies have took a few minutes, but they are finally managing to get settled in possession. Gardner and Brunt are beginning to assert themselves in the middle of the park, but still no real bite going forward as of yet.
(8’) Olsson looks to atone for his previous error as he collects the ball at the back before attempting an ambitious pass over the op of the Everton defence for Berahino. Jagielka manages to mop up though and the visitors retain possession at the back.
(6’) West Brom need to sort themselves out at the back here or they could be out of contention in this match before even getting out the blocks. That early goal for Everton has saw them settle well and they are looking confident in possession.
(4’) That's exactly the start Alan Irvine did not need! The Hawthorns was bouncing at the start of the match, but the home crowd has been quietened with haste!
