Thank you for joining me, Alex Stewart, for this afternoon's humdinger which finished Newcastle United 3-3 Crystal Palace. Enjoy the rest of your weekend and see you soon!
The big stories will be, of course, the debut of Rolando Aarons and the return of Wilfred Zaha, but mentions should go to Coloccini, who defended and passed well for the home side, and Puncheon and Bolasie, who carried a threat and worked very hard all afternoon for the visitors.
Both sides will feel they could have won this. Newcastle were porous at the back and failed to capitalise on their consistent possession and set-pieces, but Aarons did brilliantly on his introduction. Palace defended resolutely and countered well, but couldn't defend a lead.
But Eagles hero Wilfred Zaha equalised in the fifth minute of stoppage time with a well-taken goal after Scott Dann had found him in space with a knock-down.
Newcastle substitute and debutant Rolando Aarons then appeared to have changed the course of the game in the home side's favour, scoring a header after a flicked-on corner and then sending a delicious shot onto the post, which Williamson smashed home for his first goal for the Magpies.
So there we are. Newcastle United 3-3 Crystal Palace. What a match. Palace opened furiously, Gayle lashing home after thirty seconds. Janmaat equalised but the Eagles began the second half as well as the first through a Puncheon goal.
--- 90’ +7 Yellow card R. Aarons receives a yellow card. ---
(90’) And that's it! 3-3 and can we all go and lie down now, thank you?
(90’) Palace come again! This game has been quite glorious. Aarons is booked after a battle with Jedinak as a Newcastle counter breaks down. Is that their final chance?
--- 90’ +5 Assist S. Dann gave the assist. ---
--- 90’ +5 Goal! ZAHA! He's back! Jedinak lofts in the free-kick and it's knocked down by a yellow shirt to Zaha who is in a lot of space and slots a very well-taken finish low and to the right of Krul. ---
(90’) It's end-to-end now. Both sides have plenty of pace on the counter and it's pretty edgy for fans of either side. Palace win a free-kick in the centre of the park.
(90’) Cabella looks for Riviere who holds it up well. The attack falters though and Palace surge back with Zaha and Puncheon. Anita does well to hold Zaha up though.
(90’) Jedinak fouls Aarons but Newcastle cannot make anything of the set-piece. Palace have the ball and stroke it around before hitting it long to Murray. Zaha loses out though, and the home side can build.
(89’) Newcastle are buoyant now and have SEVEN minutes of extra time to find another goal. This game has been marvellously exciting.
--- 88’ Yellow card G. Murray is yellow-carded. ---
--- 88’ Goal! WILLIAMSON! HIS FIRST GOAL FOR NEWCASTLE UNITED! Oh what a story! Aarons curls another beautiful chipped shot which leaves Speroni leaden-footed. It hits the post and Williamson is there to bundle home. Aarons looks very, very good. ---
(86’) Ayoze Perez slides a deft pass through to Rivere. The clearance falls to Aarons, who sets up Haidara for a cross. Palace clear and Murray concedes another free-kick lunging in at Haidara.
(85’) Neither side seem content with a point, which you can well understand. Sissoko gifts possession back to Palace with an overly ambitious pass but the away attack breaks down as Krul is fouled by Murray.
--- 83’ Substitution G. Murray comes on for Y. Bolasie. ---
(83’) AARONS! That was a cheeky effort from the sub, who curls one in from very deep after a lovely step-over. Speroni was concrete in the face of that shot, but luckily for Palace, it just drifts wide.
(82’) Bolasie ambles off and Murray comes on as the away side look to push for the last eight or so minutes. Palace don't look satisfied with a point and, in fairness, nor should they be.
(81’) Anita sends in a cross towards Ayoze Perez who goes down under the slightly clinging challenge of Dann. There's no real penalty shout though. The ball goes straight down the other end but Palace can't fashion a chance.
(80’) ZAHA! Puncheon sends the young striker through and Krul saves a low, drilled shot well with his feet. The rebound is pulled wide.
--- 79’ Substitution S. de Jong is done for the day. Ayoze Pérez is his replacement. ---
--- 79’ Substitution V. Anita comes on for D. Janmaat. ---
(79’) The subs combine, Anita crossing for Aarons, who rises well against the big centre-backs of Palace but can only head wide.
(77’) A breather as Janmaat receives treatment. The Dutchman can't continue and is replaced by another, Vernon Anita. Ayoze Perez has also come on for de Jong, who has not contributed as much as might have been hoped on his home debut.
(76’) Sissoko and Cabella play a one-two and the ball breaks to Rivere, who plays it to de Jong. The Dutchman conceds a foul and Zaha breaks, but the ball goes out of play. This is frantic.
(74’) Palace have a Campbell goal ruled out for offside and Newcastle come again. Cabella drags a shot wide after a neat lob in from Haidara. That Aarons goal has shaken the game up even more, if that were possible.
--- 73’ Goal! AARONS! What an introduction! Finally a set-piece pays off and after a flick into the middle of the six-yard box, Aarons sends a lovely looping header into the top left of Speroni's goal. It's 2-2! ---
(72’) ZAHA! He forces a great low block from Krul after a bursting run. It's fair to say that Palace look more dangerous in attack at the moment, for all Newcastle's possession.
(71’) The ball comes to Zaha in the box after a cross from Puncheon but he is surrounded by black and white shirts.
--- 70’ Substitution W. Zaha enters the game and replaces D. Gayle. ---
(70’) Zaha is on and will provide pace and a counter-attacking threat for the away team. Palace just need to defend and then hit on the break. Newcastle have a lot to do and only twenty minutes in which to do it.
(68’) Gayle is getting treatment and Zaha is ready to come on.
--- 67’ Substitution R. Aarons enters the game and replaces Y. Gouffran. ---
(67’) Aarons' first cross is good, but it's headed clear. Gayle is hobbling after a naughty challenge from Coloccini and Palace may be about to lose another striker to injury.
(66’) Aarons is very highly regarded on Tyneside and will provide a stern test for Marippa who has already been booked.
(65’) Lovely skill from Riviere after a ball from Haidara, but it's well defended. De Jong then lofts a back-heel into the path of the Frenchman, but that is cleared too. And Newcastle are bringing on exciting prospect Aarons, a quick and direct winger. Gouffran, who has been pretty dire, is going off.
(64’) Dann does well to block a cute through ball from Colback towards Cabella. Gayle wins a free-kick to relieve some of the pressure on Palace.

HT: Tottenham 0-1 Liverpool. Raheem Sterling's strike gives Brendan Rodgers a deserved half-time lead on his 100th game in charge of the club. The visitors have looked dangerous every time they have gone forward, with Mario Balotelli spurning several good chances to score on his debut. (16’) Liverpool have settled into this game excellently and they are forcing Tottenham into individual errors with their quick pressing game. Brendan Rodgers looks on happily from the touchline.

(11’) Incidentally, that was the first goal that Tottenham have conceded in the league this season. Aston Villa are now the only side who have a perfect defensive record.

The former Milan striker starts alongside Daniel Sturridge as Philippe Coutinho drops to the bench. Martin Skrtel misses his first Premier League game in a year after sustaining a knock in the 3-1 defeat to Manchester City on Monday while Glen Johnson also misses out with a thigh complaint. Mamadou Sakho therefore partners Dejan Lovren in defence while Javi Manquillo starts at right-back.

Nacer Chadli and Erik Lamela will be looking to continue their impressive early season form, while Eric Dier continues in the right-back slot after enjoying a dream start to his Spurs career. Nabil Bentaleb and Etienne Capoue start in the centre of midfield but there is no place in the Spurs squad for Sandro who has been strongly linked with a move away from the club. Emmanuel Adebayor starts as the lone striker, with Roberto Soldado sidelined with neck and back problems.
Liverpool fans will have fond memories of this fixture last season as a 5-0 thumping at White Hart Lane brought the curtain down on Andre Villas-Boas' reign at Spurs. Luis Suarez was the main man that day but with the Uruguayan now out the door, it's time for Mario Balotelli to shoulder the responsibility -- and the 16 million pound Italian makes his Liverpool debut today. With two wins from two in the Premier League, as well as progression to the Europa League group stage, it's been a dream start for Tottenham head coach Mauricio Pochettino. Leicester now go on to play Stoke City after the international break, whilst Arsenal face a tough clash at home to Manchester City in two weeks' time, before an important game against Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League three days later. Wenger will be hoping that he has acquired another striker before then, as a Giroud-shaped hole in the starting line-up desperately needs to be filled, and quickly.
As for Arsenal, they will be frustrated with the point, as they will have wanted to claim all three in order to keep the pressure on Chelsea and Swansea City at the top of the table. Giroud's absence was both noticeable and costly, as Sanogo struggled in front of goal, whilst the Gunners also struggled at the back, particularly when having to deal with Leicester's dangerous set-pieces and lofted balls.
Another excellent performance from Leicester means that they have earned themselves an impressive point, one that could have been three if Szczesny wasn't in such inspired form when called upon. The hosts caused Arsenal plenty of problems when attacking, with their pace and power proving too much for the Gunners' back four to deal with on more than one occasion. Leicester defended admirably as well, with Morgan in particular putting in a fantastic shift in the back line to deny Arsenal the opportunity to leave the King Power Stadium with all three points.

The two sides are back out on the pitch ahead of the start of the second half.

Leicester have defended well so far but they will be well aware that it is only going to get harder as the game goes on and legs begin to tire.

Siem de Jong went closest for the Toon, forcing a good save out of Guzan, Newcastle enjoyed the better of the second half until Williamson's dismissal. Half chances aplenty, but there wasn't the quality on show - Villa miss Benteke while Newcastle need to bring in additional reinforcements.
FULL TIME! It stays goalless at Villa Park, with Aston Villa and Newcastle playing out a rather drab contest. The goalkeepers had little do to, despite both outfits having dominant spells, before Mike Williamson was sent off late on for his second bookable offence.
(90’) Agbonlahor tries to win a header over Janmaat, but the Englishman is penalised for pushing the Dutchman. Heavy rain is effecting the final couple of minutes, with Villa desperately pushing forward. Off the ball, Gouffran lands awkwardly on his lower back and stays down.
--- 90’ +2 Substitution S. Taylor enters the game and replaces Ayoze Pérez. ---
(90’) Ayoze Perez is withdrawn by Pardew, despite having only been on the field for ten munutes or so. Steven Taylor is introduced, as Villa go on the attack. A deep free-kick is floated into the box, but De Jong beats Baker to it and concedes a corner!
--- 90’ +1 Red card! M. Williamson gets a second yellow card and is sent off! ---
(90’) RED CARD! Williamson receives his second yellow card in the first of four minutes of stoppage time. The central defender has no complaints, bringing down Delph due to simply not being able to get out of the way.
(90’) After a stoppage in play, due to Villa fans behind the goal refusing to give Colback the ball, Guzan is able to punch away a Newcastle corner. There isn't long left, but the Toon are in the ascendancy.
(88’) Good save from Guzan! Ayoze and De Jong combine well, before the Dutchman fires a powerful effort straight at the goalkeeper! Guzan can't hold, but pounces on the loose ball at the second attempt! The away fans start making plenty of noise again!
(87’) Westwood flights in the resulting free-kick, but Janmaat is the man who gets closest to it! Nobody makes contact, ending up in a Newcastle goal-kick. It's a cagey end to proceedings, with neither outfit wanting to lose now we're at this stage of the game.
--- 86’ Yellow card M. Williamson is yellow-carded. ---
(86’) There's less than five minutes left of normal time, with neither side appearing to have the tools required to find a winner. Carlos Sanchez is booked for a cynical challenge, before Williamson joins the Colombian for an off-the-ball tug on Bent.
--- 85’ Yellow card C. Sánchez gets yellow. ---
(84’) Big chance for Ayoze! Cabella sets back a pass to the advancing Dummett, before the left-back whips in a dangerous cross to the back post! Baker misses the header, meaning that the former Tenerife man is slightly unsighted! He swings a leg at it, but blazes way over!
--- 82’ Substitution N. Baker enters play, replacing A. Cissokho. ---
(82’) Cissokho slowly walks to the bench, after deciding that he isn't able to continue. Nathan Baker warms up and is quickly slotted into the back four, but Newcastle might feel as though they can exploit the new substitute before he can settle into the pace of the game.
(81’) Play is briefly stopped, due to Cissokho landing awkwardly on his ankle following a header. Ten minutes remain for either side to find an opening goal, but neither goalkeeper has had a great deal to do in the second half. Janmaat cuts in well from the right once again, but Delph dispossess him brilliantly as the Dutchman looks to shoot.
(79’) Bent goes close! Delph drives well from the centre of midfield, before clipping a left-footed cross into the penalty area! The former England international meets it, but can only loop the ball onto the roof of the net! In retrospect, the linesman had his flag up, so it wouldn't have counted anyway.
--- 77’ Substitution Ayoze Pérez comes on for E. Rivière. ---
(77’) Newcastle also make an offensive change, replacing the hard-working Riviere with Ayoze Perez. The Spaniard can provide plenty of positive running, but also has the lethal touch in front of goal when asked. With not long left on the clock, the substitutes will have to start well to have an impact.
--- 76’ Substitution K. Richardson is replaced with D. Bent. ---
(76’) Villa win a free-kick 25 yards from goal, allowing for the hosts to load the box. Before the dead ball is taken, Bent is brought into the fray in place of Richardson. The poacher could have a profound impact on this game! Senderos rises well at the back post, but loops his header high and wide.
(74’) Darren Bent is now the man Lambert is turning to and rightly so. Villa have mustered up plenty of half chances, but nobody on the field has the goalscoring instinct required to translate them into goals.
(72’) Westwood releases Weimann, but the Villa forward is flagged offside and has to watch his mouth given his earlier booking. With narrowly over a quarter of an hour left to play, Villa are sitting a little deeper courtesy of Sanchez helping to shore up the midfield.
--- 70’ Substitution S. de Jong comes on for V. Anita. ---
(70’) De Jong takes to the field in place of Anita, which probably spells out that Pardew isn't happy to settle for a point. This game is ready for the taking from either side, with neither coach believing that a loss should be on the cards this afternoon.
(69’) After appearing to control a crossfield ball with his arm, which the Austrian forward was penalised for, Weimann is booked for dissent. De Jong is stripped off and ready to go, with the Dutchman possessing the technical ability to make a difference.
--- 68’ Yellow card A. Weimann gets yellow. ---
--- 67’ Yellow card P. Senderos gets yellow. ---
(67’) Senderos is now given a yellow card, for bringing down Riviere off the ball. It's end-to-end stuff, but there really isn't the quality on show for either side to stamp their authority on the match.
(65’) Sanchez clips a brilliant pass over Dummett to find the chest of Hutton, who can't quite hook a cross into the six-yard box. Villa win the corner, but Westwood's delivery is absolutely terrible. The home fans applaud the Colombian's first contribution in their colours.
(63’) N'Zogbia is replaced by Carlos Sanchez, with the Frenchman's earlier yellow card perhaps making Lambert's mind up for him. With the former Elche man plying his trade as a central midfield presence, Villa might be switching to a 4-3-3.
--- 62’ Substitution C. N'Zogbia is replaced with C. Sánchez. ---
(61’) A few corners in quick succession, as Pardew's men look to continue their good start to the second half. Carlos Sanchez is warming up for the hosts, with the Colombia international being prepared for his Villa debut.
(59’) What a chance for Williamson! Cabella picks up possession at the edge of the box, before clipping a brilliant ball towards the back post! The former Wycombe man watches it all the way, but attempts a volley rather than a header! He misses the ball entirely, much to the amusement of the home fans. He had too long to watch it and over-think, perhaps.
(58’) Newcastle are growing into the game more, with Villa giving the ball away needlessly throughout play since the restart. Riviere is picked out by another cross, but fails to turn an acrobatic effort towards goal! Agbonlahor is given a warning by the referee after shoving Williamson to the ground.
(56’) Janmaat goes close! The Netherlands international cuts inside from the right-hand side, before unleashing an effort across goal with his left foot! It whistles narrowly over the angle where post meets crossbar! Guzan wasn't getting there.
(55’) Siem de Jong begins his warm-up for the away side, as Pardew might just be starting to tire of the lack of presence the Toon have in forwards areas. Riviere has worked incredibly hard, but possession isn't sticking to the former Monaco striker.
(53’) A couple of half chances already in this second half, with Newcastle seeing the early possession. They certainly look rejuvenated, but Riviere is still cutting an isolated figure at the head of the Toon attack.
(51’) Janmaat is denied by Guzan! Colback's deep free-kick is nodded back across goal by Williamson, providing an opportunity for the former Feyenoord man! The Dutchman gets his head on it, but can only direct straight at Guzan, who tips over for a corner - which is cleared.
--- 50’ Yellow card C. N'Zogbia gets yellow. ---
(50’) N'Zogbia picks up the first yellow card of the game, as the former Wigan forward rakes his studs down the back of Cabella's calf. It wasn't a nice one whatsoever from the Frenchman, who apologises to his compatriot.
(49’) Williamson looks for a lofted pass over Vlaar, which Riviere attempted to run on to, but the Dutchman just about manages to put in a defensive header. Weimann then tries to break, but slips as he attempts to shift play over to the right-hand side. The atmosphere has gone a little bit flat at Villa Park.
(47’) No changes for either side, unsurprisingly, due to a solid first half from both outfits. As we progress, offensive changes may need to be made, as applying the finishing touch hasn't been either team's strong suit. Partly, perhaps, down to the absences of Christian Benteke and former striker Loic Remy for rather different reasons.
(46’) We are back underway! Both sides will still feel as though they can go on to win this game, though thus far the lethal touch has escaped them. The Magpies need to take at least a point from this afternoon, as something of a confidence boost if nothing else.
Pardew's men are pressing well and making blocks when required, with Krul called into rare action in between the sticks. Guzan has had more to do, but Newcastle's offensive four aren't combining to great effect. Be sure to rejoin us in a quarter of an hour for all of the second half action!
HALF TIME! It's goalless at Villa Park, but we haven't been short of chances! The hosts have looked very dangerous on the break, with both Hutton and Cissokho offering plenty of energy on the overlap. Riviere hasn't had much service for Newcastle, who faded during the last ten minutes of play.
(45’) N'Zogbia feeds Hutton, who darts inside and sends Anita the wrong way with a clever body feint. The Scot dips a cross into the back post area, but there's nobody from the home side to meet it.
(45’) Brilliant play from Westwood! A clearance down the line is controlled on Westwood's knee before the midfield flicks a pass around the corner to N'Zogbia! The Frenchman drives inside and tries to find Weimann, but Newcastle press well to force their former winger wide.
(43’) Hutton covers across excellently from the right-hand side to defuse a dangerous situation for Villa, before being adjudged to have been fouled by Janmaat. The Scotland international limps back into position, but there isn't much wrong with him. Only a few minutes until the break now.
(41’) Weimann tries to shoot from 25 yards, ignoring two clear options on his left-hand side. Off-the-ball, Cabella takes a long while to get back to his feet after seemingly being caught in the face by N'Zogbia's hand. There doesn't appear to be a lot in it, but the Frenchman stays down long enough for his team to put the ball out of play.
(39’) Agbonlahor is found by an excellent cross from the left by Delph, but the Englishman isn't able to get enough contact on his header to place the ball into the bottom right corner! Villa are looking dangerous on the break, but their leading Premier League goalscorer should have done better there.
(38’) Despite all of the pressure on both goals, both 'keepers have only been forced into very routine saves. Both Agbonlahor and Riviere haven't been given good enough service to have a fair chance to put their team ahead.
(36’) N'Zogbia breaks to the byline once again, but Colback tracks back excellently to deny the former Newcastle man. Villa win the corner, allowing for their big central defensive two to come forward, but Janmaat beats Cissokho to the header to clear. Riviere breaks, but is stopped by a firm sliding challenge from Richardson.
(34’) Slightly over ten minutes until the break, with this contest incredibly hard to call. Neither appear to have the cutting edge required, either on the pitch nor on the bench. Both sides' offensive weapons are slowly blunting themselves after smashing themselves against the opposition defence with no joy.
(32’) Riviere has half a chance! Cabella manages to slide a pass in behind Senderos for the former Monaco man to chase! He goes to ground in order to get a shot away, but from a tight angle can only send the ball straight at Guzan, who gets down well to smother.
(30’) Half an hour has passed and this game is still crying out for a goal. Neither side is willing to commit too many players forward to leave them short at the back, but Villa break upfield. Delph creates a yard of space on his left foot to shoot, but the former Leeds youngsters blazes over the crossbar!
(28’) Weimann delivers a teasing ball right across the length of the six-yard box, but nobody is present to slide in and poke it home! Villa are whipping far more telling balls into the opposition penalty area, but as of yet they haven't fallen to a claret and blue shirt.
(27’) Delph plays an excellent ball in behind the Newcastle lines for Richardson to chase, but Colback tracks his man and clears. The ball is whipped back into the box, with a half chance for Agbonlahor, but Janmaat slides in well to make a vital block!
(25’) Riviere continues to have to come deep to find the ball, giving the Frenchman plenty of running to do. Newcastle are looking the more likely to make things happen, but Villa haven't surrendered any real chances on Guzan's goal. Gouffran sees a shot blocked by Hutton, before the rebound is sent bobbling wide by Cabella!
(23’) A poor backpass from Hutton allows for Riviere to hopefully chase the ball back towards Guzan, but the USA international hoofs upfield before the former Monaco man can get a touch of the ball. The Frenchman has been busy, but hasn't had much good service.
(21’) Sissoko wriggles through a gap in the centre of midfield, muscling past Westwood and Delph before being pulled back by the former Crewe man. Mike Dean gives the Magpies a set piece opportunity from 25 yards. The former Sunderland midfielder blasts high into the stands.
(20’) Sissoko appears to be shifted over to the right-hand side in order to track the gallivanting runs of Cissokho, leaving Cabella to sit more centrally in attacking midfield. Tracking back certainly isn't the best side to the latter's game.
(18’) Colback concedes a free-kick from 25 yards, chopping down his man. N'Zogbia tries his luck after a well-rehearsed dead ball routine, but swerves the ball narrowly wide of the right-hand post! Krul was worried there!
(16’) Newcastle continue to see more of the ball, but Agbonlahor and N'Zogbia have shown promise on the break. The Mapgies work possession out to the right-hand side for Cabella, with Riviere darting in front of his man at the near post expecting the ball, but the former Montpellier man's cross is awful.
(14’) Much to the delight of the home fans, Vlaar is slowly back to his feet and runs off his knock on the touchline. On-field, N'Zogbia drives down the right before jinking inside Dummett, but the Frenchman is penalised for shoulder barging into the covering Williamson.
(12’) Gouffran manages to win a corner from a slipping Senderos. Cabella is the man to take, lofting it into the near post area. Janmaat gets the flick-on, but Gouffran can't apply a finish at the back post! After the Frenchman innocuously clashed with Vlaar in the process of his terrible effort, the Dutchman goes down holding his knee.
(10’) Cissokho marauds down the left flank once again, before fizzing in a threatening cross, which Krul has to be at his best to race out and smother at the first time of asking. The Valencia loanee is having some joy against Janmaat thus far.
(9’) N'Zogbia nods narrowly over! Cissokho delivers from the left-hand side, whose looping cross finds the Frenchman at the back post! The former Wigan man tries to lift a header over Krul and inside the far post, heading back across goal, but the ball lands on the roof of the net!
(7’) Cabella chops inside before sliding a pass into the path of Janmaat. The Dutchman whips in a searching cross to Riviere, but Westwood is able to get rid. Newcastle are looking much more threatening in the opening stages. Colback launches in a free-kick from deep, which Williamson can only meet and steer well wide with his head.
(6’) Dummett's poor touch allows Villa's counter to develop, with Agbonlahor cutting in from the left flank and shaping to shoot. Williamson slides in to make a good block, sparing his defensive teammate's blushes somewhat. A lively start at Villa Park!
(5’) Dummett overlaps down the left-hand side excellently, before whipping in a devilish cross to the back post. Cissokho is forced to hurriedly hack behind for a corner. Newcastle play it short, but an eventual shot is deflected, looping comfortably into Guzan's arms - allowing the hosts to break.
(4’) The Magpies continue to look composed on the ball, with Pardew's men trying some quick triangles in forward areas. Gouffran tries to switch play and find Cabella on the right, but the Frenchman overhits it and fails to find the chest of his compatriot.
(2’) Vlaar starts as he means to go on, shielding the ball out of play excellently under pressure from Riviere. Newcastle have the early possession, with Villa happy to sit back and look to break with their lively midfield runners.
(1’) We are underway in the first half at Villa Park! The home side struggled somewhat at home last season, with this afternoon constituting an excellent chance to kick-start their campaign. Lambert's men are in their claret and blue strip, while the Toon are in their customary black and white stripes.
We're not far away from kick-off now, with both the hosts and the Magpies coming out into the afternoon air. The Premier League's early game is about to get started, with the two competing sides seeing this as a realistic opportunity to take a much-needed three points!
Only ten minutes until the two teams will be making their way out into the turf, victim of plenty of expectation. New Villa signing Carlos Sanchez is on the bench, following a solid World Cup campaign with Colombia. Plenty of exciting talent has been brought into Pardew's side, leaving Villa captain Ron Vlaar to try and keep things watertight at the back. Be sure to stick around for all of the action!
Newcastle substites: De Jong, Perez, Haidara, Elliot, Obertan, Taylor, Abeid.
Newcastle starting line-up: Krul; Janmaat, Williamson, Coloccini; Dummett; Colback, Anita; Cabella, Sissoko, Gouffan, Riviere.
Aston Villa substitutes: Sanchez, Baker, Bacuna, Cole, Bent, Given, Grealish.
Aston Villa starting line-up: Guzan; Hutton, Vlaar, Senderos, Cissokho; Westwood, Delph; Weimann, Richardson, N'Zogbia; Agbonlahor.
TEAM NEWS: Emmanuel Riviere will continue to search for his first Premier League goal as a lone forward, with new signing Remy Cabella aiming to continue to excite on the right-hand side. No changes for Pardew's outfit either, after a very impressive performance which pushed Man City to the wire. Jack Colback and Vurnon Anita are partners in shielding the back four. Siem de Jong takes a place on the bench again.
TEAM NEWS: Paul Lambert's side is unchanged from the one which defeated the Potters on the opening weekend. Alan Hutton continues with his shot at redemption at right-back, while loanee Aly Cissokho retains his place on the other side of defence. Charles N'Zogbia, Kieran Richardson and Andi Weimann provide the offensive midfield running to support Gabby Agbonlahor.
I'm Simon Harrison and I will be keeping you up to date with all of the action from Villa Park, as the hosts attempt to keep their winning run going. With both coaches confident with their previous starting line-ups, there isn't much in the way of change - if it isn't broken, don't fix it. At the moment, the Toon sit bottom of the league, but given we're in the embryonic stages of the campaign, it isn't a reflection worth paying any attention to.
Hello and welcome to live coverage of Aston Villa versus Newcastle United, as both sides look to kick on from promising opening games and grab some more early points. While the Magpies may have lost to Man City, there were plenty of positives for Alan Pardew to take - while Paul Lambert's men managed to defeat Stoke City courtesy of an Andi Weimann strike.

So that was CHELSEA 2-0 LEICESTER CITY. I've been Alex Stewart (and as far as I know I still am). Thank you for joining me for today's LIVE coverage and I hope to see you again soon.
All in all, while the first half was drab, the second was very lively, and Chelsea were certainly the better side. Are they the best side in the League? It's an absurd question this early, but when Chelsea start to move through the gears, then they look pretty unstoppable.
The two young goalkeepers gave decent accounts of themselves too. Courtois and Schmeichel are both good at claiming crosses and dominating their areas, though the Leicester man might be cross with himself for Chelsea's first.
The biggest single worry for the Foxes must be the ability to convert chances. Nugent fluffed two one-on-ones, and though he forced Courtois into good saves, he should have scored at least one.
Leicester showed the same resilience and occasional enterprise that saw them gain a draw last week, and the performances of Moore, Morgan, Hammond, and Schlupp must give Nigel Pearson significant hope for the season.
A slightly tawdry first half gave way to a vibrant second as Chelsea stepped it up significantly and two good goals, the first after superb skill from Ivanovic teed up Costa, the second all Hazard's own work, gave the Blues a well-deserved victory.
(90’) FIN! And that's the final whistle! Chelsea have run out 2-0 winners over a solid and at times enterprising Leicester team.
(90’) The three added minutes of this game are up but Willian is still receiving some treatment. He has been bright since his introduction.
(90’) Drogba is in the Leicester box making a nuisance of himself after a Matic cross. Hazard has the ball out wide and tries to run down the clock a bit. Willian is on the floor holding his back. This game is defintely coming to its end point.
(90’) Chelsea and Leicester have both continued to have a go. The centre-back pairing of Moore and Morgan win the ball from Drogba. They look exhausted.
(89’) Cahill heads into Schmeichel's hands and he releases Nugent, who tries to feed Wood. Credit to Leicester: they have continued to have a go. Hazard fouls De Laet but Chelsea win the ball back and Willian comes again.
(88’) Leicester try to attack again but Matic, how has been quietly good today, smothers the attack. Willian forces a good stop from Schmeichel as his shot heads high and central after a surging run.
(87’) It is! And Leicester win a corner. It's comfortably headed away by Ivanovic though and Drogba frees Ramires. The Chelsea attack stutters though but Leicester's clearance is weak and the Blues come again.
(86’) Schlupp is fouled by Ivanovic deep in the Chelsea half wide left. Let's see if the delivery is better from Albrighton than it was from Mahrez.
(85’) Leicester are still trying to get forward though. De Laet swings one in from deep towards Wood but Courtois grabs it. He then, as is his wont, hurls it out to start another Chelsea attack. He really is a class act.
--- 84’ Substitution L. Ulloa is done for the day. C. Wood is his replacement. ---
(84’) Wood is on for Ulloa as Ivanovic heads over. The Serbian has been a real attacking threat from full-back today.
(82’) Leicester get their first shot away in a good while. Schlupp squares the ball to Albrighton who hammers on low but Courtois gathers. Nugent's misses are looming large in the mind now, given how Chelsea accelerated away.
(81’) Chelsea are still attacking but mostly as a way of keeping the ball from Leicester. The pace has dropped off considerably and Ramires has certainly helped to tighten up the Chelsea system.
--- 80’ Substitution Diego Costa is replaced with D. Drogba. ---
(80’) Mourinho is still prowling his technical area but he must know this game is in the bag now. Ramires slips a cute ball through to Ivanovic but the Chelsea move fizzles out after a cross is headed away.
(79’) Costa is off after a goal-scoring home debut to go with his goal-scoring debut debut. Drogba is on and the Chelsea fans are delighted.
--- 77’ Assist The assist came from Fàbregas. ---
--- 77’ Goal! GOAL HAZARD! That was beautiful! He drives in from the left and takes out a few Leicester defenders with a sudden surge of pace, before slamming it low into the far corner. When Hazard is good, he is pretty special. ---
(77’) 2-0 now to Chelsea and that really should be it. There was deflection from the unlucky Moore for that Hazard goal. And now Drogba is warming up. Willian, looking lively on the right since his introduction, keeps a Chelsea move going.
(75’) Leicester are by no means dead and buried but their efforts lead to a Chelsea counter. Costa runs forward but his effort to find Ivanovic at the back post is pretty bad.
(74’) Schlupp bursts forwards after Willian nearly catches out Moore but the big defender manages to put it clear. Leicester take the throw-in but lose it immediately. Chelsea lump it foward but lose it themselves.
--- 73’ Substitution G. Taylor-Fletcher enters the game and replaces D. Hammond. ---
(73’) This is a more settled, content Chelsea now, keeping possession and playing it around the back. They know they don't need to press the game and leave themselves open to the sort of chances Nugent spurned earlier.
(72’) And we're off again. Chelsea stroke it around and Willian pings one out wide towards Hazard. Hammond is off and replaced by Taylor-Fletcher.
(71’) A respite from the action as players take on water and Hammond gets his legs seen to.
--- 70’ Substitution Willian enters the game and replaces Oscar. ---
(70’) Willian is straight into the action, neatly playing it around with Ivanovic. Hammond falls over with some cramp.
--- 68’ Substitution R. Mahrez is replaced with M. Albrighton. ---
(68’) Hazard makes some space for himself by playing a two-one with Costa and flashes a low shot in but he scuffs it slightly and Schmeichel gathers.Oscar is coming off and Willian is coming on, which is pretty like-for-like, really.
(67’) Morgan shoulders Costa off the ball to bring a Chelsea free-kick. Albrighton is going to come on for Mahrez for Leicester. Albrighton is a quick winger who will look to feed the front two, especially Ulloa.
(66’) Mahrez's corners have been consistently poor. Oscar bursts forwards at pace and there is some neat interchange in and around the Leicester box, but it comes to naught as Chelsea concede a free-kick as Oscar brings down Hammond.
(65’) Chelsea will surely settle into their stride now. They dismantled Burnely in twenty minutes and could well do the same to Leicester here now. But Leicester have a corner and the lumps from the back are up again.
--- 64’ Substitution Ramires enters play, replacing A. Schürrle. ---
(63’) Ramires is on for Schurrle. Classic Jose.
--- 62’ Goal! GOAL GOAL GOAL FOR COSTA! A home debut goal for the big Brazilian! A glorious step-over from Ivanovic and it looked like Costa had miscontrolled the slide pass, but he slams it home. Unlucky Leicester, but it had been coming. ---
(60’) Chelsea win the ball back and go long but it goes out for a goal kick. We can all catch our breath for a moment.
(60’) The Chelsea front four are now in their rotating, floating swing. Costa is forced off the ball by Moore, who has been the archetypal rock. The ball is pinged long and Nugent is well marked by Cahill.
(58’) Schurrle cannons a shot off the resolute Liam Moore but Chelsea come again. This is frantic now and both teams have had superb chances. Chelsea build and Fabregas has a shot comfortably smothered by Schmeichel.
(56’) FABREGAS! Oh what a waste. Fabreags tried to clip over over the advancing Schmeichel at his near post after a delicious through-ball. The Dane stood tall though and it was a wasted opportunity.
(56’) The first ten minutes of this half have flown past as the game has opened up enormously. Chelsea have clearly had a rollocking from their manager.
(54’) OH NUGENT! A second one-on-one is fluffed by the Foxes striker, though Courtois did save it well. That was a second gilt-edged chance for Leicester. They win a corner.
(53’) Claims for hand-ball there as Oscar's shot is blocked by some part of Morgan. Schmeichel saves brilliantly and from the resulting corner Leicester pour forward.
(52’) Courtois gathers superbly under pressure and then releases Oscar, who feeds Schurrle. Schurrle's shot goes over from wide left though and we can catch our breath a bit.
(52’) This second half has already kicked on a lot from the first. Leicester have a corner. Both Moore and Morgan are up.
--- 51’ Yellow card D. Hammond goes into the referee's book. ---
(51’) Hammond is booked and immediately forces a turnover from the free-kick, releasing Nugent, who forces a good block from Courtois with his legs.
(50’) Schurrle is fouled by Hammond and there is some writhing. Hammond looks sheepish because that was a bit clunky.
(48’) Oscar curled one onto the post there before Azpilicueta stood up a cross for Ivanovic. Chelsea win a corner, which Ulloa forces out but the Blues come again. Hazard concedes a free-kick after nibbling away at Schlupp's heels.
(47’) OSCAR HITS THE POST! And then IVANOVIC has a header clawed away by Schmeichel! Chelsea have come out of the blocks here.
(47’) Schurrle appears to be pushed more centrally with Oscar wider on the right. It's not a classic 4-4-2 but it might offer more penetration to Chelsea.
(45’) The teams are back out and Chelsea kick off.
Stay right here for all the action LIVE from the second half of Chelsea vs Leicester City from Stamford Bridge.
For Leicester, I suspect Nigel Pearson will be demanding more of the same and seeking to instil confidence into his Foxes side that they can grab at least a point from this game.
The question of the second half will be at what point Jose brings on Didier Drogba and whether he moves to a 4-4-2 or uses the Ivorian as a replacement from Costa.
Chelsea will certainly be disappointed to go in without scoring, but they retain the ability to make something from nothing, especially with Cesc Fabregas on the pitch. Leicester will rely on snapping away and countering, but they have played well and it would not be a surprise if they got something from this game.
For Leicester, it is hard to pick out a player from the defence or the midfield who has stood out, as all of them have worked extremely hard and done very well. Schlupp has caught the eye, certainly, but Moore and Morgan have been very solid at the back as well.
Fabregas looks a class above everyone else on the pitch in terms of creativity, though Hazard showed glimpses towards the end of the half.
It's half-time here, as Chelsea and Leicester head into the changing rooms with the scores level at 0-0. Leicester have worked hard, pressed and harried Chelsea, often forcing good turnovers and counter-attacking.
(45’) Schmeichel's physical goal-keeping style is so similar to his father's, spreading his arms and legs wide when coming out to make blocks. The Dane has been mostly solid, but it is his opposite number Courtois who has been forced into the only real save of the game.
(44’) Schlupp slides in to halt the Chelsea counter and then King crosses but Courtois gathers. Chelsea come again and Fabregas clips a ball through to Schurrle. Schmeichel hurtles out and clips the German, but he was offside anyway. Fabregas is so very good at that sort of thing.
(43’) Chelsea are doing their best to force the issue before half-time. A sublime piece of Hazard skill produces a glorious ball, cut-back to the penalty spot, but Chelsea can't capitalise.

The two sides are walking out of the tunnel now at Selhurst Park and the match will be underway shortly. Can Palace hope to achieve what they did last season without Tony Pulis? Can West Ham's new signings bring more goals to the side? This match won't be able to tell us all that, but could give either side a much needed boost very early this season!
Conversely, the home side will want to look at generating more chances today than they were able to last match at the Emirates. It's never easy for a side like Crystal Palace to maintain possession or the majority of chances against a team like Arsenal, and they did nearly hang on for a draw, but scored off of their only shot on target of the match. A solid foundation, but one that can be improved on.
One thing the visitors will want to improve on quickly: converting shots into goals. The BBC notes that they took 18 shots against Tottenham last week but failed to score on any of them. Continuing to generate that many chances will be vital for West Ham this season, and it's still very early, but three of the last five meetings between Crystal Palace and this side have ended in 1-0 draws for the Eagles; one goal may be all it takes today as well.
For the match, the off-field antics will have to be pushed from the mind of the home side who have historically struggled in the league against West Ham, with only 5 wins in 26 meetings between the two. Recent history is kinder to Crystal Palace, who won home and away over West Ham last season.

(74’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have lost three consecutive away matches in league play. They have not lost four in a row since January-February of 2011 (three of which were against teams who now play in the League Championship).
(72’) WHAT A TOUCH BY BROWN IDEYE! The striker takes a pass and takes a lovely first touch, spinning between two defenders, bursting clean through on goal. Forster rushes off his line and sticks a foot out to make a very important save!
(70’) OFF THE UPRIGHT! James Ward-Prowse stands over a free kick from 25 yards out, and curls a wonderful effort over the wall and past Foster, but he can't beat the post! So close to a breakthrough!
(68’) TADIC! The first real scoring chance of the half as Long chests a ball down into the path of the Serbian, who hits first time, firing just inches wide at the near post. Closer, that, from the hosts.
--- 66’ Yellow card Clyne picks up a yellow card, and more importantly concedes a free kick about 35 yards out from goal. There are plenty of options in the centre, but Gardner ambitiously goes for goal. Forster makes a comfortable save and the chance is wasted. ---
(64’) We have reached yet another stand still in this match as the ball is passed around amongst the defenders, without any moves forward. Fans are beginning to get a bit restless and you cannot blame them.
(62’) Berahino commits a hard foul on Tadic and Southampton win a free kick near the sidelines, about 35 yards out. They play it short and immediately give it away as yet another opportunity fails to materialize into a chance.
--- 60’ Substitution J. Davidson enters play, replacing S. Pocognoli. ---
(60’) Into the side netting! Brown Ideye's first touch of the ball is a good one, as he beats his defender at the far post to get onto the end of a cross, but his header goes into the side netting from a tight angle. Meanwhile, Pocognoli seems to have picked up a knock and his day looks to be done.
(58’) Tadic starting to come to life as well for Southampton. Every attack is being run through the Serbian. This time he cuts into the middle and onto his favored left foot. He has a go at goal, but it is a bit of a weak effort that Foster collects importantly, with a few players waiting to pounce on a rebound.
(56’) STAT ATTACK: Five of the last seven goals scored between the two teams in league play came after the 60th minute.
(54’) Shane Long gets on the end of a cross, but puts his effort over the bar. It was a difficult ball to direct onto goal. Long has just provided a bit of spark though early in this second half, and gives them another option going forward as they try and break down a Baggies team defending with nine men behind the ball.
--- 52’ Substitution HERE HE IS! West Brom's record signing, Brown Ideye, comes on to make his debut with Victor Anichebe struggling with an injury he appears to have just picked up. Can the Nigerian add some flair to the Baggies attack? ---
(50’) Southampton starting to take the match to West Brom, but continue to lack pace in their attack. They are working it into some good areas here, but they are a bit too patient at the moment, content on keeping the ball as opposed to attacking the goal.
(48’) A lengthy delay as the second half can hardly get underway before Mulumbu goes to ground and requires attention. He is forced to go off for the time being, and play can finally resume.
--- 46’ Substitution S. Davis is replaced with S. Long. ---
(46’) Southampton kick-off as we get this second half underway. One important change to tell you about as Shane Long comes on to make his home debut, replacing Steven Davis. The arrival of another striker should tell you a lot about Koeman's approach in this second half.
STAT ATTACK: Just four of Southampton’s players against Liverpool last weekend were in the line-up when they defeated West Brom on the opening day of last season.
On the bright side, the lack of attacking prowess from both sides means we may not have to wait long to see Shane Long and Brown Ideye brought into the match.
HALF-TIME: SOUTHAMPTON 0-0 WEST BROMWICH. A lackluster opening 45 minutes at St. Mary's, with chances were few and far between. The game is there for the taking, but neither side looks ready to take a risk at the moment. Who will provide the breakthrough, if anyone?
(45’) Referee Roger East sounds his whistle, finally bringing this first half to an end.
(45’) Two minutes to be added on at the end of the half here, as the hosts finally get themselves into the attacking third on the ball. They pass it around well, and are very patient in their build up. Tadic eventually sends a good ball into the area, but there is no one attacking the ball. A lack of movement off the ball has really hampered Southampton when they get forward.
(43’) As we approach the break, both sides look content on going into the half with this same scoreline. Southampton keeping possession well, but they appear to have no interest on getting the ball forward.
--- 42’ Yellow card C. Brunt is cautioned by the referee. ---
(41’) Chris Brunt is shown a yellow card, the first of the match, for kicking the ball away after the whistle. Not sure where the frustration came from, but something seemed to agitate the midfielder. Ridiculous decision, regardless, as he picks up an unnecessary caution.
(39’) The game is beginning to open up a bit, but it has come a bit too close to half-time. West Brom break on a counter and Anichebe nearly picks out Berahino who could be through on goal, but Jose Fonte just beats the striker to the ball and manages to clear.
(37’) GOOD SAVE BY FOSTER! Ward-Prowse works a give-and-go with Tadic. His clever return pass gives Tadic a clear look at goal, but Foster gets down well to keep out the effort. Still no breakthrough as we inch closer to half-time.
(35’) Tadic is being given little to no space to operate in this first half. A promising move from Southampton develops thanks to some smart play from Nathaniel Clyne. He picks out Tadic atop the area, and he is immediately surrounded by three defenders and eventually dispossessed.
(33’) STAT ATTACK: West Brom have won just four league games since the start of 2014, fewer than any other Premier League side, including those relegated last season.
(31’) WHAT WAS FOSTER THINKING?! The goalkeeper rushes out of the area, but a failure to communicate with his defenders causes Wisdom to push the ball past his keeper, and subsequently give it away to Tadic who has Foster out of goal. He crosses in for Pelle, but it is just an inch too high for the striker as the chance goes begging.
(29’) Back the other way come the hosts. Tadic and Bertrand link up well on the left, the Serbian sending a perfectly weighted pass to the left-back who cuts it back for Pelle. The striker hits it first time, but Jonas Olsson is there to make an important block.
(27’) Dorrans causes a turnover and breaks with great pace on the counter. He runs at the defenders with real intent, with options to either side, but sends a horrendous pass towards Berahino as the attack fizzles out.
(25’) It is a real cagey affair at the moment. The midfield is very congested and neither team looks too eager to take charge. There is little flow to the match as the constant fouls are preventing things from really taking shape. The game needs a goal as much as any.
(23’) Pocognoli getting the short end of the stick early on as he is again fouled, this time by a late tackle from Vincent Wanyama. The ensuing free kick, from about 40 yards out, has a poor delivery and Southampton regain possession.
(21’) A give away in midfield allows the Baggies to break on the counter. Brunt delivers a great ball into the area, but Bertand does well to stay strong on Anichebe and prevent the striker from getting to the cross. The left-back appears to have gotten the worst of the collision as he becomes the latest player to go down injured.
(19’) Pocognoli is back on the pitch now, much to the chagrin of the St. Mary's faithful. Meanwhile, West Brom are keeping their shape very well, and Southampton cannot find a way through at the moment. Their build up play is far too straightforward. They need to change something or this cagey affair will continue.
(17’) Scary moments here as Pocognoli appears to be in considerable pain as he collides with Pelle on his follow-through. There was nothing in the challenge, but the left-back certainly appeared to get the worst of it as his leg gets ripped out from under him.
(15’) Successive corners for West Brom, but nothing comes of it. Brunt with two good deliveries. The second is whipped in towards the far post and headed back towards the centre where the towering Fraser Forster comes out to collect amongst the mess of bodies.
(13’) STAT ATTACK: After losing both matches to West Brom in their first season back up in the top flight in 2012/13, Southampton returned the favor last year doing the double over the Baggies, winning both their meetings with by a score of 1-0. However, neither player who scored for the Saints is still with the team.
(11’) Southampton with some nice build up play, as they move forward with pace. The ball is worked out to Tadic on the left, but the winger's first time cross is into the waiting arms of Ben Foster.
(9’) West Bromwich get forward for the first time and win a cheap corner as Jose Fonte rushes a clearance. Dorrans sends a high, looping cross into the box, but it takes far too long to reach the danger area and Southampton manage to clear with ease.
(7’) Ryan Bertrand gets himself into a good attacking position and wins a free kick to the left of the area. Ward-Prowse delivers, but fails to get enough elevation on his cross as it is cleared by the first defender.
(5’) The hosts enjoy the bulk of possession early on, but have yet to threaten West Brom in attack. The midfield is quite congested at the moment which has made it difficult for Southampton to advance the ball into the danger areas.
(3’) Dusan Tadic sees the ball for the first time as the crowd cheers in anticipation. The Serbian winger sends a cross in for Graziano Pelle, but it just eludes the striker as West Brom clear. But you can see early on just how excited these fans are about their new signing.
(1’) And we are off! West Bromwich get us started, moving left to right, sporting their white tops with blue stripes, while the hosts wear their new red and white striped tops. It is a beautiful day for football!

Swansea City's back-to-back victories have set them up perfectly for next Saturday's clash at home to West Bromwich Albion, whilst Burnley, who have lost both of their opening games of the season, now face a tough clash at home to Manchester United in the weekend's early kick-off.
Today's clash was a game of two halves, as Burnley bounced back from a first half in which they were second best to Swansea City throughout by bossing the second period and causing the hosts' defence a plethora of problems. However, the Swansea City back four remained strong and refused to give in, with Williams and Amat putting in particularly impressive performances. Despite not playing at their best in the last 45 minutes, Swansea City arguably deserve the victory, as Burnley were presented with a multitude of good chances to equalise but were unable to make any of them count.
FULL-TIME: SWANSEA CITY 1-0 BURNLEY
(90’) Barnes chests the ball down, turns and volleys towards Fabianski but his shot is too powerful and it clears the crossbar, bringing an end to Burnley's chances of leaving the Liberty Stadium with a point.
(90’) One last chance for Burnley. Shackell fires a long ball into the heart of the Swansea City penalty area that meets the head of Arfield, but he's only able to send the ball into the hands of Fabianski.
--- 90’ +1 Substitution M. Sordell enters the game and replaces D. Jones. ---
(90’) Swansea City win a free-kick near the halfway line and, as expected, they take their time with the resulting set-piece, trying their hardest to waste as much time as possible as the full-time whistle fast approaches.
--- 90’ Substitution D. Tiendalli comes on for W. Routledge. ---
(90’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be three minutes of added time.
(88’) It remains all Burnley at the moment as they search for an equaliser with little over two minutes left to play. They've played wonderfully throughout the second half but the Swansea City defence have matched them with fantastic strength and discipline from start to finish.
(86’) Burnley continue to try to carve out a chance down the right flank. This time, Trippier sends a great cross into the box that almost meets Barnes, but Williams sticks out a foot and just about makes contact with the ball at the last moment.
--- 85’ Yellow card G. Sigurðsson is cautioned by the referee. ---
(84’) Sigurdsson lunges in and commits a poor challenge on Shackell just inside the Burnley half of the pitch. The visitors take the resulting free-kick quickly and work the ball up towards Ings on the edge of the penalty area where he is seemingly brought down by Ki, but the referee ignores the protests from the Burnley players and fans and waves play on.
--- 82’ Substitution L. Jutkiewicz is replaced with A. Barnes. ---
(82’) Swansea City have pushed as many bodies as possible back into their half of the pitch as Burnley try to score a last-minute equaliser, with Ki and Shelvey now almost playing as centre backs in the middle of a back six. Burnley are pushing hard but the hosts are refusing to be beaten.
(80’) Once again, Swansea City are awarded a free-kick not far away from the Burnley penalty area after a clash between Duff and Montero down the left flank. It's played short and eventually finds it's way to Ki on the edge of he box but his attempted volley flies just over the crossbar.
--- 79’ Yellow card M. Duff goes into the referee's book. ---
(78’) Wallace commits a poor challenge on Routledge just outside the Burnley penalty area and the hosts are awarded a free-kick. Sigurdsson sends a deep cross towards the back post but it's cleared away from danger before the referee then awards a free-kick for Burnley after a scuffle in the box.
(76’) Ki sends a wonderful ball into the path of Routledge, who is completely unmarked on the right hand side of the Burnley penalty area. He has plenty of time to set himself up before crossing in towards Gomis but instead he decides to fire a pass in early and, as a result, the effort is poor and easily blocked by the Burnley defence.
(74’) Wallace steps up to take the resulting set-piece but he fires his effort into the wall. The ball bounces back into his path and he tries another shot on goal but, again, the wall of white shirts in front of him are there to keep the danger away from Fabianski.
--- 73’ Yellow card J. Shelvey receives a yellow card. ---
--- 72’ Substitution R. Wallace enters play, replacing M. Taylor. ---
(72’) Ki loses possession in the middle of the Swansea City half of the pitch and Marney embarks on a marauding run forward, only to be stopped by a poor challenge by Shelvey 25 yards away from goal.
(70’) Burnley have arguably been the best side in the second half, particularly in the last 15 minutes, but no matter how hard they try they still can't find the back of the Swansea City net. The hosts are on thin ice at the moment.
(68’) Fingertip save by Fabianski! Ings muscles his way through the Swansea City defence before squaring the ball to Jones, who fires a great shot towards goal from just inside the penalty area. Fabianski just about gets a finger onto the ball to tip it round the post and just out of the reach of the fast-approaching Jutkiewicz.
--- 66’ Substitution J. Montero enters play, replacing N. Dyer. ---
(66’) Montero, just moments after coming on for Dyer, turns around Trippier and gallops down the left wing but is unable to control the ball properly and accidentally runs the ball out of play.
--- 64’ Substitution B. Gomis enters play, replacing W. Bony. ---
(64’) What a great chance for Burnley! Jutkiewicz is presented with a golden opportunity to equalise for the visitors but his headed effort misses the goal by mere inches. That was easily the best chance Burnley have had all day and the miss could prove costly.
(62’) Jutkiewicz and Williams clash near the halfway line, resulting in a free-kick for Burnley. They try to work their way patiently down the right flank but Neil Taylor cuts out the danger before sending the ball up towards Bony.
(60’) The tables have turned and it's now Burnley that are bossing possession in the Swansea City half of the pitch, but Williams and Amat are looking as strong as ever in the centre of defence.
(58’) Shelvey gives away an unnecessary free-kick by the corner flag on the left wing with a poor challenge on Matt Taylor. The resulting set-piece is whipped into the box where it meets the head of Bony but his clearance only goes as far as Marney, who tries to volley the ball into the back of the net but his effort is wild and it fails to trouble Fabianski.
(56’) Taylor sends a beautiful ball over the top of the Burnley defence and into the path of Routledge but the Englishman is just offside, bringing an end to another promising Swnasea City counter attack.
(54’) Burnley are enjoying a good spell of possession at the moment but are still finding it difficult to beat the Swansea City defence, who continue to cause Jutkiewicz and Ings a multitude of problems.
(52’) Arfield is presented with a wonderful chance to equalise for Burnley but he skies his shot from the edge of the penalty over the crossbar.
(50’) Great chance for Burnley! After nice play between the Burnley midfielders the ball ends up with Jutkiewicz by the far post. He sets himself up and goes to shoot but Williams throws his body in the way of the ball and sends it flying out for a corner.
(49’) Bony somehow finds himself onside and competely unmarked in front of goal, but he takes too long on the ball and is dispossessed at the last minute by Shackell.
(48’) Arfield brings down Taylor with a poor high challenge 30 yards out and Swansea City are awarded with a free-kick in a dangerous position. Sigurdsson decides to roll the back out to Shelvey who fires a rocket of a shot towards goal, but the Burnley wall stays strong and blocks the effort.
(47’) Swansea City have started the second half just as they finished the first; confident, stylish and full of flair.
(46’) And we're off once again!
The two sides are making their way back onto the pitch ahead of the start of the second half. Can Burnley find a way back into the game or will Swansea City hold on to record back-to-back Premier League victories?
As for Burnley, Ings came closest to scoring for the visitors when his shot from the edge of the penalty area just cleared the crossbar, but apart from that they have struggled in Swansea City's half of the pitch and will have to do a lot of work in the second half if they are going to find a way back into this game.
Apart from five minutes or so of Burnley possession midway through the half, Swansea City have dominated this opening 45 minutes and are deservedly 1-0 ahead. The hosts always looked like they were going to go ahead first and have been wonderful in attack, with Dyer and Routledge being constant thorns in the side of the Burnley defence.
HALF-TIME: SWANSEA CITY 1-0 BURNLEY
(45’) The fourth official has indicated that there will be just one minute of added time.
(43’) Another good chance for Swansea City to make it 2-0, as this time Bony finds himself in space on the edge of the penalty are and decides to shoot, but the effort is weak and it rolls across the ground and into the hands of Heaton.
(41’) Great chance for Sigurdsson after wonderful slow and patient build-up play by Swansea City! Dyer is able to send a cross into the centre of the box that Bony decides to head back into the path of Sigurdsson, but his volleyed effort is just a little bit too powerful and it clears the Burnley crossbar.
(39’) Swansea City seem happy to keep hold of possession and the one-goal lead as we enter the final five minutes of the first half. However, they are still finding so much space down the flanks.
(37’) Ki is caught napping in possession and almost has the ball stolen off him by Jones, but referee Craig Pawson deems the challenge a reckless one and awards Swansea City a free-kick. If he had decided to wave play on, Burnley would have been able to break away on a swift, and potentially dangerous, counter attack.
(35’) Burnley are looking slightly more dangerous in attack now. Arfield breaks into the Swansea City box and looks to set up Ings but he loses his footing before he is able to do so.
(33’) Matt Taylor and Marney try to embark on a move down the right flank but are stopped in their tracks by Shelvey, who dispossesses Matt Taylor near the corner flag before teeing up Neil Taylor to clear the ball up the pitch.
(31’) Once again, the pace of the game has slowed down somewhat after several minutes of Swansea City pressure. Burnley are slowly but surely trying to navigate their way into the hosts' penalty area but are having no luck whatsoever.
(29’) Arfield and Ki clash 30 yards out and Burnley are awarded with another free-kick in a promising position. It's whipped in towards the heart of the penalty area but Bony is back to help out his defence and he does so with a fantastic headed clearance.
(27’) Swansea City have been full of confidence since going ahead. Once again, they take advantage of the space down the left wing before Marney slides in to dispossess Routledge before he's able to send a cross into the box.
(25’) Arfield is brought down by Neil Taylor on the right wing and Burnley are awarded with a free-kick in a dangerous position. It's whipped in by Matt Taylor but it's far too deep and Fabianski is able to punch the ball away before the referee blows his whistle for a foul on the Swansea City goalkeeper.
--- 23’ Assist The assist came from G. Sigurðsson. ---
--- 23’ Goal! GOAL! Swansea City get the first goal of the game and it's richly deserved. The space opened up for Dyer and he took advantage of it, galloping down the right flank before cutting into the box and slotting the ball past Heaton at the near post. ---
(21’) After 20 frantic minutes, the pace of the game has slowed down somewhat, with both teams now seemingly happy to take their time keeping possession in the middle of the pitch.
(19’) Dyer and Routledge are finding a lot of space down the right and left flanks, respectively, and their pace is causing Trippier and Mee a plethora of problems.
(17’) Shelvey sends a great long ball across the pitch that Routledge picks up down the left flank. He shows great skill and composure to bring the ball down and under control before sending a terrific cross into the path of Sigurdsson, but the Icelander's first time shot is low and easily saved by Heaton.
(15’) Ings has had a wonderful start to the game and has already been an important part of several Burnley attacking moves. This time, he twists and turns his way around two Swansea City defenders before swinging a dangerous cross into the box but it's just about cleared out for a corner by Taylor.
(13’) With the quarter-of-an-hour mark fast approaching, neither side are looking like they want to reduce the tempo of the game just yet. Both smell blood, and it wouldn't surprise me if we see a goal very soon.
(11’) Both sides are looking dangerous up front, with Burnley now firmly back in the game after a few worrying moments. After swift build-up play, Ings tries to send a low cross into the path of Jutkiewicz but Fabianski dives down low to grab the ball before it's able to find the Burnley striker. If it had found its way past the Swansea City goalkeeper, the ball surely would have been buried into the back of the net.
(9’) It's end-to-end stuff at the moment! This time, Sigurdsson breaks into the Burnley box before firing towards Heaton, but Duff's outstretched foot denies the Icelandic midfielder the opportunity to put his side 1-0 up.
(9’) Burnley push forward and find Ings on the edge of the Swansea City penalty area but his effort flies just over the crossbar.
(7’) Bony, yet again, is able to set up Routledge down the left wing, but this time Trippier is there to cut out the danger. The Burnley back four are finding it extremely difficult to deal with Swansea City's front line.
(6’) Fantastic football by Swansea City yet again! Bony, 10 yards inside his own half, evades two challenges before sending a long through-ball that meets a completely unmarked Routledge, but the Englishman is marginally offside.
(4’) Great chance for Swansea City! Shelvey wins the ball in the middle of the pitch and breaks away quickly before teeing up Routledge on the right hand side of the penalty area. He then whips in a lovely cross into the heart of the box that Bony meets with his head, but his effort is cleared off the line at the last moment.
(3’) Burnley have started the brighter of the two sides, taking advantage of a few gaps in the middle of the Swansea City midfield. However, they have yet to find a way past a resolute defensive line.
(1’) And we're off! Burnley, in their black away kit, get us underway, kicking from left to right.
The two sides are making their way onto the pitch. The atmosphere at the Liberty Stadium is fantastic, with both sets of fans in fine voice.

FULL-TIME: EVERTON 2-2 ARSENAL. A drastic second half turnaround looked to be all for not, when the Gunners found themselves with the same two goal hill to climb with 10 minutes to play. Wenger's side showed some incredible fighting spirit, however, as Aaron Ramsey pulled one back before Olivier Giroud equalized in the final minute of regular time. Everton will be gutted with the result, but they only have themselves to blame, falling asleep after such a fantastic opening 45 minutes.
(90’) It's all over at Goodison! The Arsenal fans taunting the home supporters as they roar back in the final minutes to steal a point, and rob the hosts of two points.
(90’) Arsenal look content with the point they never thought they would have 10 minutes ago, while Everton want to see this one out before it gets any worse for them. Less than a minute to play here, with the two sides content on running out the clock.
(90’) Into the first of four minutes of added time and Everton are stunned. The free-flowing, confident side we saw in the opening frame have been a shell of themselves in the second half, allowing the toothless Gunners a way back into the game.
--- 90’ Assist The assist came from Nacho Monreal. ---
--- 90’ Goal! Nacho Monreal does incredibly well, showing some great work ethic to track down an errant pass, keeping it in near the by-line. He cuts back and crosses in for Olivier Giroud who just out-muscles Distin and heads it back across Howard and into the bottom corner! What a comeback! ---
(90’) OLIVIER GIROUD BREAKS EVERTON HEARTS!
(87’) Cazorla tracks back to try and intercept a pass, but Naismith senses his presence and goes down to win a foul. Everton in no rush to take this free kick from about 30 yards out to the left of the goal.

(85’) Still life for the Gunners who are flowing with confidence, as they smell blood. Everton has a bit of a nervous play to them as their victory is being threatened really for the first time this half.
--- 83’ Assist Cazorla gave the assist. ---
--- 83’ Goal! Cazorla finds some space on the left, looks up and sees no one in the penalty area.
